Latest_Reviews.Comment: Good lecturer but sometimes gets carried away, midterms are standardized so some questions might come as a surprise if he didn't go over it too much in lecture. If he provides sample exams, do them, even though he says they're not gonna be similar to the real exams they will be. Textbook is optional. Easy biweekly quizzes.
Attendance not required for lecture or discussion. Passionate and funny guy. Homework is easy, quizes and tests are at the ttc and are easy.

BOWERS IS GOATED! LEs and DISs are suggested but not mandatory. The two midterms are fair. 4 Quizzes online, with 3 chances per question, given a practically identical practice quiz beforehand to prepare. Bowers is very knowledgeable, and his 8am was worth waking up for. He could prolly teach math to a sea slug he's that good at teaching. TAKE HIM
The class is super easy. The homework is optional but if you do it you're basically guaranteed an A. Lectures weren't super interesting, but clear and informative. Overall, would highly recommend.

Good lectures, provided examples and extra practices. Biweekly quizzes at AP&M, provided practices that were the same problems. Like any math exam, there were stuff that were never taught/discussed but weren't too bad. Just do the hw and quizzes. Final was also at AP&M, was told they were like the quizzes, but were pretty different.
Chem 4 had a lot of homework but he gave great feedback to students and made sure we were prepared for tests.

Difficult for an introductory class. Lots of hw that don't align with lectures so you need to figure it out on your own. Tests bi-weekly but you are allowed a cheat sheet that doesn't need to be handwritten. Nice professor and points out some topics that will be on the test during lecture.
AMAZING!!!! My favorite professor yet! Makes content engaging and interesting, the class is laid out very clearly and gave lots of partial credit on exams. 100% recommend!

Sometimes his lecture helps and sometimes it doesn't, but it's not mandatory. I spent the most time in this class for this quarter cuz his tests are pretty hard if you don't prepare a lot. The reading quiz is a lot and really confusing cuz it's mostly materials that he will not cover in the test and things we don't need to know. Overall not bad

Prof. Bussey is a very good professor, it's just the course content itself that's difficult. It can get tricky to keep up so it's important to communicate w/ your TA and ask for help. I didn't go to lectures but I was fine due to taking the class P/NP. Grading is quite fair considering the fact some things are dropped at the end of the course.

Good lectures, kinda long. Exams are all multiple choice but he doesn't give practice questions/exams. Online chapter quizzes are open book and untimed. You have to read the chapter from the textbook even if he doesn't go over some things in lecture because he'll still test you on it, lectures aren't mandatory but stuff from them will be on exam.

Amazing and hilarious professor. Made sure to listen to students and answer every question. The course itself is a little bit difficult but if you keep up with the readings and attend lecture you'll do great

Best professor at UCSD. Super passionate about his field & teaches it amazingly, easy to digest. 4 exams & he replaces your lowest grade with your final if its higher. Super caring & I struggled at first, went to office hours & got a lot of help, barely snagged an A- (90.03!) at the end! He personally complimented my commitment, amazing person/prof

There's a few exams that aren't cumulative and they are all multiple choice. The content itself is difficult since I didn't take AP PSYC in high school. The professor himself is very knowledgable and knows what he is talking about. The grading itself is very test and quiz heavy. They are also based on lecture and book so make sure you go to class.

Two midterm and one final, testing on very detail stuffs that I had almost forgotten I had even learned. His course require you to read textbook carefully, because many of the exam questions were not covered in his lectures. and Almost no curve.
He just is my favorite professor in the entire world. He is so kind, so approachable, and SO GOOD at teaching. Midterms and Final in person, but he preps you well!
GOAT of cogsci department for a reason

He was a very good teacher. He was very kind and passionate about his work. He genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed. 2 Midterms and Final online. There are extra credit options as well. Lot of info, but slides are clear and marked with what's important to know.

Not easy class, expect to memorize the entire eye & ear neuroanatomy! Class is dry & dense content but the prof is very passionate & he makes it digestible. Exams aren't easy & def requires studying + there is graded attendance. I averaged 83% on all my exams and got an A-

Taken fall 2025, this time tests were in person and not on canvas. Memorization heavy because tests aren't open-note, but can get difficult when taking other classes that require you to memorize. Fun professor and genuinely care about his class, I feel like I just have test anxiety no matter how much I study.
He was very dramatic and let kind of chaotic lectures.
he was enthusiastic, but didn't work out any of the problems, didn't fully go through any of the examples in class with full steps.

He was the worst experience as a professor for a first year student. I heard more then 80% of students failed. I ended up retaking the MPE to get out of his class and I actually ended up placing in the Math20 series (thank goodness). If you bomb any test just kiss your grade goodbye.

If you can, pick another professor. Content isnt hard but I had to learn it by myself since the tests are always significantly harder than the practice. No curve and a lot of homework. He is very nitpicky about answers and not flexible at all with dates of tests or assignments. The class itself isnt hard so if he is the only prof I would still take

Taking this class is essentially a form of academic self sabotage. I have never seen a professor go so far out of his way to watch his students fail.The midterms are designed to bury your GPA, with averages so low they're actually insulting

Peasani is an easy professor,  his tests are all super easy(easier then CHEM 4) and are all multiple choice. The only problem are the lectures, it is easier to understand him when watching podcasts rather than going to his class. Gives a lot of extensions and is super understanding, even let some guy use his phone as a calculator during a test.

This professor is being very responsible for his students; he responds to messages quickly and with full patience and detail. He tries pretty hard to keep the class engaged, although attendance is not mandatory. Some accent is confusing, but overall, he is a very fun and cute professor:D

This class is somewhat difficult even if you have prior knowledge from AP Chemistry. His lectures are boring and his accent makes it harder to understand. He uploads slides but half the material on the slides is gatekept because he wants to make the slides "more engaging". The homework is very frustrating. Avoid this prof for the sake of ur sanity!

He cares about the course, but lectures are fast and homework ranges from simple questions to highly conceptual. It's hard to keep up!! Class might be harder because he teaches higher division , take him if you have a good understanding already.

Professor Paesani is a really good teacher. I'm still in the process of taking his class but I genuinely enjoy it. I recommend watching his lectures outside of class to help with understanding so you can pause and rewind to take notes as many times as needed. He goes a little faster during lecture. He's just sweet and has a cute italian accent.
Worse than HitIer

I'm taking him for 50. I don't know have any idea about my grade. But Jason might be the best prof I've had at UC. He's a little scary but funny and makes fun of himself. Strict about assignment expectations.

Very pragmatic, respectful, logical professor who adds nice elements to class at times with his jokes, background, even his dog. He is intensely passionate about teaching, and is happy to answer questions. Not only this: importantly, his proficiency in breaking-down new concepts CLEARLY is palpable and consummate. This was the worst class i have taken in my life

Bad teacher. Do not choose him if you want to keep your gpa

Definitely a professor that is prepared for class. The lectures are easy to follow, and she explains topics in a way that clicks. One of the best professors in terms of relating the course to current research efforts.

She covers the latest topics in NLP.

policies depend on who you are. because you come you can leave 40 minutes but I came late once and I couldn't get attendence? yeah weird and during my time in her class she wouldn't nearly enough acknowledge her female students

You can tell she cares so much about her students and wants the best for them. She has so much energy and passion even in the morning. Her workload is very reasonable and she grades very fairly and give you chances to fix your work. I went out of my way to do CCE 3 wither her too.
Kat is so chill. Has a really cool dog. This was for CCE 3 by the way
The best professor that you could possibly take for CCE1. Highly recommend!

Kat is the goat. She's nice and has a cool dog? The only thing was that instructions and rubrics can be a little confusing. But all you have to do is ask her. Not very good experience. The project appeared poorly organized.

Yiying is a nice professor, and CSE 291A is a standard research course. 2-3 paper readings per week with questions you answer before class. Lectures are spent going over the research papers. Hard to follow since he explains things in a very math-proof style and skips over some necessary background that to him is obvious, but isn't (to me). He definitely knows his content well and is very approachable and stays a while after class to answer questions. You can tell he's passionate about his subject. Grading was generous.

Very solid professor in teaching complex analysis. Love how he look like a painter with his apron, gloves and toe shoes. Exams def got harder as qtr went on tho. however did seem grumpy at times. Very funny however. overall a solid professor in the way he gives practice exams and makes it somewhat like actual exams.

Eggers was a great professor, I didn't take calculus before this but if you read the textbook before class, the lecture should just clear things up and it's not too hard. Practice problems are honestly the way to go.

Homework makes a good chunk of the grade, but after taking his midterms, it doesn't even matter. Lectures aren't mando and arent really helpful; he does podcast. Discussions are also mando. If you take this class make sure to cover literally everything and spend alot of time on the problems so you dont fall behind.
Hard to follow along lectures, no lecture slides

He is very passionate about what he teaches, though I think he is sometimes unaware of the exact question people are asking, especially if it is a more basic one. His lectures can be pretty funny at times, and he does not call out on people, even if no one is answering, which I respect him for. He does rely on you reading the textbook.

idk why she gets so much hate, if you go to class and listen you will score higher. so many people don't go to class and then say the grading is too harsh when it honestly isn't. she also is getting rid of the journals next quarter so you won't have to worry about that. she's a great lecturer and genuinely cares about her students. just go to class

Not gonna lie the reading for this class is tedious. There is a LOT of reading and reference to the written materials. No they are not long but they are *incredibly* boring. Professor McKay is excellent, please don't believe the "Awful" reviews. Yes, there are weekly 450-word paper that requires critical thinking & attending the lectures matters. Do your weekly readings (~3 articles per week, actually applicable to your life & work which is useful). She is committed to her students succeeding & deeply cares about them.

Has you write a 450 word essay every week off the 2-3 reading but grades very harsh. Leaves very few comments on how to improve but when improved you still receive the same bad grade. She makes you go to the triton testing center 4 times over the quarter, 2 of which are writing assignments about the readings and the other 2 are multiple choice test

One of my favorite professors ever. McKay is a really eloquent speaker who genuinely cares about her students and how her class affects them. I learned so much about myself and human nature from her class. If you get the chance, take this class!

She is very caring and wants to make sure everyone understands the material. I love how much she explains equations rather than just throwing them at us. Workload isn't too bad but exams can be difficult. She has a grade replacement program where if you do better on the final it will replace your midterm grades. I took her for Chem 6A and 6B.

she is awesome and so kind. prob the best chem prof at UCSD! lecture isn't mandatory but discussion is. lectures are also recorded. there are weekly homework assignments and online quizzes. the grading is very fair. i would say that i struggled quite a bit on the exams but it is such an accessible class

Lectures are very easy to follow and she explains it in depth, if you don't understand. Very patient. Follows a skeletal note-taking where she fills out the lecture notes as you go along. Only downside is how early the class is.
shes the most goated professor ever, super duper kind and caring, has a lenient grading policy, and really easy to understand. shes the best
Lectures are fast-paced but very clear in structure. Midterms are all MCQs which helps me a lot.

He has hilarious lectures. He was great at explaining topics and there was really nothing to complain about. A solid professor all around. If I did have a complaint, it would actually be to have some more homework because I found myself wanting more practice when it came to the place up exam.
I guess the lectures were good but exams' difficulty was insane compared to previous quarters. No cheat sheet either

I don't doubt he's a great teacher but I think the structure of his class and the new Math 2 system is not conducive to a successful environment for students. I attended class and completed the hw's but I still failed the PUP-Exam. This system of a cumulative class to move on to the next level is not helpful and will cause more problems.

Quarfoot is actually goated. He makes topics extremely understandable and completely changed my way of viewing stats (blew my mind over and over again). From my experience so far taking UD math classes, he's the only prof who I don't need to go back and review any material to understand the course at all. Absolutely amazing, 11/10.

This is a nice class, although the homeworks are due twice in a week and his tests are quite difficult. Lectures are very thorough and it is very straightforward to understand the content, but the questions themselves are difficult to solve. No cheat sheets, so it is a good idea to make flashcards from the beginning to memorize lots of formulas.

She's bad ngl. She just reads from the notes and it makes her class boring. The work she wrote on the board is too tiny and faint and impossible to read. She also assigns lot of homework and they all take forever.

Hammock's amazing, people only complain because they are deflecting their struggle onto her. What makes her great is how she gets straight to the point no b.s. she states what is relevant and what isn't. She is relatable and fun. Only complain I see justified would be the homework as they can take a lot of hours to finish, otherwise she's amazing.

Confusing lecturer. She posts all the notes at the beginning of the quarter and just goes through them in class -- nothing new in lecture, don't go. Got 35% on the first midterm going to her lectures, then 100% after I skipped and learned from the textbook. Drops lowest midterm which is why I got an A-. Take if you're willing to put in the time.
48% avg on both midterms and no curve. No cheat sheet when there are around 20-25 ways to solve 1 type of dif eq. plz stay away if you can. teaching style overall is also kinda strange.

Veryyyy good lecture notes with examples that are so helpful when studying. Grades are based on your best midterm out of two, online homework, and the final. You can tell she genuinely wants everyone to do well and discusses study tips pretty frequently.
All of the tests are multiple choice and lectures are option but well taught and organized.

He is not the best lecturer but definitely thinks he is. His grading is pretty generous, and the class is curved. I got a D on both midterms and failed the final and still got a B-. I only had to take one chem class so I didn't try. If you but any effort at all you'll be fine. It's an intro class so he really isn't trying to fail anyone.
Great professor honestly. Very hard to get into his or Schurmeier's class though unless good enrollment times and first passing it. Lots of chances for extra credit that basically carry your grade.

Great in the sense that he's easy to talk to but lectures and hw didn't really reflect the difficulty of the exams. Sometimes he will go off topic during to keep students engaged. I liked the way he graded as exams did not make up most of one's grade. He allows cheat sheets and had a grade improvement plan. Hated how Achieve was required and $$.

Great energy and funny stories but sometimes too many stories for my learning style. With longer lectures, he would try to implement stories to keep us from burning out mid-class, but I felt like they were a bit time-wasteful ultimately. Sometimes it felt a little unclear when trying to get content answers from him.

His lectures are amazing and he can explain everything perfectly clear. He also is willing to help you out during office hours. His exams are easy and he gives plenty of partial credit. However he's strict with attendance so unmotivated people who just want an easy A don't like him
Easily the BEST math prof at ucsd. Just focus on lecture, do the homework, and reach out to him for help (he's every willing to help you and offers plenty of office hours) and your guaranteed an A.

His goes fast in lecture and you have to have a solid foundation of the prereq to follow along. However I learn so much from him. Very helpful during office hours too. Exams are easy once you understand the course materials.
Best math prof ever! His lectures are super engaging. The exams are easy with plenty of partial credits. Gaojin should be promoted to full time prof and put in charge of every math class at ucsd
The GOAT! Take his class if you want to learn math under a brilliant and inspirational mathematician
Insane amount and length of homework, lectures are unhelpful, prelectures are long and difficult. For an intro class the difficulty and lack of teaching is way too much

Super long lectures plus pre-lectures that can't keep students focused. Heavy pre-lecture quiz. Most of the PAs need to be types from blank or from creating the file. so much homework and teach nothing. go teach yourself.

Overall, Benjamin Ochoa is a nice guy, and if you can withstand heavy workload from homework, getting a high score isn't hard.

She's hella chill. Mainly graded on the 2 midterms and final, but you can replace midterm grades with how you did on that section of the final. No cheat cheat but she gives you all the equations and values and tables you'll need. Podcasted lectures.

Nicest prof ever. Two midterms and a final, all multiple choice, and she provides all the notes you'll need as a handout provided with the exam. Super easy course, and she curves. Very open to questions/connecting with students. Could not recommend her enough!!

HUGE test curve!!! Need to invest a good amount of time outside of lecture. Pretty fast paced but possible to catch up if you fall behind. Lectures are a little unclear but available during office hours and very welcoming. Kindhearted but a little hard to follow.

Very kind and wonderful lecturer. I went into 6a without taking AP chem and pretty much no chem experience. Prof was amazing in lectures; you can tell she loves art history, but kind of detached from what was happening with the sections. Lots of memorization needed for tests. Trust me when I say if you land on a good TA you'll be ok.

super easy class attendance not mandatory

Amazing prof, has a super stacked background in molecular bio and lectures are great. Test format is tricky, but with the amount of extra credit in the class an A is obtainable (EC is thru HW and lecture attendance).

if its your only choice, oh well. But be ready to be bored and get to class on time!!!

Overcomplicated material, strict grader, tests are difficult, and unlike practice exams. Expect yourself to rewatch many lectures to understand the material and struggle in this class. I would NOT recommend taking this professor's course.

Awesome teacher, awesome selection of TA's too, overall easy class, I'm pretty sure all of the bild 4 classes are relatively easy and I would recommend Stanley Lo just for his charisma since the lectures are sometimes long and unrelated to the lab work.

doesn't post lecture slides at all. lectures are just him reading off the screen. midterm 1 median score was despicable. good luck if you take him youre just gonna be learning the whole course by yourself.

Very kind but I found doing homework to be more helpful than going to lecture sometimes bc it's very fast paced and not everything is explained well + skips steps. This is my queen.

I'd say definitely a VERY good professor! PASSIONATE! patient and supportive! HER notes cover all the things you need to know
She is really a nice person. Love her class.

This class was amazing! Pretty easy class he is very passionate about teaching this class, and he makes the class even more interesting. He is very understanding if you need to make up an exam or have a family emergency.

Professor Noble's lectures were very interesting, sometimes time was not on his side. The class is very do-able, attendance is not mandatory (he records lectures), and the midterm and final share the same format (multiple choice and 2 short written responses).
super amazing professor, and a great lecturer all u have to do is just sit down in lectures and listen for an easy A.

Great class, interesting lectures. Concepts weren't overcomplicated and homework and readings were fairly light. Final also wasn't cumulative and was pretty much a second midterm. Just study for the tests and you'll be set.

young but knows what he's doing; interesting lectures; his website is really all you need and light weekly reading and homework; not hard just some simple memorization and application to real-world topics; never went to office hours; midterm and final accurately reflected what was taught in class and final was not cumulative; never went to OHs
Very knowledgable and enjoyable if you show up. Tests dont really test intuition, but I didnt really care.

Prof. Muralidharan is one of the best professors at UCSD. Lectures are extensive but are always engaging and presented clearly so you can understand the material and prepare for tests. Multiple papers are discussed which help give more insight into the research process. Exams are in-depth, but reflect material and past exams. Great class for all!

Prof. Muralidharan is the best professor I have ever had. He is incredibly knowledgeable about communications and speaks of it in an extremely sociological context. Don't take his class. Not clear with grading, and very harsh. Has this kind of stuck up attitude, where he requires you to particpate in class, but embarrasses you if(when) you saying something wrong. Just save yourself the stress and dont take.

Everyone on here is trippinnnn, or maybe he just changed as a teacher, but I took him for COMM164, he's a genius. Class feels like having a conversation with a smart person. He is very interactive with the class and gets you thinking. He likes to ask questions to get students involved and he doesn't believe in testing (no final or midterm).
He is a great professor. Don't have much to say, just an awesome, kind, and fun person!

There were only a few people got an A in my class. He went through the lecture very quickly and do not allowed us to get his PowerPoint, also do not provide the recording. There are no slides to follow; he only assigns readings and then just talks about random, unrelated stuff in class. The structure is very poor and unorganized. I thought he was funny! Passionate about what he teaches. Has accent, but very understandable. 

Lectures/readings way harder than tests. Posts most L. notes, kind of hard to follow.

-funny and a little awkward
-do not let the reviews discourage you from taking this class

I am weak at math/stats and this was my favorite class I've taken at UCSD. Professor Holloway will teach you lots of things, but almost nothing about writing. His feedback on the essays were AI generated and his discussions in class made up the majority of your grade and it all depends on whether he remembered you spoke or not. If I could give a 0/5 I would.
raised my hand every class and was told i needed to raise my hand 3x a class for participation to count?
really confusing/unclear what was expected
Very easy class. Only two essays. Fun discussions in class. He follows his grading pledge. And if you ask, he'll tell you what you need to do to keep an A.

Really great professor with the reverse classroom thing. He is very kind and willing to help when you ask or attend OH. In his exams, you are allowed 1 sided 8x11sheet and the final both sides. Professor Root was so great! The lecturers were recorded, the class time was for practice and these questions were similar to ones on the test. He is also so funny without trying.

One of my favorite professors at UCSD. Flipped classroom, with recorded lectures being a little long, but pretty engaging still. Exams and problem sets all come from the lectures, no tricks or unexpected questions. Really fun class, especially if you're into neurobiology.

Overall dense and not very engaging but makes it easy to get an A compared to other bio (extra credit, practice problems, note sheet on exams). Recordings were long but helpful, but he gave very unclear answers during live lecture reviews

This was honestly the best course ever! Cory Root is an amazing professor! Everything you need to know for the exams is based on past exam questions or the problem sets. He also gives roughly 5 points of extra credit or more.

She is a really kind and straightforward professor. Her lectures match the exam questions and there is extra credit at the end of each exam. I don't know how this professor is this overrated. It was not bad but I rather take other professor if I were you.

very kind Prof! material is VERY reflective of lecture content. the class is straight memorization tbh (ex. 20 amino acids, glycolysis, CAC, etc, and all it's reverse reactions). must also memorize chem structures of ALL reagents in the mechanisms. lots of ec opportunities: ec questions at the end of each test + a whole ec assignment (20pts).

this is by far the goat teacher at ucsd. graded on 3 quizzes and a final that are all very representative of course material. she makes it very clear on what will be on exams and offers ample ec. if you are taking bibc 102, you can't not take this prof.

Fave professor at UCSD so far. She truly cares about her students; can't stress how nice it is to have a professor who treats you with empathy and compassion. Dr. Chandler is approachable and cares about her students. She can give very helpful feedback about students' writing. AWP 4A 4B is a nice path for students with limited writing education before.

Professor Chandler cares very much about her students, she left helpful feedback quickly and was very clear about expectations in the class. Learned so much in her writing class, much more confident in my writing skills.
Dr. Bailee was an amazing professor and she truly cares about each of her students. The course is designed to help you prepare for college writing and trust me its very helpful for your future.

I would recommend Dr. Bailee to everyone. She is a great professor and super approachable after classes! If you struggle with the essays, definitely go to her office hour. I feel like the face to face feedback is more clear than the online feedback. However, AWP 3 requires a lot of work so be prepared to spend around 5-10 hours per week.

If you're placed in the AWP program, trust me, you belong there. It's designed to help you improve and succeed in college writing. The professor provides fantastic feedback, and I highly recommend attending office hours, even if not required. Boring lectures, would mumble into the chalk board and not engage with the class. Had to go to the other professor's lecture to understand the content. Homework was fair, tests were alright. Not the best.

Lectures notes are great and HW & tests are very fair. OH very helpful. He's Very very accommodating. "cons"-does not podcast and is super unresponsive on piazza so go to OH if you have questions. Brilliant! Don't quit his class just because his voice barely has any pitch changes. He actually cares about students A LOT. Has fairly clear lectures, fair(and easy) tests. HWs are light compared to most math classes in UCSD. HW are on textbook so getting one is necessary(also get correct version!).

Although extremely monotone, content was clear and easy to understand. Lectures aren't podcasted/recorded so I would recommend going to class, but you can definitely pass without going every day. Exams are 90% of your grade, but cheat sheets are allowed.

Prof. Treuer is an extremely nice and knowledgable person who does his best to help the students learn. Exams are little hard, and attending the class helps a lot since he goes over topics that you need to know for the exam.
Literally does way too much for an uppergrad sociology class, dont waste your time taking this class

Professor H is a great professor, her lectures are so intresting. She is very detailed in grading big assignments, but her courses are not as tough. Just read the material and pay attention to her lectures. She is very caring and flexible with work.

Get ready to write as soon as you enroll in this course as multiple assignments consist of writing a couple pages long from the get-go. Great professor who writes a clear feedback on your assignments and states what she is expecting from you.

She is very passionate about research. I still have no interest in research but I can see why people do because of her. You'll be writing a lot but she's flexible. She talks fast so be ready for that and your going to talk a lot in class.
If you don't know how to do excel, you won't be able to do anything unless you learn outside of class.

Long lectures watching him click around Excel, longer homework assignments, classes cancelled. Openly admits to playing favorites among students to staff his own private company. There is a reason this man has made a career interfacing with his computer.

Professor Moeder has no idea how to properly teach a class. His lectures are long, boring, and unorganized. Best music professor in UCSD, interesting lectures, several written essays for HW, grade depends on TA. Only one midterm, fairly easy. Final is a longer essay. Overall strongly recommended!
Extremely tough on the midterm and exams. Completely based on heavy readings. Quiz on every reading. Lectures are not mandatory, but if you don't go, you will not pass. Based on the TA's grading.
He wishes my downfall. He makes sure to use language that no one understands. He enjoys my pain. He diddys my GPA.

Chang's lectures are interesting and easy to follow. Workload is tedious and heavy, and too much for a college GE. Class is passable without doing all readings but amount of effort that goes into midterms and essays is insane. Unnecessary amount of work, annoying to deal with.

Never felt such hatred towards a history class, the only reason I took this class was to complete my MMW requirement. The exam didn't evaluate your knowledge it was just memorization. If you have medical problems, don't take this professor. Very rude in his emails and overall demeanor toward students needing accommodations. I'm honestly surprised there are good reviews at all.

Knowledgeable and thorough explanations but fast-paced, watching podcasts of lectures to refine notes may be helpful. Cooper was a decent lecturer who sometimes skimmed topics & dove deep on others, but explained concepts clearly with simple examples. SUCH a picky grader even on hw. I think he is a good professor and the discussion work is helpful. The homework is very managebale and you have a week to do it. The content can be heavy but he has a midterm drop policy.

Emails are never answered. Extra credit was offered but not counted in final grades.. Many students contacted him and TAs, and he responded by saying grading was correct and told students to stop emailing. Confusing lectures, hard exams, poor communication.

Klosterman is goated if you have some extra time to make use of his extra materials. He does review sessions that r v helpful and he offered test corrections (1 question). Wouldn't recommend for ppl w packed schedule tho

Prof K goes above and beyond for his students, he even stays late every Friday to give review sessions and makes sure everyone's' questions get answered. He is the kindest professor I have ever had and gives great lectors that are not on slides so you can follow along and take good notes. OChem is a tough course but he makes it enjoyable!

He's very enthusiastic about Chem 41A and cares about your success in the rest of the sequence. He offers many chances for receiving help and even a redo on one exam QUESTION of your choice. This class is super easy. Her lectures are great and the discussions aren't bad either. There was one essay for the midterm and final is 2 essays as well. She lets you do open note and its honestly a great class.

professor clearly knows her stuff but can be a boring lecturer. mandatory discussions, experience depends on the ta. weekly take-home quizzes and two essay exams. skim the readings so you can use those as sources on your exams. study guides and review sessions for exams were helpful, make sure you dedicate the whole day to the essay. optional final

Professor Ferree is a well of political science knowledge, especially African politics. She can seem like a normal lecturer, but only when going over topics she isn't passionate about. Such a great class! Only attendance that is required are for discussion sections. No homework, only three papers and the last one is optional. Professor Ferree is so kind and her lectures are very engaging. Although attendance isn't required, I recommend attending them! DO THE READINGS! They make wiring your papers super easy.

She was super nice and her lectures were very engaging (I say this from the perspective of a political science major). Only two major essays and they were both take-home so not too much pressure. Final optional, only had to take it if you needed to raise your grade after the two midterms. Would 100% take a class taught by her again!

The class is pretty unorganized and she will cancel lecture a lot, but still expect you to stay on top of the coursework and decipher what she wants you to know. Tests are challenging and she grades really harshly. Lectures are very fun though!

I thought she was a reasonable professor before she decided to go off on people for criticizing her exam's short answer questions. Very friendly and helpful in office hours. Stuck close to the book. Very clear lecture notes, which were posted soon before class started.
Professor Ioana explains very well and has clear and concise notes.

Great lectures, and workload was relatively light (though this might be mostly due to the course itself).
Super nice professor. His exam was not that bad, and neither was the qual.

Exams are worth 85% of ur grade. There are 3 exams and they were all 60-65 questions long. Unlucky for me, it was an 8am class. Lectures are super dense. Try not to take other lecture heavy classes along with this one. I wouldn't take her again. Exams were super hard and class average is low!!!

Boring. Attendance checked by code &question prompt. lectures recorded. 3 exams Tests are actually very difficult she made a lot of mistakes & corrected grade accordingly and even with that the average score was a C in the class. not much homework so that helps study for the test its just end of the week prompt 2 paragraphs what was your fav topic

Professor Dobkins is a great lecturer, class content is a little dense but her teaching style is awesome. Overall, great professor!! She is very caring, calm and knowledgable. Subject is very information heavy, there's a lot of materials and small details that we must memorize. Grade consist of 3 test and weekly reflections. Test can be a bit tough but all multiple choice. Always accessible outside of class and lectures are interesting and fun.
Dobkins is a great lecturer! Her grading criteria is a little weird, but the class is generally straightforward. The material is VERY dense but if you pace yourself it's an ez dub.

Her lectures were the worse. She would call out students for little things such as being on their computer. The pop up quizzes and quick writes were annoying and didn't help with anything. Your grade heavily depends on TAs which almost all are super harsh for no reason. So frustrating and worse hum class ive taken here and I usually enjoy them.

The lectures were pretty grueling and you can't skip because there is basically a pop quiz each week on the lecture material. They go super easy on grading the essays and final but it is a ton of reading.

Lots of reading so be prepared. Gives a couple extra credit opportunities, I would recommend to do them all. Lecture are not really mandatory, however she gives unscheduled quizzes so do at your own risk. Definitely recommend to go to lectures. Keep up with the readings. Mandatory discussions. Final “ is a reward for going to lectures.” (Her words)

Great professor that offers insightful, “outside of the box” ideas about the books studied. Essays feedback was precise and pinpointed my flaws. Came out of the class as an improved writer. Final was graded generously.

Didn't necessarily like her lecture styles. Tone in which she talks about religion is very condescending. She is the department chair for HUM, and she oversees peoples grades, I am certain she is the reason why people rarely get A+, think its because she thinks they deserve it based off of how close she knows them, not because of their work
Have her as a sub while my professor was traveling. Her lectures are hilarious. Would have taken her section if I know she is that funny.

The class was fascinating and she was one of the best lecturers I've ever had-engaging, funny, and clear. She wasn't very approachable, and answered questions like they're obvious.

-Good lecturer and explains content very well.

Valerie is an awesome lecturer! Her homework is tough, but I loved how she taught the course content.

very nice professor, super clear lectures, no tests and projects/assignments are very doable

prof. kennemore is extremely caring and demonstrates her passion for what she teaches effortlessly.. it made this class very enjoyable! her class can be content/reading heavy at times but she does a great job at making sure material is understandable during lecture

Professor Kennemore has really flexible policies that are super understanding of students and their time. No exams and final was a group project. Awesome prof and respects students time / that they have other engagements outside her class.

She was a great professor. Almost weekly discussion boards which are not hard at all. You dont necessarily have to read, you can get away with skimming. Weekly portfolios. Attendance and discussion are not mandatory. Super easy and fun class. She is passionate about what she teaches. Looking to take her again for another course!
Three hour lectures were very difficult to get through and retain information, especially due to monotonous voice and lack of enthusiasm.

don't don't take, the material is easy but the exams are so confusing with the way they word them, they haven't taught the class since 2009, 3 midterms, Lowest dropped , cumulative final, you can miss 3 lectures, average for first midterm was 40 after a curve

One of the best professors I have ever taken a class with, although your grade is entirely made up of midterms and the final exam (which can be dropped if you do well enough on the midterms), the exams are super super fair and publishes a study guide which tells you EXACTLY what will be on the exams. Offers 7% extra credit if you go to lecture.

Soooo much extra credit. There is extra credit available on each exam, he drops the lowest exam + extra credit for attendance. He also has detailed study guides that are very helpful. I really enjoyed his class and he seems to rlly care . His lectures were super dense though

Professor Leutgeb is great for a start in Human Physiology Class like BIPN 100. Giving kind ECs for 7% attedance(70% show up), 2% for pre and post-assessment, and 3% if 80% students finished the SET. I actually took this class as HILD 60 but it was easy and the only thing mandatory was the discussions. The midterm and final are also easy and she gives alternatives too!
Best professor I have had at UCSD, the class was genuinely interesting and exams were simple/reasonable.
Easy A, midterm questions are given to you and final project can be an art project or an online essay. Not a hard class, very interesting, very educated professor.
She is genuinely very knowledgeable about history, and always remains objective. She made lectures very interesting even for those that don't enjoy history and has manageable workload.

She is wonderful! She's very passionate about what she teaches, she's an amazing speaker and knows how to keep you engaged. There was only one midterm and a final. Her exams weren't crazy. So long as you do the work and read you'll be good!
He is a very funny person and makes lectures engaging, midterm and final are online with homework assignments every 2 weeks.

He just seems like a guy who is so passionate about teaching. He is SO open about answering ANY questions in class. homework is light, midterms are light, final is light. Lecture content is basically common sense, and it's a good class to get started with public health.
The best professor ever.
Easiest class ever bro. And He's hilarious

I personally felt that attending lectures wasn't very valuable, since it seemed like Professor Trinidad mostly read off of the slides. The homework is very light. Prof Squires was great! Def very theory and case study based, but he does his best to put things into context and make the material make sense. Super understanding as well. If you put effort in the class, it comes back to you. Would love to take more of his classes in the future!

Nice prof, but lectures and study guide can be confusing. Lots of errors that get corrected last minute, which made studying more difficult than it should be. She's a great professor. Since it's her first time teaching this class, you can tell she's putting in a lot of effort to make it engaging and enjoyable. The homework isn't difficult and is exactly what appears on the exams, which makes it very fair. She also offers a generous test drop policy.

Really good professor and overall really easy class. Lectures are really easy to follow and understand. The homework follows what was taught in the lectures and the test is very similar to questions on the homework. She drops one of your 3 test which is very clutch.
Goated Professor. She gives all the content needed to study right at the start and learning how to do the practice material should consolidate a 70-80+ on every exam.

MY QUEEN, she literally drops one of your exams (whichever one's your lowest) and this includes the midterms and the final. I skipped the final lol. Homework is lightwork you get like 4 attempts. Genuinely the nicest the professor I have ever had. REALLY CLEAR LECTURER. I love her sm.

Absolutely goated econ prof. Easiest class I've ever taken in my life, high school included. Very helpful office hours. Three hour lectures are difficult to get through, but engaging questions during class helped. The lectures a so long and content heavy it would be 100 slides and they wouldn't tell us what part of the slides we would need for the test and since a midterm is every 3 weeks it's roughly 300+ slides to review.

I took her BIPN 194 course but I didn't have the option to select that course. Overall, very interesting course with a professor who cares about her students and wants them to excel.

Her lectures were great, the content is very hard. Just be sure to study and you will do well. Tons of extra credit points (10 points to exams category which is the biggest chunk of the overall grade (70%)). Just remember, study, study, study. That is how you can do well in this class.

Prof Leutgeb was a really great professor for this class. Her tests are tough but they're fair. justin is truly the goat

Justin Eldridge is a treasure, he's those one in a million professors that you learn so much from and genuinely wants you to succeed. He makes incredibly difficult concepts approachable and understandable.
One of the best professors in HDSI. He explains concepts incredibly well and is super organized. You can reach him, always available during his office hours.
He really is a great professor. He lectures really well and makes me genuinely appreciate data science. Highly recommend him as a professor for any of your classes.

super organized and probably the best DSC professor i've taken. he provides great support out of class and his lectures are very clear and interesting. genuinely wanted to learn more in this class and would recommend to anyone

He's a passionate professor but sometimes hard to understand during lectures. He often goes of topic or just explains things a little more complicated then they need to be. GOAT. Love the course and everything.

prof. trottner is great. he is the only econ prof ive had that is visibly passionate about economics + has a great and interesting lecture style which connects the econ content to financial history/systems. take the course you will not regret
The best professor I had in UCSD that made me passionate about Econ. He explains the concept really well. As long as you pay attention to lecture, you will do well in class.

Dr. Romero's lectures can be a bit difficult to absorb, so I stopped going to class and watched the podcasts so that I could pause them and truly understand what he was explaining. I really hated his teaching style. He writes his lectures on paper and projects it on the projector, makes it very hard to follow along. He goes super fast & writes all over the paper. Dr. Pitt's a chill guy and very entertaining during his lectures. The assignments are pretty simple and straightforward but still study the materials because they can be heavy.

Not my favorite profesor but he's not as bad as everyone says. Extremely entertaining lecturer, just expects things outside of scheduled class times. Dr. Pitt is really entertaining and made the class really engaging. The goat. I am a sociology major passionate about the discipline and one can see that he is also passionate and knowledgable in his field. I took 4 of his classes. Personally I really liked him and his lectures, they were very interesting. As long as you go to class and take notes you'll most likely get an A.

I took Professor Park for 2 different classes, his lectures can get a little boring bet are generally very informative and he's a very sweet professor. kyong is a national treasure. his work is very ahead of the curve - unknown to the rest of the world, but a  visionary architect.

VIS103A; Lectures were super interesting, while attendance was not taken or part of the grade, the only assignments were turning in your notes from class during week 5 and week 10. Lectures are long, not podcasted, but the class is insanely easy if you just take lecture notes every once in a while in class. Midterm and Final are just "answer questions posted after class" and cite using the readings.

Bliss is a good and fun professor and her class is very helpful for basic fundamental understand of finance concepts. Prof. Bliss is a great professor. The class itself is really hard but she breaks it down for you and she is really good at teaching. Professor Bliss is clearly brilliant and dedicated to her craft. However, I had her for a three-hour lecture weekly, and never in my life has a class been so boring. Chill and straightforward professor. Homeworks can be long, but as long as you do them, it's an easy 25% of your grade. Midterm and final are open note/book. For MGT 180! Nice professor, just lectures extremely fast as its one class a week for 2 hours and 50 minutes. TAs are very accessible. Just a midterm and final for this class, all multiple choice. It's easy to get a good grade if you focus on the lectures and readings. Attendance isn't mandatory, but he does recommend it. Sometimes gives lectures over Zoom or invites guest lecturers.

His lectures were engaging and I learned a lot of new topics that really got us thinking and reflecting. Graded by a midterm, attendance/participation (automatic points even if you don't show up) and a final. Exams were multiple choice. Very chill guy but utilize the resources he provides and have very detailed notes. Slides don't always have words
Very passionate and makes lectures fun. Goes above and beyond to guide students and encourage them to continue studies in anthropology. Amazing professor

Professor didn't grade anything all quarter and didn't post the grades within the time frame every other professor does after finals. He's really passionate about teaching, so his lectures are very interesting! her class was easy, weekly reflections on readings but its more like a journal entry very easy grading. the group project was a large part of your grade but i got a good group. however the material itself and lectures were not structured and boring
easiest A ever, lectures were so boring just reading off slide, every week its a 2 length paper due on an article, no final, group project, and final project. TA is super sweet

Easy to get a good grade, readings are pretty easy. Just go to class for attendance points and do the weekly take-home quizzes and you should be good. All the exams were literally one page and were easy.

Go to class. My grade dropped significantly because of attendance alone, even though I got near perfect scores on my papers + project + homework. Mandatory lectures (in-class prompts, but you do not have to take notes). Lectures are very boring and she does not make an effort to engage students. Jordan really wants you to learn and improve at writing. He made me feel more comfortable participating, even though I was really scared to at first. He's very easy to talk to, helpful, and understanding. He provides genuine feedback that helps revise.

Winter 2025. His lectures are quite interesting for what I consider a not-so-interesting course. Eloquent speaker, makes you feel heard (good in a discussion-based class such as this). Very encouraging, made me emotional during the last class.

Cool and respectable guy. The issue I had with this class is how I felt the prompts to the assignments where "open ended", so I personally had a more difficult time in his class. Professor Escobar was really nice, and the lectures are pretty chill and easy to follow for me. Very nice and engaged professor. Truly cares about his students and make it fun
uses iclicker for attendance, each lecture is a different guest lecturer which makes formatting confusing for the exams but allowed a page cheat sheet

Mostly guest lectures, some were better than others. Same work each week on different topics, so pretty easy to keep track of work. The grading was fair and clear. Really good class! I took it for a GE, but was really interesting, most of the lectures are done by guest lecturers, mostly MDs or DOs. dont take. too much hw. currently drowning

Very fun and interesting lectures! Funny guy. He was super responsive to the energy in the class - if we were tired or quiet he would rush through the last of the slides. Great guy and would definitely take again!

0 grades inputted by finals week...we wrote a 12 page final paper with no idea what our grade is. No communication and no help.

Prof Frank clearly knows what he's talking about (he literally invented the word walkability) but he's not a very good lecturer and assigns ridiculously long essay assignments. Wouldn't recommend taking this class honestly, it's been disappointing

Spends all class going on tangents and not going over class material. Quizzes almost every class based on dense readings. The midterm was full of trick questions, it felt like he was trying to set us up to do bad and half of the questions had mistakes/ were misleading.

he does lecture the entire time and tell stories, but its honestly not too bad. memorize key concepts in the weekly readings and you will be fine for quizzes/ tests. he is intimidating at first but does not bite unless you cheat or scheme against him. just show up to a class you signed up for and read

pls don't take this prof. you get a quiz each week. you don't get any study guides for any exams which is also insane bc the midterm was a bunch of nonsense we didn't even learn. not a good prof. Lectures mainly consist of off-topic tangents about his personal life, with relatively minimal explanation for the incredibly dense readings. He is funny and charismatic, but cut it out when I am trying to learn because grading is 33% pop quizes on the readings 33% midterm 33% final. sad becuase content is interesting.
good class good professor
Super interesting lectures, tests were easy, he's super sweet and wants it to be an easy, fun class.

10/10 Professor. Class is graded on attendance for lecture and discussion, midterm, and final. He does attendance the first 15 minutes of class and never got mad students left early. This class is survey-like so there isn't much in-depth discussion into any specific topic. Nothing particularly good or bad, and she seemed passionate. Would recommend as it satisfies significant writing, but didn't feel like difficult writing. This class needs more organization for it to flow better and be able to absorb the hands-on and lecture materials. Not enough time with EEG labs or MATLAB. just really bad

Professor Leigh provides an adequate amount of material to help you prepare for labs, assignments, and exams. He keeps the conceptual material straightforward.

He was a really great professor. Lectures were really interesting and you really got a sense of his personality through his lecture. Professor Smith was great. Would recommend attending his office hours even if you don't have any pressing questions. Interesting course content & reading, but lectures were not engaging and hard to pay attention to as he would often talk for the entire 3 hours nonstop. Attendance was optional & lectures were recorded. Tests were open-note & aligned with readings, so take good notes & you're set.

Very nice, but not the most tech-savvy, and gets easily distracted during lecture. TA's, in my experience, are tough graders and give minimal feedback. If you ever want an introduction to law classes as an undergraduate, I reccomend this one. Attendance and participation is mandatory but his lectures are very interesting and he makes accommodations for students who are shy

I've taken MGT16 and MGT 181 from him, and he's good at what he does. You can tell he wants to teach and challenge students. Professor Buchanan knows how to teach his students! You learn the content outside of class through his prerecorded lectures and do practice problems in class. While the topic of this class wasn't hard to learn, I found his lectures to be very boring and not helpful to understanding the material. The homework assignments were really long, and difficult if you didn't quite understand how to use the software for the course.
NEVER TAKING HIM AGAIN!! I will not be taking him ever again. He talks extremely low and the lectures are very boring

No midterm but the final exam is lengthy and covers a lot of content.

Really interesting lectures, but he doesn't use lecture slides or anything so be ready to actually listen to what he's saying to take notes. He was a very nice guy, I dont think he liked when students would ask questions tho lol. just go to the classes and DO THE READING or for the test you will be horribly underprepared. the final and the midterm are the only things graded, so if that works for you, take this. if it doesnt, maybe steer away from this class

Impossible to get ahold of outside of class.

Lectures are completely disconnected from test material.

Lectures were unorganized, and he often talked about his memories in the Middle East. The TAs did the grading, though. At the time, I didn't enjoy the class, but it actually helped me learn what not to do as an educator.

Professor Provence is so knowledgable on the middle east, it is very impressive! I feel like I have learned a lot in his class. its important to attend the lectures because it helps you connect the assigned readings.
Truthful guy

Professor Provence's personal connection to the events is very inspirational. He has traveled to the regions and is a expert in the subject. Was ridiculously hard to get in touch with outside of class. Would turn architecture into a political talk and ramble around random stuff. The class is graded off of 1 midterm and 1 final and there is no outline or rubric whatsoever. Avoid this class at all costs.
One of the best professors I've ever had. He talks a lot, but he's very sweet and understanding. Very inspirational and hardworking man.
Wish class was more focused. Very disorganized and disgruntled TA's. Final was a mess and had to report multiple times of group mates not participating yet nothing was done.

Extremely theory based class, more so poli sci w/sprinkling of vis arts ideas. Prof Cruz is VERY passionate and I respect him for this, though, this class was DISORGANIZED. i am currently taking his vis 100 for FA 25. I wish attendance wasn't graded, you basically have to teach yourself the material because her lectures have little content. mandatory attendance or you lose a third of a letter grade. nothing on her slides. her readings are only on course reserves and very hard to access. i forgot to include a quote on a discussion board and she gave me a zero (it met word limit and everything else). she is very nice but don't take her class.

Has to be the absolute worst professor I've ever had. Her syllabus says she wont repeat anything from lecture because she doesn't like it when people don't pay attention. Definitely knows what he's doing. He lectures from a note outline, which he fills out during the lectures, which honestly isn't my cup of tea, but it's alright. Good teacher

He is one of the nicest professors you will encounter in your Physics journey. He offers a lot of extra credit on quizzes and the final exam. Going to office hours is very helpful as it helped me get a lot of conceptual gaps filled in.
