I think he is one of the most inspiring professors that I have had. His passion for physics is clear and makes me want to come to class to learn. The only reason my rating is not a 5 is that his lecture style is a little all of the the place, making some concepts a bit confusing. But if you want to feel excited about physics take this teacher.

Professor Averitt is really chill. Super engaging lectures, but very tedious homework. Quizzes are never that much different from lecture, hw, and practice problems, etc... He's very fair and offers extra credit on quizzes. The class isn't curved but the grading scheme makes is hard to fail. I would be happy to take one of his classes again.

Could be better, but not too bad. Course was challenging overall, and there was weekly homework which required a lot of thinking, but was graded on effort. Lectures and discussions are mandatory, which is quite unsatisfying. Maybe not the best professor in the school, but surely not the worst and was generous with extra credit.

Four mandatory lectures, discussion, 2-5 ~25 min supplementary videos, every week. The class isn't difficult if you study things that are not assigned for the class, like other mechanics textbooks. At the very least he offered a lot of extra credit on the final.

Word of caution to those looking to take 4A, Math 20A is not an apt prerequisite.

Amazing and sweet professor! Lectures are engaging and she encourages participation in class but doesn't force it. You can choose to have graded attendance or not, she accepts late work with no penalty, assignments and tests are easy and don't require too much. She's an easy grader just as long as you meet all the requirements. Highly recommend!!

WOW! I loved Prof. Crofts' class! Very engaging, invites discussion but is also understanding of every students' circumstances. Fun assignments and discussions; since I took her Food class it was often applicable to daily life. Attendance is mandatory if you want to to be! (you can choose which is cool). Take her classes, you won't regret it.

SHE IS AMAZING! I actually took her for soci 137: sociology of food! She is very caring, flexible and understanding. For the class itself, class is mandatory if you choose it to be (she gives you the choice). There is one group paper and the rest are papers instead of a midterm and final! Very chill easy A class. Take this class with her!

Lectures are actually fun never minded attending. optional occasional group work or solo. grade is mostly homework and a take home final and yeah that's it. the actual content was really good too honestly so it made it even easier to actually learn something without it hurting.

Professor Crofts is one of my favorite professors at UCSD. Her class is structured so students can succeed. You have the option of getting graded for attendance or opting out if you plan to miss more than the number allowed. There's numerous assignments and papers due throughout the course so get ready for busy work, but she does grant extensions.

Lectures focus on personal research rather than course material. Quizzes are difficult to prepare for, as questions cover niche in-class comments. The quizzes format on the classroom screen cause great pressure.
Most useful class I took, learned a ton and developed my own research interest through this course. and the prof is super nice, all his lectures are really interesting.

The final was easy if you have gone through lectures; it is open-book anyways. He introduces a wide array of topics related to HCI and invites PhD students to host interesting lectures that they are passionate about. Although he only started recording lectures after like week 4, he is an overall caring, passionate, and kind professor.

Very exciting materials. Most interesting course I have taken. If you are expecting spoon-feeding, this course is probably not the right for you. Quizzes can be challenging if you don't come to the lectures.

I don't think the instructor is even experienced or prepared in teaching... He covers lots of his own research materials for a class that should've covered a lot broader than that. His quiz questions can be extremely subjective to his own thoughts which the scoring distribution doesn't resemble any classes I took at UCSD. I feel so weird.
Super nice professor, allowed me to have my essay regraded and was extremely polite when conversing.
pretty hard class, wouldn't reccomend

Matt Crum my GOAT. I took both HUM 2 and 3 with him and his lecture style is super fun and thought provoking.

Lectures aren't strictly mandatory, no in class quick writes or quizzes but he will talk about the definitions of key terms that will appear on finals. I had to miss classes due to other midterms but he's super understanding about it

I love Crum. The nicest person you will ever meet. Most humble down to Earth and caring prof out there.  interesting lectures & gives good interpretations of the texts. essay prompts aren't too hard. HUM=lots of reading and TA grading, but where Crum can be helpful he is. Wrote him an email a qtr later and he still remembered me. Absolute class.

Professor Crum is super helpful and his lecture content is interesting. The final is short ID (he went over all possible terms in lectures), and 2 short essays (gave prompts before hand). The texts he chose were also super fun to read through! But like all humanities, your grade really just depends on your TA.

Lectures were very hard to keep up with because she already had notes prepared and would not explain her work, it would be very crammed and hard to see or understand what's happening. Midterm did not directly reflect off of practice problems and homework she told us to do. The concepts were easy but she would make them harder than they were.
I even thought I was going to fail the course, but my final grade turned out to be quite good. The teacher was very gentle and didn't have any unreasonable demands.

Decent lectures, bit of an accent and trouble understanding questions. Huge curve in the class and easy exams, very sweet person. Made a good amount of mistakes in lecture and graded late, theory heavy lecture with application based exams and homework
Lectures were too theory heavy, and was more focused on proving theorems than solving problems. Attending them wasn't exactly useful because I'd have to learn on my own to get through the homework.

Decent and friendly professor. Was unsure often when asked questions. Often made mistakes in lecture, leading to many revisions in posted slides. Much easier exams than homework, but late grading. Would recommend looking into other sources rather than just her lecture
She's super passionate about art and really cares about her students. Attendance is enforced but lectures are interesting. Great class!

(Taken Spring 2025) VIS 3 has mandatory studio and lecture attendance. Assignments and final are to create sculptures. No quizzes or tests. Time consuming class. TAs grade all, so scores are luck based. Professor is kind but strict on showing up. Lecture material is art history and honestly has nothing to do with assignments.

This professor was a 10/10 if I can take him for more Spanish classes I would. His work was not bad, it wasn't hard and topics were interesting so it was nice to do his work as a break between other classes. He is very nice and I would recommend taking him for LTSP 100.

BEST PROF EVER! Doesn't believe in grades so you choose based on the effort you think you put into class. Classes are mostly discussion based and not lectures. Very easy to talk to and definitely cares about their students. If you have the option, take him 100%. Our class was at 8 am so i was kinda dead but i wish i had participated more.
such kind professor and really easy going, courses are extremely interesting and you can tell he's passionate abt what he does

I could've done so much better if I didn't miss lectures so much. His exams are super similar to what he teaches. There's a curve to the final grades. He uses Uflo, an online platform which actually enjoyed beside the price. One midterm and one final. He's funny and entertaining.

The lectures can sometimes be interesting, but they don't reflect the difficulty of the actual exams even tho they get curved pretty well. you get a good amount of easy points but it's a difficult class to follow along.

avoid this prof at all cost. midterm is alright but finals is difficult. your exams are graded by an AI so it does make mistakes sometime. lecture is extremely boring and bro over complicates everything in my opinion.

My final exam was graded by ChatGPT and made mistakes. Be ready to use regrade requests. Makes you pay for his buggy website that contains lecture slides & required quizzes. A test question was too ambiguous, heavily penalizing me. Uses too much profanity during lectures. The exams are difficult but worth studying for.  There is a generous curve.
Never replies to emails. The midterm is very easy, but be careful the final exam is difficult and will significantly lower your grade.

Dr. Albizati has been the best chem prof I've had at this school so far. His lectures were very clear and easy to follow, and practice exams were very indicative of what the real exams looked like. He had a great personality, and it was easy to see how much he cared for his students. Very straigthtforward class and professor if you dont fall behind

Overall great professor, teaches content well, easy to understand. Homework on Achieve, which is required for the class; HW is due the night before exams, includes stuff not taught/on tests (be wary). The lowest HW grade is also dropped. Test grading was flexible; some questions were changed to partial credit depending on grades. Course curved.

Efficient, makes course easy to understand. Assigns homework on Achieve (which you do need to pay for), due the night before tests; sometimes HW includes material not taught/not on tests. Funny, lectures are enjoyable. Slightly flexible with test grading; may drop questions or give partial credit depending on grades; curves the course.

Love love LOVE this professor. I like his class because his tests are all free responses and that is what chem is about...showing work. That way I can get at least some credit for showing work. He truly cares about his students. Has online homework, 2 midterms and a final, lectures/discussions are not mando. TAKE HIM IF HE TEACHES.

Easy exams, exactly like practice exams given. Homework more bust work than helpful, much harder than the tests, however, does not count for credit just competition so it was whatever. Very chill dude, brought dog treats for dog. Lecture and section not mandatory.

very dependent on how your TA is for the lab and what your group is like. lots of writing assignments but worth it for this professor. lectures are bit boring and repetitive since it's a recap of AP Bio.
Great choice for BILD 4

Keefe is a good professor with a lot of insight, passion, and love for students, but it was hard to study for tests and quizzes alongside not knowing the true criteria for coding assignments. He creates his own coding assignment grader that may miss points or fail your entire assignment even if you didn't make an inherently big mistake.

Chill professor with a once weekly lecture and then lab. Lab is all group/pair work, so be prepared to work with others. Very fun class and easy A. Outside of class content, he also lectures about how to find a research lab and how to do well in STEM. Very invested in helping students succeed.
He only had one lecture per week, so not too much to say on him, but he was funny and very encouraging.

Worst professor I've had. Ironic that professors who center research on "education" are the worst at teaching. Spent too much time joking around than actually clarifying concepts. Would pause during explanations to say a joke, leaving us to self-teach. Prerequisite was only BIPN 100 but I felt I needed an entire genetics background to understand.

Really good professor. I got an A but because I attended PLA's OH. Class is very content heavy and you will need to look for help outside class but he's a good professor, my class was only once a week for 3 hours and still my fav class that quarter. Make sure to do your work and you'll get a good grade.

Professor jokes too much instead of teaching material. Does not teach the mechanics of physiological systems as much, does more application. Make sure to go to discussion as worksheets are very similar to midterm in terms of content and format. Try to attend SI and review sessions because they will tell you what topics are on the exam.
please do not take! time rushed exams, poor and boring lecture, extremely unhelpful slides, extreme poor podcast quality

He was a bit "quirky" in class, but it help make the 3 hour lecture more tolerable. He very picky about what is consider a correct answer for quizzes/tests and Discussions are not mandatory, but highly recommended since they provide you with review stuff and test format (might be dependent on TAs but if provided SAVE THE LINKS to each weeks slides)
sooooooo boring. The lectures were just him droning on about climate injustices There are also a lot of readings. I ended up changing the grading to pass/no pass after the first midterm.

The class itself was easy. There was did-you-do-the-readings style assignments, essays, and two exams. The exams were tough because of limited time. The grading was extremely lax and I'd consider this class fairly straightforward. However, lectures did not align with class content/learning objectives. Often made questionable comments.

he was a great professor, although there were times when his lectures were a bit too much. 
Something to keep in mind is that he posts 2-3 articles every week and they are long, I typically skim through them to get a gist of what they are about. 
for the midterm and final, its pretty much the same format, an online-timed exam.

I don't actually like writing so this was hard for me. The midterm and final are all timed writes and there's 3 essays due over the quarter. Discussions were bothersome because the assigned reading were 10-20 pages twice a week. I'd take Prof Stewart again but not ANTH 10. This course is also comparable to ANTH 23, same format and all.

Discussion posts 2 times a week, attendance mandatory, three papers, and midterms has 1 essay, final has 2. Lectures were interesting but for 80 minutes straight I often fell asleep. You don't need to read readings fully. I skimmed 3-5 pages on long ones and snored away in class. You'll easily get away with an A if writing is your thing :)
Just take her, the best math professor ever.

She is genuinely one of the best teachers you will ever have! She's super kind, genuine, and helps you prepare for tests very well. All you have to do is attend class, do the practice exams, and put time into the homeworks and you will be good. Definitely do the discussion worksheets (will help you a LOT).
I love her so much. to study for exams, she releases her old exams from past classes and they are SO helpful, the exams literally follow the same format. TAKE HER!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
Very helpful and easy professor, super understanding.

Very understanding professor and easy to talk to. Exam practice questions align well with actual exam. Only thing is discussions were not helpful (some times made more confusing), the content we worked on there didn't seem to align with pacing of lectures at times. Seems there needs to be more communication between TA and professor??

The class has only one midterm and a final which means the midterm will never clash with midterms of other classes that have 2 as they will occur at different times making it much less stressful, once a week simple homework and although lectures may be a little boring the slides are super helpful covering all important details, great teacher.

Extremely boring lectures. Midterm included topics he hadn't taught yet, and a question about a specific example discussed during a lecture. Discussion is only about the homework. Grading criteria for exams is weird, and you can't view your whole midterm unless you go to office hours
Professor rickard does not deserve these low ratings. He is extremely sweet and understanding and gives you a curve at the end! His tests are not too difficult as long as you study.
Great lecturer and HW is super easy, surprising there was no curve with the class being so test heavy.

Had AP Stats experience, found this class manageable. Understand EVERYTHING on his slides and lectures & that's all u need. There are nuanced ideas that he explains very concisely in class, so u likely won't grasp the full complexity of his points the 1st time - rewatch lectures, pause to understand things fully & know key class examples used.

Relatively easy class, exams are time consuming but all online, lectures are somewhat long but you can just watch the recorded lecture on 2x speed and take good notes to reference for the exams. Other than that class was chill and I'd take it again.

Pros: online lectures(and recorded) and online exams with a total of 3 exams and a final. Lots of extra credit opportunities. Cons: syllabus and course outline over time was a little disorganized. Exams questions can be tricky and can be based on stuff he rambles about. Lectures can feel like a drag but its doable and okay.

Cool prof who goes on random tangents at time (but I didn't really care). Exams were all online and multiple choice. Had the option to watch pre-recorded videos, attend lecture on zoom, or in-person. Could also go through the slides if you wanted but that's your choice. Overall, chill class and would take another with him.

DO. NOT. TAKE. 
Take him only if you're willing to endure listening to monotone lectures rife with creepy sex jokes and taking midterms about untaught content. The course itself is not difficult, but enduring through the psychological torture was the hardest thing I've ever gone through at UCSD.

The class wasn't difficult but the professor does not respond to emails and is very unorganized. The lectures are incredibly boring but you don't NEED to attend as every exam is online/open note, however they ask questions never discussed. Ultimately, he's not a hard professor just not a good one.
Avoid this profesor at all costs he will drop your gpa over small details don't waste your time and take another profesor there are thousands of better profesors to take other than him.

This profesor made my school life so much harder than it needed to be. He gives out tons of homework which is unclear and procedes to grade harshly. You could do all the reading and do everything right you still won't get the grade you deserve. Don't take this class
I will never be taking this class again, no matter how hard I studied and did the readings you get at best a b-. It seemed like everyone in the class agreed I do not recommend this guy.

Class is barely about psych, more about econ, policy, history, and climate justice. 20 page readings before every lecture. Weekly quizzes and exams ask abt very specific details from readings and labels on graphs in the slides, rather than capturing understanding of the content. Lecture is just repeat of the reading but with graphs and rants.

Professor Aron made PSYC 193L so much harder than it needed to be. He changed our individual assignments three times and the group assignments twice during the quarter. During week 8, he announced we would have a final when we were never supposed to have one, because he thought everyone was using Chat GPT. He assigned soooo much reading! Avoid him!
Lectures are unhelpful and unclear but mandatory. Quiz and exam questions focuses too much on reading homework and are way too specific. Generally bad and unhelpful.

Professor Hollan may be retiring this year (2026). It is pretty cool to be in the presence of someone so groundbreaking in their field. With that being said, though, there is a BIG separation between lectures and tests. The lectures are unintelligible ramblings of his experience, some concepts related to the course, and unrelated content.

I found his lectures really boring and the questions on his tests ridiculously specific. For both the midterm and final, I was surprised to see questions not about big picture concepts or overall takeaways, but about specific and little details in the readings, which I did and still couldn't answer because I studied to understand the content.

really interesting class, and prof makes it so engaging and fun to listen to. the subject matter is fascinating and it's so fun to learn about all the different consequences of technology, and about the history of tech itself. a bit challenging, and you really need to be paying attention for the quizzes and exams, but it's well worth it.

Really nice prof and understanding. Just put in the time to actually do the readings and stay on track and you'll do well in the class. There is a lot of readings. Exams can be tough to get an A on bc there's lots of tiny details to remember

Prof. Flagg is really tries to help students learn. He's very engaging in lectures and OH to help u understand content. Kind of luck based when it comes to group work. Going to and being engaged in lecture is ur best bet at passing. Final difficulty wasn't reflective of previous midterms, but wasn't impossible.

Overall, this was one of the most frustrating courses I've taken. Students must sit with randomly assigned partners and spend the first 15 minutes of each lecture on unproductive ‘talk-to-your-neighbor' & other activities. Lectures were low value, and the final included material never covered in class set you up for failure and definite grade drop.
Matt Flagg is a great professor that genuinely cares about his students. Yes the final was a little difficult but over all he is a very fair professor.
The final was honestly really rough and didn't feel fair or reflective of the class. I hope the next group of students has a better experience @Flagg

In previous quarters, Dr. Flagg was known for fair finals and strong ratings. Now that he mainly teaches graduate courses and sits comfortably at UCSD, the class changed. The final appeared intentional and caused widespread grade drops, revealing a fake, self-serving personality. Completely disingenuous and only nice when it suited him.

Do not take this class for a GE. Intensely boring 2 hr lectures and 3 hr sections that are mandatory and NO TECHNOLOGY. Print out some homework and bring it in if you are to take this. Professor talks on and on without saying anything of substance. You have to spend so much money on this class getting Adobe and printing out posters every week.

i hated this class icl... lectures were 2hrs long (though once a week) on monday nights. she recommended no notes needed and to just soak in all the info. i fear there was too much info. 3hr labs seemed initially daunting but my class got pretty close with each other because there were roughly 20 of us and critiques really bond you lol

I took this class because it is required for the ICAM major. Lectures are very long, and the large lecture hall makes it hard to stay engaged. The course structure is confusing. Thankfully, my TA was helpful and easy-going. Overall, the class is unorganized but doable if you keep up with the work. Good luck!

The lectures are extremely long and attendance is mandatory. My TA takes forever to grade... it is now finals week and I am still yet to get my midterm grades back. Its an easy A, or so I think. So if you are looking for a GPA boost, take it and just bring something to doodle with during lecture.

A sweet teacher but all she does is yap and read off the slides, even though the slides are posted to canvas. Takes the whole 2 hours, and super boring. But for some reason attendance is mandatory?? Does not make sense to me but as long as you attend you'll be ok.

Geniunely top-tier professor. Might even be the greatest of all time. This guy cares for his student & loves what he is teaching. Super fair grading and heavy curve. 

But the course itself is something else. Content-heavy, hard and time-consuming, you gotta put a lot of effort in. Office hours are a must, and the content is a lot to digest.

Anyone who thinks Conte isn't a good professor cannot be trusted. Prof Conte is the greatest and most caring professor I have had. This class was not easy but he has many office hours that are very helpful. He also explains problems really well. He wants every student taking this class to succeed, truly. CONTE ROCKS!

I took SE 125 with him in Fall 2024. Weekly hw, 1 close-book quiz, open-book midterm and final. Go to office hours to get the hw done otherwise u will fail this class. He curves generously. He's very knowledgable and even gave me his textbook for free
Fantastic professor
I love the big conte

FOR CHEM 200! Dude really knows his chemistry! Very competent lecturer, though he does goes a bit too fast when transitioning to other slides so be weary of that. Thankfully most of the content he goes over is not overcomplicated, it can just be a lot for people unfamiliar with chemistry. Still, just lock in and you will most likely be fine!

GOAT! I thought I would hate CHEM 7L, but Dr. Jazzar's lectures are consistently concise, inspirational, engaging, and helpful, an extremely rare feat for professors who teach lower-div STEM courses. He clearly cares about his students and wants the best for them; he is also super interesting both as an instructor and as a person. Highly recommend!

He was very good and helpful for the lecture portion of 7L lab class. He clearly explained how the lab works and gave a lot of content that was on the exam during lecture. Your grade in this class is mostly dependent on TAs grading your labs (as are all lab classes) but he is very generous.
The professor himself was amazing he was a great lecturer and told us basically what was going to be on the exam. I am quite sad to find out I was part of the last class he taught.

I was really worried to take this class considering all the things I've heard about it, but Professor Jazzar made the class so enjoyable for me. He is such a kind professor. He is very encouraging to students and wants us to learn and understand the material. I'm sad he won't be a professor at UCSD anymore because he is a great professor.
Not useful in giving feedback. AT ALL. asks for something and then when delivered she changes her mind.

Gotta make sure to be on top of the schedule and readings as she won't always remind people and you will be expected to know it in class. She says that a physical version of the textbooks from the bookstore are needed but realistically you can get away without using them. Very caring but won't take bs

Super nice and understanding. The class looking back was not hard pretty similar to AP Lang. Muir Writing just recently changed the grading scale so def not as hard as it was in the past. She has no control of the class but I still think she makes it pretty fair. Very interesting to listen to. Would've loved her for literally any other class.
Professor Nur is by far the most caring out of the MCWP teachers. She brings treats on peer review days, and if you get to know her outside of class, you will definitely excel.

I really liked this prof. The curriculum created by muir college is rough/hard and not her fault, but she does her best to help you and make sure you're successful despite it. If you think something is unfair its prolly a muir rule not hers. She really nice and gives clear feedback. She's also really accessible through email and office hours.
Taught pretty good, but kinda a yapper
tell too many stories of personal anecdotes I felt didn't positively effect class.

Super kind and passionate professor, as well as very informative and insightful during her lectures. Quizzes and tests were not difficult as long as you reviewed the lecture slides + she gives extra credit, which helps you out a lot since the class is based on total points.

Very kind and passionate professor with impressive field experience. The material isn't hard and prepares you for other upper div global health classes. Make sure to do the extra credit assignments offered.

great professor and caring. The only disadvantage of her is that she uses a lot of personal analogies in her lectures and it can feel just a bit repetitive. Some of her stories and experiences are really interesting though. Extra credit is offered.

MAE101A: if you plug in numbers before getting to the final step you lose most if not all credit for the problem (even if you got all answers right, if you had "different" steps you lose credit). hes unwilling to change test grades even if you got it right. If you care about A or learning, dont take, tests arent always "based on the homework".

Took him for MAE 120…Hard grader and your entire grade is based on exams. No cheat sheets or calculators allowed, so you have to memorize 30+ formulas. Lectures were unclear and concepts weren't explained well. He cold-calls students and can make you feel embarrassed for not knowing complex nuclear energy details.

MAE 120. Took as a technical elective and it was one of the hardest classes I've taken at UCSD. Your grade is 50% midterms and 50% final exam. I don't think I learned much because he would go on tangents each class and never fully finish explaining an idea, he also made people feel embarrassed for not knowing random fun facts about the topic.

I took this class for MAE 120. The professor is outright disrespectful. Grade determined by tests only. A calculator, note sheet, or formula sheet (must memorize all formulas). No TA. Lectures did little to aid understanding. Homework/exams loosely related to lecture material. Claims exams will be like the homework; they are not. Do not take.

Took MAE 120 not 118. I don't think I learned a single thing in this class. Only tests are graded, no homework. Midterm 1 is cake but midterm 2 and final were really hard. He doesn't teach, just rambles. Workload is really light, just study the homework solutions. Again, if you want to actually learn something, don't take this class.

Professor Rebeiz has this uncanny knack of knowing how to engage his students in lectures and getting them to pay attention. RF/Microwave material is difficult on a conceptual level and you won't pass if you don't put in the sufficient time. He's the reason I'm pursuing RFIC.

He is the best professor can teach you about antenna! So he is the best! But you have to study hard, go to office hour, the material is hard! He is tough professor, and you need to concentrate all the energy in the class, If you lose focus, you will falling behind. So good luck! you will learn lots but tough class!

Professor Rebeiz is the real RF boss, see? Talks S-parameters like a speakeasy king slingin' signals. Lectures hit like a Tommy gun—no fluff, just pure RF juice. Word is he's into insider tradin'—that's gangster, see? If you get the chance to take his class, don't think twice. It's an offer you can't refuse, see?
Best prof, learn a lot about insider trading. Best business course ever taken.

If you aren't ready to commit a large amount of time to understand this material you will not pass. This won't be like anything you've seen before and the professor says it himself. Don't fall on his bad side as he'll sometimes call out students for doing things that weren't disruptive to anyone. TAs are very helpful, and easy labs. Study hard.

He actively ensured students had resources to excel but was a bit disorganized due to graduation. Quizzes were super easy I studied for around 10-20 minutes for each and completed them in ~10-20/50 minutes allotted. Final was also easy with no studying. Overall the material is easy and he taught in a digestible manner in the classes i did attend.
Trying to understand this guy gave me a headache, every lecture had a mistake and he never planned ahead, announcement's were always made last minute, I definitely do NOT recommend this 🧑‍🏫
Professor Ganapathy was new when I had him so he may have improved but he rushed through a lot of the material and wasn't very clear when explaining concepts.
He's new to teaching the course and there were difficulties translating the concepts but the tests were fair.

do not bother watching lectures or showing up to class,just read the textbook and do practice problems. his handwriting is borderline illegible at times which made his attempts at explaining his thought process even more convoluted. ive spoke to other students about this and its not just me who feels like this. try taking with other instructor

I love this prof she honestly is an amzing teacher and actually keeps you engaged. The class has a 2 point completion HW due each friday, 2 midterms and one final but honestly as long as you go to class I promise you will do great!

I waited for my time at UCSD to end since I don't like hiding behind anonymous reviews. Dr. Yilmaz is an amazing professor and she got a wrongfully convicted man out of prison. Take the class (especially if ur pre law) to see what I'm talking about. Some find the class hard, some don't, I personally did. But I loved the class. 

- Aria

This class is loaded with a lot of content, but it is doable and is super interesting. The hardest part was reading the textbook that really did not involve much of the lecture info and the final cumulative exam. As long as you follow along with great note-taking you really could pass. Extra credit also helped A LOT.   Overall a kind professor too!

If you're not a good test taker, I highly recommend to not take her class. If you study well however, it is possible to pass. There are weekly readings that are worth 2% and that's it. There are 2 midterms and a final. She does offer extra credit and happened to add more extra credit because of how poorly students are performing. avoid the class.

Professor is passionate about her course however while she is helpful all of your grade is made up of the 3 exams which are very tough. Around 3 questions missed =10% of your grade. She also tells you to read the whole book chapter while not really  giving any extra information about what sections should be focused more on that'll be tested
Lecture notes are very clearly written. Aram tells you exactly what's on exams, and as long as you understand how to do the practice exams you will do well.
Prof is extremely clear and does not trick you. Wish I could have him for all my ECON classes. Grigoryan will not disappoint you, he is truly a G.
Aram is a king. Love him. Teaches well and tests fairly. Love you Aram!!!!!

The structure of his class is very clear: 4 homework assignments, 2 lowest are dropped, and the midterms and final study guides you are given are basically what is on the exams (same type of questions, different examples obviously). Make sure to attend lectures and discussions or watch them to understand the material.

He's a very slow and dry lecturer, so I stopped attending class after the second week. He's really passionate and knowledgable about the material but just boring to listen to - not his fault though, 100B is really easy after doing 100A. Tests and homework were very fair and graded leniently.

Prof Wardwell gives very compelling lectures and is never boring. The class was graded on just the midterm and final, which were both take-home exams. She gave the answers to the ID section and tips for the essay section in class. I really felt like this class was more about learning than grades or assignments.
Very amazing professor. Super knowledgable and lecture is always very engaging and fun to learn.

Accent isn't really a problem. Very passionate about the subject and very nice. Each lecture consists of a bit of lecture and watching a film. Grade is determined by attendance, 300-word diary entries for each film, a film review, and a final film analysis. There's a lot of room to write about what you personally enjoy for the review and analysis.

Really good teacher. lots of cases and laws etc to learn about but you should know a lot of them from high school or other American history classes. class was once a week, he teaches off a white board but it was class discussion. come prepared!!!!! only grades were midterm and final but it was take home 3 hour exam. he is smart respected teacher.

worst professor i've taken at ucsd. the GOAT of multivariable

super kind and thoroughly goes over the content. midterms are pretty tricky though.

Professor Hoffman was pretty chill, lectures can feel boring but I think it's just the nature of the content. Allowed cheat sheets for each exam, weekly quiz on lecture content. Pretty easy class just a bit tedious.

She wasn't that accessible out of class. God knows how many times i emailed her or contacted her through piazza with no response. Shes very knowledgeable about what she teaches. Quiz every week about last weeks content+reading, readings through perusal, No mandatory discussion, group video project

This was the only class that truly inspired me to show up. Professor Jacob brings in incredible entrepreneurs and guest speakers you can connect with, and she takes you on field trips! Her advice boils down to cold calling from a phone book... in the 21st century. Weirdly out of touch comments about students. No clarity

He's a nice and honest guy that is passionate about his career, but he is easily the worst instructor to take for this course. I have friends that have the class with other professors and now I see he really is a lot more stuck up with his versions of the same assignments.

Really great professor! He gave great feedback at office hours and when I emailed him. He seems to really care about you understanding what we are learning. Overall, the class and assignments were easy; you just need to show up to class since there are in-class check-ins.

While I enjoyed content that she taught, sometimes it felt like she was being redundant in her lectures and it'd be hard to track what I should explicitly know for the online quizzes that we had b/c the notes were meant for discussion. Ngl I didn't really attend lecture but when I did, what she talked abt didn't really have to do much with the projects. The weekly lab and quiz basically makes up your whole grade. Professor Smith is awesome. Lecture slides are clear and he teaches the content very well. His rating should be way higher. He is a funny good person, but he don't know how to teach....

Prof is an amazing lecturer! I absolutely hated physics before this, but he makes it interesting with lots of connections to biology/medicine and he's a rly funny dude. Highly recommend taking him!

Loved this professor! Good lecturer, clear about what was on exams, clear and fair grading. I'm not very skilled or interested in physics but this professor made it very manageable. Grade was entirely exams, but if you didn't do homework you would lose points. He was ok. Be aware that since it's a language class it will be everyday and you will need to study and participate. Overall, the class was really fun and I'm glad I took it!
officially logical
Doesnt know how to teach with no clear lesson plan ;  hard exams which are not reflective of HW at all ; Says he uses Artin, but doesnt ; Hard exams and HW ; Is accessible outside class though
i love logic
very good, 10 hour OH
Great class on logic. He covered a ton of content from David Marker's An Invitation to Mathematical Logic, and the homeworks were really heavy yet fun.
The tests are very difficult and unrelated to the course content taught in lectures. Lectures are also very confusing.

tough grading scale, you're only graded on a couple things with hard rubrics. Her TA's are harsh and will fail you for no reason. the lectures have nothing to do with exams and you're better off taking over the summer or with a different prof.

boring; so boring. There was absolutely no need to attend lecture, we were never tested on lecture content. Your research paper could have nothing to do with it. I regret attending any of her lectures; I did not learn anything I already learned in fifth grade. I love history and this class hurt me.

She was a nice professor but boring, would just lecture and read off of slides. The class is based on a research paper that you write from week 1 due on week 10 on a chosen topic. Lectures had nothing to do with anything expect for the midterm and final which was a prompt with a 500 word limit. Didn't read sources much, skipped class, and passed.
Boring but so easy. Skipped all lectures and ended with an A. Depends who your TA is tho mine was stingy w the grading...

I had him for 100F, which is the heritage speaker class; I learned Spanish in high school, and even though I wasn't technically supposed to be in that class he did a great job making me feel welcome and I really respect his teaching style. The class is incredibly accessible if you can speak, read, and write conversationally in Spanish. W class
He is a great professor, he teaches interesting topics that aren't usually talked about. I really recommend him he is chill and gives good feedback! I would take him again.

I took Professor Cabrera during Summer 2020 and his class was easy. Definitely recommend him, he is very smart, concise and likes to engage with the students. This class made me change my major to latin American studies.

One of my favorite professors ever, hands down. Luis really emphasizes students' participation in discussions (he doesn't lecture, but rather facilitates discussions) and really encourages you to think critically about your assumptions along with the material you read/watch for the class. There's a lot of reading but you can usually skim it.
The class I took was Almodovar. I learned a TON about Spanish history & a lot about Freud. He likes to engage with the students (this class was tiny).

I adore Dr. Siapno for her care in what she teaches, the context she brings from her lived experience, and her prioritization of her students' well-being. Her class is easy in terms of academic rigor, but she provides an overwhelming number of opportunities for students to teach themselves and engage in active conversations. 100% would take again!

Genuinely has no curriculum or plan for class, but a super easy A. Never graded a thing all quarter, made inflammatory or insensitive comments, and I didn't learn a thing. She's very intolerant of other viewpoints. 
One discussion post per week where you respond to 3 others, 1000 word essay as the midterm, and group presentation for the final.

She claims to be all about justice and all but when met with skepticism, she ignores or shuts people down. Maybe instead of acting hostile towards students and bragging about it to your other sections, you should take time to help people unpack what they believe. I was never subject to her verbal teardowns but it was an uncomfortable environment.

Took this class expecting open discussion, but was the opposite. Prof often singled out students, made backhanded comments & implied the use of AI based on how they spoke. She shared misleading info as fact & discouraged differing views. Syllabus didn't match class content & expectations were unclear. The course felt performative than educational

Prof. Siapno often mentioned wanting to quit and seemed overwhelmed. She sometimes gave out incorrect info & didn't handle disagreement well—twisting words or shutting down the convo. If your writing doesn't match how you speak in class, she might accuse you of using AI. Class is easy if you keep up, but expect a tense and discouraging atmosphere.

I took professor Ruiz twice during my undergrad and I think he did a good job as a professor. His lectures need to be more interactive because he has a soothing voice and was putting me to sleep sometimes, my classmates too were sometimes dozing off too! He is a wonderful professor and you will learn a lot if you stay awake and take notes.
Professor loves to engage students and cares about you doing well, one of the few memorable professors I've had.

Professor Ruiz's class was enjoyable and easy! At time it was so easy that it was..hard? If that makes sense, like the rubric for our Midterm Essay was very vague and so it was kind of intimidating but he's very open to questions. Very lenient professor, you will NOT fail this class. Lectures are mandatory (but he posts the class code online...).

I really enjoy his lectures :,) he does encourage participation which does lead to awkward silences but he is very fair on his grading. heavy reading but nothing you wouldn't expect from a soc class :,) yay mr. jon

One of the only teachers who will care about you here. You can turn in midterms late as long as you advise ahead of time. Your grade depends on how you do on the essay midterms and final. Easy to understand, genuinely a good class if you want a grade-booster. Discussion attendance opts as your lecture attendance so show up to those.

I took HUM 4 with Prof. Henson just to fulfill my fine art GE for Revelle, but it ended up being my favorite class that quarter. Despite being essays the assignments were really fun and did a good job of getting you to really think about the pieces and themes in question. Lectures were always super interesting and engaging, worth being there at 8am

Matthew was amazing for Mus4, it was his first time teaching but he was constantly enganged and incredibly positive and energetic for an 8am class. The music pieces we reviewed in class were really interesting and he managed to make everything very captivating. Also he was very funny at the most random times and the class was a really easy GE
Cool dude, made a GE class pretty interesting. You'll probably enjoy it, and it doesn't have a lot of coursework. Bumped some of my attendance points too

I LOVE professor Henson. He's such a caring guy and I love his lectures, the content is pretty cool and unique if you like music even a little. Its also super easy, attendance is 30% of grade with 6 misses allowed and like everything else is easy assignments. He literally told us what would be on the midterm and how to answer it, median was a 100.

It is relatively easy to get full points in assignments, so don't worry about your GPA. We have about seven papers to write, and each of them will be unlocked after he finishes discussing one unit. The assignment prompts are fairly clear, and he consistently reminds us about deadlines, lectures, and other important details.

While a lot of people in the RED major give him a hard time for being a slow lecturer who gets off topic, Anderson is an extremely competent teacher who gives very useful commentary and interesting insight from his ample experience. Midterm is easy econ, projects are easy, and he is very sweet

Amazing professor with decades in the industry and a lot of experience, also loved to help with students about inquiries into non-class related opportunities. Assignments were mainly handled by TA, and readings were assigned (I got by without reading). Go to lectures, study the section material, and it's an easy class.

The only assignments throughout the quarter were readings and memos. This is a pro and a con as your grade only relies on these + the midterm/final. The lectures can feel boring as he speaks about his life story at times. He's a nice guy and genuinely seems like he cares about his students. Not a bad class, but don't know if I would take again.

This professor is a little boring at times, but he means well and genuinely cares about his job. As long as you watch the lectures and stay on top of the material, you'll do fine. He's a sweet guy who wants his students to succeed. The TA was incredible too! Plenty of time to complete HW assignments. (three of them), the rest of the grade mid/final

Professor Anderson uses a lot of stories as examples for concepts and terms, his class is podcasted, and the only homework was an Excel project, writing a short essay, and optional reading from a textbook. The only con I can think of is he put a few tricky questions on the midterm/final, but the exams overall were reflective of what was taught.

Kyle Adam Blaire is an angel on earth. He genuinely loves music and is so entertaining and engaging. There are no midterms, just 2 performance attendances and write ups on how they make you feel. Lecture attendance is required but you get 2 free passes (same for dis).  Final is online, open all week, open note, take home. TAKE HIM IF YOU CAN!!!

Hes a very kind and nice professor. If you did something wrong or missed assignments, he will be very patient and give you another chance let you get full credits. His lectures are very amazing and easy to understand even for 0 basic students. You might take some time for hw but it's unlimited trials. Exams and final project are not hard. Pick him!

Blair's class was amazingly simple and complex at the same time. Teaching introductory music theory in a way that although myself am a musician, still found learning opportunity, which was refreshing. Great lectures and engaging material, highly recommend.

I've been playing an instrument for almost 5 years now but professor Blair explained music theory better than I've ever understood. The class was fun, and attendance was only mandatory to encourage participation. Easy HW on an interactive platform called Artusi, very comprehensive. Online, open book midterm and final, would recommend as a GE
First time teacher, not fond of her confidence level. Often gets corrected by students
She tried her best and clearly cared, but her class made me very confused. Her explanations were longwinded, overcomplicating pretty simple concepts with her answers to questions.

Professor Fedorov is well meaning, but her lectures are difficult to get through and very boring. I find that this class overcomplicates very simple problems, and her lectures didn't offer the best environments for participation. I found that the midterms were incredibly easy and left me unprepared for the difficulty of the final.

She's inexperienced at teaching which is kind of clear because she isn't confident in her explanations. She'll explain smth then if someone doesn't get smth she'll explain it again but in a more confusing way that just makes it worse so be careful. Also her tests and hw are super easy. You get a notecard on all the exams but you hardly need it.

If you do the work you will be very well prepared for all the tests. TA office hours were VERY useful. She would go through stuff before/after the tests for people who were paying attention and is a pretty lenient grader.

BENG2; Teacher barely taught, everything was handled by the TA; for a two credit class the amount of work given was absurd, labs and hw every week, questions were hard, only got help going to the TA, even then still got points off on it; mid term and final was fine, just review her mcqs, the study guide wasn't helpful; gave flipped classroom vibes
Really easy class mostly taught by the TAs

beng1 is incredibly easy to pass - basically the only way to fail is to have 2 unexcused lab absences (you get 1 grace absence). everything is pretty much just graded for participation, so even if you end up with a bad lab group, it doesn't matter. labs are very straightforward - they tell you what to do and you do it

Entertaining classes made the 8AM lecture worth it; super funny and personable. TAs pretty much run the course, which can make or break your grade. For my section, discussion attendance was mandatory, as was participation. Lots of reading for HW, which is incorporated into tests, and reviewed in discussion. Fairly easy if you took APUSH.

Widener is very funny, lectures are very entertaining. I feel like the TA you get can make or break your grade in the class; for my section, discussion (not lecture) attendance was mandatory, you were graded based on how much you participated, and the TA was a strict grader. There's also a lot of reading, which is incorporated into the tests.
lectures were terrific and definitely worth attending. Grading depends on discussion involvement and two exams, which requires reading the textbooks. Most students would get an A.

Ragebait professor, he is only here to spread his political agenda and sell his book. Class itself is very easy, TAs grade very easily, if you want a free A go ahead. His final he requires you to have 3 textbooks, one of them being his, also being the most expensive.

Just go to Discussion, I never went to a single lecture or did any of the reading and I got an A in the class. Like the class is exactly like APUSH, but the essays aren't even graded. I honestly don't know how there are people that did not receive an A in this class.

He seemingly expects you to have a good understanding of everything going into the class. The lectures are way too fast to actually learn anything, and there is an absurd amount of homework. I was working for around 10 hours a week for this class doing everything I could to pass it (anything below a C is failing).

Passionate about the subject but not good at teaching at all. Provides no feedback and 75% of the students were failing before the final. Lectures, homework, and tests were all covering different things and you have to self teach yourself the content. Never updates canvas. Take this course at community if he's the only professor available here.

Lectures are fast, hard to follow and exams are extremely hard. Homework and exams include techniques not mentioned during lectures. Don't take unless you already know the content and expect to work very hard and find outside resources for a passing grade. Passionate about math but doesn't care about the class and laughs about 30% averages for exam

Just don't even choose this man. Run far away. He makes the test way more difficult than what he teaches us and expects us to know it. You can spend HOURS studying for his exams and still manage to fail because of how difficult the problems are on the exams (exactly what happened to me)!

Run. This prof makes simple concepts so much harder than they have to be and doesn't care about his students succeeding. No extra credit, no curves, 80% of your grade is midterms and the final, and a 70% is an F.

She's cool but she does a flipped classroom thing that I was not a fan of. Just do your work and pray you don't get a bad partner/group for labs and final project bc that WILL ruin your grade. Email her if you have issues bc she is very understanding. The final is a breeze just pay attention to the lecture quizzes bc the questions are the same.

VDE's class will give you a solid understanding of SE concepts and of what to expect in the major. The class is VERY homework heavy and requires setting aside a lot of time to work on assignments and attend office hours. Make sure to choose your teammates wisely for group projects as this can make or break your experience.
The class was heavily group work with a lot of involvement. You'll be working with a lot of classmates on weekly assignments. Not a bad intro to SE.

No tests, but there is about 20-27 hours of work a week which will eat up your weekends. The class is extremely exhausting but "fun", in that in the end you learn a lot about the multiple softwares used by engineers. I would highly recommend only taking two other courses that are easier, because you will be exhausted by the end of every week.

VDE doesn't do tests, so she assigns a TON of homework instead. They're mostly busy work assignments that are meaningless. She does teach well though, and does care about students. The TAs also grade harshly, and often mark points off for arbitrary reasons. Expect about 8 hours of work a week.

Taking a class with this prof. is a disservice to your education. You'll learn more by taking a Udemy course or watching a YouTube video. Prof. needs to scope down what he is teaching. Take the class with anyone else if you care about learning the material. Avoid!

This is one of the worst classes I have ever taken. There is SO much material presented (but not covered). He tends to ramble a lot and it is rarely clear what specifically we should take notes on. He provides a tsunami of information and selectively goes over the material at a very high-level. The assignments are lazily put together. Avoid!

He enjoys teaching and his lectures are interesting - that doesn't make the class any good. Attendance is mandatory and unnecessarily weird. Homework assignments are often extremely vague and take forever to do, and exams are often just about how much can you memorize from lecture. The class is designed to make our life hard.
The GOAT. If Dwight from The Office had a brother, then Professor Powell would be that person.
Took the lecture back in 2024, professors lecture was fun but honestly not a lot of useful stuff, yet still had to attend for participation

Ming is a phenomenal professor and person. He shows up everyday with a smile on his face. His lectures are extremely clear and he repeats important concepts frequently to make sure we fully understand. He's very accessible in and out of the classroom. He's very supportive, often celebrating mid lecture to tell us he's proud of us for showing up.

Ming is actually the best professor ever.  He is so passionate about what he teaches and he truly cares about his students. His lectures are clear and his exams follow the practice questions almost exactly. He makes this course about as easy as it can get so I would recommend taking it with him! I would take a bullet for Ming tbh he's the goat

Ming is passionate and knowledgeable, but he is a tough grader and the course demands a lot of time. Many students advise not taking it alongside other heavy classes. There is also little accommodation for students who are busy or can't regularly attend office hours.

While some students may have found the resources sufficient, that was not my experience. The course was extremely exam-heavy, and exam difficulty felt disproportionate to lectures and practice material. With no curve, a single poor exam had a major impact, making the course feel unforgiving despite effort and office hours.

Mingyu Yang was a great professor and you could really tell he cares for the course! The course was test heavy and a lot of work but similar to any other upper division course work. Everything was manageable with the amount of resources provided both in class and out of class (OH, emails etc.)
Soooooooooo boring, hard to stay awake. Lots of reading and weekly assignments. Not the worst but I did not have fun, she means well, but I don't like her lecture style. beware. be alert.
she means well but she is really boring. lectures are very content heavy and it's ok for a ge requirement, but no one was interested.

The professor is very nice. Fulfilling class content with clear logic of lecture arrangement. It's an introduction if you're into serious media studies, but could also be a way too boring academic conversation if you know nothing with no interest in this field. It's fine taking for GE since lenient grading though.

Media and art isn't for everyone, however, if you are someone interested in this field, the course was interesting and provided historic and relevant context to film, media, video, art, etc. Lectures can get boring, DIs can be interesting, NO Midterm, Final is a straightforward project, discussion boards do matter + readings, and weekly worksheets.
Class was easy and fairly manageable, but lots of reading. No final or midterm (only a final project). Lectures could be a bit of a drone at times. Super nice professor though.

An exceptional professor who truly cares about his students. He maintains high academic standards while being understanding and supportive, especially during difficult circumstances. His kindness and professionalism make a real difference in the learning experience. I'm very grateful to have taken his course. He is the MOST AMAZING PROFESSOR EVER!

Professor Grant is really nice guy. Attendance is kind of mandatory - depends on what project is done that day. Some lectures went really slow, then sped up the last 30 minutes or so, which made it difficult to get the last codes. There were multiple breaks in class, but most of us just wanted to leave early instead.

This is my first time writing an RMP review and it's been only one week through the quarter, but man he deserves a much higher rating! He's such a nice and kind professor and always lectures with a smile. You can easily tell that he truly cares about his students and loves what he's teaching. Protect at all costs.

I think Dr. Grant has modified his teaching style since previous reviews because I have had a great experience in his class. The learning curve is steep at first if you have no prior coding experience but Dr. Grant and the TAs are super supportive. I feel like I've learned so much in this class and really enjoyed it as well.

took NANO15, thought my familiarity w coding/matlab would help... boy was I wrong. SUPER confusing. Prof. Grant def knows his stuff, but I felt like he would forget we were students sometimes and would just define things once and move on. The material's rlly dense to go through on ur own. Also, SO MUCH HW,, wish I didnt take this class w ochem :"|

He is a really nice professor that greatly cares about his students and is willing to even schedule one-on-one time with students outside of class to help them understand the subject. Highly recommend.

Made organic chemistry very fun and interesting to learn. Tests were not too bad and there was an insanely generous 1% curve. Be prepared to study your hydride shifts. Honestly, 99% of the class is based on your understanding of hydride shifts so be sure to master them. Also makes great music!

Darius Yohannan is a Vikings fan. His purple Vikings jacket always inspired me to do structure elucidation problems with ease. The TA's beach attire goes with the overall vibe of every exam. Every class was tranquil and soothing, enjoyed learning about NMR. What about a hydride shift?
Clear and concise professor. I still look back at his Lecture Notes for future classes since they were very well made. 10/10!

The BEST math prof at UCSD!!! Lou truly care about teaching and he really knows how to make a difficult course comprehensible.
He is extremely proficient in the subject, explains everything clearly, great lecture notes, reasonable & responsible, clear communication & expectations, fair exams, fast grading. Can't think of a negative thing about him.

Not bad, but his slides are a bit disorganized. He does not split them up by lecture, and handwriting can be illegible at times. His explaining makes up for it well enough. I found the content very interesting and quizzes were fair, questions are usually word for word from the practice questions he does in class. Heard the final will be bad tho...

Professor Pecore is the goat, he's extremely knowledgeable and passionate when teaching, he genuinely cares and just wants you to succeed. If you have questions, just ask, him and TAs are always very responsive. HW can take awhile but quizzes are always super manageable.

Final grade consists of 7 out of 9 total in class assignments, 2 projects and 4 quizzes. The class was very interesting and straightforward to me (business major). Just go to lectures (not podcasted) and study the slides for the quizzes and you'll be good. He's a goat prof, took him for MGT 45 too, overall recommend this class for all

He's a great professor. Grade is 3 quizzes, 3 homeworks when I took it. Homework takes a good amount of time, but it's not hard if you manage your time. His office hours are extremely helpful for HW and quizzes. Not a hard class to succeed in if you put in effort and use the resources.

I love Joseph Pecore! HE IS THE BEST! GO TO OFFICE HOURS IF YOU'RE CONFUSED. He is caring towards his students. I love his teaching. Homework is tedious, but go to office hours! Would ABSOLUTELY TAKE AGAIN!!!!!

Professor Pecore is the MAN! He is a phenomenal professor and I would highly recommend him! His class is extremely doable and is great real life knowledge to know. With years of successful corporation experience, he brings a unique skill set that I was honored to learn from. THANK YOU!

Rated on her teaching style and attitudes overall against other professors because there's only 3 options for DOC. She goes over all relevant content very well, lectures are a little on the boring side, can be a little demeaning and passive aggressive. About as professional as a Karen can be. Overall good for getting an A in DOC.

Prof. Solomon was a great choice for DOC. She's passionate, thorough, and even gives nudges to what to possibly expect on the midterm and final exams. Despite DOC being a text-heavy and therefore overwhelming course in general, Solomon at least makes it interesting. I would take her again if I could. In general, attendance is key.

All the DOC professors follow the same syllabus so doesn't really matter who you choose. I thought Prof Solomon wasn't the best lecturer (spent a lot of time calling on students instead of explaining the material herself) and could be a bit overkill on certain policies. However, she definitely does care about what she teaches.

She is very passionate about what she teaches, and you can tell she cares. The course is very passable if you put the effort to try, tho there's a lot of reading. Attendance is mandatory for both lectures & discussions, but u get some free skips. She's great, just don't be late (you'll be locked out after 5 min.) & do not whip out any electronics.

You can definitely tell she's passionate about the subject, and her lectures will keep you engaged. Fair grading policies (i.e., 3 unexcused absences allowed, late windows for big assignments). Strict about no technology, but so are all DOC 1 profs. The midterm and final are very doable if you pay attention in class (a cheatsheet is allowed).
Had good notes, very thick accent, exams were very hard. Very nice person, very strict grading. Good for people that just want notes. Attending lecture did not help me personally.
Talks so fast, would go over lecture time often, went to every lecture and was very confused by her teaching, the tests scores were bad and there were no curves. big fail rate for my class

If you're going to make a choice about this professor she stopped teaching at SD and has come to Berkeley. Check out her Berkeley Rate my professor to see how she horrendously ruined kids math experience.

Homework and discussion is worth much less than other 20 series classes. Exams graded heavy as 70-80% of everything. Thick accent, pretty fast. Admittedly didn't attend lecture but only because of the above reasons. Averages on midterms were D and F on the final. No curve on exams or total grade. Disagree with anything less than 5 difficulty.

Heavy accent, move pretty fast with insufficient explanation on how to handling different type of problem for each concept. Admittedly, she covered all the required topic, but the exam is super hard. the 2 midterm is some how fair, but the final is extremely hard (tested focus unexpected). The homework is a great practice, but heavy calculation.
You will learn so much from this course. I would recommend taking it and being prepared to think critically.
I showed up to everything and did all the assignments but the reading responses were kind of miserable. You need to read a lot. Course was interesting though.

Everybody complaining about the workload are procrastinators. There are not a lot of assignments, just a few big ones that are really not hard... unless you put it off till the last minute. If you show up, like you're supposed to, and follow along you will be just fine. It is not hard to get an A.

Prof. Harpin was the sweetest professor I've had in my college career. A lot of readings and she can be a tough grader, but as long as you pay attention in lecture and do the readings youll be fine. The journals are very time consuming. Overall highly recommend if you want to learn critical race theory. Really enjoyed!

One of the best profs. Make sure you start the assignments asap, they take a lot longer than you might think and you will spend hours on reading and writing. Class topics are interesting and engaging.

Dr. Nguyen is a tough professor and can rub some students the wrong way. HOWEVER, she is extremely caring of her students if you at least try. She wants the best for her students and if you make an effort to try or go to office hours, she will do everything she can to help you pass and become a greater student. Do not be intimidated!
This professor was the worst one Ive had throughout my college career. Avoid her at all costs.

She is super nit-picky about everything!! She knew some of us had class after hers and she said "I understand some of you have a class after mine but I teach until 1:50." She made this class and its material harder than it has to be. The homework doesn't really help understand the material and the group projects are slightly overwhelming.

This professor puts way to much effort into making your life difficult. She has the most nit picky directions for no reason. Her way or the highway. Does not like when students have long winded answers or questions and will cut people off mid sentence to tell you why you're wrong. Rude and difficult to understand because of how quickly she talks.

Nit-picky with assignments, and not friendly. Assignments are very time consuming and do not really help with understanding any concepts covered in class. I recommend taking this with another professor if you can.

A lot of self studying is necessary. The lectures are based on simple 2D/3D visual diagrams with explanations (very little math) whereas the quizzes are entirely math and intuition heavy. Not very reflective of the content taught in class and there's no partial credit or grade replacement policy
pretty bad. all good ratings you see came from when the quizzes and exams were taken online.
This class is quite difficult, there is a quiz every two weeks, but it's fine if you study the concepts. Lectures aren't useful so self-study.

Lectures on complex math concepts by just talking about them, rather than walking through concrete examples. Gives a quiz on a mid-term's worth of material every week. On top of this, there is a final and three 2-2.5 page projects. Starts every lecture 10 minutes late. Gives prep materials and makes quiz nothing like prep materials nor lecture.
Hard Quiz, lecture hard to follow

Not sure from other comments what happened; however, the first midterm does reflect the course content well, albeit not easy. He provides score predictions to match historical MATH 189 grade distributions, so as long as one works hard, this class is not impossible. AI is allowed, but how to use it wisely depends on the individual.

Changes the grading scheme from project-based to test-based, and the tests are under a heavy time crunch with low averages. His lecture notes are ok but sometimes unclear, and there are no lecture recordings. Very unflexible with homework deadlines.
Used to be a group-project heavy class but now it's just unnecessarily difficult exams

Literally take the class with anybody else who will stay true to the integrity of the class. No podcast to try to incentivize attendance not like his lectures help anyways. Not group project based its 2 midterms, 1 final in which he genuinely does not prepare you for. Also does not accept any late work. Oh and if you dk latex good luck!!
He has no podcasts and makes an easy class (historically project-based) unnecessarily difficult with 2 midterms and 1 final :'( I'm so dead

Good professor. Took mus7 last year so maybe a hazy memory but the class was very easy, had very few assignments but were also very engaging and I learned stuff relevant to my other interest of making music. Very interesting lectures, good discussion section, good guy.

Took this class for GE credit. I do have a background in music but it was very clearly not necessary to have success in the class.
Assignments ~every two weeks, were very easy, and he essentially completes all of them in front of you. No midterms, only a final project. Extremely lenient, super nice and approachable guy. No purchases. Fun lectures.
Professor Ahn is so far one of my favorite professors here at UCSD. They're really caring, funny, and passionate for their job. I think they are really understanding and is good at lectures.

Prof. Ahn is amazing! They care about students, and the class is well-organised and enjoyable. Instead of weekly quizzes, there are quizzes based on lectures, there is a midterm group project, and a final group project. They focus on practical learning, and they use movie clips to teach, which makes it easy to grasp the concepts.

The class is for the JTCCER, but was very interesting. A good breather from STEM with engaging lectures, field trips, and forgiving grading systems. She's just a great person. Very passionate, accessible and understanding. There is ample room to do the few major assignments and the great majority of the grade is just engaging. Would take again.
Greatest and my favourite professor in UCSD. Really passionate in teaching and provide tons of help both during the class and after the class.
Lectures are fine but his exams and quizzes are so difficult and long given the time.

10/10 would take him again! The professor is super nice and explains the content very well! The first 3 lectures were economics based, which made me a bit nervous, but it was actually very simple and easy to follow. After that, it's all about psych. There are 2 midterms, one in person, one online, and an in person final and he gives study guides!
I enjoyed the professor's teaching style, and each class was engaging with useful material.

You should take Prof. Wilson's psych 184 class if you're a business psych major. The only difficult parts of the class were covered in your econ lower divs, and the lectures blend economics with psych in a really cool way. I enjoyed this class, and all the discussion of self control prepared me for a busy quarter. 5/5  !

i signed up for this class thinking it would be about psych. it wasn't, it was just economics. very test heavy & super difficult for me. not a lot of homework but the lectures are podcasted so that's a plus. the professor was very nice though, just not something i'd take again.

Best class at UCSD! teaches you so many things about self control and decision making across a bunch of different fields. SLOW lectures. Can not understand anything in class. Discussions not helpful at all. Exams- super hard. Avoid her at all cost.

Lectures are extremely boring and slow, found myself going back and watching them at 2x speed. Exams are very difficult, discussions and office hours aren't helpful. Does not offer helpful advice on how to do well. She's just not it.

Caring but grading scheme was not for me. Feedback had me constantly feeling like I was not doing good enough. Readings, watch parties, free-writes, discussion boards/responses, essays, projects, peer reviews.

Sometimes gives Google Forms for attendance
Doesn't really give good guidelines on what you need to study or focus on in terms of content

Disorganized and did not learn much.

Professor Daly, Is absolutely amazing she is well versed in a lot of constitutional history and native American history as she is a tribal member herself. Did not care for this professor or her class. She seems disorganized. I do not recommend.

Awesome class! Dr. Daly is the best! She teachers 102 most quarters, but the subject of the course changes depending on the quarter. I took it when the topic was Indigenous Food, and every Thursday we got to make and eat foods discussed during lecture! Absolutely amazing experience and great prof!
Seems pretty young but definitely a great mathematician. Actual course is pretty tough but concepts were taught well.
Way too hard

Love this professor, very passionate about teaching.

Didn't allow cheat cheats despite the millions of formulas/equations to memorize. He tends to rush through content, which makes it a bit hard to keep up. But, he was very passionate for the subject and seemed to care about his students. He tends to rush material during lectures, making it a bit hard to keep up. But, he was very passionate for the material and seemed to care about his students. We didn't get cheat sheets on any of our exams, but both midterms and the final were very fair, sometimes included questions we did in class. The content itself is just a lot to study for.
Great teaching style with engaging lectures, HW is super helpful and tests are of reasonable difficulty and grading.
Good informative and entertaining lectures with very fair tests that aren't super difficult. HW is graded on accuracy but can be done in groups.
Informative and entertaining lectures that are clear and easy to understand, tests are fair and HW is super helpful.

This is a great class, although Professor Jones goes really fast in the lectures, so it can be difficult to understand. Going to office hours weekly will be very helpful for this class both for homework and understanding the content. Tests are very fair.

Sometimes he goes pretty fast in lecture which sucks cuz this course is pretty different from any math I've done before. HWs go from easy to progressively harder but you can work in groups. Exams are much easier than HW and are fair. Overall Miles is a chill guy who is approachable and this class has made me more curious abt proofs/number theory

I really like Chapman! He's chill, cracks some jokes in class, and the homework is easy. There is a decent amount of reading involved, but I personally found the topics interesting. Graded mainly on attendance, homework, one exam, and a vignette (u watch a movie and diagnose a character in groups and discuss, which was easy). Would take again :)

Too much busy work homework. Course is fine, boring if anything & annoying. Only goes into super general clinical stuff, I felt like I learned nothing. Chapman is one of the worst professors I've had in my life. He is an extremely easy A if you go to class and read the material. He cares very little about his students and certain situations regarding group projects that he enforced. In some classes he also forces people to do "service learning". Failing to do so means -10% to your final grade

Super super strict about attendance. Only one super easy exam at the end of class, the rest of class is filled with online busy work. He's a great guy, but this class seems like it could be taught at a high school due to the format and rules. Material and work is not difficult.

A very easy A. His lectures we pretty summarized from the textbook, but he is a funny guy so it helped getting through lecture. Lots of busywork homeworks that are super easy, just tedious. Weekly journal reflections. Mandatory attendance and he likes participation from students in lecture. No midterm, just a final that was really easy.

This class is hard, but the professor is by far one of the absolute best in the CSE dept. If you loved Niema, you'll love Deepak even more. 5 PAs, about 2 weeks per PA. 2 exams. Curves based on rank. Professor Kumar is a very cool person with an easygoing style. His slides are well prepared and the lectures are engaging. He is available outside class to students and really gives time to address any concerns. He encourages mature, logical conversations in class and is open to crazy ideas.
