His first ever class but it went well. Clear that he cares about students and learning, lax about grades as long as you make an effort and show up. Engaging lecturer and is open to feedback.
I'll report back after taking his 227 next quarter.

Research advising was quite hands-off and mentorship felt limited, publication progress seemed largely student-driven. The professor streams the lectures on twitch.
Professor was very fair to students. Lectures were informative and he is so funny! Class was easy as long as you put in the work.

Good professor, lectures are very clear, easy to follow, and informative, just a bit monotone at times. Assignments were pretty relaxed and grading distribution was fair, with around a B+/A- average. Would recommend.

Prospective students, beware. HWs and assignments weren't too complex and lectures were decent, however, the grading on the assignments didn't sit right with me to say the least. The class is mainly guests who come and lecture instead of the professor. Grading really depends on the TA. She allows a cheatsheet only on the front side. My suggestion if you take this class is to pay attention during discussions because most of the midterm questions are from the discussions, but are more in-depth.

super easy class and an amazing professor. there are weekly hws which are based on lectures. reading is given out but no one does it and honestly you don't need to finish hws and tests. hws are graded on completion not accuracy so just make sure to answer all parts of the question. dr. reese is so nice and just wants respect for guest speakers.

She mostly had guest lecturers come in to teach different lessons, which can be really interesting! There are weekly homework assignments that are graded by completion, so your grade mostly depends on the midterm and final. She is a pretty chill professor and cares about her students.

Almost ALL guest lecturers & most of the info is useless for exams as it's to see if you're interested in their topic (gets boring). only important info is on the weekly hw. Prof. also yelled at students multiple times abt respect for talking/doing something for another class during lecture, which i thought was unnecessary. readings are optional

The course is mainly guest lectures. The midterm and final exam is free response but it's fairly easy. I highly recommend using the discussion slides to study!! Also she gives you a cheat sheet (1 side for midterm and 2 sided for the final).
BEST TA!!! Cares about his people, help you prepare. Best TA you can have.

Emre's passion for teaching history is extremely evident-- as a TA, he is so kind and caring towards his students, offering many office hours before midterms and the final. He makes everyone feel welcome and his puppy, Haru, always brightened the mood during early morning discussions. Would absolutely recommend. This guy is like Keanu Reeves Jesus.

Emre is my GOAT. He is the chillest, nicest TA ever and his dog Haru Gaia is such a cutie patootie (he lets us pet her :) ). Everyone can do well if you do your best and talk to Emre. 100,000,000,000,000/10 recommend.

Emre was my TA for MMW 11 - dude is the chillest, nicest, most caring TA I've had so far :D
He had a lot of students, but really did make a very strong effort into getting to know everyone. We

Emre was an amazing TA. Really cares to get the students prepared for the exams and understand the content. Provided helpful resources you can use to study if you take notes on what is done in discussion, but also they're available on Canvas.
"Interesting professor"

Her exams are easier than her homework, and focuses on concepts mostly. Her homework tends to be really long and time consuming. She's pretty helpful when you ask for it, and her lectures are pretty interesting, but also really closely tied to the textbook.

In the middle of rewatching lectures and Prof. Kester is genuinely one of the funniest professors that I have ever taken a class with. Never a boring time, even if its on Zoom. He is a really great teacher and made the lectures super interesting, even when they were on zoom. BEST PROFESSOR EVER. He literally changed my life.

Kester might be interesting if you actually care about art, but he really loves going on tangents in his lectures. Overall, he's extremely knowledgeable on the class topics, his lectures are amazingly thorough, and he brings a great energy to class. My only gripe with this class is the workload. Honestly, do the work and you'll be fine.
Professor Bronstein is engaging and allows students to share ideas about material during lecture. She also considers student feedback from SET evals.
Grades mostly come from TAs. Course content can get boring with odd readings but the films are always fun. She's a good lecturer too but you need to attend for participation credit

2 weekly assignments usually plus weekly in-class writing. Grade of writing determined by TA but assignments graded for completion. If you do your assignments, you likely cannot fail. Not technology allowed in class. Write no more than a paragraph. Discussions don't help with writing usually.

Mandatory lectures and discussion. Lectures are not very useful. Your grade pretty much depends on the weekly writing which is graded by your TA. The lecture quizzes are easy. If you do your homework and get decent scores on the weekly responses then you'll be fine. TA basically determines your grade. Overall easy class
Lots of busy work, professor does little

This course felt overloaded with busywork, making it hard to see real value beyond boosting a GPA. The heavy reliance on AI grading, while fast, was frustrating and impersonal to deal with. She let me into her class late and was understanding about my circumstances. She ensured I would still learn the concepts I was behind on and seemed very passionate about teaching her students. I had her for EDS 124AR and EDS 124BR and I enjoyed these classes a whole lot. These classes are different than others because it is not about the grade that you get, but it is about learning. Professor Simon truly cares about her students and she wants her students to do well, while learning a lot from being in her class. Good electives to take!

It's a class that benefits from being online. Though material can be tedious to complete grading is very forgiving as Dr. Simon's goal is to teach not to trick. A lot of reading and a lot of watching videos.

Content wasn't difficult but he just replays old lecture podcasts in lecture. Made class difficult, was hard to understand because of chronic throat problem and also didn't write clearly on chalkboards. Class was just frustrating but he seems nice.

The homeworks assigned are not very relevant to the exam topics. The problem sets handed out in discussion are also not very relevant and much more difficult than the exams. He posts practice exams which are relatively similar to the real deal, but sometimes puts really difficult questions that even TA's think are too hard.

The first five weeks of the class are a review of Calculus 1. The last five are "new" topics that you can just watch Bower's videos for. Practice midterms and final reflect the actual exams almost identically. Got away with not attending class at all and just watching Bower's videos a few days before an exam.

A few days before classes started he told us he had chronic throat soreness and only played videos in class. His videos were pretty hard to understand, so I stopped going to lectures and only watched Prof. Bowers's videos which were rlly helpful.
Had a throat infection so he didnt speak. Practice exams exactly like exams. he seems nice but didnt teach at all, dont take him if you struggle with math. attendance not mandatory.

Late to every lecture, strict / high expectations on following directions to a T even tho they were extremely disorganized and unclear. Loved Professor Davis!!! Her work is not as much as people say it is! Lots of group projects though. DEI, don't take this course

She is so amazing. Literally the most understanding person I have ever met. She will make you love the class and make you want to take her again.

Very caring professor who incorporates current real world issues into lessons. Some group work and sharing with your neighbor in class, but there is an option to work alone for the final project. Master of deception on world issues.

Get ready to complete the small assignments that are assigned almost every week as they serve as a crucial component of your grade. Visit her office hours since she is flexible on regrading and accessible outside of class.

Tricia is great! She is extremely knowledgeable and so much experience to back her up as a lecturer. Her workload is easy for SOCI but there is a lot of group discussion as it is also an EDS class. He skips lectures without prior announcement. He also says he'll post the lectures he missed but never posts them. The midterm also had two whole problems with wrong numbers that left me confused.

This class is no walk in the park. Make sure to attend every lecture and take notes or you will suffer because most of this stuff will not come intuitively. The professor cares about the student's understanding when he explains things in class and explains concepts/train of thought mostly clearly. Pros: Clear and logical board work. Very responsive to students outside of class and actively adopts our suggestions. Homework is well-targeted and helpful. Generous implicit curve. Nice taste in sunglasses😎

Cons: He has an accent, and sometimes it feels like he is mumbling or talking to himself during lectures.

He puts a lot of effort and energy into his lectures and makes sure you understand. Get ready for a lot of class discussions and youll have one written midterm and then a project. He doesnt use canvas much and will have you use a journal (he gives you one if you need it)

Awesome professor, guides you through the content and is very genuine. Is super up to date on announcements and information, very clear guidelines and rubrics. Would recommend for a genuine learning experience without having to worry about unclear, harsh or ambiguous grading.

I loved this class. No exams, just readings, discussion posts, a presentation, and a really fun final project. Lectures moved a bit fast, but if you did the reading it wasn't a problem. This class has and probably will continue to be the bane of my existence. It is currently week 6 and this class has been the one thorn in my side all quarter. The quizzes she added this quarter are actually insane and completely untested in a way that I feel like we're her guinea pigs. No curves, no drops, just insanely specific fill in the blank.
Took her over summer. Course was great. Clear instructions, fair tests and replied to email immediately. I learned so much. Take her if you can.

Amazing course! A blend of microbiology and food. Not to heavy on the science, but enough to change your perspective of biology. Homework are inspiring. I learned so much about different cultures, their food and more about mine.

Take her for the Global Seminar in the Galapagos and Ecuador. Amazing experience! We saw places that I had always dreamed of. Did research at the Charles Darwin Center, visited the Amazon, saw a harpy eagle, pink dolphins, marine iguanas, giant tortoises. I will do it again.
She is great. Cares about her students. Exams were ok if you study every day. Sit in the first rows and find a buddy to study.

He's a nice person but his teaching style isn't the best. He talks really really fast and just super lecture heavy. He only grades 4 exams , his study guide didn't match his current exams and the study guide is outdated. I haven't received my grade yet .

Prof. Gentner is an incredible lecturer. His tests can be challenging, but you end up understanding neuroethology and ephys at a very detailed level. His class helped me connect concepts I've learned before like phase-locking and ITD. He is an engaged mentor and makes time to help students during office hours, even if it's not related to the class.

Grades only on exams, which are non-cumulative and occur after every 4 lectures. You need to study the material outside of class because just going to lecture will not be enough. Reading the textbook is helpful. He is knowledgeable but exam-only makes it difficult to grasp the material thoroughly.

I am writing this review before I get my grade so I am not persuaded to give a worse review than I want to. I really enjoyed this class and how the professor taught the class. I was very skeptical at first to take this class because it seemed like it would be too hard, but I enjoyed it! He made connections about the content to the real world.

Taking him rn, and it's actually insane. Midterms are 60 MC and his lectures are all over the place. He talks very fast and he kind of sidetracks the material. Like he'll talk about the material, but in a way that's not super straightforward, so you don't even know what's going to be on the test. There's so much to cover. Need to study all the time

pretty good for a GE. No exams but  6 pop quizzes throughout and a final project. The quizzes are pretty hard and based on his lectures (he does post slides and notes) but he drops one and the weekly activities and project check ins make up lots of your grade. The weekly stuff can be complicated but office hours can be helpful, with TA or prof.

I feel like he came to class with some small chip on his shoulder, especially when lecture attendance is low, that made me not enjoy the energy during lectures as much. There were some times that I saw a more positive, lighthearted side of him and I wish I saw more of that. I liked his jokes and his grading was fair and relatively easy.

Professor makes this lower division class much harder than it has to be. He does not care for his students and will not respond to emails regarding the class. No discussion section which makes the content very confusing. Would never take him again.

This course wasn't what I expected, which was shocking since it is a class primarily taken for GE requirements. First few weeks were astro-physics heavy, and the remainder was more so geology oriented. The 3 reports are time consuming, and group work is required. Prof. Stegman's lecturing style didn't work super well for me (a humanities major).

Pretty much everyone who would take this class is taking it for a GE, and that being said it was harder than expected. 2 Individual research papers 5+ pages, Final is a group project which is pretty cool. Weekly canvas quizzes worth the same amount as Lab attendance.
Denise is great! I have had her for 1A - 1D, she is a great professor. Participation and attendance is important but all the homework and word tests are really easy!

I took Denise for LIPO 1A-1C and absolutely loved her. She made class fun and interesting all while helping students make progress acquiring conversational Portuguese. Denise is an amazing person as well as an amazing professor that will work with you to learn the language.

soooo cute and soo fun. she would celebrate our birthdays in class and give us gifts. she would decorate the class for halloween and Christmas and gave us all goodie bags. we would do arts and crafts too. It was like being in elementary again.

professor was nice and very funny, but lectures were sometimes unclear. i learned more by doing the homework/going over notes on my own. that being said, going to office hours helped a lot. concepts could be hard to understand but once you get it, it's pretty easy

Amazing prof who I would recommend for any class he teaches lectures were easy to digest and left me feeling prepared for any future classes that might require this material also very sweet and more than happy to help with any issues that may arise.
Super nice guy, I love his deadpan style of humor, he's great at using analogies to make complex math concepts easier to fully digest

All his exams are FRQ. 2 midterms and he has a grading system which allows you to drop a midterm if your final grade with the better midterm score and your final score is higher than your grade with both the midterms inputted into the gradebook. Practicing the problems from the notes and discussion is enough to be ready for the exams.
Great lecturer! Straightforward and easy to follow. Exams are easier than the homework problems, so as long as you get in the practice you'll do fine in the class.
super easy to learn the content. pre-lecture readings to understand material and clicker questions for attendance for examples of the content. shes really nice and cares about her students.

The material was definitely difficult and time consuming to understand, but I kinda preferred the flipped classroom for practice problems. You have to focus on understanding her learning objectives and take advantage of office hours, the TAs and PLAs often explain the material in a more digestible way. Requires a LOT of outside hours though.

I agree with the other comments here about her tests (unnecessarily hard, discussion problem sets/in lecture problem sets are helpful for the formatting of the exam, BUT are not super representative of the content). You 100% teach yourself. She also has EC, but it's random surveys that are worth 1-2 pts. Writing assignments (3) are graded SO HARSH.

3 midterms and a final (can drop one of the midterms), but midterms are very difficult as there are many questions and are worded in a confused way, they take points off for basically anything they wish and the rubric seems arbitrary. homework at least every week with writing assignments, flipped classroom setting so you teach yourself, good ec tho

So much work, I went through long-term depression to the point she pruned my synapses, and I was hopeless. I'm in need of a calcium potion to revive my long-term potentiation at this point. I'm so burnt out, it is concluded there is no light at the end of the transducin.

Her class is really chill as long as you show up and take notes. Unfortunately a physical iclicker and the textbook is required but it may be doable without the textbook. Discussions also are mandatory, however I'd say they're pretty engaging. Overall, easy if you're good at memorizing content.

Loved this professor. You will need to buy a physical clicker to take attendance (which is mandatory), and you will also need to read from the textbook (which I didn't do and still passed, but I would still definitely recommend doing). Loved the way she taught and all of the topics in class. You will need to study a lot.

I took BILD 3 as one of my first classes at UCSD. She is an amazing professor who cares about what she teaches, and does all she can to help set us up for success in the course. Make sure to keep up with daily quizzes and do the readings, and use the learning objectives to study for exams! You can miss a certain amount of lectures!

Her lectures are amazing and the course itself is really easy. I didnt do any of the homework but still got an A since most of the content on the exam is lecture based. Get your attendance (for class and dis) and do all your daily quizzes and you are likely to succeed. She does not curve so know how many points you need for your exam and prepare.

Prof stockwell is super sweet and you can tell she genuinely cares for her students. Insane amount of extra credit (I got >100%). There is a decent amount of content but as long as you're on top of things it'll be fine. Go to office hours if you need help. The average for my class was a >B

Godula was a very nice professor but his notes can be scattered at times. Graded very leniently for the final exam. Will drop one exam as well. Final project given to get points back easily if the smallest amount of effort is put in. Midterms and final were also take home in Fall 2026. Would take him again in a heartbeat, kind and engaging.

Don't do it if you're an undergrad. A lot of prior knowledge is expected. Lectures are so incredibly hard to follow I would give up taking notes. Exams and homework questions are very random and difficult.

My jaw dropped when I saw such poor ratings for Dr. Godula. If you are a good student, he is an amazing professor. Do your work and stop pointing the finger at others. He is a great lecturer. He is kind. He hears his student. He is supportive! I was the least likely to get an A but he helped me learn and I got an A. Do your work and you'll be good.

Actually pretty easy for upper div biochem. Just go to lecture and collect clickers, and compile good notes for tests (They are online) Material is very specific and niche but thats the nature of the course. Interesting topics covered. Great lecturer, good delivery and energetic.

I personally hate this course since its a waste of time, but you can use him as a back-up at least or enroll with a friend.

Great experience. Doesn't assign all that much reading, but it's important for being able to participate in class. 2 big projects- an essay and a presentation- and he gives amazing feedback throughout an extended planning/revision process for each. Grades a lot on effort/participation, so just show up and be engaged.

One of the hardest classes I've taken, but the most rewarding class. For most weeks, you are writing an essay about the weekly reading . The essays have very clear grading criteria. Most of your grade is based on these essays and your participation in discussion section. She treats this class like a grad course, she cares a lot about your learning.
amazing professor. the lecture content is clear and the pdf is extremely helpful for me to understand everything she tried to explain.

The lectures were boring a few times with lots of information thrown at you. But, it was an easy course because everything was online and open note. Ensure to take good notes and you'll do good in exams. There was also homework every week but they were similar to midterm/final questions. Discussions also weren't mandatory.

Many things to learn, which for sure makes the course tough, but the lecture is engaging and she gives clear notes and slides to help you overcome the exams. It is the first biology course that I spend most of the time understanding instead of remembering. Homework is annoying but just do not use tools so you can learn much more.
She is a monotone lecturer. Everything you need to know is on the notes she provides.
Professor Lubarda does talk fast at times and the notes are lengthy. However, he is funny, explains well, and answers questions during lecture.

I took this course online(exams were in person) and I found him to be a very chill guy, easy to talk to and communicates efficiently. I found the course itself not intuitive and memorization heavy but I know a lot of people that found it very easy. The professor himself is a very good, effective teacher but the class he teaches is a headache.

For someone who has prior coding experience, this class was quite easy. No need to go to lectures, unless having the textbook repeated at you verbatim by a man with an Eastern European accent aids your learning. He is a very nice man but not a very good professor.

I didn't go to a single lecture and was fine. Easier if you have some background in coding, and tests are pretty much just semantics memorization, logic (for loops etc..), and paying attention to detail. Pretty easy for someone who didn't have coding background and tests are very crammable. Graded on very few things so you need to be precise.

Final and midterm were really easy since it was multiple choice, never went to any of the lectures. The grading for the homework is straight forward, class was easy for someone with a small background in coding. Overall would recommend, the majority of people passed.
The grading criteria is very clear, however starting this class out felt like being thrown in the water and being expected to swim immediately. Great professor but not a great introduction.

One of the best lecturers I've had at UCSD honestly. I came into this w/o much interest but it quickly became my fav. Midterm-35% final-50%. Both formatted T/F, short answers, and 1 essay at a set time on canvas for x time w/ open notes. Participation-15% need to come 7x for QR code. The only issue is he lectures rlly fast and is content dense.

His lectures are super organized, and he is super helpful. You only have to attend 7 lectures to get participation, and his midterm and final are online. He also gives a comprehensive study guide. As long as you go to the lecture and take somewhat decent notes, you will do well. He also rounded my grade up to an A- god bless him.
Tons of reading for each class, super dense material. Don't miss a lecture!

for online midterm and final, there are mcq's, saq's and essays. he releases a comprehensive study guide with possible questions before so do the whole thing since they verbatim show up on the tests. lectures not recorded, but you need to go to a certain number and says important info not on the bare slides. highly recommend, amazing class to take.
Nice professor, good lectures, easy class

Professor Payne is just one of those gems of professors that you'll get and you'll never want to take a class with anyone else. She's super caring about her students, responds to emails, her lectures and slides are very clear, and she's a super fun and bubbly personality. I always learn a lot from her classes too! Cannot reccomend her enough.
Study hard before midterms and finals and you will be fine. Discussion attendance mandatory (10% of grade)

I took SOCI70 was a very interesting class. Learned so many new things and was always engaged in the content. Professor Payne's teaching style is very energetic, and it's clear there is a passion to teach the material. Only 3 exams 2 midterms and a final, which were all really straightforward. Make sure to pay attention in discussion for an easy A.

I took SOCI 70 with Professor Payne (the course was not listed as an option to review). She was amazing! Her lectures feel like TED Talks-- so interesting, passionate, and engaging. Attendance wasn't mandatory, but you best believe I was SAT in Center Hall (all the way from seventh!) 2x every week. An easy A, too, as long as you do the readings.
Professor Ganesan answers questions during lectures with kindness and patience, so don't be afraid to ask if something is unclear.

The pace of the class is incredibly quick. The professor is not very friendly towards students and she is an OK explainer. She committed a lot of algebraic mistakes while doing examples and was unclear in some contexts. It gave me the vibe that she wanted to end lecture ASAP so she could go home or something.

I stopped going for lecture after week 3, course content is easy. Prof means well, and was a good lecturer, but went far too slow in class for me to pay attention. Homework does pile up, and late submissions is the reason I didnt get an A

She was trying to be helpful and indeed spent lots of extra time. However, I constantly went to her lectures and they were confusing. Frequent errors were made and they are always the most basic ones.

All notes and worksheets are posted decently. Past exams are posted for review. Lecture and notes are very clear. Homework is not heavy. Discussion is about doing worksheets, so I recommend you to attend. I went to all discussion and did all the worksheet and past exams, and the exams are pretty fair. Like her lectures and notes.
The homework instructions were kind of vague sometimes. However, Professor Bigham is enthusiastic and his lectures are intriguing!
Best teacher I had this quarter and the only class I would actually be happy going to. Very easy class and he wants you to get the best possible grade.
Just make sure you care about the topic because I found his lectures extremely boring.

In my opinion, lectures are useless and boring, but he takes attendance, and they count for grades. Your grade depends on your TA; all the work in this class is done in discussion: easy class, easy articles, easy assignments. A good chunk of our assignments were graded as complete/incomplete.
This professor was super flamboyant and creative, always showing up to class with amazing outfits! He is extremely cheerful and funny, with entertaining lectures and engaging classes.

he's a good professor, as a transfer it's def an eye opening uni class, nowhere near the difficulty of the cse 20 class i took at community. huge learning curve, use resources (TA's offer 1 on 1 tutoring so clutch) and study hard this class is not easy by any means. the lectures are easier than the actual hw and i def blacked out during exams. gl!

Real talk, Jones is the goat. His lectures are a bit fast, but he does go over everything and records his lectures. GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS!!! He is very helpful, and gives you clear and concise feedback for your work. Grading is clear, he doesn't usually curve. That being said, his classes shouldn't be taken lightly.

Hes a great professor with engaging lectures. The homeworks are graded strictly. The midterm is extremely easy but the final is challenging. He curves the class so even if youre getting points cut consistently in homeworks its not that hard to get an A.

Very helpful slides, let us print out our cheat sheets, HW (challenging but doable) could be done in groups and was a big portion of our grade, reasonable curve, took without prereq of CSE 20 (b/c not required for major) but still manageable

Great guy, great prof, great class! It was rigorous and decently challenging, especially the homeworks, but during OH he patiently guided us through finding the solutions. Exams are super fair. He offers extra credit if you need it. Very approachable guy, funny, and really understands class content and mathematical rigor.
Professor Kenworthy teaches you to question your assumptions and always check the evidence. This class will greatly improve your critical analysis and thinking.

Literally the most boring class of my life. No technology permitted for notes and professor has the most monotone voice and no slides. AND it's mandatory. Otherwise easy class. TA was kinda annoying and weirdly intense, a bit of a tough grader on papers but shouldn't be hard to get an A. Easyish A, Prof is a nice guy, but wow I dreaded lecture.

literally everything he says is wrong not even the exam prompts make sense because he teaches in such a distanced, objective, white man way. the entire class is him saying "um actually American society is getting better. be positive." while blatantly ignoring the horrific things happening to minorities here everyday. also boring. I learned nothing

I enjoyed coming to lecture because Professor talks about his own research which is definitely different from other sociology classes (which usually lecture off of history or others research) I found it to be useful to learn more about GDP, what can cause a GDP to go up or down, what makes a good society. Lecture Heavy but online quizzes and hw!

Such a boring teacher. really has nothing to do with sociology because its based on his own research. hes so monotoned and wont engage with us at all! the TA was so bad. she also had no idea what was going on and would also talk about her research! easy class though its 2 weekly quizes that are verbatim and 2 essays. take a different lower div!

I adore Prof. Sasaki and her course. It was manageable, with one to two asynchronous lecture videos a week (often no more than 10 minutes), and a required online discussion once a week. Her TAs were sweet and dedicated as well. Work was very manageable and actually interesting. This was my favorite class the quarter I had it, and I'm a STEM major!

Overall, an enjoyable and interesting class. Lectures were asynchronous, with a short video you had to watch every week. Graded on discussion attendance, 5 canvas quizzes, 3 discussion posts, and a final video project. Would definitely recommend taking for your GE!

This class is extremely manageable and the information is very interesting. The discussions are led by the TAs and they are very chill and light- just in place for students to ask questions and ponder the weekly topics in this course. I would highly recommend taking this course for DEI like I did! Also, the lectures are async and watchable whenever
The online classes are free. When taking the class, all video lectures were recorded, so taking this class is at the student's pace. Very good professor and would recommend!
very easy and manageable. we did discussion. discussion is mandatory with ta but they very cool and understanding. final is  a video but was also easy. an easy A.
The slides are lengthy. Professor Donald is caring and encourages students to be authentic and attentive to their well being.

Nancy was a very easy professor, but had some questionable teaching moments. Anth 10 is one of the easiest classes you can take, and Nancy is awesome. If you find anything related to climate justice intriguing, I highly recommend taking this class with her. Assignments are very easy and graded in a relatively timely manner. She doesn't ask for much aside from attention during class, making things very easy for students

She is SOOOO incredibly confusing. It may be just me, but the homework is confusing, the tests are confusing, her lectures are confusing, like what we are actually supposed to understand. Honestly you know its bad when even the TA and IA say that Professor Rana makes this class so much harder than it has to be and that she is so disorganized and not good at teaching to the point its makes them frustrated as well.

She is not good at teaching all she does is read her slides off do not recommend not even sure allowed to teach UCSD

Course had 4 quizzes, weekly HW, a final, and a group project. TAs and IA were not helpful, discussions felt pointless. No calculators allowed on exams. Did not follow syllabus and was disorganized wrong dates, information. Teach yourself.

Prof Groisman lectures as if you already know physics before this. For an intro physics course for bio students, that is not the case for everyone. This is why I do not like him, no teaching from the ground up. Make sure to actually get an understanding of the material, you will need to actually learn to get a good grade. Be on top of it:)
Boring guy but the class is fine. Lectures are impossible to listen to but if you understand the homework you will succeed on all the quizzes. 85% is an A so its pretty easy.

If you are comfortable with math, you will do ok. Uses iClickers for attendance and allows cheat sheets for the 4 quizzes and final. Lectures are dry and uninformative though, so be prepared to teach yourself all of the concepts.

Groisman was not the best choice for me as a beginner in physics/STEM. Lectures were challenging for me to follow along with since he taught without offering much background, fundamentals & explanations. I had to do a lot of work outside of class. Exams relied some on memorization, but one's dropped. Thankfully 85% is a A and there's extra credit.
Attendance not mandatory but iclicker was extra credit. Homework allowed multiple attempts and was very helpful preparation for quizzes and tests.

Such a fun teacher! You can tell that he loves what he does and knows what he is doing. Kenneth Anderson my goat

Knowing that many take this course for GE requirement and a P/NP, he was strict on phone usage and attendance, intentionally making the 3 hours on a Tuesday/Thursday night the worse nightmare in the whole week. Additionally, the comments that said 'he often ends lesson early' is definitely a myth.

Took his Black Music class at City College—loved it. He's knowledgeable, funny, and caring. Lecture-heavy, so take good notes. Make a shared notes doc with classmates at the start of the year in case of absences. You'll learn a lot—more white students should take his classes. I gained insight and perspective that stuck with me. Highly recommend!

i absolutely ADORE mr. Anderson. He fills his classroom with love and care and a lot of laughs too. It's like you know for sure that he would be there for you if you called him in the middle of the night. And he actually said that that has happened before. He's so amazing. He talks way too fast and just reads the slides or textbook instead of actually explaining the concepts or walking student through how to solve problems. Really bad
passive-aggressive

Prof is hilarious and genuinely cares about students. 6B is just time-consuming.

DO NOT TAKE IF EMPLOYED. Blazes through content with little explanation. Need help? OH is once a week and even worse its on zoom! Lectures for 10-15min then quiz.Hard to recover from mistakes. Cool dude though.

Mixed-bag... gives a good amount of EC, and quizzes are pretty straightforward. Final was definitely more difficult. Sweet professor, but her lab manuals and work on canvas are extremely disorganized. If you're willing to put in the effort, an A is very attainable. She drops the lowest exam and the two lowest homework assignments. Also gives extra credit on tests.
The queen of extra credit. She gives extra credits for each exam. She is nice and caring. I didn't feel overwhelmed as a student who is not good at science at all. Also getting A is pretty easy.

caring and great teacher. attendance is mandatory. grading on frq of exams is a little annoying but overall exams are fair. cheat sheet allowed for every exam. not that hard just make sure you try to actually learn the concepts, memorization is not enough.

V lecture heavy class, lots of content taught in just one lecture, and tested on a lot of details about it on exams. Grading structure is lenient tho with EC after every exam and dropped scores at the end of the course. I hadn't taken bio in a while so that's probably why the content seemed difficult but definitely took some studying. Good lecturer

This is a challenging class no doubt and he is not a great professor. However what you need to know is in the lecture slides verbatim. The examples he uses will be the same questions on the tests. Don't really bother reading the textbook so much as understanding the examples in lecture. Go to lecture, go to office hours, and yes he does curve.
Quite literally the worst professor in the history of professing.

The class is really hard, but he curves an extreme amount, and a lot of partial credit was given where it didn't need to have been. My one advice is that the lectures aren't that helpful, but the office hours are for both the TAs and professors are extremely helpful, so go to those if you have to choose one.
Wow… hey people. I knew 40b would be difficult, but not this much. This prof really isn't helpful and I don't recommend him at all. He was the only prof for fall quarter s

I'm not going to lie, this class is REALLY hard. But a lot of his test questions are examples from his slides. I really struggled in this class but going to office hours helps, and the curve at the end of the class really helps.
Great professor, great insight in optics, and grate lectures! Exams can sometimes be difficults, at least some questions, but overall, they are aligned with the class syllabus and materials.
The best class i took this semester. Deep insight in optics and made me decide to continue in grad school.
Too hard to understand his accent. In exam, he puts questions out of the syllabus he taught. Awful teaching
Prof. Kante has deep knowledge of the material and taking the class changed my choice and I will pursue optics in grad school.

Wastes so much time during lecture talking about unrelated things, flies through complicated material and his lectures are very hard to understand. HW is very difficult, takes 12+ hours each, and often on material barely mentioned in class. Exams are difficult, 3-4 questions and only 25% was on concepts we've gone over in class or in HW.
He is very good at teaching bad science.

I had the pleasure of being in Dr. Gabriel's masters program on Climate Science and Policy. He is well liked among my cohort and regarded as a great leader. Our summer courses with him were thoroughly enjoyable. If you get the opportunity to be in the MAS CSP program, TAKE IT. It's intense but you'll learn more than you ever thought possible.

Best professor I have ever had. More difficult than other WCWP classes but I'd argue its for the better since you are actually learning something for the class. Amazing person as well, makes the class personally engaging (he made it a point to know everyones names from the first class), cool person to talk to about other topics.
Amazing professor, I've never had a professor that cared so much about our own personal development rather than grading harshly than Prof G.

Amazing professor! I had him for a first-year seminar course on "happiness" and had a great time every class. He was very genuine, down-to-earth, and funny. In terms of the class itself, work/ reading was minimal and short journal responses were expected every week. Would highly recommend him/ any first-year seminar courses he offers!

Professor Gagnon is the sweetest and so genuine! it was a first year seminar so work was super light (only a couple of reflections). mostly based on the science behind happiness. "homework" includes short articles and videos for class discussion. a great class to destress from core classes. if you can i definitely recommend !

Professor Gagnon made me rethink how I write. The way he teaches his class is revolutionary, and his progress in contract-based grading, where assignments are either graded complete or incomplete, is fantastic. Faux-structured class: too many assignments & unclear directions. Randomly assigned group + TA is an absolute pain since it affects grade. Refused to let me switch and I lost points due to bad teammates.
Final exam grading was the worst I've ever seen: inaccurate grading and didn't approve regrade solely because I wasn't "close to a grade boundary"

The professor is very supportive and attentive to students. The class project is well-structured and closely reflects real-world SWE internship experiences. Class is not structured very well. Some TAs are good, while others don't provide prompt and constructive feedback. We didn't spend time with React as the previous class did, but instead made games for K-12 students using Konva.js. Lectures are mandatory and not very useful, while labs are busy work.
Very good teacher. Just give a least a little bit of effort and pay attention in class and you'll be fine.
Great professor, won't make you fall asleep in class.

Super sweet and funny prof, grade is based on completion of assignments, and as long as you put in a good amount of effort, you get full credit. If she doesn't think it's finished, you have lots of time to revise and get it turned back in. This class is what you make it

Super chill professor, easy class with light requirements. You choose what grade you want and complete whats asked of you. Just make sure you follow assignment requirements for the three projects exactly how she wants them. He's very much a "hello fellow kids" type of professor, which I'm sure many find refreshing, but personally I found it to be slightly too much. Love him as a person, amazing personality and funny character. Would not recommend taking his class if you like structure. LOVE LOVE LOVE RANDY!!!!! The tests are hard butttt everything on the tests are on his study list and he will only test you on what is on this list! He has so many resources and is very easily accessible. Yes, lectures are mandatory but you get to miss about 6 and going to lectures help! You have weekly quizzes but they're basically free points.

Randy is very funny and a cool guy. His lectures are very entertaining, but not organized or clear. His tests are brutal and make up most of your grade. Though there is a lot of work, she is fair with her prompts and discussion post. In other words, if you truly understand the materials, it shouldn't be too difficult for you, plus there was a fair amount of extra credits! ^^ 
I had to drop out because there is quite a substantial amount of reading, and the material is inherently hard to understand.

The lectures are just her reading off a script, and makes absolutely no sense. The first lecture had no context whatsoever and felt completely disorganized. Canvas and recourses in general are also so disorganized. Everything about her class is miserable.
I wish she had in person lectures. The zoom recordings are sometimes hard to hear. Otherwise, one of my favorite professors and some of my favorite classes that I've enrolled in!

Horrible! lazy prof that gives us old recorded lectures for us to learn and ridiculous questions and answer choices. One of the most understanding professors I've had at UCSD. You would have to put a lot of effort to not pass. Honestly not as bad as people say he is. Lectures are fast but there are podcast recordings. Midterms were literally just like the homework slightly changed up, so as long as you take your time to learn from the homework you'll do well. Would take again.

His teaching is unclear sometimes, and assumes you know a lot about C (at least the syntax) before you get into the class. He lets you choose the exam time, but assigns people a random time that I have clearly chosen to be unavailable during.

Tbh, this professor is the severest professor I have ever met. He made attendance mandatory during a summer remote session for both lecture and lab sessions. You have to actively participate during the session and respond to every question he asks. His homework is also tough, expecting you to program 20+ programming problems in C in the first week.

PA's bi-weekly, weekly labs, weekly quizzes, 3 tests. PA's could be resubmitted for credit and up to two test could be retaken during week 10 (in replace of final). PA's were pretty difficult, so I would recommend going to office hours as much as possible. Test content was really similar to PA content and quizzes. I learned a lot from this class!

His office hour are really helpful. As long as you make some progress, he can guide you neatly. Like a previous review said, his quiz is hard (median 30%), but midterm and final are better. Thinking and doing on and beyond HW problems is essential, as his tests are not in format similar to HW but still related in deep core. He also podcasts.

Zlatos is well known in the math department for having the most difficult 140 classes, and 140C was no exception. The class is difficult, but if you take advantage of the resources available (discussion, Zlatos' office hours, TA office hours), and put in the time to digest the material, you can do well. You will learn a lot in his class.

Horrible teacher. Lecture material did not prepare you for the homework and exams. Not sure why there is a good review about Zlatos considering that student got a C (if you got a C, does that really mean your teacher taught you well?)

He's a solid prof for this class. It was no easier than it should have been, but his lectures were, for the most part, clear (and if not, he records and usually makes sense upon a second listen), and homework decent length. Strict at times (no dropping homeworks or exams), but his performance expectations are quite realistic given the difficulty
Fair, Exam similar to and easier than HW.
PLZ NO. DONT. JUST DONT.
OH MY GOD!!! NO!!! PLEASE STAY!!! DONT TAKE THIS!!!

I really liked Dr J. She's kind, did well at at simplifying coding and showing us practical uses in bio, and gave us a fun final group project where we really had creative reign. Weekly homeworks, a few quizzes (no midterms), and the TA's were very helpful. I didn't try nearly as much as I should've, think it wouldn't be hard to get an A in here!

Professor Juavinett is amazing! She handled the pandemic so well and is super understanding. The class is lab report heavy but they aren't terrible, try and you'll get at least a B. Labs are done in groups and we do a group grant proposal at the end. I recommend this class! Love the class but hate working in groups so much.
Great prof! Taken 145 (neurobiology lab) with her as well as the neural data science course (BIPN 162). Both courses are engaging and teach you a lot.
Don't get me wrong. His lectures are wonderful so that it is worth going despite he does podcast. Hardwork is of course expected for this class, BUT it will be rewarding.

Class is straight to the point. Grade consists of three memos, group presentations and closed book midterm/final. Downside; rude and has yelled at the class for talking before a presentation, but not many people talking. Could've approached it differently. Regardless, if you're ok with group presentations & closed book exams, take her, its doable.

Don't reallt enjoy his teaching style. Quizzes aren't based on understanding, but moreso, your ability to not get tricked by random things. I feel like they hardly measure how much you know in the class.
Run!! Bad classes, weird accent. Wouldn't take again.

Even though I skipped alot of my lectures (despite being mandatory), when I went, he makes all the content clear and concise to us through prewritten notes with additional commentary and code that he handwrites during lectures. Projects aren't super difficult and redundant, you just need a good idea of Java logic to understand most of the content.

Great lecturer who knows the material well, but workload can be somewhat busy with PAs every week and zybook readings. He's very patient and answers questions clearly. Overall a great professor to introduce you to data structures. The notes template he provides is also helpful.

I'm not going to lie, I skipped a lot of the lectures even though they were mandatory (you need an iClicker). But the ones I didn't skip he was a great help. He's great with questions and really wants you to understand the concepts. It also feels like he has a good grasp on the material and how to help students understand the concepts.

He is very knowledgeable and brings unique real-world experience. What truly sets him apart is how much he cares about students beyond academics, like sharing networking resources, career advice, and genuine mentorship. He's also fun and approachable, often sharing movies and places to explore in the new city with the class.

Professor Cohen was a good professor and lecturer. The exams were a little long but fair. Discussion section is not mandatory but definitely recommend to attend. Also, going to office hours and his review sessions were very helpful. O-chem is hard regardless of the professor, you just have to put in the work and you will be fine.

Professor Cohen is truly the best professor I have had at UCSD. It is clear how passionate he is about Chemistry, and his teaching style reflects that. His lectures are engaging, and he allows many opportunities for participation throughout the course. His exams are fair, and if you go to lectures and follow his advice, you will do well!

Prof Cohen genuinely cares about his students & puts in the time/effort to make Ochem click. Its a hard subject (you're gonna have to accept that) but he makes it manageable and even kinda fun. I used to hate chemistry, but he really did change my perspective. Plus he puts consistent effort towards learning everyone's names, which is really sweet!

One of the greatest professors I've had so far. Very passionate about the subject and makes an effort to get to know his students. He shares a lot of analogies and uses his molecular model kit to simplify hard concepts which helps a lot. He also holds exam review sessions that are helpful and exams are pretty reflective of problem sets.

Genuinely the best professor ive ever had the joy of taken. Extremely passionate in his work, made every single lecture interesting and engaging, wonderful funny and kind guy, labs were kind of tedious with the work but was feasible every time. I miss this guy. Take him if possible.

One of the best professors I've ever had. Cares about what students are interested in learning about and what students struggle with. His lectures are amazing; very informative and descriptive. Nothing about this course was difficult to me in any way.

I took his GS(global seminar) class when studying abroad this summer. He 100% meets the expectations that r written everywhere in any ratings students give him. He made Switzerland fun; I recommend it for students to go there! iI happy I'll still have close ties with him/his wife- they r AMAZING PPL!!

Very passionate about his subject. I took his seminar on rocks and had a lot of fun. The assignments are just writing a bit about what you learnt every class and thats it. Doesnt take any time, just attend the seminars and you'll learn a lot
Just had to show up to class to get a P!
Great class to take for credit. Very manageable if you attend lectures, and he's really hot so that helps too.

Many of the test questions are information provided on his slides, and as the quarter progressed we mainly switched to online learning. I learned quite a bit on language policies in the overarching world here.

Prof was really invested in this course; it made a big difference in how much effort I put into the class. Lectures are sometimes hard to follow because he reads off the notes at the bottom of the PPT slides, which we can't read. Midterm & final were MCQs. Truly a prof that wants to teach and see students learn.
he cares about his students and teaches for more than just a paycheck, would take again

Professor McIntosh is very passionate about the class, making lecture entertaining and interesting. I would definitely take more classes with him if I could. Attendance isn't mandatory, lectures are recorded and posted on Canvas every day. Midterm reflects class material and is pretty straightforward. Overall a great instructor.

Tests were unnecessarily difficult and frankly he's just not a super nice person. Would always tell us we needed to ask more questions when the test averages were bad but would respond rudely to people when they asked things. He is clearly very smart and knowledgable about chemistry but it doesn't seem to transfer very well to being a teacher.

he's so rude it's actually hilarious. someone asked how to do the log of something and he said "what are you going to do this weekend? learn your logarithms" and someone was talking in lecture and he said "can I speak now?? okay?" anyways his exams were so hard. if you got a 33% overall you passed with a C- lol

lowkey take a different professor. Lectures aren't the best, and his tests were very hard. Averages for the midterms was around 40% and 50%. He does do grade replacement, if you do better on the final, but overall just take someone else.

He is a great professor but the exams are very difficult for the level of the class. VERY VERY heavy curves (35% and above) for the final grade passed. 35% was a C-. If you show up to lecture and to the review sessions you'll do just fine. Exams are practically almost identical to the midterm, with them just being rewritten.

wait i kinda liked him.. he explained the content well and did examples during lec so it wasnt bad. he also had review sessions before midterm/final that were helpful! the midterms are hard tho so u have to study but like that goes for every class so.. and also the final was so similar to the midterms that it wasnt too bad if u studied the midterms

Anna-Joy is very sweet but her lectures are very disorganized and it feels kind of pointless to be there, however attendance is required for the most part so you have to put up with it. Quizzes and writing projects were so easy, don't listen to the people who say this class has tons of assignments because the work was completely manageable.

It's my first time seeing such novel teachings. I enjoyed the fun exercises and creative writings. Some reading materials could be graphic to those who prefer a trigger warning. The quizzes weren't the best indicator of efforts as they were short and could be tricky. Last but not least I love my TA, she made me feel valued.

BEWARE. I have never poorly reviewed a professor but I felt the duty of a student to warn you. I know college is about a lot of work but I'm a third year and I have never received so much course work. Her class is very unorganized from her lectures to her overall canvas. She would oftentimes add things to assignments last minutes, study guides too.

I would not take her again. She would add things to already long assignments last minute. She's nice but her lecturing and structure of the course is highly unorganized. From canvas to the actual course work. The TA's are nice and helped a lot probably the best part of the class were the discussions.

I love Anna Joy, she is so sweet and this class is incredibly easy if you give at least 10% effort. The only thing I think is a "negative", is that lectures don't really matter. She is not a great lecturer, but she is a very caring teacher and if you go over the slides yourself, you'll be fine. You don't have to do the readings to do well.

Prof Pun is AMAZING! He uses the chalkboard exclusively, but for a class like 40B where all the content is basically mechanisms, it's super helpful to see his reasoning and follow along with him. His pace during lecture is perfect, he explains questions really well, and exams and problem sets are super fair. Can't recommend enough!
boring class and ineffective.

(Taken Winter 2025) Dr. Pun is kind and knowledgeable about the subject. Organic chemistry is DIFFICULT no matter the professor, so can't blame him for the tough material. He writes on the whiteboard which helps with speed. Only thing is sometimes he assumes students know more than they do. Fair curve for exams. Homework helps. MEMORIZATION BASED.

I think the people complaining about Andrew are people who just struggled because ochem is difficult in its nature. Andrew uses the chalkboard and draws out each mechanism so you know what is happening in each step. I hated ochem until his class. I learned so much, and I finally feel like chem, in general, makes sense to me. Also, fat curve in end.

He only chalks so the class may seem intimidating at first but eventually the content builds on itself and it all starts making sense. The first midterm scores were very low but improved by the time we got to the final. Classes aren't mandatory but go, and midterms/final do matter. I still got an A though despite failing Midterm 1. You learn a ton!
Best teacher of the WCWP series!
One of the best professors on campus, cares for students and their grades, as long as you put work in you can definitely get an A.

Really easy class and teacher. Contract graded and is really chill with late work and late attendance even if it violating contract. Genuinely a really nice person that assigns a reasonable amount of work that shouldnt take you more than 3 or 4 hours a week on average. Leaves meaningful feedback and puts effort into helping you improve.

Cares a lot about her students and gives great feedback on essays. Grading contract makes it nearly impossible to get a lower grade than you want. Would take this professor again for every WCWP course if I could.

Emma is a very nice instructor, she is caring, and just in general always comes to class with amazing energy. The class is fairly easy and simple, read/annotate, and write essays. Emma makes writing easy as her feedback is nice! So if you struggle with writing, Emma's feedback will help you become better at doing so.

The course focused heavily on Universal Design, which felt unengaging and not very practical for an introductory English class. The instructor was friendly, but grading was very strict and closely tied to the rubric, with little flexibility despite a relaxed tone in class

She is a nice person, and the class is pretty easy, but the class is very uninteresting and barely focused on learning about writing. She spent a large chunk talking about Universal Design and accessibility in class design, which seems very random until you realize that she used to work in design accessibility (which she actually cares about).

Prof. Martiniuk tells you everything you need to do to get an A! The workload isn't too bad, so as long as you keep up and be mindful of deadlines, it will be fine. There's also revision opportunities! She's also super nice and understanding as long as you're reasonable! :)

Dr. Martiniuk is a very caring and sweet person, but overall, I'd say she is pretty tough. DO NOT MISS CLASS. I missed 6 and got a B- ToT . If you miss two or turn in your readings late, you will not receive an A. Overall, she's a good professor, but she's very strict with her syllabus; also, you can miss up to two classes.

Professor Martiniuk is a great teacher. The work is not hard at all, and she gives feedback quickly, which then gives you the opportunity to resubmit the assignment for full credit. There are readings due before each class, but they are fairly easy to get through, it takes 30 mins max to get it done. Highly recommend taking this class with her.

Very interesting class. It is a fundamentals class, but I believe that you needed to at least have some sort of grasp on technique, like video editing and camerawork. Professor Kroopf is very accepting, inclusive, and also well-known in his field. He fostered an environment where everyone actually talked to each other.

Her class is highkey awesome. Huge precurve. Detailed, organized lectures with slides available. Down to Earth. My only issue is the grading scheme. You can get literally everything right on a test and still lose point bcs u didn't specify sumn on a graph. That bothered me heavy. But I genuinely feel like a pro at thermodynamics.

super unorganized , doesnt upload test solutions, she is always late, one time she was 40 minutes late to a 50 minute lecture. Midterm hasnt been graded and is in less than 24 hours and we took it 2 weeks ago.

I honestly don't get how she has such good reviews. I had to TEACH EVERYTHING TO MYSELF. THE LECTURES ARE JUST HER WRITING ON THE BOARD AND GRADING IS EXTREMELY HARD. Thankfully there is a curve, but she just killed all the excitement I had for this class. Definitely not prepared at all. she's a good person, but awful teacher.

Professor Nomura has improved since last quarter in MAE 11. Her teaching style is great, and she often yaps topics out of the scope of the course. Her procedural techniques should reflected on homework and exams for success. Highly recommend taking MATH 20E, MAE 30B, and MAE 131A before this course.

Never had a worse professor at UCSD. We just got our midterms back and she said that the class average was a 55% (she said she will not curve). I don't understand why there are so many high reviews because I've talked to so many people and all of them only have bad things to say about her. Terrible professor and I will not be taking her ever again.

Professor Stone brings a lot of insight to the class. I've always learned something new after every lecture! Attendance is mandatory, and the writing assignments are pretty simple and straightforward. Make sure to pick your sources well!

Professor Stone was an exceptional educator with a keen eye for detail. Her thoughtful language made complex historical events engaging. However, one TA, James Diokno, grades harshly and is biased. Look up RMP for him as well. To avoid poor grades, it's best to align your essays with his expectations, even if it means compromising truthfulness.

Professor Stone is very passionate about what she teaches. I received helpful and constructive feedback on my essays, and I learned more about race than I thought I knew before. Extra credit is offered during lecture, whether it be through optional reading quizzes or participation. Exams were open book. Make sure to put time into the essays!

All of the homework, tests, and essays are about lectures and the reading. Though the work itself is very easy and manageable I think my TA was a bit harsh on the grading. I often felt pressured to lie about my opinion of things because if I didn't agree with something it would affect my grades. I did not feel comfortable in this class.

I shared my experience with American culture as an immigrant (we were talking about different cultures in the U.S) She basically told me to stop talking and it very much gave "your story doesn't matter because you don't look like what I think immigrants look like" I never went back. Her TA is amazing I don't think he likes working under her though
This class is online, and the lectures were straightforward! Grading criteria was also clearly outlined. Make sure you get a good team and submit assignments on time.

This was a fine class, but incredibly disappointing. The class is online and the TAs grade brutally and provide you with zero rubric. Class is simple, but you gain little learning and 50% of grade comes from a final project w/ minimal instruction. Incredibly frustrating and feels super slimy. Don't provide 0 educational value and then tank a grade.

Was a fairly chill class, You have 1 maybe 2 individual assignments, all the rest which is like 1-2  assignments per week, usually 1, are all group activities, that you really only need like 1-2 people for. If u need the credit take it.

It's a fully remote easy course but not well executed by the instructor. The lecture presentations lack a logical flow, coherence, and many concepts are out-dated.  Overall there's a feel of hastily done lectures with an apparent disengaged attitude toward the students. The professor does not respond to student's emails. Take it for an easy A.
Everything people say about him being lazy and vague is so true. He also spams your canvas inbox like crazy because his course isn't well structured. Easy A tho

Way too much reading, just know the general concepts for the quizzes. Discussion attendance is mandatory and the grading on your writing relies heavily on your TA. It's a class you don't need to stress for and it does get interesting at times, however I don't think the lectures were helpful for me.

The class is quite dependent on the TA; the lectures are slow but cover interesting topics. Lots and lots of readings. The quizzes are pretty easy, Professor Wilson gives a nice and helpful study guide to help prepare for them. 6 total 300-word blog posts you have to do throughout the quarter. One group project in discussion. Discussion = mandatory

There are a lot of dense readings for this class, but Professor Wilson is great at incorporating a summary in her lectures that helps solidify your understanding. The lectures were sometimes a little dry and to the point, but they helped me learn. I liked how she posed questions to the class and encouraged participation.

The class is very easy, but there is SO MUCH READING. You don't need to know specifics for the quizzes / final, just general concepts. You must do 6 , 300-400 word writings throughout the quarter. Discussion is mandatory with a group project. Lecture isn't recorded but I'd argue you don't even need it as it is just expanding on the readings.

Yes, this class is a lot of work, and a LOT of reading, but I liked the challenge. The concepts I learned in this class have literally changed the way I view history. Dr. Wilson is VERY passionate about what she teaches, which I LOVE. She connected me with the Global Health department, too! If you participate and do the readings, you will get an A.
Highly recommend.

Coming in with previous coding experience certainly helps, however, I think if you work hard you can learn it quick enough. Importantly, he emphasizes how different concepts work together. He provides the textbook which there are online quizzes for but they're easy if you do the reading. Exams are fair and open book/notes. Highly recommend.

I had taken a circuits class before, but many concepts were still unclear to me. He explained them so well that I finally understand them now. If you start the practice exams early and well before the quizzes, you will do fine on the exams. His lectures are engaging because you actively solve problems and get direct feedback from him.

Conceptually difficult and the tests are hard, but Curt does a great job of giving students all the resources they need to succeed. Whether that be constant tutoring hours, tons of previous exams to study with, or his bootcamps. If you can manage your time well and study effectively, you can do well. If you only try to memorize, expect to fail.

His lectures and practice exams are really helpful. He is also willing to help you with any questions during office hours. However, the work is really fast paced and challenging even though I had some programming experience.

Don't listen to all the bad reviews. Yes, she discourages using devices in class, but if you are engaged, she won't care. Sometimes the rate my professor reviews are spot on, in this case, i dont think so, their is probably some credence to others' experience, but if you need this class for a credit, take it!

Take McKay. Her class is way easier and there is no group project to sabotage your grade. Meyer was nice to me, but I would like to think it was because I participated. She was a bit odd, but also nice and caring. She asked all of the students who stayed after the final to get coffee with her, she is better than the reviews make her seem.

MGT 119:super disorganized since she taught this class for the first time as an undergraduate rather than graduate course, can be rude and impatient with students, can be a pretty harsh grader when the assignments we're given aren't even fully clear in deadline, rubric, or point of them in terms of the class--  but the people in the class are great

She's emotionally volatile. Don't talk to her if she's in a bad mood (you'll be able to tell very easily). I haven't heard of a good office hours experience with her. Class holistically isn't hard, BUT she's very strict about very particular things (no devices, sentence count). Write the max amount the rubric asks, and over-explain every answer.

This class is an easy A, if you're of particular race (car color) that she likes (She's a Nascar racer). If your car aint white, you ain't right is her philosophy. I actually learned a lot from her class, I learned that

He never gave enough time for quizzes or knowledge checks, and he would make us read textbook chapters and complete homework before class (I'm not against that) but then just copy and paste the textbook into his lecture slides. And then made attendance mandatory. It was strange and not a good use of flipped classroom. TAs are really helpful
Nope!!!!! Nope Nope Nope, rethink before you take this professor.

Grade consists of 4 quizzes, 2 exams (final non cumulative), weekly homework and knowledge checks. Lectures not podcasted and attendance was taken in class through knowledge checks. The lectures were mid, sometimes boring. I studied a lot and did good on Exam 1 and most of the quizzes.

You have 20 minutes to answer 12-15 questions that can take up to 5 min to answer on the quizzes. Lecture is mandatory but learned nothing from it. Most learning came from the SI sessions. UCSD better hire more professors to teach this class.
This guy is terrible gives out quizzes and test like theres no tmwr and makes them extremely difficult. Dont take him
Prof Kidman is incredibly engaging, knowledgable, and fair. Workload is super managable. Would definitely take her class again

Don't listen to the reviews below about her not caring. That's just false. No, she isn't the greatest prof i've ever had, but she's definitely passible. Graded on 3 midterms and a Final Reflection. Part 2.  On top of that, she laughed in one of my classmates face when told that she wanted to pursue journalism.
