In the beginning of the quarter, the professor was very positive and ready to teach the lectures, however not even a month in she turned very negative and rude, and stayed that way. Genuinely have not met a professor so pessimistic about our careers, telling us it's pointless to be a communication major as they are no jobs in the future for us.
Genuinely one of my favorite COMM profs at UCSD. She's so knowledgeable and her lectures are incredibly engaging. Truly a one of a kind professor.

10 quizzes and a final (lowest quiz dropped). The class is curved a lot at the end by 10%. He worked hard to even bring previous Nanoengineering graduates to tell us about industry. Lots of the reading but the textbook is very clear and the AI tutor makes things even clearer. Quizzes were exhilarating. Overall, it was a rollercoaster of fun!

The class requires a lot of reading but it really isn't that hard if you just read the section twice and do the practice problems he gives you. He gives good explanations in class but you will still need to learn on your own. The curve is really heavy (~10%) so don't worry too much.

Interesting prof, but the course design is deeply flawed. Expectations far exceed what is explicitly taught. You self-teach from a poorly written, sometimes inaccurate textbook and an ineffective AI tutor. 8 quizzes (lowest dropped), some cumulative. TA grading lacks consistency. Prof OH and problems are the main sources of clarity. Some ECt.

Lectures were often hard to follow without prior prep, so learning the material independently took a LOT of extra time and work, which felt excessive for an intro class. Weekly open-response quizzes were poorly aligned with lectures, and in-class explanations were often unclear. The textbook content was interesting but VERY challenging.

Prof is very nice and passionate about helping students but class was too difficult for an intro course. Lectures were not helpful and you learn only through the dense textbook (50ish pages per week). AP Chem, Phys, Calc are an unofficial requirement. Harshness of grading is dependent on the TA, but the median is adjusted to match previous year's.
I cannot recommend Harb enough. His lectures are enaging, clear, and well organized. The workload is fair and super manageable. He'll never try to trip you up!
Manageable workload, and engaging lectures. There are weekly journal entries, and some writing assignments, but they are not difficult. There is no final.

Super fair class. All you do is just make sure you do the readings. Everything was take-home, except one in-person final, which consisted of T/F, multiple choice, and some short answers. You actually had to try hard not to get a good grade. TAs were helpful and gave good feedback, and were clear about the grading criteria. Would def recommend him.

Ok class with an Ok professor. You DO have a midterm exam which was a new add to the class and was lowkey hard. My TA never responded to emails so I was left on my own. Prof Harb is very politically motivated and pushes a lot of bias'. Class was mid. Wouldnt take again because he is just so politically focussed in a comm class. Also hella boring.
Great lecturer, very engaging, you should read everything, but the lectures pretty much cover everything. Work wasn't very difficult. I liked it!
Such an awesome professor you will not regret taking him !!

He's awesome! He is super funny and nice. He can be very quiet so BE PREPARED TO LISTEN! Otherwise no complaints!!! Weekly quizzes and written assignments, but they are easy as long as you pay attention to lecture and read! The tests are super easy and very similar to the quizzes. Material workload may seem intimidating but they really aren't :)
This professor has changed the way I view the world. His lectures truly changed my way of thinking and perspective on others. I could not recommend him more. He is so funny and I loved his class.

Please take a course taught by Dr. Dykmans. His class was the most enjoyable and eye opening course Ive ever taken! Prof Dymans has a great sense of humor and you can feel his fun personality and passion in his lectures and slides! I learned a lot, laughed a lot and had fun EVERY lecture. Show up, study the slides and you're golden!

Great professor for it being an online course! We were to submit a super easy and short assignment weekly, quizzes were short and simple & test are based off a lot of the requiered readings, quizzes and lecture videos. Overall, super easy course and great professor!

Paula Saravia is one of the best professors I've had at UW, she is very caring and understanding, which is very much needed for an anthropology professor. When you sign up for an anthropology class, lots of readings should be the expectation, especially when the course is on a particular anthropological subject that requires supplemental content.

Genuinely one of the best professors. She has such an incredible way of navigating class discussions. She is so caring and so respectful of everyone. Her lectures are interesting, and she made the class enjoyable.

Boring, I wouldn’t take her again tbh. Depends on the TA for her grading. Didn’t go to any in person classes LOL but I could still take the exams/ and write the papers. Her rubric isn’t always clear and when I asked her for clarification on the final, she said how she couldn’t help…

Awful the midterm and essay portion was extremely confusing, she doesnt know how to word her essays and does a terrible job at explaining her point. Lectures are boring and she needs to do better as a professor in terms of lecturing and doing a better job at wording her essays I dont ever understand what shes trying to get us to discuss.

Very disorganized and confusing class, mostly because there were no guidelines and ambiguous instructions for everything. The exams are very difficult for no reason, often covering material that was never taught - she then blamed the class for the low test scores. I would avoid her at all costs and only take her as a last resort. good luck

This guy has genuinely had me crying-laughing during class before on several occasions. He's so eccentric, but if you actually listen to him, he is saying some important stuff that everyone needs to hear. I need to smoke with him. Please take his class its the easiest A you'll ever get and just a hell of a time.

Pablo is very eccentric and if you haven't had him before it will catch you by surprise, but he is incredibly kind and caring and wants the best for his students. He keeps the class fun and the workload light so that you can enjoy it without adding to much to your plate - it was the perfect course for my final quarter. Attend class if you can!
HE IS GREAT! MY FAVORITE PROFESSOR. SUPER CARING AND FUNNY.

Dr. Torres is AMAZING, I felt class is worth attending, always left class feeling that we deserve to take space at this institution. Class is straight forward, his summer session only requires 4 weekly reflections that is based on effort and completion. No doubt he LOVES what he does and tries to radiate that energy towards his students. LOVE HIM!

All around, Professor Torres is an incredible Professor. His care and interest in his students and the material he teaches are unmatched. This is my third time taking one of his classes, and that is because he is a genuine and unique Professor. I have nothing but amazing things to say about him, and I highly recommend that people take his classes.

This is my 2nd time having Tsai and he does just NOT teach at all. Barely passed the 1st time. Expects you to have essentially learned everything prior to lecture. Workload is EXTREMELY annoying (pre-reading assignment before EVERY lecture + weekly hw) and clearly doesn't realize that students are taking more than one class! Do not recommend AT ALL

He is super organized and has a lot of resources for students to use, including explanations of every concept and equations. He also has extra credit and quiz/hw drops which gives us extra boost in the grades. His lecture slides are very neat and easy to read, I was able to use them well even after class

Professor Geller is an amazing professor. Her courses are very straightforward and if you apply yourself you will do well. She cares so much about her students and it shows.

P/NP 1-unit, professor is very caring.

No curveball exams, but they take a lot of studying to understand overarching concepts. Barton is also just a good guy who cares about his students' engagement with their major and has open office hours at SIO.

Andrew is a great lecturer and i believe covers all his material in detail in lecture time. 70% of your grade is from exams but they were mostly MCQ and pretty simple and straightforward. Attendance is mandatory for lecture and discussion so be prepared. Overall, i would recommend.
oh my god this was the worst experience that I could ever have in UCSD.................................like PLEASE DO NOT TAKE THIS PROF for real

his class is unbelievably unorganized. he's making up the structure as he goes, which in turn, leads to a mess.

homeworks were given extensions which was nice, but what was on the homework doesn't reflect on the exams. difficult relational algebra stuff covered in class was not on the exams.

everything is chaotic. don't take

In 4 years of (very difficult) Math and CS coursework at UCSD, this guy is the worst prof I've ever had. Constantly condescending to students in every lecture, exams are ridiculously unachievable within the time constraint and cover things NEVER mentioned in lecture or homework. Zero practice problems or guidelines for exam content. AVOID!

awful af. do not take. wants very specific things in his assigned project assignments but when you try to ask questions about what he wants, he says "you are asking for answers now" if the project is not as open-ended as you claim it to be, then give us specific directions like bffr
it's a miserable experience to take his class......

He's a very passionate and funny lecturer, but doesn't record them so you must show up to class to watch. Attendance mandatory, but you get a lot of skips. Grade is based on 4 in class quizzes worth 20% each, with a final exam and attendance making up the rest. You need to do the readings if you want to get a good grade.

Professor Fulkerson's lectures are very entertaining and informative. He explains things in a digestible manner. The concepts are easy to grasp and don't go very in depth. All of the material is given thru the lectures so it is difficult to recover from missing a class. Tests were pretty easy. Would recommend as easy credit for psych majors

Had him for Philosophy of Psychology, great lecturer. The readings could get a bit long and dry at times, but the course content itself is quite interesting. Grade is based on attendance, four quizzes one course content that are graded leniently, and a final paper.

He makes lectures really engaging and entertaining. Definitely makes the confusing topics he teaches easier to understand. He gives many recourses and is super accommodating. He's one of the best professors I've taken at UCSD, you can really tell that he cares.

Moral Psych (phil 137)
Professor Fulkerson is an incredible teacher and thinker. Unlike some teachers who have ultra strict class structures with rigorous timelines to meet certain material thresholds, Dr. Fulkerson takes his time to discuss with the class and engage in real time philosophical thinking. He is also just a nice human being!

Prof Willdonger is one of the few professors at UCSD who genuinely seems to want to teach. She has a very refreshing attitude and makes it so that everyone can succeed. The exams are identical to lecture / discussion material.

I love Dr. Willdonger! She is so caring and genuinely tries to keep lectures interesting, but you do have to take a lot of notes. Tests are based on lectures and homework almost word-for-word, so study the material and you're all set!

Great lectures, he was incredibly invested in the class and theories, which I appreciated. 2 MCQ quizzes (midterm & final), which had lots of questions like: "if x says y about argument 1, then what of the following options are not part of x's criticisms of 1?" :(

Amazing lectures and visual aids that make the topics clear and easy to follow. Graded on two quizzes and two essays, with a lot of reading assigned. Attendance only recorded for discussions, but lectures help a ton with the material. The TAs were excellent as well, highly recommend Prof. Roeder

He's a very effective lecturer and makes complicated material easy to understand, but he's not particularly engaging.

The class isn't hard but it's not an Easy A, per say. Your grade is dependent on four things (2 essays, 2 quizzes), so you have to do well on everything. The quizzes are tricky but accurate reflections of lecture content

Prof Roeder was great! Lectures can be a little monotonous but are very clear about exam content. Quizzes are difficult but curved and graded readings mitigate them. You're only graded on readings, 2 essays, and 2 exams. Very accessible outside class! Make sure you have a good TA because the readings can be dense and difficult.

Great professor! neat slides that do well in helping summarize information. Slides are bare, write down most of what he says aloud/rewatch his podcasted lectures to get a good understanding.  quizzes should be taken as if they were midterms or finals, you cannot just skim. rewatch podcasts! Two easy essays and easy weekly readings.
I didn't go to a single lecture and everything was online and it was really easy but just time consuming

Didn't learn anything from the lectures, but great study hall time! Random extra credit just for attending lecture, breeze of a class. Prof gives extra credit at the end of the quarter if you participate in class often.

Professor Laske is amazing! There is a weekly quiz through canvas, not hard at all. She gives a pop quiz like once a week for extra credit and it is very easy. Homework takes a long time but is not hard, she has a video that you watch that helps answer them. No midterm or final, so I don't mind homework. Definetely take this class!

This class is really, really boring and time-consuming. The weekly homework has almost 50 questions, and most are stuff like "what is the name of the elementary school in this news clip" - which gets frustrating. Professor Laske is very nice, but she makes the class so complicated for no reason.

Attendance is not mandatory but quizzes are given in class once a week for extra credit. There were no midterms or finals but weekly tests that were taken at home and one beach project. Homework was weekly but she provided a video explaining how to do each question and where to find the aster! Overall fantastic class and wonderful professor.

omg i hate codon... idk why any prof would use it since you cant review the questions you answered (unless i'm missing something??). anyways she rlly encourages you to go to OH but idk something about this class is just hard. and do not take this class if it's a 3hr!! you will fall behind! also no textbook which sucks if you learn better by reading

Lecture style was kinda confusing as most concepts were introduced through examples. Before lecture you MUST read prior knowledge that she posts on canvas, or else you'll be lost. She adjusts the grading scale so it's not difficult to pass, though I did have to study every day to achieve an A. The only annoying thing was three assignments weekly.

Honestly shes not that bad, tests were rough at times but codon is a life saver. Yall just need to actually put the effort into going to office hours and studying the material. She gave so many chances for ec so… that's on yall ….
Unclear syllabus, harsh grading, unclear grading rubrics, no extra credit, no curve

Lectures were straightforward and answered questions clearly. Lots of hw + online quizzes, but codon hw and class practice was very helpful and reflective of exams. Final was harder  but nothing we didn't cover. Recommend doing the extra pre-class readings/vids in order to succeed. No curves but has drops, multiple grading schemes, and bonus points
It's very simple. Even I, a Chinese person who isn't good at English, could get an A. He also doesn't mind if you use translation software.

this class was honestly life-changing. you do need to buy a course reader from the bookstore (around 50 bucks). reading material is fairly easy and we'd discuss readings for the week during class. essays are creative in nature. you can tell that prof. twohig truly cares about the class and his students. one of the best professors at UCSD!

GOATed professor. You get pretty short yet insightful readings and videos, then you discuss them in class. Work otherwise is just a few essays and two weeks of journaling. In-class lectures are always interesting and engaging if you participate, he makes it easy. You do have to buy his course reader and a graphic novel from the bookstore.

Probably one of the most considerate and insightful professors at UCSD. Wasn't expecting much from this class rather than a requirement, but really changed my perspective in a lot of good conversations and 80 minute classes feel very short. You have to talk in class but all conversations are applicable so it's easy to converse! 10/10 recommend.

His class is an easy A and there's a bit of reading few writing assignments. Other than that, this was hands down one of the best and most inspirational classes I've ever taken. I'm glad I took it when I did, I needed this class. He made the class feel like a community and he is such a caring professor. This is a rare gem of a professor.

There are two weekly reading questions, but they are graded for participation. The midterm and final are mainly mcqs with extra credit questions. You can find the quizlet for both the midterm and final. Lectures are also recorded. Would recommend this class!
He just thinks he's god bro
Has great stories to tell! Lectures were not mandatory, but I would always go because of the entertaining and informative lectures.

Arguably one of the best instructors at this school, extremely passionate about anthropology and can make it relevant to kinda whatever you're interested in. He's Swiss so he's super candid just be ready for that, it's pretty refreshing but he definitely will get into topics other teachers are nervous about presenting
Astonishingly good teacher and shows you connections between things you never would have thought of, do the reading and be engaged and you will get an A
I took him for comm108, there were occasional readings. The final project was a group project. No tests or quizzes throughout the class. Easy and informational class, would recommend.

(For Comm 108D) He's very caring and is more interested in students actually learning, rather than memorizing topics for exams. The grading was mainly based on a group project and attendance. He uses email, not canvas, which can be hard to find things about the course, but other than that he is a great prof
Thoroughly enjoyed his class.
Amazing teacher. Gives good grades!

If you need to take a DEI course, this is the easiest one for sure! No midterms or finals, just a paper that is divided into 3 parts. You have to show up to discussion but its really not that bad. your only grade is your paper, attendance to discussion and a once a week question that you have to answer online.
GOOD professor! passionate! care about students, detailed and useful readings! you can learn a lot from his seminars! definitely take it again!

Great teacher, very passionate and understanding. Definitely a good teacher, I took him for ANSC 124 which is a very straightforward class. 2 midterms and 1 final, all are take home essays that you have 10 days to complete. Great guy, would 100% take his class again and will miss him after I am done with my final.
Great prof, recorded lectures, interesting topics, not too much work.

He's a very caring and kind professor who is passionate in what he teaches. My fav professor at UCSD. His classes are easy if you put in the effort. Graded by discussion posts, a midterm paper, and a final paper. The discussion posts are graded on if you tried hard enough, he'll give you a 10/10. The midterm and finals you need readings. Love him!

He's a passionate teacher who clearly loves to teach the material. This was an experimental class so the class was new, but there were weekly discussion posts and two papers, which count as the midterm and final. You just have to show you made the effort and tried, and he will be generous with the points. Do the readings for the midterm and final.
Only graded on two assignments, along with the midterm and final. Class was engaging, and grading was not so harsh.

Overall a decent professor who got us through the content. Attendance was not mandatory but it might as well be, lectures were not recorded and there is a lot of content in the lectures. A lot of assigned readings and TAs were a coin toss, but overall not difficult. Not many graded things, decent class for GE or DEI requirement

Prof Whitworth-Smith was a good professor. My main problem was that he rushed through lectures, making it easy to get sidetracked. I was able to pass with an A without doing most of his assigned readings. I don't recommend it, however. Overall, caring professor and easy class as long as you have a decent grasp of what's happening during lecture.

Prof WS is a great professor who encourages class participation during his lectures. He speeds through his lectures which can be annoying but the discussion sections and guest lectures can be fun and informative. He also allows a cheat sheet and will give a study guide before exams. His grading rubric is also very clear.

Good professor overall, I felt that the discussions were very engaging. Easy class, mostly straight memory, but lots of reading. You can easily get away with not reading most the articles by paying attention to lecture or watching a quick video talking about it.
Probably would have failed this class if I didn't read the textbook.

She did not understand the content and is dependent on the slides. Canvas was an unorganized disaster. Taught the second half of the class and my grade noticeably plummeted, however gives lots of extra credit and a generous curve. Easy class (3 mc exams, participation quizzes, 4 short hws) but would not recommend taking if she is the prof.

Do not take for climate change GE. Lectures were teachers spewing information. Hard to know what you needed for exams. Tests did not reflect what was taught. Trick multiple choice questions, purposely making it confusing. Promised a curve/adjusted grade boundaries but was none. Wanted to take because of interest in oceans but not what I expected.
had the class split with another prof and her midterm was nothing aligned with what she taught and you have a better chance of understanding the material with reading the textbook than her lectures
i had this class w her and aluwihare. gille was by far the worst of the two. when she took over, her lectures were very confusing and lacked a lot of detail. pls dont take

Exam questions are mostly from the textbook. First exam was easy, but he put a "pre-req" question on the exam in which I got wrong, and guess what got a D on the exam because of it. Second exam was really hard and average grade was around a 50. And yep, that's GG for most people and even with his final grade curve I got a D.

Graded based on 2 midterms and 1 final. If you messed up on one, you basically need to 100% the others just to pass. No curve or any adjustment, almost 40% of the class failed still nothing. HAVE to attend lectures for "bonus" questions, and no partial credits on "bonus" questions so you to get it correct.

will not taking any of his classes again, only thing he would do is rejecting you, no matter what you ask, i ask him to see my exams, no. I asked him if i could verfiy my final grade by knowing how does he handle the weekly bonus questions, he just gave me a simple: no, it's not possible. Lazy professor, takes weeks to reply, grading also slow.

ECE 272A teaches concepts that are fundamental to his research, and he explains the topics very passionately. He made me get interested in control theory. It seems like he put a lot of effort into his lecture slides, with every little detail explained clearly.

Also gives extra credit pop quizzes if you attend in-person and pay attention in class.
refuses to announce important class policies on canvas, gives extra credit assignments during lecture to increase the gap between well-performing students and poorly performing students

I loved Professor Pilegard! While her online lecture videos can be a little lengthy they're always interactive and engaging. The exam questions might seem a little difficult at first but as long as you are thoroughly prepared with the material and know how to apply it you should be fine. I would 100% take this class again if I could!

Very amazing lecturer, very clear and easy to understand. Monday lectures were optional but engaging and overall very fun to go to. We got a one page front and back cheat sheet on all exams so they were quite easy.If you took AP Psych, most if not all of the material is review and we had all week to submit labs and watch lectures.

psyc 3r has one lecture a week, and she always does a good job at keeping everyones attention and teaching the content in an invigorating way. There are only a few assignments a week and they can be done pretty quick, but the online lectures are usually an hour long so taking notes takes a while. There are a bunch of extra credit opportunities

Assignments are easy, just watch some vid lectures and you'll do fine. What is taught is interesting and is taught in an engaging manner. Only thing that made me get an A- rather than an A were the tests, which I feel were quite a bit of a step up from the video lectures and assignments (especially since there is quite a bit of info that is taught)

totally recommend! take it from someone who was somehow unable to come to any of the lectures (this quarter was on monday's) i still ended with a ~96-97. professor pilegard is nice and engaging, her exams are fair as long as you pay attention to the lecture videos, and actually do the self-explanation assignments/quizzes!

OChem is hard, he does not make it easy. Practice exams aren't a great means of review for exam content, I'd more recommend reviewing lecture content or finding outside resources. Homework problems are also helpful. He clearly wants you to learn but OChem is just hard. While I'm sure there's better professors, his tests are fair enough.

the grade depended on 10 problem sets which would cover the content taught during class, 2 midterms and a final. the lectures were helpful and quite well explained, attending office hours was extremely helpful.

The exam material was not at all reflective of what was covered in lecture, and he stated that he expected the class averages on the exams to be between 50-60%, which is ridiculous because why is he making the test so hard that he expects people to fail? Overall, the professor was very discouraging, and honestly, it felt like I was set up to fail.

Had him for 41A, 25% both midterms and 50% final is all your grade is based on, and homework isn't mandatory, so hold yourself accountable. Fast lectures that are very messy because he uses chalk. No examples. Would not recommend taking him, you will have a breakdown over his tricky exams. Ochem is hard, and he makes it harder. Avoid if possible.

Orgo is already hard and he makes it harder. expect D's on his exams. His class average was in the high 50s and no one got 100s on the final. the only solace is that he's such a bad teacher that everyone else will also fail, so he curves intensely. Otherwise a nice guy, just not adept at lecturing; he moves super fast and doesn't explain problems.
Math follows logically from environmental concepts that aren't too challenging to understand. Review sessions and practice exams reflect exam content well.

Solid prof. His lectures aren't super engaging, but he does podcast them. If you're an econ major, the math is pretty light, just gotta grasp the environmental context. If you're esys, it's gonna be a little harder for you. Just make sure to go to the review sessions cuz you're whole grade is essentially just the midterms and final.

Econ classes are tough no matter what. My issue is that the tests are not representative of the practice problems/exams. You can study the practice exams thoroughly but then get asked about a very specific thing on one slide in the lectures. At that point why bother do the practice exams? You basically need to study everything to get a good grade.

Took him for econ of the environment, I learned almost nothing, the tests were hard and made up almost only of math problems even though there was mostly conceptual stuff in lectures. Most of the class is not econ majors and none of us have a clue what is going on as he doesn't really describe Econ terms and ideas well. I will say he curves nice.

Prof.Jacobsen made economic concepts easy to understand and tied them to relevant issues,keeping the class engaging for all majors.The course had 4 problem sets (lowest dropped, 5%), 2 midterms (25% each), and a 45% final. Exams representative of problem sets and lecture.The lectures were clear, and TA's office hours were helpful. Highly recommend!

Prof. Dhir is one of my favorite professors that I've ever taken. She is soo kind and you can tell she really wants you to succeed and really does listen to you and your thoughts. I really enjoyed her class. Although there was a lot of reading and having to discuss with others, she made class enjoyable! I recommended her to all my friends!!

I usually never rate my professor but for her I needed to she is amazing. Best writing Professor at UCSD. She doesn't give out as much work and really cares for her students. I am also taking her for WCWP 10B. That's how good she is. Would suggest picking her out of all the other writing professors.

Professor Dhir is so caring. She really wants you to learn and never judges you for not knowing the answer to something. I definitely recommend taking her class, I look forward to enrolling in her WCWP 10B.

She's a caring professor and very interested in students as individuals. Although she does repeat herself often taking up majority of class time, she is interested in what you have to say even it's similar to your peers. Very thorough with her critiques in writing that helps you create work you'll be satisfied with. Would recommend!
Best teacher I have taken at UCSD. Professor Dhir is kind and clearly wants her students to do well. I would 100% recommend.

Class was interesting. Lots of reading and there were reading quizzes but they were very easy. Lectures were boring and long but not too bad. Really slow grader. I still don't have my official grade back, and the credit still isn't there. Also not very accessible and difficult to contact outside of class.

Took for P/NP. Prof lowks boring but nice. Boring lectures, readings, and films. No recordings so you kinda have to show up, and slides don't help. Midterms and finals are essay-heavy and reading-based, but she does change it to whatever is taught/what students wanna get tested on. Idk abt other TAs but Steven was THE goat. Idk how I passed ngl

There's a lot of reading but the class is not really hard. Quizzes are open book and you have a week to do them. Also she has you work with maps and other documents and watch documentaries and that helped me understand the lectures better.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR UNLESS FORCED. Most boring class ever!!!!! Prepare to read unnecessary long readings and watch very boring films. All she does is read off the lecture slides and they are not interactive or engaging at all. This class is so BORING I cannot emphasize this enough!!!!!!!

This is NOT an easy class if you are not used to reading but the quizzes are open book and you can skim for discussion section and then go back and read the material carefully for the quiz. You do have to attend class because she doesn't post lectures and attendance counts alot in your final grade but the lectures are interesting.

Forces you to pay for an AI platform for discussion posts. Lectures DRAG, go past allotted time by at least five minutes daily. Often seems confused by his own concepts. Lots of work written on chalkboards that you cannot read, especially critical equations. Exams are best studied for by review rather than attending lecture.

WORST professor at UCSD. He talks so slow with an "umm" every few words. Takes a whole lecture just to explain one chart. Always goes over the lecture time. During our final presentation, he was on his phone and yawning (for all groups). His tests as also nothing like what he teaches. Easy material, but would not recommend taking because of Slade.

Definitely tough class, and frankly very boring subject matter. But Professor Slade tries his best to make it engaging, and he is a good lecturer. Outcome very TA dependent for sure, lots of writing. A little bit too much busywork and detail, but clear guidelines at least. Lab tours at end were nice reward, props to him for that.

Prof. Slade is a very solid professor. The lectures were decent enough to understand the content, and grades depend on your TA. Labs are done in pairs, and lab reports and data tables are shared between you and your lab partner. Released good feedback on reports to fix errors in future reports. Has a final, but isn't that difficult.
Slade was an okay professor. His tests were so dependent on the lectures as were the online quizzes. It was difficult to pay attention in lecture though even when the material was interesting.
Professor was highly active on the class discord server, which helped immensely with the homework.

Go to lectures, go to office hours, and do the practice problems he posts. The homework is very hard and not always what you learn in class. One thing I liked: Professor Wesley is good at helping you when you are stuck and makes time outside of class. One thing I thought could be improved: the material seemed crammed/rushed at the end.

If you want to, you can contact him via multiple ways. You can either attend his office hours and get to know him more, or you can always ask him about homework questions. We had a class discord and he responds super fast. About 1-2 hours of course load out of lecture per week, so he is really chill about it. You got review sheet before tests too.

prof is young, chill, has a discord for the class and responds really quick if  @ him. 1st midterm was all on calc 1, 2nd midterm was on integration by parts, complex numbers, partial fractions, polar functions, improper integrals. final was on all the above plus series and sequences, power series and taylor series. tests 95% are of grade.

Really enjoyed this professor. I would highly recommend this professor to others. Even though Calc 2 is a hard class, the lectures were beneficial and not boring at all. The only downside is how test heavy this class is but that is not a professor problem, it is the math department problem.

Honestly the whole class was decently easy, although I find it ridiculous that he uses AI in grading as part of his course. On top of having to pay for a reskinned canvas. I received lower grades on average when graded by AI and it pushed my grade down. The final touch was that grades are based on percentile, so I went from a 93 to a B+.

The reflections were graded very harshly. It was very difficult to get full credit even if you read the lecture and watched the peer videos. The grading scheme is by percentile ranking in the class, not actual grades. My final grade was lower than the actual grade I should have received based on assignment grades.

Easy class as everything is done asynchronously. You meet with your randomly selected partner each week to conduct a negotiation and they are usually quickly completed. Journal assignments every week analyzing other's videos and lessons you learned. What I didn't like was how we had to pay $45 for what is essentially a reskin of canvas.

Definitely an easy class. there are recorded lectures that i watch some of the time. every week you are paired with a classmate and you record yourselves on zoom doing a negotiation which is very easy and takes very little time(25%). after that you do a write up on 3 other negotiations(75%). its very easy and takes little work. definitely take it.

Very disorganized, no podcasting even though his lecture slides are outdated and don't match (usually just filled with images, so you don't even know what's happening), good information but can't tell if it'll be tested or not. Curves so the average is a B. Had practice test for 1st midterm but not 2nd for some reason. Discussion unhelpful too...

Professor likes his subject and lectures were interesting. However, the canvas was very messy, lecture slides were less than adequate for studying, and the exams were questionable. No hw, whole grade is based on 2 midterms and the final. Advice: record the lectures, or make sure you keep note of what he verbally says will be on the exam.

his exams (which are the only things that go into your grade) was made up of very specific things that weren't really covered in class and he didn't teach a lot of the material he expected you to know. does not podcast, very sloppy slides, lectures are not really helpful, exams are unfair. class is graded on a curve. DO NOT TAKE!!!

Okay, I'm going to clear up some misconceptions about this prof. Is he the best? No. Does he have fair expectations? Yes. His exams are EASY, if you know how to study*. He tells you exactly what to expect on the exams. Audio record his lectures and replay them while taking notes before the exam. If you are reading this: memorize the amino acids.

Alex is an awesome professor, with very clear laid-out practice exams, well-organized content, and sometimes very meaningful life lessons. His lecture slides are easy enough to follow without the need of podcast. Highly recommend him if it is your first time learning biochemistry, can't think of a better professors who is as good as him!

He is super nice, very passionate, and knowledgeable. He posts lecture slides, discussion attendance is mandatory. Exams were kind of difficult but he provides everything you need to know. He cares about students and MUS17 is a fun class. Would definitely recommend.

I can tell Prof Burr is enthusiastic about his lecture but his lectures are just a snooze fest because he speaks in a very boring tone and the class is just honestly very easy. All the exams are all multiple choice questions and 60% of it are "guess the song" questions. Take him for that easy 4.0, but do not take him if u wanna stay awake in class.

Professor was good, very chill. However his lectures are long as it's 3 hours in one day. You can study the lecture slides he leaves on canvas. Everything on tests and mid terms are what he lectured on.  minimal effort was put and I still passed. Overall great professor.

The professor himself is great. Super nice guy that understands that people don't really care about the class. The 3 hour lectures are a joke though. There's weekly quizzes that are meant to encourage attendance but he posts the slides so you can just take the notes without going. Also there was an annoying amount of work required for the papers.
Super easy class, only issue is that attendance is weighted super high (25%)

One essay per week. Discussion is mandatory but lecture is not. Lectures are simple+boring and tbh this is more of a geology and history class than music. However, extra credits are generous if you showed up on certain special events or present at lecture. The content is boring but it's not her fault. Don't take this class if you want real music

Professor Guy is v passionate & funny! Many questions are based on odd lecture-only/discussion-only/reading trivia, so I highly recc going to lecture(!!) & discussion, and noting EVERYTHING. If memorizing random facts is your thing, it'll be fun for you (I'm neurodivergent lol, but also I kept forgetting the weekly(ish) content checks). EC on tests

UCSD course description LIES it's entirely an East Asian music class which I wasn't expecting. Lectures not recorded, discussion mandatory, lectures are extra credit sometimes. Questions on tests are random sometimes and are just memorizing facts. Lectures were fine but slides were mildly bad and hard to study off of.

Overall very passionate professor who cares about the material she is teaching. Lectures are not mandatory, but TA discussion sessions are. Course was more difficult than expected, with more memorisation of facts than actual music knowledge. Lots of reading, especially during the second half of the quarter when it's asynchronous lectures.

The class is super easy and enjoyable if you engage with the content. I would say, her TA's helped a lot for the quizzes so definitely go to discussion (it's mandatory), but everything was already talked about in lecture or canvas. The lectures can put you to sleep, but she is a nice professor who just wants you to learn.
Super nice and class was really easy, the only thing that rlly matters is the labs

Maybe it was the 6:30pm-8pm lecture, but I found prof to not be an engaging speaker. Thankfully, lecture material isn't complex, especially if you've taken AP Bio. Having a good TA helps a lot as they grade all your HW and some are more nit-picky. Amount of work makes this feel like a 4 unit course. Get good lab group, you stick w/ them all quarter

It is a very easy course, the lectures are extremely boring and lengthy, which sucks due to their mandatory nature. The professor seems to care and clearly wants to make it an enjoyable experience, however, our final presentation was extremely unorganized and he screeched for people to shut up during it; very unprofessional and unnecessary.

There were so many assignments for a 2 unit class, but that is just how it is structured (not by prof). His lectures were so boring I was trying not to fall asleep, and they were mandatory. Your whole grade in the class depends on your lab TA. The quizzes were super easy and take home.

The lectures were mandatory but super long and boring with content that was rarely useful in lab. The lab instructions were often confusing and difficult for beginners. Grading is mostly TA based, and from writing assignments/quizzes with random information. The prof clearly cares, but I found the class quite unhelpful for my lab development.

Kartik Seshadri is GREAT. I don't understand why there is bad ratings. All you gotta be is interested in learning a classical instrument and practice here and there. He is very calm and patient. Sweet as well because even though we didn't sound the best he still gave us assurance. Clear with exceptions and cares for us to learn and engage!

This class was an introduction to Indian Music, so there was not a lot of content to cover anyways. It is mainly meant for people who have no prior experience with Indian Classical Music. Overall, it is a fascinating topic and very different from other music classes.

He is very mean and arrogance to students. When you don't understand a part, he doesn't come over and teach you how to do it but goes and criticizes you in front of the whole class. He is not patient at all with his students and frowns every time he counts the bad things you do. I never felt any encouragement from him.

Professor Seshadri Kartik is a TERRIBLE teacher. He is so ARROGANT and UNFRIENDLY that he often asks some students to drop the class in class when they do not play sitar well and make some small mistakes. He prefers to laugh at students who do not do well rather than help them to learn. NEVER take him again. WORST professor @ UCSD.
Pial Bossman Hossain is an awesome TA. He teaches indian music with an entertaining twist. He's as sardonic as they come and I look forward to his witty remarks every wednesday. Pial FTW.

I am surprised by what I understand to be some of racist comments against Professor Patel. Her lectures were beautiful, inspirational, and always related to the readings and more. She also shared amazing lecture slides. This year she lost her mother but still showed up for us. Thank you, Professor!
For a class like this, I was surprised that the professor introduced such controversial views and did not listen to any dissenting views.

Professor Patel is the best professor at UCSD she is amazing in every way! take her class!!! She is very understanding and KNOWS what shes talking about, I cannot stress what an amazing professor she is.

*Decolonial Muslim Feminism* - Professor Patel is my favorite Professor I've had in my entire college career. She is thoughtful, inspiring, and has a collaborative approach with her students. She truly cares for us. This course is so important, I hope UCSD continues offering it. It changed the way I see the world. I am integrating it into my life.

:( Incorrect and heavily biased materials. She goes on lots of personal tangents that have little to no relation to the class. In discussion, she only supports what she wants to hear and doesn't really allow for any statements that don't fit her preconceived notions. I'd genuinely rather drop out before taking a class with this professor again.

Super sweet professor! Never saw him angry or annoyed! Very laid-back and wants the best for his students. Willing to practice and go over things multiple times. Ends class when he grasps like we are on tracks and is able to read the class room well! Definitely take him! Nicest Professor you can ask for!

assignments+in class exams are 80%, assignments have a completion grade: you did it, 100. exams are music basics and grading is nice.
20% are discussion participation.
Lectures a a bit boring but you can skip those that does not has an in-class exam

Had him for MUS 2A and 2B and he was nice and accommodating. Lectures were pretty basic level stuff and boring so I skipped a lot (including sections, which brought down my grade a bit). The quizzes were a little scary and intimidating, but he grades pretty graciously, so you can still probably get by.

I took MUS 2A and MUS2B with professor Carlson. It's an easy class: he gives biweekly quizzes that are easy to pass as long as you study, and only a couple homework assignments every now and then. He clearly loves his job and his passion for the subject makes the class enjoyable. Super nice and chill guy who's always willing to help students.

Easy class with very clear instructions. He is lenient with deadlines in the sense of tests. More than enough preparation before every exam. Doesn't take attendance and the homework is minimal and casual, and the grades are based off skills exams that happen aurally during classes. He drops two exams if you miss them and doubles the grade prior.

He is a great professor! Truly can tell he loves to teach music. Wears t-shirt's related to the lecture! He's nice and always willing to talk about anything from the lecture to questions and concerns! Interesting topics and 2 basic easy essays where we determine what artist to right etc. Great class and hit some awesome genres! Take him!

There's a reason why he got a one point something. His lectures are really hard to follow and extremely disorganized. Getting an A is REALLY easy in his class because there's 25% extra credit for participation, but you'll have to sit with uncertainty all the time and the tests are not easy. He's a nice guy, but he's too old to teach.

Incredibly difficult to follow along during the lectures cause of his monotone voice and how he just reads off of slides with text copied straight from Wikipedia. But the course was kinda interesting and grading very fair and easy to get an A so i recommend for the climate change requirement. He's an nice  person just not qualified for this course.

Has good lecture notes and cares about our learning, but his lectures are so dull that you won't learn anything. Fails to answer questions, and simply gives away HW solutions during discussion section without proper explanation. Poor guy didn't have a TA, so he procrastinated all the grading and started grading HW 1 on the day grades were due.

this guy sucks. His slides are more outdated than this school just a bunch of jibberish all over the place. he will teach you nothing. lectures go over no examples and he basically is just an audiobook reader just regurgitating the info on the slides.

The worst professor I've ever had. His slides are unorganized and confusing, and his "teaching" makes zero sense. The hw and test questions are unreasonably difficult and he doesn't go over any examples in class. He doesn't give the hw answers at any point and grading takes forever, so there is no way to even learn from your mistakes. AVOID HIM!!!

Not a very hard class, but a very unorganized prof. If you're actually interested in the material, take a different prof. He canceled class often, and his course schedule was constantly changed. It was hard to understand where we were in the course, and what we had to do. However, exams and final project weren't too hard and his lectures are okay.

He really doesn't assign a lot of reading, especially for a history teacher, so I'd suggest taking his class when you need the credits during a quarter you plan on being busy. He gave us the exam prompts beforehand, so there weren't any surprises. He yells during lectures (not at students, but just to be heard)

Vitz was nice and his lectures were engaging. There was 4 discussions, 2 short quizzes/exams, 1 short writing assignment and a final. I found that the assigned readings and lectures were relevant to what was being tested and gave a lot of info. Assignments and tests were very straightforward and he gave detailed expectations nothing was surprising.

Highly recommend taking his class during the summer. I didn't spend too much time on homework or our midterm and final papers. Consisted of mainly films in which some are boring and others are entertaining. Disclaimer: I don't know how different this class is during the school year but save your time and take it during summer!! I got a 93%

Professor Vitz was the worst teacher I've had here at UCSD. I took a film class with him,and he didn't make any of the films accessible. We had to pay to watch some. When we rose this concern to him, he did nothing. The class also had a really low average, and he wouldn't relook at people's assignments when asked. Be prepared to regurgitate info.

This guy reads off slides and sometimes talks about real-world applications which aren't testable material and detract a bit from the class itself. Otherwise, his practice material is very similar to the actual, hw is similar difficulty as assessments, and he shares useful insights for approaching/solving certain problems.
Final was much different than the practice material provided, but still overall pretty fair. Pretty straightforward class overall, a lot of it is just knowing what equations to use when.
Decent professor. Quizzes are kinda similar in difficulty to homework, sometimes harder. Iclicker attendence but you can miss up to 6 lectures so not bad. Lectures were easy to understand.

His lectures, explanation-wise, are okay, but he often speeds up during the second half and runs through the slides quickly without explaining things in much detail.
His tests are fine since there's practice quizzes and equation sheets. But the topics covered in PHYS 2C are generally newer and more abstract, like thermodynamics and fluids.

iclicker for attendance. His lectures and explanations I found useless, just reads off slides. Homeworks are very simple. The tests I found to be more difficult than the homeworks and discussion worksheets and any in class problems. Required a lot of self studying and doing a bunch of practice problems to prepare for quizzes. Do not recommend.
Dr. Ornelas is an A+ professor!
Best professor ever

Keep devices away until attendance question at end, don't talk while she is, and at least try to discuss content w/ partner when it's time - you won't have a problem in lecture. I found her lectures to be helpful in understanding readings, and readings are interesting if you're willing to engage w/ it. Midterm and final were writing on demand.

Super easy midterm and final. But she does tend to get very upset about minor things like side conversations during lecture and not taking notes. The DOC program also has a no tech policy, but lectures are podcasted.

Professor Strom is a great professor! However, DOC 1 is just so text heavy that it makes it difficult to fully enjoy the readings and the general course. She provides decent information on the texts and for midterm/final prep, but your grade mostly depends on your TA.

Very easy class, just the reading is annoying. Her lectures do cover enough of the information needed so you don't have to read closely; a light skim should be fine. Attendance for lectures and discussion sessions are mandatory. There is a no technology policy for the DOC program. She has gotten mad at people for being late or not taking notes.

Reading is not needed to get an A in this class; her lectures cover everything, and the exams are super easy. She can be stingy about students not having notebooks out to take notes, and electronic note-taking isn't allowed which is kinda dumb.

Coursework is definitely manageable, and weekly quizzes are easy if you do the readings. A good chunk of your grade will be group deliverables throughout the quarter. There are many opportunities for extra credit, which is helpful. Travis is a great professor, and the class would be enjoyable for any student. Highly recommend!

Travis is a super caring prof with lots of opportunity for self-improvement and networking. Large part of the grade was based on group projects and class participation. Lectures were calm but could be definitely be more engaging.

Reading quizzes every lecture and a bit hard because he asks super specific questions. Midterm and final are super easy though, only need a basic understanding of the readings to get 100%. If you get a good group for the project the class is easy but if you get a bad group that does not want to put in some effort, your grade will tank.
Very nice and easy class to get at least a B+ in. Lots of group work but great way to meet new people as a freshman, highly recommend. Extra credit points available and midterm/finals were very easy.

Travis is a very kind, supportive, and helpful professor. He really trusted that his students were putting their best foot forward. The workload was reasonable, with three group projects, almost biweekly readings, a midterm, and a final. I wouldn't call this class an easy A, but I honestly found the course really interesting and fun regardless.

In my experience, her advising approach was excessively punitive and often justified as “high standards.” Publicly she emphasized fairness, but private interactions were dismissive. She focused on internal politics than mentorship, frequently ignoring student concerns and penalizing perceived mistakes, resulting in a highly stressful workplace.
Warning to PhD advisees! Avoid her at any cost. Avoid, Avoid, Avoid. I have witnessed many academic careers demolished by her.

All that Tara's victims seem able to do now is share their experiences through negative reviews here. She often flags even these reviews. Typical thin-skinned academic: the kind of dish-it-out-but-can't-take-it variety. If she is this intolerant here, one can only imagine how she might respond to criticism in person, behind closed doors.

Tara is well aware that most grad students she has mistreated feel too embarrassed or intimidated to speak out. When a rare student does file a complaint or even protests, she points to the many silent ones as evidence of her innocence. It's best to steer clear of any interaction with her altogether.

I went through one of the toughest experiences with her, and I'm still picking up the pieces—dealing with lingering trauma and seeing a therapist. Never thought professors like her could get away with such behavior. Don't put blind trust in the univ system. They're not here to support u. They're here to throw their weight around and intimidate.

Straightforward class. There are four quizzes, a group project, hw, and a final exam. You can drop your lowest quiz. Rana is sweet and wants the best for you; she rarely, if ever, throws any curve balls on tests and will subtly hint at what we should expect to see. She is always happy to help you and never makes you feel bad for not understanding.

4 quizzes, a final, a group project and weekly homework. TAs were not  helpful, discussions felt pointless, most people who scored well did not attend. Professor Rana knows a lot but is disorganized, wrong dates,untimely feedback etc. Does not follow the syllabus Do not fill out the survey about being a transfer or first year etc. Teach yourself

She teaches with the expectation that you remember the prerequisite required for this class. REVIEW previous stats content before taking this class!! Otherwise, easy grader. So much EC, it's almost ridiculous.

Dr Rana is knowledgeable and respectful, but her lectures are disorganized and the slides are confusing. Be prepared to teach yourself most of the material, I did and I was fine for the final. However, she is very accommodating and wants you to succeed in the class, on an exam she will help if needed. ATTEND discussion w/ TA Jazmin and youll be ok.

AWFUL
Let me start by saying that I have rated professors whose class I got a C in 5/5 so I'm gonna be fair here
She is awful, her one good TA taught us the very little we know
Extremely boring person with no structure, jumped from in person, online, zoom, sometimes even had an in person class then a video to watch. 
Shes smart but can't teach
RUN

Straightforward class. Mandatory attendance. Stay on top of your assignments, as they can accumulate quickly. Exams were moderately difficult. Overall, the class was easy; if offered by this professor, take it!

Her class is really easy just very tedious and annoying to deal with. She's very unclear about a lot of assignments, very weird and odd due date times which makes it kind of hard to keep up with the class. Attendance is required and her class is extremely boring.

I have to agree with the other reviews. Professor Mcmenamin was very condescending, she often would scold the class when she was disappointed. It felt very high school teacher. If you have no choice, take her because the class itself is easy she just is not a welcoming person.

Too much busy work that is unrelated to lecture, unclear expectations on assignments and projects, extremely strict about the final. This class would've been interesting but she reads off slides. Talks at us and not to us. Condescending and defensive when receiving feedback. Should not be teaching and stick to research.

She was pretty condescending. The class was easy overall, but she made the content boring. During the final, she kept interrupting about every 5 to 10 minutes to tell us about a mistake or typo that she made it was very distracting. At the very least proof read your final before distributing to an entire lecture hall.

Liked the professor, but the course was disorganized. Several classes were canceled and replaced with old videos that didn't always match. Dense material, tangents, and skipped topics appeared on exams. Final project was last minute and unclear; grades weren't shared.

I personally wouldn't take him again. The quizzes, midterms, and finals are harder than you think. Although they are open book and online, which is truly a lifesaver, it was still a headache to take. There's just so much memorization and information packed in that I barely even remember what was being taught.
He's an interesting lecturer. Explains things well though he does stutter at times - but it's usually because he's thinking and trying to make the points clearer.
amazing prof, amazing lectures. clearly cares about his students and made the class so interesting. the discussions were fun and insightful and there were lots of examples

Really boring class, and professor would not follow the slides, rather he would go off on tangents/get in discussions with students. Topic was uninteresting and quite hard to understand, especially at first, but ultimately it wasn't too difficult to score well if you did the reading, since the exams were open book.
As part of a UCSD neuroscience program in La Jolla, I took Professor Thomas Ta's course. It was one of the most difficult yet rewarding courses.
Really great prof with industry experience. Lives and works in La Jolla and NYC.
Def recommend. My fav prof while at UCSD.
He's a great prof with real world experience.

Great professor! Planning to take another class of his this fall. Professor Thomas Ta is probably the best one at UC San Diego. He reminds of a CS professor I had one summer at Dart mouth. Really great teacher with real industry experience.
Super straight forward. Teaches exactly what you need to know. Direct and great for learning subjects like 2C.

Professor Tan explains challenging topics well and is a quick lecturer, sometimes too fast for taking notes. He's very nice, and his quizzes and finals are similar to the practice. I highly recommend taking him for 2C.

expect a lot of work from this class every week. lots of quizzes to keep up with. class isn't particularly difficult but can easily lose points on projects and homework assignments. material is better learned through labs and lectures are extra supplements.

I can tell she really loves teaching and assisting students whenever she can. Lots of online resources and office hours. Lectures kinda get boring, but my attention span is kinda cooked so it's wtv. Lots of homework, but very useful. Grading distribution is very lenient so doing poor on the midterm/final wont damage you too much.

Great professor, great lectures, and the DSC10 website is really organized and well put together. The exams and quizzes were pretty difficult coming from someone with prior college stats experience and no Python experience.
She is pretty good. She gets straight to the point and has many resources available to help you. She gives you everything you need.
Great professor. DSC 10 is a hard course. The good thing is that resources are very organised.

Difficult class and often no one raised their hand to ask questions. Professor sometimes would assume we already knew things or didn't explain too well in class, but he answered everything during office hours. He's definitely very knowledgeable about quantum chemistry and very articulate. You will likely spend a lot of time on this class.

The only bad thing about this class was the TA, Zhiyuan Yin. The professor, though, was really nice. Sometimes he has a hard time grasping what students questions are about the content, but he does a good job explaining topics. My advice is to NOT study the proofs he does in class, just focus on their implications. Study hard for the quizzes.
Very detailed and straightforward lectures. Go to his office hour if you need help, plus you can get extra credit.

He did the best. You need to talk to him after class. It seems that he went through every thing quickly, but it's the class's problem. Quantum in ten weeks is nearly impossible. I would not be convinced if this class is not a candidate for Nobel Prize in medical science for curing hypotension permanently.

Lectures  error analysis, unhelpful for lab reports. Doesn't go over any lab/pchem (condescends if u ask), assigns random labs so you can't ask peers for help. TAs don't hold lab sections and instead have poorly organized OH where you're in the waiting room for 1hr. Prelab oral quizzes to get data. Curves on "class behavior." Teaches nothing.

You have little to no interaction with the professor because the lab is run entirely by the TA, but there is an edpuzzle "lecture" for each lab that's just review of basic physics concepts. It's true that lab reports are graded pretty harshly, but the instructions are very clear on what is expected. Just show all work and have a coherent process.

In 1AL you don't interact with the professor except for edpuzzle videos, so depends on your TA. Lab every other week. Lab reports graded pretty harshly and quizzes difficult, but you get to drop one. Just keep writing on lab reports and show ALL work. Labs are monotonous and pointless, but no getting around that.

As long as you follow the instructions for the lab reports and show up to lab and actually try to do the pre lab video assignment and questions, you will be good to go, just always make sure to show your work and follow the rules for the uncertainty calculations for the pre labs, but this teacher's Edpuzzles definitely helped a lot for his quizzes.

I can spend two entire days grinding a lab report, learning the material in this class to get a 70 percent on it for not "showing proper uncertainty calculations" or I can spend two days studying for an upper div bio class to get an A in the midterm. Tell me why a lower div physics class is harder than any class I've taken in my three years of uni.

The course follows the format similar to all other physics courses in the 2 series.
Quizzes where the lowest will be dropped from your grade + a final.
The quizzes were pretty challenging but not too difficult. The final was extremely easy.
Iclickers will be used in lecture for attendance.
The lectures werent that helpful.

Dr. Graeve made class interesting and relevant by using current real world examples. In-person tests are open-notes and have a 15 minute discussion period with a partner which was very helpful. The test content was an accurate representation of what we had learned. Overall, I liked how it was encouraged to ask and discuss any content.

Dr. Graeve changed her teaching/exam style since previous classes. All tests were open-note. You were also allowed to discuss the questions with a partner for a bit before working independently. Midterms had out-of-class portions, and the homework was optional (But bring it to exams). I'd say more good things, but it won't let me. She was great!

I think Professor Graeve is a good lecturer without considering her personality. She is very willing to listen to her students and answer their questions. During the lectures, the professor provided an interesting and clear talk about crystallography. The homework is not mandatory but necessary for her exams, I was inspired and more curious after.

Worst prof ever. She is the reason I do not want to continue my masters at UCSD and transfer to another institution. There is a heavy lack of prompt grading as well as any assurance to anything. Dr. Graeve also expects you to know a great deal when she herself doesnt even know and refers you to Wikipedia immediately when faced with a difficulty.
Professor Graeve told me make a good review for her to get some extra credit so here I am, hopefully this is worth sacrifice of dignity.

The class is centralized on the idea of "contracted grading," so you get what you give. You have to work towards the grade you want with a clear outline of what you need to compete. There are 3 main writing projects with a couple of presentations and readings. Overall, pretty simple.

You're in good hands if you have Dr. Merryman. He's a very relaxed teacher with clear expectations. His feedback is helpful when you're researching for and revising your essays (which are called "Projects"). You select the grade you want at the start of the term and work for it by completing said projects and other activities. You will write a lot!

Pretty easy and chill class. Expect some daily (ish) readings to do before class and to participate every class but other than that you only need to do 3 essays, 2 easy presentations and you're good. You pick the grade you want and work for it.
Best WCWP professor at UCSD. Good lectures and a very easy to follow grading structure. He is also very understanding. You can only miss two classes for an A.

Takes time during lecture to ensure students grasp concepts and clear up misconceptions, which is especially helpful toward the second half of the course; his accent does not affect his teaching, and his tests are very fair. Overall great experience.

Great prof, straightforward hw and fair exams that actually reflects the hw. He's very responsive to questions and also goes through polls and why the wrong answers are wrong. Does have an accent though, but not too hard to understand.

course content is already difficult enough, but lectures are very drawn out and boring. couple this with his really thick accent and this course is just a nightmare. seems like a nice enough guy but, definitely wouldn't recommend

Lectures can be convoluted. I oftentimes screenshot slides to ChatGPT to help simplify concepts. Tough grading standards, difficult homework. Class structure is also frustrating - 2nd midterm on Week 10 (close to finals) and we got back grade day before final so less time to study mistakes. Nice guy, he's not the worst, but don't fall behind.

essentially a combination of abstract algebra, very basic graph theory and regular languages. The most difficult part of this class is the proofs. The exams are almost entirely proofs so its very easy to perform poorly on them. The lectures are very long and not necessarily engaging. The prof is accessible through OH but this class was HARD

No midterms, yet 60 pts from Final exam focused on last 2 wks of concepts and we didn't get back any quiz/hw grade pertaining to any of that material. There's a significant mismatch between Instructional support and exam difficulty. If ur taking him be prepared to self-study

Slides are incoherent text vomit, rambles throughout lecture like a buffering video. Got angry at the class for leaving early on Thanksgiving week while he himself didn't attend his own office hours on at least two occasions. Released two HWs on week 10 due to being 2 weeks behind schedule, and said we'll drop one anyway according to the syllabus.

Avoid taking him. Two HWs squished together in the last week, changed a quiz date last second on thanksgiving week and blamed us for wanting to change it, lectures incoherent, finals was only based on a couple of topics. Only take if you're familiar with 101, save yourself the headache.
My goat when he doesn't attend his own office hours

The class is disorganized. Homework was released later than scheduled, causing multiple to be due in the final week. Grading is extremely slow. Even after the final, only 5/8 HWs and 6/8 Quizzes are graded. The final exam is 48% of the grade, not representative of the class, and only covers a few very hard topics.
Online lectures every other week that were posted and they never went the full time. All the homework answers are in the lecture but the labs are graded tough though.

An angel. He really wants to make sure his students understand and be able to apply the material. Made it really clear what the final would look like. Final was exactly like homework. During the pandemic and injustice going on in the world, he was very empathetic and understanding. Amazing teacher and amazing person :)

The professor himself was fine, but the class was very heavy and challenging. Lectures were not mandatory, and grades were based on lab reports and a lab final. His lectures were not very engaging but had interesting facts embedded in them.
Great professor!!! Makes himself accessible for office hours. Quizzes are very fair. Definitely one of the best professors in the Physics department. Take him!!!

Kaixuan is an amazing professor, he made the material easy to follow which is saying something. He posts his lecture slides and podcasts online. Homework is extra credit and you can use Wileyplus, or do the problems in the book, which he posts solutions to online. The quizzes and final were reasonable but you do need to put in the hours.
He's such a COOL professor! He does live up to all of the ratings students give him
everything everyone has said about him, 100% accurate! what an amazing person this guy is

If you have the opportunity to take a class with him, DO IT! He is one of the kindest and most chill professors I ever had at UCSD. He really takes the time to interact with students and help you on projects. He assigns weekly projects/writing assignments but they were pretty doable.

Professor Halm is one of my favorite professors I've taken at UCSD. Every class felt like a no stress environment with great conversation and good lectures with lots of wisdom to learn. Highly recommend.

Loved this guy. He has probably been one of my favorite teachers I have ever had. His lectures are engaging, and he has good stories. I felt like I learned a lot from him and his class. Assignments were chill and the midterms were very simple and straight foward.

Sweet guy and will definitely take him again if given the chance.

The lectures focus primarily on very basic concepts, similar to a high school–level overview, which may be helpful for beginners. However, the exams are significantly more challenging and require a deeper level of problem-solving than what is emphasized in lectures or homework.
I acknowledge the creativity and care invested in the course materials. Yet the grade distribution is remarkably harsh, and it has regrettably left a negative first impression of UCSD.

I had 255A with Alon, he does his best to make you learn and cares about you learning, he is not the best lecturer but does his best. The homeworks are copied from the book so it is not too difficult to complete. Be ready for very difficult exams. The grading is fair I would say. Best point about the great Lord Alon is that he is a very nice person

I took his class three years ago, and I'm just beginning to heal from that experience. His lectures were hard to follow, and without podcasts to revisit, missing one point felt like missing everything. The stress brought me to depression and caused acne breakouts that left permanent scars on my face. It was a nightmare I'd rather forget...

The lecture slides are nigh incomprehensible. The only way to effectively review lectures is to rewatch the entire lecture, which isn't always an option. More importantly, the professor *failed half the class*. In a graduate class. A class that's required for many people, including myself. He made so many of our lives so much harder by doing that.

His handwriting is actually impossible to read and exams are notoriously difficult. He brushes over topics quickly and talks very fast. The only way to pass this class is reading the textbook, I ended up with an alternative textbook as well because the one he uses is so bad.

this guy is very funny and caring, but cannot teach to save his life. lectures were very unorganized and difficult to follow. seems like a great guy who is very passionate about his subject, but not built for teaching first year intro classes
He is an amazing professor and extremely knowledgeable. Exams tend to be more abstract and conceptual. Learned probability theory at a rigorous level.

His lecture covers all the knowledge but in a not that organized way: he prefers to talk about examples and within them introduce the formula and theorem. His homework aims to let students know the principles and deep application of the knowledge he taught in the lecture. Final and Midterm 2 are difficult, but the curve is generous.
His lectures are super unorganized and the homework & exams are unpredictable and not very reflective of the course content, but he curves very generously

Overall great prof! Lectures are great + as long as you understand lecture content, you're pretty set for exams. HW readings were super long tho. All exams are open note and the exams are not terribly difficult. Lectures aren't mandatory but there are extra credit pop quizzes. Took this course for the dei ge as a stem major, but highly reccomend!

super sweet. LOTS of reading hw. lectures aren't mandatory but she gives pop quizzes for extra credit. discussions were mandatory. midterms were in class hand written literary analysis essays. if you write abt what's on the lecture slides you'll get a 100 on ur exams. final is an essay, if u score >85 avg on the midterms u can do a creative final

Prof Suzuki is super nice and chill!! Most of the content is based off of the readings, so keep up on them in the event of there being pop quizzes (dont worry! they're for extra credit only). You get tons of prep for the midterms, & the final is super chill. Your grade is entirely decided by your TA though and some of my friends did not luck out D:

5 extra credit quizzes throughout lectures. Midterms and Finals were graded easy. Taking AP Lang helped me a lot. In the midterm, you are given 3 passages from the various stories, and 1 Ai passage, and u select 2 of the real passages to analyze through lit analysis. Tests are also open note. TA was very kind. Mandatory, but very useful discussions
Great prof, the lectures and reading were interesting and its easy to do well in the class

P. Lee is great! I think all lang classes are easier for heritage speakers, but prof. Lee does a great job of making everyone feel included. You WILL participate no matter what, and she offers EC for going to the Kor. fest. HW are due in the midday which was eh, but HW=completion and test material is exactly what was covered in class.

Prof Lee is so nice! Always cracking jokes in class, she has the whole class smiling and engaged in learning. The class itself is manageable if you participate, attend daily classes, and set aside time to complete assignments and study for each bi-weekly test. I recommend!

Prof. Lee is hilarious. Her jokes made it easy to learn the material, and it was always a joy to be in her class. Her test questions are directly from lectures/homework.
However, the class is taught entirely in Korean and you are expected to write 3-page papers. I would probably avoid taking this class if you are a non-native/heritage speaker.

Attendance and participation make up a great portion of the grade, classes are Mon. through Fri., which gets draining. 2B is much harder than before, with harder grammar. There is an exam every other Monday. But if you go to class, and go over ppts, you can memorize answers to all exam questions (which is hard to do but possible). 2-page essays.

If you pay attention to the material, this class is not hard at all. Just participate, and be ready to be called on to answer questions. This professor is not the youngest Korean teacher I've had so they might not be fun in class, but the class is still enjoyable if you are interested in learning Korean.
I really enjoyed his class, I felt like I learned a lot and class was a very positive and fun environment. He was very fair with grading, which made the midterm and final less stressful.

Took for my art requirement. It's an easy A as long as you participate in class, which consists of learning different routines/ sequences. Midterm and final are group projects (4-5 minutes self-choreographed dances). There are a few written assignments and mandatory dance shows you have to attend/ dance in.
