I took his online asynchronous course through UCSD extended studies. Professor Barbaro was approachable, clear in his grading system, and thorough with his material content. We had weekly quizzes and one discussion post per week with due dates on Thursday, Saturday, and Sunday. The schedule each week was the same so it was easy to keep track!
Very well put together course.

Mr. Brett Barbaro is an excellent professor who genuinely cares about his students. I took this course online, and I appreciated that his assignments really encourage critical thinking. He allows students to create their own discussion questions, which makes the coursework much more engaging. He is a very fair grader and gives extra credit.

Very knowledgeable professor, and very caring and wants his students to succeed! He would weekly send email updates to make sure we knew what was due and the material that was being covered that week. His lectures that were uploaded had subtitles making it easy to take notes and follow along. Would take another class with him if possible!

He did a relatively good job of making difficult concepts clear and when there was confusion over the lecture slides, it could be easily understood by reading the book. Also extra credit is offered which helps augment the difficulty of the tests.
Fun class, just have fun!

Very great professor, you can see that he is passionate about what he teaches with the way he talks about theatre; like its a whole different world.Only one assignment a week; due friday. Moreover, throughout the whole quater we only had one quiz, which was like a terminology quiz and which told you the exact terms going to be on the test. #EASY A

Mandatory discussion and lecture- he is accommodating. Weekly journal assignments. Lot of self reflection. 1 big quiz and one midterm, lot of presentations in discussion. He is really passionate about it and you can see it in the way he carries himself in class

Very easy class, with not a lot of effort. Lecture & discussion required. Discussion group creates a play to present at the end. Paper is final with 6-7 pages but doable. Passionate about what he teaches is fun.

Todd was a great professor! There was an 8-page final, section performance project, and other papers. All TA's do the grading. I must admit, If you're not a theatre major, then you'll kinda feel out of place some of the time. However, it was cool to see how passionate other students are about acting! Overall, the class is a great experience!
Amazing funny and very specific in her instruction. Just turn in discussions and you're good. (I didn't so yeah)

She is a very fun professor who is very passionate and has good stories. The class mainly involved weekly discussion posts from the lectures and was pretty easy. I would definitely recommend this class! She would sometimes take attendance to avoid people from skipping, but you could definitely miss a few lectures and communicate with her.
super easy and chill class

Super fun and kind professor.  Lectures are mandatory and honestly very interesting and funny.  Terry really enjoys what she does and gives great insight.  Weekly discussion board is very simple, midterm and final is online and multiple choice and short essay with open notes and book.  Easy A and a genuinely interesting and entertaining class.

Professor Wilson was an amazing professor who was so real. She was very straightforward with course material and made the class engaging and entertaining. She was understanding. The coursework can catch up to you if you fall behind, and it is highly recommended to read all models and buy the book. Weekly homework assignments are very important.
Really great Professor, nothing to add.

Had him for USP25 and 153. There was a lot of overlap in the material, some slide decks were straight up reused. Attendance isn't mandatory but would recommend just because the slide decks themselves don't contain too much information. Readings for important for exams. One in-person online midterm with cheat sheet, and final is take home online.

The most pick me "I'm not like other white men" I have ever met. Makes weird, un-funny jokes, and laughs at them. Thinks he's everyones favorite prof. Super organized--not responsive AT ALL. Kept changing the midterm date. Would give quizzes and tests on stuff he forgot to teach us, or just never did. Late. All round insufferable man.

Unreliable professor. Missed a midterm because he changed the date last minute and when I emailed him to reschedule, all I got was "Yes - sent from my IPhone" with no follow up or further information. He just kept ignoring my other emails asking for when I could take it and when I confronted him in person... he just told me to email him again!

labs (10%), quizzes with unlimited attempts (15%), a midterm worth 25% with 25 multiple-choice questions, and a final worth 50% with 50 multiple choice questions plus 4 FRQs each with 4 parts. The exams aren't impossible, but you definitely need to study and actually use the practice exam he provides. The class is curved pretty nicely too.

very easy. lectures once a week and very long but quizzes/exams are easy as well. Nice group work and very doable with a heavy courseload. Love Professor Hayes. I did not need the textbook, I never bought it nor used it.

I enjoyed this class. The class set up is straight forward and all the assignments are well explained and doable. Woking in my group was quite enjoyable since there was a huge emphasis on accountability. The stories from the guest speakers were insightful and it helped see the application of the concepts. 10/10 I would recommend class

Professor Hayes is one of the most caring professors I have ever met. You can tell she truly loves teaching and she goes out of her way to get to know her students. Professor Hayes is a big inspiration of mine and she has coached students in the past. Work in the class is easy, homework is fair and easy, exams are straightforward. No surprises.

Best Mgt class @ UCSD! I applied our coursework to projects, my life, and project management job applications & interviews. Class was paced well. Stay on top of quizzes, participate in lecture & group work! Lectures are used for exams, so create practice tests from study guides. Sherry is amazing & truly motivates students! 10/10 recommend!

Professor Sherri is an absolute gem of a professor! Her course consists of 5 group projects which are pretty easy to do as long as you follow the given prompts. Her quizzes and exam questions are fair as long as you follow the learning guides she provides for each module. TAKE HER YOU WILL NOT REGRET IT!!!

I got 30-35/100 in midterm, and it was curved to 50, its lower than average. At final I got a score close to average. Quiz were hard but I got a score higher than average. Final score is curved to about 80%, still a B-. It's funny. Everything in this class is unspeakably difficult.
I would not recommend UCSD ECE only because of this lecture. Grading is extremely harsh so be aware.

Not much useful concepts are covered (you can learn most of them from the first half of a course in Bayesian statistics, which is much more comprehensive). Materials are outdated and many typos remain unfixed.

The homework and exams are irrelevant to the lecture. Be ready to teach yourself everything. You are assumed to know a lot of math not taught. It is highly possible that you know everything in the lecture but fail the exams. Even though the solutions of the homework were given, they are still poorly explained.

This course is insanely hard. The HW and exams have basically nothing to do with leture. Even if you review every slide and finish all the homework, you can still easily fail the exams. If you don't have a math background, you won't get a good grade in this class no matter how much effort you put in. The class is like a self-study math course

I found ECE 251C to be an enjoyable experience. The grading criteria was fair, exams were fair and no surprise or trick questions showed up anywhere. Had a cool class project of your own choosing which was very broad. The instructor is very accessible and is always happy to take questions and has multiple office hours and gives good feedback.

Professor Parhi is very friendly and keeps lectures engaging with lots of examples and practice problems. The class isn't easy, but wavelets aren't easy. Professor Parhi is happy to take any questions about the class material both inside and outside class. He actively tries to clarify every doubt. Attending lectures is necessary for the midterm.
His grading is very arbitrary. He does not record lectures. However, he is very accessible on Piazza and outside of class.

Dr. Day is a fantastic lecturer with a lot to say, which made discussion very engaging. However, he is poorly organized: his Canvas is a mess, the rubrics are vague, and he grades slowly. Exams are hard, open-note FRQs; rote memorization won't work. I enjoyed this class, but strong mol bio fundamentals & self-study skills are necessary to succeed.

I agree with the other ratings for BIMM101. He is the absolute sweetest and you can tell he really cares about his students but omg his in lab quizzes were made 5 min before they were given to us and they make no sense. What taught in lecture is not a good reflection of his quizzes. The final was also the worst i've taken. I had a rlly good TA tho!

Super funny, but mainly teaches through examples, so don't take him if you can't handle that. Lectures are pretty dense but he's always open to and enthusiastic about any questions you may have. Just make sure you fully understand the concepts since the tests are entirely free response, very heavy focus on application of lecture.

The lectures and tests are not a 1:1. Still possible to do well in the class. Do the practice assignments attend the review sessions/look at them online but make sure you do the assignments. 90 on the first midterm forgot to do 2 assignments and that was -10%. Yes that was not smart. Just practice and ask questions. He is easy to talk to.

I took this class and lets just say that you will have to teach yourself majority of the time. He gives you a quiz every week that is HARD, a CRISPR paper due, and a final that is two parts. I repeat his Final is ridiculously hard and he always forgets to post what's due and what were learning for the week. Also, is not organized at all.

ECE 164 is a dense class that is hard to study for. The professor skims over many things that are important to know for homework and exams. It's like a transition from undergraduate to graduate-level circuit design. Project was 4 weeks of painful work, but very rewarding in the end. Tough exams; focus on conceptual understanding, not memorization.

Superb scheduling, every lab felt improvised.
Hardware was limited, often broken, but inspiring.
Amazing freedom: no manuals, no guidance.
Brilliantly avoided EDA, layout, and PCB design guidance.
Independent learning thrived, Piazza became Reddit.

TAs and Prof are super tough graders. Course material itself is top notch. But, the way it is taught is terrifying. HW1 is released in the very 1st lecture before having taught anything at all. Lects can lack detailed explanations. As a student you are under a LOT of stress due to weekly hard deadlines and tough exams, -the prof doesnt care at all.

Worse professor and I don't know how this guy manage to keep this teaching position. Doesn't give a crap about students. Nit pick everything. Never specific about what he wants on midterms and homework, and then take off points off. Lectures are useless, just throw equations and vague explanations at students. This man has large ego, and is lazy.
Hard, but fair. Great teacher, makes sure you really learn the material.

Homework are light to decent amount, but they prepare for tests well. Also give practice tests before both midterm and final which reflects format well. There are questions in midterm and final that are not easy, but only a very small portion. In addition, MATLAB code writing is not in tests.
Professor Tian is very caring and always kind when answering students' questions. Make sure you do the homework, discussion worksheets, and practice exams and you'll be fine.

She is open for questions during class and very chill. also she does extra credit if you do a presentation on a certain chapter in class which helps to keep the class more engaged especially since its a math class.

Very nice. Listens to student's advices (only put HW on gradescope in beginning, but put it on canvas either later) and also rearrange canvas to make to clearer for students. HW are light, yet thought provoking. However, it contains coding in MATLAB, so definitely work harder in beginning if have no experience of it before.

Good lecturer and a very nice person too. Allowed us to drop some exams and quizzes. Very straightforward and discusses concepts in great detail. Just make sure you attend her lectures and all is fine

Dr. Zeigler is an excellent online instructor. Her course was clear, well-organized, and genuinely engaging. She explained complex topics in an approachable way and was always responsive and supportive. Grading was fair, and expectations were transparent. I truly felt supported and motivated to learn. Lab is pricey/pay close attention to directions
Tough grader. Don't take this course if you need it for a grade boost.

Professor Zeigler was an extremely fair grader and stuck to the syllabus. If you put in the effort, research your weekly written assignments and do not plagiarize you should perform well in the class. It is up to the individual to decide the grade that he or she deserves and this professor gives you the opportunity to succeed.  Will take again!
He made an 8am class very engaging, and he cares about students. He is also thorough in explanations. The only thing I disliked was the grading scheme.

He stops for questions and goes over quiz questions if they caused trouble for the entire class. Class was 90% exams (2 midterms + final) and final was no-fault. He clearly does not like guilt-tripping in response to a bad grade. His slides are a little hard to understand at times when looking after class so attending lecture is essential

Professor Russell is incredibly caring, yet maintains professionality. He heavily emphasizes and re-explains what material we should know for each test. Tests are not cumulative. If you pay attention during lecture, and review before tests, you will do well. Office hours are very helpful, and he is very accommodating.

Grade is basically just test scores. Tests were hardly curved. Refused to give any extra credit  even after multiple students had requested it, and proceeded to basically mock them for it at the next lecture… Wouldn't recommend.

Sad cause students used to love this prof but I think after catching them cheating last year, he's changed his attitude towards teaching/students a bit. Tests (90%) and weekly quizzes (10%) were fairly difficult, and I think he maybe used to “curve” more than he did for us now. Sweet guy objectively but not the nicest when it comes to being a prof.
easily the worst prof ive taken a class with

I'm not one to EVER complain about professors or even write reviews, but Kramer needs one. REFUSED to publish exam / hw solutions. Forced the TA to do basically ALL the teaching for this class. REFUSED to provide practice problems, insisting that we find them ourselves in the textbook, as he had better things to do. Very condescending.
Avoid at all costs.

We need more professors like this. Amazing lectures, very kind, answers questions, accessible, but very difficult class. You actually need to study and know your stuff for exams but he is self aware and trying to make you a smarter person. Math heavy, and just hope this is the only hard class you have that quarter.
Highly recommend you stay away

Class was easy but professor didnt teach much. You have to sign up to go to her office hours which is a 15 minute slot on Calendy and filled up really fast and I had to wait months to see her even for a mandatory accommodations meeting because she didnt respond to my email. My TA was amazing though, shout out to Mikkey, definitely reccommend.

The TA will make or break your experience (and grade) for the class. The Professor herself is very nice and has office hours that you can schedule to talk with her. There is 3 quizzes and 4 writing assignments and the writing assignments definitely take at least 2-3 hours. Can miss up to 2 lectures. Final is a group research poster presentation.

Professor Gamboa is so sweet and cares a lot about her students. She makes sure to clearly go over all of the conceptual material necessary to understand the lab for the week. My IA was Mikkey Compuesto and she was AWESOME. She made the lab setting feel less scary than it seemed and was very patient with everyone learning lab ettiquette.

Professor Ivonne González-Gamboa is an excellent instructor who genuinely cares about her students and their success. Her lectures for BILD 4 are engaging, well-structured, and focus on helping students understand the material rather than just memorizing it.
Gamboa lays out instructions and purpose of the lab at the start of the week so it should be an easy class. Lab is very fun if you get the right people. Would recommend this class!

Professor Trumbo is a great lecturer with easy-to-follow, interesting slides. I highly recommend taking her course for UCSD's JTCCER requirement. There's not a lot of math involved, and the pace is very manageable. The topics she covers are fun and will prepare you for the weekly homework. Discussion sections are helpful if you're stuck.

Such a kind person and easily accessible outside class, lectures are engaging and interesting. There's no final exam but instead an essay and a related project. Textbook is free and used for the weekly hw but also super helpful with understanding mathematic concepts as it provides simplified examples that are easy to follow. Highly recommend!

Great experience! Graded by 3 quizzes (equally weighted, no final), attendance and some easy HW assignments. She genuinely wants students to do well & if you understand her slides, the quizzes are very fair and doable.

A JOKE OF A PROF. Never knows anything about requirements, always gave incorrect word counts and corrected them 6 hours before it was due. Seems nice but knows nothing about whats going on and never helps. NEVER gives a straightforward answer to any questions. Dont bother going to office hours. Wait for another qtr and dont take it with her.

This class is known for being tough, but she makes it completely manageable. She's clear about what's expected, helps you develop your ideas, and really supports your writing. Pick a topic you actually care about and put in the effort, and you'll do great. And this is coming from someone who barely passed MCWP 40.

Professor Carter is a nice person but she is a headache as a professor. She will tell you that not going to class for a day is good as it will not affect your grade but IT INDEED DOES!! You really don't have a free day on the class which doesn't make sense. She is very picky with grading and does not tell you much into why points were taken away.
horrible. she can be caring but it can be hard to meet her expectations.

she claims theres a lot of wiggle room with learning check points which is somewhat true but when she asks you to summarize an article and you don't provide a specific detail from memory she will give you a 0
The lecture pace is a bit fast but other than that the midterms and final difficulty was as expected

Good lectures but can be rushed at times. Not an unreasonable amount of homework. Tests are fair and very similar to the practice tests. Discussion section attendance is mandatory, but lectures are not.

The midterms and final were pretty fair based on the lecture content and given practice exams. I honestly stopped showing up to the lectures after the first midterm because it felt like he went over the content too fast. Homework problems were okay and the lowest HW grade gets dropped.

Went to lecture like twice. His lectures are a bit all over the place, not very helpful. Used YouTube instead. Tests are honestly easy, I just barely studied. Homework is reflective of exams. Practice tests are very reflective of exams, just uses different numbers. Probably one of the easier 20D professors by far.

Pros: provides the material/formulas to succeed in the class and homework preps you for exams. 1-sided cheat cheat for midterms; 2-sided for final. Cons: no proofs or intuition for formulas. The class was effectively plug and chug because "the formula works." I would've waited a quarter for a different prof if I knew it would be this way.
the goat fr

Very passionate and lots of class/seat partner participation. Lectures and tutorial sections are both mandatory but she gives you more than enough resources to succeed in the class. Very nice and patient.
I took her one of her 135 classes and she was so great. So sweet and caring and overall great professor! Def one of the best I've met.

Iwamoto sensei is so sweet and caring! Her classes are well structured and organised. There is also a lot of repetition so the information sticks and doesn't go away after a couple days or so. Super fun class highly recommend!

kind, beautiful, the most caring soul you'll ever meet. her smiles make angels cry. i can hear harps playing when she speaks. to be honest, japn 20a has pretty difficult course material but she's definitely the kindest out of all the ucsd japanese professors. she really cares about all her students.

Professor Candido's ECON 110A class is very clear on the analysis of different long-term macroeconomic models and their applications. She is willing to help her students all the time and very responsive.

Professor Candido is my favorite lecturer at the economics department at UC San Diego. Her 120A class is not hard in general. It helped me build a solid foundation for statistics and future econometrics classes.

Professor Candido is the best economics professor at UC San Diego. I have taken three classes with her. Her instructions on econometrics are super clear. And she is always willing to help her students.

Easy course. Opportunity for extra credit by going to lecture. Practice exams are given that look like the real exams. Lectures aren't super helpful but you can learn from the slides pretty easily and lectures are recorded.

I had to drop the class before the first midterm because she had so many skips and wasn't lear about making up for those missed lessons, not even a simple announcement. Econ 120C is a challenging course and she doesn't really explain well, I don't even know what I learnt for the past month. Recommend someone else.
BIMM 128 with Hao was the easiest A I had. He definitely wants the best for students and specifically makes the class low stress. As long as you put in some effort, you're good.

Professor Hao's class was a great bio elective class. Class was mandatory as clickers (60%) were given at the end of each class. One group project that was worth 40% of grade but very clear grading if you went to office hours to get help. Readings were needed for clicker questions but was manageable just watching the presentations. Great class!

One of the best profs, so kind and funny. Course is focused on student learning and there are multiple papers to read, a quiz every class, and group presentations. You will learn so much in this course without high stress.

He intentionally makes the class low-stress so students can enjoy "learning about the science of aging research." One of the coolest classes I've taken at UCSD. Keep up with the readings and you'll learn so much! iClicker Qs are very straightforward and simple, and he grades the paper/presentation fairly. Please don't be rude and leave class early.

Such an incredible class and professor, and I can't recommend it enough. The content was so interesting and he was very knowledgeable about everything, it truly helped me understand so much about aging. He is very lenient with grading and just genuinely wants you to learn. 40% group presentation on a paper and 60% iClicker for other presentations!

Nice guy. Class had 10 readings that u use to write a synthesis + argumentative essay. There was little direction given on how to write but he gave very helpful feedback on the portfolio draft + held extra office hours in weeks 8-9. U get out what u put in so if u do the readings, attend class, go to office hours, + apply feedback you'll do well.

Sam is so kind and truly cares about his students succeeding. It is a difficult class with lots of reading, but incredibly doable. Sam provides so much great feedback every step of the way during the writing process. Also he is super funny. I wish he could be my writing professor for all my future writing classes too!

Nice dude. Gives lots of feedback to your writing, which can come off as harsh for some, but it makes it easier to understand the issues in your writing. There can be little direction at times for how you should write, and is mostly reliant on the textbook that he assigns you to read. Expect to talk during class and you will revise with your class.

He is amazing teacher he considers what the outcome will be in portfolios if you revise within his comments and feedback and do all the assignments with great participation, you will definitely going to pass the class. Although this class in general is hard to pass and lot of workload, he will do anything to help the students if you work hard.

He is incredibly lenient, so much so that it feels like high school level on that part. Do as your told and put in genuine effort and you're guaranteed to pass. He gives really good feedback and will work with you. He wants you to pass.

McCartney is very lenient with grading and gives take-at-home exams (which is why most people like him), but his lectures are very boring. He is not very accessible outside of class, and he seems to have difficulty communicating with his TAs about the curriculum and grading.

Professor professional is unclear, unfair, biased, condescending, and providing difficult, irrelevant, or boring content, with common complaints including confusing instructions, lack of rubrics, bias against differing opinions, and making students feel unintelligent.

I love McCartney in terms of his friendliness and leniency. His homework and exams are graded leniently and the average was A-. Weekly hw + lab, 1 midterm, and 1 final. Put in work and you should be fine. Definitely take him again

Professor McCartney is one of those few people you meet in life whose passion and knowledge of a subject shines through in every word they say. The man literally made a class about dirt engaging and interesting! I was really glad to have taken this class with him, and the UCSD SE department is lucky to have him as their department head!

Very traditional style of teaching, not suited for everyone. Lectures can feel disorganized at times. Tests are structured similarly to the homework, but are still very difficult. Very charismatic person, fun to interact with. Expect to struggle; the class isn't easy at all. Strongly recommend reading the textbook before class.

This professor is not for snowflakes, but if you care about the material and want to fully understand it, this is your guy. Exams and labs are tough but he cares about making sure you know your stuff and not just memorizing.

Professor doesn't really explain any of the topics at all and he goes off topic during the lectures. He also mentioned that if you any more elaboration on the topic, you have to go to the 140L lecture.
Alex is the best, but his CSE 140 is more like a 2-unit class while his CSE 140L is more like a 4-unit class, so the workload balances out.
Probably one of the hardest classes I've taken at UCSD, but also possibly my favorite. Alex is a great lecturer and he really changed the way I think about computer engineering.

Took Psyc108 & 169 with Prof Adrian. Very straightforward exams with clear study guides. Extra credit lecture attendance & sona. Engages with the class very well & material is so interesting. Lots of topics so if you're unfamiliar w neurosci- it might be tough. overall great experience :)

Exams were very fair. She provided a study guide that guided us on the content she expects us to know. Her expectations were very straightforward. Some parts of the exam could be confusing, but it's not ridiculous and is extremely fair. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you do get extra credit for attending!

Professor Adrian was super chill, and you see she's very passionate about the subject. Extra credit for attendance, three exams total along with weekly quizzes. The TAs and PLAs where very involved and provided great resources alongside the prof's OH. Straight forward study guides and no tricky questions on exams.

Attendance is optional BUT is extra credit, very transparent for the study guides and what is gonna be on the exam. Pretty straightforward and a decent teacher. I personally recommend as the lectures help a lot and its free extra credit for the class ur paying for

Though the content can be difficult, she has a great + clear way of explaining things. Never felt lost in her lectures. 2 midterms, 1 final (cumliv), quizzes that are basically hw/practice questions every week. Provides a study guide, if you can answer everything off of that you're set. Didn't expect to enjoy the class as much as I did!

Class was chill but writing heavy--grade determined mainly by midterm & essay, and then final (SAQ+essay). Very reading heavy so understand the reading quite well & in essays use philosophical language. Requires bluebook and a lot of writing.

Prof. Lamey is good. Idk why people are hating on him. Phil isn't my major but I enjoyed this course. Def thought-provoking and encourages discussion which is rare. Lots of reading and random, unscheduled quizzes but only 2 essays and a final exam essay. Overall, I'd say it was pretty easy. Prof. is funny and a selfproclaimed "benevolent dictator"
Easy class good teacher
This class was very enjoyable. The professor is good at teaching and I understood the material very well.

The professor is very lenient and allows you to miss 4 clicker without it jeopardizing your participation points. In this class you're graded off 3 papers and you get to choose what you write about,  with the list of potential essay topics given to you by the professor. Also, make sure your TA is not a critical grader.

Super easy A. Graded on quizzes and a final that are all online and asynchronous. Professor is very passionate about the subject and lectures are great when they're in person. However, she isn't very accessible outside of class (office hours are just after lecture) and canceled a lot of lectures to be online and asynchronous.

Super easy A. Graded on quizzes and a final, all of which are multiple choice and asynchronous. She is super passionate about what she teaches and in-person lectures are very engaging. However, she doesn't really hold office hours (just after lecture) and canceled a lot of lectures to be made up online.

Professor Boroditsky really cares about the subjects she teaches and it reflects in her lectures. Quizzes and final are online. The lowest quiz score is dropped. No homework assignments, except for the extra credit that is easy and quick to complete. A lot of reading. Lectures are posted if you miss class. Could not recommend more.

Easy A+ class! Bi-weekly quizzes and a final, all are online. She made the class very straightforward and interesting, she's very passionate about the subject and her outside research is also very cool! The hardest part is keeping up with the readings, I spent about 2+ hours weekly reading + taking notes on them. Definitely recommend

Class was pretty chill, online exams and final, weekly quiz's, content of the class was pretty cool if you like learning about perception, optical illusions, memory, etc. Overall a pretty easy class. Lectures were fairly engaging and Professor Boroditsky was always willing to answer questions and seemed excited to teach.
Very much regret not looking here before signing up for his class. He requires a group project that is disorganized and graded based on whatever he chooses that day, rather than his own rubric.
This was an unusually disorganized course and incredibly dry. It seemed like he phoned in the course entirely.
Group project is graded from whatever he feels like

Group project is INSANE. One of my group mates dropped and he told us we had to do her part. Fine, except the other group member refused to help with the other part and ignored me constantly, did her part wrong without giving me time to edit it and even though I messaged the prof several times about the problems I was having he almost failed us.

Course is unnecessarily hard for a 3 unit course. I deeply regret taking this course as I only needed a 3 unit stats course but the amount of work makes it feel like a 5-6 unit course. The group project had no clear set of directions and the discussions were also graded with no clear rubric.

Overall, the class was fun and a breather from separate classes. Class mainly taught by TA (Kennedy Tolson) who is overall great. Work load is more than do able, periodic reading (Free) + Q&As, 3 speeches that are graded lightly. Class involves speaking exercises/speech practices = step out of comfort zone = better public speaker.

Carla is an absolute joy. She is one of the most kind, caring, and intentional teachers I have ever experienced. She is a consummate professional and manages time perfectly. Her feedback is so unbelievably meaningful and genuine. Her patience is extraordinary and one of a saint. You can see and feel the passion and joy she has being here!

The class is mostly based on your TA, I had Kenneth and he was genuinely the greatest mentor I could've ever asked for, but Carla stopped by a couple of times. She was so sweet and caring and obviously so passionate about what we were doing. Such an amazing class would take and recommend a million times over.

Super easy class. However, the class is taught entirely by your TA. I saw Professor Harting twice during the quarter. Participation is important, and attendance is mandatory. Easy grading, just show that you put in effort and you'll do well. There is a textbook, but it's free and you only really need it for the biweekly quizzes.

Best course ever taken in UCSD. Gets you out of your comfort. 90%of the class got an A. And unlike most easy A courses, you actually get to learn SO MUCH from this course in public speaking. Course is led by TA, and my TA was the best. So easy going, and chill, you can literally talk about anything you want in the class. 100% recommended.

Really passionate and engaging professor. As a non-lit major taking this class for gen-ed, I really enjoyed it. The material is complex, but the professor discusses it thoughtfully and clearly. Essays relate directly to the readings and are usually open-book or open-note. Highly recommend, especially for lit majors.

Wonderful, kind, and passionate professor! Midterm and final are in person, but you are permitted any handwritten notes and your books. If you keep up with the lectures and readings, you will do great! Assignments consist of quizzes and writings done in discussion, along with the midterm and final, so take good notes! Would highly recommend :)

Very nice professor, more on the quiet side but has a great understanding and explanation of the subject. Pop quizzes and in-class writing assignments are done during section. The midterm was short response and the final was two essay questions, both done in person. 4 books total as well as other poems/short stories in his course reader.

Great professor, really cares about his students and is open to hearing different perspectives. He can be a little awkward at times, but you can tell he just wants everyone to participate. Midterm was an essay, grading criterion were pretty clear. The final was a creative project; he gives you a lot of freedom to focus on what interests you.
Ameeth is a very cool guy. He knows his topic well and always inspires his students to further their thinking.

I went to her office hours one time to ask her a question and she said she couldn't answer my question because she was "busy". With no warning on Piazza that she'd be busy on her office hours. This happened multiple times too.

Her lectures move very quickly and often times you're trying to catch up. Her grading rubric is very confusing and you get points off on things you shouldn't. The exam itself has no study material prep. The TA's don't provide much help and often times tell you to just use chat GPT.
Pretty easy class, and she gives a lot of extra credit opportunities. I certainly felt like I learned a lot of deep learning in this class!

Yes she's an easy A as long as you do the busy work, but not like that matters given how rotten her personality is. Class was absolutely not set up in a way that promoted student success and you'll be mocked for asking an honest question. Not gonna lie that she's probably a brilliant researcher, but that's what she should focus on, not teaching!

She may be a good researcher, but she is definitely not a good professor. She is kind of arrogant and her lectures are not clear. She says strange remarks, such as: for multiple answer choices, if you don't know all, you don't know; instead of complaining, you should give constructive feedback on improvement.

If you're considering taking this professor, do it. He is very understanding, caring, and wants you to succeed. His PSYC 104 class has the same exact content as Michael McCullough's PSYC 6, so if you took that class, take this one immediately. Lowest exam dropped, attendance not mandatory. Highly recommend.

i dont get the bad reviews prior to this. its my last year here and this upper div was one of the easiest ones ive taken. lectures can be a bit boring, but the exams have been SO easy compared to other classes. there are no trick questions, so just watch lecture + reviews and you're good. he drops one exam, curves, and gives extra credit. TAKE HIM!
Don't take him. Exams are worth 90% of grade.

I hyped up this prof. halfway thru the quarter. Regret. 
I got an A, but be ready to put up with extremely slow grading timelines and late-quarter assignments with little guidelines and a passive-aggressive professor. 

A is definitely attainable, just know what you'll be dealing with. Exam 2 wasnt graded for 6 weeks for some.

Very disorganized and passive aggressive, the entire class was a mess and extremely unaccommodating to students. The canvas was not organized until halfway through the semester, there was barely enough time to take the quizzes, and some students didn't even get their midterms back until AFTER THE FINAL. Interesting material but horrible execution.
dont even try w this prof. save urself time and dignity.
Took almost two months to grade midterms, quizzes, and assignments. The TAs grade harshly. Do not take any class with this professor. would not recommend.

takes forever to grade (took almost six weeks to receive grade on midterm 2); no real opportunities to actually practice what is learned in lecture; confusing lecture format and difficult to study for quizzes
The course was challenging, and at times the grading felt unclear due to her vague expectations!! Lectures were very difficult and did not always align closely with exams.

Get ready for very challenging exams, difficult lab reports, and two finals in the last week worth almost 50% of your grade. She is not very supportive of students without a strong molecular biology background. Homework questions are extremely hard and you lose points often. I would take this class with anyone but her.

Class is very hard and concept is not easy to follow. She expects student to know a lot of details about molecular biology. Exams are super hard and she does not care about class average and wants to challenge students. TAs are not good and helpful and they do not answer questions. They are very fake.

Wonderful prof who not only knows her stuff, but cares about you actually learning it. You get a lot of review/practice material that help solidify the content. Really doable class for anyone and she's super accessible and will help you learn the material.

the BEST bild 1 prof. SO sweet and genuinely wants her students to succeed. 3 midterms (drops lowest) and a final. tests were difficult but you're allowed a study sheet. lectures are mandatory but very engaging! pay attention in class and have a good study sheet and this class will be a breeze.

Course was Comm115. The only thing on Canvas is the readings. Attendance isn't mandatory, but she gives worksheets during class sometimes that you can use during your final, and she doesn't post slides. The only thing graded is the final exam which is a 20-30 minute conversation w/ the prof. You smell a lot of things in class and very engaging.

No work, just an oral exam (conversation) as a final that was pretty easy. Confusing grading criteria but still received an A for demonstrating some ability to connect topics to communication. Course was COMM 115.

Comm & Social Machines was a fun, intellectually stimulating class. You could tell she was passionate about this subject because lots of the readings were co written by her! Homework was frequent but easy. She's not a fan of Canvas so don't expect due date reminders or slides being posted so make sure you go to class/know someone if you miss.

Professor Morana is very knowledgeable and well-read, so to keep up with the class you have to keep up with he readings. Although attendance isn't mandatory, go. The slides alone are useless unless you attend and hear what's being discussed in class. Also, ASK QUESTIONS, she loves it! TAs are useless tho, so study hard and you'll be ok.

Easy to attain full credit for hw on weekly readings, lecture itself was very long, boring, and fuzzy. Lectures not mandatory but suggested, doesn't record her lecture and lecture slides don't contain lesson material. Hard to follow along what she's trying to teach because she isn't clear on subject material, you rely heavily on TA's to understand.

SO MANY READINGS. Did I do them? No. I gave up after the first week, she goes over the readings in class. Graded literally only on the 2 midterms and final (and maybe attendance idk). Lectures not posted, slides could've been better.

Prof Nelkin is really supportive and caring towards her students. Because of my schedule conflicts, I cannot make her regular office hours, but she always makes the effort to find alternative times to meet with me. In addition, I can feel that she attempts to remember students' names.

Professor Nelkin is kind and nice. I think this class is helpful for me. I do speech and debate, the content taught by this course can be helpful sometimes. The lecture also is good, it helps you understand reading materials better.

Very kind and understanding, and clearly very knowledgable about the subject matter. Willing to adapt to help her students and their needs, and was very accessible. Clear lectures, and the content of the exams are clearly laid out in lecture and the readings, so as long as you engage with the course material, you'll excel.

I say this with all sincerity, avoid this class at all costs! The other reviews stating that she is boring, uninspiring, and makes the class material unnecessarily confusing are completely true. Lectures dragged and we were always left scratching our heads

Once a week, watch a movie, complete a 5 question true/false quiz for participation. One 35 question midterm and final (same question format). Super easy, fulfills Fine Art requirement, highly recommend! Prof tries to host discussions each lecture, I do recommend saying atleast something to break the silence, doesn't have to be remotely profound.

super easy fine arts ge, she lectures for 30 mins and then you watch the movie. 5 question attendance quiz on lectures due at midnight the next night. 35 question midterm and final on canvas open until midnight the next night + optional extra credit paper on a cult film of your choosing. gives extra credit for set evals too. low stress, i recommend

Great person, she is clearly very passionate on the subject and movies she teaches and discusses. Class is super easy, she talks for a few minutes, we watch a movie and discuss afterwards. After each class an easy quiz is required (if missed it won't open back up for you). Class is graded via quiz, final, midterm, all super easy and on canvas.

One of the best professors I've had, and an interesting class. Easiest class, graded by only midterm, final, and attendance quizzes from lecture content. Open book exams, and you can look up the movie if you don't wish to stay during the time. Extra credit paper for a 5% grade boost. Honestly would 100% recommend!

AMAZING! My media/film literacy was kinda bad, so I took this class to grow in that. I wanna take all her classes now, I learned so much. AMAZING film picks. All you have to do is show up once a week and watch the movie. Take some notes during her lectures before & after the film, and you will get 100's on the exams, they are very straightforward
Exams are really fair and easy to follow. There is 15% only attendance based on clicker questions. She is very nice and concept is very easy to understand.

Not so bad at all. The lectures were pretty easy, not too difficult to understand. As long as you understand her iClickers, you can do well on the exams. She only does midterm 1 and final exam, as always.

Pretty straightforward class, not really tricky.

I LOVE PETRIE! She is so sweet, and her lectures are engaging. She draws little doodles, and explains concepts very nicely. Easily my favorite class this quarter. She is very understanding, and grades in a reasonable matter so long as you put in effort to learn (attend lecture and section, do quizzes, etc.) She offers extra credit, and is fair.

I loved Dr. Petrie! She's so funny, and I loved all her doodles on lecture slides that make concepts easy to follow. We get cheat sheets on exams, and I always rarely needed to use them, besides an equation or two. No calculator on tests, but math was always simple, dividing by 1000, etc. It was a fun and easy class to take in my last quarter here.

Petrie clearly outlines what the key takeaways for the class are. She is approachable, has a way of simplifying concepts, and tells you what she expects from all the online assignments. iclicker & discussion is mandatory but there is plenty wiggle room. Those who complain about the class structure clearly only care about getting an easy A.

Class was a yap session. I'm a Bio major who know nothing abt USP. Lectures were lacking a key takeaway topic. TA was nice but harsh grader. Feedback on my essays was basically "needs more depth". My essay was 1,000 words I didn't know what else to say... Grade was made up of 3 essays + 1 group project. Give real effort on your essays i guess

Pezzoli seems like a great guy, but his teaching style is all over the place. Assignments will have 3 different docs all with differing instructions; it is very confusing. The lectures aren't that related to the assignments either. My TA was also a harsh grader marking us down for things that weren't even specified in the rubric or instructions.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU HAVE ADHD!!!

I deeply respect Keith Pezzoli for everything he's done for the USP department and I admire his expertise and passion. HOWEVER -- this class was impossible to follow and frankly a pain to get through. He says so much yet so little. His instructions might as well be in a foreign language.

I feel really terrible giving Keith anything but 5 stars because as a person he is incredible. His class however, was a mess. He somehow said SO MUCH and yet so little. Lectures were unorganized and just him rambling. It will probably be better next quarter because he was trying a new project and he worked out most of the kinks with our class.

LOVED Pezzoli! He is very passionate about his work and teaching. Assignments consist of one paper, a take-home midterm, and final project. For the lectures though, it's important to at least skim the readings otherwise you won't know what's going on and it will be impossible to write the paper. Overall, the material was interesting and engaging.

Professor Pham is very caring and genuinely wants his students to succeed. He gives lots of partial credit and his tests are very fair. The class is definitely not the easiest, but Professor Pham is a great lecturer who makes the content palatable.
I felt like lectures were unhelpful. I studied most of the content by reading the textbook. The homeworks were unusually hard.
Nice class
His classes are very fair and is an excellent professor

I have never coded before, so his class was hard for me. However, he is a caring professor to help you outside of class and wants you to successfully learn from his classes. Homework took me a long time, but was relatively similar to the lectures. Understanding coding took a while, but I was able to successfully finish with the TA's lab sessions.

Course MGT 105. Chill dude. Lowk nonchalant. First test lowk took me by surprise, but I did good the other two. There's two individual small projects and one group project at the end. Three-hour lectures were longgg, but he gave a break in the middle. Didn't take attendance, but doesn't record the lecture. 3 exams are around 47-50 questions.

Very laid back class. Just studying the slides and taking some notes are enough to pass the class. If you like marketing than it may be the class for you, but otherwise its kinda boring. 3hr long lectures do make it a drag to get through but not a hard class at all. Chill guy as well.

engaging lecturer and interesting professor, but provided poor support and lack of guidance to students for exams and final project. three hour lecture format is difficult to focus and he does not record lectures. material was not difficult overall, just get ready for a LOT of memorization
Great teacher, the 3 hour class just made it hard for me to stay focused. I ended up doing textbook readings which helped a lot for the tests. The group project is also really straightforward!

One of the best lecturers at UCSD imo. Very engaging and just generally a cool dude. The class itself is a lot of term memorization, so quizlet will be your homie for the tests. The hw is super light, maybe an hour per assignment. There's also a group project, so make sure you take this class with some friends if you can. Overall a chill class.

Amazing, sensible, intelligent, courteous and down-to-earth professor and overall inspiring human being. Fascinating and diverse class material (e.g. Soviet Science Fiction: Hard to Be God; artistic films: 'Stalker' etc.). Do yourself a favor and register and learn good Russian-Vy ne pozhalete! My only regret is not taking the course for credit.

Rebecca is such a G. She is clearly passionate and cares a ton about her students. Discussion sections count for participation points so make sure to go. There are weekly quizzes but they're not bad and she grades on the easy side. She is always there if you need extra help and makes the classroom such a fun place to be. She always has a smile on.

Professor Wells is amazing; she really cares about her students and overall is a pretty easy grader. There is about one quiz per week on the topics covered that week as well as a final at the end. Participation and homework account for the rest of the grade. She is super flexible and wants to help her students. 10/10 prof.
Amazing teacher! It cant be easy teaching on Zoom but she still manages to pull it off! Great teacher and am really hoping I can learn from here in an actual classroom setting!

Rebecca is a really good Russian professor. She always is sure to make us actually speak and apply what we've learned to an actual conversation, but the participation never feels hostile. Her little rhymes and sayings stuck in my head and became useful later when forming sentences and such. Just show up and participate and you will be good.

TBH just make a solid cheat sheet for exams. Lecture slides posted right before exams and attendance isn't mandatory. The grading policies for reading memos (pass/fail + point deductions) weren't as clearly defined as I expected, so I'd recommend clarifying memo expectations early. He's responsive to emails.

Prof Navon is such a good lecturer! I really looked forward to going to class each day. His curriculum was really interesting, and he made time for discussions at the end of class. Weekly pass/ fail reading memos, one midterm, and the final. Completely recommend!

He genuinely has the best lectures ever – they're so engaging and easy to understand. He also replies to emails quickly and is so accessible outside of class. A double sided note sheet is allowed for the midterm and final. Attendance isn't taken but you should attend regardless because lectures aren't posted until the week of exams. Take his class

Amazing course content and super engaging lecturer. We got a note sheet for the exam, which really helped me do well on the midterm. I really like Professor Navon -- he is kind, engaging, and informative. I would definitely recommend this class!

Professor Navon is an excellent lecturer! Lectures are not mandatory, but are not recorded and slides are not posted until the week before an exam. Sounds intimidating but very do-able! We had a double-sided cheat sheet for our Midterm and Final Exam. Would greatly recommend this class if you need to fill a requirement or even if you're a soc major

Great professor, accessible and clear lectures. Weekly homework problems. 1 Group Project, just a large homework assignment. Professor will give homework and project answers in Office Hours. CENG 110 was fun, added lab section to CENG 100 course, same material and pacing.

Best professor I've had so far! Good lectures, plenty of example problems, gives practice tests that are very similar to the exams. She is passionate about her work, fair tests, lots of feedback, and always accessible in office hours. I'd definitely recommend taking her over anyone else if given the opportunity.

My favorite chemical engineering professor so far! Professor Powell explains things clearly, has excellent slides, and is readily available during office hours and outside of class. Can't recommend her class highly enough
Professor Powell is fantastic! The content is very challenging but she teaches it well, sets clear expectations, and has generous office hours. Would absolutely recommend.
Great professor, very clear with what's going to be on tests, provides ample practice material, homework is never too difficult, and her lectures are really easy to understand.

Overall DOC 1 was a pretty interesting class and Dr. Villegas was a great professor. The class involved a lot of reading (anywhere from 5-50 pages of reading per lecture) but very few assignments and in-class exams were fairly easy. Each assignment and exam had very clear rubrics and class wasn't difficult.

Probably the nicest DOC professor. The class is pretty much the same despite which professor you pick, but I believe her tone of voice is less monotonous/boring in lectures. She also brings her cute little dog sometimes.

She's so woke it's annoying. She is uneducated about anything having to do with real life and doesn't understand anything to do with politics yet that is what she teaches she preaches about being inclusive but hates white people and doesn't accept religion would never want to take this class again

I LOVE PROF VILLEGAS! You can tell she's passionate about what she teaches, which is so inspirational. Her dog is the cutest ever which she brought to lecture a few times. Other DOC teachers yell at their students, but she's patient with usnot strict at all. Pls take Villegas if you want an stress-free doc class. Can't wait for next quarter w her.
Pretty chill lectures. Has a cool dog so thats pretty cool.

professor genuinely cares for students and loves what she teaches. very short MCQ quiz in the beginning of class and 1 midterm + final that are mostly short answer questions. there's a group project throughout the quarter so make sure to contribute because ur members rate you based on that. + a short 5 minute presentation on week 10

She's an amazing person but the class can be a little work heavy especially if your group for the project is not very involved. However, the final and mt had reasonable Qs (MC+short ans) so if you study the lectures/book you should be good. There's a reading quiz every class 4 Qs, pretty easy but you need to buy the book or go to geisel reserves.

Dr. Deal is a phenomenal teacher and inspirer  she takes every opportunity she gets to help students improve their conceptual understanding of the material and she makes it fun along the way! Do the reading, pay attention in lectures, be a helpful group member in the group project, and you will be successful.

Professor Deal is one of the sweetest people I have met. She cares about her students and it honestly made me sad when people wouldn't participate. I had personal issues while taking her class and she was more than accommodating and considerate. A little unorganized with the assignments but overall funny and caring.

Professor Chatti was respectful, took student feedback seriously, and is obviously passionate about the subject matter. The course itself has readings for hw, five 1000 word essays, one individual presentation and group presentations for the midterm and final—seems like a lot of work when written out but easier than it sounds. Highly recommend!

Took CGS 134 at UCSD this quarter for an upper div climate change class as a STEM major, and I have never enjoyed a class more. She is so nice and amazing, and she made me love a subject area I usually hate. The class is mostly a chill class discussion. Don't get scared on the first day because she makes the class seem like a lot of work.

When I say I hate CS, I mean it. I suck at it, but she made me want to wake up at 8 am four days a week for her lectures. No complex coding involved. She makes lectures beginner-friendly. You can retake quizzes and midterms—except the final. You get 4 free lecture absences and 2 lab absences. Tutors and TAs are helpful. She genuinely cares& helps.

Taking this class at 8 am was a trip ngl. I liked this class and how it was structured– quiz at the beginning of class on Tuesday, lab the following day, homework due Sunday but could turn in up to 24 hours late (no penalty). 2 midterms and 1 cumulative final. I barely studied for anything but still passed. I have no prior programming skills btw.
Just don't take this professor

This class itself is easy but the attendance in 8 in the morning is not that necessary. This professor uses webclicker, a live poll to take your attendance for most of the time, sometimes handout. 8 in the morning it is just hard to paying attention.

The hardest thing with this class for me is probably getting up on time for the 8 AM lecture, participation is count using a site to answer question during class. The class has weekly quiz but if you follow the lectures and assignments I think the quiz are pretty easy. Can be a bit hard for people with no coding knowledge but overall its fine.

She was great. Lectures were optional. Quizzes were online with 2 attempts and problem sets also had 2 attempts. The final was also online which was convenient with 1 attempt allowed. She cares about her students and her grading is fair. Highly recommend.

(Fall 2025) This class was mainly online. Lectures were optional, but extra credit was provided for attending discussion sections. Dr. Pekkurnaz enjoys presenting up to date research, and she seems kind to interact with. Lectures were mixed between engaging and filler content. The discussions were most helpful with covering exam topics.

This class was my first at UCSD so I did not know how to study. However, she does cover a lot in class and talks a lot about her research lab. However she curves the class like crazy, I don't know how I got an A but its possible. Get ready to study a lot because the topic is tedious and yes its hard but thats just how biology is in general.

Great professor!! You actually LEARN something. Everyone complaining about the extra credit and the bad test averages needs to stop; she curves the class very generously so most people get As. Chill out. But the lectures are fascinating and so is the Proff. She's very smart and still one of my favorites to learn from and talk to. Recomend!

The professor promised us bonus points on extra credit assignments and then went back on her word and removed our extra credit 50 point bonus for our assignment, she had changed it to 5% instead. She does care about the students though, very considerate of making sure we understand the material by using lots of examples from her own lab. Like alot.

he seems like a cool guy who is passionate about his work but if youre looking for structure in a classroom its not here. no grades on assignments, only a got a final grade a week after quarter ended. classes usually felt like seminars, where you talk about your work + design in general, but he gives very helpful feedback + has alot of knowledge

The most unorganized, poorly designed course I've ever taken. Harsh, unclear grading rubrics, ambiguous instructions, and probably the most unserious professor of all time. An overall insult to the integrity of UCSD. Spare yourself the time and effort and avoid this class. You can learn the entire content of this course in 15 minutes.
Do not take his class!
doesnt even show up to class and has extremely unfair participation rubric. multiple students spoke out about the poor structure of the class and little to no changes were made.

this professor was very unorganized—the rubric was changed mid-quarter, which frustrated a lot of students. it often took a few days to get email responses, and the TAs were either unresponsive or graded harshly and inaccurately. lectures weren't mandatory, but discussion sections were. easy to get an A if you do your work correctly.

His class consists of lab reports, participation, and 2 presentations. There are no midterms or final. It's a lot of walking since lab data is collected all over campus. The lab reports require R studio but he is more than happy to help you figure it out. Attendance isn't mandatory but he has participation points for data sheets during lab.

This professor is very chill. The class uses the R software for the assignments which can be confusing but you have plenty of time during the class to work on it and get help. There is lots of walking and field trips that are optional. Two presentations during week 9. Overall pretty chill lab, probably the chillest one i've taken at ucsd.

Class consists of 6 labs, 2 presentations, and participation. Lots of walking required. He uses the coding program R for the labs, which can be pretty frustrating if you do not like/know anything about coding. Also, he's a very tough grader when it comes to the labs. Class can be a bit boring at times but just show up, do the work, and you can pass

He podcasts all of the lectures which is nice, and he posts the slides before class. His lectures are really interesting if you're into bugs, but its a lot of information. The exams are pretty straight forward especially since he gives you a study guide. Not an easy A but possible.

Grade is made up of three exams and a bug collection project. It's not that hard but if ur not too interested in bugs I wouldn't rec this class esp if ur just looking for a 'filler' class (lol). Bare minimum...just fill out the entire study guide, memorize it and you'll probs manage to get an A. Also do the bug collection early it's easy and fun.

I did not realize some professor at UCSD still don't understand that there are +/- in the grading system, not just raw A, B, and C. half of the class failed in the other section and > 1/3 failed in ours, I highly do not recommend him for math 103

I took Professor Suk in Spring of 24, solid professor. Lectures are podcasted, exams cover material from lectures mostly, and exams (minus the final) are entirely explained and the material on there is fairly taught. The final was MCQ due to the TA strike but should be normal during most years.

Andrew Suk is a great professor. It's ok if you are simply taking his class for credit. However, if you really want to learn something, I'll recommand other teachers' class. Suk's courses is based on book, but the textbook is more elaborate than his lecture. I can't see any points attending the class.
super fair and grades fairly. one of my favorite profs here at UCSD

Average teacher.   Examples are straight from the book.  Some of the material on the test was learned just a few days before the test.  He would review test material during the class before test which was helpful.  Tests were fair.  Discussion attendance is mandatory.

This prof makes this class so much harder than it needs to be-especially the exams. It is very difficult to sift through the 250 slides to find the right information to study, my best advice is to teach yourself the main concepts from the book.

No matter how many lectures I went to I could not understand how his exams worked. His lectures are interesting and makes sense. But, his questions format need to change or his teaching needs to change according to the formatting of the questions. A class on making the workplace better, should also apply to the learning environment as well.
I lost interest in my career path because of this class

Terrible lecturer, extremely hard to tell what's going to be tested. Material is easy, but exams are unreasonably difficult. Doesn't make study guides as he claims his lecture slides are "extremely detailed". They are 250 pages long and have vocab copied directly from the textbook + meaningless news articles. 

Nice guy, but shouldn't be teaching.

Good professor that cares about students. Class based on 2 midterms 1 final and 2 papers. Papers really easy. Exams are hard (if you do bad on one you'll likely get a bad grade in the class) there's nothing to balance out the grades (no homework). Exams based on slides 200+ slides per exam. No studyguide and hard to study for. Dont buy textbook!!

Good prof. Exams hard but material youve seen before. Final is extremely hard but he curves the class 1-2 letter grades. The HW is long but representative of the exams. Expect to spend 10 hours per week on this course.

Brutal final exams that are worth a lot of your grade. Try not to get caught up on the midterms and your performance in them, and focus on deeply understanding the later half of the course since it matters a lot.

Amazing lecturer, but not so great at emphasising what is important for the exams. I found the office hours schedule with the professor and TAs wanting - a class this difficult needs more opportunities to ask questions during the quarter. Extra hours before exams do nothing. Work through the book, lectures do not cover everything you need!
he genuinely cared for his students and took feedback. it was just a hard class in general lol

If you try to enroll in his Math 142a and Math 142b lectures, I strongly suggest that you enroll in other professors' sessions. My five friends and I all find him terrible at teaching his course. The exam is very hard, and he didn't give partial credit for your answer in the exam. I don't understand why people are giving him a good rating.

He is such a sweet and caring professor, and always makes sure to explain things if we don't understand. He is a good lecturer and makes the content easily digestible. A lot of extra credit for going to lectures/discussions, and only the midterm and final go in the grade book.

Super nice, his lectures can be wordy but I think this is inevitable with molecular bio. Grade is based off of only exams, but they're extremely similar to the weekly optional problem sets and all multiple choice. Attendance is extra credit!

Actually goated. He writes all of the problem set and exam questions so they're all very consistent. Class is mostly memorization but his slides are very organized and easy to keep track of. Very accessible and answers questions without making you feel dumb. Belongs in the UCSD hall of fame with Matthew Flagg.

GOAT. His lectures were quite engaging & well-organized; he was always accessible to students and eager to answer questions. Grading is 60% final and 40% midterm, but you get 7% extra credit for lecture/discussion attendance. Exam questions are very similar to the weekly psets. Tests are mostly multiple-choice w/ some multiple-answer. Fun class

Really helped to explain concepts in a way that was digestible and understandable. I did really well on his first exam due to his teaching style. You can tell he really wants students to succeed. Only got a C due to unforeseen personal circumstances. I would highly recommend this professor especially to those who may be a little shaky on molec bio.

I have no advice because this class is very difficult if it is not easy for you to remember trivial details. Curve is aggressive. Skip lecture and learn the slides. Very detail oriented tests. Can't emphasize that enough. TA Neal was great be sure to study the review session worksheets. The questions came up a lot on exams.

Never went to a single lecture in this quarter and only reviewed based on the slides. The slides are very detailed and indeed required time to understand. Going over the slides twice will be enough and it's helpful to study with your friends when it's getting hopeless.

Grade is based almost entirely on midterms and finals. Everything is based on lecture slides, which are very specific and dense. Prof is very passionate about concepts and research, but not a very good teacher. It's possible to do well if you dedicate a lot of time to it. Do not recommend, especially if you have a heavy course load.
He's passionate about science and research but a terrible teacher. Just reads off the slides, no class engagement, no homework assignments or structure, 3 exams = your grade.

Late review by I had him in the fall and liked him. His policy is anything on the lectures is fari game on exams, so if you learn the lecture slides you'll do fine. He tends to emphasize in lecture what will be on the exam. The TA (luke!) was phenomenal with helping for exams, not sure how this class would have gone without luke.

Prof Morris is a great guy who is enthusiastic about his lectures. He adds a lot of fun facts which is good because it gives the students some mental prep before fully committing to ECE. His labs are fun but he does not really provide a lot of help on them, the TAs do all the guiding and helping though.

Professor Morris knows how to make the class engaging while still teaching the material. Labs can be difficult at times, and are time consuming. Directions can be vague at times but don't shy away from asking the IA's for help.
The lectures were engaging and helpful. Homework is required but you don't actually have to do the problems. Labs were somewhat helpful, if not kinda infuriating, especially the last two labs.

prof and TAs are very nice. the final is a group project and the homeworks are labs. prof offers office hours and explain coursework very patiently. attendance to labs is mandatory and counts for points. he also has a short 3 or 4 question quiz each week on stuff he covered in lectures.

The class is tough but if you put in the effort you will do well. I don't know why the other students said it was so hard. This is a major class.

Professor Drazen Petrovic is the best Math Professor at USD, he is extremely kind and understanding. He wants his students to suceed.

The best teacher I've ever had at UCSD, and I don't say that lightly. made 20B an amazing class considering the difficulty.

I loved prof Gwen for syn1. She was super caring towards her students and her office hours were very useful. Loved her! She was very kind and engaging and fostered an environment where students felt encouraged & comfortable to interact with each other. She is a very nice and understanding person, which makes the class more enjoyable. Since AWP3 is a required class, attendance is mandatory and the final grade depends on the final essay. Maybe it was just the course workload that made it difficult paired with my other courses that I had to write papers for but she definitely doesn't like her job.

Cool prof. Obviously, the TA you get matters more when it comes to MMW classes, but Carreras is chill. Professor Heyman is very involved in developmental psych and really knows what she is talking about, but I feel her lectures are weak. Test are heavily based on lecture. Manageable if you attend and pay attention to lecture. No recordings. Lectures are super interesting.

I don't really know how she's ever gotten any good reviews. More than half of the test content is basically "One time I said..." It's not about any actual material and her structure is a complete mess. Save urself the time and effort.

Attendance not mandatory but no recording or notes(barely) posted. His teaching was.. okay, but the homework load was crazy. Super passionate about linear algebra. He really knows his stuff and it shows. Lots of homework, and he doesn't upload lectures but show up to class and you'll be fine. easy A, has a small ego/hard to talk to at times, a lot of hw, difficult to understand lecture at times but just go over ur notes like a normal person, hw can be VERY difficult but nothing like the test lmao i feel like a math 18 student can take that final and pass if i were to teach them for a hour.
prof very passionate n good at teaching. good

Hugely caring professor, incredibly engaging lecturer. You will learn so much.

Suraj the GOAT! Had him in EECS 245 this fall. His lectures are engaging and digestable, office hours are super helpful, and the course notes are very in depth and helpful for learning. Class was difficult content wise but it never felt overbearing with how helpful the teaching staff was.

Suraj is amazing. Had him for EECS245 (UMich) and he lectures very clearly and in a way you can follow. He's very kind and eager to meet and discuss, and cares about students beyond the class. Took Practical Data Science at UM. Suraj was an incredible professor who was able to break down everything from pandas to clustering and between flawlessly. BIEB 141 is a difficult math class and does not feel like a BIEB lab. Worksheets are confusing and even after paying careful attention in lecture students were having a hard time. Very strict grading. First midterm felt doable, but after that, the concepts were not very well taught and rushed.  Quizzes have trick questions. The content of this class is fairly straightforward for most bio majors. Prof does not like questions or respond to them respectfully. Homework is graded very tough and help is not provided.

Quizzes are often intentionally tricky.

Prof is clearly trying to be generous but his approach to teaching is that students should know the content coming in
It was also a very easy course, the previous rating I put 5 as difficulty as an accident but it doesnt let me edit
Best professor ever, I took both USP 5 and USP 25 really great person and would recommend

I never write reviews but Professor Sun is literally the best. He makes challenges lectures so simple and walks you through everything step by step. He is also super supportive and always willing to help if you don't understand the content.
He really is the goat. Explains everything so well, and the assignments are very straightforward.
He's the Goat.

The course itself is not hard however, if you're not a theatre major it will be mind-numbingly boring and be prepared to act. She has an enthusiastic teaching style which keeps the class interesting. Skim the plays and pay attention to the lecture slides for the quizzes in discussion. She's really enthusiastic and you can tell she cares about her students. I was skeptical about taking this course but professor jade made it worth the while.

She is a really good professor and I strongly recommend her. As a Bio major I took this class for a GE and now I might end up using it for a minor. Her class isn't hard at all but you do learn a lot, and stuff you can actually see in the real world.

AMAZING PROF!! shes so sweet, understanding, and caring. there is a lot of hw and quizzes but thats because of the japanese program, not her fault. fun lectures!
She is such a kind and awesome teacher! I loved her class and felt like it was super helpful. Definitely recommend her.

I took Takeda Sensei for 20A-C and she is the best Professor I've ever had! She is so kind and caring and an amazing teacher. Great Professor!
Super nice and easy

The professor had interesting (mandatory) lectures. The course was fairly easy overall since there were no tests, but I felt that some of the rubrics for the homework and research project were vague and sometimes points were taken off without explanation.

Awesome prof!! would take again!! He's so sweet and makes lectures fun! Discussion are also great. Weekly readings and quizzes but they are extremely short and easy!! Iclicker is required. 3 Projects throughout the quarter but super easyyy. No exams and class is mandatory.

Professor Amoa-Bosompem was engaging and gave interesting lectures. Lectures and discussions were mandatory, but assignments were easy and helped teach the material. So so so kind! Grading depends largely on your TA, but they are all lovely. Shoutout to Rachel! Guest speakers often for lectures, and clickers are used to answer questions during for attendance points —> important! But you don't have to answer all to get the points. Assignments are straightforward, no exams! Weekly quizzes off a reading, but good.

I can't stress how amazing this professor is, he was passionate about the subject and welcomed discussions during class making the class super engaging! Weekly readings and quizzes but they're relatively easy. You have 2 papers and a group presentation instead of midterms/final, not extremely hard either. Take him if you can he's awesome! :)

Wants you to learn by trial and error. Sweet and very pretty. She doesn't give feedback at all which sucks. Attendance is absolutely mandatory. Miss once? You're dropped. Don't do the academic form? Passed the class P/NP. P/NP, 1 unit. All you have to do to pass is show up and do the worksheet of the day. Easy class, just being introduced to CENG concepts.
