Kind person, and good feedback because she wants you to learn through trial and error.
pass or no pass class. slightly rude at times. found the TAs to be more helpful personally.

Pass/No Pass class. Professor Li is fair and straight to the point. She gives good feedback and general insight toward the major of chemical engineering. Attend every class and submit every worksheet and the academic planning form for a passing grade.

Took Popko for 1 credit P/NP stress management class. Was a fun and easy class, only having reflections at the end of every week. Made a good variety of new friends from this class. Great prof, fun and engaging stories, and really nice to talk to. I'm taking her for CAT 2 next quarter.

Popko is a chill professor, and you can tell she loves what she teaches. We were required to make a guide/presentation about our zombie world and be as creative as possible. I took her for 3CE. She was very lively and passionate. She is super lenient and understanding. She has amazing memory; she learned all of our names in on class (the honors class is very small). Very insightful and fun class which really challenges the way you analyzes texts. Kind of a harsh grader, but she just pushes you to become a better writer. Very passionate about the topic and and is very accessible. Always willing to give feedback for improvement and is one of the sweetest most caring professors I have encountered here.

Dr. Popko was great! I took her class for CAT 2 CE and I really enjoyed her subject. She is very understanding and she wants her students to do well. I highly recommend her class and especially the CAT CE program. Look into it! We did lots of readings, but that is expected in a writing class. Her grading is clear and fair.
Was one of the most useful classes with a great professor

Took the cross-listed equivalent master's class and it was a great class for practical application. For the motivated student, this course was excellent! Easily the worst professor I have ever taken across multiple institutions. I would avoid taking him for any class you have at all costs. You would be better off taking his exact class at a community college or even by watching other University's youtube lectures.

Prof is very passionate about his area of study. Lectures are clear and engaging---he loves to discuss with the class. lectures not mandatory. discussions are. lectures are very boring, he just reads off the slides. very easy biweekly quizzes. one paper. the final consists of some mcq's and 3 essays (500 words each). pretty easy if you understand the material and do your readings.
i mean he's ok. the lectures are extremely boring and a crap ton of reading. only grading discussion sections, a paper, biweekly quizzes and the final ofc. i'd probably avoid him tho
Really boring lectures

Did not like this class at all. Ngl he was pretty boring and on top of it very boring lecture. thought it would be easy bc it's ethics based, but it was pretty difficult. they grade the papers like you're supposed to have a masters in philosophy. literally insane. try to avoid.

Prof Brink is a nice guy but Phil13 is pretty boring.  Reading assignments before each class which were needed to understand his lectures. Dense reading that can be difficult to understand. Many bad ratings below might be bc of him having his own personality. He won't just go with your way all the time and act all supportive, but he's a good teacher afterall. he is chill. slightly less rigorous than others. but he wont give you meaningful advice when you are revising your essay. (he will give you the basic feedback, and that's all) and the grading criteria of the essay is confusing. so good luck.
in all a nice person, but he and his classes can't help you with writing.
also the awp course isn't useful

Took for AWP 4A and 4B where 4B was what i got the grade for. Jerrod is one of the nicest professors ive had so. Went to office hours so many times and he was able to help clear thing up and gave excellent feedback on how i can improve my writing

Because AWP 3 is designed to be a tough course, there will be a lot of reading and analyzing involved, but Heiser makes the learning process fun and engaging by cracking jokes and asking everyone for their opinions. Very laid back professor. He makes class fun and engaging. Lectures are not mandatory, but no podcasts Lectures go over the readings so you can skip lectures if you understand the readings, but the readings are like 40 page long papers. I didn't do the readings but went to lectures and did really well on all exams

Class itself not hard. The content isn't bad but the grading for the midterms we're pretty harsh. It's manageable and not hard but definitely not an easy A. I am skimming the edge of letter grades even after hours of prep for exams. If course load is moderate to easy take, if heavy/rigorous don't.

I love Professor Brandt! I have taken 3 classes with him thus far and every single one has been so interesting. He very clearly explains the expectations about his assignments, and if you go to lectures and works through the material the class is very easily understandable. He's also very kind and stays after class to clarify any questions you have

this professor is great, especially for philosophy majors. as a non-major, lectures were sometimes hard to follow. the TAs—especially the male TA—were very kind and good at teaching material. grading is based on two midterms and a final, with both multiple choice and essay questions. attendance isn't required, and lectures are recorded.
Very nice and funny guy. There are a lot of readings, but just know the main ideas and be able to explain them in essays. He's not too harsh on prose, and gives good essay feedback.

Easiest class I've taken at UCSD, there's weekly guest speakers and we have tests based on their talks. 5/6 quizzes are for 5% each, and 3 midterms worth 25% each. graded only on exams and quizzes and everything is basically online open-note. she is really strict on not reopening exams or quizzes if they are missed, only if you have documentation. i had a family emergency where i had to go back to LA but she said if i didn't have documentation nothing can be done. just beware but it cost me my grade :(

This class with this professor was so easy. I never really attended class because everything was online. But, she is a very caring professor who is passionate for what she does. The discussions also weren't mandatory but helpful in explaining more about lecture topics

AMAZING prof!! she is so sweet and her class is very interesting because she brings in guest lecturers weekly to speak about different topics that then get tested on. the tests were take home and there is no final. she does quizzes basically every week online as well based off lecture content. it's very easy to stay engaged, shes a great person!
Because of the class structure she doesn't talk much, but she is helpful and communicative if you have any inquiries.

Kassy Lee is the GOAT!!!!! My GOAT is TEACHING!

He is a nice professor, but compared to other honors professors, he doesn't teach as much.

Great Professor, he explained Linear Algebra with its motivations really clearly. Although his class is a bit hard, it's an Honors class - what do you expect. But, he's a really nice professor and teaches extremely clearly. Recommended class.

He gives awesome lecture. Attending class is a necessity to achieve a good grade. Takes good care of his students to make sure everything is fairly graded. Lots of research papers to read but super interesting and on the tests. Asking questions helps.

took this class in order to fulfill my upper div election and DEI requirement, I could've chosen so many classes but im glad I chose this one. The professor is great, easily one of my favs

The class itself is a fascinating topic because it challenges one to consider economics from a different perspective. However, the TAs and the professor leave a lot to be desired. Took class in WI24 & forgot to rate him. Definitely one of my top 3 professors. Lots of readings but breaks them down in class so don't worry. He gives ample study materials & the class is not hard if you pay attention. Also is easy to talk to & very engaging during lecture. I wish he taught more undergraduate classes to I could take them.

Took this Winter 2025. Made topics that seemed incredibly difficult in the textbook a lot more manageable. Moves very quickly so read the textbook before class. Material is very difficult, notably at the beginning and at the end.
I like this professor she was good. A little slow. Hope she'd go faster sometimes.
Makes my brain much smarter and smoother

I'm taking her for 100A, but the BEST professor in the math department. God bless this lovely woman! She's so nice and caring and always accessible for help. The most down to earth prof here. I can't stress this enough.... TAKE HER IF YOU CAN!
Great professor. no notes! You have to work hard for this class but she makes the material very easy to understand.

His general aura is that of a stereotypical uptight Cambridge elitist professor, but then his exams were extremely light. Lectures were a little boring, yet still very informative. Definitely recommend.
Easy class with a great lecturer

buy the textbook; you get good practice problems for the tests. 3 midterms (material gets progressively harder) but you can skip the final if you do well. discussion not as helpful, you have to learn it on your own. prof is soft spoken and is often vague in lecture with his instructions. you just have to practice practice practice. good prof tho

Professor Shields himself was very clear in lecture and straightforward for exams, but my TA was incredibly unhelpful and disorganized. Doing the textbook practice problems was NECESSARY, you won't pass the tests if you only go to lecture and don't do practice problems... 3 midterms and a final. Unnecessarily heavy for a GE, wouldn't take again.

Lecture and discussion sessions are completely optional. Grade is fully reliant on exams throughout course. Subject is simple and gets progressively more tedious. Practice and studying is necessary for a good grade. Professor explains well, but can often times be non-engaging and soft spoken. Still recommend though, as course is doable.

Very clear lecturer, and the class was accessible for me as someone with little programming experience. Exams were fair but made so that little mistakes can cost you huge point deductions. Lectures and programming assignments are crucial to getting a good grade on exams.

Really engaging lectures. Attendance required. Relatively easy open-note tests. Programming Assignments were generally fair. However, you have to connect to a virtual machine at UCSD and code through the terminal which I found unnecessarily complicated and unintuitive.

This was a very straightforward and easy class. The lectures and prelecture notes were informative.

The mid term was extremely easy. The final was a bit more difficult but still on the easier side.

This is the easiest programming class you can take at UCSD and it is very beginner friendly. Just make sure to stay on track with assignments
Best Lecturer for ECE at UCSD. Keeps the content flowing at a good pace and answers any questions you might have with the level of detail one can expect from a professional.
He's chill and teaches well. The class isn't overwhelming and the PAs are very reasonable. You can ask him anything during class or office hours and he'll help without judging

Super interesting and engaging lectures. I may have not gone to a tone of them since attendance wasn't mandatory but I never fell behind since her class and assignments were pretty straightforward. Really nice and accommodating TA's as well! Take her!

LOVED this course!! I knew some ASL and this was a great refresh. Super engaging and interesting content on bilingualism. Dr. Jones is so inspiring and intelligent, she has lived all over. TAKE HER. The easiest class I've ever taken. She requires APA but just the basic purdue owl and my errors haven't docked me points. The assignments are super easy, attendance is not mandatory, and final is a paper or presentation(paper took less than 3 hours). Assignments are all papers/discussions. So far she's been super helpful and responds fast

Professor Jones is a caring and amazing individual, but is very unclear when it comes to project deadlines, rubrics, and is very critical of minor errors of APA format. The directions to assignments are also unclear at times, even after asking many questions. You work on a large group project with many parts along the way throughout the quarter.

Super kind professor! My class was organized, although no one showed up to lecture, it was always me and about 3 other students. I got great feedback from the TA's and great grades so I'm not sure what other people were doing differently.

Talks way too long about things that dont necessarily pertain to class/material. wsnt very prepared for class-including final (she was 15 minutes late, printed wrong versions, had spelling mistakes).She also doesnt communicate things well-thanksgiving lecture was apparently online but some students showed up to class because she wsnt clear about it

Hill was a wonderful professor. She demonstrates her extremely large amount of knowledge in every class and is willing to be flexible as long as you communicate any issues with her. 4 discussions, 4 quizzes, 1 midterm paper (1-2 pages), and a final paper (4-5 pages). the content is really interesting, and we watch a lot of films in class

I really enjoyed Prof. Hill last quarter! She did assign a lot of work, but I expected that and put in the effort to get an A. She cares about her students, listens to feedback, and is flexible and easy to access. Super interesting class as well1

Honestly, I'm not one for long lectures, and this lecture was so long. I feel like she took up the room with the talking and it felt like it lasted forever. It was about 2 hours long. Prof Hill is a very genuine and nice professor. Lectures although they are very long are still fun and very engaging. Overall, very interesting class and great professor!

This prof was such a genuinely cool dude and I could tell he really cared about his students. He was really easy to get a hold of over email and always made sure to address any questions. Attendance is mandatory and you can only miss two lectures. There is A LOT of reading but as long as you skim it before class you should be good.

Mr. B is a reasonable & charismatic guy, but bro needs to realize HDS 175 isn't the only one we are taking. Lord Jesus Christ this man wants so many long and detailed assignments each and every day. Several readings, reflections on each, discussions on each, reviews on each, it's consuming. I just need this class to pass the totally unnecessary dei requirement. Wish I knew that the amount of homework he assigns is so heavy please be forewarned.

Dr. B is a good prof. I liked being in his class. There is a lot of work, but he was willing to push back assignments if we needed more time. He is good, just not the best professor I've had. You'll do okay in the class if you do the labs and homework assignments.

Prof. B is an absolutely amazing prof!!! HDS 181 is a lot of work (3 papers+weekly hw & readings), but he makes it manageable and easy to handle. He encourages participation and asking questions, which if you do, you will succeed in his class. The most caring, inspirational, and thoughtful prof I've ever had. Cannot say enough good things about him

such a great professor, this is probably my favorite dsc class of all time. sam is really nice and chill and all the assignments are graded super fairly as long as you put in some effort to be creative. the TAs are also awesome

Don't understand why this professor ask you to vedio tape EVEY SINGLE PROJECTS and LABS!!! and knocks point off for vedio quality not being HD? We already submit our websites with required visualizations why can't they grade based on the websites??? Why need additional vedios????? Adding workload for nothing.
Really enjoyed his class!!
Professor Lau is great at teaching and genuinely cares for his students

Sam is nice but the grading for DSC 106 is very subjective. If you fulfill all project requirements you will only receive 80% on that assignment, must have exceptional creativity for higher grades, depends if the TA likes your project. D3 and JavaScript are not taught well in class so you have to learn them on your own. Two group projects.

Kolovos is one of the best professors in the DSC department. Kind professor, goes over all the lecture thoroughly, and makes sure to stop and ask students if they have questions. The class is assignment-heavy and very, very difficult if you don't start early. If you don't have a strong background in Python, avoid this class; it will not give you time to learn it. Overall, the professor is the best, and his exams are very simple, there to test your knowledge, not fail or trick you in any way.

Professor brings a lot of energy to lectures. 2 easy exams, spends the lecture before exams going over practice problems. 3 homework assignments that can be done in groups. Assignments are difficult because there is no explanation or introduction to the programming languages used (dask and spark) so you have to figure everything out yourself.

He is very understanding with giving extensions and is very caring. His lectures can get pretty boring and you aren't allowed on devices so you kind of just have to stare at a wall for an hour and a half. He cares a lot about the subject he is talking about, but as a STEM major it's hard to be engaged. Overall super nice though.
This professor was understanding and clearly cared for his students. Some lectures can be boring, but the class is overall very easy.
Boring lectures, grade is heavily dependent on your TA.
Lowkey a harsh grader without clear guidelines for grading. Lectures were all mandatory and tedious. Slides were vague, as lectures are primarily oral. The best way to get help was from the TA.

So much content and texts to cover but he explains it fairly well. Final and midterm were somewhat challenging, have to identify speaker and text out of so many readings we did. Overall an okay professor but lectures could drag on at times. Very strict on AI so all written assignments are in-person. Just do the readings and take good lecture notes.

Honestly not as bad as everyone makes him out to be. His lectures can be boring at times but he is very thorough in his explanations and going over content. In-class writing response for each of the five Shakespeare plays, midterm, final, attendance/participation. Midterm was heavy and had too much to do for the 50 minute period but final was okay.

I struggled in this class due to limited communication and lectures that were hard to hear. The professor mostly read from the text, and slides weren't very clear. Office hours were short, so I relied on the TA for help. Overall, the course structure felt unsupported.
This is one of the most densely packed course I've ever taken. The content he goes over in class doesn't nearly prepare you for the homeworks or the exams.
Very good lecturer, energetic and clear.

Professor Cloninger makes complicated concepts accessible, and he is responsive to feedbacks. HWs involve a lot of coding (not just playing around with parameters but writing from scratch), which is surprising since the prerequisite doesn't require any coding background.

no midterm and weekly hw assignments every week. Wish more respect was given to the science of teaching. For hearing these things for the first time flow of information feels ironically unoptimized. There were not many visuals time is spent writing on the chalkboard every lecture

Personally felt like the flow of information in lectures, as an audience member hearing these ideas for the first time, wasn't super coherent, and felt like lecture material did not prepare us nearly enough for the difficulty of weekly homeworks. Besides that he's a swell guy
Very nice and caring professor, will be taking again for 10B
Super kind and was a great teacher for a beginners Japanese class. Her instructions were always clear so nothing was confusing. She also responds fast to emails!

Sato Sensei is a great professor, and her explanations were quite clear. This class is a lot of work regardless of who you take it with, but I think they are very very clear and give lots of reminders about deadlines

Professor Sato cultivates a fun and welcoming learning environment and is accessible outside of class via email or office hours. 1 minor con is that her English isn't the best, so explanations on grammar or terms are a bit hard to understand; however, if you do the assignments and participate in class, the class shouldn't be too difficult.

Sato sensei's lectures were very engaging and easy to follow. She was also very friendly and caring for students' progresses. Very solid professor for Japanese learners at all levels. Definitely recommend her and will take her again.

Prof Zroka is definitely not a very animated lecturer and a lot of class was spent being bored, but she does care for her students and makes great effort to engage students in class, she also led good discussions that helped us understand the readings. Feedback she provides on essays is vague but she is very responsive and will help you if you ask.

Professor Zroka's lectures felt very inhuman. She was basically reading off a script and her voice made it seem like she was screaming at us the whole time. But, as a hum, your grade really depends on your ta.
She was nice and as long as you try and do your work she give you fulll points on assignments. no the best writer but I got an A in class and passed my portfolio.

Prof Zroka helped me with revising my essays, I would say go to office hours once you start writing them instead of going until the end of the quarter as that's when everyone decides to go. I went early and her feedback helped me and she made time to clarify any questions that I had. Overall a good professor but class can get boring.

Professor Zroka is an alright professor. Her lectures are direct and straightforward but are pretty boring. Helped me touch up on writing in this class. Her feedback is straightforward but isn't very detailed.

Really knowledgeable as a VLSI researcher, but not a good teacher at all. I had to self-study everything and the lectures were not useful. He also goes out of his way to make practice hard for students by not providing answer keys for practice problem sets and did not even provide any practice problems at all for the last chapter before the final.

Amazing prof. Approachable and explains every concept in a detailed and easy to understand manner. Exams can be challenging, but the class exercises and problem sets prepare you well. Very transparent about grading and expectations. Would highly recommend taking this class!

Worst class I've ever taken at ucsd. This dude will give out recordings delayed by a week. And he gave 0 practice exams, problem sets are unrelated to the exams themselves. All grades were based on exams and lab. No curve, TA bad as well. No examples in lectures, only bunch of theory and he explains them poorly. Take mingu kang instead of this guy.

Really good professor. Explains concepts in a clear and understandable way, and is clearly very passionate about the topics in VLSI. Answers questions with patience and want his students to learn everything that he has to offer. Take ECE 108 with him, highly recommend!

Took LIPO 1AX w/ her. God bless this woman. Some technical difficulties with the homework website. She initially said 50% credit for late HW. Turned around at the end of the quarter and gave us full credit. Brought her cute ass dog to the final. Literally so kind and funny + genuinely explains so well! Way better than French class in high school.
She is super nice and lovely, definitely a firm grader but she is a wonderful professor and have taken many classes with her.

Amazing professor, teaches everything incredibly clearly and accessibly. She speaks only Portuguese in class but does so in a way that it completely understandable, and she'll clarify things in English if you're confused. Tests are fair and getting an A is certainly doable, but most people take pass-fail anyway. Take this class!

NICEST TEACHER EVER. i took her for SOCI 104. M/W zoom, F workshops. the whole class is about a research project with a group. the midterm is individual and then the final is a paper and a presentation over your collective research question/topic. easy homeworks each week + field note submissions every other week! TAKE ARNAL shes so helpful.

Class was on Zoom M,W and in-person Friday. Was so nice since it was an 8am class. Prof Arnal is so sweet, and the topics covered in class are so great! Easy to get an A+ if you follow rubrics. Super understanding and will work with you if you communicate. TAKE HER!

Professor Gupta is an excellent instructor. I took COGS 118A and 118B with him, and his lectures made machine learning clear, interesting, and motivating. He explains concepts well, cares about students, and his classes had a big impact on my path. Highly recommend!

Professor Gupta provided everything a student needed to succeed in his course. The materials were well explained and content was organized well. The professor was also very accessible, which is something very important regarding online courses!

Professor Gupta provided everything a student needed to succeed in his course. The materials were well explained and content was organized well. The professor was also very accessible, which is something very important regarding online courses.
I was able to learn a lot from this class and I would definitely recommend this professor because he cares about whether you are understanding the content of the lectures/quizzes/assignments!

I really enjoyed taking COGS 118A with Professor Gupta! He's very knowledgeable and organized. His lectures make complex ML concepts easy to follow, and the projects really help you understand how theory connects to practice. He's approachable, accessible outside class, gives great feedback and genuinely wants students to learn.

He does what he can with the material, but iclickers are needed for every class even though he's lecturing on stuff that has almost(!!!) nothing to do with the actual work. I like that he's clearly passionate about what he's talking about but the entire course could be taught without him, as my TA went over everything we actually needed to know.

(The class I took was MMW 121 & the grade format was complete/not complete)
Professor Adamiak is a good professor, BUT my TA was BAD, in this class you don't have a final exam, instead you write an essay that you built during all the quarter, the problem is that my TA graded very bias. You have a lot of non-sense guidelines that you need to follow.

they want this to be a community building class for new students yet they make it somehow more labor intensive than my organic chemistry class or any other stem class for that matter its enraging honestly because  all the other colleges get normal classes without a trillion guidelines and readings and here we with a billion things going on.

I took MMWR and it was an easy A. However, your grade depends on your TA. 
The lectures were helpful. There were no exams, only papers and discussion board questions which needed to be answered.
An amazing and entertaining lecturer who is passionate and knowledgeable on his field of study. I love attending his lectures, already sad to have the quarter end.

Great professor that has a lot of passion for the subject and brings in a lot of real world applications on how we can observe mechanisms using lab techniques, if you wanna succeed in this class you must be going to lecture consistently. Ask questions she is very receptive and helpful but know that this class is not easy at all so good luck

doesn't go in depth about concepts and very surface level lectures, but exams consists of very in depth content. super heavy on lab methods and need to KNOW those to excel more than the actual cell bio itself. extra credit opportunities given but overall not a good lecturer

She's super sweet and easy to talk to but exams are difficult. I guarantee you there will be at least 3 typos on every single page of your midterms. Avg for each was a D. Update: avg was a D for the final. No curving. Highly regret taking this class with her.

She's very sweet and does her best to help you outside of class. Her exams however, are extremely difficult and require a lot of application. She doesn't really explain the topics and concepts of cell biology very well and her exams and homework questions go way more in depth than she does in class.

A quiz question marked correct shows up later with a different marked correct answer. He proceeds to blame students for picking the same answer as previously graded as a lesson to not... trust the professor? In his own words, "Did you really think what you thought was the correct answer did really sound correct?" Professor, you are the expert here.

Krysl does not teach the material he will test you on, and when you try to get help in the discussion forum he will usually respond with a sarcastic, rude, one sentence answer that does not actually answer the question. For SE131 he's okay, but do not take 130B with him because you will not learn anything. Also, he uses python instead of matlab??

When 80 people show up to a 9 pm office hours the day before the final, all confused about how to solve a practice exam, that's how you know you've failed as a professor. Somehow he will try to blame it on the students though.

worst professor i've ever had. exams were all about hand calcs, while homework was all about using the professor's provided python code. he was often rude on piazza and did not create a welcoming environment. sometimes he had valid takes every now and then tho.

This class was about 90% coding and 10% hand calculations, yet ALL exams are 100% by hand. Not a hard class but he makes it difficult, don't think about asking questions because he will respond like this," Wait, you are serious? You have not heard of clamped condition before?" ,"Good questions. I mean for you to answer. (Your homework, after all.)"

I really loved this professor! He is so sweet and definitely cares about his students. I found him to be understanding and responsive to my concerns. Definitely not the easiest class but I think that suits the subject material. Ng is a bit soft spoken though, so sit in the front. Overall awesome professor, very knowledgeable. Would take again.

No regard for special circumstances for students and making up for missing attendance, even though it's worth 25%. Highly opinionated and interpretable quiz questions. Very interesting content, but if you have any emergency situation don't expect any leniency. Also, doesn't respond to emails.

Professor Ng himself is a really nice guy. His TA's are extremely harsh graders and nitpick everything. He has weekly quizzes, 2 essays, and a final. Overall not that much work but the harsh grading made it difficult. His lectures were pretty normal and he provides slides and a final exam study guide. I wouldn't take again bc of the harsh grading

The professor is knowledgeable but can be hard to understand at times. Luckily he has transcripts to read over when recordings are posted. He grades participation too
He's a nice professor, but I feel he needs to prepare more for lecture.
Where is this guy
Very kind professor who's assignments are pretty easy to understand. Most of it done in groups, which is fun but there are also individual alternatives as well

Such a great professor! SO caring for his students. Assignments were group projects, but the project and materials were very fun and educational. Readings and lectures were great and educational as well. Super great if you need a fun easy class!

Professor Byung made sure lectures were super fun to attend and I looked forward to class every week. Although most assignments were group projects, he does give students the option to submit individual assignments as well. Would take his class again 10/10
Professor Kang is very nice and all the TAs are very helpful. Was taking to fulfill the requirement but loved it.

Took him at CSULB but he's not listed on there so this is close enough. I can't decide who's worse him or his TA. Do NOT take this class unless you need to. Philosophy might sound interesting to you but I promise after this class it won't anymore. He's a rly nice guy and i feel bad but the class is so boring and no one pays attention except for 2

DO NOT TAKE- he is a very strict grader and barely gives above an 80. He needs to get off his high horse. This is a gen ed class but treats it like you are a philosophy major. This is a UP review where he is adjunct - this class was by far my least favorite in college. Very boring, redundant and irrelevant content, harsh and unreasonable essay critiques and grades. Taken for Political Philosophy. This is a professor that loves what he is teaching. Go to class and enjoy the entertaining lectures.

He is supposed to teach a Gen Ed class and yet his structure would be like taking a major standing class. With the class being worth only 40 points total, it is much too difficult for a Gen Ed. However, there is very little work you have to do. There were 5 papers, one page each, participation, presentation, and a final exam. GO TO CLASS!

I am not even exaggerating when I say I might cry while writing this because I genuinely cannot express how much respect and admiration I have for prof Naoi. One of the best classes and professors I have ever taken. Prof Naoi is extremely knowledgeable, smart, and passionate about what she teaches. 2 big research assignments and one midterm exam.

Very nice professor, brought interesting perspectives to class through readings, learned a lot. Just show up and try to take notes and you will be fine. Fun projects too, honestly enjoyed writing my essay.

A good professor unless you make a mistake. I made an error on the midterm due to the way that it was written, so did half of the class originally she said we could get points back then changed her mind. She kept switching back and forth and did not give any reason why.

Knowledgeable & passionate professor when it comes to explain political science concepts and making connections between learnings and real life. Came into this class with no political science background knowledge, but was still able to do well by attending lectures and investing some time to study concepts before midterm. Final is a project.

She's not a very nice or helpful professor. I had to appeal my grade (which I won) because she refused to give me credit for an assignment for petty reasons that weren't even in the rubric. The class itself is fine as long as you don't have a single problem come up because she won't help you if you do.

joke of a class. I had over 200 responses on the pollev and didn't get out of the final bc it was only 60% rate but when I asked the TA he said we need a 60 to 70% participation rate. so you literally need over 300 responses on the pollev SICK JOKE!! further pushing my hatred to this school. thank you im dropping out
He is so knowledgeable and kind! Interesting material and lectures. Mandatory attendance, online midterm and final! A must take!!

Besides mandatory attendance the class is very chill. Easy A!! You're able to be exempted from the final if you have a 96%+, 100% in attendance (via iClicker or paper attendance), and a good participation grade. The average for the final was like a 95%!

Weekly discussions & quizzes, attendance is mandatory through I-clicker (phone). One group project that was easy, he cared more on discussions during a presentation with one shared paper to complete. If you participate in Pollev, and you have a 96%+ you do not need to take the final exam. One midterm that is online, not in class. Fun class

I gave him a 5 cause the class itself is sooooo easy. Boring and reads off the slides but very very easy A+. I have not listened a single time, never did the readings. If you participate you will not have to take the final which is 30% of your grade. Participate as much as you can and you will do great.

The class is very easy so it does feel unimportant to go, but she is nice and respectful to her students. Her feedback is okay, sometimes it would definitely help with my writing, but other times it would feel basic. Other than that, easy class to pass and she does many office hours and zooms to help.

Took her for AWP4A and 4B. For AWP the workload is quite heavy especially in 4B. Ms Wilson was a good and caring teacher as she would try to connect with the students. For me, the feedback was average, sometimes it felt good though. There was just a lot of inconsistent feedback a lot of the time which made it difficult in revising the essays.

This was for AWP 3 and I did not learn anything in this class, hence the reason why I did not preform well. Her feedback was below par and all she did was rant off about her personal life and how she has problems outside of class that she deals with every day and how she is not mentally stable. Always beat around the bush with questions.
Good instructor, is nice and respectful. Overall she tries her best to take into consideration of everyone's ideas and makes convo almost out of anything.

Professor Natalie is an amazing professor in and out of the classroom. She gives you good feedback and wants you to succeed. AWP was harder than other classes, but I found that her feedback and office hours made the course so much easier to understand, I recommend AWP with her. She made me like writing and everything that goes along with it.

I'm taking this for my major and I hate physics. He can be tough to understand but is super helpful if youre confused. The quizzes are almost exactly like the practice quizzes he gives out, some questions are identical.

He was not very helpful in learning this challenging material. Homework was 20+ questions a week and sometimes the TAs would not even know how to solve some questions. Gave a crazy curve at the end though so I am sure some people felt that it was worthwhile. I feel like I tried so hard but barely learned anything

His lectures follow the textbook but he talks quietly; studying the textbook is ESSENTIAL. Classes use clickers, and he's generous with homework extensions for exams. He drops the last quiz if students evaluate his CAPES. He's also active on Piazza. It's a test-heavy physics class, but that's expected. I recommend this professor compared to others

At the beginning of the quarter, this professor was terrible. He just read of the slides, did not really engage students. However throughout the quarter as he listen to student feedback, he got better and I actually started to enjoy his class. If you have him and don't like something he does during lectures, talk to him, he is a nice person.

Can learn nothing from the lecture. What he is doing on the lecture is showing us formulas but never explaining. I don't even know how to use the formulas and use what formula when doing homework (I can't even understand homework hint after listening to his lectures). Be prepare to struggle for learning everything on Youtube

Homework and Labs were not required, but heavily recommended. Quizzes were challenging, with averages hovering like 40-50 percent. The ARM coding language and environment is specific to the class but straight up didn't work on my computer with no real alternatives found online, so tough luck if it doesn't work on yours. The curve was very generous.

class is content heavy. Prof does a good job explaining the concepts and lectures are useful. grade is based solely on quizzes, final, project (all of which are hard) so if you are bad at test prep or takings tests in generally you will probably suffer. otherwise you'll appreciate not having hw, unless you actually do the labs, which are optional.

The workload isn't very crazy for me (6-8 hours), but the lecture and pre-lecture recording is boring and easy to get distracted. Some quizzes and the final are tough, and the study/example problem sets aren't very sufficient to test your knowledge thoroughly. No homework is graded so only quiz, final, and a project contribute to the final score.

Good professor, explains concepts well. It is a flipped classroom, where we watch pre-lecture videos to learn the concepts, and then during the lectures, the professor shows examples. There is a lot of work for this class, at least 20 hours per week.

Get ready to spend a lot of time on this course. You have to watch around 40 min of pre-lecture before each lecture. Quiz are open notes while online, but not for final. Project is in pairs and if your partner disappeared, you may suffer. This course is hard and the online nature makes it harder. Be prepared to choose this course and spend time.

For RE majors, his previous class (USP 5, 151) are great. He is demanding but is also fair if you reach out, does really want you to succeed but you have to put in the work. For 185A is a tough grader but will help you out if go to office hours. "You get out what you put in" ahh class. Chill guy and super expressive! Take him.

At first I was scared to take his classes because he has a strict attendance policy such as calling on you randomly to see if you're paying attention and if you can't answer it it can affect your attendance but I think that kept me on my toes! I enjoyed it because participating was fun and his lectures are clear! 100% would take again! best profess

I loved Boomhower! From the beginning of the course, he is clear with what is expected of students, what quizzes will look like, and how the class structure will work. There was a guest lecture almost every week with real-world professionals. Most exams are open book. Amazing teacher, would take any class with him in the future.

Great professor for USP 5! Only downside is the 3-hour lectures but all of the information is accessible on Canvas slides, he made adjustments for my final preferences, and clearly taught about the real estate development process better than any professor I've had so far. Only weekly question assignments from the textbook, midterm, and a final.

Pretty easy class, the readings aren't too much and can be skimmed through. Usually two assignments per week but they're never too difficult to complete, plus a short reading check. The class more-so depended on the material you were given to read and do assignments on rather than the lectures but the professor's great and pretty lenient too.

LTSP 100F - great class, there was reading almost every week which wasn't too bad. Just do the reading, participate and it will be easy. There was a project at the end of the quarter but he isn't too harsh on grading just make sure you have everything.

The topic for this "advanced" class didn't seem too advanced. Felt like we were just doing busy work most of the time rather than focusing on the structure of our final assignments which were confusing and again, lacked guidance. Nice guy but, poor execution at an advanced Spanish class.

Professor Bessett is a professor I would recommend to anyone. The class was interesting and pretty easy. There were about 3 hw assignments each week, but they were relatively easy. We had 3 projects which took some time to complete but it was actually fun to do. The midterms and finals were all online. Participation was not mandatory but it helped.

I loved her notes, they were immaculate and easy to refer back to. Some people say that her lectures were boring but I honestly appreciated the thoroughness and clarity with which she taught very abstract and complicated concepts. When I took her there were no exams and we only had 4 homeworks, these were comprehensive and lengthy but fair.

Not from DSC140B, but 200% not recommend this Professor. She has no empathy for students, so don't expect her to do much. Her lecture is quite boring because she can take an hour to just talk about a simple concept. If you expect to learn things from her, you will be disappointed because she only teaches you how to get points on the exam.

Class was easy, only graded on 4 hw assignments and an optional project. At the start of the quarter Lily emphasized how difficult the class would be and encouraged people to drop, but I'm not sure why because nothing was particularly difficult. First half of the quarter is basically a linear algebra review. Lectures were clear and straightforward

Bolin was my first ever professor whom I enjoyed having. She is caring, takes time to review your work, and gives back feedback in a reasonable amount of time. She's also pretty hilarious and makes you open up to everyone without you noticing.

Dr. Bolin was very sweet and gave amazing feedback on essays fir AWP 3. Keep in mind that you will have to buy books and do annotations which may take a bit of time. Dr. Bolin was engaging and made conversation while leaving a lot of time to answer questions. The class is good to take if you want to learn how to write better academically.

i love marina i've taken her for 20 and 40b and she's so sweet and passionate. if you talk to her and actually pay attention during lecture you will understand everything. will admit tests are a little tricky and they're a hit or miss. but she genuinely made me love certain topics that were otherwise boring!

Great lectures, lots of visuals on her slides. She's always very prepared and explains things well. Her labs, homeworks, and exams are well written and really make you think about how the algorithms work. I don't even like DSC that much but this class was interesting.

Took her for 40B but it wasn't listed as an option. 

Marina is the goat. Definitely one of the best dsc professors, passionate about teaching, willing to explain topics more outside of class, breaks down concepts to make them more understandable. I can't even be mad that the class is hard because she puts such a genuine effort into teaching.

Marina gives great lectures and use simple analogies to explain concepts. There's 1 Hw + 1 Lab every week and 3 reading quizzes on canvas so there's a lot of work. But don't worry too much about coding if u only have dsc10 coding experiences. She's super nice and willing to answer questions, truly caring your learning.

Very nice and good at explaining concepts in fun and interactive ways. Advanced algorithms is an interesting class and Marina gave us lots of time to make sure we understood the material, even adjusting her lectures to match our feedback. Each week there is a lab and hw assignment. Final is optional if you are satisfied with your midterm grades.

he's clearly a very smart guy, but not a great lecturer in my opinion: his explanations usually aren't too clear or organized and he often overcomplicates it. his grading is quite harsh too and the rubrics aren't always clear either, however there's a gigantic curve at the end which is nice

Daniel Kane is brilliant and down to earth. His lectures might require you to rewatch it again to understand but he's a thorough lecturer. Prepare to spend a lot of time on the HWs since they're proof based, but the exams are leagues easier than HW and he has a generous curve. I would take a class just because he's my prof

Kane is by far the most brilliant professor and just instructor in general I've had in my life (no joke). His homeworks and tests are very difficult especially the proof parts but there's always a significant curve at the end. He does tend to go fast and go deep into things during lectures which most cant follow but hes such a great guy overall.

The class has a harsh grading scheme, the grading criteria isnt very clear it is just "justifiable" for proofs. The prof himself is really good but his lectures arent super clear, he writes and moves on fast but he is also open to even fundamental questions so that is good. His grading criteria is tough but he also gives a heavy curve

tests were quite challenging and the homework was also incredibly difficult, but i do feel like his lectures were thorough and i liked how accessible he was over discord. i got a 28 on the first midterm and ended with a B+ in the class. it required a lot of effort but he is a great teacher. trust the curve + partial credit too

It is heavily dependent on your TA, you will never interact with the professor. That being said, my TA was absolutely fantastic and clearly cared about all of his students. I cannot give this professor a 4 or 5 due to the class being entirely taught by a TA. I would recommend looking at other professors before gambling on this one.

When I took this course it was managed by the professor and led by my TA, who was fantastic. It truly helped me grow as a writer. I'm not a great writer and took it during a time of incredible hardship, but I still did well. The program is strict on deadlines, but if you're honest, extensions are granted. Do the work, and an A is achievable.

I got her this quarter and not a TA. She is nice and funny, but class is kinda boring and participation heavy. She only teaches one section a quarter and the rest are TAs. If you get her, she's great! Gives good feedback on papers and not a tough grader. Lots of reading. The class itself is awful but that's not her fault tho.
Amazing professor! Super helpful and easily accessible. Would definitely recommend taking this course with her!

The best professor you could get if you care about improving your writing. She's the director of the MCWP program, so she knows her stuff. I got her (not the TA/IA) last spring, and her feedback improved my writing drastically. She genuinely cares for her students and wants them to succeed. Somehow made me excited to wake up for a 9:30am class!

Good professor because she's clearly passionate about teaching and cares a lot about your work by giving you good feedback.
An amazing professor who genuinely cares about her students is very sweet and provides helpful feedback.
She's very nice and understanding!
Not a bad professor. The only complaint is that she changed the class for exams, so you only have one notecard for the midterms and final instead of a whole page. Try writing in 2pt font.
Great Math professor, uses guided notes so if you don't have an iPad it might be tough. Overall very clear and accessible outside of class. expect to be challenged in a good way.

MSOE MTH-2140 (DIFFERENTIAL EQUATIONS): Dr. Zhao is caring and wants to help students. He is new and his accent is a bit difficult to understand, and his lectures are extremely fast-paced. Worst prof I've had in 15 years. Seems nice but acts rude and super strict. Harsh grader and took points off because I wrote cosec instead of csc. I like him but the class is hard, even if you have already taken calc.

sweet prof but thick accent and generally can't teach well. practice exams are somewhat helpful for final, but you're better off finding last quarter's exams. have to teach yourself through the book, but he provides a cheat sheet for all tests. hw has 20 attempts but cengage is weird with syntax. take another prof if possible, but curve is insane

Can be kind of rude at times. Content is pretty interesting it's just kind of hard to stay focuses because his slides are bland and boring. Just two essays 5 quizzes and a few other stuff. Put in a little effort and you'll do well in the course

listen. there's a lot of people saying that he sucks and that he's arrogant and all that, but let me tell you he seriously not even that bad. he has a habit of rambling on and on during lectures and i think he just gets the low rating because of how he teaches. he rambles a lot but the work is really easy. just do well on the essays for the class.

This professor has an extremely arrogant attitude towards students and likes to target certain individuals. His course does not require a lot of work. It consists of quizzes, 2 papers, and a final. Unfortunately his attitude really didn't inspire me to take any more of his courses. Pretty easy professor. Your whole grade is based on bi-weekly lockdown quizzes based on lectures/readings/videos and 2 essays. The final is no-fault and a lot of the readings/videos aren't hard to understand.

He is warm, welcoming, and inspiring. But you have to do the work. If you are able to do the work, you'll get a lot out of the class.

You will be asked to speak in class. A lot of group discussions occur so make sure you do the readings and homework.

Robert Castro acts like he's above everyone. He pushes students till they cry. He saw a girl crying but made her keep talking. Cannot understand why UCSD has such a great ditecting program but robert castro is the professor for the directing class… he is a cool person but not ideal for the job of teaching directing. Took this class online over the summer of 2023 and had a great time! Prof. Castro is super nice and we spent lectures watching movies and he gave small lectures beforehand. he would be the example of the word pretentious in the dictionary. robert constantly talks over his students in a condescending manner, and made me afraid to come to class. he teaches empathy and understanding, but lacks these qualities within himself. he also assigns so much busy work that is not helpful, and gave us so much work for the final.

Professor Dinco is one of my favorites I've taken at UCSD. Every time we show up to class it just feels like hanging out with friends and laughing the whole time. He's very knowledgeable when working through projects and creating media. Highly recommend.

Do not take this professor. It's as simple as that. Don't let the low volume of reviews confuse you. He is not qualified and proved it with his unprofessionalism and lack of effort. Worst vis professor Iv'e taken do not take this teacher by any means.

Great professor to talk to but he gets distracted easily and is a tough grader. By missing one deadline, it messed up my grade. Great instructor! Very professional and passionate about dancing, and also have great personality and teaching method.

A great professor who genuinely likes ballet and cares about her students! She takes the time to learn about everyone, and gives feedback tailored to what you need. I've never done ballet before, but she is very easy on beginners. Enjoyable class!

Kristin is an amazing instructor. She makes sure that students have proper form and takes time to help those that are struggling. She is also very talented and has good music taste. An easy grader, but for good reason. I loved this class!

Ive taken her several times, so hopefully that tells shes a great teacher. I didnt grow up dancing, but she really devotes her time to help anyone. Shes so patient too! She really wants her students to achieve in her class. However, sometimes she does cater a lot more to the advanced students of the class. 10/10

The class has a variety of tap styles to experiment with. Your experience doesn't matter because she caters to all levels. Her grading is generous too because it's based on attendance, 2 performances of a routine we learned in class and a paper. I would recommend this class to anyone who wants to raise their GPA by having fun dancing.

Attendance and participation not mandatory but such a fun professor you should attend. Exams were quite difficult as it was vocab. Prof included tutorials how to use the program. 100% recommend this course with this professor. Huge extra credit opportunities. Responds to emails same day usually same hour.

What else to say other than WOW! I took Anthony in Spring 2025 for POLI 30, notably a difficult class among other POLI majors. He made lectures fun, made short videos to guide students regarding SPSS, and even decorated the class one time for one of his famous special lectures. Tobe is a wonderful teacher, I would highly recommend him if you get the chance to study painting with him. He gives really good critiques and is kind. I do think the group critique sessions can feel pretty long but it's overall very worth it.

I forgot to do SET evals so I figured this might be beneficial too. Professor Tobe is a very experienced artist and professor. Probably the worst linguistics professor I've ever had to deal with. Tough grader, won't accommodate to your needs, always dtm.
Be prepared for hard material, but the professor is good and supportive

This was for COMM 101, not 101N, I just couldn't change it in this rating. Danny Boy was the best professor I've ever had and probably will have. It's evident that he loves his job. I love this man. He makes everyone laugh every single class. So quirky in the best way. He is so sweet and such a great professor. I hope to take more classes with him in the future. The projects were relatively easy and I learned a lot from him.
Real easy going guy, just do your work on time, literally can't mess it up [the class you take with him].
Lots of projects. Great teacher and teaches incredibly well.

COMM 101K - Documentary Sketchbook class. Really inspiring lectures. He's really passionate & is a filmmaker himself, which is awesome! Easily holds the entire class's attention with how interesting his lectures are. He's too nice. Gives out undeserving As & Bs. Pretty interesting if you're into the theory of t-ism and insurgency (I was not) but relatively easy. Overall the expectations for this course were clear and Wagner provided ample opportunity to succeed. My one complaint was the non-recorded lectures and sometimes repetitive material. The tests were not very reflective of the lecture slides. The class is only worth 500 points, with 400 of them related to exam scores, so make sure to study. clicker attendance

Lectures were enjoyable and interesting. pro:

Professor Fulton is very nice and an expert in the subject. Assignments were straight forward and easy to complete. Read the textbook if you really want to enhance your knowledge and it makes the exams easier.

Unorganized lectures, seemed like rambling a lot of the time, and did zoom for like more than half of our classes (I didn't sign up for an online class). 3 pre-lectures (average between 15-30 minutes each) and 3 lectures a week so prepare to be so locked in. falling behind is the most detrimental thing you can do. pretty good at explaining concepts and curves generously to scale to class scores. difficult class but he's a great prof!
Makes all of his test purposely hard so youre never prepared no matter how much you study and he makes it clear that he makes it hard on purpose so idk whats worse.

Great professor, but his lectures could be a little less monotone. His love for science is definitely reflected in his coursework and the way he interacts with the lab help and students. Great teacher if you are not an auditory learner. The guy excels everywhere else.

I love how caring Prof. Marino is! His lectures are definitely important to listen to since that's what all midterms are based on. It's a lab class, so you do have to participate and put in effort. Marino is awesome. He's there every lab sash, which haven't had a prof do before and it makes a big difference. He's also so funny and super chill, so asking for help isn't intimidating at all. Lectures explain things well, tests are pretty fair + you get a cheat sheet. Lab itself is interesting and I learned a lot, def a worthwhile class

She is a great prof!!! I would take her again 100%. She gives great feedback. There are 2 essay and one project. Her class is super fun and I loved how she put us into groups. You pick the grade you want to work for. One online book u need 2 buy. They're a chill prof. There are roughly 2 readings to do before every class and 2 essays due in the class. If you want an A you have to do a small 5 min presentation on one of the readings. very ez class

Very sweet, genuine, honest professor. Grading pledge was clear and easy. Cares about her students and genuinely wants you to work on becoming a better writer. she was such a kind and chill professor. I had mental health issues and she was accommodating and understood when I communicated with her. Her work is super easy, and there were like two essays total. extremely easy and fun class

The grading system was contract based so you choose a grade you would like and that determines your workload and how many readings and absences you can have as well. Amazing professor.

Pepe is just 'okay'. He rambles in lecture and grades toughly on just a few assignments. If u lose points, its hard to recover. not the right classcode but took it for his sci-fi class & had so much fun. lectures were interesting so I always looked forward to going to class. interesting readings w/ writing responses. great professor would def take again
He is great and an easy grader. He does notice when work seems AI so a mix of AI and own work is advised.

Very creative professor, I think he's fun and what he teaches is very artistic and out there (I've taken 4-5 classes with him. Professor gave great feedback and very accessible outside class.

Prof Merryman is so sweet and understanding, and wants the best for you. She is very lenient (to any extensions) and provides great feedback. Most CCE classes teach the same thing, but she makes the content more enjoyable. They only thing is that I think she makes the students do more in-class discussions/activities compared to the other teachers.

Ash was so kind and caring. I would highly recommend them. Since CCE is regulated by 8th College most of the classes will be similar, but Ash approached CCE 1 with much care and willingness to help. Ash provides amazing feedback on everything and is lovely to work with, especially in this small class setting. Ash is so knowledgeable and it shows

I've really enjoyed taking her class this quarter. There were in-class writings graded on completion once a week, a relatively easy midterm, and a final paper with an interview component. She is very caring and wants people to have open discussions about class themes and readings. She explains everything very well and adds complexity to topics.

I feel bad for Dr Popmintchev; this class was bombarded with several severe disruptions, confusing many students about grading. Nice guy, cares about his students.

He is a nice professor, but he doesn't explain the concepts well (he reads off the slides). Lots of EC, quizzes/test are medium-difficult. Attendance is confusing, but there is a certain # that is mandatory for full credit. Questions go unanswered or are not answered when you ask.

He is not a good lecturer, he just reads off the slides, and barely spends time on the iClicker questions. Great professor who just wants you to do well in his class. Provides so many extra credit opportunities (extra credit for correct iclicker questions, bonus HW, bonus exam questions, SETs, etc.) & HW is only biweekly. Honestly I could've missed so many more lectures if I knew this beforehand.

Fair. Lots of extra credit opportunities. Not curved but you will get a higher score this way trust me. EC goes a LONG way. I clicker is representative of exam questions. Pay attention to the pre reading KUDU questions. These two things are most like the quizzes. B in phys 1A, C in 1B. A- here. Grateful for this professor. Effort = success here.

Very Fun Class, he stays in character as if there is a ongoing zombie outbreak. Dont fall asleep or doze off in class because he'll make sure that the zombies will get you. Never had such a fun easy class where I actually wanted to go to a class for almost entertainment.
prof. dominguez is a great + caring professor give this man all of the money

I did not know what to expect going into this class but I am so glad I took it. I have never rated a Professor but Professor Dominguez has been one of my favorite at UCSD. The lectures are mandatory and you use online I-clicker but his lectures are interesting and he's extremely passionate and nice. No final or midterm just one movie to watch and write about each week. Definitely take this class if you are wanting to! 10/10

Professor Dominguez is amazing! You can tell he is passionate about his work and never fails to make the class laugh. Not only is he extremely understanding but also very interactive with his feedback on weekly assignments. It's crazy how much time and effort he puts into his responses. I hope to take a class with him again!

A good professor who makes sure to keep you entertained during the lecture, but is very unorganized. She has way too many personal problems that interfere with class and grading. I really enjoyed this professor. Lectures are not mandatory but they are really helpful for the midterm paper and final paper. If you attend lecture you should end with a good grade. My midterm ended up being curved from a 95 to 98. I think for the most part this is an easy A but I def struggled more towards the end of the quarter.
Professor Rogers is very fair! The assigned material and lecture style were ideal for an introductory course. If you pay attention, you're likely to learn a lot and receive a decent grade.

Class was easy, but prof seemed disorganized and just read off the lecture slides during class. Midterm was an exam but final was a paper, so there was something to play to the strengths of everyone. Honestly what made this class for me was having a great TA.

Most chill class ever. Flexible policies, quizzes are easy to do and open-note, midterm is easy if you do the study guide, and final is take-home. TAs are v chill and helpful, discussions go over material like the study guide, review for the midterm, + time to work on papers and the final. Will definitely take another class with her in the future!
Professor was very professional! You will really learn from her.

Beware! She is a very tough grader for discussion posts. She rarely responds to emails or any questions you have about discussion posts or anything related to this class. Her feedback on discussion posts could be better, too! Extra credit is available, which helped boost my grade. I would avoid her at all costs if you need an A!

Overall she is not great at her job. She seems distracted, maybe in her personal life. Comes off rude. She doesn't respond to questions or care to help. Recorded lectures are terrible in quality and continuously paused. Not sure she really knows what she is lecturing on.

Her lectures are difficult to follow. Her voice often trails off, and she frequently pauses the recordings. Often, it seems as though there are many uncertainties about the content she is delivering...
Extremely tough grader. Very unforgiving in discussion posts. Will take off a lot of points for a very small mistake and just being rude when talking to students.

Sam is absolutely amazing and I highly recommend taking him. He is so thoughtful, caring, and makes the classroom environment so comfortable. His course was like therapy for me. We would discuss a few weekly materials but could talk about our own personal experiences and thoughts related to them. I am so thankful for the community he fostered.

This class was amazing!! I recommend taking this course! Even though you do have to make time on some weekends for activities, it gives you a new perspective for the topic. This class is more based on hands-on experiences and group projects, but every once in a while, she has lectures and group discussions about the assigned readings.

Professor Lewis is an incredible professor! Highly recommend, especially if you are prepared to put in the effort. Definitely a high-impact high-reward type of program (Climate Justice and Action Scholars Program). Lots of homework, but learn a lot and have a great time. Fosters a welcoming and close-knit community.

Dr. Lewis is easily the best professor at UCSD. She's extremely kind and compassionate, and is very knowledgable and accomplished. If you have the chance to take a field/practicum course with her, I would very highly recommend it. Being able to work with her in a small group setting was really great, she creates a super safe and inclusive space.

PROFESSOR LEWIS IS INCREDIBLEEEE!!! This class was amazing, from the lecture material, to the readings, to the films- Dr. Lewis went in!!! Exams were quite tricky, mostly the first midterm. Two midterms and a policy brief (that's graded quite roughly by the TAs- especially that butch TA). Aside from that, Dr. Lewis slayyyyedddd!

Very tough grading and the exams are really tricky. If you're a typical A student, get ready to receive B's even though you're putting in A level effort. Super nitpicky TA/prof. She is funny and the class is really interesting but I cannot recommend her if you want a class where you are rewarded by the amount of work you put in.

Take this professor! She is amazing and it's fairly easy. 3 short assignments a week. TA is very nice and grades fairly. Midterm and Final online and very similar to lecture slides. Attendance is not required and only extra credit if you attend!

I really loved taking Professor Hedges' class. She has a lot of experience in the field of project management and she gives a lot of real-world examples from her own experience to help us understand the course material better. This is an assignment heavy class but ut is pretty easy if you do your reading and attend class.

Professor Hedges tells amazing stories about her work experiences and it really helps you with learning the content of the class. Attendance is not mandatory, but she does offer half a point of extra credit if you attend 4 of them. She usually also ended lecture 30-50 minutes early.

Cool professor who integrated her real life experience as a project manager in lectures. The assignments/homework were pretty easy and the quizzes/exams were open note and open book. She also ends  30-45 min early so it's nice not having to stay the whole 3 hours for lecture. Wish she taught other classes at UCSD. Content is useful for life/work.

A great primer in terms of learning about project management, especially at the undergrad level! Her lectures are amazing- she's an incredible communicator, entertaining to listen to, loves participation and you can tell is enthusiastic about teaching/management. She's incredibly caring, is interested in you and your development!

One of the best professors I've had with my time spent at UCSD. The professor will make sure you get the material and won't test you on anything she isn't sure you'll know. You can tell she cares for her students and their well being. Would definitely take her again!

Professor Beyhan was overall really good for genetics, she's very knowledgeable and well-versed in the subject. Her grading scheme was clear from the beginning. Her lecture slides do include a lot of information at times however classes are recorded, non mandatory and slides are posted. TAs also super helpful. Tests are difficult but not too bad.

Graded on a few things but easy to do well if you study. Allowed a double-sided cheat sheet that can be printed and with images, and she gives a lot of partial credit on the exams, which are free response. I would definitely recommend!

Caring and interesting professor. There was a lot of material covered and it was hard to know what we would or wouldn't have to know for tests and in how much detail. Midterm and final were both all FR, which meant that some concepts were tested in-depth while other major ones weren't tested at all. Generous grading + partial credit helped a lot.

She's honestly not good at all. Does the simplest practice problems in class, but then goes over the moon in her exams. Some questions in her problem sets are way more complex than what she teaches. She's a nice person though and she does help outside class. Her exams are insanely difficult and are completely conceptual. Free response only.

Loved this class! Latin takes a bit to get the hang of but Professor Murray makes it super easy and accessible, and is a friendly and engaging professor to boot. Attendance was encouraged but not monitored and homework and practice quizzes were graded on effort and not correctness. Both the midterm and the final were take home and open book.

Professor Murray is a great professor and makes learning a new language very straightforward. The class is super casual and very beginner-friendly. There are 5 quizzes, a midterm, and a final. The quiz content is given in advance and the midterm was a take-home exam over the weekend. She is super caring and the class makes learning a language fun.

It takes a minute to get a hang of Latin but Murray ensures you don't feel overwhelmed/is always willing to help. All quizzes are taken online, the midterm/final are take-home + open note, and you don't have to turn in any translations; you get out of this class what you put into it. Prof is hilarious and approachable. Couldn't recommend her enough
AMAZING. Very good at communication and giving feedback. Goes more towards the grammar side of Attic Greek than Myerston which I liked. Tests were take-home open-note. Very friendly and helpful.

With learning a new language, there is a lot of homework translating text. Murray was a chill professor, if you miss a quiz, go to office hours. Didn't do that part of the homework, just say you didn't do it, but have something prepared. She often got off-topic, leading to a humorous lecture. This either made a phrase memorable or not covered well.

There is a midterm, final, randomized group project/essay. For the midterm and final, there is 2-3 parts that consist of multiple choice and short answer questions. To study, she stars the slides that are going to be on the exam. With the starred slides, create mock exams since she doesn't provide study guides, but the TA's create review sessions.

nothing against her, however, the way she distributes group projects can be overwhelming. Her team falls behind on grading, expect 1-2 group projects p/week (almost one every class), you have to participate in class or discussion boards, can't choose your group, exams are divided in 3 sections and NOT enough time is given.
very good fair teacher

Great professor. His lectures are very helpful and they were all I needed to get an A on the course. The final was a bit more challenging than the midterms as one question looked like something we had never done but it was still easy to score good marks.
He explains MATH 20C concepts really well and very clearly.

Had him for math 20c in summer session 1. His lectures were very straight forward and easy to understand. His TAs were pretty helpful too during discussion! He would walk through how to solve problems with clarified a lot of misconceptions. Nice guy
I would recommend this professor!!

Best Japanese lecturer at UCSD! 137 series is incredibly useful. We learned business manners, interviewing, and did a cool entrepreneurship project. Workload is ok, but attendance is strict. If you show up and do the small assignments, you'll get an A. I got an A+ with just JAPN20C experience. She is warm and truly cares about students. Take her!
Very fun teacher. Very nice teacher. I TOOK JAPAN 332 BUT THAT ISNT AN OPTION FOR COURSE CODE. She was very caring and I actually learned alot from the class. Very fun. Just show up to class.
very unhelpful in terms of when you have to be absent and setting a standard for what she wants when we do assignments.
Sensei Tokuda is so so sweet, I absolutely enjoy her class!
The most amazing Japanese professor at UCSD
I personally didn't enjoy her lecturing style; attended one of Voelkers lectures and he definitely explained concepts more intuitively.

lectures were very insightful and interesting and prof sepuya's voice is lowkey soothing idk did anyone else think this like bro has a silky smooth voice it gives me hella gender envy at times if he sees this hi
if u get my goat jamil as ur ta or as a professor during the spring ask him about sundance
