Professor Hansen is pretty chill. Lectures are very informative but can sometimes get kind of boring because he is pretty monotone when he speaks. He answers questions very well and welcomes debates in class

I TOOK HIEU137! Easy class but you have to show up cus he does mini response discussions on Tuesdays and small quizzes on Thursdays that requires access code. Doesn't give out homework but he assigns reading and/or watching movies before class for the material you're learning that week. Boring lectures though but he is a lenient and easy professor.
Great professor! No other writing course has explained in such detail the mentality of how to be an effective  researcher. The  content was engaging and the  grading was easy.

It's GE so I wouldn't have chosen to take this class. But with that said I got way more out of the experience than I would have thought. I'm a better writer and thinker because of the teacher. Definitely worth taking.

easy class, weekly assignments are relatively simple but tedious/boring . I would recommend taking this class if you want an easy A. However, I will say that I got absolutely nothing out of this class. I dreaded going to this class (attendance is mandatory) and oddly enough the prof speaks down on community college but this is a transfer course.

Professor Young taught the best class I have taken at UCSD. Initially the syllabus seemed very stressful and threatening, but it seemed a lot nicer after he explained it in the first class. Attendance is a HUGE factor, but he is very understanding. The class is fantastic. A lot of discussion about modern topics like AI and technology. Def recommend

The textbook is 80 dollars and you have to get it. He makes it seem like "you try hard, and you can get an easy A." It just isn't true. His grading for many assignments seems arbitrary and his feedback is minimal. Lowest grade I've ever gotten in a class. Would recommend choosing anybody else for this course.

My absolute favorite professor! As someone who often struggles to focus in lectures, he has a way to make them fun to attend. I would take his classes again if given the chance. Super fun take-home essays that require you to piece together and analyze cases as if you were in the CIA lol, definitely more effort-based than anything though.

Professor Joseph is a good lecturer and the content of the course is fun! A decent amount of reading--and I would recommend doing the readings. It's not too difficult to get an A, so long as you put in a respectable amount of time into the course. Not many rubrics and not a particularly well-organized course, but in my case, grading wasn't too bad.

Professor Joseph was funny, knowledgeable, and you really will learn a lot in his class, but I often found his lectures a bit hard to follow and disorganized. I was also a bit confused going into the midterm and final - I didn't do poorly, based on the grade breakdowns I don't think anyone did, but it was just a bit confusing. Proceed with caution.

Prof. Joseph has great, engaging lectures. Note that there is a lot of writing involved. Midterm and final were scenario-based papers, and then there was a research paper, and a statement of participation (pretty easy). Grading is pretty easy, but writing/planning process is tedious. The bulk of the work in this course was concentrated at the end.

Most of your grade is centered during finals week literally 75% of it. Super easy class though as long as you try a little. Didn't go to class after the midterm and still got an A. The midterm and finals are just simulations.

He taught everything in an easy to understand way. This class was definitely a lot of practice outside of lectures, but his exams were fair to the content he taught and expected you to read from the textbook.

This class was so bad, I wish I could give it a score of 0, but I can't, so I'm forced to give it a 1. Very test-heavy, but all the questions are coming from the textbook. No homework, just recommends doing the practice problems, with no clear answers or guide given in response. DO NOT TAKE HIM.

Good fundamentals but just an awful personality. Called me out in class for asking my friends a q about the content then insulted us every other class. After a midterm he'd act mopey about the grades and complain the class wasn't trying. His TA did more of the teaching (and the grading) than he did. Also he thinks he's funny (he's not lol).

Ternansky is a sourpuss, but my main gripe is his laziness. Some protocols have major oversights which can cause even well-prepared students to have serious issues if their TA doesn't correct them. Lectures are straightforward but dull, and he acts annoyed to be there. His final exam was also very sloppy. The actual experiments were fun, though.

Demeaning to students in lecture. Not engaging lectures (material and vocally). As someone said, not being picky with sig figs and lab reports was somewhat easy. Had an A the whole quarter, to drop to a C+ with an impossible final (which even the lab coordinator warned). Not to mention his specific disrespect towards Latinx.

Great professor. Lectures are straightforward and informative. Hes the best physics professor I have taken at UCSD. He gives out extra points if the quiz averages are low. Quizzes and exams are very fair.
He was extremely chill and made his class very fun. With that said, your grade is like 85% tests and they were very hard, but at least there was a decent curve at the end.

He is a nice professor who tries to help his students succeed. He gave out 4 quizzes (very brutal), worth 50% of the grade, and a final, which was worth 30% (also brutal) of the grade. The homework, discussions, and in-class questions are worth 20% of the grade. Conclusively, the content is hard, and the quiz averages are low.

Prof Meyertholen provides plenty of resources to succeed. Do the interactive textbook content, it will prepare you for trivial MCQs on the quiz you may otherwise not get. His lecture content is extremely clear and he does not deviate far from it.

He is the teacher you wish you had for every class. He makes E&M really easy to understand and I feel had I taken any other professor I would have been struggling. What makes him amazing as well is how respectful he is and his dedication for students first. In my class the average quizzes weren't great so he would help boost up the scores as well.

Format of this class is abysmal. When I took it the grading scheme was 65% final exam+35% quizzes(9 quizzes), but now the exam is 100% of your grade. All MCQs (no marks for attempting). Class average is extremely bad so he curves it. No assignments which doesnt help because you dont get practice. Dont take ECE 45 with him unless you have to
You learn nothing. EVERYTHING IS JUST MCQ and you end up learning nothing because actually solving everything will get you no answer
The people that failed used chatgpt on the quizzes.
This class is so funny

If you value your grades you'll wait to take it with a different professor. Class average this quarter was a C- after curving. Probably used to be good when he cared about teaching and curved properly.

Professor Watkins was kind of a really bad lecturer. He didn't say anything relevant to the texts that wasn't surface level or already on the slides that he uploads. But, as a hum, your grade really depends on your ta.
His lectures were absolutely horrible, but as HUM usually is, your grade depends on your ta.

His lectures were so unbelievably boring and useless. He read off the slides for 50 minutes. The grade is discussion participation (easy), 2 essays (kinda hard), and a final (idek what i was writing). People did so bad in that class, but HUM is a requirement, so you can't really be picky.

Watkins is a knowledgeable professor, but I found his style of lecturing a lot less engaging than other HUM professors, and staying interested in the readings and assignments was difficult. He gave the hardest HUM final I've ever taken, as I spent almost the entirety of the 3 hours writing and nearly filled up an entire blue book.

Very nice prof, but I found the content boring and essay prompts were vague. The final was one of the most treacherous exams I've ever taken. I think it was two long essays and like 12 short answers, in person, in 3 hours. My hand was numb for a full day after. The content on the final was very intensive, you definitely need to go to lecture

Professor West was not the best lecturer. I feel like a lot of the stuff you are actually expected to do in HUM is on your own for this class. He didn't go over any important concepts from the readings. That being said, he had a different format for a final and his lectures are definitely important for that because it's memorization based.

Professor Watts just loves his coins and honestly I'm all for it. On top of that his lectures are super engaging and interesting, and they are online as well so you can review easily. Oral final is easy as long as you pay attention in lecture and study for a few days before. Essays are tough though, but its Revelle Humanities so what can you expect

The oral final was incredibly challenging, requiring extensive memorization based on everything discussed in lectures. The expectations are unrealistic, considering that HUM 2 is a Revelle writing requirement, and most students are STEM majors. The class is boring, too hard, and the information we are forced to learn is so irrelevant.

People have been lucky due to Covid and protests. AVOID. Misleads you into bribed free labor for wife's charity work; 5 weekend hours chastised and yelled at for HELPING as a VOLUNTEER, then he changed the worth from 2 overall grade points to gradebook points. The best part is the oral exam for a writing class. The irony. You memorize coins. COINS.

If you're taking this class as a Revelle student to improve your writing, find a different professor. Most of his points are discussed verbally with few visuals and his lectures are boring. However, he doesn't develop your writing in any way, and does not provide any writing advice. He will not help you improve at all. Rely on the TA's.

She is an amazing professor. The lectures are informative and they are a bit fast paced but it wont be an issue if you pay attention throughout the class. She does post her slides and the exams are easy. The iclicker questions are based on correctness, however, they are very basic and its harder to get them wrong than right.

I really liked Prof Murillo's lectures; they were super clear to follow. Clicker questions were easy if you paid attention. I though the midterm/final were very fair and easy even without much studying, and not essay heavy. I hated the research paper, but she wasn't involved with that really. Overall one of the better MMW profs, I recommend.

I LOVED Murillo. I was scared by her reviews on this cite but I feel like she's so underrated. Her lecture content is so well organized and easy to follow. I enjoyed the readings (she assigned relatively lightly), and she cracked some funny jokes during lectures. She really grew on me and I went to her OH once- she was so kind and fun to talk to.

Murillo is a clear, fast paced, and concise lecturer. Her lectures/tests focus on themes and concepts, not so much the small random details. Take good notes, do the lecture learning objectives, review the study guides and you'll succeed. Most of your grade will come down to the TA and the essay but her exams help to bring your grade up.

Attendance is mandatory with a physical Iclicker remote in class which she grades responses based on correctness. Her voice is very hard to listen to for the entirety of lecture as well as she goes through the content very fast. She does not allow to take photos of slides and only posts them at the end of the week to catch up on content.

One of the easiest classes I have taken at UCSD. 
There was a decent amount of homework but the mid terms and final exam were all extremely straightforward.
The lectures and notes were very helpful and all I needed to study for the exams

I really, really liked Seward. He was a great lecturer and clearly cares about his students' learning processes. He would often pause and ask if  there were any questions and if we wanted him to go faster or slower. His notes were really neat, accessible, and easy to follow. I wouldn't change anything about how he taught the problems.

Overall, the course is not extremely difficult if you put in the work. The tests are similar to practice exams and he does not give true or false questions on the exams which makes them much easier. He is not great at lecturing and you do have to spend time outside the class learning the materials but overall it is not too difficult to get an A/B.

Ended up watching Brandon's podcasted lectures and going to his office hours as my lecture section was taught by a very disorganized teacher. Brandon is great at explaining things, and likes to provide helpful proofs and definitions. Very organized lectures and very helpful office hours.

Professor Seward is a very kind and experienced professor. His lectures are so clear, including both concepts and corresponding examples. Some of the mathematical concepts we learned in math 18 are abstract, but as long as long you understand his lectures and do the homework, the exams will be easy for you. It's easy to get an A.

I took this professor over the summer so this review is late but I had to come back and say that this guy is by far the best professor I've ever had in my almost 4 years attending UCSD. His lectures are very structured and he clearly cares for his students, as he will go out of his way to grade things HIMSELF and provide personalized feedback. GOAT

The best professor I've had for ECE so far. His reviews are no joke. I love how the structure of this class is straightforward. Despite homework being time-consuming, it will be worth it as they help prepare for the exams. I wish he were tenured.

If you're here trying to decide whether you should take Prof. Alcantara and you're suspicious of the glowing reviews, don't be. He really is that good. By far the best professor I've had at UCSD, clear in his goals for the class and clear in his way of seeking them. I wish he could teach the rest of the EE program by himself.

Greatest prof for signals ever. Goes through step by step on every analysis technique and explains what every single equation means. Exams are one to one with practice exams. Writes pages upon pages of supplementary notes for HW and exam questions. Borderline impossible to fail with a lick of effort. Wish I had him for every single ECE course.

Hands down the best professor I have had. Lectures were incredibly easy to follow. Hw was time consuming but preps you well for exams, which were very fair. Makes an effort to get to know his students personally and is very open to feedback. Understanding this material has helped me so much in my other upper division courses all thanks to him

Prof. Awad is really an exceptional professor for BIOCHEM. I did a lot of research before deciding to take the course through UCSD Extension, and with Prof. Awad. I was most appreciative that she has minimal work due each week, but is clear about her expectations with each assignment (a discussion board and a quiz). She also offers extra credit.
Highly recommend this online Biochemistry course! Dr. Awad was a great instructor and guided the class with ease. If anyone is looking to take this course post-grad as well, 100% worth your time.

Prof was very bad at teaching the material. However, the class/grading system made it very easy to get a good grade. The tests were comically easy, but her lectures are very fast and impossible to keep up with.

She genuinely cares about us learning more than the actual grade. Our second midterm was rough, so she gave a lot more flexibility for our final. She doesn't provide a direct study guide, but her lecture before the exams is basically what is going to be on the exams, so the lecture really matters.
The best professor at UCSD. Goated
goated professor wish i could take her for 6C.

Genuinely one of the sweetest professor I've encountered at UCSD. I'm terrible at chem (hence my grade haha) but she virtually ensured that students that put in effort will succeed in her course! She cares a lot abt her students and wants to see them succeed! Would DEF build my schedule around taking her class.
Unorganized class. Lectures are extremely difficult to follow, had to fully rely on outside resources + textbooks. Quizzes are questions from HW, Final was difficult but well curved.
yutyum tutyu tyu y yuytu
bad teacher

He's super confusing and the more he talks the more lost he gets himself, hard to understand w/ the accent too. Dropped the class that day and saved me from a poor performance. L prof

The course material is easy if you have a decent grasp of basic Linear Algebra from lower-div Linear Algebra. Very kind!
Ross Sensei is very caring and does her best to help her students. She provides many resources to learn the material and responds quickly to emails.

Ross-sensei is really caring with her lectures. She makes sure if you are able to understand the subject even if you are really confused. There's a lot of homework but it's honestly really chill. I had Domyo-sensei as my TA, and she is really awesome. Even when only speaking in Japanese, she makes it really easy to understand. Memorization is key!!
Took her JAPN20A. She is a very lovely and caring professor. She is very patient in explaining concepts. Sometimes she can be funny too. In her class you feel very welcomed.

She is a funny and caring professor. However, in terms of the quality of lecture and teaching, there are other Japanese professors at UCSD that are a lot better than her. She tends to not able to finish slides and grammar points in time and wouldn't talk about it in the next class either. The class felt very rushed through.

To be honest, this class depends heavily on your TA. Grading was confusing because during TA hours, most of the new TAs were unclear about the requirements, only a few knew what was truly expected. The professor is approachable and often gives extensions. I found out too late that you can reschedule the midterm if you are really sick.

This class was brutal. Templates didn't match rubrics for lab reports so even if you followed the template to a t, you would still lose points for mundane reasons. Also, exams were solely testing on how good you are at deciphering trick questions. I think it's unfortunate he got laid off and I wish him the best. But, I feel the class was unfair.

He got laid off, made a grand spectacle about it on his last lecture, BUT ... if you see him at any institution, STAY AWAY! You can read through every experiment, take his worthless practice tests, study late, you will NEVER do well on his exams. They are designed for you, or anyone (I challenge you TA's and other professors), to fail. WORST EVER!!

Toughest class ever, made worse w/ this prof. Was super unclear and unhelpful in answering questions and stating what he wanted out of the lab reps. We just tried to guess what he wanted from us bc he didnt release the rubric. The exams were AWFUL. Every question was a trick. Averages were C- and D, but he still didn't curve. Sad he got fired.

He's a nice professor, BUT that's about it. His grading is very unclear. His lectures do help with lab reports, but he makes them very vague. He does not provide the rubric for lab reports. His finals and midterms were particularly challenging and required a thorough understanding of the wordplay in the questions to find the correct answers.

Dr. Marino cares SO MUCH about his students. He replied to ALL of my emails and there were too many. He is kind, compassionate, and respects his students. He wants students to learn and he teaches you  without stressing you out. I love this man's approach. You rock Dr. Marino!!! This is for BIPN 160 btw. Code was not listed so I chose BIPN 140.

Definitely the hardest class I've taken at this school, the way he teaches it is basically as if you were in med school already so take that with what you will. The curves pretty good but only because all the students struggle with the content. Final is around 4 hours and about 15+ pages with problems consisting of multiple parts. STUDY!

Yes he curves generously, but that's only because there are so many horrible grades and a low average. He treats the class like everyone is headed to med school and needs to be “tortured” just to pass. He rushes through the material, and the exams are insanely hard. He doesn't seem to care about students whatsoever. Save your mental health and GPA!

It is one of the hardest class I have ever taken . Exams are so long and very difficult but he cares about grades and he curves very heavily. He does care about your progress during the quarter and he is very nice . He is very accessible during his office hours and would like to help students to improve and understand the concept very well.

He is overall a good professor and very generous with the curve (each test). SO MUCH STUDYING!! His tests are almost entirely application based so you can't just know facts, you have to know in detail how things work and how they're all connected. Overall a good professor, but if you don't remember much from BILD, expect to be a little lost.

I loved this professor. I genuinely took something away from her lectures bc of her genuine passion for teaching the topic. She was super accessible outside of class for feedback and graciously took a lot of time to help me succeed. Highly highly recommend taking this class with her. TAs are great too!!

Professor Feuer is a very engaging lecturer, and although attendance to lectures aren't mandatory, don't skip! Quizzes are really easy if you attend the lectures, and attendance is mandatory for discussion. You write a lot in this class, but they give you time to revise and improve your papers.
The professor is knowledgeable but he has no idea how to teach. The lectures, homeworks, and exams are on similar topics but all seem disjointed. Expect a lot of self-study.

He is a nice professor, can be tense at times and unapproachable, luckily my TA was simply amazing. he speaks a bit fast on complicated subjects giving less time to understand the material. The course layout was very simple and many resources was provided through Google classroom, overall organized and learned a great deal on his course.

He is bad at teaching seriously, not making the lecture interesting fun but instead making the class tedious and painful. Those online lectures really are old, and unclear. I dont know why he can still be a professor in this class and he doesnt care about the class.

McCulloch is a major jerk.  He won't take the time to answer students questions or help at all. I email him a question once and he just said, "Ask somebody who went te lecture" even though I went EVERY lecture.  His tests are very similar to previous years and come straight from the power point sildes that he posts.
Professor is amazing, very friendly and great at teaching. Really easy course. Programming assignments were interesting and not too difficult. Exams were very easy if you paid attention in class.

Professor Porter is amazing! I really struggled learning coding but he gives you chances to retake quizzes and then averages your score between your first attempt and second attempt. He also is very flexible and cares about his students learning, theres 3 projects total but they are fairly easy to do if you understand the material.

Genuinely SOOO sweet. He is good in his lectures- does iclickers (not graded for correctness) just to check if students understood and then revises his lectures to help more students understand. willing to edit syllabus if enough students ask for it- very caring, answers within like 30 mins on piazza. he wrote his textbook and quizzes r reasonable

We used Github's Copilot (an LLM) to help us code for this course. If you are disciplined enough, it's possible to learn Python with AI but do not get too dependent on it as it will not benefit you for quizzes/exams. Lectures were somewhat helpful. Prof. Porter tried to make it interesting by giving us free choices on our projects which is a plus.

we used AI so i can see why ppl were like "oh i don't know how to code" but if you want to learn you have to put in the work! i think this class was really easy like as someone who didn't know how to code before this class, after putting in the time and effort and also really just actually trying to learn what we were learning, i think it was fine!
Really friendly professor. Course programming assignments are really interesting but a lot of work. You will learn a lot though. Exams are very easy if you understand the content.
Hard course but helpful

The class content was quite disorganized because it was the new CSE 30. Slides need to be more referencable and Prof. Chin needs to work on lecture pacing. Besides that, the class content was very interesting

Prof. Chin is very knowledgeable and friendly. His lecturing style is very inspirational, I love his pet of the day section. He tries his best not to make the lecture stressful, but if you are not interested in the course topic it still will be hard. Homework problems takes time, so be prepared to start early. No midterm, 4 quiz+redo and a final.

Slow and repetitive lectures but you learn a decent amount from doing PAs. Final exam was similar to the practice final and clicker questions from lecture. Very generous, extended deadline for two of three PAs and extra credit available for all three.
Really caring professor, he makes the topics he teach really interesting. Hands down one of the best professors at UCSD. Course was a breeze and I learned a lot.

Great professor, gives good material to study well from (provides a textbook, read it cover to cover!). Tough exams but doing well on the PAs means you will be fine. Programming assignments were interesting and intellectually challenging. Well structured class!

Prof. Pasquale seems passionate in OS, but I was a pretty turned off by the excessive obfuscation. Apparently there was a scare about cheating prior quarters, and there was excessive reign on code as well as lot of deliberate redundancy added to material, including PAs. His presentation was decent, but his methods and theory were severely outdated.

I was one of many students who attended every single one of his lectures in Center Hall (except for two of which were over Zoom due to the floods) despite he doesn't require attendance. Those lectures were unforgettable and the highlight of my time so far at UCSD. For the first time I felt like this is what university is supposed to be like.

This guy won't use a normal OS like Linux. 

He only teaches on Zoom and avoids helping students with PAs. 

PAs are brutal and tested with his "black box". 

Don't get me started with his Italy campaign... 

Don't take Pasquale.
really amazing lecture experience. He will lead you step by step to study the steel bible with full of details.
amazing lecturer. made topics really easy to understand and hw was a good reflection of the topics covered in class

My favorite professor this quarter. Fantastic at explaining things in an engaging way. The class is super difficult but I had more fun than my other classes just bc he made it a great classroom experience. He gives zoom as an option but in person lecture is way better (he won't let you zone out. "Look here!" lol)

Uses analogies to make sophisticated concepts easier. Often refers back to what we learned at the beginning to remind us of the foundation. He's always willing to go back and re-explain. He's blunt, funny, and practical.

HW was tedious but it exposed us to every nuance that we could encounter so if you can do the HW, you can do the exams.

One time I got 0/20 points on an exam question simply because I had misinterpreted the assumptions needed to perform the calculations. When I asked for a regrade Professor Uang had a personal 1 on 1 session with me and let me explain my design. He realized that I knew what I was doing and ended up giving me 19/20 on that question :) Great guy.

Dr Chapman was my favorite professor during my time at UCSD, I took multiple classes with him and enjoyed learning under his guidance. Just make sure to stay organized and on top of deadlines, also class attendance is mandatory as he does class codes to input into attendance quizzes.

TAKE HIS CLASS! Professor Chapman has been the most inspirational educator that I've ever met. I loved his course and I plan to take more during my time at UCSD. Pay attention to his lectures and review the slides for his exams and you'll do well.

Dr. Chapman was my favorite professor throughout my tenure at UCSD. I took 3 courses with him and would have taken more if I could! He genuinely cares about the relevance, relatability, and understanding of his courses. You can tell he is passionate about what he does and excited about impacting the next generation of psychologists. Funny too!

Entire course is basically just Achieve work, 3 credits of psych study work, and 1 hr of reflection circle. Very easy and doesn't take up much time if you manage your time correctly. Very interesting class would recommend.
I cannot recommend Professor Chapman enough! I have taken 3 courses with him and his classes are some of my favorite classes I have ever taken.
simply incompetent

I had a great experience in Data Science & the Arts. He was accessible at office hours, fun to chat with, and goes the extra mile for students.

Professor Twomey is amazing and is such an approachable professor outside of class. Last quarter, I would attend his Office Hours almost every week just to chill since he's a genuinely nice guy to talk to. He's very clear about what he expects on homework and exams, and is there for you if you're not understanding concepts.
A nice guy, but extremely clueless about how to teach specific dsc20 content but slightly compensated for it by making the final optional.

His lectures cover basic knowledge, which means we need to do research on our own if we want to learn the more advanced stuff. This is what I expected after taking multiple CSE courses, so don't expect that just going to the lecture will get everything covered, you need to work on your own now if you want to be successful.

Very disorganized professor. Grading kept changing, didn't cover anything that would already be covered in an undergraduate comp arch course. Dropped 1 out of the 2 homework assignments and the final project. Exams were medium difficulty with a few questions being very ambiguous and some out of syllabus which were dropped.

Took 240A. Funny and engaging lectures but definitely need to put extra time to study. Difficult exams, prepare with P&H's books (hardware-software interface helped the most).
This is course is a chaos. The professor will be absent for lectures and be super fast to catch up. The grading component is a mess and keep changing. Exams are tough.

took cse240a in 24fa and expected to learn a lot. But unfortunatly,I learned absolute NOTHING from this course, LITERALLY NOTHING! Professor is really knowledgeable and learnt a lot through the course. Teaches okay but doesn't really spend much time on the course. Questions were rarely responded to on Piazza and assignment were released way behind schedule making the finals week very hectic.

Worst class ever taken. Is attendance not mandatory? So does the professor - not shown up for almost half of the lectures, just letting his PhD students do the lecture. Even no notification when a lecture was online.
Only take if you already know machine learning. What he teaches is related to the homework but the homework is impossible unless you already know machine learning.

Professor Su tends to cover large amount of topics in computer version in CSE 152. You will learn a lot if you attend every lecture. The exams were hard but professor he gave large curves. Definitely recommended if you have a decent math background.
Recommend to take 253 and 252 before taking this course. Prof. is a leading scholar in 3d machine learning, will give a lot of insight in this field. Heavy workload but grading is good.

Half the class is lecture, the other half lab. If you do not know the basics of programming, do not take his class. He doesn't really help a lot and belittles new students with a lack of programming background in front of everyone.

The professor's teaching is generally clear and well-organized, and they explain the material in a structured way. omg she talks so much and doesnt let you do anything during class. just sit there and listen to her talk about her job and marketing skills and communication skills. not very interactive or organized. very easy class though so take it as you will. you're able to collaborate on your grade.

Great professor! Take her as ur professor for wcwp 10A
Prof Susi is very accessible outside of class. She is very easygoing and willing to connect with her students. She is very flexible with grades and deadlines.

Prof. Karna is the best professor I have had at UCSD. His learning material is very detailed and easy to read. His lectures are quite engaging and his exams are easy to ace. 11/10 He was so polite in lectures and Piazza posts! Greeting students with the utmost respect. Understanding our other commitments, he was very generous with deadlines, offering support and HW extensions. His genuine goal was for every student to succeed in Verilog, staying highly active on Piazza, available and responsive almost 24/7, amazing guy

One of the most caring and in-depth professors. He has a ton of resources for students who are interested in hardware engineering, and clearly spends a ton of time answering questions and writing guides on class related topics or even useful classes to take at UCSD. The lectures are good and the workload is doable, take ECE111 with him if possible!

Amazing professor! Cares so much about his students, and went out of his way to provide extra help outside class. Extended deadlines for homework, because he prioritized students actually learning the content over anything else. Far and away the professor who has cared the most about students' learning.

Her upper division bio lab is super easy, but honesly it's because she doens't really care about the students. Her TA's do literally everything, and she's pretty unaccessible bc of her research. I guess she's an easy A? Just doesn't really care about students.

Class is very easy & you'll have no homework or assignments outside of class. Also does not require a car as every place is accessible with public transit. Class was great but professor lowkey gives passive aggressive. but def take the class probably easiest upper div bio lab out there

She requires an iClicker for attendance and it is mandatory for a grade. Talks really fast and goes through content quickly. Aside from in-person lecture, she assigns videos to watch for homework (15-50 minutes long). Definitely note heavy.

She requires iClicker, had 4 tests with the lowest dropped, as for the tests I would normally score around and 80 or 70, but I feel like even though I studied for weeks the lecture aren't well represented on the tests rather the videos (from) she posts, so for studying watch the videos they go more in detail about the topics on the tests.

Professor Butler is heavy on group activity so make sure to pick your group members wisely. The professor not only exposes us to R coding with is beneficial to students in ESYS majors, but also makes sure that each individual student understands how to do it properly. The TA's were also extremely helpful and patient with students.

I took her during SS2, she's great! Cares about students, nice during office hours. Attendance not mandatory, podcast on Canvas. Only multiple choices for exams I heard that she usually has questions that require the whole process, but no need to afraid, she gives partial credits for them (meaning that: formula written: bingo, points).

Prof. Hopkins is an amazing Chemistry professor. She really cares about her students understanding the material and genuinely wants her students to succeed. As long as you put the work in to this class, you're going to get the outcome that you want. Attendance is not mandatory but the lectures and discussion sections are very helpful.

Grading is really straight forward—total 500 points, 200 points final, 150 each on midterm and homework. Hopkins is overall a good professor, she is really sweet and willing to help. But she is not the the most passionate or best at explaining concepts—reads off slides. Took her over summer session, office hours are only on Saturday morning.

Only one midterm and a final, both were very easy and fair. She chooses the easiest problems from discussions/lecture/HW for the questions, most of the test is MCQ, the rest is free response. Honestly just know the basic concepts and how to do the calculations (keep practicing, none are hard- just intricate) and you'll pass easily.
Generous curve. Lectures were ok. Tests were reflective of lectures and homework. Homework graded on completion.

Fred Harris, get into his class while you can. A DSP legend, he's guided me from grad admission to RF career prep. Every lesson has a story; nothing is random. He's mastered and pioneered the craft. Learn all you can while you still can. He's a real G.
Did not learn anything from this professor. Class is super unorganized and useless.

Incredibly difficult class but so rewarding. Victor recorded all lectures for Canvas which was SO helpful. Lectures >>> scribe notes (I never read them). Insanely tough grader but curved generously (I think my avg was like ~79% and I got an A- lol). Necessary to go to office hours! This class has been invaluable for my other work.

HORRIBLE experience taking his class. 

Material covered in lectures and discussions are shallow. Professor does not provide any practice or past exam to review from. On the midterm and final, he will test you with things you've never seen before. The two exams that he does not prepare you for are worth 60% of your course grade.
Very poor explanation on the material. No practice exams, don't even know what will be tested. Lecture slides are almost useless.
Very bad, very hard, no time to answer exams, material not enough, not enough explanation, very fast paced

overall poorly designed class with little thought about students learning. class content is insufficient to teach material, and to do well in the class, you really have to go beyond the class resources. tests are obtuse and hard as well, and instructor did not give regrade window or release final. avoid victor vianu if possible
Prof Nady helped me to improve my scientific writing, so glad she provided good feedback! Discussions are worth 1/3 of the grade, so you need to do well on Discussions.

I took Professor Natalie Nady in Fall 2024 and really appreciated that she allowed you to submit an idea for an extra credit paper that definitely took me from an A- to a solid A. She has clearly communicated expectations, is passionate about the subject, and was super nice. I appreciated that she replied so quickly to any inquiries I had.

Amazing Professor! She really cares about her student’s success, and is very clear and thorough in her lectures. Only 1 quiz and 1 assignment per week, no exams! The quizzes are a bit hard, but she offers unlimited extra credit opportunities to make up for lost points, so you can do well in the course! Dr.Barbaro also taught, and graded easy!

Online Biochem class. Pros: Well-organized course and extra credit available. All lecture materials are available at the start of the class. Cons: Professor didn't answer a single question I posted. There is so much concern for cheating on the open book exams that you can't see what questions you got right or wrong.
Easy class, prof is reachable and quick to provide feedback. Lots of extra credit opportunities. Mandatory discussion posts

This was by far my favorite professor at UCSD! I studied abroad in Berlin with him for HUM 3 and 4, and it was SO much easier than during the normal school year. He was the most caring and sweetest instructor I've had here, and incredibly passionate about his job. Just participate and try and an A- is guaranteed at the minimum in Revelle in Berlin.

Took him for LTTH 115, the articles assigned are challenging but intellectually stimulating. There is a weekly 200-250 word review of one out of the 3 articles assigned that week. There are two papers required, one of them being the final of 1000 words. The prompt is very loose, you pick a topic you want to explore more on based on the readings.
His lecture is interesting and inspirational, though I hope that he could talk about less plots and interpret a little bit deeper

Its like any Hum course it depends on your TA for grading. His lectures were pretty boring to me and he talked super duper slow. Better to not go to class and watch the recording at 2x speed to save time. He's nice but just boring. 2 essays. The final was 3 hours for explaining 10 different quotes and then 2 mini essays. not hard and graded fair ig
The kindest, and most passionate professor. Very open to conversations and connecting. His lectures are not always directly relevant, but very interesting nonetheless.

Uncaring, lectures extremely difficult to follow. Feels like he's out to get you, because he is. All I know is he took a break from teaching, and apparently used to be good. Something happened while he was away, and now I consider him one of the worst professors I've had in the ECON department. The only positive is his exams being nearly identical.

Now I can say I know a lot about CAPM model and expected utility theory. Professor Du is the perfect pofessor at UCSD. The Lecture is clear and recorded. The tests are fair and he is approachable and caring! My only regret is I took 100C with another professor a quater before he is the instructor.

He's an amazing professor and is available for appointments for those who couldn't make it to his regular office hours. If you practice all the problem sets and practice exams before midterms and finals, you will do well in this class.

A great man. Lectures cover relevant material for exams, practice/past exams he provides are almost identical to the upcoming exams. He extended my due date by three days on an assignment when I switched into his Econ 171 class during week 2. He's awesome.

He made the final exam optional due to the strike, which was great because you are basically done with this course in week 8. Exams are easy if you be careful enough (almost got an A+ if I didn't make silly mistakes). 5/5 recommend taking him for your last econ course.

Took her class online over the summer. 4 very easy quizzes and a couple of discussions per week, which are graded on completion. She gives out extra credit, which can boost your grade by up to 10%. There's a final paper at the end of class, which is also graded on completion. An easy class that fills the DEI requirement. Grades were given out late.
Really enjoyed professor Chapman's CRT class, she was very insightful and explained content well! I recommend her to anyone!

She was so great! I really enjoyed her. She was so powerful in the way that she carried herself, and her style of teaching was really a conversation with her students. The assignments were really reflective and made us challenge our current views on urban education. She's super approachable as well and is so funny!

The lectures were scattered and disorganized, making it difficult to follow the material or stay engaged. The structure and clarity just weren't there. I would recommend considering a different course or professor if you're looking for a more focused and worthwhile learning experience.

attendece not required but gave you EC if you attended. Textbook could be found online but was also provided. Midterm and final were online. Funny and chill professor and TA was very kind and passionate about climate change.

Professor Rivera-Collazo is amazing! The course was easy - the exams were all take-home and open-book. One thing that kind of made my learning difficult was her fast talking. She gives amazing lectures but sometimes skips through the slides a little too fast. I recommend having her slides open on your laptop because it's often hard to follow.
I wouldn't recommend this class unless you absolutely have to take it. She is incredibly disorganized.

The class is extremely easy and all the tests are online, but she is probably the most boring lecturer I have ever had. You get extra credit for attendance and even then, the class would be empty. Easy A with barely showing up.
Took this class over summer and prof. Jenkins was great. Final grade was based on attendance, participation in discussion, and one essay. I enjoyed the material we covered and her lectures.

I really liked her lectures. you basically meet once a week and students do most of the talking. only thing that is graded is two essays about 10 pages each. she's not a hard grader tho. if you like to talk to others then take her class.

Jenkins is kooky and (to me) hilarious. Her lectures can be a little scattered, but they're almost always interesting. Prepare to have your preconceptions of culture and health challenged and overruled. I think this can be a life changing course for some. I'm a Global Health student now because of it. Come to class and read, you'll do fine.
Funniest professor ever. Professor Jenkins knows her stuff and also happens to be a professor of psychiatry at the UCSD med school. Culture and Mental Health is a great course for premeds

This class was extremely interesting. Read the textbook since it was on the midterm. Her lectures aren't really tested but very interesting otherwise. Going to office hours is also extremely helpful & informative. Good class overall and would definitely take it again.

Michael comes across as so dismissive of differing viewpoints and beware!! he tends to dominate discussions in a way that can feel belittling to students. His frequent use of profanity feels unnecessary and forced, which makes the classroom environment unwelcoming. His teaching style makes it difficult to engage meaningfully with the material.

I honestly enjoyed how relaxed he was about teaching and grading (not in a slacking way). He teaches very relevant things pertaining to international politics and he grades based on content of your essay rather than the writing style.

Took him for CENG 15 during summer session II. Homework can be tough, but he gives out amazing notes and guides us through problem sets. Final exam was a bit tough, but it was similar to the homework.
No homework, just in-class labs. He is a very good teacher and helps with advice about chemical engineering career choices.

Absolutely terrible. Took this class as a GE and it was the most difficult class I have ever taken. Was definitely not an intro class. Humbling experience to say the least. Do not recommend if you aren't familiar with coding.

Professor's handwriting on the board is amazing, especially with that fancy chalk! Lectures were very clear and helpful for doing the homework. The lectures are based off of his textbook so I would recommend reading through the discussed chapter either before or after lectures. The examples in the book are very helpful in doing the hw.
CENG4 is a very fun class as a new engineering major, professor is super nice on top of that. Great first quarter experience

Flipped class lecture style. No curve. 94% for an A. 4% of extra credit provided you show up to class. 

Weekly quizzes comprise most of the grade. Quizzes are fair and easy compared to homework. Do the lecture problems to do well on the quizzes.

Reading is required before lecture. Minimal review lecture in beginning, rest of time is practice.

Don't let the 'Ok' average rating fool you, Grinstein is the worst professor I've had at UCSD. His exams are unbelievably difficult compared to both lecture and homework problems. He also claims that since he includes formulas, he can make the exams harder, these formulas are elementary and completely unhelpful. Zero partial credit given on exams.

The class felt very disorganized. As others have mentioned, you read outside of class, but if your (assigned!!!) source material is not good, it can become confusing very quickly. 

To do well, I recommend
1. The two openstax books (university/college physics) 
2. Halliday Walker Resnick Fundamentals of Physics (pdf on internet archive)

The most abstract and hilarious professor I ever had. He DON'T teach at all. The class is practice problems and us working on the problems only. He got a strong accent and it is difficult to follow along. He explain the answers only briefly and it is very difficult to understand. The hw, and quizes are very hard, especially when the content is hard

I mean, he is a good guy. But his lecture is not teaching anything only doing problems and some of the question he didn't go over. You need to read a lot from the book. Also, his homework answers are awful. It is messy and not easy to understand. He didn't even give a practice quiz.

Fantastic prof and class. Amazing structure: 9 quizzes and 3 were dropped. Quiz corrections added extra points, clicker questions boosted almost 8%, homework on kudu and the final exam had 50% of repeated quiz questions! Great content and lots of opportunities to boost the grade. Definitely worth it!

Most uncaring professor at UCSD. Lab manuals have incorrect directions and the grading rubric doesn't clarify. A joke of a class. Homework, lab reports, mandatory lectures, lab sessions of 4 hours that will take you 8. No choice in picking your lab partner. He randomizes it for you. Wait another quarter if you see him for any of your classes.

Avoid the combination of him and PHYS120 if you can. The class (not designed by him) is already poorly designed and outdated and he made it even worse. Having an organized class material and clear instructions should be the basics of good teaching but unfortunately not in this class.

The worst professor I had at UCSD. He didn't accept my quiz corrections because I didn't include a screenshot of the original quiz question, despite having them all written down on the paper I submitted with all the work and correct solutions. He refused to let me send them afterward, too. I ended up failing his class by 0.9% as a result.

You definitely have to try a lot for this class in order to get an A, but definitely achievable. Does not do a good job at explaining the material, so you definitely have to teach yourself all the material.

Lectures were long and heavy, but the information were pretty interesting sometimes. No technology allowed during lecture but weekly assignments were easy and were able to be done during class. Grades heavily depend on TA and a final group project.

Prof. Glaser was always very passionate and high-energy when teaching the class. She always encouraged us to participate in lecture discussions because she was genuinely interested in our thoughts. Only thing I struggled with was the no laptops in lecture rule, otherwise, I would recommend taking her for CAT if you're interested in translation.
The professor doesn't allow to have laptops out, and this sucks for a class where you don't have to listen to the lecture at all. So I can't even get any other work done.

My favourite prof at UCSD so far. Honestly, I have no complaints. She really cares about the class, the subject, and her students. Plenty of opportunities to get extra credit or get feedback from her. The midterm was super easy. The final paper is long (2K words) but you can opt for a creative project or reach out to her for help. 11/10 prof.
Such a goated prof and class, my TA was strict but easy assignments. Crib sheets for exams, but understand the lectures and topics from textbooks and you'll be fine.

Prof. Borsa is very passionate and funny about his work! HW is mainly instagram posts, he does surprise attendance checks on random days and those count as EC. There is required reading but I didn't do any of it because I was broke. He drops lowest hw score and has a generous curve. Got a B with little to no effort! 1 cheat sheet on midterm & final

Should consider not take SIO anymore, the exam will be on paper and really annoying. We being told this change one day before exam. No matter the change is reasonable or not, this literally change the syllabus or rule for the exam without knowing. If this change is made at beginning of the quarter then we can understand it or change grade option.

great professor, very easy class. he says textbook reading is necessary to get an A in the class, but only about 10% of the midterm was textbook content. you can tell he is passionate about the content and cares a lot about providing an amazing learning experience. HW is easy and took me about an hour at MOST for each assignment

By far one of my favorite UCSD profs. Taking this class for GE and was pleasantly surprised. Genuine professor, interesting lectures, clearly cares about students' learning experience, easy and clear grading criteria, I couldn't have asked for a better professor. I couldn't recommend a professor/class more

Pretty straight-forward summer class. Relatively light on readings compared to a full 10 week course which was good for closer analysis. The class was asynchronous except for a book club meeting each week. Usually only two writing reflections/short essays each week as well. Prof Wesling knows what she's talking about and is well-respected.

graded on weekly book club assignments, two socratic seminars, and a final exam. she doesn't podcast or use slides while lecturing, but she's amazing! u should def take a class with her if you can. she's a lenient grader, and you'll love the class discussions!!!!!

Professor Wesling is HILARIOUS. She requires you to purchase a 50-dollar workbook/textbook, but it was used consistently throughout the quarter and overall very worth it. She does talk fast, but her lectures are generally easy to follow. The final grade is based on open-note exams and a reflection, which was not difficult. I recommend taking her!

Prof Wesling is very passionate about what she teaches, very kind and open. Her class was super easy. 3 exams, all open note (but preparing your notes for the exam takes hours so avoid procrastination). Would recommend to everyone!
Open-notes for tests
Great professor. Lectures and notes are very clear. Quizzes are fair and helpful. Final is slightly more difficult.

I took this class during summer session and online. He seemed to struggle with the technology and taught using powerpoint which isn't very effective for math, so I had to teach myself a lot of the material. However, he did seem to care about his students and the exams were not difficult.

He is very good professor and only wants to see his students succeed as best as they can. He assigns a lot of homework, but the quizzes and tests usually are very similar to the homework, so really study them and you will for sure pass! I took him over summer, so it was a bit rushed, but I do not regret taking him for two math class. Math sucks :(

He's actually very nice and really caring of his students. He is very helpful in office hours. He has some accents but it is not a big deal. He is very organized and study guides are great for quizzes and exam. Make some friends in class so it can help each other out and get good grades.

He is a very good professor. Even though he has some accent but his exams are very easy. I took his class after I failed MATH142B in Spring. I felt very lucky to have him in summer session 1, and I graduated successfully after finishing this course. I hope in the future, the UCSD could let him teach MAth 140 series, which is a nightmare for me.

Professor Diagne seems to love teaching students. He often engaged with his students during lectures and actively solicits student feedback and questions. He doesn't record lectures and strongly encourages attendance, though it is not required. His homework is fair and allows students to correct their own work. He picks accessible textbooks.

Professor Diagne is an outstanding instructor who genuinely supports student learning. Coursework is fair, exams are reasonable with study, and he is always available for help, including review sessions before exams. His clear and engaging teaching style creates a challenging yet rewarding learning experience.

The professor truly cares about student learning. Homework is fair, and exams are manageable with proper study. He's approachable, offers Saturday review sessions before exams, and is always willing to help. Friendly and supportive, he makes the course both engaging and highly recommended.

I feel like the material could've been taught better. Half the time lectures seemed very unhelpful. But he does explain well if he understands the question. Exams were curved which was life-saving. Homework is not bad at all. If you want to truly understand and learn material, might not be best class.
Awesome professor and hilarious! Awesome guy

Professor doesn't do anything. Everything is through a 3rd party website that costs $80 to access- the textbook, homework, quizzes, etc. are all through this website and everything is graded automatically. Doesn't respond to students. If you haven't taken a stats class before, I don't recommend this one. Didn't actually cover PCA or linear algebra.

You need to put a lot of efforts to get a good grade. Try to make him know you and engage in the discussion. I personally don't see any wrong with him but I agree it's too much for a GE class. He is a tough grader, and he likes analytical writing not descriptive. 
I overall liked the class but dont take this class if you're worried about gpa.

Attendance mandatory AND every assignment is graded on a pretty strict 3/4 scale, so this is really annoying if you're trying to maintain a good grade in the course. Readings are okay, and he's nice enough, but overall would not recommend Professor Henry unless you're dedicated extremely to his course.

Prof Henry was clearly passionate about his area of research and his students' learning but assigned LOTS of reading. Some didn't feel entirely necessary. The class isn't difficult but the grading was vague and heavily depended on the TA. Only one person in the class got an A. Wouldn't recommend unless ur really into history tbh.
Weekly quizzes but the questions are so stupid. Really upset at how they are administered given 2 minutes for a quiz every week based on complex readings

Professor Henry is very kind and his lectures are interesting. The readings weren't too difficult to get through for this class but the grading was just so harsh... each assignment is out of 4 points. Final worth 35% of the grade, after receiving an A on every single other assignment I'm going to get a B in the class because I got 3/4 on the final.
Steve Widerman, a globally renowned researcher in data analytics, is a highly respected professor who brings exceptional value to his students.

I took SEO Tools and Analytics with Professor Wiideman, not only does he want to make sure you learn the subject matter but he's willing to share all his wisdom to make sure you do. His class is filled with hands on learning, which requires you to stay on top of the material. He is readily available to help. Highly recommend!

Professor Wiideman made SEO tools and analytics super interesting and easy to comprehend, bc his lectures were very clear, had fun humor, and were structured with step by steps of how to set up & use the tools we were learning about! He is also really responsive, gives great feedback, & genuinely cares for his students. Can't recommend him enough.

I took an online class with Professor Steve Wiideman, and it was a great experience from the beginning. He made complex topics easy to understand, breaking down the material in a clear and approachable way. His teaching was super practical and kept us engaged throughout the course. Would definitely recommend him 5/5

I enjoyed Steve's class- he gave students hands-on, practical experience. Instructions were clear & he was always available when I was stuck. He spoke in layman's terms, a plus for non-technical students. I made it through the class & did much better than I thought! It's clear Steve's a SEO expert and I feel lucky to have learned from the best.

She was an amazing, caring, charismatic professor. She made the class interesting and never made ridiculously difficult exams. The exam was based on subjects clearly spoken about in lecture. She provided slides and podcasts after lecture. Discussion was mandatory but participation was easy. Overall she was one of the best I have had!
Super cool professor! Very inspirational and changed a lot of my thoughts about socio-environmental issues.

Amy Lerner was one of the best UCSD professors I've had. Took her for ESYS 103 spring 2023, and it was such a refreshing class. She explained the concepts so well, you can tell she is passionate about what she does. Courseload is super manageable and she understands her students have lives beyond the class. SHE IS SO CARING10000/10 recommend!

She is an incredibly funny and amazing professor! I would 100% take her again in a heartbeat if I could. DO NOT hesitate to enroll in her class. She is lecture heavy, but her lectures are so bright and inviting, and her class engagement is unmatched.

Taking her for ESYS 103 right now and it is awful. She seems very nice, funny, and overall a good person. I just hate the class. This does not feel upper division. I do not care about the material what so ever. I don't think it is her fault that the course sucks, but it does.
Dude straight up played past recorded lectures on zoom. Avoid avoid avoid.

Professor Nie is caring, and kind, but his lectures (especially in the summer term, when we're dealing with 2 hours of content every other day) are not engaging and difficult to understand. It is also hard to clarify anything since the lectures are videos that are played on zoom, and not him actively teaching. The discussions/hw are good.

To excel in this class, it's essential to thoroughly engage with the lectures and make a solid effort on the homework assignments. Professor Nie is a kind professor. He is a fair grader and is highly accessible through email and office hours, making it easy to get support when needed. Overall, I would highly recommend him for Math 170A!

Nie cares about his students. He explains things very patiently if you have questions. Just go to his office hours or write the email. This class has videos, clear notes, detailed solutions. These are all really helpful. I saw the comments of heacy homework. But he actually shorten the homework a lot based on students' feedback.

I took this course during the 5-week summer session online. While the course is challenging, there were ample resources available (notes, solutions office hours, discussion boards) and there was always an opportunity to ask and his efforts should be acknowledged in providing good communication..
Compelling course with interdisciplinary multimodal, practical, projects. TA's were quite helpful, in assisting in the real-world implementation of engineering theory. Highly reccomended.

The professor gave amazing lectures and had a lot of other interesting ppl present too. The study approach was very research oriented and hence made you understand the topic pretty well 
. Homeworks were basically similar to what was done in class . Exams were very chill too

His class is light work and doable. Weekly hw, 1 midterm, and 1 final. There are quizzes' polls on Zoom every lecture and lab and u have to participate to get the attendance credits. Overall, the TA and prof Kuester are nice and approachable. I recommend him to everyone

I am not sure why these reviews are so negative; Dr. Kuester did an excellent job of teaching a tough subject in a very short amount of time. Lectures were always very clear and helpful, and both homework and exams were challenging, but fair. Plus, if you can get through the material, you get to see some neat things in the world of engineering!

One of my favorite professors and classes at UCSD. A great opportunity to explore your engineering skills and put them to work. This is not a theory class but rather a hands on experience. Expect to go beyond your skill set, and learn a lot about other engineering fields and colleges. A team building class that prepares you for the real world.

I loved prof. Smith so much! Her class was really fun and engaging, even as I took it online, I feel that I learned so much about genetics. Her homework and exams were reasonable, with many opportunities to get points and demonstrate your learning. The class was a lot of work but it was worth it to me, and it's clear she wanted everyone to succeed.

She was definitely very knowledgeable and passionate about genetics. The lectures were easy to follow; it was just dense content (which was more on the class than the professor). The TA's were much less intimidating than the prof when I asked questions---they were great. Discussions were really helpful and went over the problem sets that were due.

I would not take a class with this professor again. The class is graded on a very few amount of things. The midterms are difficult and if you miss one little thing in a free response, question she'll mark you off. She is very unaccommodating with bad circumstances as well.

Despite being a virtual class, super easy to communicate with Professor. She teaches with a genuine enthusiasm for genetics, which made lectures very interesting. So long as you take good notes and treat the HW seriously, all exams will be simple and straightforward. Wish she taught more remote biology classes!

Professor Smith's lectures were engaging and made the material clear. The homework and exams were challenging but aligned well with the course content. Using unstuckstudy alongside the textbook helped me prepare effectively. Overall, it was a rewarding but demanding class.

Professor Saad was an excellent instructor who focused on problem-solving in class, making complex concepts more intuitive. His chalkboard lectures helped me absorb material better, and he always took the time to explain real-world applications. He created a welcoming environment and genuinely cared about our success.

For ECE65—Prof. Saad is amazing lecturer. He's chill and really cares about his students, always making sure everyone gets the material. His lectures focus on solving problems, so you actually learn how to do things yourself. He's great at explaining things in different ways until it clicks, and he makes the class a really welcoming place to learn.

For ECE 65. Elite knowledge of industry (as of current, working at Google), elite knowledge of future ECE classes at UCSD. Gave us an extra hour (4) on the Final so everyone could do well. 2 labs a week will destroy you (pacing, not difficulty). Always be ahead by 1 lab. Use the initial week to get a lab done, don't wait. Great person to be around.

Professor Saad was awesome. He clearly cared that we were understanding the content of the class. Unlike some other professors who just blast through the material whether you understand it or not.  Most of the lectures is problem solving, which I thought was awesome because you learn how to SOLVE THE PROBLEMS. Really cool guy.

I have a feeling a handful of students will be less than impressed with the lectures, but personally I found Professor Saad to be a great professor. I learn very well using the reverse classroom style he promoted. It helps a lot being able to actually do problems during lectures with your peers and having the professor/TA walk around to help.
Very understanding professor. Understands people's living situations and gives them grace when it comes to homework submissions
Easiest class at UCSD. Fulfilled my GEs

Nice guy overall but the contents and how he lectures could use much improvements. The 103 class is just a repetition of how bad militarism (especially the US) is with examples taken out of full context. Mainly narrates the lectures and examples with bias and basically repeats that until the end of the quarter.
Fun class, learned a lot and the professor was clearly very passionate!

He is the best. His lectures were straightforward and informative about the Asian American history. Also, my TA was awesome as well. If you read assigned readings per week and attend discussion sections, you will be good.

Arrogant would be an understatement. He would get super upset and take it personally when students didn't agree with him. Would often lose his train of thought and end class early. He was more sharp in prior semesters.
Awesome professor!

It's an honor being in his presence. TALK TO HIM. He cares about his students IMPROVING. He is always willing to offer help/advice. He's brilliant in his field of study. That being said, the class is rewarding. Don't expect to get an A unless you work for it. I'd take any class he taught. Wonderful experience.

As much as this guy is a legend and very wise in his field, he similarly expects you to be as well. The TA's show no mercy, they worship the ground he walks on. Tremendous amounts of reading and extremely unclear standards for essay tests. Even if you do all of the readings, if you fail to point out untold specifics he is looking for, your screwed.
I did not care for this professor at all. He is boring and arrogant. There are far better choices

My first intro to upper division math - If you're not used to an unforgiving grading structure, I would beware. The lectures were OK for introducing the content, the exams seemed fair but were graded hard with no posted solutions to learn from. Homework is doable, and the TA's were fantastic. Mini-projects!!! (fav part of the course)

He is a nice person, but he does not understand the material himself. He basically copy off of the textbook when teaching, you can feel his pressure when you ask him questions, and he does not understand it and make things up.

I rarely dislike a professor to this degree. Inconsistent and unncessary attendance, forced readings every couple days on a terrible textbook, forced weekly quizzes, bad logistics. He can barely teach the material. I think he's trying too hard. Also please stop using Zulip, grade the quizzes faster and maybe give notes or practice for tests.

Makes attendance mandatory when his teaching skills are subpar. Luckily, the material is easy to digest to compensate for said subpar teaching. Weekly Quizzes, easy HW, fair exams. It's a manageable class overall but don't expect anything outstanding from him as the only thing he is good at is taking attendance.
Robotic lectures, defines things differently than the book.

He is not a good professor. Very hard to look at and also a lot of reading. His tests make no sense and he marks down points on each question for the tests. Also doesn't respond properly to emails and is very boring. This class sucked

One of my favorite classes+profs at UCSD. Professor cares about his students, tests are a true reflection on deep understanding of papers and methods. Attend class! Not a difficult A, content interesting as it is a reflection of things we see today rather than the more theoretical side of econ.

Class is just 25% 2 midterms, and 50% final. READ LECTURE SLIDES and study previous exams,THEY WILL HELP. Professor is really passionate about material which is rare to see. I slacked off in the beginning, but if I didn't I would have gotten a higher grade, my fault. Prof encourages questions and will help you. Material can be old but interesting.

Prof Betts is fantastic! The material is interesting, the exams are straight forward, and he's just such a pleasant, helpful person. This is honestly one of my favorite courses that I've taken at UCSD. It's not a hard class, but I enjoy going to lecture.(No textbook, added bonus!) I would definitely recommend!
awesome class!

Professor Vinciane is absolutely AMAZING, you can tell she cares that her students understand and learn. She finds good examples for you to understand and memorize everything. If you want to learn french and actually have fun doing it definitely take her!

I'm sure Vinciane is a nice kinda lady during in person classes but she thinks you're cheating when you're taking online courses. Can't even focus on the exam because now you're hyper aware of yourself.
This professor falsely accuses people of cheating.  Avoid her if you can

Madame Vinciane is so nice and she cares so much about her students. Her lectures weren't overwhelming and she always made sure that we understood the material, even if we were too shy to say anything. She loves active participants, but sometimes she will call on random people. Definitely made a hard class fun and manageable :)

Had Professor Aliabadi for MATH102 and MATH109. Take him if you get the chance. I would go as far as to say that he is one of the best in the department. Very genuine and teaches the material in a comprehensible way. Can't appreciate this man enough... give him a raise!

Took this class Summer Session I. Lectures were prerecorded and a bit boring, but he explains concepts well. Weekly HW, online midterm, in-person final—all very fair. Exams closely match HW and lecture examples. Only issue was nitpicky TA grading on partial credit, but prof's fairness and clarity made up for it. One of the fairest profs I've had.

Prof made a notoriously hard class feel manageable. Lectures and HW were aligned with exams, which were fair and reflective of the material. I actually found the content fascinating. TA was a bit nitpicky, and grading could improve slightly, but overall a solid professor.

My second class i took with him, and his lectures explain this topic way better than probably many other professors for this class. He is one of my favorite math professors here. If you want a good grade you have to work for it and his tests and homework reflect that, pay attention and you should do fine. Great class, improved mathematical skills

Tbh I HATED math 18 and was expecting this class to be a huge battle, but Professor Aliabadi was great! Unfortunate lecture time 6-7pm, but if you attended lecture would give massive hints and basically solve test problems. Explained everything thoroughly and encouraged asking questions, he was awesome and I did way better in class than I expected
Really good!  He explains topics masterfully!
So good So good So good So good

Most people find this class easy but personally it's difficult for me. The entire class is about MOSFETS and amplifiers. Make sure you study small signals pretty well and other topics that might repeat from ECE 65. Definitely review your ECE 65 prerequisite stuff as well as other things from ECE 100. Professor is very kind and answers questions.
I find him really inspirational as a professor in neuroscience, having a unique way to transmit knowledge

"Mindshift: Break Through Obstacles to Learning and Discover Your Hidden Potential," offered by McMaster University, was an exceptional course. The professor guided us with expertise and passion, making the learning journey incredibly rewarding. She made the material fun, easy to understand, and highly informative.

BIPN 147_No podcasts or slides. Miss class=get notes from other students. DI mandatory+recorded. Grade=DI participation, Midterm, final, Paper review. Hard to reach prof. Professor REALLY knows his material so ask ?s in class. Best advice = Learn some of the formulas and understand their purpose. Very little structure so confusing, but possible.
Excellent learning experience

Dr. Sejnowski is a very good lecturer. He gives information about brain parts and its processes, neurotransmitters and so on. But his explanation was so good and clear that even a person without biological background like me understands all things. He also doesn't give unnecessary information, only basic elements that you need

As long as you show up even to discussion&watch lectures,you should be fine.Lectures were a bit boring, especially @ 8am, & hard to understand at least for me, but clearer on podcast.The Assignments(3 of them)are fairly simple if you know what you are doing,you can work in a group(I did it alone),but tedious.The quizzes just take your time on them.

Prof. Rossano is very sweet and understanding but his lectures are pretty slow and not the most entertaining. The grading is a bit tough and the projects are pretty detailed (even though the instructions are vague) but you can work in groups for all of them, even the final project, and there is no final exam.

Lectures can be boring and slow, but the professor really cares about his students and often brings in guest lecturers. Midterms/quizzes can be kinda challenging and specific but can be done. Assignments are manageable.

Solid professor. Great lectures and really digs deep to explain the "why" of many ideas. Quizzes/exams are somewhat challenging because they cover smaller details from lectures, although all is still relevant. Group projects highly encouraged but not required.

Class was based around group projects (optional to work by yourself) Rossano is super passionate about what hes teaching. He does have an accent, but its not difficult to understand (as a native English speaker). Overall class isn't diffiuclt. Assigns long research papers as readings but they arent 100% necessary to read

Lectures are meandering and he often goes on tangents that are interesting but irrelevant to the class. Did better when I skipped lecture and just read from the book, which is really hard but even then it's more useful than going to class.

Ken is a great guy! From time to time he will totally geek out on physics during lecture and it's so cute. I ended up not really going to every lecture because he would often go on long proof-y tangents. If you can do all of the assigned homework you can easily get a AB in this class.

He is alright. He always starts the week very well and then things get worse as the week proceeds. He usually goes over lecture slowly (lots of proof) and then throws out a bunch of things in the last 2 minutes which make everyone confused. However, the book is very handy. Just read the book and do HW problems and you shall be fine, for an A ;)

A lot of people have said that he's not a great lecturer. I understand why they say this, but I really liked him. You need to apply the important things from lecture to your homework, and then to your quizzes. He brings a lot of demos which are really helpful. He has a dry sense of humor, but I found him hilarious at times. I would take him again.

Professor Intriligator, while friendly, has pretty bad lectures. They are mainly based on proofs, I guess with the assumption that you will go to problem sessions to learn how to do problems. The class itself isn't too bad, though, and his final is mainly old quiz questions.

I took this class as part of preparing for CLS programs and found it very easy to follow. Your grade is based on 5 tests + 4 assignments, but the tests are very fair if you pay attention. Lectures can be a little long. Sad to see people complain about Dr. Dowey's accent. I didn't find her difficult to understand at all.
