At your own risk. Course is 2 credit, 5 test, 50 questions for each test, 75 minutes, test weight 100 points 4 long HW,

Her lectures are very long and hard to hear. I read the textbook in combination with the slides to study for this class. If you want to argue for a point on the exam, she probably wont reply back to you. Exams are based on the lecture slides.

Blackboard only, heavy accent, impossible to follow. Homework useless for exams, no solutions until last minute. Midterm avg 33/85, then random +10. Last week he left, promised 2 videos, gave 1. Dumped HW answers day before final. Final no curve, 50%+ got D/F. For a 5-week course this was a disaster — worst teaching I've seen at UCSD

She is VERY organized. The class is difficult, but just make sure you can answer the learning objectives. The 3 midterms were mostly short responses & some MCQs. challenging but were fair. The final was all MCQ. she gives lots of EC, MAKE SURE TO DO IT. Very clear lectures. Attendance wasn't mandatory. LOVED HER

You can tell she cares deeply for this topic. Her lecture style is very calm and easy to follow. Tests covered a lot of material, so study early! Final was tough bc the mc questions were cumulative so try to memorize pathways the most! Lots of extra credit opps.

The best prof I've had at UCSD!! She genuinely cares about her students and is accessible + approachable. Every learning outcome is clearly described in the syllabus and she always communicates her expectations. Also gives credit for unfair questions and is generally very fair when it comes to grading

Amazing professor.Lecture is very interactive and you actually learn-LOTS of material covered tho. Exams are not super close to lecture material and they are hard-MC and Free response.3 MTs and a MC final w/ weekly PS.Very kind and really cares.learned more from this professor than 2 other classes covering biological systems.Taking again for a Lab!

She was great! Lectures were super comprehensive, covering everything you need to know for the tests with examples, checkpoints, and diagrams. Look at the learning objectives on her syllabus, know her slides and you will do great. Plus, she offers tons of extra credit. Great prof, makes a hard class better

I found the reading materials to be challenging (but very interesting), and the lectures filled any gaps of understanding I may have had. I appreciate the lack of textbook as the texts seemed to be selected purposefully and carefully. Very clear Prof. Zhang knows what he's talking about and is passionate, would love to have him as a teacher again.

Super easy class, just make sure you study for both the midterm and final. All assignments take around 10 minutes to do, and then theres two papers that again are very easy. Very easy grader, the only annoying part was having mandatory lectures.
Mhm. Mhm. Mhm.

weekly assignments (either reading, writing, or analysis). quizzes every class for attendance (class code shown during lecture and graded on completion). midterm and final is super easy if you study based on provided study guide - 45 multiple choice questions.
TA's make the class pretty simple, very easy ge.

made us buy a textbook around $50 that we didn't use at all. She wrote the textbook so maybe thats a reason why its nessecary. Other than that she was caring and nice, had zoom as an option to join in on class which was very considerate of her.  Hard to reach outside of class tho. Only 6 assignments, 3 mini essays and 3 art projects no exams.

After taking multiple classes with Professor Cartwright - I am confident in saying she has the most aura of any UCSD professor. You wont stress about grades, but you will appreciate the quality of teaching and lecturing she provides. She's experienced and knows that her classes are large so is very generous. Yet she can spark a passion in some.

Slides and lectures were disorganized in structure. Also, for a course focused on visual culture, her slides sure were designed in a way that made it unnecessarily hard to read (so much for accessibility..) Her assignments had no clear criteria. Thankfully, my TA was super capable so I didn't leave the class with nothing at all.
an OK GE class, 6 essay HW through quarter where one can choose from weekly topic, pretty passionate about the topic
refused to curve my grade by .2% to a b- it was genuinely insane to me.

Dr. Caballero is a very kind and caring professor! This class had a lot of smaller assignments (4 papers, 7 homeworks, and weekly in-class group quizzes) which made it more time consuming on one hand, but also easy to get a decent grade even if you don't do so well on a couple things

Her lectures are very easy to digest even if you haven't done the reading (please still do them). She gives a lot of opportunities to participate and share experiences regarding the topics in this class. The quizzes are easy as long as you do the reading, which are pretty short compared to other classes.

I really enjoyed Profe Gaby's class! We have 2 readings a week (Tues, Thurs), and a reading quiz every Thurs. There's only 1 midterm (covers weeks 1-5) and a final (weeks 6-10). Her lectures were very interesting and engaging. I really enjoyed the class and highly recommend Profe Gaby and this class if you find Linguistics an interesting subject!

She's awesome! if you're hesitating to take her class, this is your sign to just take it! She makes the class content super enjoyable, eye-opening, and easy. Theres an essay project but she guides you through it throughout the quarter, and there's only 2 midterms and no final so its not something to stress over! I definitely recommend
Pretty interesting material and fairly easy exams.

I guess its okay if you're a fan of hip hop. There's 2 essays and 2 exams. As long as you study for the song recognition portion the rest of the stuff people just cheat on. 3 hour lectures are painful but its only like once a week so I guess it balances out. Attendance technically required but he can't enforce it.

Your grade in the class consists of the midterm, final, short paper, long paper, weekly quizzes, and discussion assignments. The lecture was hard to focus in because it was long like almost 3 hours but you can tell that the prof is passionate about music. He has interesting extra credit like visiting Bario Logan and taking pics that you went.

Very chill professor, Highly recommend this class and instructor. Class attendance is not mandatory (once a week) but greatly helps with weekly quizzes. 1 Midterm, 1 short paper and 1 final paper, and 1 final exam. Rubric is very clear and the class is straightforward. Discussions mandatory. Would highly recommend!

Truly passionate about music and its inspiring. Lectures not mandatory but helpful for the weekly quizzes. TA's do not reply to email but prof responds quickly. 1 short paper and 1 final paper (5 pages). Midterm and final difficult bc of IDing songs by listening to short clips. Overall great class and easy. Fun extra credit opportunities too!

If you want a simple A grade, do not take this Professor. Exams questions are pure intuition and not at all representative of the book problems recommended. Hard grade cutoffs of A, B, C. Not a terrible Professor but for all unsuspecting first years, you will have a much easier time with another professor where it is more computationally focused.

You do one quiz each week. The quizzes combined make up 60% of your grade.
Very bad timing issue. During the tests, the clock was wrong and we would end 5 min early each time. The quizzes were hard because we had never seen those types of questions before. Later quizzes and the final were much easier as they were questions we had seen already.

Amazing professor. Weekly quizzes but they are fairly easy, most of them are just problems we already did in class but with different values. She drops one quiz and her grading scheme is very nice since 85% is an A. Final was slightly harder than the quizzes but still doable since she put some quiz questions on it. She gives iclicker extra credit.

Passionate professor with lectures that seriously engrave the material into your brain. Quizzes are quite fair (lecturer examples often show up on quizzes) and make sure to do the iClicker extra credit! The final consisted of primarily examples from past quizzes. Note that her grading scheme is not the most lenient (average GPA in class 2.25).

Quizzes made me question my life. Final is the easiest thing I've ever done in my life (past quiz Qs). Quizzes are meant to truly probe your conceptual understanding. The final is meant as a grade booster. Medium and Hard never show up. If you want to see the beauty of Physics, take Dudko. This is not a plug and play class. Look past the equations.

Her online ethics class is AWFUL. What is ethical about reusing decade-old lectures and not updating any of the material? I can't believe I paid $700 for her to quiz me on her worldview. She has clearly never worked in corporate accounting. Her lectures are long-winded, boring, and dated. I hope I can get a refund.

If you work, or are planning to take a full-time course load don't take her class! Her class is very time consuming. Her assignments are very long and time consuming for very little points. The exams and quizzes are very long. This class will take up to 20-25 hours per week. This class will take up more time than all other classes put together.

I really enjoyed my cost acct class with this professor. Her lectures are pretty funny. She does not have due dates throughout the quarter but everything is due at the end. This made it easy to balance my other classes. I feel like I learned alot in this class! Take her!
I took her for an ethics class as well and she was solid all around.
made cost accounting fun!

I decided to drop because it seemed like a lot of work for me over the summer. 3 hour lecture, 2 readings, 2 films, 2 quizzes per week. 1 midterm quiz and 1 final paper (5 pages). The quizzes required lockdown browser and some questions were misleading which led to me doing bad. The material did seem important. I just wish the class was more chill.

3 hour class was 1 hour of lecture + 2 hours of watching a movie every week. Overall very chill. You take a 5 question quiz after every class. Midterm included in class essay which sucked but grading was fair, if you go to class it's an easy A. She's clearly passionate about the subject and the movies were pretty interesting.

She is an amazing lecturer and passionate about the course material. I took this for my Fine Arts GE and I'm so happy I did. Grade based on 6 quizzes after watching the movies in-class, 1 midterm, 1 final essay, and three points of possible extra credit. Midterm was kinda rough but I was able to pass the class! 3 hour lectures were kinda long tho

Amazing Professor. Eye opening into the current life of Native Americans. Burelle is passionate about this subject which makes her lectures something to look forward to. perfect elective course: easy A & interesting. 40% midterm (only a few basic questions), 40% final essay, 20% 5 quizzes at end of class. All extra credit  120% in quiz category

prof burelle is amazing, passionate and caring. the first half of class, she contextualizes a film's history and related vocab, and the second half we watch a film. the four pop quizzes were based on slides and the content of the film. the midterm was based on understanding of a few key terms. the final paper was based on clear grading criteria.
Clear lectures, approachable, and genuinely cares about students. Fair and generous grading, although the material can be challenging for short summer session.

Last Econ course at UCSD. Good at explaining things and lectures are recorded for those who can't make it to class. Mentioned no extra credit but in the end provided opportunity for 5% bonus. Overall, tough class for summer session but good material. Be prepared to study and take advantage of the previous exams he provides for study material.
Great prof. Exams are reasonable as long as you do the practice one.
Prof Ma seems serious, but is nice if you talk to him. Lecture slides are clear, good examples. The practice exams are helpful. Tests are representative of the material. Not too much homework.
Clear lectures and well-organized. Grading is transparent and fair. No surprise questions in the exam.
I miss you. Come back

He's really funny and chill because he lets us use any notes we want during the quizzes/final. He offers us extra credit after every quiz and one homework extension. There are biweekly quizzes and weekly homework. He is a good lecturer and responds quickly on piazza. He also has zoom and recordings of the lectures if you can't make it to class.

My grade was due to a few missing homework assignments, but he gives extensions when asked within a reasonable amount of time. No midterms, just homework due every Sunday. The final was really difficult, however a lot of the homework problem and previous quizzes were on it just reworded or reworked. Allows digital notes and previous quizzes.

He was chill, attendance not mandatory, recorded lectures, and also via zoom. Had 4 quizzes every 2 weeks with 8 questions. Only bad thing is if you literally get 3 question wrong you're screwed. Hw is worth the most, 25%. Final can replace your lowest quiz score. He gave 0.5 bonus points after every quiz.

I literally hate physics and he made me like it. He really went out of his way to make it really applicable to biology and help us understand why we'd ever need to know this. Explained things SO well with the time that he had
It's such a shame that he won't be coming back for the next quarter, cause he's literally the best professor I've ever had.
Hes so babygirl. Love this man. Hes so accomodating and cares about his students.

such a great professor. doesnt see a point in memorization. tests are open note and group work, as well as homework. doesnt flood us with assignments. took him for cell bio summer session 2. take this guy!!

One of the best professors I've had. Definitely a tough course, but he makes everything super clear and you know what's expected. Great at teaching and makes you apply your knowledge, making you think like a scientist and a physician. Open-everything exams and can work in groups, with lots of extra credit. Favorite class in my four years here.

Dr. Tat allows students to take their exams open-note, open-book, and open-computer. Exam and homework questions rely heavily on whether or not you can apply the things that you learn in lecture. Exams are hard! However, there's lots of EC opportunities, especially when you can speak up during class. BIMM 110 is a tough class, so study hard!

During Summer session 1,Professor Tat is very passionate, and his lectures are very interesting all that is a plus! however, he is a very strict grader expects so much from you and Homeworks are very hard all based on readings.midterm is 40+ questions but definitely makes you think. I recommend taking him only and no other upper division. good luck

He is goated. He is passionate about teaching, good at explaining concepts, and cares about his students. He even remembers everyone's name (I took this class over summer, could be different over regular school year).

The material was not the easiest at times but Deepam was very good at being patient and breaking down the core concepts. For a non major class, we were not expected to come in with an in depth understanding but I certainly came away with a much better understanding of genetics. Very generous grading scheme too!
She is the GOAT. Lectures are actually fun and engaging. She is super passionate about teaching and wants her students to succeed. Grading is clear and the curve is massive.

lectures are clear and well-organized, with transparent grading from the start. She knows chemistry is tough but gives you all the tools to succeed. Although she is new to teaching, she is already amazing and clearly loves her job. The class is challenging, but she makes it enjoyable and rewarding. She is one of the best professors I've had!

!!!!TA!!!! NOT PROF extremely harsh and irregular grader, doesn't seem to follow professor's grading rubric. jeopardized our entire 200+ classes' midterm grades... as a second time having this difficult TA, I strongly advise against it. I've never received such low grades besides her grading as a double major. AVOID for your grades sake

Sam is awesome. Hes super funny, approachable, and genuinely care about students. There's lots of reading and it's awks to come to class without prep, but it makes the class discussions way more engaging. The grading system is really low-stress and focused on learning instead of points, which I loved. Great class and an even better professor!
Hard to make out what he's saying during lecture.
Lectures are very clear and organized, although a bit slow. He's very knowledgable on the topic and has written a whole textbook on it.
Super solid professor. He was funny in class, and his lectures provided good intuition about the subject. Probably the easiest professor for Math 140. Definitely take his class if you see him!

Don't be intimidated by his Asian name! He has no accent at all and is a great lecturer and an awesome teacher! The 140 series is literally one of the hardest series in UCSD math major, but he taught it in a way that is much easier to understand than any other professor here. I have experienced 3 professors in the 140 series and he teaches the best
Do NOT MISS this WONDERFUL professor because of this rmp grade for him. The 2.8 is WAY TOO LOW for this good man
Incompetent and unprofessional professor. My grade wasn't recorded properly on my transcript, and he doesn't respond to emails. The class wasn't difficult... but first time facing this

An amazing professor who I would definitely take again. Grade is based on attendance and two 6-8 page essays, and prompts are released weeks in advance. A decent amount of readings, but definitely manageable; ~30-50 pages a week. TAs can be unpredictable graders so maybe just go to their OH before the midterm. Otherwise, a perfect poli sci class!
Great Professor, both the midterm and final are essays that you are given 2 weeks to complete. Apart from that, you need a clicker remote and to be present at lectures.

I enjoyed Professor Fisk's class! He's very passionate and informed on the subject + he does a great job  tying in current events to themes in the course. Attendance is measured witch iclickers but there's a lot of leniency imo. Two essays, clear criteria. TA feedback can be a little vague but they're very approachable in case of questions.

I couldn't keep up with this class. There's a lot of info to absorb and it depends on your TA's grading. Two essays for the midterm and final are 6-8 pages and attendance is mandatory. I hardly did the readings and managed to get a B+. I would not take him again, but I am giving him 4 stars because he was a nice person and wanted us to succeed.

I took Prof. Hendrickson for during summer and I found his class to be very engaging. He doesn't just use slides but incorporates some really interesting documentaries, podcasts, and even music. Assignments were all reasonable and as long as you attend class and engage with it you will be able to complete them with ease. Highly recommend!

Clicker questions are used for attendance and based on the readings. No midterms, just two essays and a final (in-person essay). Professor is very passionate, he is born for this. The class is easy and interesting. If you join debate you'll get extra 3%. Only bad thing, we get limited feedback about our essays, and it took some time to see grades.

Clicker questions are used for attendance and based on the readings, but some classes don't require attendance and he drops five of the lowest grades for the clickers. No midterms, just two essays and a final. The class is very easy and discussion attendance is mandatory. He also calls on people to speak in class randomly so be ready for that.

Loved this class. Uses I clickers which count towards grade. So have to attend class. But no quizzes bc of iclickers. 2 papers. The material is super interesting. Mandatory discussion but can miss one. Lectures not recorded.

Only complaints No Podcast and $80 Book. But this man definitely knows what he's doing. The readings and lessons for his class are very interesting and applicable. I could've gotten an A or B in his class if I put in 100% effort. NO EXAMS ALLOWED IN THIS CLASS! Clicker Question easy if U read or use CHATGBT. I used CHATGBT to study for the final.

SUCH AN AMAZING PROF! Gave lots of EC and always open during office hours for help on HW and any other questions. Was rlly supportive on giving me options for exam makeups. Listened to feedback on how to lecture and taught in a way that was simple to understand. would take him 1000 times over again

Prof. Watson was my favorite professor at UCSD. He was very passionate on immigration issues and was very engaging in lectures. I felt so called to participate in class which I cannot say happens to me normally. He was able to make students expand on their thoughts and gave positive pushback to our answers, deepening critical thinking.

AMAZING PROFESSOR! Super passionate and active in the subject of immigration. Lectures are engaging as well. Tests/midterms are easy as well, just based on class content and readings. Amazing professor to connect with. Overall would recommend him to anyone and everyone! 10/10 :)

Lectures were not mandatory, but I highly suggest attending them. Professor Watson's lectures were often interactive and insightful regarding immigration matters. I experienced thorough feedback on assignments, regardless of performance (which I greatly appreciate)! This class left such a positive impact that I declared a minor in Sociology.

It was a really tough course but I am really glad that I took it. Probably the most useful class to prepare me for internship in pharmaceutical industry. His class is harder than other lecturers', very math heavy, but covers a lot more than just doing the lab.

This class is a lot of work with very time consuming lab reports every week. They are more strict, frequent,  and time consuming than the reports from 108 and 109 which are 6 units. The final is unethical, but the grading is really generous with a massive curve and the professor is great at lecturing, but since this is a lab your TA matters more.

He is a really great lecturer. The homework's are not very difficult but are very time consuming. The exams are very difficult research application questions. If you understand the material on a qualitative level the questions will make sense, but still require tough math. I strongly recommend this class for all chemistry students.
I took a gradate course with Dr. Lomakin in UCSD. He is a real phenomenon in Electromagnetics. I am proud with him. He has an exception knowledge in Electromagnetics.

A great teacher who focuses on the fundamental aspects of electromagnetics. The lectures are primarily designed for PhD students or individuals with a strong mathematical background. I really enjoyed the course because it not only teaches physics but also demonstrates how to apply mathematical methods to wave propagation systems.

Difficult course, but Lomakin teaches with a lot of enthusiasm. Seriously he's always happy, it's contagious 🙂. Has a slight accent and teaches fast, "don't worry you get used to it" and prefers "old-fashion" method for questions outside of class but is often available. 1 midterm - final, HW, and Lab. Fair exams. MASTER 107 material prior to 182.

Difficult class. There are three quizzes, two of them being pop quizzes that can happen at any time. The lectures are difficult to follow along because there are many equations that are usually taken straight from the textbook, but copied with no explanation.  You will almost certainly have to self-study from the textbook outside of the lectures.

The majority of this class heavily focus on theories and math, and professor hardly explain the math and how to solve problems unless you ask him. The lecture slides and homework haven't been updated for many years, and professor doesn't give too much exercises to prepare for exams.

Adam's first time teaching CSE 107 after TA'ing it multiple times. Lectures were fun and engaging (dice hat!). He made the material interesting, encouraged feedback, and responded thoughtfully. Lots of in-class activities and direct attention. I highly recommend taking this class with Adam.

Probably in my top 3 list of professors at UCSD. This man in his two quarters teaching analysis at UCSD has been one of the best experiences. Super approachable, amazing grade curving and genuinely cares about all his students. Wish you the best Davide!! UCSD will miss you!

I had Davide for 142A/B and I genuinely loved this class. He was always very supportive, always checked in during lectures to make sure we understood, and was great at giving feedback. His lectures were very organized and clear to understand. His exams were always very fair as well, and he always curves his classes. He 100% wants you to succeed.

Best professor I have had at UCSD, only one I wrote a review for. Very succinct in communicating the important topics, accessible outside of class, above all else focuses on the real world application and understanding beyond the classroom. Highly recommend.

Challenging class if you're not strong in calculus. Lectures felt unorganized, quickly covering problems without enough explanation. Grading based on Edfinity homework, textbook problems, one midterm, & a final exam. Discussions are optional, & both exams are in-person without notes or calculators. 
Significant grade curve at the end of '23 quarter

Super chill guy but since analysis is very hard the average for the midterms is around 50% or less so just fyi...

hes very sweet but sometimes he seems kinda dead when hes doing the lectures but hes always open for questions during class so thats nice
Wow, old fashioned teaching style, difficult personality

If I could I would have never signed up for this class, it was very difficult to understand this professor and I definitely struggled to grasp concepts. I barely made it and I had to get a lot of extra help from YouTube and other teachers to pass this class. I would caution those moving forward to take this professor. Hope this helps.
Not the hardest but not the easiest. you gotta put in work outside of class but his expectations are straight forward. Only test based

Graded only off three exams, final worth 50%. Material is challenging, mostly memorizing pathways. Exams based on correcting false statements and short answer q's. Attendance and textbook not required and lectures are podcasted. He reviews prior lecture material at the start of each lecture. Had to do review by myself on YouTube after each class.

horrible prof, avoid if you can. He teaches at the med school and you can tell he expects us to be at that level of understanding already. Confusing lectures and hard tests that he expects you to know everything for... do not recommend

Amazing prof I had for PDE (partial diff equations). Not an easy class by any means for a non proof oriented class, but so is the other upper div math classes at UCSD for the most part. Tests and homeworks are pretty challenging so do your best to understand each chapter the best you can. He will change the cutoffs knowing the exams are difficult.

Class was hard but doable if you put in the work. His midterm was definitely a lot harder than the final but he has a grading scheme where the midterm is only worth 15% of your grade so don't worry if you do really bad on it. He made the final a lot more doable and fair and as long as you put in the work, that will carry your grade.

Great professor, passionate about his stuff, wonderful learning experience. I used Anvaka's Field Play to visualize the concepts and it was a great tool to have for the course as well. Also teaches at a reasonable speed and answers questions while letting students catch up. Would totally take his class again.
this guy is the goat professor. super fair tests, very precise and clean explanations, and accessible outside of class. would love to take another class with him if i get the chance

You go to office hours and you'll know exactly how to solve any problem given to you. Lectures were challening to follow and his expectations were slightly higher than expected, the class itself was made a breeze with this man. Would take him if you want an actually good professor.

Does not podcast or publish slides so you just have to come to lecture and hope and pray. Reported 20% of students to the Academic Integrity office for cheating when he did not have solid proof (he is genuinely paranoid that everybody is cheating). Gives weekly quizzes worth nothing. He did waive the final because he said we did well on midterms

Forces you to buy his own textbook to do homework that's worth 60% of your grade, mandates in person attendance where he just reviews the material on the homework whose deadline has already passed. Gives weekly pop quiz worth 0% of the grade, but if don't score well on these quizzes, he suspects you of cheating. Least effective teacher I've had.

Need to spend at least 20 hours a week on the homework. Be prepared for the communication sessions (quizzes, and would call out people's name to explain concepts). Prepare for the live coding in a limited period of time.

Pevzner's unique teaching style does not have bad intentions but has the potential to traumatize students who have done nothing wrong. And with 60 programming assignments in ten weeks, it is universally agreed upon that this course is the hardest in UCSD's CSE department. Expect to spend 20-50 hours a week doing PAs.
Fail final fail the class. 20Hr+ work on homework. Not a friendly class for people who are not good at programming.

Bafna isn't the best lecturer like i feel like lecture does drag on, however he makes this class not too difficult. I'd say he is quite lenient when it comes to homework and exams, and he is super sweet just a bit disorganised.

Slides oftentimes make no sense, and explanations are worse. TAs aren't useful - grading criteria is extremely harsh, and don't bother asking questions on Piazza if you want answers. Disorganized HW assignments where questions are changed or removed entirely several days after being assigned. Avoid at all costs.

Prof Bafna isn't the best lecturer (class feels like it drags on); however, the podcasts makes the course material much easier to follow. The exams are graded very leniently, so don't worry if you feel unconfident walking out of them. The class might be more difficult if you haven't taken CSE 181 but is still doable.

Well. I think Professor Bafna can explain concept better. It is important to give student outline of different concept and explain the logic. However, all he did during class was reading the slides. The assignments were not well prepared. The questions were not clear at all. Especially the TA graded hard on the questions.

While I didn't love this class, I thought the professor was great. The lectures were pretty slow and because of this many people do not go to lecture, however if you podcast the class and can speed it up and down, Bafna teaches the material very well. He also gives a very generous curve, he does want to see his students succeed.

Very empathetic and sweet professor. Gives great feedback and really cares about students. His lectures are a little boring, but they are brief. As long as you complete assignments and show up, you will get an A.

Didn't have for SYN 150; Had for SYN 1. Vega is a caring guy who wants the students to succeed in his class and only does things to try and help them. You can tell he enjoys discussing the material that he covers and gives great insight on how students can develop and communicate their ideas. Flexible grader who emphasizes process and learning.
Confusing assignments, and says that grades are openly discussed but can be changed the last day of class. Will still be strict on attendance regardless of emergencies.

The class consists of random writing assignments that culminate to the final project which is creating a hypothetical proposal with a group in the form of an essay + presentation. The grading system can be confusing but essentially you're graded on effort put into your work rather than entirely the content. Not the worst class to take

He's enthusiastic and prepared, but he tends to be repetitive when explaining, even for simple concepts. Explanations could be more concise. Lectures are not recorded, no annotated lecture slides. The course grade was 40% midterm and 60% final. It would be nice to account homework, to encourage students to do problem sets and raise their grade.

You're much better off watching crash course videos or reading your textbook as opposed to attending his lectures. He's a bit unorganized and his lectures are hard to understand. It's possible to get an A on his exams without attending lectures, just study on your own.

One of the worst Professors ever in UCSD history does not know what it means to be a professor. Constantly went on on tangents during lectures and then was shocked when people did poorly on exams. Never had a consistent grading policy because he kept messing up, and the final was 50-60% of everyone's grade and it was TERRIBLE.

Very good professor, he explains everything good and it is easy to understand. Midterms, and homework is very similar so there is not a tricky exam or anything. He has an accent which for me made it better to emphasize with the professor since I also have an accent, and thanks to that it is a very comfortable class to be in.

His lectures are unclear and grading rules are restrict and not fair. The whole course grade is only determined by two exams. Every exam has 24 questions and they are mostly jointed. If you do not know part a, you do not know ho to answer the followings. Many questions require you to find a lot of unknowns, write short answers and graphs.

While Wilbur has a strong resume, students shouldn't be fooled into thinking this means a helpful course. The learning environment was dampened by what felt like constant confrontation between the students and Professor. He refuses to listen to feedback and prefers condescension over advising. If you want an A, self study, don't bother with OH.

Super nice professor and cares about what he's teaching. Participation is not just showing up, but "verbal participation". HW is optional and he gives no answers to them or the practice tests. Tests were T/F, MC, and a few frq but if you left them blank he gives 2/4 on frq. Good luck guys!

One of the worst professors I've had at UCSD. Didn't show up to his office hours and didn't show up to the first midterm. Also TA is rude and unhelpful.

Definitely take the other professor who teaches MGT 100. 

Grades favor student who want Bs. Impossible to get an A unless you basically ace his test. The curve is unfair cuz he caps the A to 8%. 

Just take the other professor. You can check sets and capes to see why.

The professor's lectures are not engaging and seemed to have issues with students throughout the course. Although class contribution is worth 10% of your grade, the average score was a 0.9/5 which significantly impacted grades. Attendance policies are strict which is frustrating as this is college, not high school. I don't recommend the professor.

Prof Ellis is the way to go if you're new to programming. This class was extremely accessible, and even made much easier by my elementary CS knowledge going in. There are a lot of assignments, but LE/LA attendance is optional so I had plenty of time. This was a really well-structured class and there's a ton of support and opportunities to succeed.

Probably one of the easiest classes I've taken so far. There's a ton of material provided to better your understanding and it's clear from the get-go that this class is meant for those with no coding experience so the class is reasonably easy.
she made the class less intimidating bc one the first day and week, she made sure that everyone knew that this class was INTRO, and which types of students she would expect to take this class.

This is probably one of the easiest and most useful classes you can take at UCSD. She takes students from zero experience in Python to a level where we can apply it in the real world. Just show up to lecture for the extra credit, and do as many practice problems as you can, if you understand those, you're golden.

TAKE HER!!! She is an amazing professor who actually wants you to learn Python! She is extremely reasonable and gives a lot of extra credit. I had ZERO experience with Python and ended with over 100% and a good understanding now. If you keep up with the material, you will do great! She also gives out plenty of opportunities for help along the way.

I stopped going to in-person lectures after week 2 and start looking at videos. The lectures are interesting but one can do the hw even without the lecture materials. u do have to complete a group project which is a major part of ur grade so I'd say that TAs are more important cuz they are the ones that actually grade it

His video lectures are extremely boring as he speaks in a monotonous tone. Exams were difficult. They often ignore students' questions on Campuswire. Homework would be posted at an inconsistent interval, and their respective LaTeX template didn't even go up at the same time with the pdf, resulting in days where no progress could be made.

Just got my final grades and the averages are terrible. The class had less than C- avgs on assessments which are 50% of our grade. I'm hoping our class is due for a curve because otherwise, this class is the hardest I have taken at UCSD. The content itself is pretty cool and better than other DSC and MATH courses though and the prof is chill though

To submit all homework/project assignments you need to take an individual picture of each problem when there's literally a google doc template that you can download and submit. This guy is terrible, avoid at all costs if you value your grade. Honestly the worst instructor at UCSD, he shouldn't even be a TA, let alone an instructor.

Class was easy and relied mainly of invited speakers but was unorganized and confusing on why they were relevant for topics. Didn't learn much about urban planning felt more like a DEI class and though she preached inclusivity and caring her class narrative was VERY biassed and one sided. If you're good at BSing DEI stuff definatley an easy class.

Difficult to understand, seemed narcissistic, flighty, and unpredictable. Didn't seem to really care about people. Avoid!
She asks alot of her students, but is willing to do whatever to help us reach that. she can be hard to follow (unorganized) but just ask her to clarify

She is really nice as a person, but the worst professor I had EVER!! Her classes are caotic. She is totally unorganized, doesn't know the GIS program well enough to teach the class, and is constantly talking down to students. She only helps those students who are her favorites. AVOID HER CLASSES!!!
CSE 101 is a hard course. Professor wasn't bad at all as some of the reviews are saying. Teaching was fairly standard. I wish there were more office hours offered by the Professor.
I learned a lot from this class. Exams were hard but manageable.

As you can see from the reviews above Professor. Saha's course was a disaster. My biggest criticism of her was her handling of criticism. When students used piazza to communicate there issues she responded with a lengthy reply telling students they were wrong without any supporting logic. She would then shut the post down for further discussion.
Hardest class

Genuinely one of the worst professors I've taken at UCSD. Staff was so unorganized, we had a total of 4 assignments and received feedback weeks late for each one. We got a syllabus in week 5. That's unheard of!! What upsets me is that the material of CSE 101 is actually pretty important too. Wish I had a better professor for this one.

The class was interesting and taught how business operations function. The exams provided enough time and allowed for open notes which gave more room to study about the math of it than the examples provided. He also gave a small break in the class since it was 3 hours long from 8-11am. Would def take again!
great lectures, made difficult concepts seem easy. I got a lot out of this course.

I learned a lot in this class. If you do the reading before class, then his lectures are easy to understand. The prof. was easily accessible outside class and during OH. His lectures lean more toward quant and data than anecdotal and industry examples.

Avoid if possible. The lectures are confusing, presents the material with minimum explanation. Language in quizzes are vague and does not reflect what we learned in lectures. Gives out simple examples that is not helpful at all for the quizzes you have to take. Barely learned anything from this class. Slow grader for the group project.

Lectures don't feel complete to do well on the quizzes as the weekly quizzes are designed to trick you with wording and detailed understanding of concepts. There are no other resources available. Just lectures and OH where the info from OH should be in the lectures! If needing a remote class for remoteness, there is an in-person group project

AMAZING PROF! He really cares for the students. There was no midterm and 2 "finals" which were really easy (easy A). Attendance is mandatory, but u could easily just write your name in the attendance sheet and leave class. There is a lot of reading, but all readings are interesting and are in Perrusall.

Professor Fusté is amazing, he cares so much about his students and tries to be as accessible as possible to ensure that every student feels prepared in class. The readings he assigns are interesting and his lecturers are great for anyone with ADHD/ADD because he speaks at a pace that is easy to follow. I love his classes!

ABSOLUTELY TAKE HIS CLASSES !! he's so caring and you can tell he enjoys his job and cares about the community, he's very sweet! everyone felt comfortable to share out in class. he made me realize I want to study more into ethnic studies :) readings are also great I was showing some of the articles to my whole fam bam, they've very interesting

AMAZING!! i love him I'm going to be taking his classes in the future for sure! he's very easy to talk to, he makes lectures fun, i rlly enjoyed his class. he gave everyone extra days to turn stuff in if needed which is very generous. theres a lot of readings assigned but they're super interesting. Best prof ive ever taken we need more like him :)

Professor Fuste is very charismatic! In his lectures, he likes to hear what the students have to say, and his grading style makes you feel less restricted on assignments. He does sometimes get distracted during lectures lol and there is a bit more amount of assignments throughout the course than in other classes.

I took this class this spring and it was really easy. There is a lot of reading, which most of them can be confusing. Lectures are interesting and well organize. Midterm and Final were also really easy and doesn't have to be perfect as long u reflect on the material.

Such a great professor. I would 100% take class with her again!! lots of reading and writing but overall really easy. Everything is basically online. Sometimes she'll take attendance by asking us to write a paragraph regarding a reading. Final was 2 essays.

I took Professor Whitley for CGS 105 and I thoroughly enjoyed coming to her class and engaging with the readings every week. That said, DO get ready to do A LOT of readings (could be up to 30+ pages), though they do get your mind working and are beneficial to participate in the in-class discussions. Our format was 2 essays + 3 writing assignments.

I took CGS 106. Professor is nice but overall class is just ok. Grade consists of reflective writings, participation, and final. Classes go over readings for each week. Readings are VERY LONG and pretty confusing. Hard to follow along in my opinion.

I really enjoyed Professor Whitley's class. She is a really cool lady. The lectures are well-structured, informative, and explain complex theories very well. The midterm and final were super easy and take-home essays. Overall great class.
Nikolay is a perfect professor
Projects are very hard but Nikolay very willing to help and is always on Piazza!

Nikolay has been one of the best professors I've ever taken a course with. Even though this course is extremely difficult and time-consuming, he and his team of TA's are always available on Piazza and do actually care about the effort you put in and not just your final results. The projects are difficult but also very useful and you'll learn a lot!

Very rigorous course, but he absolutely makes it enjoyable. I loved all the homework's and the projects and they're super useful to clear concepts. Would absolutely recommend if you want to learn robotics properly, one of the best professors i've been taught by. 

10/10

His assignments and projects are challenging but meaningful and make you have a better understanding of the applications that you learn. However, the problem statements can be unclear most of the time so make sure you ask any questions on Piazza. He replies questions promptly.
Amazing professor overall!

No reading. Fun lectures. Lectures are very note heavy. Lowest midterm gets dropped, but exams account for 90% of your grade. Lots of opportunities to make up bad grades. Top 5/9 weekly quizzes, top 2/3 midterms, and SONA. Very easy exams and fun course.

Great Prof! Exams were very representative of class content. Exam averages were always really high. I studied a good amount, so the tests were super easy. I didn't study for the last midterm and still got an A (but I do review my slides for a bit right after lecture so). She's engaging in my opinion, and I loved her voice lol.

Dr. Tallman's class was really fun to take, and every lecture introduced an interesting topics. I went to her office hours several weeks to ask questions and she's really nice! Her class is mainly graded by weekly quizzes and midterms (some get dropped) as well as the final. I definitely want take her courses again in the future.

Professor Tallman is one of my favorite professors I've had so far. She's really engaging & passionate about the material she covers. Her PowerPoints are concise & she is extremely clear about what will be on the exams. There are 3 midterms & a final, all in-person (4 exams total), so it is exam heavy. But she prepares you well in advance.

Dr. Metwalli is by far one of the best professors I have had. He is extremely passionate about the subject and it shows through his teaching. He relates a lot of the lecture content to the clinical setting which I found very helpful because it made it interesting and applicable. Tests are fair, quizzes are fair, he will tell what u need to know.

Dr. Metwalli gets a bad rap, but as long as you submit your assignments on time, regularly put effort in your assignments, you will get a decent grade. Important thing I learned from discussion boards: make sure you relate your learnings from previous chapters (ex: in the Reproductive chapter, relate to concepts from the Endocrine).

This professor is probably one of the most confusing graders I have ever encountered. 
He has weekly discussion posts that have no rubric but he grades very harshly and will give you confusing feedback. 
lectures are "supplemental" that he recorded for an combined A&P class.
Test are fairly straightforward
STUDY

Not the biggest fan of Professor Metwalli. Sometimes he wouldn't respond to emails. Not sure why. Other professors at UCSD are more responsive. No extra credit. Timed tests. The lectures were helpful, so print them off.

Very kind and knowledgeable BUT disorganized. The lectures don't connect dots between varying concepts and he jumps around a lot. Towards the end, only half of the class stayed for lectures. I used youtube lectures. Be prepared to organize your own lab time for studying and read the textbook to integrate concepts together. Make flashcards!

Prof Nguyen was pretty nice but can be tough to follow in lectures. He lets you drop lowest test score which helps a lot but the class wasn't curved at all. I did better than I expected but it was def one of the hardest classes I've taken.
I think this guy has something going on internally.

I came in this course expecting it to be difficult because genetics is just a tricky subject in general. It was unorganized at the start, but became more organized further in the course. Attending discussions helps a ton even if it's not mandatory, please go. Tests are a bit difficult since its FRQ, highest I got was a B.

Professor Nguyen is a kind professor who notices patterns in the classes understanding of the content and adjusts in real time. He is also pretty receptive to advice. Lectures cover about 60% of what will be on exams, leaving the rest to homework. Lectures can be hard to follow at times. Discs. are not mandatory but will prolly help u.

Professor Nguyen is a very nice guy and was quick to adapt when the class was struggling. The homework is a lot and is due at 5 pm, which was very annoying. Besides that, he is a pretty good lecturer and offers lots of extra credit opportunities. Discussion was not mandatory, but helpful especially for reviewing for midterms.

This was a 6 week summer course I took and this class was overall pretty easy, all you had to do was watch a couple of videos then take a quiz based on them and answer a question based on the video. A large worth of your grade is based on essay exams, but he gives you the questions to them a couple days prior. The class felt like a history class.
he is one of the best!

He is one of the best professors I have ever had so far & I'm not even taking chem anymore because I switched majors. He gives you so many opportunities to do well in this class although I'd have to say the amount of quizzes and midterms is insane. You have to always be on top of this class in order to succeed.

This is probably the most difficult course that must be taken by ERC undergrads. Allen isn't trying to make it harder but he isn't just serving you a hot, juicy A either; he's very understanding and wants you to give it your best. Very knowledgable of the material and overall, a real good guy. Would recommend, for sure.
This class was very interesting! Bolar is awesome! he was always willing to help and the t.a. was cool too. A lot of reading but it was interesting. I would definitely recommend you take his classes.

I appreciate Prof. Papen coming out of retirement to teach our class, he'll always get a 5 for that. I just wish he had recorded lectures, but that's mookhjeas fault for picking 8 AM. Still, He was very enthusiastic about optical engineering and constantly motivated the class with real-time developments in the industry. Please enjoy retirement sir!

Good lecturer, speaks clearly. Tries to give intuition and go beyond just the technical aspects of the class. Tends to get a little excited, but that's good especially for a class at 8 AM to keep you awake. Midterm and homeworks weren't too hard with high grades. Final was harder than expected, but grading was very fair. Overall recommended

Great lecturer. Very clear, and slows down when he knows its confusing. Tough subject matter, but he gives you what you need to do it. 5 homework sets, some pretty long, a midterm, and a final project. If you really understand the project and do well on it, youll probably get an A, even if you did poorly on the rest.
a
Values foundation + a great lecturer! definitely take this class. :)

How come no one left a review for 136? Anyways, Grading: Lab reports 90% Lab pop quizzes 10%. Like 135B, you need to be very efficient at plotting data, functions, anything. Excel def should be a prereq. Labs are boring since the TAs handle everything, but working in the Nano3 cleanroom is amazing.

Lots of ground to cover thanks to Kuzum, but Dayeh values deep understanding over grades 24/7, emphasizing fundamentals. He still remains sharp and dedicated to the undergrads, updating his slides prior to every lecture, and extending his hand to any student eager to learn. Hopefully in another 10 years students will still leave his class smiling🙂
a good professor. clear lectures, go thru equations step by step, make sure you understand the content, occasionally makes joke to keep you focus and awake in class.

Professor Dayeh goes out of his way to ensure everyone understands the material clearly. Semiconductor physics takes some time to sink in, but I started to grasp it much better after learning about the different devices throughout this course. It gives a good understanding of electronics from fundamental principles.

An ideal Professor. Always well prepared and delivered clean, lucid lectures while sprinkling in a couple funny jokes to keep the class engaged. Exams were challenging, but intellectually stimulating. Held extra office hours to ensure we grasped the material. Provided guidance beyond the classroom. More than a teacher, Professor Dayeh is a mentor.

Had a 96.5% before the final, which meant that even if I didn't do well on the final I should still pass the class. Proceeds to fail me because I missed class. Clearly he's a professor who prefers people who are willing to be slave employees that show up at specific times to listen to him yap.

This class was difficult, but Professor Hardimon is great. He is clearly passionate about what he does and you can tell that he enjoys engaging in conversation with his students. He has a great sarcastic sense of humor and is very understanding. Attendance is mandatory and you are graded on few things so be sure to take good notes/ask questions!
Super interesting class, but hard papers. Final isn't too bad. Prof. Hardimon is quite a funny guy and he's very understanding. Hard class but good prof! (this is for PHIL 33 btw)
Read all of the assigned reading! And the feedback for essays isn't great but the content is super interesting!

Phil 33 SP23-Super caring and funny in a way that is natural! His classes are lecture heavy and mandatory. So are discussions. Be prepared to take notes! He does not upload any sort of lecture slides so it is important to take as much notes as you can. But he is super helpful and so was the TA. There are 3 papers, no midterms, and a final.

He is a great mathematician, but he is not a great teacher. Expects way too much of you for an undergrad analysis course. Sometimes he would make problems more tricky than they were supposed to be, so it would be harder to know how to prepare for an exam. At this level of math, you cannot randomly change problems and expect to solve them fast.
I love how professor Mohammadi teaches. He explains hard concepts very well and answers questions in a way you can understand. I would love to take a class with him as professor again.

I took this with him during Summer 2 2023. As far as I know, this is the most rigorous version of this class taught. His lectures were very clear and engaging, and he made the homework quite proof-based rather than purely computational. Only complaint is that the quizzes were quite time crunched, but overall very fair class for summer session

I don't even know where to start. Tests were beyond unfair. Homework was doable, yet the tests were far more difficult and the averages speak for themselves (which both the midterm and final were like 30% average). Barely curves and barely gives partial credit for any tests. Class GPA was 1.8. Save yourself the headache.
Really tough class but it made me a much better mathematician. Prof Mohammadi is also really funny and an amazing lecturer.
very rarely does he ever fail people. the class is very hard no matter where you take it or who you take it with but goatpat is your best choice

It is so obvious that Professor O loves teaching and understand the students' perspective, and it made me want to do better in his class. Besides occasionally hard tests (which he recognizes), there is nothing bad I can say about him. Generally he is just an amazing guy. My favorite professor in the CENG department!

Very awesome professor. The material is not complicated. He covers everything very well so reading the textbook is not that necessary, however, the textbook is needed for some homework problems. There are not many homework so they weight a lot but they are simple. Midterm is fair and straightforward. Final is take home and can be done in pairs.

He is very funny and knows how to keep class entertaining. Tests are representative of the materials covered in class. If you know how to do homework questions then you should be fine on tests. Online homework can be troublesome sometimes because you have to enter the exact answer in order to get credit. His first time teaching but still very good.

Dr. O is one of the most awesome professors if not THE most. He is super clear in teaching, giving us a lot of examples. Tests might be time consuming but fair. Project is not that bad. Really caring, he spends lots of extra time outside of class to help students. Generous curve. Doing hw definitely helps with performance on tests. Definitely take!

I've never had a professor as bad as him. He never gave enough time for his exams and often went over material that wasn't even relevant to behavioral neuroscience. lectures were almost pointless to go to. i have to retake this class with a diff professor and its incredibly different than his lectures and much easier to understand. do not take him.
Honestly don't understand why theres so many tough reviews, class was pretty easy if you review the slideshows and go to office hours. Lots of opportunity for extra credit as well.
tests were so difficult, but were made up by the fact that if you showed up every day, you received extra credit which went into your final exam score at the end, and helped a lot.

Great professor, I understand  that the 2 hr long lecture videos were long but his class helped me get interested in research a lot more. He's passionate about his work and you can tell through his lectures in class. Attendance is not mandatory but if you do attend, you get extra credit which really boosted my grade. Neuroscience is hard ya'll!

exams barely reflect material in class, lectures in person also barely helped, only the multiple hour long online lectures would help which is difficult to keep up when you have other classes as well since you have to watch them on your own time, calls on random people in a huge lecture. if you wanna keep your gpa up do not take this class

Traditional-style math professor with neatly organized lectures and notes. Homework questions are very relevant to course contents and of appropriate difficulty (tend to be challenging but are fun to solve and really nothing crazy). Exams are proof heavy but reasonable. Would recommend taking his course!

Class was extremely small, but I've had him for courses with 40+ students. Pretty chill guy with a good sense of humor. Lectures aren't usually podcasted, but he posts (terse) notes for them. Tends to give tougher problem sets and exams than other professors. He's friendly and easy to talk to, so don't hesitate to bring questions to him.
One of my favourite lecturers so far. Really engaging and understanding and puts in a lot of effort to make sure everyone is doing the necessary things for the class.

This man's the GOAT. It was a very small class, so he went over our homework live in his office in pairs of 2 to 3 people at a time. His lectures were very organized and we were free to ask him interesting questions, and he typed up all his notes for us to see.

All the questions on midterms and finals are the kind of questions that you probably never seen in hw/ lecture notes. He is really clever in terms of combining all the concepts together in exams. Be prepared to learn a lot and really absorb the knowledge. I do go to his office hours often and he is very accessible outside of classroom.

He is very intelligent and listens to music uploaded on YouTube created by him. I love his band and the Music. The course is pretty light and I would recommend taking his course if you can. Thank you Professor Borgo, music is very interesting thanks to you!
Easy class with lecture videos and four short writing assignments making up the entire grade. Great way to fulfill the fine arts GE requirement!

Class is fully remote and attendance is based on completing lecture video quizzes (2 true or false questions per lecture). Grade is ONLY based on 'attendance' and 4 writing assignments sprinkled throughout the course. This class is extremely manageable and the concepts are genuinely super interesting. He gives extra credit for attending discussion.

Took MUS20R as to complete my DEI requirement. Amazing class! Lectures were interesting and the four writing assignments that he gave were doable. TA's were also amazing! (shout out to Daniel) If I have to take a music class in the near future I would definitely take with him. Seats do fill up quick so might as well take it when available.

His lectures were very digestible and the coursework isn't demanding. Pulled content and readings that was interesting enough that it made me explore more about the topics, studies, etc. mentioned in them outside of the class. The guidelines for writing assignments are described super well--I never had to ask for any clarification about them.

The class is 90% tests and 10% participation points that can be obtained through lectures, office hours, discussions, or IA office hours. All tests are given buffers so you can miss about 10% worth of points and still keep a 100. Final was 50 questions but max points was 40

Dr. Ernst is an amazing instructor! I would 100% recommend taking this course. It is very content heavy but Dr. Ernst makes amazing review sessions where he clearly indicates the material we should focus on for the midterm and final. Attendance is not mandatory but you still need to get participation points which is 10% of our grade.

Course was structured with 2 midterms and a final, with 10% coming from participation. Overall course was very content heavy, but the tests were very fair and reasonable. Course was fun but definitely need to put the work in for memorization.

Dr. Ernst is a fantastic professor. He sets students up for success in every way possible -- he's very clear and kind, includes review slides in every lecture, and has super straightforward exams. As long as you engage with the course material and pay attention to the concepts he emphasizes, you'll do well in his class. Would 10/10 recommend!

Professor Ernst is very organized, clear, and always starts and ends lectures on time. He uses clicker questions that closely resemble exam material. He's responsive and accessible in class, office hours, and by email. Grades are based on 2 midterms, 1 cumulative final, and participation via discussion or research presentation.

Dr. Farley is an amazing professor and person. Lectures not mandatory, EC, problem sets, 3 midterms (one dropped), and a final cumulative exam. She is great at explaining hard concepts and often goes over the previous lecture to help.

Great professor! 3 midterms and a final, all based on problem sets and iclicker questions. Great lectures! She does take a bit of time reviewing past material but I found it to be very helpful to understand the content well. Would highly recommend taking her class! Plus there are many extra credit opportunities.
🐐 Professor.  Exams are based on lecture questions and problem sets with lots of opportunities for extra credit.  She is the best professor I've had at UCSD, would recommend.

Honestly, one of my favorite professors. Her lectures are clear and easy to follow. The problem sets can be a bit long, but they're only assigned once a week and are really helpful for exam preparation.

She structures the class really nicely. Emphasizes understanding of concepts rather than memorizing, so exam questions are never asking you to explain an entire process, etc. Generous extra credits for attending sections + participating (5%). Class is 94% exam and 6% PS completion. Exams are very doable, very similar to things taught class.

Professor Goran just yaps relentlessly with no end in sight. I had him for an online class with lecture and lab back to back; he talks the entire way through the lecture and the majority of the lab session. He goes off on my tangents that sorta relate to the content but then goes nowhere.

Goran is awesome. He can be standoffish, but only because he wants to push you to think critically, connect concepts, collaborate, and communicate confidently. His raison d'être is to train young biologists to navigate a chaotic and ignorant world with courage, humility, objectivity, and aplomb. If you work hard, you'll do well -- and learn a lot.

This professor goes on too many tangents that have nothing to do with the course. He makes students feel dumb because he feels his way is the only/right way of doing things. He comes off rude oftentimes by the way he says things. The course content is easy and fun, he just makes it insufferable to the point where students dreaded going to class.

Professor Goran is an amazing orator. He keeps you occupied with the material, however be wary if you primarily use lecture to study — he will have numerous tangential moments where he starts talking about his outside endeavors. Also, be wary if you are simply trying to get a letter of recommendation: he may promise a letter, but not guaranteed.

Goran isn't the best choice if you're genuinely trying to learn. He will teach everything but the class content. Also his grading criteria is pretty unclear. There's little to no connection between lectures and labs, so you're mostly on your own. He can't be reached outside of class either. He's good for life lessons, but not bioinformatics.
His grading system stressed me out even though I ended up getting an A. I appreciate how his lectures were recorded

weird taxonomic grading structure. 2 midterms, 1 final, but you can retake midterms on the final if you do bad. tests include a lot of FRQs so  know stuff from history he talks about in lecture. boring lecturer but go since podcast is not timely. forgot to grade my midterm and messed up my final grade (but i emailed and he fixed). very caring prof

grading scheme is a little weird, but curved and is caring. very conceptual and requires some memorization. overall not bad if you put in the work and pretty rewarding as it is pretty interesting. would take again

Fairly straightforward course if you understand the grading structure. He wants everyone to do well and as long as you understand the material you will. Provided practice tests twice which really helped on midterm and final.

Forgiving grading structure which allows you to retake midterm 1&2 on the final. Lectures and engaging and good, practice problems are great practice as well. lectures are recorded. Albeit confusing grading structure it is more than fair and also weights stuff outside of exams. Nothing bad to say about Prof. Rondina.

Professor Gentry's ratings scared me initially, but I quickly learned that he wants his students to succeed. He's super clear about what material from lecture will be on the test, provides nearly identical practice midterms/finals which were official tests from previous terms, and is overall transparent with how the course is graded. Super fair!

The class was hard with 2 midterms and a cumulative final but It was worth it. You just have to memorize whats on the slides and he provides practice test, which are literally most of the questions on the test. He gives the BIGGEST, GENEROUS CURVE AT THE END, like a WHOLE GRADE Letter! also, he is a very understanding proffesor and you learn a lot!

This prof was one of the best I had, you have to try and fail the class, he's very happy and helpful. We had iclickers for lectures, mandatory discussions which were alright, not extremely helpful but good review, easy first midterm harder after that. The problem sets (homework) were difficult but thats more of the class material than him as a prof

He is honestly a really good BILD 1 professor, his exams are quite similar to the practices he provides. He is very clear in lectures, but always review on your own time. Homeworks are just problem sets and everything is based to what he sees in lecture.

Good teacher, cares about students, only need to know what is on slides, gives practice tests VERY similar to the test, do the practice tests go to class and u will do good in his class. he is very knowledgable and wants u to succeed

Honestly I dont have much against this professor, however, I found the many (not all) TAs/ tutors to be a little rude/blunt. I once submitted regrade request and a tutor just responded "No" w/ nothing more. Like a third of the class were retaking, which often meant grades would be somewhat inflated b/c they had a head start.
So far, he is the best professor I've had, and if you're struggling, go to his or the ta's office hours for a deeper understanding of the material.

Incredible professor. He cares about his students and is a fair grader, and he teaches with passion and energy. CSE 30 overall is a tough class, but he did a great job at making it enjoyable. Highly recommend Professor Muller.

Ignore the bad reviews. He gives you everything you need to do well: office hours and review sessions, etc. Lectures fast so ask questions to slow him down. Chill about life circumstances. Tough weekly homework, so start early. Hard tests/quizzes but partial credit galore. Knows a lot about the tech industry. Take his class if he teaches again!

Absolutely phenomenal professor. Sad to see him go as it's not very often you have a professor who is both at the top of their field and is so adept at explaining high level concepts in such a digestible way. Very lenient grader as well, I had performed well on the final but other parts of the class were lacking, but he gave me a fair score.

Professor Phiroz was one of my favorite professors at ucsd. His lectures are engaging and reflective of the exams. He cares a lot about his students and is willing to go above and beyond to help his students with anything they need. There is 1 hw assignment a week, 2 group case studies, and 2 exams so not a heavy course load.

Professor Phiroz was an inspiring and approachable instructor who genuinely cared about his students' success, both in class and beyond. I gained many new skills during the course and found the material truly engaging.
This is definitely one of, if not the best professor I have ever had in UCSD. He is incredibly respectful and caring. He responds to email really quickly and trie his best to accommodate students.

He cares so deeply about students, emphasizing to always reach out whenever and that he truly wants to help. Assignments and case studies tend to be lengthy, but enough time are given to do them if you start early. He wants you to succeed!!

Zal is a really great prof who cares for his students. I had it online, lectures can be dry (just the nature of the content) but he does a good job of making the zoom meeting interactive. We were put in groups for a couple assignments. Grading is clear and assignments and tests covered the exact material from lectures, no surprises.

100/10. So incredibly kind and understanding. Workload is manageable, grade consists of quizzes and final w/ mandatory readings before each lecture. Prof is so patient with the class, and is open to changing the structure based on class feedback. Law is not an easy subject but he really makes it enjoyable. Recommend!

I was extremely disappointed with the class taught by Sami Ortoleva. Assignments were poorly explained, deadlines were inconsistent, and feedback—when given—was vague and dismissive. It often felt like the instructor was unprepared or uninterested in supporting students' learning.  I would not recommend taking a class with this instructor.

He's a cool person who clearly has passion in what he teaches. He is accessible outside of class and is very kind. However, there is a clear disconnect between his lectures and tests. He required the students to use mathematical techniques that were not required for this course, but if you had Calc 3 experience, you'd scrape on by. Very tough class

I agree with some of the feedback here that the tests are VERY hard, but that is because the homework was graded on completion and the rest of the grade was just attending lecture. And they're also 24 hour take-home. So, even if you averaged a C on tests, you could still get an A. Overall, hes a cool dude and a great lecturer, would recommend

Professor Ortoleva is a very engaging and fun lecturer. I found that the daily 80 minute lectures held my attention better than most 50 minute STEM lectures at UCSD. The course was math heavy, and because I didn't have a strong math foundation, I had to study A LOT. However, if you put in the work, the course is designed so everyone can get an A.

Although Prof Ortoleva is a really nice person and attending lecture wasn't boring, I found that there was a huge disconnect between how he teaches and how he tests. I spent several hours studying each week and doing the hw but I still struggle on the weekly quizzes. He does grade on a curve though so hopefully that will help

Prof. knows her stuff but constantly updates her content alongside research- Slides were freq. unorganized or glitched- OH sessions are great for ?'s- Exams mostly fair but some ?s are tricky- EC clicker ?s in lecture- DI are mandatory w/req. readings. Busy work, but manageable- There's a NeuroTok  - Kind prof. who will reach out, but responds slow

Dr. Halpain is experienced and passionate about neuroscience
-Tries to keep class engaging
-Slides can be unclear; tech issues and Canvas mismatches were common
-Exams mostly fair but some tricky questions
-Discussions had occasional scheduling confusion & are mandatory for grade
-Includes 3 midterms, 1 final, NeuroTikTok assignment, & extra credit

Very nice person, just her slides are kinda messy,and the MTs are hard.Pick the best choice can be 3 of 4 answers sometimes and you really have to know your stuff-very detailed.3 MT and all are MC 30 Q with a Final MC too. Section is mandatory and you read articles before class and do Qs- kinda pointless not working with research like catalog says.

3 mini MTs + final. tests were hard, mainly because the q's were extremely tricky and u rly need to know ur stuff to answer them correctly. there's a lot of select all that apply q's. Doesn't release the tests so you'll need to go to the review sessions / OHs to get the questions. She's obv a neuro expert but goes off on a tangent sometimes.
studying for this final is making me lose my will to live. too much info.

Exams/Assignments were easy and the material wasn't hard, but assignment grading was poorly handled. The autograder only ran once with minimal feedback, and staff refused to re-run it even for small bugs. Many students proposed fixes, but were ignored. Several TAs also seemed unqualified. Not a bad professor, just needs to fix the assignment issue.
super super good material, great lecturer and incredibly relevant for swe industry work.

The professor does an excellent job of explaining the material and it is very organized. Get ready for a lot of projects that do take some time for you to do, but you definitely learn a lot. The theory and the practical are correlated and help understand the material very well.

Personal Experience:    
Very good lectures. Professor is very active on Piazza. 1 of the 6 assignments was tough. Midterm was easy. Final had 1 tough question out of 20+ questions. Assignments take time to complete.

Advice:    
Take CSE224 only if you can spend around 10 hours on each assignment and code reasonably well.

He cares a lot about student questions - very active on Piazza. His slides usually have most of the details, so sometimes even listening to lecture is not required. A very good course - teaches a lot of the practical details about building networked applications.

I never saw this dude the whole quarter but my TA Alessio was chill. Lab reports were kind of annoying but they drop 1 lab and 1 quiz so its alright. Anything about 90% is an A or A+, so generous cutoffs.
Physics labs suck here. Quizzes purposefully try to trick you, and you don't get feedback. You also barely get feedback on lab reports. The reports are mind-numbing and repetitive.

What even happened. Bro had good reviews and now it's really bad. Bro never shows up for the labs, and his TA's were pretty dog too. Like how do I a -1 deduction for including my raw lab data???? Make it make sense! Crib sheets are your only way of doing somewhat decent on the quizzes. And I think bro has a thing for uncertainties like holy cow.
Terrible professor and the worst three classes I took at this school were taught by him, yet he never shows up and relies on his unqualified, incompetent TA's to do the instructing.
Just wait for another quarter to take ANYONE else. You will regret it if you take this class with this professor.
She is very helpful and caring! Attendance isn't mandatory, so you can treat this course like an online class. The final consists of papers and discussions for hw, Take her!!

Super nice professor. She makes everyone feel respected and included. Really wants to hear what you think in the various papers. I only watched the recorded lectures and she makes everything really accessible for students. There was so much writing but I took this for a UD writing breadth so that's expected. Highly recommend! Very interesting.
Amazing professor! She is very passionate about the class and her lectures are very engaging. Easy to pay attention too. Listens to students allows lots of questions. Lectures are podcasted

Took her EDS 126 class for my DEI class, which was definitely the right choice. Dr. Jones is genuinely one of the most sweet and caring professors I've had and she's very passionate about the subject, which made me appreciate the class even more. The TA's were also great and we had about 6 assignments in total that were all easy for the most part.

I'm honestly so glad I took her class, I felt so invested in learning about school system and it helped me learn about why I was educated the way I was. Dr Jones is so amazing and her lectures are very engaging.

This professor is kind, caring, and heartwarming—I have so much respect for him. His instructions are clear, his teaching is easy to follow, and his grading is VERY FAIR and lenient. If he's your instructor, you'll fall in love with Linear Algebra! The TAs are also extremely helpful. GOATED TEACHING TEAM, I LOVE PROF PATRICK!

honestly best math prof here. very clear lectures though on chalkboard, explained concepts well, practice tests similar to exams, unlimited hw attempts. doesn't podcast but posts his notes. use the textbook and do extra practice. those saying he was a bad lecturer haven't met some of the other math profs or don't want to do the work to succeed
