Although this course is supposed to be hard, this professor made the class easier giving exact formats of how to study for midterms and the finals! Lectures weren't recorded but notes were posted on canvas. I would recommend this professor as I took him for Math10a as well.

I mean like a majority of people I talked to agreed he was pretty good. Pretty straightforward too. This class is a hard class though because it's basically introducing new concepts that you never learned in precalc.
He's honestly pretty good and his lectures are too. You can tell he puts in a lot of effort into teaching and he actually tries to teach well. Would definitely take again.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS!! He does not record lectures, so in a way, attendance is required to obtain lecture material. His exams were incredibly hard and unjustifiably long! He had baited my class with "pop quizzes" as a motivator to boost lecture attendance (beyond diabolical for that). This man hurt both my academic transcript and ego...

Told everyone who didn't make perfect marks on curved arrow diagrams on the first midterm to drop out of college. Not only would he go on random tangents about material we didn't need, he was so demoralizing I quit trying (even though I made an A on exam 1) and just aimed to pass because he was so miserable I couldn't make myself go to lecture.

You have to put a lot of effort for this class. Topics aren't explained super clearly, and a lot of material that I found helpful was covered outside of lectures especially during office hours/help sessions. Go to those and you should be ok. He rambles a lot during lecture. No HW, but definitely study in your own time.

This class is undoubtedly hard- but that goes for all OChem classes. Prof. Oconnor has very tough exams, and you should work the optional hw problems and go to optional section to maximize your learning. His lectures are the most important study material (he is also quite funny). Accepts plenty of questions during lecture so make sure to ask.

ATROCIOUS class. I got a 95% in 40A, the midterm avg was 37%; the final avg was 50% bc it was online and not proctored (you can connect the dots). Reads off the ppt slides and uses jargon that makes lectures so confusing, there's no point in attending. His advice was 'just know the chemistry.' Ruined my love of ochem, made me regret choosing UCSD.

Professor Alexandrov made BENG 100 a great learning experience. His lectures were clear and engaging, and he always took time to answer questions thoroughly. The weekly notes and practice exams were super helpful for understanding the material. He really cares about his students and creates a welcoming, supportive environment.
That professor was really great! Even though the class was quite theoretical, he had a way of explaining things that made it all clear and relevant for our exams.
This professor is very kind and considerate. He explain all the concepts very well.
Very nice and open to all kinds of questions. Very concerned about students.
Amazing professor. For such a theoretical class, he was able to successfully break things down and teach us what mattered for exams.

Prof.Marechal is very knowledge and passionate. She takes time to answer our questions and provide resources to explore further if we're interested. She encouraged students to discuss our thoughts beyond lecturing us. (her lecture is phenomenal by the way) Therefore, her class was fun, engaging, and full of great discovery.

Patricia Marechal is one of the smartest people I have had the pleasure of being a student for. If you just look her up you'll see her CV is 13 pages and she has been invited to speak all around the world. She has her PhD from Harvard. She is so intelligible in creating philosophical scenarios and blowing your mind. I would only take her if i could

Good lecturer, very knowledgeable. Attendance was not mandatory, but I say you should 100% go to understand the readings. Philosophy texts are not easy to understand but Professor Marechal explains it all in lecture which helps a lot to prepare for the midterm and final exam. The exams are mixture of multiple choice, matching, and writing.
Really kind and passionate professor. Class was pretty easy and required very little work outside of class, just a discussion post every week. Would recommend for an easy A and a fun time!

The professor does a lot to prepare students for the midterm and final with practice questions completed in class. There's also weekly online discussions that are pretty straightforward, so those definitely help to balance out the grade. Otherwise, Professor Marechal is great at teaching her subject and cares about students.

Professor Wildonger is super kind and caring, this is molecular biology so you have to study hard and put in work! HW is doable and not hard, she gives extra credit! But for exams and final you really have to study hard!!

Dr. Wildonger had good lectures, fair exams, and extra credit opportunities. Despite being ambiguous with grading criteria at times, she is fair to students—often dropping questions most students miss. She's a kind and caring professor who generally answers every question thoroughly and to the best of her ability during and outside of class.

Grade is based on 7 weekly problem sets (2% each), 2 midterms (30% each), discussion attendance (6%), final (20%), 2 extra credit opportunities (2% each).
Despite some ambiguity in responses, the professor is kind and truly wants us to succeed. The exams are similar to the psets and TA's review sessions (def watch them as they are really helpful!!)

She made me feel like a kid again excited to go to my first science class. She's a lovely person, good lectures and slides, and fair exams. Lots of EC opportunities and gives credit for completion and attendance to balance out the exams if you don't do well on one. Go to her if you need help, she makes every student feel valued and special.

Prof. Wildonger just eminates PTA mom to me. She's just so nice, but her lectures can be super dense. Everything she talked about in lecture coul be shortened significantly. Her homework is based on completion and extra credit is given out.
There were like 3 assignments are 2 quizzes the entire quarter. He cancelled the final. Attendance code given during lectures so just show up and you'll be fine. Truly one of the greats.

I dealt with a lot this quarter, but he was very sweet and accommodating. Attendance is mandatory and a part of your grade, but it is fair, considering we had little homework and few exams, which were open-note and fairly simple. His slideshows were entertaining and great visual examples of what he was teaching

He is a great professor, only graded by a few things  that are the same every week: Discussion post, Weekly quiz (with three attempts), small writing opinion in class, and reply to discussion post. The class has only one midterm and one final. The final and midterm are only worth 15%, while the weekly quizzes are worth like 21%. Easy class for an A

Phil 35: He is not a good lecturer (goes on rants and isn't concise), lecture participation is mandatory and there's extra credit for additional discussion posts. There are 2-4 readings (25+ pages) each week, the midterm guidelines are similar to the final (1 midterm/final), and there are multiple choice quizzes each week.

Took phil 181 with him. Lectures were really nice in the beginning but as the course went on I only went once a week. I think it was more the material i didn't care much for. in class assignment once a week, discussion post every week and quiz. But he gave a pdf of quiz on canvas and that helped me get through the readings. Lectures not recorded.

This is my 2nd time taking Professor Tolley  He's very nice and talks about a lot of interesting topics in class and plays cool songs Everything is very doable if you pay attention in lecture and do the readings :)

Weekly tests that are take home and due by friday and one final paper.  Lectures are extremely interesting and engaging.  Tolley is really open to what students have to say and, in a way, he allows the students to lead the discussion.

Easy class, that only meets up 1 time a week. Also, every week you will have a mini quiz which is about the movie watched in class; very easy quiz and does not require much thought process. Also, the final was a bit hard, but as long as you show up to class, you can get an A. Also, the movies we watch in class are very thought provoking.

Three hour lecture once per week including a short lecture and full length movie screening. Usually there's quizzes at the start of class based on readings/movies you watch before going. Midterm and final consist of short answer questions and essays. Class is easy as long as you go to lectures and do required readings/movie screenings.

Professor was very passionate about the topic. It was a pretty easy class, started off with a short quiz (5 written questions) based on previous lecture. Went into lecture regarding the director, specific themes, and culture that were going to be in the movie of that day. As long as you go to class, pay attention, & do readings you should do well.

The class is about Middle Eastern women on film and it's one of the best classes I've taken! We were dealing with a really difficult topic & she handled it really well, and the movie selections were interesting throughout the quarter. Weekly quizzes based on assigned movie, 2 midterm short papers, a final paper, attendance + participation points.

Do Not take this class with her. she is not a good professor at all. she will confuse you in class and although she seems fair she will not be fair on your exams and grades. overall a very bad experience. should not be teaching at a 4 year university.
Bo is a very caring and nice guy. Definitely take his class.
Really kind but is not very engaging in lectures. Attendance is not mandatory. Class is fairly easy.
Easy professor. Clear lectures and pretty good lecture notes.

He is the best math prof I ever meet in UCSD. His lecture is very clear and his notes on the blackboard are really helpful. I always go to his office hour, and Bo is very nice and friendly. He likes to answer your questions and give you objective feedback. I would like to take his other classes for sure. BEST PROF IN MATH DEPARTMENT!

I like this professor. His class is not very hard and his lectures explain things well. The only difficulty is that he does not allow any cheatsheet or notecards during the tests. But in terms of MATH 18, I believe it's not difficult to get a good grade even without a notecard since the materials are way easier than other math classes.

Claus' class was wonderful. The class became much more difficult at the midterm, which is good to be ready for. It's clear that he truly cares about students and their learning. I hope he teaches more undergraduate courses in the future. Definitely take him if you can.
Excellent lecture quality.

Dr. Sorensen is great. He gives very organized, well-paced and detailed lectures. It is important to closely follow everything he writes because of how precisely he structures it. He does not always present conceptual interpretations though. He typed his own notes for the course which are as good as any textbook. He's also a really nice dude.

Excellent professor for algebra. Lectures are well-organized and useful. HW is tough, but TAs/prof office hours give lots of hints/details. Exams are fair if you study lectures and HW problems (recommended ones too).

Although he is a nice professor, I would not recommend his class. He is a really smart guy and he has a very high expectation of his students so he doesn't explain his examples because they are "obvious" to him. Definitely go to discussions if you want to pass. I did not learn anything from the professor, or from the textbook that he wrote.

The class lecture can be a bit boring, but they do provide you with all the information and knowledge you need to know for the midterm and final writing, and the lecture recordings are online as well. Professor Rose does explained the artwork in his lecture with many details and historical background, its better for you to take notes.

Cool professor, passionate about art history. Lecture is not required but section is. Only 2 assignments which are essays during midterms and final. One  week to complete them. TA's will help you with them if needed!

Two papers, one midterm and one final that make up your entire grade in the class. Lectures are a snoozefest, don't bother going. Discussions are mandatory, but other than that really easy class and no work at all.

Definitely an easy A, or even A+ if you go to all the discussions and finish two essays. TA will guide you for the essays, in my mind they are helpful enough for your essay so I seldomly go to lectures. Phones or devices are not allowed during lecture but the professor is passionate about art history and lectures well.

Your grade is based on attendance to discussions and two papers. Papers are easy and as long as you understand the paintings you are analyzing you will be fine. Average on both papers was about a 94 so as long as you put in some effort you will get an A. Lectures are boring but somewhat informative but overall take this class for an easy A.
As a full time working professional, I appreciate how organized the course was. Multiple reminders that I received throughout the week were helpful too. Fast responses were an added plus!

Spent a lot of time on this class. Grading felt arbitrary & nitpicky. Points deducted without feedback, making it hard to learn. When I asked for clarification, I was met with more questions instead of answers, which felt unhelpful. I didn't feel supported in understanding the material or improving.
Instructor's positive encouragement really makes the course engaging and enjoyable.

Professor Ahuja is an exceptional master teacher. Her in-depth knowledge is excellent. She effectively communicated complex anatomical physiological concepts so they are easily understood and presented the course material in engaging, creative ways. Her ability to incorporate real-life examples and case studies was fantastic. She's an inspiration.
I enjoyed the enthusiasm that she has for teaching. I did well in the class. I usually repeat science classes, but this time, it will be only once, thanks to the professor.

A great professor whose passion for the subject really comes through in his lectures. Projects and exams are tough so you really have to put in the work, but it is extremely rewarding when you come out the other side.

One of the best classes I have had at UCSD! The lectures are joyful, an experience in their own right. Professor Snoeren wonderfully highlights the key systems concepts in the papers, enabling a deep understanding of the topic. The class requires a lot of effort, but its definitely worth it. You come out of this class as a different person.
Took this course last year. Hard course and time-consuming PAs. Prof. Snoeren cares a lot for students' learning and holds amazing lectures

4 projects due over the quarter, 2 big ones and 2 small ones. You code a router packaging TCP packets, congestion control and then router topology forwarding IP and ICMP packets. 2 midterms and 1 final. class is taught an engaging way tho there's a lot of content covered. have to make sure you don't fall off

Professor Devereux is an easy-going and fun professor. I enjoyed his class on Medieval Spanish history and would love to take any of his future courses. There are 2 essays (a short and a longer essay), discussions, and a written final (blue book). He is thought-provoking and would recommend any student to take him as their professor.

Professor Hanna is an incredible professor. He always offers nuanced arguments that make his students think about the world of the people living through the English, American, French, Haitian revolutions, and Latin American independence movements. You have 4 short papers, a midterm, and a final. Take any of his classes because you will learn a lot.

Prof. Hanna is such a great lecturer, and everything you need to know about this class can come from lectures. He can make even the most random people in history interesting. Homework is just 4 short papers (usually 1-3 pages each). Exams are extremely fair and easy as long as you took good notes during the lecture. Trust me take one of his classes
Goated professor. He's really funny and knows so much about pirates the papers weren't too hard but they happened very often.

His lectures are really well organized and entertaining. The classes "text book" was his own book which he provided for free on canvas. He did not choose to use his own book because he was writing the book when he was creating the class. He is also very easy to talk to and is OSD friendly. Alot of 2-3 writing assignments. did about 20 pages total.

Lectures were very interesting and I learned more from them than I did in his textbook. Lects. give context for papers. Papers have unclear grading criteria but prompts are very open-ended which gives you some freedom. TAs grade all papers so go see them for help during office hours. Make your life easier and choose primary sources w/ translations

He is a fantastic and knowledgeable professor. Even though I had class with him at 8 a.m., he made the lectures entertaining and interesting. In the lab sections, when presenting my robot, he listened first and then offered helpful feedback. MAE 3 is a brutal class with too much homework. Thus, if you want to succeed, take Delson as your professor.

Professor Delson is very kind and brings us a lot of energy and enthusiasm at 8 am. He is a good professor that explained the physics concepts well. It is just the class that is so time-consuming, frustrating, and makes you feel hopeless.

I got an A+ on both midterms (class avg. ~60%). The final comes around and I get a 5%. The class average was 15%. This was due to a HORRIBLE grading scale. Almost no partial credit if you got the final answer wrong. The final exam was also much harder than the midterms. With his curve (since 95% of class had a raw F), he failed half the class. HALF
Certified Chiller, too much work outside class.

Lectures seemed unorganized, with a lot of slide reading. Lots of HW, but full credit is available after corrections. Midterms and final were the worst part of this course; partial credit was either sparse or non-existent, and the final was quite a bit harder than the practice finals, resulting in abysmal final grades. (class average was a 35%)

Lecture notes are insightful (even better than the book at times). Sadly, HW is graded and due weekly (textbk problems). I learned a lot from this class, but the dense midterms/final admittedly added unnecessary stress. Otherwise, prof. is easily accessible, helpful, and quite understanding, I think. Great class for math majors.

I'm sure he tried his best considering Differential Equations are somewhat difficult. Will trail off sometimes and stare at the board when working through lecture problems. Midterms and the final felt tedious, but he was super generous with curving and grading scale for this class. Hopefully, he can improve himself for the future.

Not great at lecturing, just kinda lists out theory without much explanation so it's hard to follow along. Will get confused, stare at the board for a minute, then correct his mistakes often. First midterm was really easy, second was very hard. Homework is really short and easy. Doesn't podcast and his lecture notes are also hard to follow along.

Would not take again, acted incredibly full of himself. He made comments about how students who didn't attend lecture clearly didn't care about their schooling, even though lectures weren't mandatory. He also took down lecture recordings the next day, which made it hard to review before essays. Attendance should have just been mandatory.
Just like any HUM class it is reading heavy. He makes the material actually interesting tho. For a HUM prof he is not even bad.

His lectures were profound. Very consistent in terms of grading which depends on which TA you have. There are daily short answers 2-3x a week (20 per quarter) but they are relatively easy as long as you come to class. Very easy to get an A as his grading system is really straightforward as a 100-point class. Attendance mandatory and very worth it.

very engaging lectures, graded by in lecture daily short answers (pretty easy so a nice grade boost), 2 essays, and in class writings, which are also lenient in grading. Hes very fun in lectures and has good humor, good at summarizing themes and giving head starts/explanations for essay prompts

Amazing professor! For context for the review below, he gave zeros for plagiarism and cheating. I think it is pretty "rational" to deny credit for work you didn't do. Lectures are well-structured and engaging. Super open to feedback. Always provided nuanced and thoughtful reflections on readings and their application to life.
He definitely had some issues during his childhood; otherwise, there would be no reason to surprise students with his passive-aggressive attitude.

Honestly, I didn't attend the lectures during the second half but managed to pass. Didn't really talk to the professor but he wasn't that arrogant. I got TA Andrina & she was the best! She made her sections as half zoom class and some outside going on exhibits. If you get the chance, get her!! (was able to give extra credit; so i was able to pass)

I'll be honest, I didn't go to many lectures and was still successful in the class. He set it up so everything is very accessible online, and the projects, exams, and assignments were very clear in what was expected. The material was also very interesting, and you can tell he enjoys teaching. Idk what he's like as a person but class was v organized

Professor Serlin's lectures are not the MOST engaging but it does help. Reading does help a lot with the assignments. The grading for the midterm was honestly confusing.

He seemed cheerful, and I did not experience any rudeness or passive aggressiveness from him. TA Alexis is great, and you have the chance to have her, pls do so!
he definitely deletes reviews and makes his own reviews. Do not trust the good reviews . Stay as far away from him .

Professor Simpson is a great lecturer and a very kind, approachable person in and outside the classroom. It is made clear what exactly is needed to succeed in this course and the resources are provided abundantly. Focus on lectures and on memorizing pretty much everything that is presented on them, nothing out of the ordinary for a biochem class.

Disengaging lecture style combined with frequent digressions from core material, made the class unbearably tedious. There's a clear lack of coordination between the TAs and the professor; midterms were graded using inconsistent rubrics and criteria. Final curve was reasonable but doesn't justify the professor's disinterest in teaching. Would avoid.

The professor was so difficult to understand during the lecture, I felt as if the TAs would have done a better job at teaching and allow us to fully grasp the material. The professor at best just reads off his slides and half the time does not even want to be teaching. He also says he doesn't judge but also judges us when we get iclicker ? wrong.

Professor did not even teach well and it is honestly a waste of time to go to class because he just reads everything off the slides. However, he makes students go to class by doing iclicker questions which is where you are graded on accuracy instead of just counting it as participate even if you get the question which is where the learning begins.

Prof is a very well respected researcher who knows his stuff. There's a lot to memorize but if you stay on top of it it's doable. Managed a B with 4 UD biochem classes including 2 labs, but if you can dedicate more time to this class you'll do just fine. Textbook is more cohesive and better for providing context than lectures

Really digestible and interesting lectures. Wixted's eyewitness memory research is really fascinating. Pretty test heavy, but I personally prefer that. The readings are dense, but only account for ~20% of test questions so you aren't penalized as much for not recalling it as well. Generous curve, too. Overall, one of my fav PSYC classes at UCSD!

You're graded on 3 tests and that's it, no assignments, small amounts of extra credit and if you want to get an A it will be pretty difficult as you will have to read the long long chapters from the reading. He did curve a fat percentage at the end of the class. I will not lie he is a pretty good professor but has hard tests, expect a C or a B.

For PSYC 162 & 144. Wixted is a brilliant researcher but not a great lecturer; he went off on a lot of tangents which made class interesting but did not help in time for exams. This is especially bad because your grade is fully exam based. Tons of reading & you're forced to get the textbook. Exams were also not always reflective of what we learnt.

For 144 &162. He's a great professor! He gives interesting lectures that have a lot of examples that are great for our understanding of the material. He's very helpful with our questions and nice. Our grade is entirely exams, usually 3 in total, but as long as you actually attend class/ pay attention and do a bit of studying you'll do just fine!

Wixted is a kind professor with repetitive teaching. For 10 weeks, he would always say the same thing: Eye witness memory is reliable on the first test. Be sure to remember that! The exams had many trick questions/answers. It was so frustrating since our grade is only based on exams. Also, be sure to read the textbook we're forced to get!

COGS 1 is primarily about understanding Cognitive Science, so there are different guest speakers for each lecture. This professor grades on section attendance, weekly quizzes,  midterms, and a final from the lecture and assigned readings. So the professor himself never really teaches, but you have to understand the content presented.
basically guest speakers and readings. weekly quizzes on canvas. quizzes, midterms, final are all open note

Seminar was kind of boring, but it was a super easy class. We just had to show up and maybe had two assignments the whole quarter. He was pretty nice, but I kind of got the vibe that he wasn't really religious when talking about religion. I'm not completely sure about that, but if you're taking his class do with that information what you will.

I love this professor as a person, but not a good teacher. Goes on long and confusing discussions about the material. Another main issue is the audio podcasts instead of video podcasts, which were desperately needed! Wording in lecture slides is also hard to follow. Rough overall course

Passionate professor who goes on a lot of rants and says things aren't on the midterm, but they are. It's hard to reach through email, his slides are repetitive & don't help. 2 sets of reading questions a week. Doesn't curve the class, but if you're really on top of your readings, you should be fine. But still wouldn't recommend the class.

Professor Romero was really generous when it came to curves and extra credit opportunities. He was always available to have one-on-one meetings which were really helpful. I also liked his lectures a lot since he would go through real world applications of what we were learning and the group project was also insightful in that same way.

If you are taking this class to learn and challenge yourself, this class is for you. Lectures are mainly focused on reactions, but looks a lot into each functional groups chemical properties. He helps set up good foundations and leave the students to learn through their own actions. Had an interesting approach to curving, C = 48%, B= 68% & A=84%.
He is a very nice and friendly guy and is very open to questions. However, the tests are very hard but he curved to a B where like 60% was a B-.

Professor Romero takes a bottom up approach to understanding reactivity. He forces you to think critically about chemistry. He cares about his students, knowing many of them by name. The tests are very difficult with averages lying around 45% for the midterms and 65% for the final. SmartWrk is an unhelpful tool. He curved the average grade to a B.

very low averages. praying for a curve. failed all his exams. maybe its a me issue but the class is very hard. no answer keys for discussion worksheets which are used in the test. this class made me depressed chat im so cooked help me

final 50% of grade and you have to write out code not just mc. quiz and lab due every week. lab can be done in discussion (optional) or by yourself. stata (week 2-4) is easier than r (week 6-10). midterm week 5 only on stata. very accessible in office hours and good at explaining code in lecture. a bit of a boring lecturer but he clearly cares
Arnold is definetly one of the best professor I've ever had in UCSD. He gave us enough materials for self-study. His also very generous in giving grade
Requires you to memorize an insane amount of code. Final is worth 50% of your grade and actually makes you write out code. No meaningful extra credit.
Make tricky exam and let his graduate student teach the class who barely knows teaching
Curves like crazy. The material can be difficult depending on how your brain works but curves the overall grade heavy and makes it easy to get help.

This professor just gives everyone an A+. He loves telling students to use chatGPT and doesn't care if they learn anything. Those who really want to learn and want our grades to mean something get screwed because he makes it look like we're the same as students who are flunking the rest of the program. This professor is undeserving of presitge.

Yi-Zhuang You is a phenomenal professor and he gets really excited talking about the subjects in class, which makes me excited to learn. I greatly enjoyed this course. He showed a new perspective on quantum for me and made me appreciate its beauty!

if youre considering taking this class dont even think about it.. just do it. prof you is amazing. experience some of the clearest and most informative lectures you will ever have delivered by a seemingly genius dude.
Dude's wicked smart

Exciting, engaging, informative, overall one of the best professors I have had! Prof. You is clearly a master of quantum mechanics and his quantum information approach to the subject was very refreshing and clear. Numerous classmates expressed an interest in the professor's field while taking the course.

very nice professor. He made jokes during lecture that were funny and added to the enjoyment. Class isn't mandartory but highly reccomend or you'll fall behind. Exams were closed note so memorize how to solve the problems! Weekly HW assignments on canvas open note and weekly review session hosted by the TA
Really awesome professor and chill, fun class!! :)

Super nice professor, great lectures but very difficult to apply the content at times. If you do bad on the 5 assignments, it's hard to make it up on the tests since they're weighted heavily for the midterm (35%) and final (50%). Don't expect this to just be an easy course to fulfil a math gen ed. Doable but study and go to review sessions.

Definitely not a class you should take if you struggle with keeping with with live lectures or with test-taking. Class builds off itself and is very detail oriented. Take your time with the assignments. Curve was really forgiving. Would take P/NP

Prof. Kehler is a good teacher and you can tell he enjoys the company of his students. Lectures aren't mandatory and there's no discussion. He also podcasts his class and has it via Zoom. The assignments are worth 15 percent but they do add up in the long run, both final and midterms (2 midterms) are in-person. Just STUDY!! he also curves the class

Sean is the best lecturer, super intellectual, has a great sense of humor, and is easy to approach. In this course, you will learn beyond just AI and Programming—a life-changing experience. However, don't expect to gpt through the course for that "easy A", this is the course that reminds me of the joy of learning and why I'm here in college.

Sean is a tremendous lecturer. He is great at chalkboard lectures where he seems to be trying to coax or persuade the class of a concept using math "for your amusement only'. Sean is not concerned with assignments or using tests to gauge performance instead he appeals to your desire to learn. I can only assume he cares a great deal.

150B is an excellent class for people who want to take their first step into the world of AI. Furthermore, Professor Gao made the lectures intriguing enough for those at any skill level. It's not the easiest, but all the efforts will pay off. It's worth mentioning that he responds to questions quickly and clearly, and his OHs are worth the visit.
BEST CSE PROFESSORS! THE GOAT!

One of the best classes! Professor Gao makes sure that students really understand the subject. Working through his thoughtfully setup assignments really helps with the finals (which is fun and also challenging to the perfect amount). Professor really cares about his students and is extremely witty - you feel smarter just being in his presence.

Good professor, class just has a really heavy workload with 2 4 hr labs+2 postlabs due every week+final report+exams. He can be unclear about extensions(sometimes giving them the day something was due which was really bothersome) but your grade for labs is dependent on the TAs not him. The exams are just based off his lecture slides.

Professor Mrse is a really cool guy who cares about the students. This class just totally sucks. The workload (even for a 6 unit class) is immense.

Postlab papers due every day, written prelab due every day, midterm, final, AND a formal lab report (roughly 15-30 pages). Truly an unbelievable amount of work.

I LOVE MY PROF!!! Most kind, sweet, loving and caring prof ever!!! As a person, he is just perfect. So sweet!!! He cares a lot for his students and never fails to brighten my day! The class as a whole is not hard, the final is online and the curves are huge! You could never fail this class just give it a little effort! i literally love him

He is a cool professor, he genuinely cares about students. Will often move HW deadline to accommodate students. Class will be curved. 1/3 quizzes gets dropped. Quizzes are reflective of lectures, but you MUST understand the content and study in order to pass the quiz. One downfall, he lectures extremely fast and cannot keep up with note-taking.

He tells you what will be on the quizzes, and is funny and caring. You need to have a good grasp on the material though, quizzes are all short answer. He will curve the class, and is going to make our final online bc people are struggling. My biggest criticism is how fast paced he is, he goes through over 100 slides in two days.

Scott is THE BEST professor I had so far. He really cares about student and worked so hard to make everyone understand the material. Super generous on the exams, so many extra credits, and his lectures are clear in explaining concepts. Also really want his students to become a virologist haha

One of the greats. Only 4 exams in the class, one of which is dropped. Practice exams are incredibly similar to the actual exams, almost down to the word. Very very clear on what will be on the exams. Weekly homework is just free points. I don't think he's teaching bicd100 again but if he is take him.

He was one of the best professors I ever had at UCSD. He gives so many extra credits and opportunities to boost your grade. There are 4 midterms and lowest one will be dropped. Midterms are similar to practice exams. He is so nice and caring.

one of the nicest and most caring professors i've ever had at ucsd, his practice exams are very representative of the real thing, offers so much extra credit and drops the 2 lowest hws, definitely take him!!

Such an iconic professor! He always listened to students' feedback to improve his teaching. Sometimes rushed topics, but overall did amazing at lecturing! Very forgiving course grading systems. Created such a warm class environment and even his TA's were amazing. Exams were pretty representative. Great upper div introduction. Take him if you can!
Horrible teacher. Sure, this class is an easy B+/A- if you want that. But she comes off as aggressive. Refuses to listen to reasoning. 164 based off quizzes in which she gives the worst slides for.

Quizzes are very difficult and not very reflective of the lectures. Group homework and group projects are a significant portion of your grade. Kind and understanding of extenuating circumstances. Fun lecture videos and extra credit opportunities

BIEB 164: quizzes are ridiculous. Even if you watch the lectures 5 times over it wouldn't be sufficient to get a good score on the quizzes. Having 0 students get full points on a quiz in a class of 200+ is not reflective of the students' performances, it is due to insufficient teaching and unfair questions. Really hope she addresses these concerns.

(DO NOT TAKE) I took her BIEB 164 class and was disappointed as the material tested on the quizzes is not reflective of the class. In addition the lectures are poorly organized as material on the slides doesn't encompass needed information for testing. She also doesn't use books so your only frame of reference is the poorly composed slide decks.
do not sign up for her class, you will regret it. not an 'easy A.' the amount of questions on quizzes in the allotted time is unrealistic

Worst professor I've had throughout my entire 4 years in college. It's true that your grade is based off how much she likes you. This class felt like it was more about making what caters to her interests rather than producing independent works showcasing individual creative processes. Tbf I knew what to expect after reading the other reviews.

I was hesitant to take this course since I've read all the terrible reviews about her, but I need it to graduate. Yeah. It's true. She really is probably the worst "professor" at UCSD. I really don't know how she even became a "professor" at this school. She's very condescending and rolls her eyes quite a lot. She always looks kinda out of it too.

Took VIS70N for Fall 2021 and it was by far the worst class I've ever taken. It was an absolute mess from start to finish, I felt like the syllabus never carried any weight. We had a book required, but no one ever read it. We had a final exam but that was canceled. Felt like the syllabus was changing every week. It was a waste of everyone's time.

Her 3 hour lectures are excessively long and boring, all the meanwhile degrading your work. She never updates grades until the very end. She seems very unorganized overall and carries a very specific viewpoint towards film. She expresses many of her dislikes about some of the filmmakers that the majority of the audience love.

Pass the class with a solid B. she is the worst professor at UCSD and does not prepare for each lecture. Her lecture is not organized at all. She reads the book for half hour, when I ask questions during her lecture, she only responded with one sentence without any clear definition. I feel this 6 units course like a 2 units course. She is a mess.

Prof Smith is really sweet and wants everyone to succeed. She talks a bit fast, and there's a lot of content, but the class is very manageable if you set time aside to study. Discussions/OH are extra credit,  and there's no homework. Weekly quizzes (open-note) and the midterm/final (closed-note) were online. She gives a lot of extra credit!

Dr. Smith was super caring and accessible outside of class, her lectures made so much sense and she was always willing to answer questions, I 100% recommend her, I took her class spring 2025 and it was the best choice ever, physio is very difficult so still expect to study a lot in ur own time, her exams were tough but online.

Took Professor Smith in the spring 2024 and was nervous because it was her first time teaching but it ended up being a great class. The midterm and final were all MC which made things a lot easier. However, it is a BIPN class so don't expect to not study!
Grading is lenient and had a lot of extra credit opportunities. We often ended lectures early and her tests are pretty fair.
She is honestly okay. She doesn't explain things clearly, but she isn't difficult and the exams are easy in my opinion. Very inaccessible outside of class.

She's very blunt and lenient. If an extension request needed, she would give to you. The course overall has a few major essays and extra credit opportunities. Attendance is based whether you complete the daily quizzes or based on the group projects/assignments (presentations). May excuse an absence once used your one time pass.

Slightly annoying millennial, kinda boring class. Treated this course like a crazy complex upper div topic (incredibly easy, high school like material), waste of our time (respectfully), has these awful in-class group exercises that SHE KNEW no one participated in but continued to assign them and would act SURPRISED when no one participated.

Great professor. She is very blunt, which I enjoyed. Reading is required as you take 1-question quizzes based on the reading for participation every lecture. Lots of engaging with your classmates, too. She was very lenient on hw extensions.

Grush is an amazing prof! I chose to watch his lectures through YouTube and it was easy to follow along! 6 quizzes & a final. Chapters 3-5 were harder for me. I failed the first quiz but did good on the rest! My TA was very helpful, going to discussions is EC and helps a lot! Just pay attention to lectures and do lots of practice problems!

PHIL10 with Professor Grush is pretty straightforward. The textbook, lectures, and YouTube videos provide great resources to learn the material. With plenty of practice problems and helpful TAs, it's easy to do well if you stay on top of the frequent quizzes. unstuck study is a handy study tool to supplement the course resources.

As a non-philosophy major, this class was really straightforward and easy to follow. The textbook is the same as the lectures/videos, but I'd still recommend buying it because it helps to do practice problems on paper. Lots of quizzes, but plenty of practice material & help is available. Definitely go with Grush if you need PHIL10, great professor.

I used his youtube, lectures and textbook as resources and i averaged a solid 88 on all the quizzes. The only way i can explain this class is like math without numbers, and its not horribly difficult. The more practice you do the better. Sometimes i did find it pretty fun. Grush is pretty chill, very nonchalant. There is so much help available!

the textbook is helpful for examples and all of the lectures are posted on youtube, which i would recommend watching more than going to class because he is very fast paced. don't fall behind because quizzes are VERY frequent. the final sections replace quiz grades so not getting a good grade is your fault tbh (it was mine). rick is cool too
Just avoid her please I beg you all

It's a hard class at first. I recommend going to the workshops for the class instead of discussion. You definitely need to review and summarize each lecture to save some trouble. It's overwhelming at first and the way she lectures is at lightning speed. But overall it's manageable in the end. I just think she gets wordy in her explanations.

Professor Lam is a solid lecturer. During lecture, she moves at a great pace. Yes lectures can be complicated, but that's just because chemistry is a complicated subject (which she makes known at the beginning of the quarter). For exams, she gives you one side of a half-sheet of paper, so learn how to write small.

I honestly struggled so much even with the first midterm. I had to watch other professors past quarter lectures because it was extremely difficult to stay ahead with Prof Lam's lectures. Though there are many practice problems given, I just dont think it was helpful especially since she moves very fast on lectures.

Professor Lam is hard to understand, gives boring and confusing lectures. She allows half a piece of paper, single sided as a cheat sheet. I taught myself the material from this class online because her lectures are useless and she is very unclear. Study hard for her tests and you will pass but she makes the whole process unnecessarily difficult.
I loved the class, he was really insightful and he knows what's up with his field. I recommend he is a great lecturer, and has passion about sharing his knowledge. Amazing!

Easily the worst professor I've ever had. Disorganized, poor lecturer, and wrote a book about basically himself named "Mayan Mars", with part of the abstract reading "Gustavo [] escapes into his teaching and aerospace research and obsessively surfs the La Jolla waves on his time off. An affair with a sexy young student..."

Really??

Professor doesnt lecture very well and puts a lot of emphasis on derivations while making elementary math errors. Exams were based off of a pool of questions with one each of each includiing a derivation, a conceptual question, a book example,and a homework problem. Is funny on ocassion but horrible lecturer overall obbious researcher not teach

Class was full of very disorganized, unstructured lectures, and challenging exams. 4 questions for 4-5 chapters, overall exams are 75% of grade. TA helped a bit and was cool, but we got lucky with her. Otherwise this class is purely self-study, and you learn no practical knowledge. It's basically a chem review class. Very disappointing.

Knowledgeable professor, but terrible job at teaching/communicating the material.  Class was easy enough, but I got very little out of it.  Needs to work on applicability of material, and not just spend the entire class deriving an equation.  Sure, he makes a funny joke or two, but this was honestly one of the worst classes I've taken.

He should try to learn how to write neatly, his handwriting is bad and I could not decipher the words during lecture while sitting in front of the classroom + glasses. Another thing is that he is stingy and won't upload lecture notes or recordings while other 20C teachers do both. So I would recommend studying on your own and don't rely on him.

Hand writing isn't legible. Confuses himself during lectures often. He lectures way too fast to comprehend or make note of the material taught. Refuses to upload lectures on time whereas the other 20C professors do. Shakeel makes what should have been the easiest class in the Math 20 series into the hardest class in the series.

Do not take this professor unless you want to lower your gpa. It's not worth your time going to lecture because his notes/handwriting are incoherent, and he stopped recording and posting lecture notes halfway through the course. I ended up having to learn the material on my own and the resources don't really prepare you for the tests.
Same tests and finals as the other profs. I wish I could understand his lectures tho. And notes. Notes look like something id find inside the pyramids. Ancient hieroglyphics.
Cant understand him. Ended up going to another professor to learn the material. Midterms and finals were the same, so it did not matter.

There's a lot of negative reviews and I really don't get it. Yeh a caring professor and the workload was extremely manageable. I'd do the readings two hours before lecture and I was fine. The grading is generous. A lot of the bad reviews are saying "reading is hard" or "attendance" but if you can't handle that you're cooked in every other class.

She seems very passionate about the subject, but she made it really difficult to enjoy it. No slides, no recorded lecture, no outlines. Writing and reading heavy, so pray you have a good TA. The readings were sometimes interesting, but sometimes difficult to understand. Watch out for discussion questions because they are a surprise.

Took this class to fulfill the DEI requirement. Although it's a lower-division course, there is a heavy workload with constant reading and writing. Assignments often lack clear prompts, which makes it hard to know what's expected. Attendance and participation are mandatory, and students are randomly called on during lecture.

Welp yall ruined it. The bozo reads these and she made attendance mandatory. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. I'm tired of professors claiming to be “old schooled” and then complain that they are not caught up with students. Please grow up lady

Required long readings for every lecture and she doesn't teach about the material, only asks about students interpretation. Reading assignments every week but as long as you turn in something you get 80%. Easy B with little to no effort and I skipped every lecture after week 2.
Nice class- learned quite a bit although exam was a bit painful!

Class moving to online format but still well structured and packed with useful knowledge. Caring professor who responds quickly to student comments and uses tools like Piazza. Class TA was slow to respond but Professor always stepped up and took care of questions. Must-take class at UCSD.

Out of the 7 weeks worth of material he assigned 40-50% of the exam's points based on ONE week of unit econ material. Not to mention the fact that econ shouldn't even be part of this class. Also the exam does NOT give you enough time, also the study guide and practice questions were completely disorganized and formatted horribly. Horrible, terrible

I was very fortunate to have taken a course by him before graduating. He is one of the best professors, especially at the Rady school. He is an excellent communicator, incredibly caring and interested in student development. He's incredibly forward thinking, he is technically savvy, is keyed into the modern business world (which is rare) & patient!

This class is easy. I dont think i learned very much. He is a little hard to understand and he talks about the same topics a lot and things seem repetitive. its nice that its online tho. the tests were easy and the homework was really easy. the group project was also not bad. its an easy class its just kind of boring as the quarter goes along.

He was pretty good.The biggest issue I had with this class is that the lectures were kinda unorganized in my opinion, but overall he gives lots of support outside of class through OH and Piazza as well. His homework was very helpful for exams,and the exams themselves were on the easier side of the usual upper division math exam, overall pretty good

He's a kind professor! The weekly assignments are doable and he gives us about a week to process the content and do them after lectures. His exams are fair and the final turned out very well for the class. He is also very responsive on Piazza, so I appreciate it. I would recommend him for Math 194!
He explains concepts clear, fair exams and homeworks.

Best math professor I've had at UCSD, and top 3 in any department. He's very knowledgeable and gives an engaging lecture. Great professor if you're interested in learning. Probably a bad professor if you're super lazy like some of the people on here appear to be...

Everyone should take this professor's class. Otherwise, you will have no chance to experience the worst math professor in UCSD. Lectures don't make sense, and his exam is not related to hw at all. He is definitely the best candidate for the topic "who is the worst professor you have ever taken in UCSD" in Quora.

Exam avgs were 40%, yet 1/2 q's were from hw and the other tested you on problem solving (mainly computational) Exams have time pressure bc 1q = 10 min, and it's usually an integral with multiple parts (e.g., surface: parametrize + jacobian + bounds + eval). tbh practice*3, the more hw probs you do the more prepared you'll be. 10min/q is manageable

Very funny / nice guy in lecture, easy to approach. However, exams tended to be fairly difficult with our class average being around 40% between both midterms. Was a very picky grader on the final, lost points for not writing out a formula I used and took half off a question for a small algebra error in integration. Would take again, but be aware.

Very nice guy but not nice enough to take it easy on you. Homeworks and exams are very difficult, with exams being designed for you to not finish. He doesn't podcast so go to lecture if you want to understand the material. Do not take if you wanna spend any time enjoying your life, otherwise if you're looking for a challenge this is your guy.

Strict and lots of HW, but it is 140. Funny professor, helpful and wants the best for students. I like that he remembers people's names. You will learn the most from doing the HW early. Midterms are 4 questions in 50 minutes, final is 6 questions in 50 minutes, both meant to not be finished. Know your definitions and theorems!

The class content is hard (obviously, it's 140), but his lectures are fun, interesting, and he tries his best to know everyone's name. My only criticisms are that his handwriting is a little hard to understand, and his exams have unnecessary time pressure and no one finishes them (the final exam was literally 50 min long). Very generous curve.

Professor Herreño is the best Econ professor I've had. He cares about your learning; he's always open to answer questions during class and office hours, but it's up to you to fully learn the material. His lecture slides/notes are informative, but don't miss his lectures. He's highly knowledgable and his accent is not an issue. Highly recommend! :)

110B is hard, but Professor Herreño teaches a legitimate course with tons of info. His lectures were informative and he encourages participation. You get what you put into it; read the lecture notes and go to discussion and you'll be fine. The course was challenging, but it's curved at the end. One of the few actual useful econ courses IMO.

Idk how I feel ab him tbh. Doesn't record lectures, doesn't upload answers to practice exams so you can't really prepare well for the midterms/final unless you attend BOTH lectures and discussions. 2 quizzes are supposed to alleviate weight of midterms/final but they were ridiculously hard. But he moved final to online, so he cares somewhat

lecture notes unclear with lots of grammatical errors. Slides and lectures do not match. Lectures are not recorded and accent makes it hard to understand. Uses too many graphical data to illustrate concept rather than teaching the actual concept. Practice test have very unclear grading criteria. Hardly responds to emails.

Prof did a great job at teaching material. He encourages questions, so ask! He wants you to do well & will explain a concept if you're having trouble understanding something. Graded by a few things and is clear. Do the practice test and attend discussion! He put resources to help you, doing the minimum passes you but its an easy class to do better.
Too many assignments for an online course

Very disorganized. Leaves a lot of loose ends in her explanations, her video classes are extremely confusing. She covered some topics that I was already familiar with, and I was mesmerized on how complicated she made them. Questions are not worded well and are unclear. She has a lot of experience, but her teaching style does not work for me.

She is the first professor I have taken for the Accounting Certificate. I love her! She is such a caring professor who was very accessible. Asynchronous format so no lectures to attend at set times. She grades the course on points which I like. She allowed for late assignments and a few times she extended deadlines. You will learn in her class!
Class extremely easy. Just have to go to seminar every week and do a presentation once during the quarter. Final is the exact same problems that we do during lecture just with different numbers.

Caring and passionate professor!! Will gain a new appreciation for math and collaboration after taking this course. Minimal homework, but you must participate in class in small group presentations and at least one presentation in front of the class. Attendance is mandatory with one free pass. Final exam is also fair.
Steven's tends to stamp out curiosity which makes her a very unpleasant teacher.
Stevens is an awesome math prof - her lectures are clear and she encourages questions. Use Unstuck study alongside the practice exams to ace this class.
good math prof, discussion sections helped a lot

she literally told me my essay should've been “looked over by an native english speaker.” I was literally born in the country and grew up here, almost was a literature minor, and chatted with her at office hours. textbook micro-aggression. lost a lot of respect for her.

Dr. French is very condescending. One of the worse mistakes I made was to TA for her. I am currently a medical doctor. This is in response to others who said "you want your doctor to know the material well." Dr. French can teach the material without being condescending. She needs to take courses on treating students, with respect.

Dr. French likes to test on things that she only peripherally covered during class time. Because of this, succeeding on tests really just boils down to having to memorize all of her lecture slides, note outlines, and textbook readings. If that sounds easy to you, then take the class and find out for yourself why everyone hates her.

Dr. French is challenging. She's willing to test your ability to apply concepts to questions you've never seen before. Really, she's not bad at explaining the material - it even feels like she's dragging on a bit for some of the easier content. Her biggest weakness is that she might skip topics (kidneys), which can be important in future classes.
Makes you work for the class. Know the outlines by heart.

This two-credit course took about 8 hours a week (2000+ word reports). His lectures are challenging, but he's hilarious and nice. Your grade depends on your TA, but as long as you do the lab reports diligently, you should get an A. The final assesses your lab reports and is a fair assessment of your work. REMEMBER UNCERTAINTY AND T SCORES!
He is fun and all but makes a 2-unit class a lot of work. 2CL is a lot more chill. Lab reports were all 10+ pages and beware of pre-lab quizzes! TA's were amazing life saviors though!

Professor Sharma's lecture is so boring and not clear. He spent little time on the physics formulas that are difficult to understand by ourselves. We had to use iclicker app for midterms and final, and each question is timed. When students ask him about exam time and grading criteria, he asks them to figure it out by themselves...

Prof. Sharma is a really funny guy but this class was pretty hard in my opinion. If you have not taken high school physics before, you will probably have to put in more work. Sometimes the lectures were very long, almost 2 hours (which is hard if you're online). Your grade is only based on the weekly quizzes, midterm, and final.

Strong professor who knows his stuff. For this class the grading was pretty heavy on the TAs, and things were returned very slowly. Do a good job after the first few labs and you'll pass with no problems. Be honest with errors and voice concerns early and you'll get an A. Final was VERY based on lab processes.
Had plenty of office hours after every single lecture to help with the qualifying exam preparations. Very kind and understanding man. He's great.

3 professors teaches 20e in Fall 2021, and I take them in first few week. This guy is undegraded in RMP but is the best profess this quar. Test is easy. HW is from textbook. I don't know why this guy is 3/5. Although you need some extra effort to do HW, he teaches the concept very clear with example. WITH EXAMPLE, which other prof does not make.

He's very caring and understanding but his grading scheme is too test heavy with each exam worth 24% of the final grade. He curves grades so that there are a proportionate number of students with A, B, and C grades, approximately 30-30-30. So even if you would've normally gotten an A, you could get a B if enough peers do better then you.

Prof. Roberts' lectures generally do not help, so be prepared to learn outside. His notes are not very legible. HWs generally reflects the exams, so make sure you understand all of them as exams are very similar. The exams are not very difficult, but they are not forgiving. Missing one complete problem almost means going down a letter grade.

Nice guy, but not good at teaching or explaining things. No piazza set up, and his lectures are boring. Had to learn most of the material myself by going through hw problems. While the grading on HWs are pretty lenient, the final was terribly hard. Truly horrible.

holy mother of pearl when god gave a gift to the earth that gift was Galia. seriously this woman reignited my love for chemistry after mark young from 6b. her tests are comprehensive and fair, with a fat curve if necessary ! her lectures r easy to follow and understand, not too much hw and discussion work, and extra credit too!!!

Best teacher by far for the CHEM6 series. She is very caring and doesn't lecture to make sure all the content is covered, but instead lectures at a pace that students can understand. Very generous with extra credit and all the exams were curved with lots of points. Discussions are mandatory if you want extra credit, but they were very helpful.

Great professor! You can do well in this class regardless of how 6B and 6A went for you. She does lots and lots of practice problems during lectures which helps drill them in to your brain. My only critique is that the homework, while not difficult, marks you off for incorrect attempts, so ppl who use chat gpt on them get 100%. But she is great!!!!
My favorite chem professor so far. Makes chem easy to understand and truly cares about her students.

Recorded non-mandatory lectures and extra credit if you go to discussion. She gave crazy good curves on the midterms and finals (10-12 points) and her lectures are easy to understand if you pay attention. She used achieve for homework problems, marked off for every wrong attempt.

Professor is well-meaning, funny, and knows his stuff, but I learned nothing from this class. Exams were just "how many facts and statistics can you memorize from lecture?" simulator. There's extra credit, but it's a lottery system based on luck, not merit. Felt like a waste of my education. Still, easy A if you attend lecture and do what he says.

Attendance is not mando but if you go you have a chance at getting E.C. pts for midterm + final. Your whole grade is your midterm and final. There is also a policy memo but if the class avg is high, he makes it optional and that 25% gets slapped onto your final. Show up to the reviews because he hands out the answers to midterm and final!

Super chill guy, interesting lectures and easy to keep up. You don't need the readings if you show up to lecture. He does extra credit lotteries for people who show up, but as long as you keep up with the course content you don't really need it. written midterm and final
BEST PROF EVER FR FR
Amazing professor! If you show up to class and attend the review sessions you'll be fine.

THE GOAT OF MCWP !! One of the nicest dudes out here teaching at UCSD hands down. Very funny and witty. During OH, he'll provide good critiques on how to improve your essay. Don't stall on those big assignments; ask him questions. Follow what he wants in your papers, and you can get your desired grade!! Utilize other resources (e.g., LATS). Great !

Genuinely a good professor with so many resources to aid in assignments and is very easy to approach. I really don't understand previous negative ratings because he is very fair and it seems to just have undeserved frustration lashed out on him.

While the course itself was designed to expect a lot, Prof. Morshed does his best to make it easier. He's easily accessible & office hours are super helpful and he gives great feedback on how to improve. Lot of writing but he's pretty generous in my opinion with the grading. Very understanding and funny, and a great professor!

His slides and feedback make everyone even more confused as MCWP 50 takes everything you know about writing and reverses it. You will be graded harshly for using direct quotes in a research paper. He expects originality and contradicts himself on many criticisms. He expects heavy paraphrasing on papers that need to use hard evidence and citations.
Had scores taken off for terms said in class or from slides that are not listed in the prompt or rubric... don't even need to check rubric in this class, just follow ALL things he said
This professor is a nice guy!! The classes are very long and boring but the exams are pretty easy. The textbook is necessary for the class.

He is one of the best professor at UCSD. That is why his classes are always waitlisted. Exams were online essay questions on reading/lectures that were open note. We had plenty of time to complete exams and had 2 easy homework assignments. He is easy going and awesome, You can try to take his class, you never feel regret.

Lectures are boring, since they're so long too, it makes it even more worse. He is a nice and easy going guy though and the class is easy to pass. He does the midterm and exam online so you don't have to come into class. They're both writing assignments that he gives you 3 hours for, just do them and you'll be fine. Boring class but easy stuff.

He is one of the best professors at UCSD. He wants you to learn.The class is a pretty easy A. The only real challenge is the timed exams. They require a lot of writing, but they're not too difficult. You will pass easily. Every student was very happy in class. Not stressful. I would  take him again
The professor is nice, but the grading is really bad. Especially the comments left, the comments provide no value on how to do better to get good grade.

Super easy imo. Final was online/not lockdown. Lectures were not mandatory. Mandatory discussions but super chill. There were only 4 HWs, a midterm that I felt was very fair, and a final. Lots of readings but the content is all pretty simple. Sutton is super nice, and gives extra credit just for going to lectures. Highly recommend.

Honestly I thought I was cooked in this class. I got a C on the midterm, and was bogged down by the readings, but class was heavily curved and catered towards students success. The final was significantly easier, open note. 4 assignments to becompleted throughout quarter, that are practical and straightforward.

I think the class is very interesting and informative, Prof is very nice and wants students to succeed. I feel like I learned a lot of was engaged with the material. In this class, you work with a group for some assignments and she gives class time to do so. A fair amount of reading but nothing that isn't manageable.

This class is horrible. She's nice, sure but the way the midterm was structured was a joke. I actually did study and I just barely passed it and THEN she has the audacity to take points off everyones midterms. The class structure is just weird. Its a mix of live and async but then cancels some live classes like what. Least favorite class

4 HW assignments, ea/very simple and she said herself she did not give out lower than (I think) a B on each one. Lots of extra credit in lecture and even on the midterm and final (which were a mix of MC, short answer). Her lectures were amazing and thorough, could easily replace the textbook. Section is mandatory, lecture isn't. I loved her class!
Useless class in terms of learning, but could take if you want an easy A.
Total waste of time and money- not sure why a quality University is offering such courses where students learn nothing!

This was a remote class and lectures were all recordings that you could view at your own time. However, most of us didn't know what he was trying to teach us the whole time. A lot of group work, so make sure that you pick the right group to work with. I don't believe that I am learning anything from this class but I had to take it for my minor.

Lots of group work, select members carefully. Lecture was long, attendance and participation is tracked. Class was hybrid, in-person session mandatory. TA was helpful and did almost all the work. Prof wouldn't even answer emails, relying on TA alot. Lecture is also taught by student presentations, midterm was open/note very easy, final was project.
There is really not clear grading criteria.

Nice professor, giving great lectures. But please try to avoid a TA call Phuc because she grades harder than other TAs and gives really aggressive feedback on your assignments instead of giving supportive and constructive feedback. And she acts differently from what she says. But overall, the course and the professor are chill.

Dr. D was great! This is a great class if you need an upper div chem GPA boost, and the material was super interesting. Exams are online but he said he may change that moving forward, and they were cumulative to help reinforce important topics. He is super sweet and funny and the material is useful for anyone interested in drug design.

I personally really liked his lecture style (I could sit and listen to him for hours). Exams were asynch on canvas open-note (but I hear he might change the structure of his class next year so beware). Only complaint is the team exams and group project cuz I got stuck with a crappy group.

This class is super easy, especially compared to the grind that is most other chem upper divs. If you want to just relax and take a GPA boost, it's a great choice. The subject matter is interesting and you do learn a decent amount about pharmacology, but the lectures get really dense and hard to follow. He also talks quietly and can be a bit boring

Dr. Dan is a very caring and fun professor. He is willing to answer any question you ask him (which people often underutilize) and is glad to hear feedback about the course. Asynchronous exams and group "team exams" and drug project, with randomly assigned groupmates. Very fair professor and would gladly take another course he teaches.

This is the easiest class in the chem department, even easier than most bio department courses. But this guy is really great at teaching. It may not feel like you learn anything at first but since the exams are cumulative you really do learn pharmacology by the end even if you put no effort into memorizing anything.

Overall amazing class and amazing professor. Her grading criteria is very straightforward and weekly assignments are easy and not time consuming at all. The exams were fair as well as long as you paid attention to her lectures. Attendance is counted with iClicker but she gave us 2 mental health days spread out throughout the quarter.
She is amazing, the exams are in person but the exams are very fair as long as you study the slides you're good TAKE HER

Professor Brashier was so awesome this quarter. She's really funny and a great professor. We had one assignment a week which was easy and her lectures were podcasted. We even had mental health days where we didn't have to go to class. Would definitely take her class again!

she's so nice and caring, tests are reflective of class material, and even sent me an email when i did well on the second exam compared to the first one, she truly cares for her students and is funny too

I wasn't particularly interested in the Belief in Weird Things content so the lectures were kind of boring to me, but it's not a super hard class to get an A in I guess. You just gotta make sure you understand the findings of the studies she discusses and what theory/concept it applies to. Loved her energy though she's a queen. 3 exams, drops 1.

Professor Rose is really passionate about these topics in class and provides really cool examples of real world events. His slides don't contain a lot of words, but his exams consist of direct in class examples so make sure to pay attention. He even said himself he just takes a few descriptors off of in class examples for the midterm and final.

Great lecturer. Obviously passionate about what he teaches. Super understanding about illnesses or other circumstances. Gives extra credit opportunities and opportunities to make up lost points on midterms. Homework isn't long and I once got feedback half an hour after turning in an assignment. Also, kind of looks like Pedro Pascal

Dr. Roses's class was not bad overall and some of the class content was very interesting. I took him for BIEB 156 and the class wasn't bad. Attendance is required for 10 of the 20 classes, but if you show up to all 20 and fill out the attendance quiz for each, you will get 10 points extra credit.

Professor Rose is an okay instructor. The class could get a bit boring every now and then, but overall it was very informative.  The only thing I disliked about his class was that he locks your grade in Canvas, so you are basically unaware of the grade you have. I am currently praying for a C in an elective class.
Heavy material in course but test is very fair and only tests what is featured on the slides. Ended up curving the class upwards. Great professor!

Prof covered material fairly concisely, with all pertinent information included in slides and lectures. grade is based solely on best 2 out of 3 exams, but retaining info and preparing are fine enough with detailed notes and studying. lectures included interesting papers (not all tested), and prof contextualized the course contents very well.

The syllabus says "Do not expect to be graded solely in comparison to your classmates (ie a curve)", but then the entire class was curved down and the explanation was that we were graded by our performance compared to the entire class... which is the exact opposite of what was understood for the last 10 weeks.

The class itself was interesting, and the students did really well (A's). He said there was usually no curve, then suddenly set a curve that LOWERED the grades students worked for from our A's into B's. Don't take this class. You can read research papers outside of it and it's really not worth it if your hard work is going to be discounted anyway.

The professor made the grade cutoffs extraordinarily higher than usual at the end of the course, and seemingly wants to harm student's grades more than help. The cutoff for a B- was absolutely ridiculous at 84%. This is extremely misleading when the professor doesn't give a grade scale at all in the beginning of the course.

The tests are exactly the homework questions; this class will require intense and rote memorization just because of that.  Answers to the homework questions are given during discussion, so make sure to attend those. Lectures can be a bit dry, but he will bring guest lecturers towards the end of the semester and I found those to be more fun lol.

He def knows his stuff, but lecture's a bit monotonous and not very stimulating. Your grade is hw, 2 midterms, and 1 final. Exams only have questions off of the hw, so it's an easy A if you're good at memorizing. He never had OH, and some students got an F on the final for no reason and he was MIA when they emailed him. Apathetic but knowledgeable

If you try to ask the professor any questions, he gets annoyed and turns you away. The entire class is focused on a specific set of findings in fly genetics from his own lab, which is irrelevant and useless for anything in your life (unless you work in his lab). the material is a complete waste of time, you wont learn any developmental neuro.

Awful class , awful professor, awful TA's.  It is all mundane memorization, and unless you have psychic abilities, even if you are correct but do not word it exactly how it is on their answer key you lose a lot of points. Worst of all, the prof doesnt care about you, the class, or the TA's.  His lectures are scattered everywhere and hard to follow.

no podcasts, and no office hours. good luck trying to ask him a question beforeafter class. If you enjoy memorizing thousands of names of genes and proteins, and not learning a single concept, take this class. To be blunt, the material you memorize in this class is  completely useless, unless your becoming a fly biologist.

Bellare knows how to make a class! Not too trivial, not too overwhelming. It leans math-heavy, likely what fuels the CS community's unjustified phobia against it. But if you're patient and like solving problems (2 per HW each week), it's like 105 and 101, maybe easier. Great intro to cryptography. Gave 4 for difficulty because the final was tough.

One of my favorite professors at UCSD -- CSE 107 is a hard class, but you will seriously learn cryptography through a mathematical, provable security lens, taught by a brilliant researcher whose spent his career defining the area. Challenging but super fun homework and exam problems -- make sure to study his slides carefully! Strongly recommend.
Very discouraging in office hours and would refuse to answer questions.

This professor writes some of the most confusing pseudocode I've ever seen. Being as he pre-recorded his lectures you can't even ask for verification. The professor does not believe in giving examples for what he covers either, and slides are just generally written confusingly. He also expects you to know things he has never covered, nor are reqs

Quizzes are tough, but final is fine. Definitely one of the most challenging classes in CSE. Prof. explains concept quite clear, but don't expect he would give much example (and don't ask for it). Recommend to watch lectures on podcast with 2.0x speed.

Definitely recommend taking his class. There were 2 midterms and a final, one of the midterms can be dropped if the grade you got on the final was better. His lectures were clear and understandable, you could use a cheat sheet on the exams, and the exam practice/reviews he gave out were very similar to the problems on the actual exams

Lecures not mandatory but helpful, he uses different colors of chalk to make things more fun. The textbook is free and just supplementary. The practice exams are basically the exam so study those a lot, and you get a full page of notes to bring in to exams. He's very sweet and tries to make sure everyone understands the content.

His lectures don't require attendance but he doesn't record lectures so it's basically mandatory unless you can get good notes from your friends. The professor is very caring and was always helpful especially during office hours. He writes on a chalk board so it's not super difficult to follow even though he goes over topics pretty quickly.

1-3 homeworks per week, 2 in-person canvas quizzes, 1 final presentation/business plan, participation is tracked. There is a lot of group work to create a business plan for a fake startup. Quizzes tested on group work and study guide provided (TA checked tab logs). Even though I had a 97%, I STILL got a B+. It is a pretty easy CSE course though.

Class curves down. Got a 95% in the class which translated in a B+. Missed ~1-2 questions total on exams throughout the WHOLE quarter. 2 students in the whole class got an A or above. Will ruin your GPA if you're a good student.

Dr. Simonson is very knowledgeable and well-meaning. I learned a lot from her class and her research. It is structured like a grad course, and your grade is determined by few things (only HW, 2 presentations, 1 midterm, 1 final). All exams were take home.
