She also does not give feedback/grades back on time, and she sometimes didn't show up to OH.

Dr. Childs is what education is about. Eloquent, inspiring, dedicated, passionate. Lectures were captivating and significantly impacted my understanding of the world. It is a privilege to be able to have listened to his teachings and am SO glad I got to take his class. Take the opportunity if you can. Pop quizzes can be rough, rest is chill.

I have taken 2 courses with Professor Childs and have thoroughly enjoyed both. He is incredibly eloquent and engaging and provides very interesting readings. As long as you have the interest, I believe the class will be a very rewarding experience.

Loved Dr. Childs, he knew what he was talking about and he had a lot of passion for the subject. Pop quizzes aren't hard, just do the reading on time. I didn't annotate the reading and still got 100s on the quizzes. It is a lot of work, so I wouldn't take if it's for a gen ed or DEI requirement, but highly recommend if it's for major or interest.

I think if you see any negative reviews from someone it is because they disrespected Dr. Childs and could not take accountability for their actions. Other than that, there is a pretty lengthy amount of reading but it is to be expected. There are pop quizzes so just go to class. Dr. Childs is amazing and really knows what he is talking about.
Horrible class do not take this professor. Professor doesn't use canvas at all so it makes it hard to keep up and there's SO much reading. If this isn't your major do not take it

one of the best professors I have ever had at ucsd, he is so passionate about teaching and genuinly cares for all of his students success. Make sure to attend lectures because he provides so much more information than what is on the slides, midterms were very fair and reflective of course content. This course made me love my major and physiology.
This is the goat prof. Very digestible slides and straightforward concepts. The whole course is graded on 3 simple exams. He genuinely wants to see students succeed and have fun.

Amazing professor! Really cares about students and makes BIPN super digestible. Slides aren't the best so going to lecture is necessary. You are graded only by exams but he makes them extremely simple and tells you exactly what is on them. Also offers considerable extra credit and is very forgiving. Highly recommend for this infamously hard class!

Professor Madigan and her TAs are so thorough with their explanations I really appreciated all the work they put into the presentation slides and the mandatory discussions. The only thing that stopped me from getting an A+ was I missed a discussion class, but they give you 2 free excused absences so thats on me. 10/10 would take again

Dr. Madigan's class has been one of my favorites by far. As a non-biology major, the class content was fairly easy to understand and really interesting, especially the historical aspects. She is also very passionate about what she teaches. Discussion is online and there are 5 short quizzes (not cumulative) every 3-5 lectures along with a final.

Loved this class. Not a stem major so was scared to take bio but it couldn't have been more manageable. She used iClicker multiple-choice questions for attendance and discussion was optional. 4 midterms all online open note multiple choice, and same for the final. Loved it overall.

She goes fast during lectures, you can tell she is only reading off the slides. I felt like she didn't care if there was a mistake in her syllabus or study guides, outdated. Attendance is required now, I did bad with attendance but still managed to get A. Exams are poorly worded and can get confusing but should be ok w videos and extra studying.

Mandatory attendance via iclicker attendance polls that are worth a good chunk of your grade - lots of opportunity for extra credit - short exams but can be worded difficult at times - good lecturer and TA's who were always accessible outside of class

BEST PROF TAKE HIM. I took this class for a GE and best decision I ever made. Lectures are recorded. Weekly attendance quiz, unlimited attempts. Has mandatory discussions. There are 2 papers in the class. One midterm and one final and that's it! Homework takes 30 min it's not bad at all. TAKE THIS CLASS.

This professor is honestly amazing. Two essays that are 5 pages long, but double spaced. Super cool professor that is really engaging with the class, and they really want you to succeed. Gives you variety like you can pick your reading and such. Super chill class and also amazing professor! He has passion for music. Take this guy if you can.

Very nice and understanding professor. If you watch the lectures at a minimum, you can pass the class with an A. Discussion sections mandatory but you are allowed to swap with permission. Midterm/Final are papers on a topic discussed in week 1-5/6-10. Weekly "attendance quiz" on canvas but they're not graded.

super awesome professor that has no attendance policy, always gives extensions, respectful of everyone AND his lectures are really interesting and fun. i'm sad that i will probably never have him as a professor again because he's so great. all the assignments were so easy including the midterm/final paper.
The guy just makes stuff up…

he's honestly such a great prof. he's really nice and his lectures are very straightforward & detailed which i found to be super helpful. exams can be a bit challenging, but they really just try to test your understanding of the material beyond a surface level. + he does throw in easy questions that you can easily get if you somewhat studied.

Professor Boomhower is great at explaining things. If you didn't understand, watch it again or go to OH. This class was challenging and mentally stimulating in a great way. The exams are hard but heavily scaled, you only need a 66% to get an A. Make sure you understand problem set and practice exam questions. I do wish grading was less exam-heavy.
meh. class had me stressed. glad it's over. i would take with someone else but he's not the worst.

Great guy but exams are hard. More conceptual thinking is needed for his exams and it kind of strains your brain. Looking for an easy A, go with a different professor. Get ready to study 25/8 if you do take him.
he talks lil slow but his one of the best professor I've ever took. I wanna take his class more

The class was okay, with heavy reading assignments that I never completed, but I still ended up with an A since the tests were based on a lot of lecture and slide material with easy discussion posts. He is a great lecturer, but a very harsh grader when it comes to his essays. I recommend running it through TAs or himself to get a good score.

I liked lectures cuz they exposed me to a wider range of artists/artworks n builds on my knowledge. Class is effort+creativity not skill based

He did say that he was expecting a normal distribution for every quiz, but that was because the questions were extremely simple. 2C isn't that difficult if you spend ~ 1hr everyday after lecture to read the textbook (there is no calculus). He encourages you to figure out solutions instead of writing things out for you, just ask questions.

This professor cares way too much about having a "normal distribution". When a lot of the class did well on the second quiz, he only commented on how it wasn't normally distributed and that he may have to actively have to make it harder so that he can bring the grades down. That is insane to me. Explains concepts okay but cares about prestige a lot

50% of grade was on 6 quizzes (1 dropped), 25% was final, rest was attendance and homework. Overall, the class was very fair, he basically took the key concepts (equations) from each chapter and put them on the quizzes and homework. Homework and lecture notes were greatly reflected on the quizzes. Did not curve but gave 3% extra to whole class...

The curve is gigantic. I probably would have gotten a C- without the curve. He uses iClickers for 5% of your grade (all of which are trick questions!) He enjoys teaching and his lectures are pretty good. Your textbook will not get dusty, though, from teaching yourself. It is a physics course so get ready for homework.
This dude is very cool!

whoever see this message bro just go to youtube. Way better step-by-step explanation and no accent. I self studied 10+ hours outside the class to get the grade. If you have another choice don't choose him

Although he's really nice as a professor, his teaching style is very confusing. The final was incredibly hard compared to the midterms, and he had a 50% average on each test. If you fail the final, you fail the class so beware!

This professor is so sweet and grades very reasonably! He did curve our grades but lectures were very quick paced and did not thoroughly explain the material. If you're not already familiar with the concepts, you may want to prepare to go to tutoring or office hours to get extra help with this class.

Dai seems like a nice guy, but generally lost as a professor. Despite his class being introductory, he teaches calculus in an overcomplicated manner that alienates even students who have taken previous calculus classes. I would agree that he improved over the quarter, and I'm sure he will continue to improve, but I still cannot recommend him.

Amazing professor. Focuses on the mechanistic view of biochemistry, and I personally love it. Explains everything in a very easy-to-digest manner, and exams are extremely fair. Final was third midterm. Would recommend and take again.

Easily one of the best profs at UCSD. The way he taught mechanisms makes them actually understandable compared to Ochem. Exams are super fair based on lectures and homework, and he's super willing to work with students. His lectures are informative but also super interesting, and easy to take notes with. He has 5 stars for a reason!!!

Budin is an all around great prof. Lectures are straightforward, he's really caring about his students, and clearly loves the subjects he teaches. I cannot find anything bad to say about him. 10/10 would learn about the citric acid cycle again

I was very hesitant to take this class as I previously had dropped it with a different processor due to the difficulty, however with Professor Budin he explains it in such simple terms and analogy it makes it easier to understand. I struggle a lot with Biochem since it is such a topic that requires a lot of memorization but was able to get an A!

Professor Budin is a nice guy. He's passionate about what he's teaching and explains it in an easy/straightforward manner. The class is heavy on mechanisms so you will have to study but the practice exams/lectures do reflect the midterms/finals. Always willing to answer your questions and is probably one of the best profs I've had in my 3 yrs here!

Really nice & understanding! Lets you choose between simplified and traditional, there's alot worksheets, but they aren't hard. Also means that the grade is madeup of a lot of things and there is room for improvement. The class is very interactive & you do a lot of projects throughout the year, but overall, my Chinese skills have improved a lot.
greatest of all time

Love this class! Chen laoshi is always a caring professor, which makes class a supportive environment. There is some homework and a few projects, but there is ample time to complete them. Take CHIN100 with Chen laoshi if you have the opportunity; you won't regret it!
Took for entire 10M series. Really good teacher, helpful outside of class, fun projects.

No time to study bc im trying to finish the hw. Characters taught not organized (ex. we learned Taipei and marriage but not little brother). Lots of ppl are already fluent and just want easy credit, so if you're like me and NOT fluent, you'll feel like the dumbest person in the room. I have to mentally prepare before going to class so i don't cry.

Marchetto is super knowledgable and the class is easy. Mandatory discussions but not lectures, one weekly assignment, and asynchronous, open-note tests. She also posts her powerpoints and you can supplement them with optional reading. Very content heavy but overall super interesting class. She will sometimes bring skulls to class!!
Maria is so caring! she truly cares about your education! New TA Jose is awesome and he is truly passionate about teaching! love this TA more than the other one that was boring and falling asleep
Just dropping this for people wondering whether attendance is mandatory. Lectures are not mandatory, but discussions/lab attendance are now worth your grade. This is an update, as of April 2025.

Easy class, but it's also genuinely interesting and Prof. Marchetto is very passionate about teaching.  One lab assignment per week based on topics for the week, all midterms and labs are open note/material, powerpoints posted to canvas.  Would definitely recommend!

Course is quite easy to do well in and fascinating too. Attendance to both lectures and discussions are both optional and both are recorded and uploaded as well. There were weekly "labs" which were just quizzes, 2 midterms, and a final which are take home and online. Also all of the answers to the exams are easily found online too.

The class is easy with only 2 short essays and a final project. That being said, the final project is a 10-15 page paper about a community in SD + presentation. With the content given in class, it was definitely tricky to have things to write about/ having a direction for the project, but it was doable. The TA graded pretty harshly as well.

Our final paper was a 10-12 page essay requirement with a poster presentation. I didn't mind it but for the amount of content we learned (not a lot) a 10 page paper was ridiculous. He was very nice though and the material of the class was interesting.

When I first took this class I had almost no interest in the subject. After I walked out of the last class I can say this professor changed my view on planning and sustainability.  He's very clear, has a good sense of humor, and knows his stuff.  He doesn't post lecture slides though, so be ready for a lot of note taking!

Lots of reading. Make sure you know how to write fast. He doesn't provide the slides he goes over. I found him inspiring for the subject. Reading is a lot but I think he dis well in clarifying what he wanted us to know and what we were going to get tested on.
GOAT, absolutely amazing lecturer
I enjoyed his lectures, although I do with they were a little bit more organized. Rlly nice and understanding.

If you ever get the chance to take Marc's class, DO IT. He's seriously one of the most caring and professional professors out there.  He makes complicated stuff like phonetics feel way less scary, and you can tell he's really passionate about what he teaches. Plus, he's super approachable if you have questions or suggestions.

Marc is great and you can tell he really loves phonetics. He takes the time to learn everyone's name and lectures are usually pretty enjoyable. The final paper can be difficult but it's fine as long as you keep up from week 1. They do have cute outfits :3

Marc is an amazing professor he is a great lecturer which is good because you will definitely need them for your homework, which isn't that bad he is just very very strict on the pronunciation and you WILL get docked for small infractions. Overall I loved his class and I would definitely take it again.
simplifies semantics a lot, i feel like we could have learned a lot more but it made the class way easier compared to other versions of the class taught by other profs so yay

Just such an incredible guy, really focuses on knowing his students, making sure everyone is heard, and making sure everyone's opinion feels valued. Cool assignments and readings. You can tell he loves what he does. Contract grading. There are "class exercises" which are basically pop quizzes/attendance, but he has alternatives if you miss class.

I think that this class is very interesting and Prof is nice and respectful, but the grading was a little weird, more the fault of the TA but did not receive grades until week 8. Prof changed the grading scale because of this though. The class should be an easy A if structured a little better but was missing that this quarter.

Read Angela Davis' "Are Prisons Obsolete" and based weekly lectures off of the chapter read. I found the topic very interesting, and Professor has a lot of experience in the field, so he has a lot of information to share. You can get by without reading, but it's a fun and intriguing topic.
Great class, would love to take Hankins again

CGS 87 is a very interactive, engaging, and fun seminar on the Prison Industrial Complex! Only one chapter of reading each week and you pretty much just discuss it in class and Hankins will pull in more relevant info. It's very contemporary and open to discussing pretty much anything related to the subject! 10/10 recommend if you want a chill class

Professor Dominguez genuinely cares about her students. Her class was really easy but still worthwhile. Enjoyed talking to her, definitely get the sense that she is fun and kind, it truly matters to her that we do well.

If you have to take this spanish course, take this professor ! One of the best i've had at UCSD she is super caring and funny. She won't judge if you can't say certain words in spanish she allows you to say them in english. Assignments are super easy and quick.

I loveeeeee professor Dominguez. She's so kind, so understanding. She does have weekly writing assignments and some projects, but they're easy. She doesn't judge you regardless if your Spanish is bad. (lol) She's also very inclusive. 
Easy class, love the professor.

Prof Dominguez really cares about her students and gives plenty opportunities to practice Spanish. Participation and attendance are mandatory, but she cancels Friday classes. Half of the classes are w the TA (covers grammar), the other half with the Prof (goes over textbook). The weekly movie assignments were fun! No tests, just a final project.

Amazing professor. He talks about companies a lot and how to analyze them. 1 midterm, attendance taken, 1 group project, biweekly hw. He genuinely cares for his students, especially during office hours. Feel free to ask him questions. He seems rather distant at first, but once you talk with him, he is rlly willing go out of his way to help you out.

Professor Long is new but really cares about her students and wants everyone to do well. Each week, students have to give a presentation on the weekly readings which are mandatory and everyone has to go. Quizzes on readings happen every Tuesday, and discussion prompts are due the Sunday before the quiz. Actively participating in class is a MUST.

Not bad in terms of lecturing but that's the only good thing I can say. The final was 2x harder than midterms. You can get extra credits for answering questions in lectures, but she picks favorite and will rarely let you answer if you were not one of her favorites. I raised my hand in almost every single lecture but she only called on me twice.

Labs were disorganized and the instructions often didn't match what we were actually doing. Grading felt inconsistent and confusing. Feedback was vague, and getting clarification didn't help much. It felt more frustrating than educational.

I never write these things but I hope someone sees this from the chem dept. Why is this professor still teaching here, don't students deserve better? Professors with a known record of questionable behavior that has been reported multiple times should not still be here...

Lecture was hard to sit through, pick someone else if you can. Wish chem dept would find inspired teachers for our classes...

but i guess if you have no choice then just suck it up and get through it

Professor Stauber was amazing! It is definitely a difficult class but she teaches it very well. On the exams a good amount of partial credit is given, and be aware of homework since it's worth about a quarter of the grade. Wish she taught 120B, she was great!

Avoid! He doesn't leverage Canvas MLS. Instead teaching material linked to his server. Spend 1/2 your time trying to find the course work. When you ask him questions, he immediately recites his resume. This is to impress & intimidate you, But has nothing to do with his teaching ability. He might be a competent consultant, but terrible instructor.

The class description says its a level I course. I believe this is very misleading. The class uses very difficult examples and is really a intermediate course.  Lots of the homework revolves around debugging compiler issues.

The professor requires you to purchase his $60 which is only available in hard copy at first. The fact that he requires you to pay $60 for a bunch of garbled lecture notes is insulting; the quality is not worth $60, at all, and it's clearly a way to make quick cash by shaking down students. I'm surprised UCSD extension permits this profiteering

The other reviews are a bit harsh. Professor Mitchell is a good teacher you just need to ask better questions. Don't waste your time watching the recorded lectures unless you're multitasking. READ HIS BOOK. Everything you need for success in his class is in the book! Don't procrastinate like I did and I guarantee you'll make an A.

Course lectures are very dry and just refer to sections in the textbook instead of explaining the subject. Course assignments aren't that bad but the instructions are verbose. The class feels like it's being run by a bot. Given the large number of freely available resources on the subject I would not recommend.

Works in the industry so he genuinely cares and knows the industry in and out. His lectures were fun and engaging. There are quizzes, reflections, midterm, project, and final which may sound like a lot, but they are spaced evenly and are fairly easy to do. He explains things in a manner that makes it easy to understand.

Professor Felke is awesome! Has vast experience (currently works at BD and has also worked at Kodak/Qualcomm) which he uses to connect to topics we learn during lectures. There is a lot of reading but it's interesting. Quizzes/exams were a bit tough but form a good study group and actively participate in class. Wish he taught more classes at Rady!

Professor Felke is an absolute delight. Great professor who makes the course fly by. It's an easy class objectively, so come with the intent to take as much as you can out of it without stressing too much about whether you'll pass or not.
His class does have some reading. If you do all the reading and the homework then you will easily pass this course. Mr.Felke is a great teacher and he is good at inspiring students during discussion!
Professor Magus is super responsive to emails and reachable after class. Would definitely take his class again if I could.

Prof. Shi's explanations of fluid mechanics are crystal clear—attending her class makes the fundamental concepts immediately understandable. The recorded lectures posted in the Canvas Media Gallery are incredibly helpful; I often revisit them to reinforce my understanding. Her lectures distill all the key concepts and essential takeaways.
Awful teaching. Did not even teach. Just posted lectures she has done during summer.

It was a fun class and I felt academically supported by Prof. She and the TAs. The class was very fair and representative of what was taught, which cannot be said about other classes. I am glad I got to be part of Prof. Shi's class.
Professor Kenley is super understanding and knowledgeable of the class content. Be ready to participate in class discussions and write about yourself.

Professor Kenley is AMAZING. I'm looking forward to taking her class again next semester. She is so understanding and the curriculum itself is so flexible. The class had a good amount of writing but they all had "Recommended Due Dates" which is AMAZING. She also obviously loves her job and it reflects a lot in how she teaches.
great professor! awesome researcher! get ready to study study study but his lectures are amazing and organized, and contain all you need to get a great score

Cell bio itself is a difficult course because its mostly memorization but he explains everything in lecture to the extent that you need to know for exams and relates everything to real life scenarios. Is very kind to students and is always open and ready for questions. Great class overall!

genuinely cares about students success, always making time for questions! his enthusiasm for research and discovery is very radiant, and he encourage critical thinking rather than just memorization. lectures are very interesting and informative

I had an incredible experience in Dr. Manor's cell bio class. His passion for the subject is truly inspiring, and he has a unique ability to break down complex concepts into clear, understandable explanations. Lectures were always well-organized, engaging, and full of real-world applications that made the material feel relevant and exciting.

professor manor has really made me interested in cell bio! tests are multiple choice and very straight forward as long as you study content on the slides and pay attention to what he emphasizes during lecture. attendance is not mandatory for lecture and discussion, but i highly recommend going to them since you can earn participation points!

I had the pleasure of being in professor Villafuerte's first ever class, TAKE HER CLASS! I learned so much and the weekly assignments aren't hard, along with one midterm and one final. Midterm is a paper and Final can be either creative work or paper, up to you. She's awesome and I really hope she continues to teach in the future.

This class is class is one of my favorites I have taken. Very interesting content and would definitely recommend for those coming from immigrant families. Nadia is very sweet and passionate about her work. Class is MWF with Friday being asynchronous. Course has 4 reading responses graded based on completion, a short essay, and creative project.

Overall a pretty easy, pretty interesting elective course. Everything for HW/Exams came from lecture slides and topics he emphasized in lecture. This class is definitely more interesting if/when people ask questions in lecture, as he likes to discuss things with people and go more in depth based on what you ask. Not hard, would recommend.

Final 50% Presentation 40% Participation 10% Mixed class with grad/undergrad Most of the class/final is based on your peers' presentation slides on papers related to fluorescent probes Prof gave like 3-4 lectures for entire quarter Pay attention to presentation or you'll bomb the final (though curved) Boring class, take something else

boring lectures, no discussion sections. The midterm and the final are open book, Laptops are allowed too. Two problem sets each worth 10%. The midterm was long and difficult. you do not even have time to look at your notes. The best way to get an A is fully understand everything on his lecture slide and kinda memorize it. he is not really helpful
Very interested in what he teaches. Learned a lot from this class. Very nice in class and in person.
SUPER CHILL very involved lecturer and even allows for discussion genuine interest in fostering a learning environment just pay attention and ask questions

The class I think is not hard, you need a camera (can be borrow from school) and photo paper (have to buy) to print out the photos you took and show them in TA session critique. The lecture can be a bit boring, but the main thing is just to know how to use a camera and to go out and take good photos according to the assignments. overall nice class

Lecture attendance is "mandatory" but most of the time she doesn't track it + no podcasts. Only maybe 2-3 times this quarter was there a QR code for attendance. Never really went to class and just submitted the projects. Really liked my section TA (James Dailey) and overall just very easy introductory class.

You must be passionate or show enough interest in photography, in order to do well in any of her classes. Conceptualism and creativity is valued above copying your favorite photos or their aesthetic. Do your own research on photographers you love and go to office hours to discuss. She is not about free handouts or telling you what to do.

8Am and random attendance taking, you buy lots of stuff, printing lab almost always out of in or paper error-ed, lecture nothing like assignments, not graded like an intro class. If you cannot interpret and recreate certain photos its not a great time for project 3 (30% of your grade)

Class is very project based but the project guidelines do not state the expectations well enough. Because of this our grades were majorly marked down since we didnt do what we were supposed to or didnt explore the topic enough

I took the class online on zoom. The lecture may get a bit boring, but the assignments are mostly small quiz or writing response, which should be easy to answer as long as you follow the lecture & materials and know what's going on. There's also a group project slides you need to do on an assigned reading, but as long as corporate it's not hard
Boring lectures but not mandatory. Easy assignments.

Readings were super interesting and I learned a lot! Definitely isn't necessary to do every reading, just take a few notes because all tests are open-note.

Prof is very understanding when it comes to course policy (tries to make lecture engaging, made discussion board requirements easier).

ETHN 1R: This class would've been more helpful if it had been recorded or offered recorded lectures rather than live Zoom lectures. The class heavily uses the readings assigned each week, but I learned more easily from discussion sessions with my TA.

Gosin was a good professor but her lectures were kind of dull and not engaging either. A lot of the homework was reading and they were around 50 pages long at times and it was frustrating to keep up with it. Nice teacher, easy class in terms of assignments, but the readings took away my interest in the class. Final was really easy too.

He's super funny and adorable. His exams aren't hard either but his slides are not the best. I had to learn about the studies myself because the slides were confusing and his explanations weren't the best either. Mandatory attendance. Overall, this class was enjoyable, just wish it was more organized.

Really passionate about his work but causes him to digress during lecture a lot, it's not terrible. The content was super interesting and the work was manageable. Attendance mandatory for credit and if you want to pass the exam.

Funny, sweet professor! Coming to class was a delight. He has such expertise in the field, and many of the experiments he teaches are his own. Graded only by two exams (30% each), an "in the movies" essay (20%), and attendance (20%). Easy to ace the exams if you study and understand the experiments.

No recorded lecture; mandatory attendance; all you have are the slides (that aren't that good); textbook isn't helpful; lectures were not clear to follow. TAs carry that class with their study guides. He's a funny and good guy, cares about students, but I was lost all the time. Needs better organization and needs to prioritize material better.

Lectures were tough since he never released the slides before class. He expects you to take in a load of information while also noting down everything he says at the same time. The slides were unhelpful since it only had basic information and no explanation. And all the explanation he wants you to know for the exam are only shared in class.

I took VIS 32*** Lecture was dense and she mostly just talks for the whole time which makes it very hard to engage. They are not interesting in the way she presents the class. Assignments were easy though. I think about 7/8 for the whole quarter. No midterm or final. So although it was boring, easy class.

Lectures were very long and not the most attention-grabbing in my opinion. There's an assignment every week and the instructions were very vague, luckily my TA was a generous grader. I don't feel like I left the class having learned much or gained anything.

Lectures were pointless but mandatory. All the assignments could be done with general knowledge and Google searches. I only needed one class reading for one essay. The others could be done without the readings. It's a good class if you want minimal work.

The professor never answered my emails and the structure of the class was not clear. She seemed to improvise most of the lectures and attendance was mandatory. The lectures were so boring in my opinion. Lots of things that have nothing to do with CAT or sections.

I appreciated Dr. Yoldas for being very communicative throughout this course, although she was not responsible for grading any of the two essays which were assigned (done by TAs). This was okay, though, because section work was sufficient for preparation/readiness with both essays. Odd prompts though, even though I didn't like them, I was engaged.

Confused why this prof is rated so low? They joked they used to be more difficult before, maybe that's it. Idk my grade yet, but personally I really like this professor. They are very enthusiastic and it makes me excited to learn about the subject. Overall it's also more organized than average for UCSD classes. Completely recommend this prof

This review is for the Fall 2022 course. The first few assignments were somewhat hard, but late days were given without penalty so overall it was fine. The professor knows the subject very well and is good at answering any questions. I did not know much Haskell before, it was nice to be able to build a small project in it by the end of the course.

The course feels more like "Haskell crash course" than an actual PL course. We did not learn any design considerations for PL, or ideas on how to build new features. It was basically an intro-to-CS course, but done in Haskell with minimal guidance on how to actually do Haskell. Spent more time on Hoogle (Haskell docs) than I did on lectures.

another chance I'll never take her class ever again. If you really want to learn something useful don't take this class. Be prepared to teach yourself Haskellband spend at least 10 hours per week. The class has nothing to do with databases, lectures are messy and nonorganized. The Final is super duper hard, my heart was broken at the first sight.

The lectures do not prepare you for the homework at all. There is such a huge disconnect between what she expects from the students given what she has gone over in class. Every homework was an absolute nightmare and a classic case of figure it out all on your own. The final was designed for what she said to be a 3 hour period, but took 10 +.

Professor Falcon is a really good teacher, the feedbacks are clear and she always offers office hours that work for the majority of class. You just need a book but the book is for all the AWP classes. I take her during winter and she really brings help when you need and she is very compressive.

To pass this class you need to make sure that you put in the time and effort. Also, make sure you focus on meeting the objectives. It's a very time-consuming class but worth it as you grow as a writer. Dr. Falcon provided helpful feedback and I was able to use that feedback to improve my essays and overall writing. I recommend taking her class!

I've been taking Dr. Falcon's class since AWP 4A. I'm not sure what her used to be, but I'm sure that she is the best literature Professor I've ever met. She is so nice. She always encourage you I help you to find your own talent!

She does not give clear feedback for every assignment. Every feedback she provides was personal feelings that does not tell how to improve the paper. She was pretty confusing on grading and very subjective. I literally learned nothing from this course.
Her feedback does not really make sense for revising essays. I learned nothing from this course. Most of our classmates got terrible grades like C.

Took this class for fun and was so worth it. Lectures were great, she did not just read off the slides, but encouraged discussion and helped us dive deep into texts and analyzing them. It opened my eyes to the depth and meaning behind fantasy writings. I loved all the books and readings we read. I had a lot of fun in the class and loved it.

I took LTCS 11 for fun because I needed something else to fit my schedule and not a lot else was open. Ended up being one of the best decisions I've made in terms of classes! I appreciated how much she encouraged us to interact with the material and theorize about our own interpretations. Lots of reading but totally worth it. Miss this class.

I actually had Professor Lampert-Weissig for LTCS11, which is a new class, she's by far one of my favorite professors! She's very kind and patient, the readings she selected were all great. I left her class with a new appreciation for vampires/werewolves--she was very passionate on the subject! Definitely recommend her :)

The professor is very kind and passionate in lecture but I find the grading highly subjective and unfair. Your grade in the class depends on your TA.

I received a B on all 3 of my papers. I fulfilled the requirements and gave my full effort. I am a writing major. I have never received a B on an essay before. My upper division courses give me As.

I may be biased because I love old English, but her lectures were very entertaining and you can tell she is passionate about literature (though they are a bit lengthy at times lol). The TA's also care and give good feedback on papers, and the weekly assignments are short, creative and graded for completion. (Lectures are also posted online after !)

Took PHIL31 and PHIL32 with him and honestly after those classes I'd totally be a philosophy major if I knew what to do with one. Lectures were incredible and the content always peeked my interest. The expectations from his courses are clear and if you pay attention it isn't hard to do well. Highly recommend these courses.
Easy class but dude is passive aggressive. Will make rude comments about students in passing. Insecure and has a chip on his shoulder. However, analyzing some of the platonic dialogues was a joy.

Participation graded by his and the TA's perception of your performance in class. Required discussion posts and has a midterm and final oral exam. If you pay attention in lecture and understand material, you will do good on the exams. You need to do the readings. Review material and be able to answer comprehension questions for participation.

So.Much.Reading. This class is solely graded on 2 oral exams that he claims to be "the easiest" midterm and final on campus. He expects you to remember every little detail from the readings which is impossible to remember from all the different books. Don't take this class if you think it's an "easy A" g.e. you will be disappointed.

Phil 32, His lectures can be quite boring and has snarky remarks. He can be a bit passive-aggressive and distasteful, but I think he just cares about his students in a way that isn't shown the best. He had "easy" exams, they were just 10-minute discussions with him or the TA, which if you do the readings and understand the content you'll be fine.
He is a good and thorough lecturer who is also very approachable outside of class.

Very good teacher. I went to all of the lectures and I really felt like that helped me understand the content. He would tell us exactly what to study and gave us reviews that directly reflected onto the tests. Discussion attendance mandatory, could miss 3.

I'm pretty bad at math, and my final grade reflects, but I would have definitely failed without Prof. Habib. Very accommodating and helpful. His lectures are barebones within a 20 series context, but the midterms/final translate seamlessly.
His voice was so soothing that I fell asleep multiple times in class

Habib's lectures were pretty good and helped me understand the content well. No mandatory attendance except for discussions. His tests were not too difficult and didn't have anything you would be unprepared for. He podcasted his lectures which was nice too

Way too much work for an async class. Long readings, long lectures, unclear assignment instructions, no extensions, and poorly planned group work. Directions were vague or missing, and deadlines were inflexible. Felt disorganized and stressful wouldn't recommend ETHN 3R with her.
Harsh and very critical grader and often gives unclear comments on your papers. She does have one on one office hours with you that help improve your writing but can be a little rude at times.
Most caring professor I've ever had.

She is responsible overall. But I really don't like the ways she taught. She is like an elementary school teacher and focus too much on the things that have no meanings at all. She also gets bossy and aggressive sometimes. She cares about students, but she doesn't even want to understand the student's situations before criticizing.
Professor Bauer is one of the most caring professors I've had at UCSD. She is very helpful in terms of writings, gives lots of good comments. Take her if you can.
Lectures can be a bit slow at times but Professor Tronzo is very knowledgeable and approachable. Assigns 3 papers with fun and interesting prompts.

knowledgable professor....i feel like he knows so much that he gives off "secret society" vibes....excellent/interesting readings... tip: review the reading sizes prior to attending class bc he assigns readings by volunteer method, so be smart and pick the shortest reading, raise your hand first lol!

I really enjoy his class. I do have a lot of interest in Christian art but he just made the learning experience more enjoyable. I also really like the essay topic he assigned: the prompt he assigned is very broad and we can basically write about any perspective that we are interested. He is a wonderful professor.

I think it kinda depends on your TA how easy it is. There's only a few papers with a bunch of super short journals in between. He's a great guy and very likable, though his lectures can be a bit boring. He doesn't assign much reading and I didn't do much of what he did assign and still got an A. He doesn't podcast.

His CAT class was very easy. Only consisted of one essay and weekly journal entries that are extremely easy. I stopped going to lectures on week 2 and they are not mandatory. However, the discussion are mandatory. By far the easiest CAT 1 prof and a good choice if you don't want a lot of work.
If its not obvious from his RMP, this isn't the professor for you if you're lazy or think you're owed a certain grade.
truly miserable, as someone who loves math and algebra he somehow made the course hell for me. 0/10, i wish there was a lower rating than 1
Likes to make the lives of students tough. Extremely narcissistic and does not listen to feedback. Thinks he is the greatest prof there is despite all data saying otherwise.

HW was good, proof-based Qs. Needs a lot of time+effort from your side, and not straight-forward using just the lectures. But 100% worth the effort, you learn a lot.

Prof. Behrouz Touri is a good teacher and always made sure that the doubts of the students are resolved. The assignments and the exams that he gives are a bit challenging.
I really appreciated her lecture style! As someone with a poor chemistry background, she made difficult concepts easier to understand. She would hold regular review sessions especially before tests.
She is a very kind-hearted professor and is very flexible in terms of catering to students' needs. It's very obvious that she is passionate about teaching and sharing her knowledge to others.

When studying for her exams, I basically relied on her recorded lectures only, and practice from the textbook and other outside sources. professor brydges definitely cares about her student and it shows. she provides so many resources outside of lecture that can help you practice and review course material. she also takes time to teach outside of lecture hours, providing many review sessions as well as answers any personal questions you have through piazza which helps soooo much.

Dr. Brydges' lectures are engaging and easy to follow. Dr. Brydges did an amazing job of teaching this course, making over-generalized complex concepts easier to understand. Get ready for group work and lots of reading, which may end up becoming tedious (but still can be good practice). GO TO THE REVIEW SESSIONS they are extremely helpful.

Most of your grade is your midterm and final. He just yaps for hours and hours long. He explains whats necessary, but because of all that extra talking its hard to keep up with the material that ACTUALLY matters.

the most awful professor i've ever had: has no empathy for his students, "if you failed the midterm you should just drop the class now", & doesn't curve even though the avg was a failing grade. his lectures have no structure & you're honestly better off just not going to class. bro should just enjoy retirement with his wife & quit being a prof
Stay away. Condescending when you ask questions and gets mad when you ask for clarification. During lecture he just rambles a bunch of numbers without explaining how he got them.
A great professor with many "old jokes".
He didn't help as to prepare for exams even though I am struggling a lot.

Poor study materials & unhelpful in OH. We were given practice exams using a different framework and told to translate between them before using them to study without an answer key. If you have accommodations, be prepared for a lot of back and forth and indifference to your disability specialist's recommendations. Piazza is neglected for Discord.

50% exams (tricky) and 50% programming assignments (easier). EC for attendance or writing fast code. Super cool prof and awesome course staff, but content itself feels like it's mostly about array indexing.

Very engagingand funny lectures and easy to reach outside of class (mainly on discord). There are leaderboards for the programming assignments which you can get extra credit on if your program runs very fast which is actually very fun, however the entire course is on matrix multiplication.

Great professor! I really liked the class but I did find it a bit difficult and I didn't really properly grasp the concepts until after the first midterm. It was definitely interesting exploring parallel programming platforms like Cuda and OpenCL especially since I hadn't heard of them before nor had been exposed to them. TAs/Tutors were solid too.
Love this professor! Great lecturer and very quick to respond to students.
Very very mediocre. Cancelled the 2nd half of class and we had remote lectures.

Math 103B is supposed to be a more manageable version of its 100 counterpart. While most professors end up skipping over some 100 content, I think Lu did a pretty good job trying to get to all of the material. He's an effective instructor and is more than happy to address any conceptual gaps in the class. Exams are challenging, but grading is fair
Don't miss lecture, review his notes and attend office hours and you'll be fine. Always willing to answer any of my questions and was a generous grader
Don't miss lectures and make sure to go over his notes and you'll be fine. His office hours were super useful, he was always willing to go over concepts and any questions I had. Also curves

Tests were hard but gives generous curves. Really passionate in teaching and always ask us for any questions. Tests aligned with HW, but best to study with any resources (textbook sucks). His in-person notes and online notes are different so best to go to lecture to get better understanding. Highly recommend if you want to learn.

THIS COURSE IS NOT HARD. He just makes it hard since you can't understand him through his accent. The material is not bad, its just the midterms give you questions that you have not seen before or are much harder than the discussion problems. He curves a half-grade at the end.
reading the textbook def helps after lecture + doing practice problems, but generally working thru the hw helps a lot and exams r like the hw

Heavy, heavy accent. it's clear that it's this professor's first time teaching. Prepare to do a lot of self studying. Lectures is just him reading off the note. It is very clear that this is his first time teaching a college course.
He has a pretty thick accent and is tough to understand at times.
He is very unclear when it comes to explaining and is a pain, I ended up watching the podcasts of another instructor.
He is a nice guy though, but needs a lot more experience to teach a course like this.

He's a very nice professor, but his lectures are not easy to understand. He kind of rushes through some things and is not the clearest explainer. The discussions are attendance mandatory and help tons, and so does doing all the homework. The midterms were fine, the final exam was not!! But other than that I think its a manageable class

He's so chill. Just show up to class, chat the readings, and make sure you raise your hands a few times throughout the quarter and you're getting an A. There's one group project which is pretty easy. If you care (or even act like it), he will be nice to you and give you a good grade!

he's never punctual, frequently cancels class or makes it online last minute, constantly goes outside in the middle of lecture to make phone calls, travels for business in the middle of the quarter and cancels class for a week straight, goes on unrelated tangents, unresponsive to emails. the class is really easy but he's unbelievably disorganized.

Never had a more unprofessional prof. Some may see lack of punctuality as carefree, it feels more like he doesn't care. Always 10 min late (even on Zoom) goes past time, slides limited, midterm vague. Frequently leaves for important business during class. 2 assignments for entire quarter. Asks students about midterm while others are taking it.
Lecture-heavy but what he says is very insightful and interesting. Very easy-going.

ANTH 1:His readings were interesting-they were long,but they got you engaged with good information.He is the calmest and most caring teacher ever. I feel like I should drop down and bow to him every time his presence graces the room.He is funny and holds great class discussions,along with lecture slides that are good information to take notes on.

Professor Jemc was great! She was really passionate about writing, and took a lot of extra time to read our stories. You can tell she genuinely likes to help students with their work. Highly recommend this class!

Professor Jemc is a great lecturer and is super knowledgeable about fiction writing! The course is generally fun and easy, but there are some time-consuming aspects. A lot of the readings are quite long (20-30 avg.), and it takes a lot of time to provide feedback to your section's workshop stories. Otherwise, I highly recommend this prof!

Took LTWR 8C and LTWR 106. She's the only lit workshop professor I actually learn craft elements from, her lectures are useful and she doesn't dwell overlong in obvious stuff. Gives lots of practical tips rather than the theoretical stuff
Really nice and understanding person, too, and accommodating when I have covid

She was really disengaged and negligent towards her student's writing. Asked everybody to turn in stories for her to revise, and feedback was just stuff like, "ok. nice." Really uninspiring. Really easy to pass though, if you turn in the assignments on time.

You learn pretty much nothing in this class. General physics is more necessary and this course is mainly plug and chug. Also he denies his RMP rating... Cap

Chill with grades (+ lot of EC). Everyone has an A, yet you don't learn much. As long as you know how to use the formulas you're good. Guest speakers are interesting people, idk why people complain about them; its just an intro class. The bad: he doesn't care about the class much, is often late, skims through slides, and doesn't put effort.

Very unmotivated professor that puts his students second since he's always busy. Often gets to class late and speeds through the slides expecting you to know what he's talking about. Despite the extra credit for things like Halloween dress ups, HW are often hard to understand and does not give extensions. Lectures are Hybrid though so its flexible.

I LOVE KURLE!!! i hate science but this was literally the most breezy class because every quiz and test was open EVERYTHING. lectures mandatory but you can miss a lot and also show up at pretty much any time to get the attendance. you can just tell she's an amazing person and loves to answers anyone's questions.
She's an awesome teacher. The class is really easy, most assessments are online. You'll do good if you go to lectures. Lectures are mostly mandatory.
She was amazing. Her tests were all online and they were on the readings and lectures so they weren't that difficult. She was really nice and I loved having her.
She was such a kind professor and the class was super easy!

Great Professor who stepped in last minute for our class. Quizzes and exams are online and open note, (open anything basically) with no homework and an extra credit paper. She truly cares about students just make sure to attend enough lectures for full attendance credit and take good notes. Discussion attendance was also not mandatory.

Found no problems with her besides her teaching going a little fast during lectures! Not the most engaging but went over material concisely; as long as you pay attention you'll be fine. A lot of material to keep up with, but the homework and weekly quizzes (which are very & not worth many points) helps! Extra credit was rly easy too.

Larssen was great, could tell she really enjoys teaching and talking about Public Health. She was so good she convinced me to switch my major to PH! The class was not easy but it was doable if you kept up with the lectures and took notes on your own to memorize key words and definitions. The group project was not hard either.

Not the most interesting lectures, but they're ok. 1 midterm + 1 final, both asynchronous and the questions are fair. Grade mainly consists of 4 homework and 4 reflection assignments that are easy. Do them on time and you'll be fine. Weekly quizzes on lecture material, but they're only worth 2 points each so it won't kill you if you miss a few.

This class was very fair. Watching the lectures are really important for doing well on quizzes and exams. Professor Larsen was very caring and understanding and she gave a few extra credit assignments to boost our grades. If you keep up with the lectures and stay on top of homework you'll be completely fine. The class is really interesting too!
She really explains the material well and keeps class interesting. Not the easiest class, but I really learned a lot. I would absolutely take another class from her. Also very pretty :)

Paul is the best professor for a class like this. Fair grading, is accessible via email or office hours, and always friendly with students who put work in. Strongly recommend reading spending at least 45 minutes on each reading to get the most out of the class. Relevant to any kind of organisation or policy work + academic research.

Paul is the toughest grader I've come across. He does not provide second attempts in his reading classes nor provides the answers after the first attempt. He's incredibly smart, maybe too smart for me to keep up with. He's heavy in group participation. You'll have to dedicate a lot of hours to the assignments, including a 20 page paper.
Lectures are fine, but has horrible test making/TA grading. Mean on the final was 55% Don't take him if you want to apply what you know on the final.

Niehaus is the nicest professor ever!! He really knows his stuff and tries to keep lecture interesting.  INTL190 will always be a drag, but he is helpful and super sympathetic about the stupid paper.  We had weekly reading quizzes which were not bad, a 10-minute presentation and the dreaded 20-page paper.  Wouldn't have wanted another prof!

Really easy class. Just read the textbook, go to his lectures, and you'll be almost guaranteed at least a B. He's also very helpful during his office hours, and makes the class very interesting. He definitely knows his stuff!

attendance wasn't mandatory persay but encouraged bc they would talk about projects & provide other artists for inspiration and guidance to projects. ab 4-5 photo projects w 2 mini photo exercises. critique was very thorough (more technical rather than artistically) and encouraging. helps if class participates good grade based on completion mostly
Deanna is hilarious! The class itself requires a LOT of work in the lab etc., but the lectures are fun and interesting. Would definitely recommend this professor!
!!!!!! i looked forward to this class every week. i wish there were more teachers like her!!!!

THE BEST PROFESSOR AT UCSD. She'll have you cracking up the entire class period, but you'll still walk away feeling like you've learned a lot. She's an amazing photographer and an amazing teacher.
