she is awesome. extremely helpful and very entertaining. she switches between photo history and photoshop use for a well-rounded class.  she is a very good teacher (a skill more professors should have!) and you should definitely take her class if given the opportunity.

this is more of a comment on the course design - prof rose is very kind and responsive to student needs, but the first three to four weeks are wasted on the project file / assignments. i think the film watch assignments and project file stuff / film pitches can be completed in weeks 1-2. discussions are not useful.
This guy is awesome! Highly recommend, he actually cares and is very knowledgeable.

I LOVE THIS PROF! Always understanding, so fun to talk to and has such an interesting background/experience. He cares about every student and always wants to hear our thoughts. If you have the option, take him. I hope to take him again for SYN 100 :)

The lectures were very confusing and exams did not match level of lecture material. There are three exams, only your top score is kept, and it is worth 60% of your grade. This sounds great except the exams were very difficult. Overall I didn't feel I learned much, but I was stressed about this class constantly.

Only 4 exams, BUT your TOTAL exam grade is based on your HIGHEST exam score, you could theoretically bomb 3/4 exams, but if you get an A in one, you have an A in exam scores. Lectures ONLY, so you have to attend class with/ attendance, but pretty interesting. She's very sweet & I loved her. Exams are kinda weird to study for, but def managable

Strictest prof for SYN1. Course content is boring and it's likely the professor is aware of this + lots of little assignments that aren't useful for the papers you write and mostly grunt work. Email him if you need to miss class or an assignment. Does however, give thoughtful feedback, and appreciates quality work.

Def manageable, ppl expected the study guide to be EXACTLY like the exams, which is unrealistic. Her exams were definitely fair, & she let us bring in ALOT of cheat sheets. She has a thick accent, but u can 100% understand. She often skips over things so be vocal in class, many people had to ask her to clarify, which she happily apologized for. W24

Lectures could be confusing at times. Exams were pretty okay with a lot of practice problems with crib sheet. HW was online and had unlimited attempts. Overall as long as you understand Calc 1&2 you'll be fine.

practice exams were nothing like actual exams, lectures didn't help, and homework was also difficult. only good thing is the grading scale was curved. i still passed. i just didn't have great time in her class as much as others did

She was actually such a chill and great professor! Both lectures and discussions were optional which was super nice! The midterms and final were also pretty similar to the practice problems she posted. She also allowed us to have one cheat sheet (front and back) for each midterm and two cheat sheets for the final. Overall amazing and easy class!!

She is actually a really good prof! Notes are a bit hard to follow along sometimes but textbook helps a lot w that. If you have a decent understanding of math concepts ull be fine. I was confused on how she grades bc she doesnt curve but shell giv points if u get numbers wrong but concepts right thankfully. Take her!!

Prof Tran was my first ever professor at UCSD, he's amazing, his lectures are extremely easy to understand. He explains everything very well and his exams really aren't that hard if you study well enough. I highly recommend taking him.

*Took Math 18, not 20C. 18 isn't on the list here. *

Great professor. Very chill, really cares about every student and tries to do whatever he can to fit everyone's needs. Never felt like he had any intentions to make the course purposedly more difficult to pass.
Definitely one of the best professors I've taken.
very chill! would take again

Took this class online but it was a good class as my first math-college based course. Found his lectures to be straightforward to which I was able to understand every topic very well. Seemed like he cared about teaching and cared about the students who took his class. So far, one of the better math profs I've had. Definitely take him.
The way he taught the materials is very understandable. Also, the tests are strongly relevant to the course materials and the homework. Overall, he is a great math professor!
One of the best professors I've had at UCSD! Even though it's a once a week 5:00–7:50 PM class, it's so fun, and I always look forward to going. She is seriously the best—couldn't recommend her more!

Had DrRo for HDS122 and now 150. 150's topic changes every quarter, but DrRo is very passionate about her 150 topic. There is a lot of required reading and the class is conversation/group heavy (but in a very relaxed setting!). DrRo is really understanding, caring, and gives really good feedback!

This class revolves around group work (80% of your grade) so if you hate group work, don't take this class. Material is easy, professor is nice, it just wasn't my favorite class since I'm not a fan of group work.

Dr. Rodriguez is a solid choice for this class! I thought the material was very interesting and she did a good job of presenting the material and making it clear. Her syllabus was a bit confusing though. This class is mainly group work with a small assignments, a presentation, and a paper. There is a midterm and weekly discussion posts.

Dr. Rodriguez is very nice and understanding. But if you are not a fan of group projects/work, do not take this class. The whole class revolves around a group project. Assignments basically consist of a 5-page midterm paper, a 10-page group paper/project, and two 2-page reflection papers. Not too hard, but depends on your group.

Professor Welchman is the hardest professor I have had but also the smartest. He clearly knows his stuff and really wants his students to succeed. He assigned us weekly group presentations, and some group members were less than ideal. I very much respect the way he teaches, and I learned a lot, but it was a very difficult course so be warned.

everyone complains/cries about welchman's vis112 class, but i got a B and so you can too! 
tips: get you books early bc assigned group projects start immediately....next tip is when presenting (you will do group presentations at every class session) don't volunteer ton go first for the love of god! thank me later, bc time usually runs out!!!!

Great professor, I appreciate how he tries not to dumb down intricate theories and thereby preserves their nuance and complexity. Also one of the few professors who is actually funny, although I don't think many of his jokes land with the class.

Class: Art Criticism. You will have to read a lot of very hard to analyze essays in this class. Essays you have to dissect  sentence by sentence. Good thing is that the professor is very patient in answering questions and clarifying any topic. Grading was based on two essays that you turn in typed. He can view your draft during office hours.

Lots of reading, even when divided into groups.. goes the entire 3 hours and the class is mostly him talking. occasionally he'll try and get input from students and will put some on the spot. Two writing assignments, not particularly difficult but just plain confusing/with no structured prompt or anything. Would not recommend if it came down to it.

He was a super great prof who actually cared about what he was teaching, and he took the time to teach us the topics in detail. Attendance wasn't mandatory for lectures, and there really wasn't that much homework at all. Midterms were comprehensive but there was tons of extra credit. His office hours were helpful too!

Great lectures with clear examples to help understand concepts. Exam questions are similar to practice tests and weekly quizzes (you get two quizzes dropped). Lots of extra credit on exams. The workload for the class is low as long as you keep up with lectures, although attendance is not mandatory. Nice guy who's always willing to answer questions.
midterms are straightforward and exactly like the practice midterms. great prof who cares about students!

super chill professor and great lectures + slides. he includes lots of current research/breakthroughs in the lectures to make it more interesting. very straightforward quizzes, midterms, and finals. also does tons of extra credit questions on tests so you can definitely get a 100% on the class if you study!

Grades based on two midterms and a final and DI attendance. Tests EXTREMELY hard. LONG lectures. Professor seems to be really specific on the words and explains concepts in details, but like the other comment, his words sound exactly like what's written on textbook (word-to-word). Section averages around 2 (one is less than 2), but still no curve.

Pengtao Xie is genuinely one of the greatest professors I have ever had. I am a Senior at UCSD in Electrical Engineering and I have attended 2 different universities. His lectures are so interesting and well structured. He is a fantastic lecturer and extremely knowledgeable. I would take any and every class he teaches. Highly recommend taking him!

Professor Xie cares about his students very much and is always open to discussions if you have difficulties. Professor Xie gives a reasonable amount of workload but the programming assignments (PAs) are a little challenging yet manageable. You can also choose to do a group project over PAs. For the exams, just do the practice exams and you're good.
Professor Xie is patient and willing to answer any questions. He is flexible and kind in adjusting deadlines. One  suggestion: try to cover more intuition behind theorems.
professor is very nice and took many feedback from students. grace days are given to accommodate students' schedule. applications (dpp, gaussian processes) covered in lectures are very interesting.

A student-friendly instructor. He is very knowledgable in linear algebra. Can see that he puts a lot of efforts in preparing for lectures. I especially like the live derivation of proofs. Programming assignments helped me a lot in understanding the practical applications of linear algebra.

Took her for the "Tropical Disease" class. Love her, she's such a great lecturer. She also has supplemental lectures that she records, which are great when going for a walk to go over the readings. It's a lot of reading, but you don't need to read all of them to do well. I got an A+ due to the extra credit she gave at the end. Certified mother.

Literally just take the class if you guys are wondering if you should. She is the easiest history teacher you will find and she is so nice. It's clear that she cares about her students and literally she barely gives out any homework. There are group discussions but they're so easy. Take it, its such easy credit!!

"woke"? lmao that comment makes me mad oml. bro doesnt know the meaning of the word. This class is so eye opening, the prof is very passionate and amazing at lecturing, this class talks a lot about decolonization and provides a lot of different perspectives through different mediums to really communicate how decolonization has shaped society. 10/10

interesting and super well rounded class, not very woke, no tests but there are some well paced projects. You can tell Prof Edington puts a lot of effort into this class, lovely course, lovely professor

I loved this class so much! If you're thinking of taking her class, just do it. She is very engaging when lecturing and sooo easygoing. There isn't a lot of homework AT ALL, the main thing she has students do is read the material before she presents it in class. Even if you don't read it, it's still clear to understand when she's teaching it later.

Xu laoshi is the best! She makes everyone feel super welcomed and she explains everything really clearly. She's also really easy to reach through office hours and is super approachable. Your grade pretty much depends on the midterm and final, but the tests aren't hard as long as you can remember the characters. Overall 10/10, I love her!

Very nice professor. Most of the content is covered within the textbook and her lecture slides, which are all posted. Typically a small class, but she puts in a lot of effort to help and support students. Has a lot of time for one-on-one office hours and Zoom. Her commitment is great as she does Zoom meetings even when she's sick. Learned a lot.

Had her for the whole first year of Mandarin. The class is a big time commitment (but that just comes with learning a new language). Teacher is super nice and supportive! She made me feel very welcomed and I had a blast learning a new language! She's very easy to reach outside of class for office hours or any questions.

Very nice person, just be aware that attendance is mandatory and homework is graded relatively harshly--although it is infrequent. Also, your final grade will almost entirely depend on how well you do on the two tests. It was hard for me but I'm also not great at mandarin, plenty of people in my classes went through with little issue.
not a fan

On days she's not reading PowerPoint slides to us like a picture book, she's giving out pop quizzes consisting of hand picked questions from a 20 year old question bank. If she's present during office hours, she'll refer us to a TA and go back to scrolling TikTok. Best to take a different 194 course.
The class was great. She really helped us with the presentations even though we were struggling with the reading initially. Was so sweet and caring. The content was also great.

She cares about student and really expect a lot of skills of giving a presentation. I really dont recommend international students take this class because she seems expect more engaged presentation international students. (What she used to be)

Professor Jin is my favorite professor. She teaches students how to break down complex, mechanistic papers and presents cutting-edge research (Expect to read a long, dense paper each week). Grading is based on participation, so if you put in the work, you will get an A. I would highly recommend if you are interested in going beyond your textbook.

Only had her in a seminar. Seems like a very nice lady and willing to help. The information she provide is very interesting and her research topics are very interesting as well. Overall a very kind and nice professor, would definitely take her again in another class
Anisa is the best! She cares about her students and clearly loves teaching. I would take her for every class if I could. If you have a chance to take her class, consider yourself lucky!
My favorite ASL professor at UCSD so far! She signs quickly but it pushes you to get better at comprehension. Activities were very engaging and helped me learn a lot

Professor Silva gives AMAZING feedback. I never regretted going to any of her office hours. She is incredibly helpful, and if you're stuck, she'll help you improve. She was very passionate about the topic (centering Indigenous voices) and made MCWP endurable.

MCWP 50 is a difficult class but Dr. Silva gave her students a lot of support. Comparable to my suitemates, it seems as though she does not grade nearly as hard. She is understanding of situations and willing to work through your personal circumstances if necessary. Though that the topic for her MCWP 50 class is difficult to write about.
Dr. Silva was definitely a hard professor but I enjoyed her theme. If you follow the rubric you should be fine and if I got an A-, you can definitely pass her class.

I would reccomend against her tbh. She wouldn't give very good critiques and then would grade very harshly. She basically told me that my thesis for paper 3 was good but it needed to be more specific, and then when grading the final draft, said my thesis was too similar to the authors. Idk, she's not mean but she is a tough grader.

She was very clear and helpful during class time. I was not a good writer in my opinion at all, but I put lots of time into this class and my writing. This doesn't mean I just went to office hours, admittedly I only went to one. However, Professor Silva was extremely helpful at that time and helped me organize my thoughts.

Come to lectures even if they aren't mandatory, he puts on an amazing show that is equal parts entertaining and educational. Start the assignments early and ask for help since Haskell/functional programing takes a bit of time to get used to. Fair autograder given for the homeworks. The exams are tough (learn monads!!!!) but basically just lectures.
Worst professor ever. Don't know how to teach. Even get an A but still have no idea how Compiler works.

The lecture does not seem well organized and sometimes he speaks too fast and it is difficult to catch up. He seems to enjoy debugging during the lectures. And the homework is much harder than what is taught by him.
So many many many typos in his slides, websites and other materials, even in the code and mathematical formula! Copy other school's homework, spend a lot of time on solving compile error......

Jhala seems befuddled and unsure in lectures; I never really knew how much was for show. Concepts in class are easy; homework is hard and you have to teach yourself how to solve, unlike Java/C/C++, resources for learning Haskell are limited. Some material on take-home final was never covered  at all. He's mildly funny and fairly approachable.

Lectures can be non-engaging and quiet. There is a lot of information to digest at once, almost too much. Grades are reliant on online homework and exams. Exams were difficult, as information was so broad. The teacher is kind, but soft spoken and non-engaging. Also, be ready for a hefty cost, the website for the textbook/homework costs $200.

Prof Huang was a good teacher and included many example problems relevant for the lectures and what'd be on the test. Though I'm not a STEM major and don't particularly enjoy chem,she gave us every possible resource to do well and whether you took advantage of them or not is up to you. Graded weekly HW, midterm, final, and attendance on discussions

Sweet Professor who genuinely cares if you understand and is always open to helping.Has bad rep because chemistry is just a difficult topic to learn but she does a good job w/ asking if people understand. Lecture not mandatory but not recorded. Required to buy the site in order to do homework. One chapter homework per week.

I really like this professor, she is very sweet. Lectures can be fun when you understand what is going on, but towards the continuing chapters the work starts to get a bit tough. Homework is honestly not too hard, she gives you almost a week to complete it.

My initial thought for taking Chem 11 is that it is for those in a non-science major, but it was just as difficult as taking the Chem 6 series. She seemed like a sweet person, however, her teaching style was just reading off slides. I have asked her if she can record the lectures but she specifically said this course is meant not to be recorded.

Have fun with a professor who teaches an introduction to business law class like you are at Harvard. She provides barely any information in lectures, then expects you to know everything she DIDN'T cover. Midterm is a sham. She fails to provide detailed instructions and then docks you for not following the instructions she never gave. DO NOT TAKE!

If you are interested in pursuing law, I HIGHLY recommend taking one of Professor Nichter's classes. I was lucky enough to take her legal reasoning course. She taught us how to thoroughly analyze cases via the IRAC method and write legal memos, client advice letters, and demand letters. TA's may strictly grade though and write minimal feedback.

104U was one of my favorite classes. The midterm paper is released the same day it is due, and if you pay attention, it's very doable and straightforward. The final is a seven-page max paper assigned the night before. Taker her class! It seems intimidating at first, but she makes it easily accessible, and her lectures are very helpful.

I took her for both 104J and 104U this winter quarter.104J is writing-heavy with three papers, one being six pages, another being four, and the final being six pages (released the day before it's due). The papers were time-consuming and tedious, but if you pay attention, you will be fine. Take her class; she's an amazing professor and so helpful.

Great class with a great professor. Only thing to note is that final paper is 5-6 pages and is released the day before it's due, so you don't get very much time to work on it. Other assignments are usually done in class throughout the week they're due which is helpful+there's very clear instructions with rubrics for each assignment
He was so great and amazing. Unfortunately he is no longer teaching at UCSD. He spoke very fast and always let us out earlier. All around very kind and an enjoyable class to take.

Professor Day is a great professor! His class is very fair and grades are based on quizzes, exams, and discussion/lecture attendance. As long as you go to class and write down a couple of notes/pay attention to what he's saying, you'll get A's on all of his assignments. Definitely recommend him and he is super nice and concise.

Dr. Day is one of the sweetest professors at UCSD. His lectures are really chill and engaging. Attendance for lecture and discussion is mandatory. Multiple quizzes and a midterm but it's easy. 100% recommend!

Such a sweet professor. He tries to make the class enjoyable and easy, lots of listening to music pieces in class. Frequent quizzes and one midterm and final but all are online/open-note. Keeps lectures short so even though Tue/Th classes are 1h20, he usually dismisses class within the first hour. Randomly takes attendance

Very knowledgable professor when it comes to music! The course was engaging and very interesting. You are only graded on attendance and quizzes/exams but they are online and very straightforward. He is such a kind professor and is very passionate about what he does.

Dr. Kiyonaga was pretty cool, and she created a fairly easy class format. Lectures were all extra credit, discussions were not mandatory and you could get extra credit for working with other people, and tests were take home. Because the tests were take home, they were a little harder but nothing to complain about. I think I got a B on every test.

attendance not mandatory but EC is given if attended, weekly quizzes + section assignments. all quizzes + midterms are based on guest speakers' lecture so pay attention. quizzes are open note and collaborative. no "final", it was just a third midterm & not cumulative. Midterms are weighed 10/20/30%, 10% being ur worst score.

Had a different guest lecturer every lecture. The tests were based on what these guest lecturers said. So u needed to memorize every word they said to do well on the tests. Totally killed my interest in the course material because I couldn't just pay attention to what the lecturer was saying, I was too busy furiously typing everything they said.

Class is based on a lot of group work. We had to work with the same group all quarter. Wednesday lab time was spent doing group labs and Fridays were journal clubs (where we had to discuss articles with our groups). There was a group presentation at the end of the quarter. Lectures were interesting, but I wish more time was spent on them.

The class involves multiple guest speakers within the cog sci department, weekly quizzes and DI activities, 3 tests total that are weighted 30/20/10 = 60% and are based on performance. overall a really easy and interesting class

Professor Compas is wonderful! He is super caring, as he understands students' situations and is negotiable. I had no confidence and was panicking about my college writing at the beginning, and he was very willing to help when I went to his office hours, giving me really helpful feedback. I also took MCWP 50 with him, highly recommended!

Professor Compas created a very welcoming environment. He was great at teaching students how to properly write in his lectures, but his advice on the graded papers was too surfaced-level, making it difficult to improve for future papers. However, the assignments are easy, and as long as the paper is well-structured, his grading isn't too harsh.

Professor Compas is a wonderful professor. Although MCWP is a difficult course, he made it much more manageable by being clear about his expectations, having a generous amount of flexibility to make assignments easier, and generally having a very caring and kind demeanor. He truly cares about his students' success, which made the class enjoyable.

Professor Sean Compas was an amazing professor. Although his lectures are mandatory, they were really fun and interactive. I would recommend taking this professor if you see his class open as he is one of the more easy going professors.

Professor Compas is a very good professor. MCWP classes are heavy workload regardless on who your professor is. He is very welcoming and is easy to access outside of class. I will say however, if you like structure he might not be the professor for you.

(RATING FOR CAT124) - Great professor, however the grading scale for this class specfically is based on a cumulative grade from other people in sixth college that help him teach the class, and they are immensely unqualified and the feedback on projects is very vague and changes day to day. Hope that he picks better support staff in the future.

CAT90 is an Experiential Learning seminar for Sixth GEs. The class was way more helpful than I thought would be and totally set me on a good path for finding internships/careers using the experiences I've had in college. Professor was super nice and friendly, we started every class talking about personal wins we had each week! I def recommend!

Professor Geibel is one of the best CAT125 professors out there! He cares deeply for his students and is always engaging during the class. Keep up with the weekly readings before class to get ready for discussion. Would highly recommend him for this class.

Professor Geibel is a solid choice as a professor and gives a well-outlined agenda on what is required from us. The lecture was laid back and he was more than happy to answer questions about the material. The only downside was it was a communication class so a lot of the meetings felt unnecessary and skippable. Mandatory SI participation for 10%.

He made his own slides, the materials are useful. The slides are super handy and easy to read. He teach concepts in a great way to make students understand. He is kind and caring about students. He is kind of for sure he treat every students with respect. Go to class or you going to miss some good lectures. he is one of the best in UCSD
I'm not sure he was speaking English or not... I cannot understand anything during class. But, it was the class easy to pass.

Heavy accent makes classes difficult to understand. Depending on the slides won't help since they are not reliable in terms of the content or the formulae. Take-home midterm and end-term were probably the only relief in this course.

Nongraded homework with solutions posted, and entire grade is based on takehome midterm and takehome final. Pretty heavy accent and soft spoken, so paying attention is important. Lecture slides are great, but you need his lectures to clarify what they mean. Pretty good overall, for grad classes at least.

It was hard keeping up in this class. the slides she reads from are really just photos and so we have to take notes based on what she says, which is hard to do. She also whispers which can get a bit hard to understand. The midterm was a bit annoying you have to write essays. Group projects every week those were easy.
The courseworks provides you all you need to know to start a career in Machine Learning

This so-called "mandatory" course is an unnecessary expense forced on students. I would actively warn my family, friends, and even random strangers not to apply to Rady MSBA. The professor openly said in class that he did NOT care about student complaints just because the course is mandatory. That kind of attitude is incredibly unprofessional.
This class might be the point where I finally start to understand machine learning and enjoy programming.
Have a difficult in phrasing his hw.
I learned nothing from him, and during the final exam, he changed the instructions at the very last minute.

Kate lacks the teaching skills needed for this role. Class time was spent on long, irrelevant personal stories instead of course content. The syllabus lacked clarity, grading was rigid, and feedback was minimal. Even thoughtful, relevant questions could hurt your grade. Not a good fit for this expensive, rigorous program-disappointing.

Kate does not support or teach students well. Justifies poor organization, bad instruction, & tough grading by saying it's what students can expect in their careers. Wastes time providing crappy advice. She is more interested in tradition than adaptability, which most modern employers prefer. No accountability. Don't waste your time confronting it.
i didnt understand
Tough.

Ms. Wilkins is a great instructor, I had her for two classes and I enjoy having her as my instructor. Her lectures are very interesting, and she uses good examples to make the students understand the subject. She gives you feedback regarding assignments, and she will always have a smile in her face.

Easiest A ever (look at the other comments). He is not very good at explaining things though. If you want to learn then you absolutely have to teach yourself almost everything. He kind of just expects you to know many things and understand things that he goes over very fast and shortly

Incredibly easy: 5 HW's (~0-4 hours each) and a take-home midterm (24 hour window). Interesting lectures but not the best at explaining things. If you want to really want to learn ML in depth, you'll have to do it yourself.

Lectures are very boring and difficult to understand. Concepts are complex but homeworks are easy. Midterm was hard, but points were awarded for trying, so it's easy to get a good grade in this class. Not too much work overall. Professor is nice but his explanations make things harder than they need to be.

The easiest CS class you will ever take. 5 homeworks (he drops 1) worth 15 percent each and a midterm worth 40 percent each. He allows and encourages us to use Chat GPT on everything we just have to cite it. No final at all which is amazing. I would say he could get a little better at teaching though. He expects us to just understand everything.

He is a brilliant professor who brings machine learning to life with real-world examples and engaging lectures. Her dedication to student understanding and success is unparalleled, offering clear explanations and supportive guidance. Highly recommend her classes for an inspiring and practical learning journey.
Forces liberal political views on students, tests are overly difficult.

I didn't show up to a single lecture after Midterm #1. Class is 2 Midterms, 1 Final, and 3 Assignments. Attendance is “mandatory” at lectures but it was a Google Form. His lectures are boring and hard to keep up with and his slides are bad. As long as you know the concepts, *connections*, and examples, you will easily pass. ASK YOUR TA FOR HELP!

He was on pace to be the worst professor I ever had at UCSD after the first midterm, didn't give out any study guide or anything to get us prepeared. But as the course went on, Professor deWaard and his TAs did a way better job at explaining assignments and addressing what is going to be on the exams. Would definitely take his class again.

I thought this class was great and the lectures were very interesting. You can tell he puts a lot of effort into his slides. I didn't receive the highest grade in the class but that was simply a reflection of my own effort. My guess is the other negative reviews were just looking for an easy A and didn't get it.

Very difficult class as an international student. TA does not help and does not provide a study guide because "that is not his teaching style" The professor uses meaningless and difficult readings to trick students and does not make things clear on the exams.

He's very passionate about the lectures he teaches. Sure, he might go off topic sometimes, but he is very informative on the eras/topics surrounding technology's involvement in art. There are weekly readings which are sometimes confusing, but his lectures will make it so much easier to understand, so make sure to show up to them!
annoying boring nextttt

A chill professor for digital art. Enjoyed majority of his lectures about digital art & media, opened my eyes to explore more mediums of digital art. Requires critical reflections weekly, ranges from easy to difficult, but provides good feedback. 2 projects, and a 2-part final presentation (draft & presentation), interesting and fun to complete.

Interesting professor. Very chill and fun professor. His class was good, with lectures and critical summary reflections on articles relating to art, opened my horizon on digital art to different styles that I didn't know existed. Projects were interesting as well, and not too difficult. Does take a while to grade assignments however.

Very funny and nice, but I did not like his class. 3 hour lectures with no breaks, weekly readings that are really hard to understand (highly academic language about hyper specific art fields) with "reflections" but they're just summaries of the reading in MLA format. No tests, 3 small projects. I expected more activities or creative engagement.

This was supposed to be an introductionary class but she does not make it like so. We had to read and completely understand multiple research paper about in depth highly technical topics. This class was supposed to make us more interested with renewable energy but it completely extinguished mine. She needs to reevaluate her whole syllabus.ww

Professor Gonzalez is very sweet at the beginning. However, as soon at the MATLAB projects and midterm comes around, that changes. MATLAB projects are ridiculously challenging (coming from an MechE who grew up doing CS). She single handedly killed any passion I had for renewable energy. Stay away from this class.

This professor just skims through the slides and does limited examples. He needs to improve on his ability to talk to people as he is very awkward and yawns at every moment the class went quiet. He needs to get better at explaining things in a simple way as well. He over complicates everything and teaches content we don't need to know.
He speeds through all of the material without really covering it. He never notices when people are actively trying to ask question. Overall I felt like the class was just unnecessarily difficult.

This professor should not be teaching CHEM 122. He is very smart but does not know how to bring things down to a lower level of knowledge. HE WAS THE WORST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD! It was extremely difficult to understand his lectures and everyone in the class just stopped going and showed up for the exams.
Very great professor. I was initially worried about his exams being cumulative, but it ended up saving my grade: bringing things from a B- to a full A.

Puts the students first. Tests are based on HW. Very generous grader. Good grasp of the material. Young and upcoming professor, so he learned with us. Knows how to teach well and will always answer questions. Really easy final exam (did it while eating breakfast). Take him if you have the chance.

overall, he is really generous on curves at the end of the quarter. but the lectuer material was very hand-wavy solutions, fast, and hard to comprehend. He is funny and likeable, but i just felt like i didnt learn much in his class personally.

Board work was clear and comprehensive, never skips any steps in derivation process. 
Course revolves around doing homework, which is assigned weekly and not too difficult if you pay attention in class.
Overall, a passionate professor who knows what he's doing and a great course. Highly recommend.
I hope you can write fast because he lectures fast.
He was very unclear and speaks too fast.
Great Professor
Does not care about students at all. Impossible to reach and does not respond to emails. He only cares about his research and lording his power over his grad students and undergrads.

I am giving figueroa in particular a 5 - he is a great, funny, caring prof. 43A, however, is completely designed and run by klosterman, who is not the best. The grading is very harsh and nebulous, and the actual class itself doesn't teach you that much about how to work in an ochem lab. A lot of the grading is focused on super nitpicky points

He's really here just for research. His postlab rubrics are ridiculously vague and sad. He preaches fairness but does not normalize TA grading? Its clear he does NOT care if students learn cuz his final was a copy-paste of OWL quizzes. Final was an easy A, but just very disappointing for students who want/need to learn. I hope he stops teaching.

Prof. Figueroa genuinely cares about his students. Clearly, the whole reason he asks questions back to students during lecture time is to get them to critically thing about material being discussed in reports. He is enthusiastic and wants students to understand material conceptually- he wont just give you the answers.

His lectures are pointless. I stopped coming after watching him try to humiliate students during class. The lab is piled high with useless busy work. Office hours are inflexible, no help with assignments and TAs won't make office hours. Postlab questions are vague and grading is completely based on similarity to his arbitrary answer key.

Professor Brady's class was amazing every day with so many cool examples of what our mind does and how it tricks us. Tests are challenging because they make you apply the concept to new experiments or situations, but were fair.

Really loved this class, you can tell Brady cares about what he is teaching. Lectures are easy to follow and he gives lots of examples for things that will be on exams. Make sure to attend lecture or watch podcasts for sure. Exams are difficult but not impossible if you study!

Professor Brady is an amazing inspiring lecturer with so much passion for cognitive psychology that it makes me want to be a cognitive psychologist. The class has all sorts of mind blowing examples every day and he's very clear about what's on the test. The exams make you apply the concepts and predict new experiments so be ready for that.

Tim is the best professor I have ever had. For the first time, I truly loved going to school. Every lecture had fun experiments. I truly feel like I learned. I barely had to study because I ACTUALLY retained the info. Professor, if you're reading this, you're an inspiration & your students & daughters are so lucky to have a role model like you.
Love Professor Brady! His lectures are always so interesting and engaging. 10/10 would recommend his class

Professor Alon is the best professor in the department for core economic theory. His lectures are organised. Review sessions for the exams are immensely helpful for structuring your answers to the exams. I would recommend learning how to derive the steady state and growth rates through office hours directly. Speak up in class, you'll learn a lot.

Great Prof, very passionate about the topics he is teaching and encourages questions and discussions during class. Lectures can move at a fast pace but often end early so you can ask for clarification. Graded mainly on the midterm and final but there will be generous curves for both.

Probably one of the best economics professors I've ever had. Lectures are not podcasted so would recommend going but they are perfect study resources for the exams. Midterm review sessions are very accurate to testable content, and exam is very doable. He curves the exams by a lot too - would definitely recommend anything he teaches.

Overall the material was pretty difficult for me, however, the way prof presents it makes it worth it. I truly looked forward to attending class to listen to lecture, despite the fact that I absolutely struggled learning the material (at a fault of my own). Prof is genuinely a good person and most important, PASSIONATE about what he teaches.
Ex Bridgewater guy, by far the best prof in the entire Econ department. If you have any interest in markets, take prof Alon

Dr. Hollander is a great lecturer and teaches passionately. He is definitely a tough grader, but tests are pretty straightforward if you take good class notes and study. There are required readings everyday and frequent pop quizzes. The only downside is that he sometimes is misleading with his pop quizzes and which readings they cover.
Was a good class, and Professor had a great understanding of the content.

This class was a bit scatter-brained at times, students were unsure of expectations and professor provided plenty of criticisms--both warranted and unwarranted. Not the best class I have taken at Wabash. Dr. Hollander is a good professor, and when he lectures in his survey courses he is good, but I left this class unimpressed.

Professor Hollander did a great job with political science 122 at Wabash College.  The information was absolutely crystal clear, helped by real world examples, class interaction, and just overall good teaching.

Dr. Hollander did a great job teaching our Comparative Politics class at Wabash College. I had no problem understand what he was trying to convey to the class as he is very thorough in his explanations. I would highly recommend any student to take one of his courses if you would like to be enlightened about the world of Political Science.

While the lectures were pretty interesting, they also pack in a lot of info. Be prepared for some reading. It's great that we get to pick our own final paper topic and give a presentation before its due at the end the term. And the best part is Prof F! She is truly kind, caring, and listens to all our different points of view...really learned a lot

A good professor, unless you do your project area in something she's knowledgeable about. Many people were nitpicked much more during the project planning process than others. Interesting lectures and manageable content, though. The attendance policy is pretty stringent, but you have opportunities to make it up.

boring, but informative lectures. attendance mandatory. lots of reading. present early for final presentation of final paper topic if you want helpful advice - otherwise, you'll be stressed out last minute or need to go to in-person OH.

She was very sweet and caring.Always made sure to let us know that she'd be available to get help,answer questions,or anything else we may need. Lectures could get a bit dragged out but it's because she's clearly so passionate and knowledgeable about many topics. Weekly reflections, few worksheets,midterm, and final research paper of our choosing

Took her for INTL 190, also coded as ANSC 184. Grade was participation, weekly summaries, and final paper. Overall, was very easy to just attend classes, participate in discussions, and choose a research topic to write about. Jana is very caring, sweet, and understanding of her students and wants to help you have fun while also succeeding in class!

Took her at SDSU for PH395. Take her. Super kind, calm, chill, understanding, funny, and a very knowledgeable person about all things PH(shown by her main job); is overall a great person too. Be nice to her because she is super nice to us. 3x 2-3 page writing assignments and 1 final prez, very straightforward. She is goated ++++
My queen, I love her so much. She is the best and very easy going. Felt like I was with my home girl everytime in class, BE NICE TO HER

Professor Miller is the greatest!!! I could not recommend her more. I am a global health minor, yet this is one of my favorite classes. Its very discussion based, so if you talk and engage you will love this class. I would take her again if I had the chance, one of my favorite classes at UCSD

Professor Miller is the best professor I've had at UCSD. She is so caring and understanding of the fact that we are students and often have a lot going on. She is very passionate and knowledgeable about what she teaches and includes lots of interesting personal stories.

It was his first time teaching, he did great. Class was brute memorization but the discussion sessions help make content digestible. 10% of grade is participation which can be earned through lecture/discussion participation (0.5% each event) or 2, 15-min research presentations (5% each). Exams had lots of of buffer points.

Very clear lecturer, explains what parts of mechanisms you need to know, and problem sets are a very clear reflection of the exams. Class is entirely memorization but exams have buffer questions so getting answers wrong can still get you an A. 10% of grade was participation in class or through video recordings, but pretty easy to earn. A nice prof!

The class was distributed between 2 midterms, a final, and 10 part points. 
It was his first time teaching the course and I felt he did amazing, was clear during lectures, often ended early (huge plus)clear study guide, midterms were reflective of the material taught. 
The final was a little tougher, but if you do the study guides you will be fine
Expects students to sink in hundreds of hours to his projects but can't spend 5 minutes checking his emails. Don't rely on this professor for anything.

He changes his code so many times for the MATLAB project. Says that he will stick to the what's given in the write up and then expects us to add an appendix of equations even though it wasn't given in the writeup. His code and writeup often conflict with each other. GOD the worst class I've taken at UCSD.

Professor Kosmatka is one of the best at UCSD, offering great aerospace industry advice and simplifying complex calculations with matrices and MATLAB. The class is challenging but as a visual and math nerd person, it's fair. Also, it matures my engineering intuition. Mastering MAE 30A, MATH 18, and CALC 3 ARE CRUCIAL for success in this course.

"Insanity is doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results."

This perfectly sums up the experience of your MATLAB projects. After running the same MATLAB programs thousands of times and closing thousands of popups over hundreds of hours, I can surely say that this is the most out of touch professor that I've ever had.

The lowest grade I've received is a B+, and I'm calculating the grade I need to even pass this class. His lectures are awful and he goes back and forth on topics, so whether you attend lectures or you don't, your knowledge of materials will remain the same. He assigns HW two days before its due. One good thing: the trauma bond is generational.

WI25 - We only met for discussion section once as she replaced discussion section with two one-on-one meetings with the TA throughout the quarter. Attendance was not mandatory for lecture and Thursdays were workshop days. Writing assignments were graded on only completion except for the final portfolio. Loved her class :D

This was my first workshop class and I overall enjoyed it! It's fun if you like imaginative writing. Professor Hoang is very engaging and clearly passionate about writing. Her feedback can be a little obscure/repetitive and doesn't always consider the limitations within the assignment but TA's are there for further explanation and help!
Weekly assignments and readings & quizzes. No discussions, but weekly workshop meetings with an assigned group instead of lectures

LTWR 8A is a fun class and the professor is enthusiastic about the class. The class is pretty easy as long as you keep up with the work. However, the professor's syllabus is super disorganized, the grading criteria are vague and inconsistent and in general, the only problems is how the class is structured.
Probably the most engaging professor in the Literature department at UCSD
He was always making sure we understood content and really showed that he cared about our learning.

He's a chiller, but I think he's done teaching after this quarter cause he's getting his final step for PhD is done. Had random attendance, but you could make it up at the end of the year. Midterm and final are take-home and open notes. Only had to write two short papers about the music we learned about. Overall, easy A and highly recommended.

One of the best professors at UCSD. Even though the material is really easy he still makes it so interesting that I went to lecture to just listen. He really cares about the class and wants everyone to enjoy it too. Grading is also really light

Professor Zurita is so passionate about his job, he is so caring and the material he teaches in class is different from all the film classes I have been taking. a lot of time I fee like I can just learn the stuff professors saying from YouTube video but professor Zurita invite you to have critical view into art and grow as both a person and artist
Best professor I've ever had. Always pushes students to care deeply about their work. Would definitely take his class again.

Professor Zurita is an astounding teacher who inspires students and creates a safe space in the classroom for all types of art to be shared. He provides good critique and grades at the end of the quarter to give students enough time to do the best they can on assignments. He's just a chill guy, grades easily, and brings out the best in students.

Easily one of the best professors at UCSD. His teaching is unorthodox but the results speak for themselves. He made the class feel safe and was always encouraging us to follow our own paths. In his class I found my voice as an artist and made more friends than I have in years here because of the community he creates in class.

The best professor I've had at UCSD. You do have to make a film every week but how can you be a better filmmaker without making more films bro. He cares about each of his students so much. You get a lot of valuable feedback on filmmaking in this class. You will grow a lot as an artist and a person. Take him if you can!! Go HAM
Ana Maria Alvarez has such an inviting personality, she makes her class perfect for beginner and experienced dancers opening up the space to dance judgment free.
One of the most amazing grounding professors UCSD has to offer. Whether you are a dance student or not- TAKE HER CLASS

very engaging professor who cares about all of her students. She really emphasizes the meaning behind her work and encourages dancers to push themselves and improve. Being in her class was a really fun experience!

The teaching style is well established based on individual needs and community effort; if you attend the class ready to learn and give it your best shot, even if you do not have experience, you'll be fine. If you're having a rough day, please be open. Ana Maria is very flexible and understands that students have a life outside the classroom.
Ana Maria is an incredible professor. So caring, inspirational and effective. You will learn SO much from her.

She docks so many points on HW assignments (gives out F's) and never responds to questions sent via Canvas/email. The harsh grading is not necessary nor fair especially given it's an introductory biology course.

I took GenBio1 at a different university and it was such an awesome course. I thought GenBio2 must also be an amazing class as well. Then I ran into Phadke and her personal grudge against students. Her lectures are very hard to understand and scattered, her quizzes have tons of trick questions, as someone else said, she loves to fail you on papers.

He's the reason why I'm not doing linguistics anymore, hope this helps ❤️ Real review: he teaches the class as if you have had prior syntax knowledge. He also refuses to have video for his podcast when all the work he does is visual despite SO many students asking him to post a video recording.

This class was sooooo hard! I only passed with a C because I collaborated with 2 other people when doing homework and quizzes. He's a very nice professor BUT he moves on soooooo quickly bc you're expected to be an expert. You'll finally understand something and then bam, new topic already. FYI, this is nothing like what you learned in LIGN 101.

The class is very hard, the professor likes to move on very quick despite many of us still not understanding the material. Although office hours are available sometimes it doesn't help as he still expects you to have already understood the material. He's very kind but the material is very difficult.

Alex is super sweet but the class is very hard. There's a lot of content & the class would go pretty fast, sometimes he would stop to ask if we had questions but I hadn't even absorbed enough info to be able to ask one; I'd have to review the materials later. Going to his office hours helped a lot especially with the hw

Alex is great but this class is really really reaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaally difficult. Incredibly difficult. I would not take this class unless you're a ling major. My only critique of the prof is that the jump from 101 to 121 is huge and I feel like he thinks we know more about linguistics than we actually do. His lectures move fast so pay attention. gl.

I took this course with Professor Ayden Maralani years ago. His approach to teaching transistor-level circuit design sparked a strong interest in the subject. Since graduating, I've been working in transistor-level design professionally, and I still love it.
The way professor Maralani taught analog circuit design I learned a great deal. His considerations for the final grade was very helpful too. Big like!
i must say that i was very happy with the professors teaching style and his pace. he made this subject very interesting to follow and i would certainly take him again.

Prof. Maralani has proven to be a very capable professor who cares about his students' learning. He really focuses on catering to students' needs and struggles and he is very helpful in his office hours. I would definitely take him again.
He did a fantastic job teaching us this quarter. Thank you, Sir! I am happy with my grade, too ...

The lectures are clear and assignments are short, no busy work. PLENTY of extra credit given. Group project is a bit of a pain if partners don't do their share, but she can see who does what and evenly distributes points. Final was so incredibly easy if you just go to class, I loved this prof and would take more classes with her.

Grade is just final and project. The group project is briefly touched upon and she just expects you to know what to do. Received 100% on all assignments preceding the project, but when we submitted she said it was all wrong, feedback was terrible. A bit rude and condescending when looking for proper feedback, I'd just recommend taking prof Zoumas.

Dr. Hartman is caring and passionate about her work. Her class starts deceptively easy, but becomes time-consuming near the end. Expect a group project + paper and a final exam. The exam isn't too bad. Her feedback can be confusing with a lot of inconsistencies. She's a fine professor, not my favorite, but always willing to take student criticism!

Amazing professor. Is very caring and accessible outside of class. Gives really interesting lectures, not boring at all. My only complaint is that she gives a final exam, group project, AND group paper to do at the end with no midterm.
No midterm which is great. She did her best with the content. Definitely knew her stuff, very smart. Final is low stress but huge on group projects.

I took this course with Professor Ayden Maralani years ago. His approach to teaching transistor-level circuit design sparked a strong interest in the subject. Since graduating, I've been working in transistor-level design professionally, and I still love it.
