I'm not sure if this is just because I took this course over the summer, but this class was difficult and no one was able to earn anything above an A-. The essays are graded very harshly and without a clear criteria, so it is hard to improve and seems arbitrary. Ingham is also monotone and lectures are very boring. Would stay away from his classes

Professor Ingham is a great lecturer, he is systematic and accurate. The 110C reading selections are especially good. There's a lot to get out of his classes in the 110 sequence if you read everything and take thorough notes. You will likely have to do all of the reading if you want to get an A, and I appreciate that!

As a math major whose never taken PHIL or POLI classes before, I was genuinely surprised at how much the content of the course intrigued me. Ingham is monotone, with often disinteresting lectures, but he is nice and his weekly quizzes are a piece of cake (even if you didn't read). Learn the easy concepts in depth, rather than the hard ones to get A
Super worthy class ever, highly recommend. The lectures are informative, clearly-structured, PAs are designed reasonably so that you can get hang of what just learned. Really good course.

Professor Hao Zhang is an amazing lecturer and researcher in his field (machine learning system). Amazing lectures with supplemental papers reading and guest lectures(be prepared to read a lot but definitely beneficial), and TAs are really helpful. Nice curve with extra credits to make sure you really enjoy learning instead of being grade oriented.

Professor Zhang is absolutely the rock star of MLSys. His lecture is super great. It really brings the whole MLsys world to me. He is nice to student, and approachable in office hour. The class is also easy-going with homework / extra credits / readings (TAs are helpful).
Professor Zhang is very nice. I really enjoyed the course.

Professor Hao really cares about teaching, and his lectures are super interesting and inspiring. He puts a ton of effort into tweaking the course material to keep it fresh and cutting-edge, tossing in cool stories about big tech companies and famous profs to make the class feel laid-back and fun.

Very kind professor who evidently cares a lot about the things he's teaching. A good amount of reading, but very doable. Grade based on two essays and weekly short writing assignments. As long as you read, and watched lecture to consolidate your ideas, you could write good essays and get a good grade. Very fun and interesting course overall!

My actual class is pol138, populism. This is the first time I have rated a teacher in the past three years using this website. Matthew can really be called a "friend of students". It is an honor for SD and a blessing for SD students to have him serve as a teacher at SD. May God bless him.

Each class has a few required readings (10-25 pages), and the weekly discussion questions and two essays are about them. I never read a single one of them though and I did fine since the lectures are entirely based on the readings. I would not take this class if you don't care about political theory. Lectures aren't mandatory, but discussions are.

Class is podcasted. Discussion attendance and participation mandatory! You have a midterm essay and a final essay, both about 1000-1200 words. You have exactly week to write them. You don't need to do the reading, he goes over it in class. Read the necessary reading when you get your essay prompt. I loved this class I highly recommend this profe

His lectures were sometimes interesting but the discussion for the class is what really mattered. Discussion participation and attendance is mandatory. Your grade is entirely dependent on TA, but if you reach out to Prof Draper for anything he responds pretty quickly. Would definitely recommend taking this class with him.

This professor lack of organization lead to general struggle for students I don't recommend taking with this professor. She she's mistakes and student have to pay for them. Its just a matter of time and shell be fired.
the quiz has nothing to do with the sample quiz. doesn't prepare you for the quiz, very stressful.

Chatgpt explained the course concepts better than her. Examples in later lectures are quickly glanced over. Unclear grading scheme: "everything subject to change." Ignores messages on Zulip. Few TAs are literally reteaching the class for her in discussions. Loudly shames students in class for "not knowing how to follow instructions."

Suddenly changed the syllabus from "having no final" to "mandatory final" without elaboration on final details, including allowed devices, question numbers, lecture covered. Many students have no idea about the final date and time just few days before the final exam.
Her lecrures were easy, but I still hate this course more than any other tough one.

This professor gives a light amount of course work, delivers very clear lectures, understands the material himself, and all the multiple choice questions have a correct answer listed as one of the 4 choices. Everyone in the course approved of him.

Chen Lecuters is good, but his HW is hard, his tests are on a whole different level, but I had a good TA who help a lot. He's nice and patient and funny, he curves a lot at the end, I got 45% on both midterms and 64% on the final and ended with a C+. I would take him again for CENG 113 in the spring.

For lectures he just clicks through slides and repeats the same things over and over again without actually explaining anything. He'll occasionally work through something on the board very quickly and claim it's "simple," yet won't explain what he's doing. Tests are graded very harshly, along with little to no guidance on the group project.

Homework assignments can be fairly involved, but the midterms are very reflective of the lecture material. Make sure to actually work out all the practice problems he gives you for the midterms, and I would recommend reading the book prior to lecture. Clear lectures, encourages participation, very understanding.

His accent really isn't that bad. His lectures are great in my opinion - he gives tips for organizing information and step by step procedures. His lecture slides are even better. And his exams are tricky, but fair, and very similar to what is seen on the homework. Now the homework is pretty killer, but if you can manage that, the exams are cool.

She was very sweet! Content heavy, as long as you do the readings and participate in class you should be fine. She is very accessible outside of class if you ever have any concerns and is understanding, I had to miss two classes due to participating in an event and she did not dock me of any points! Be sure you turn in your assignments on time

While she is content heavy, she is definitely a professor worth taking. Be clear about any questions or accommodations with her as she is very understanding and accommodating if needed. Reading heavy.

Only grades are from 2 midterms and final. Multiple choice questions can be tricky but the curve is extensive. Gives practice problems and practice exams, if you practice with those the exams aren't that bad.

Fairly decent exams and practice sets provided. I found having a hard time with the multiple choice as its asks for really specific details of historical events. Read all the slides carefully and know how to do the graphs, good prof.

This is probably one of the most insightful classes I have taken at UCSD (in terms of content), however, the professor is the worst. His test are a poor reflection of what he teaches as he doesn't do much teaching that proves useful. You are better off reading the textbook and doing the practice test. His multiple choice is a history test basically
Great prof, lecture isn't mandatory and is recorded. Lecture content as far as the case studies go are fairly relevant to markets, the class is a good intro to global monetary mechanics

Professor Hamilton is highly respected. I loved his lectures because they went beyond textbook theories and delved into real-world case-studies. Exams are entirely based on lectures; presentation slides and podcasts are available. There was a pretty heavy curve for this class. May come across as dry, but really evokes interest in economics.

homework assignments were easy, but completely irrelevant to midterm/final. lecture was boring, but if you paid attention, it did help for the exams (heavy studying). asked random questions about what school he attended. also yelled at our TA in front of the class and went on interesting rant where he referred to himself in the 3rd person.

He is actually an AMAZING professor, IDK why people are saying he isnt. When teaching he is def strict but its at our best interest at heart. He is really easy to talk to and always avalible he is really sweet and helpful. As long as you pay attention you are fine the tests are easy. Pay more attention to what he is saying than the slides.

Very easy going and friendly professor. Super old so he has a different generation's mindset but very clear on what to study to do well. Can secure an A on exams if you know the slides well despite not attending lectures. HWs can take a bit of time but graded well and easy to get full on those. Only prof who hands out his number to be accessible.
Worst learning experience taking a MGT course

Professor Dunn is nice but can't teach. The lecture and lecture slides are poorly put together and useless overall. Homework is graded for completion but the HW material itself is also useless and irrelevant to exam material. However, you get a study guide at the end of the course that covers almost the whole final which makes getting an A doable.

Weekly hw, 2 midterms, and a final. The materials were hard so I highly recommend going to office hours for help. Study and understand everything carefully or he will destroy u with the exams. This is a hard class and he failed 21 people in Winter 2025.

Tough course but the content is great and the professor is great. Make sure to go to office hours and stay on top of the lecture content because the topics build off of each other. The homeworks are really time consuming and more difficult than the exams
Interesting man :)

Mainly learn advanced methods for hand calculation in structural analysis by applying virtual work method. Homework are long and challenging; midterms are manageable but the final is hard! He does not curve (91 for an A and 86 for an A-) so make sure you don't miss his lectures.
Great Professor. Kinda tough subject. Conducted lot of office hours. Assignments are time consuming. You'll learn a lot from this class.

reading assignments due before class and weekly team quizzes (open note). harsh grader on midterm/final: all writing on blue book, 3 short answers (2 paragraphs) and one long essay (4-5 paragraphs), cheat sheet allowed. grades weren't posted till week 7 unfortunately.

he's nice but his lectures were boring. he relied on group discussion and would cold call on people from each group like we were in high school. he didn't post our grades until week seven and grades the midterms harshly. only gave us an hour and 20 mins to answer multiple choice questions, two short answer questions, an essay. don't recommend him

Professor was pretentious when it came to grading. If you're not used to writing 1,400 words in person in about an hour and 20 minutes for midterms don't take this class. Also grades were posted week 7 and I'm not sure if that was intentional so more people didn't drop the class. If you're taking for upper div. credit as a non writing major don't

Prof Gong was nice but sometimes inconsistent with grading criteria and expectations. Course was graded on weekly group quizzes (open-note) and a midterm and final which were handwritten essays and will make your entire arm ache. My class was able to advocate for the use of cheat sheets on our exams but he might not do the same for others.

lots of reading, but he's so passionate and knowledgeable in his lectures. very engaging and makes topics fun to learn, but also easy to comprehend. depending on who your TA is, that could affect your grading criteria and experience (I had Alex and he was great!)
He is a passionate lecturer, very knowledgable. Shoutout to my TA Alex, good discussion sessions.

Professor Day is my favorite professor so far as UCSD. He is a truly passionate and very well versed man in the field of teaching. His lectures are very engaging and makes you want to listen and learn. Take home short answer quizzes are given every week with no in person tests. He is a fair grader and very easygoing.

Was a great class, great lecturer. There are 3-5 readings a week and 4 1 page write-ups with a final paper. Attendance and participation was mandatory. The class has 3 different TAs that had discrepancies in their grading and discussion sections which was frustrating because the same work got different grades depending on who you had.

I took 130B with him in summer 2024 and loved how he explains the materials slowly and clearly and very friendly and caring to students. 4 hw, 2 midterms, and 1 final with extra credits. Definitely take him again.

Dr. Chadha is a great professor. His lectures are very clear and inspirational, and the homework is very helpful for understanding the material. Watch out for the exams, though, they're tricky! On the exams, seemingly basic questions can become tricky when you only have a page of notes and a calculator. If you can take his class, do it!

Maybe the hardest class I've taken, because the prereq is not at all enough. The assignments are hard projects with many things you need to figure yourself (you will learn a lot!). But TAs are GOATED and will spend hours helping people fix tech issues during office hour and labs. I wouldn't have passed without the support of Girish (one of the TAs)

This class is a disaster. 

All we can get help from are TAs and few videos and instruction papers about the tech. There is no step-by-step guidance, professors talk about business in the class, and the weekly tech assignment just suddenly throws a big project to us to figure out by ourselves. I feel the TA teaches me through this whole class.

I loved Dr Walker! Engaging lectures and she clearly cares about her students. Lots of helpful TA's/UGIA's, and multiple extra credit opportunities. 2 midterms, the final was cumulative but tests were only from lecture, not the textbook at all. Really enjoyed the subject matter :)

Professor Walker is such a great lecturer and is very understanding! Attendance wasn't mandatory since she does podcast, but she does do participation questions for lectures which are due at the end of the week. Overall, her course wasn't difficult, midterms are multiple choice, would definitely take her again!

Whoever said she's hard or this class is hard is genuinely tripping. She's the best and the class was incredibly easy so long as you went to lectures, which I did because she is funny and engaging. Since I went to lectures the exams were straightforward and easy. Great class, great prof.
Emailed her and never emailed me back. When she did it was a rude response.

Caren is an amazing lecturer, as well as an attentive listener to ideas and questions during office hours. Tests are exceptionally easy and anyone can score high on the exams if they attend and pay attention in lecture. I barely supplemented with the readings- she tells you everything you need to know. Generous extra credit. Easiest A+ ever

With all honesty, don't take this professor. He never replies to the emails sent and he only cares about teaching and getting out of there. His exams are online but in honesty, they are quite unfair. He purposely curves by the smallest point even though averages are horrible so it does not impact the student's grade in any positive way.

His lectures are not reflective of exam material. Exams are not a good measure of how well you understand the information. Other BIMM profs are a lot more understanding and provide a lot more grade improvement opportunities and EC. Take anyone else.

Professor Akbari is amazing! The class was graded on 8 of 9 quizzes, each based on readings. Quizzes had 3-4 questions, were open-note, and easy if you understood the concepts. From Week 1, you join a group to present a paper. He's very caring, knowledgeable, and answers all questions. He even gave us a lab tour! Overall, an incredible class!

I think the class was okay. I liked that in lectures he would give real-life examples connecting to his research as well as doing a lab tour. This class is only exams so if you aren't a good test taker then this class may not be for you. Also, I felt like the wording on some questions was confusing. Dr Akbari is a nice person in lecture though.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. This whole 10-week class is based on 3 super difficult canvas exams. The questions are phrased in a way to intentionally confuse you. He seems like a nice, caring professor, but you can tell he does not care about teaching. Avoid at all costs!!!!

Sweetest prof ever but not good at lectures. The accent is fine, but the flow isn't coherent, and has a hard time understanding/responding to questions. Needs complete self study. HW are very good, similar to 271A, build a solid intuition with a mix of theory+coding. 
Grade heavily depends on group project, choose your own topic. V lenient grader.
Heavy accent, bad lecture, can learn little from her class.
One of the nicest professors I've had. Great professor who really wants to help you learn. HOWEVER, her heavy accent is extremely difficult to understand.

although I found the class a little boring at times it was very insightful and professor nguyen is very genuine and kind! unfortunately not a lot of people including myself participated so it was a little awkward but honestly class was really chill. assignments were doable and not a lot of outside work. also liked that films were a larger focus

Bi-weekly discussions, film quiz, group presentation, final discussion. Discussions are more like 300-word mini essays. Attendance is mandatory but participation not really. The class is pretty disorganized because everything is just on the syllabus, so it's easy to miss an assignment. I missed the film quiz, but it didn't affect my grade much.

Unbelievably unprepared for his own lectures (late/didnt show, etc), first year on campus. Lectures are just summaries of assigned readings/films. Barely learned anything in lecture that wasn't already covered by assignments. If you can write, you can bs and get an easy A. Grading criteria kinda clear but TA doesn't seem to know how to follow them.

Professor Ghosh clearly cares about his students and making sure everyone learns the material. His lectures are clear and the exams are fair, but there's a lot of material so make sure to keep up with the pace and study hard. If you can find patterns between the various mechanisms and pathways it'll help tremendously. Good luck!

Uses an iClicker for attendance. Definitely tries to engage with the class during lecture, but gets students confused at times. Tests have a seating chart and material on the exam is heavy with free response.

One of my favorite professors ever in the chem department. The class itself is going to be hard no matter who is teaching it, super content heavy and there is a lot to memorize. Ghosh did his best to emphasize things in lecture that showed up on midterms. His grading is fair and he is accessible outside of class. Very understanding and a nice guy

The final is worth 50% of your grade, up to 90% if you don't do well on the first 2 midterms. He brushes over a lot of the concepts, but the tests were ok. The HW is short. Be extra prepared for the midterms and finals. His lectures are clear to understand, but they are a little fast.

Since we are online, lectures weren't mandatory since he records them. Overall the class was fine and the homework wasn't too difficult. If you keep up with lectures, you should do fine on the homework. Quizzes were a bit challenging though. Make sure you really understand the concepts behind the material that's gone over. Then you'll be fine!!

-had him for 103a 
-key takeaways
-lecture heavy 
-doesnt really teach material that well
-difficult material esepecially with him 
-try to avoid him 
-final was exdtremely hard while midterms were doable but still challenging

This is my second time having Hans Wenzl for a MATH course here at UCSD. This time, however, this class was somewhat disorganized and the material along with the book used was difficult to work with. Although the material did make sense in the end, the class itself could have been better organized overall. The work was not simple so take caution.

Professor Wenzl is an excellent person who clearly cares for his students, but often times he's underprepared for the lectures. Occasionally he gets confused himself and that doesn't help the students. Overall if you know vector calculus its easy A but his homework is usually long and repetitive, they don't help you learn much.

Hans Wenzl is not a bad professor. At least when I took him for MATH 20E. I agree he does have an accent but he did teach vector calculus which made sense overall and I am glad I finished my final lower division math course with him. Wish I had walked away with an A but I did not study well enough for the Final with his practice exams. DO STUDY.
His lectures are really bad and doesnt explain things thoroughly. He also comes off as confused and very unorganized. Tests are nothing like the homework either.

He's a great prof and really cares about what he's teaching! He doesn't podcast though so make sure you can attend his lectures (you can get extra credit for attendance). Coursework can definitely be challenging so use the textbook in conjunction with his slides when studying for tests. Overall nice guy and very approachable!

This is a review for ECON 120BH, the honors supplement to 120B. The class was extremely well structured, class was informal and laid back, and you get an A if you just put in the work: a research paper outline, rough draft, peer review, presentation, & final draft. Overall, great attitude, and offered to write letters of rec for all of us in honors

This class is made extremely difficult because he does not teach students how to actually solve problems, instead making students memorize more formulas, proofs, etc. than all other UD ECON courses combined. HW insufficiently prepares students for difficult exams. Feels like this material is above undergraduates and average grades are low.

He teaches Econ 120B in an unnecessarily complicated way. Almost teaching statistics in a level above undergrad (imo). On top of this, he doesn't record the class so I can't review what we learnt. I'm forever confused in this class. I'd advise that you take any other professor who breaks things down more. He seems like a nice guy though!

Dahl managed to overcomplicate just about every single stats topic he taught. There were things I learned in 120A that I felt confident in, but the moment Dahl reviewed them, he managed to confuse me all over again. Also, he makes a huge fuss about attendance and DOES NOT PODCAST, which is my favorite way to learn, making the class even harder.

I was not his student, I was a TA for CHEM 109. He was rude the whole quarter, even though I tried my best to be a good TA to the students and Prof. Ulrich. I had my weaknesses but I tried to overcome them by arriving early to learn from the lab manager. Yet he did not acknowledge my hardwork. Its just better to take this lab with a nicer professor

Ulrich Muller is the worst professor I have had at UC San Diego. He refuses to record lectures and provide PowerPoint slides/notes. He scheduled a lecture for a non-lecture day because of a holiday and refused to record it for those who have other responsibilities, such as work. This class is so stressful because of the administration.

Professor Muller was one of my favorite professors. His exams are representative of the lectures and he provides homework questions after each lecture to make sure you understand the content covered during lectures. The class had 5 midterms and 1 final exam (lowest dropped) and the exams were 20-30 mins. Cool professor and has the best art skills!

Worst teacher that I have had at UCSD. Lectures are very disorganized, jumps from one idea to the next, does not introduce anything, just announces a question and starts solving it on the chalkboard. Tests are not representative of the material he teaches and does not assign any homework. Make mistakes during lecture which made things confusing.

Worst professor I have EVER had at UCSD. Got an easy A in 6a, and halfway through this class dropped. Guess what: I got an A in 6b with another professor the next quarter, so I clearly actually knew the material. Unorganized class, lots of mistakes, bad lectures, and no homework or recomended problems mean you will learn nothing.

Told us to not bring scientific calcs for exams; practically every student had a calc in the exam and he said absolutely nothing (you couldn't have solved those qs w/o a calc). Brought it up with him and he said he knew people were using one but he couldn't do anything about it (???) so instead I got screwed for being academically honest.

Disorganized and didn't explain things very well.  The answer keys were vague and unclear which made it difficult to check your work.  Mid-term and final are like the practice tests so I recommend studying those.  Doesn't respond to piazza.  Homework is graded on completion.

Lecturing isn't his strongest suit, as he talks slowly and can sometimes explain things roundaboutly, but his exams are straightforward, and his course notes are useful (no textbook). He is a very knowledgeable professor, and there isn't much to complain about. I enjoyed his class overall and he puts effort in to help you succeed
Just got out the final and I can't say anything was surprising. He off

The professor and his TAs were not responsive to students' questions outside of class and gave little support in preparing for exams.  We were expected to understand how to do HW problems with concepts on exams with only a few days preparation, very little guidance and solutions not being given until after the exam.

This class is difficult and heavy on memorization (perhaps excessively so), but Dr. Daugherty's lectures are highly interesting, comprehensive, and engaging. Almost all of your grade comes from exams. "Required" reading from textbook, but not actually necessary to read it to do well. 4% EC offered (+ more for SETs) and tests are *slightly* curved.

This class was very interesting and the professor was very friendly but the exams were pure memorization and hard. The class consists of two midterms, 3 quizzes, and a final so if you tank one of them, it's hard to get back on track. He does provide a lot of extra credit though. If you're good at memorization you'll be fine but if not, good luck!

There are a lot of extra credit opportunities available to you, so don't let a single bad exam get you down. This class really does implore a lot of memorization, but there isn't any out of the blue that he didn't dedicate almost an entire slide to. The lecture audio was difficult at times to understand.

if you are a master procrastinator you will be absolutely destroyed by the exams unless you have a good memory. exams are pure memorization of different virus families. uses the zoom camera on his laptop as his main source of mic for recordings and sometimes he would walk across the room and you could barely hear him. Yet still my favorite class...

The class is more focused on memorization rather than concepts, and I am not a fan of the course structure.If you attend the lectures and memorize the materials, the tests are not hard. He is someone who cares about his students, and passionate about virology.However, his voice when lecturing is monotone and makes it hard to focus on the materials.

Professor Demetriou is kind and very knowledgeable. However, it is difficult to get an A on essays as graders can be nitpicky (highest I got was an 88). Lectures not mandatory or podcasted. discussions mandatory & 20% of grade. 3 essays including the final. Final is a take-home essay (~8pgs). Readings were boring. Overall grade depends on TA.

This professor's lecture style and content lack engagement, making the material feel dry and uninspiring. Her strict no-laptop policy throughout the semester, only relaxed on the final day, felt overly rigid. She also seems to think she's quite funny, though her humor often misses the mark, leaving students more confused than amused.

If you are a massive teacher's pet or you love ancient literature, you will love her. The other 95% of people: avoid her. She will tell anyone with a laptop to put it away, and will disrespect students who ask her questions. Extremely boring lectures, and about the same difficulty as other profs. Grades depend on your TA. Doesn't deserve her rating

Extremely boring lectures, laptops/tech isn't allowed and she WILL call you out if she sees you (even though online is often the only way to access the books). Two mandatory outside of schedule events that you have to go to. Grading depends on the TAs, so she is about the same difficulty as others. She is knowledgable, but VERY boring and annoying.

Wow. Truly the most amazing humanities professor on campus. Just incredible. Every single lecture I actually bothered to attend was just so enticing and unforgettable. I simply couldn't wait to come back for more. Every moment was a masterpiece, and I was just so lucky to witness such brilliance. An absolute privilege. Truly. Best. Professor. Ever.

She is the best professor I have ever had. Very nice and sweet. There are weekly journals that takes time to do every week. Gradings are very fair and you can get an easy A if you follow the instructions . I loved this class and gained very good experience at my site.

My favorite professor. The content of lectures is interesting, assignments are relatively easy, clear grading criteria, and she is very understanding. She provides extra credit opportunities and is easy to access outside of class. Passionate about what she teaches & an incredible person. I have taken 3 of her classes and I highly recommend her.
So sincerely sweet and wants you to come to her for help. Easy grader and passionate about topic.

She is my FAVORITE professor at UCSD. I had no idea professor's could be so nice until I entered here class. She truly cares for students and wants all of us to suceed. I looked foward to going to class everyday and she presented the material in such an engaging way. I will never forget her kindness and encouragment that she gave all quarter.

Dr. Bintliff is amazing and I highly, highly recommend her! Her class is set up for you to succeed and if anything happens to come up for you, she is incredibly accommodating. She brings a lot of interesting experiences to the table, her lectures are engaging, the assignments aren't too difficult, and she makes an effort to get to know her students

At first, I thought I wouldn't like Prof Grant but the more I got to know him on a personal level, especially on a week where it was about immolation, and getting to see this other side of him makes him an amazing professor; and it makes him an amazing professor because I saw how zealous he is when teaching these things

LE can be boring sometimes but at least it ain't boring most of the time tho. Prof Grant's passion on social movements definitely resonate when he teaches the class and also does these fun workshops, where you see his excitement!
Classes aren't mandatory because attendance isn't taken but I still went because his class is enjoyable to be in. He genuinely cares about the students; if you need an extension, you'll get it, etc

He's definitely a cool prof- He makes class fun when it comes to the flag workshop for ex. MT was ez, where u have the option to submit it in wtv way u can; like students could submit it through a doc where u answer the questions through writing, but u can also submit it through audio, music, art, drawing, etc. He makes lots of things flexible!!!

Grant is a fantastic professor. Even though this is a film class, I learned concepts that I use in almost all my other classes (especially comm classes). The readings and ideas can seem super abstract and difficult at first, but he explains them clearly and the projects helped make things concrete. I loved this class, I wish I could take it again!

Such a caring person and incredible professor. She does important work at UCSD and is passionate about it. She offers interesting courses with exciting content and is always willing to work with students. I highly recommend taking her courses, especially those who are interested in bio anthropology/ epigeneticsLove her!

She is very intelligent and considerate of her students. No quizzes, but there will be essays, student-led discussions (in groups) through presentations, and lots of dense readings (also some easy ones) weekly. She shows you how to read the dense articles so it's not really big deal. She also offers plenty of extra credit outside of class.

The material is very interesting and Non promoted open discussion within class. There were no exams but discussion boards and papers. Many extra credit opportunities were given. I would say there was not a clear prompt for the papers so you could have trouble with what to write and what not to write. However, overall easy DEI class!

She seems very friendly, intelligent and nonjudgmental as a sociocultural anthropologist should be. She speaks very clearly and is also very organized. I would suggest keeping up with the weekly readings because you do have to write essays on some of them. Bluebooks are required for the midterm/final. Participation might be offered as extra credit.

Lectures can be a little dry but not difficult to follow on your own. Just need to be willing to read a few articles (not too much) and do some writing. Exams were questions that you are given ahead of time so you can prepare and reflect course material. Easy class if you do assignments & attend some lectures (or just read the assigned readings).

Professor Brenner is a great professor. Lectures can get a little boring but you can watch the podcast and just 2x speed it. This class is very easy to get an A in if you legit write down every word she says. I did this for all my exams and discussion posts and got mostly 100%. The class was 5 discussion posts, 1 midterm and 1 final.

Dr. Brenner is the best prof I have had in any college course ever. The delivery and engagement of the students is phenomenal. So, if you feel like that average college student who doesn't know if they identify with the material, Brenner's strength is giving students an ability to connect and be impassioned in what you study. Take this opportunity.

Didn't quite understand the grading criteria for the reading responses, to be honest. Attendance isn't mandatory and lectures are quite dry, so expect to see half of the class disappear by week 5. The readings are mandatory, so make sure to do those, as the tests are based on them. She did respond to emails really quick, which was nice.

The material is very difficult. He makes us read the textbook and do the homework before class. The readings and homework are very hard in the last few weeks, so beware. He is nice and tries to clear up confusions in class, but personally I do not like his lecture style. Lots of work, but good for a challenge. Also, very nice grading scheme.

Prod Dimitris is obviously very passionate about what he does, but he stutters and is unable to communicate information clearly. The class is almost entirely participation and homework based so knowledge of the material is not necessarily required. Good guy, terrible lecturer.

Maybe he's a nice guy. I don't know because I've had to drop every time I took his class. Literally the main reason I dropped the Probability specialization and just went into pure maths. this course focuses more on research and state of art topics of time series and bootstrap. therefore, I highly recommend it if you already have the background knowledge of time series and 287a class
he is really good at teaching. if you have some background on time series, you would learn a lot from him.

He's a very entertaining professor who likes to get the students involved into learning. He's always trying to get students to figure out the next step and build intuition rather than have the students memorize blindly. He goes pretty fast through content so following the notes is a must. Funny professor with hilarious stories.

Amazing professor who taught the class whilst telling funny stories from his undergraduate days. I not only learned algebraic combinatorics, but also quite a bit of representation theory as he flew through the content of 188 quickly and started teaching us more fun stuff. Congrats on attaining tenure track at UMD!
ucsd will miss his his aura when he heads to college of maryland :((

His lectures never made any sense and they got progressively worse throughout the quarter. I learned everything from either the textbook or YouTube. He doesn't believe in curves, doesn't record his lectures/ post his notes but also doesn't take attendance. Cool guy. Lectures are not mandatory but he doesn't post notes(the only downside) so that might incentivize attendance. I self studied from textbook at times. Homeworks were reasonable, and exams were very doable if you put effort into homeworks.

She genuinely cares about the students and is always available outside of class via Piazza. Her lectures are clear and she always makes sure the students are not getting lost along the way. The lecture material is representative of the exam material, and there aren't any curveballs. 100% would recommend this professor, best in the math department!

Sincerely one of the best professors I've ever had. Her lectures are clear, direct, and extremely captivating. She always tries to make sure no one has any unanswered questions, and personally responds to every Piazza post within a few hours at most. Exams and homeworks are fair and instructive. I looked forward to every lecture. Highly recommend!
The class content is very interesting and she explains everything well. Leture notes are also posted so you can spend more time listening to the lectures rather than writing down notes.

Dumitriu is a sweetheart, very caring and happy to answer any questions in office hours or during class. Also gives clear lectures that are easy to understand. The HW is reasonable, the lectures should give you all the info you need. The grading is heavily weighted on a midterm and final, but there are lots of practice problems to help you prepare.

She is a very approachable and kind Professor, her lectures are also good. The only issue was the exams were a bit too hard. Especially in the finals, there were way too many questions in my opinion. The quizzes are also very rough. 

I am not 100% sure if the quizzes have any integrity, just because of how easy it is for some people to cheat.

I came into the class without an undergrad computer architecture class and did fine, but I had to spend a lot of time reading the textbook to catch up. The class was a lot of work compared to other 200-level classes I've taken, but overall it was worth it to take this course with a legend in the industry.

This course is hard and unorganized, even if you have undergrad arch course. The professor is not caring about the workload and have >1 hw per week, and the hw is only less than 20% of the grade. No schedule of topics and the slides are not convenient for review. You will find many blanks in the slides. Don't take 240A taught by him.

Lecture style involves lots of practice questions, doing well on homeworks is vital to exam success. Entered being worried about having little experience with the hardware side of things, but could learn a lot.

Can be a bit disorganized in lecture (stuttering, hard to read handwriting) but lecture was very interesting for me even though I wasn't too interested in hardware. Learned a lot, tests were hard (expect questions to be harder than ones given on HW). Overall pretty good experience

Spell bounded ! Phenomenal and couldn't ask for a better teacher.. extremely passionate about teaching and cares a lot if students have gotten the point.. never tired of answering doubts and very organized. With no background in arch, his approach really helped me !

It's philosophy, so expect to read. Usually picks short papers (10-20 pgs) that are interesting. Weekly reading quizzes but you can usually just ctrl-F readings if you don't want to do them. Three large assignments worth most of the grade that are very easy and really don't require much engagement if you follow instructions. Chill prof, very nice.

she is probably the nicest professor I've encountered. love her class. There are readings, but they are easy and useful. Do not believe in those ratings, it is literally the best class on science ever.

no midterms, instead we have 3 homework assignments which consist of essays. very harsh grading, slightly difficult to be interested in class, however very caring and chill professor who cares about the subject of her teaching. final is 10 short answer questions, i wouldn't take this class again but she's a super cool person.

the ta's grade way too hard for no reason, and do not provide helpful feedback at all. way too much reading and effort for a simple GE class. do not take phil 12. professor does not explain the slides well, and the way she explains topics makes it more difficult to understand.

I made an account just to warn you not to take this class. If you're like me and thought that taking phil12 was a way to weasel out of taking a math course for GE's, you'd 100% be better off just taking a super easy math class instead. The professor makes no sense, and the course content is a complete snoozefest. Emphasis on snooze.

Amazing. Easily one of the best profs in the CSE department. Lectures are captivating, with a great balance of theoretical/mathematical rigor, and practical applications of the techniques used throughout computer vision (and just AI general). His attitude towards grading also makes the class more fun than stressful. Start the homework early though.
Explains topics well, including high level intuition. Also is very open to questions, which is nice.
going to go against the grain and say currently i don't feel lectures appropriately convey information to the audience. they have been using many suboptimal teaching methods

I was a bit stressed because my exam performances weren't great, though I could get through the homeworks by putting in the effort. Lectures involve a lot of review of past lectures where I believe professor tries to connect content together. Overall enjoyable experience.

Incredible teacher. You can tell he really cares for his students. Wrote individual feedback after both the midterm and final. Put a big emphasis on learning and having fun over grades. Very approachable and knowledgeable. I would gladly take any course with him teaching.

i took her in fall24 and wish she was teaching syn100. she is so sweet and you can tell all she wants is for her students to succeed. she offers amazing feedback and is also quick to reply. please take her if you're taking syn150, i promise you, you will have a wonderful time!

Amazing Professor , super bittersweet moment of class ending as super sad to be done with Professor Birberick but super happy to be done with class. She is very understanding and a super fun teacher to be with in lectures. Homework is super easy as well as class assignments . Super fun !

Professor Birberick is incredible. She cares a lot about her students and she's very personal with her teaching style, it makes the time in class really enjoyable. She's also funny and very easy to talk to, as long as you're showing up and making the effort to be engaged in class, it's an A. If you get the chance to take her, you won't regret it.
Great explanations on an often confusing topic. Really appreciate his teaching especially after learning similar material from another professor.

Antipa is amazing! His lectures complement the book's notes with numerous examples and in-class optics demos using various lenses. He never hesitated reviewing a concept we learned prior, making Fourier Optics understandable. No surprises on HWs or exams- fun at office hours. 
He's the best one no doubt but be aware he's forced to weed his 45 class
Course was hard, teaches you why something is the way it is rather than teaches how to do it. May help in some cases. gg

Grades are based on midterms and final. Good lecturer who truly tries to make a tough subject easy to understand. Midterms are pretty tough but are not something that's never been seen before. I will emphasize that questions are more difficult than what's provided during lecture.
He is a very nice professor. He always listens to students for feedback. Even though ECE 45 is a tough class, he made it manageable. You can tell he enjoys teaching.

Prof. Anderson was great! Lectures usually ended a few minutes early and you can tell he really cares about his students success, not just in his class but for a future career in accounting. Lectures can be dry, but that's cause it's tax. Exams were all MCQ and easy as long as you read the textbook with his notes as a guide. HW is light/graded easy

I only got a bad grade cause I didn't pay attention. Taken in Summer, lectures were 3 hours and heavy. You will have to read to understand Lectures. HW is kinda long due to making journals and statements and not having an iPad. To Pass with a better grade you have to be engage. He answers emails quickly and he's very understanding and will help.

The grade is mostly based off of tests but Anderson is very quick when responding to emails. Not many homework assignments and he drops the two lowest homework grades. Super nice guy and is willing to help students out by curving. Tests are kind of difficult but not too bad if you are keeping up with lectures.

Professor Anderson gives good lectures and has a unique teaching/notes style that works for his class. Make sure to read the textbook using his notes as a guide and to always do the homework. Class is graded almost entirely on the midterm and final so there is very little room for mistakes, but he does curve generously.

Prof. Anderson is a bit old school but he definitely knows his stuff. Corporate tax may not be the most engaging topic but he managed to make it engaging and went really slow to make sure everyone understood. Do make sure to supplement the lectures with textbook reading in preparation for the exams though.

He's an excellent professor who cares for his students. I just took Comm 30 with him, and students are set up for success in his class; no tricky midterms or finals, but the content you learn can be applied to everyday life. I have taken his classes 2 times now, and would take a third.

he makes LE fun! appreciate how he KNOWS attending LE can be boring and too much, where we only went to LE once a week!!!! Readings were cool bc it was mostly in the NYTimes website that is free when u use ur ucsd email. Just a fun class with a cool prof too!!

He is super great. Does not like testing and often allows a cheat sheet. I loved him so much I am currently taking COMM 30 which is just as great. Super great guy but cancels class sometimes the day of so make sure to check your email address. Overall a 10/10 professor
His midterm and final are challenging but open note, takes modern-day events into consideration when lecturing, and encourages discussion in his classes. Great professor!
Very nice, engaging lectures, a few group projects but not too difficult. Projects and exams are all weighted 20%, you get a cheat sheet for exams and they are very easy. Lots of reading tho.

I personally enjoyed his lectures, but several people I talked to seemed to think it was a bit disorganized. To be honest, I thought it was pretty funny, and didn't have a significant negative effect on his lectures.
Homework and tests were hard but doable. He's a fantastic lecturer and is clearly genuinely enthusiastic about teaching undergrads which isn't a given with math professors.
Did not follow the textbook, but had very clear lecture notes on his website
Great professor with exquisite British humor! His course notes are very very clear.

Took him for 120A(in person) and 120B(online) and didn't like the lectures but I LOVED the lecture notes. They were super helpful and the main way I learned, so I taught myself the material with the notes. Hw is very hard, almost impossible, but in discussion they give all answers. The in-person tests were easy but the 24 hr online ones weren't.

I really enjoyed this class, Professor Wu made it a great experience. He genuinely cares about his students success, regularly checks in on us, and always offers extra help. This was one of my favorite econ class, and I wish I could take more with him! The exams were a bit hard, but gave study guides that helped out a lot.

He's definitely a caring professor who really is passionate about his work. The issue is that his exams aren't really a good reflection of the lectures, or dive too deep into neglected topics discussed. Be sure to be on track and try to always ask questions, he's often more than happy to answer. Also always study days in advance, it helps a lot.

I've never been more excited to go to classes, coming from someone who always waited until right before finals and quarters to cram podcasted lectures. Professor Wu is the most caring professor I've had throughout my entire time at UCSD; he checks in on the students and does his best to help you understand academia and career options.

Thought this was going to be a cool class in Macroeconomics - it was, kinda. He does go into macroeconomics concepts, but just know the main basis of the class is solving theoretical math problems with confusing variables.

Regardless, he is great, he checks on you personally and is always there to help, very nice. Don't take this class for granted

Absolutely the best professor at UCSD. Super interesting materials from economics to finance to real-world application of current events. Very caring of each student and very accessible during office hours. He is not just doing the job of a professor but really teaching with his heart like a mentor who truly wants you to succeed.

Professor Subramaniam is an amazing professor. His lectures contain a lot of detail, a lot of which you honestly don't need for exams or homework. Read the textbook. Read it. The homework is nothing like exams but if you read textbook you will honestly be completely fine. Exams are similar to lectures.

Shankar is a brilliant professor who's also super busy. The class has a super generous curve and is mostly based on conceptual questions, which if you follow lectures you'll do fine. There's also a group project that you do which was pretty fun!
Best professor ever!! If you ever have an issue, just talk about it with him. He's more than willing to go the extra mile to help students.

prof subramaniam cares about students' understanding. sometimes his explanations are unnecessarily complicated, but he focuses on key concepts, which is helpful since homework is not assigned. the TAs office hours and discussion were very helpful, especially since they write the 5 quizzes. the final was hard but the curve was very generous.

A haphazard five week thermo course is never a good idea, but Professor Subramaniam didn't do us any favors. He's both brilliant and enthusiastic, but spent most of class rushing through long derivations for concepts he didn't bother to introduce. Homework is graded tough and is worth a lot, so find a good TA.  Difficult final,  but generous curve.

I love Mandy soooo much! They are so caring and compassionate. I had them for CGS 113 in FA24 and then took CGS 124 with them for WI25, and both classes were GREAT! They were exactly what I hoped to have when I declared my CGS minor -- so caring, kind, and thoughtful, and treats their students like adults.
amazing professor would 100% recommend

Passionate teacher! 1 Weekly HW and 2 projects. SUPER easy DEI class & could've been entirely online since 15/20 days were Zoom due to chronic illness. Discusses a lot about gender privates and easily could be rebranded into a sex-ed class tbh. She can keep class interesting for days and brings up a range of topics from current/past LBGTQ+ notions

Great professor. Class was pretty straightforward and lectures were very interesting. No midterms or exams but does consist of two papers on at the beginning and at the end. Also loved the TA. They were very kind and flexible with work. The last three weeks ended up being moved to online which was great.

He is your average Asian father, he will display his disappointment if needed, but at the same time he's very uplifting and kind. Lenient grading and grading scale, surplus resources for success, including his wonderful TA team and practice exams. The homework is time-consuming yet informative. 

Showstopper!

The best professors I've ever had. I took this class, and although rigorous, it was completely fair and worthwhile. I felt daunted by the content he was covering, but his patience and willingness to help all students made it worth it. His knowledge is admirable.

He is a very knowledgeable professor, clearly is an expert in his field. He has high expectations of his students, however, so be ready to put in the work to understand the concepts to the point where you have a good intuition about everything (practice practice practice). Exams are pretty lengthy and with a huge time constraint.

Taking a course with Prof. V was an experience like no other, if you enjoy chaos then welcome aboard!

Syllabus was unclear + she was passive aggressive towards us students for no reason.

Can't say I didn't warn you

not a great professor. she doesnt lecture or teach anything. she just expects us to talk about old english books for 3 hours. class was Advertisement as Literature which sounded interesting but ended up being a boring english class. 25% participation. 25% mini biweekly papers. 10% medium paper. 40% 15-20 page final paper which you present. not good
Still figuring out what's the punchline - All the best Shaya!

I think Danielle Williams is my favorite educator I've ever had the pleasure of learning from. Not only is she incredibly smart and passionate, she also gives great feedback and is clear and concise about her goals as a Professor. More importantly to me, though, she is one of the kindest and most caring professors/teachers I've ever had.

Lectures were great, made a lot of the difficult course material easy to understand. Her website for the class was very detailed and contained a lot of helpful resources for studying. There were two exams which I we could've had more time, but she does let us retake them. Otherwise, homework and final project were manageable.

She's a decent lecturer to be honest, who really cares about your learning. And I actually quite enjoyed the class, but my main problem was the grading. I got 100 on the project and A's on both tests, but I got a B in the class because of her stupid homework policy of A or B on 4 out of 5 homeworks to get an A in the class, which I did not do.

Difficult class, fair professor, challenging and rewarding. Minnes is kind and she doesn't make you feel dumb if you don't understand. Be sure to attend office hours and ask lots of questions! Some tutors/TAs are not very helpful (ie restate the instructions of the project, giving little to no feedback), but if you go to her directly, she's great.

She cares about the students and explains the material well, but the problem with CSE 105 is that theres simply too much material to cover in class, so you need to read the textbook to be able to do the homework, which is very hard. The class is also very well origanized with everything on one website that is very easy to navigate through.

She is a very clear, smooth lecturer and her notes are extremely organized. Exams were fair and her policy really helped (2 midterms instead of a final with two attempts each). Considering the difficulty of the class and its concepts, she did an amazing teaching it. Highly reccommend!
Dude started the quarter with "I suck at math, so please be patient with me" and I love him for it. A really engaging lecturer

He was a great professor who really cared about the class's understanding, and he also explained concepts very well. Math 20B is often claimed to be the hardest of the 20 series, but with him as a professor, it was engaging, interesting, and of reasonable difficulty.

He's really nice and he teaches well too. He likes to engage the class (at least he did with mine) to make sure that everyone understands what he's explaining. I took the class when the syllabus was designed by Bowers which was great because there's so many ways to cushion your grade. Definitely recommend Lahiri either way!

I absolutely loved this professor! He was so caring in each lecture and actually wanted students to understand the course content. This is my last calculus course so I am sad I won't have him anymore, but could not have asked for a better experience with him.

Nothing bad to say about him. He has a bit of an accent but it was not at all a problem for most. What he taught in class matched pretty well with the exams. All three midterms were online, asynchronous and allowed calculators, but the final was in person, no calculator. HW was easier than the exams. Read the textbook concepts, will be tested!

One of the coolest professors ever, he is so knowledgeable about what he teaches and truly cares for his students! If you are interested in molecular biology as a field in general, you should definitely take his class. Straightforward, multiple choice exams and no homework.

Exams are very straightforward and represent lecture material and problem sets. During lectures, text in red means that it will appear in an exam so memorize! He's also a very sweet professor and truly passionate about what he teaches.

The professor is really sweet and seems to understand the material well, but he has a lot of the same slides and I feel like it takes him forever to get to his point. It's honestly pretty boring, but his tests are straight forward and similar to the homework he gives (which isn't graded).
ALOT OF MEMORIZATION!

Can't ask for much more from this professor. Was super chill, very clear in his lectures, and would often let us know which material was important to know for exams. Course is graded by 2 midterms (lowest is dropped) and a final, both worth half the grade. Make sure your memorization skills are on point and go to IA review sessions if you want an A

I took BENG 186B, 122A, and 216. His classes are tough af (💀), but he's super nice. Go to his office hours if you have any questions. He'll literally give you feedback on everything (hw, project) if you need it.

BENG 216 Homework is much harder than the course material this course should not be allowed to be taken without a background in electrical engineering. You are not given the materials to succeed. 
Sweet guy though and very passionate about his work.

He is a very approachable person, but I am afraid his homeworks(5hws,40%) are not in the same difficulty as the class material, they are extremely challenging and require a great knowledge of electrical engineering. the quizzes are actually fine. Overall, not a good class.
He is extremely helpful. If you are struggling, just show up at office hours, and he will be more than happy to be a resource. He is very friendly and caring for his students.
Very well organized course website and references. Handwriting slides sometimes are not easy to understand.

His class is so hard, the essay shouldn't be this hard and the final is an exam worth 40% of our grade when it should just be an essay. The TA grades the essay horribly and regardless of going to office hours he gives you a bad grade on the essay. There is mandatory attendance and the lectures are extremely boring.

Your grade consist on 40% exam, 40% paper and 20% attendance which are quizzes in discussion sections! Like the final was 2 essays and MC questions in 3 hours like that's too much. His lectures are basically reading off the slides but the topics are very interesting. Grading is super harsh and worth too much for no reason, he should change that.

One of my favorite professors. He is great at giving lectures. The course isn't hard. Lectures were based on readings. Books are required. Weekly quizzes, writing assignment and final. Concepts are very easy to understand. His office hours are wonderful, he is very helpful.

By far my favorite professor on campus. I am not great with finance and thought I would feel "stupid" throughout class, but he made it so easy to understand! I did well on the first essay and dropped a bit due to health issues. In the end, class was easy and I made it out with a B+.

I'd rather drown in quicksand than take another one of his classes again(respectfully). tbh, the TA's were difficult graders and didn't really seem to know how to answer some of our questions. The midterm and final prompts were confusing and expected too much from us in a short amount of time. This gave me excruciating migraines from all the stress

This professor is the best I have had at UCSD. These classes are actually engaging, have clear criteria, and allow space for discussion.  This was my favorite class at UCSD and I encourage everyone to take this class and to go to office hours. Also an extremely interesting person and actually cares about your success.

She is passionate about her research, but she really struggles with being an educator. Never uses a rubric to grade students on, so it is up to her own whims. She assigns huge chunks of reading every class session. It is a discussion based class, but she corrects students every single time in order to mold them into her own view. Take someone else

She expects a lot in her essays, always late to class, sometimes even a whole hour late where she will only be in class for 20 mins. She is also a very tough grader so you never get full marks on ANYTHING. Tons of readings, mostly guest lectures, attendance mandatory. For extra credit, you have to look for them yourselves.

She is by far the rudest professor I have ever dealt with, i dont know why but she literally wants all her students to fail. She gets angry when you ask for help and expects students to know what she want. She doesnt give good guidelines at all and then will grade HARSHLY. don't expect to get full points on anything. DO NOT TAKE HER.

This class was pretty unbearable. She sounds patronizing. Maybe 1/4 of the class attended lecture because they are long and basically useless. 80 min of talking about her own irrelevant book which won't help you do the papers  in any way so I stopped going. Papers are easy as long as you utilize concepts from readings. Section was 100% mandatory

Worst professor ever taken. Basically emotionless and don't care for students. His lectures were not podcasted nor engaging. Poor communication through Piazza(4 days to get a response). Hard access outside of class. Sample midterms barely represent actual ones. Test materials are barely from hw nor from review classes. No sample final. No curve

In comparison to what I've seen other past 10c professor courses, Sarkar course is very fair. Exams reflect review session & sample midterms. Have that on your cheat sheet and some understanding and you'll do fine. Two grading scales, higher one is the one your final grade uses, and doesn't rule out a possible curve at the end of the course.

This is supposed to be a tough class, so get ready for studying. Three 50 minutes lectures per week, and the notes and lecture videos will be posted online through canvas. Clear syllabus and grading criteria, but homeworks are kinda hard. If you study hard enough, it should be a straight A. Good luck!

Avoid at all costs. Take Calc 3 at a CC or wait another quarter. Goes so fast in lecture, tests don't fully reflect sample midterm difficulty. Had homework due 2 days after Midterm 1 with material we hadn't learned, and he claims that extensions were not possible. If you do have him, you'll be forced to learn on your own and still fail. Good luck.

Not done with the class yet, but so far everyone I know has had a very unpleasant experience.We just took the first midterm, and I think it was a VERY unfair exam.There were only 3 questions,one of which we never had any practice on and never saw similar examples of in class.We also don't receive answer keys to homework or discussion problem sets.

I took 1A/AX and 1B/BX. Gabriella observes students with a watchful eye. class sizes are on the smaller side, so she pays extra attention to student behaviors. Sometimes it's too much, especially if you prefer to fly under the radar. coursework is manageable, but keep in mind it's 5units. analysis of grammatical structure was too intense for me.

Professoressa Pozzoli è veramente simpatica! She's really cares about her students and helps in any way she can.  There's a 15 minute final that sounds daunting at first but really isn't. There are also easy vocab quizzes every Friday (pay attention in class). I cannot emphasize how great her class is, she creates an awesome learning environment.

Fun class. You have to learn a lot of vocabulary, since there's tests on it each Friday, but I didn't think it was too hard, especially if you really pay attention in class. There's a lot of work done with peers, but never outside of class. The 15 minute conversation final sounds scary but it really isn't, it was super easy.

Amazing professor, really wants you guys to learn farsi, show that you care and put in the effort and you will be fine. love this class, took this as a complete beginner basically and she was really good to make sure I did not feel overwhelmed. amazing class, amazing community, amazing quarter.

LOVE HER!!!! great ostaad, please show up to lecture, it's mandatory but also super fun and everyone in class gets to participate; quizzes are rlyyyy easy and so is the final and midterm if you study for like at least a day

She is the best. I took this class two times and I'm going to take it one more time. I learned a lot of things and enjoyed being in her class. If you want to improve your skills, take her.SHE IS THE BEST

Amazing professor. She helps her students a lot to be successful and she is very kind.
Merci baraye hamechi :)

A great professor who clearly cares about her students. Classes are mandatory and there is homework once per week usually but it is easy and not busy work. Take this class if you want to improve your persian!

Easy A class tbh. I never showed up to class and still passed. 3 essays and one of them is the final. I would have gotten a better grade if I directly quoted him and watched lectures. Class is a bit boring; I would rather teach myself with the textbooks. ALOT of reading btw. I got a 95 and 84 on my two essays. He's passionate for history, it shows

Pay attention and write notes during lectures!!! Your midterm and final essays pull directly from the things he says in class, and it makes it so much easier when you directly quote him when making your point when responding to his prompts. I really enjoyed the way he lectured and he was always very excited when people asked questions.

Prestholdt is the best professor I've had for MMW. He is very caring for his students and for what is going on around the world. The course is lecture heavy and he doesn't have recordings, but he posts slides. Very reasonable amount of readings and videos.

Best professor for MMW, PLEASE take him. Easiest MMW professor by far. Work is easy and manageable. Took his class with 20 units and a part-time job and only showed up to lecture for 2 weeks. I didn't do most readings and still got an A. Barely any readings, doesn't post lectures but does post slides.

Professor Prestholdt was the best professor I've had for MMW. He was super chill; attendance was not mandatory and the readings were only necessary for the midterm and final papers (which were both take home essays we had over a week to do). You could easily only read the ones that are relevant for your topic. He's the BEST MMW prof!

(I actually took LTSP 2F) She was the best professor I've had so far! Incredibly kind, she was super human and taught things that were very impactful. Easy class, everyone should get an A. Obviously stay on top of the homework, but there are no midterms or finals, so I highly recommend!!! Loved her :)!
Overall such a great class to be in. Easy class and easy to reach out to if you need to email about anything.

(Took LTSP 2F) This professor is very caring and she helped me with my interest in Spanish. The projects can be a little time consuming but they are interesting and more than fairly graded. If you are not proficient in Spanish then that is completely alright in this class and there are many opportunities to receive help.

She purposefully makes sure the homework doesn't take more than an hour to complete. She makes you write a 250 word diario in Spanish once a week + 1 extra homework assignment. There are chapter quizzes that are not made to trick you. The final is a recorded presentation of you making a guided tour on google maps, that only she will watch and hear.
She is really sweat and caring. She is so flexible with homework. And the midterms and final exam, and projects are very easy.

Genuinely one of the best professors I have ever had. He cares deeply about engaging with students and fostering critical thinking. Class isn't difficult just weekly readings that are very interesting. His lectures were incredible and he prioritizes helping you think through historical periods and ideas rather than stressing you out about grades.

Took the class online during the summer asynchronously. The class is graded on discussions and weekly papers with a final paper, and are pretty easy as long as you read the required readings (around 60 pages per week).

Class was based on lectures and discussion so participation and attendance matters but he made each lecture super fun and interesting. He was super passionate and caring about the subject and, work load was reasonable (based on readings he provided and lectures). 10/10 professor would highly recommend!
This professor is amazing, and has an easy work loud. I highly recommend taking him he is understanding, and will take the time to talk to you and answer any of your questions.

Test heavy with 70% grade occupied. 2 midterms and 1 final with few curves. Lectures attendance with iClicker questions. Discussion not that helpful but mandatory. Treat your assignments well to save your final score.

Terrible command of the material, mind numbingly boring lectures, and shockingly disorganized. Her grading criteria for homework and exams was virtually impossible to figure out, and the actual number of points deducted for a single wrong answer was absurd to the point that you could lose 10% for missing one question on a 40 question assignment.

Dr. Aarons definitely cares about her students and is really sweet. She is okay at explaining things but her exams were fairly difficult. Definitely need to read the textbook and understand concepts pretty well in order to do well in her class.

Despite this being the hardest for the BILD series he is very passionate for the subject and wants you to do well. Does go on some fun fact rambles about who discovered certain things. Very helpful and flexible when it comes to lecture attendance. Discussion was not mandatory but are very helpful. Cares about accessibility.

I think he's a great lecturer. It's very simple and direct- so despite BILD 2 being one of the more complex topics among the lower divisions, he makes it very clear as to what he expects us to understand. You can tell he cares about student feedback and the accessibility of it. Classes aren't mandatory but are the key to success in the class!

Professor Schroeder is the nicest professor you'll have. He cares a lot about his students and understands if you have personal problems that prevent you from taking an exam. I recommend taking his class for BILD 2. There is no homework but there are a few quizzes and midterms but they are relatively easy if you watch the lectures.

Honestly, you can tell that he really cares about biology. He is very passionate, and through his lecture you can tell that he is very nice. My discussion sections weren't required, but attending is useful. He isn't really a tough grader, and it would be very hard to fail the class! He's definitely one of the best in the whole bio department.

Prof. Schroeder is one of the most caring, accommodating, and fair professors that I've had at UCSD. There is no homework so you do need to hold yourself accountable for keeping up with the class material. Discussion is optional but if you actively participate it can boost your end grade.

He is a very fun and kind professor. There were a total of 3 exams (Only the highest 2 scores are counted) which were on Canvas and open note. He posts the slides for every class so attendance is not required to get a good grade as the exams are very similar. However with two 50 point tests, the margin for error is small to keep your desired grade.

Very engaging and kind professor. The class is all lecture based, and he posts the complete slides before each class. The entire class grade is made up by two exams (2 midterms and a final), there are three exams but he drops the lowest score of one. The exams are open note, so if you pay attention to the lectures and take notes it isn't difficult.

Professor Miller is a great lecturer and very passionate about animals and teaching about them, you'll watch a lot of cool videos in between slides. Attendance wasn't mandatory but lectures weren't recorded either, and your grade is best 2 of 3 50-point/50min. multiple choice online exams, nothing else. He offers 3% EC and 2% more for evals.

his lectures are very engaging and you can tell he's passionate. only down side is these lectures aren't recorded, but it's understandable. there's only two graded assignments (exams) so you have to make sure you ace them. there's also reasonable opportunities for extra credit. overall chill dude :)

One of the most put-together lectures I have attended at ucsd. Professor is very knowledgable and times his lectures super well. Contents are interesting plus I really like his style of speaking so lectures were never boring for me. The downside is he only grades by 3 exams (open notes), dropping the lowest score.

Honestly such a cool prof. 6 online tests, drops your lowest score (even if it's the “final”), and they're all online. He tells you literally everything you'd need to know for the tests in his lectures, no trick questions, very straight forward. Is super understanding and gets that we're all busy students with lives outside of this class. Great guy

Amazing, funny professor. 6 Quizzes for the quarter online. 2 homework assignments. Engaging lectures with clear lecture slides. Always able to answer questions from students even during lectures. Would definitely take again and he really wants students to succeed, especially in their biology careers.

I cannot emphasis enough how good this class and professor is. I took this as an incoming freshman and would've passed with an A if I didn't forget about 1 quiz. It's very easy to pick up on concepts and he does so in an engaging and informational way. He's so passionate and the workload is nothing. DI isn't necessary but is really good for reviews
Great professor for microbiology.

Didn't CAPEs this, but there are no words to describe how AMAZING Dr. Allen is. I feel extremely lucky to have taken a class with such an inspiring, caring, & hilarious professor who made the class SO interesting and made me want to learn. I would take another class with him in a heartbeat. Truly a gem. My only regret is wishing I took him sooner.
It's the best professor I ever had. GOAT

MAE105 The professor herself Is really nice but her notes and teaching is hard to understand and there are no podcasts. The exams are fair but I had to heavily incorporate the textbook into my study to get a decent grade. The final was more difficult than expected but she grades very nicely. If you take this prof, be prepared to work for your grade

Not an easy class but ngl my classmates should know a lot of the math coming into the class. Prof was exceedingly fair. Homework was based on lectures. Exams were easier than homework but was definitely a time crunch. The final exam was legit difficult though, but was graded much more nicely. Students complained a lot and prof tried to help them
4 A+ 's, 4A 's and 0 A- 's in a class of 88 students!

Extremely tough grader. Intimidating demeanor. Strongly defends her academic stance. Super challenging to keep up, blindingly fast speed of the class. She assumes you've learned this before and this is a review. Too theoretical, needed more walk-thru and practical examples. HW does not equal lectures nor exams.

She is very nice outside of class.

Homework is super lengthy and points are docked off very easily. Class had a C- average with a third of the class failing and there was no curve. Lectures aren't video recorded and her accent makes it harder to understand.
Hw never gives a clear description and the grading is tough, also bad at lecturing.

This professor is terrible. The code she provided has a tons of bugs, and she never realize that. She never listen to the comments from students. Once you ask a question, she will send you an email to blame you, and ask you stop asking questions. What's more, her accent is also horrible. You can never understand what she said.
Quite an easy professor. Read the book and you will do fine in midterm and final. She gives our really straightforward questions. TAs are awesome too.

Ppl whined about her good slides, she held an online survey and did good board ex.s instead; ppl whined about detailed explanations of what was going to be on MT's, she gave us a point by point list of all topics and sub topics on the final; etc.  Class was during lunch time. News flash: hungry ppl don't focus well.  Good prof.  Ungrateful kids.
Easy A as long as you tried.

the nicest prof i've had at ucsd! lightly graded on 1 project bc of covid: a (6 pages single spaced) proposal for applying the material in the class to any biomedical problem. he offers to help students find a lab, either to pursue researching their proposal or another problem they're interested in. genuinely cares abt students, i def recommend!

Professor Ratnesh is a caring professor, he has a thick accent though. The course layout, HWs, and assignments are not by any means clear and concise. you have to learn everything yourself essentially, out of the concepts that are very new and alien to students. TAs are helpful too, but no matter what, this course is very indirect and difficult.

He tries really hard to make sure that the students actually learn the material. He definitely emphasis that learning is his main goal.
