He seems like a very nice person and genuinely cares about his students. During my class we had truly awful TAs which made the class quite difficult, but that shouldn't reflect on the professor.

He is a cool professor but his accent is pretty bad. Sometimes I have no idea what he was saying. However, it was not too bad because he was basically reading off of the lecture slides so all you need to do is look over the slides. The class itself is alright. All reading material is on the course website so no textbook is needed to be purchased.
The worst professor. He ONLY reads from his notes, always rushes through them, and leaves no time for students to take notes or grasp the content
Super reasonable with grading. Good lecturer.

This professor really doesn't know how to teach. Compared to other math professors teaching the same class, his handwriting and lecture notes are so messy that you can barely read them. He writes his notes all over the place and often confuses students.
Such a great lecturer!! Best Professor I have ever had!! Class is hard but he teaches well and makes it fun. A lot of homework problems but helps you understand the course

I was forced into bigots' placement test, low score bc no sleep bc a male breaking into my dorm suite, then a huge white male blonde P-T teacher abt age 75 failed my Analytical Writing Program bc I said grey is spelling in USA- he never gave me handouts &worshiped a blond UKgirl talking all classes spelling it gray & calling me, it. RACISTdept!
Good Professor!
highly recommend to take Dr. Peter Yongs awp class
Dr. Peter is a really nice person! Easy A!
THE WORST professor I ever met in my life. It is hard for students to learn anything and pass it. Trust me, you could not recognize what his hand-writing comments are.

Professor O'Keefe is great! He is easy going with his grading, responds quickly with his emails, and provides great lectures. His quizzes and exams are based on lecture videos. Overall, great professor!

Dr. O'Keefe is a great professor. He is very responsive and cares about his students. The course format allows students to explore topics of interest via the weekly discussions and optional extra credit reports. He grades fairly, and the lectures aligned well with the textbook. I would recommend this Genetics course.

Dr. O'keefe is amazing. He gives great feedback, plenty of opportunity to excel and cares about his students. His style of instruction encourages thoughtful discourse and maximum retention of course material. He is very accessible, grades fairly and in a timely manner. One of the most compassionate professors I've ever had.

Prof.O'Keefe is very knowledgable and patient. He replies to the questions with detailed information as soon as possible. Assignment grading is never late and always fair. The class is engagig specially the weekly discussions. Extra credit reports are a good chance to improve your grade. Really enjoyed the genetics class over summer.
Lectures can be kind of dry, but he is pretty chill otherwise and gives out easy assignments. Took him for 8B which I found very fun.

I really like Professor Ben Doller! I've had him for two classes and his upper division literature classes are small, close-knit, and very enjoyable. All the projects are very creative and doable, he is also very helpful if you have any question about literature in general; he helped me create a poetry portfolio. I highly recommend taking him!

He's a very good professor, he gives great advice for the essays we are supposed to turn it for the portfolio. He's very strict with the attendance and tardiness policy in the syllabus tho, but if you don't miss lectures and participate in this class you will do well. I missed two classes and turned in three late assignments and I still got an A.

The class itself is flawed IMO, not much to do with the prof. Grades weigh heavily on prelab quizzes and reports. Quizzes are 5 Qs but they try to trick you. Reports are VERY repetitive and tedious, and feedback for me was minimal. However, the professors are accessible through piazza and quite accommodating. Still my least favorite class so far.
if you are a masochist take this class, the work load is insane and she does not know how to teach, she quickly reads over the slides and doesn't explain anything

I wont lie, the class was hard, graded strictly, and there was more work than most of my other classes. However, I think the extra work definitely helped me master the material instead of just learn it for the test. Professor Arlett is super accessible outside of class, incredibly kind and helpful, and also offers a bunch of EC which is nice.

Professor Arlett really does care about students' success in her class. She gives opportunities for EC (up to 4.5% grade boost for my class). Some of the EC came from answering peers' questions on piazza which she's very active on as well so it's easy to get questions answered. The content is hard but the amount of work and its difficulty is fair.

Professor Arlett really does care about what she is teaching. Her exams were difficult because the content itself was difficult, but they were fair. The quizzes did not weigh as much because there were different kinds of HW and participation, which helped my grade. My biggest issue was the lecture slides because they were messy and hard to discern.

Lectures are not necessary since he follows the textbook to a tee. I agree with other reviews that practice quizzes are easier than actual. Course content gets more difficult with time, but this is to be expected as proofs become a larger focus. The best thing you can do is read the book and practice. Shoutout to the grader, he was super fast.

First 5 weeks easy and chill, then once you cannot drop, everything turns 180 and he starts giving 20 proof questions per week and undoable 2nd midterm. Sly professor indeed as said in other comments. No partials on quizzes and lectures are terrible. Please do not get baited.

This is a sly professor. He tries to be nice before the final evaluation, giving easy homework and midterms, to get good evaluation from students. After everyone give good evaluations, his final exam is super hard and can not be regraded.
Professor Xu gives good lectures and mock quiz, but his final is much more difficult than the quizes and hw. Final will draw down the total grade greatly.

Concepts on lectures can be quite unclear. He solved lots of practice problems but it's difficult to apply them. He gives mock quizzes then makes the actual quizzes much harder. For the final, even knowing exactly what you're doing, you won't finish the test and there so no curve for it...

Dr. G is very straightforward. The grading scale is clear and she even gives EC for office hours and did a 10 point curve. Your grade is entirely dependent on how much you understand and put into the content. There are a good amount of assignments, however, they all really help cushion your grade. Attendance is mandatory because she does iClicker.

Honestly she's not that bad of a lecturer but she kind of just reads off her slides. Her slides are detailed but she doesn't give you any time to write it down so be ready to have her lecture slides pulled up. She has 3 midterms and 1 final and in every midterm so far there have been inconsistent grading techniques and questions about her wording.

Professor Glasgow enjoys biology and her research. She transmits that love for science through her lectures and presents real-world examples. She emphasizes critical thinking and having spent time on the material she covers during lecture in order to do well in exams. She is accessible outside of class and is willing to engage with students.
I would study and take notes going by the learning objectives. The subject is a lot of information, but staying on top of lecture notes and answering the objectives is key!

I really enjoyed her lectures, but her class was so overwhelming. Weekly quizzes, Bio journals, sections were mandatory, section problem sets, and midterms every two weeks. Midterms and final are mostly free response but some multiple choice. If you're going to take her class make sure to put in the work to keep up with the material.

Each & every assignment had very broad instructions & when emailing for more clarification, not much info was given. Then points get taken off for each assignment & no comments or feedback is left at all! So you're losing points and you have no idea why!!! So incredibly frustrating and pisses me off bc then you can't even improve or change things.

Love Ms. Wartell. Had her for GIS and Beer in the Urban economy. She is extremely nice and knows a lot about what she teaches. She also cares about her students--she even followed up with me about an assignment I did for another class because she was interested in my research. She is definitely the kind of professor you wanna go grab a beer with.
Really accomplished prof. Methods training is rigorous.
Great class!

I took him for MAE 113 this quarter because I am pretty sure they took him out of retirement to cover for Professor Zadeh. But he mainly just copied off of textbooks and gave like four difficult homework assignments. His lectures were those once-a-week 3-hour lectures, but our final had content from 3 chapters that we never got practice on.

I took MAE101 A and B with professor Bahadori, he's wonderful. He doesn't only teach examples but the concept behind the subject; if you get the concept you'll do great on the exam. HWs ad\nd exams are fair and are based on the material from his lectures. highly recommend him!

Fantastic professor! Probably my favorite. He's a very kind and knowledgeable professor as he teaches so many classes. Had him for MAE2, MAE11, and MAE 101B. Read the textbook while he lectures for deeper understanding. Follow along/do the example problems in the textbook. Attend the problem sessions. Do the homework. That's all you need.
Tests are easy, homework is hard and thoroughly graded, great professor though.

Professor Bahadori did an excellent job of simplifying the fluid Mech materials and teaching 7 chapters in a 5-week summer session. He taught the concept very well and his exams were based on that, so if you attend the lectures and grasp the concept behind the examples you can solve all other problems. He's very well educated, I'll take him again.
Not best lecturer

Summer Session 2. 3hr class twice a week. Slow talker, but if you're interested in supreme court cases or other important cases in the US, the class will be interesting. Classes are recorded. Grade depends on reading assignment (graded on completion) midterm paper, project presentation, and final (project & final based on same thing). TA is great.

Just make sure you attend ALL lectures. The only information he gives you that's helpful for the essay exams are in those lectures. And make sure you're paying attention and taking good notes because the lectures are not recorded. Visit the TA too! since the grade mostly depends on the TA.
Do the group projects well and should be good to go. Lectures can be dense sometimes.

The class material itself had a lot of controversial topics but prof Golan was very neutral and expressed arguments on both sides. He really wanted students to understand both sides of topic. He makes the lecture very interactive although he doesn't post his slides online. He gives 2 papers and group presentation.
Class was quite disorganized... It was never clear what was due when, and lectures were hard to follow. Professor Matsumura seems kind though. Just wish the class was more organized and structured.
I did not find her lectures very engaging, but I thought the class topics were interesting.

Prof Matsumura is so kind and cares for her students. The lectures are interesting even though she can get a bit off track sometimes. The class can be taken fully online which is nice, but going in person is honestly worth it and can help with the online discussion posts. Highly recommend if you're interested in Japanese history or need a GE.

Recommend to take her class. Most of UCSD professors are crap but she is different from those types. Of course, you have lots of reading materials that she has to offer. However, as long as you'll put your efforts into it and prove her of your work, you'll be just fine. You'll also learn about current issues.
Super chill and nice prof! You basically give yourself a grade (like seventh's SYN sequence). She rambles A LOT but its still relatively interesting. Try to go to her class and talk to her!

Good professor, his lectures are really interesting. If you come to the class and pay attention the assignments, essay and final shouldn't be hard and he is really funny. the midterm was super easy and take home, essay was a bit harder and final is answering 5 questions that were cover in class

His lectures are very interesting and he definitely makes a lot of effort to keep the students engaged with the course material. The course could be overwhelming for some folks, however, if you are on top of the course material, you should be good to go.

The lectures are really interesting - plus most of the test material is based on lecture (so I wouldn't skip out even though he doesn't take attendance). He tries to make exams easy during the quarter so that more attention can  be put towards the major assignments. He's also pretty funny.

This professor assigns long readings and doesn't have a clear grading criteria, which makes it tough to stay awake and pay attention when there's a lack of structure. Additionally, he needs to be more reachable and clear; he doesn't answer emails or messages at all, making it hard to get the support we need.

I took his course (Mexican Literature before 1910) to learn about my Mexican heritage despite history being my worst subject. This professor is amazing in his lectures. He explains everything in great detail and encourages productive conversations about the readings. He ties the course material wonderfully. Take his course; you won't regret it! :)

TWS22 was alright. Lots of readings and films that were sometimes hard to understand. Make sure to read because he expects participation. Paper is a big chunk of your grade, but he wasn't too harsh of a grader. The two midterms were alright, make sure to study for the second one. Weekly film reviews, don't forget to do them if you choose this class

The class is overall pretty interesting. The readings and films are intriguing. You should read because he would test you on quotes from the texts on the midterm. There are 2 midterms and 1 final paper. The paper is a major bulk of your grade, it worths about 40%. There are also film reviews every week. Recording his lectures would help to do well.
if you are taking this class for GE and for P/NP, do not take it! lots of readings. class is kinda demanding too much out of you. class is boring too.

Best professor I ever seen so far, she really doesn't care about what major you are or if you have taken a dance class before or not, just try to follow the others movements as much as you can, and then you'll be fine. Most of the classmates there are friendly too, strongly recommended! Love Pro Mack!!!

The best professor ever! Not hard class at all. Really enjoyed it. If your not a complete nerd that is afraid of dancing infront of a few people, consider taking this class!!! She really cares about students

I took Professor Pickett in Spring of 24. EASIEST PROFESSOR FOR BILD 1 BY FAR. Materials covered are not difficult, all lecture material appears on quizzes (which are 60-odd questions long), and the final was not cumulative but lasted three hours (I got out in 30 mins). She's really kind, really accommodating, and I highly recommend taking her.

Really kind and helpful professor when you are having a hard time in the class she is really friendly and do not be afraid to send out an email. Pay attention on lectures as the pre lab quizzes do reflect them in broad and sometimes very specific details.

I love Professor Pickett!! Her exams are extremely representative of the material you learn in class and she tells you exactly what types of questions will be on the exams. She is very supportive of you as a student and gives you many resources to help. I wish she could teach all of my bio classes!
Literally so chill, she's great and also is very supportive of students finding labs and different opportunities through providing useful information!!

Literally only saw her once a week but she was nice. Spent most of the time with the TA and I was thankful to have gotten a great TA so it was a fun class. Groups matter because you spend the whole 3 hour lab working together. You don't get to choose them but I was lucky to have gotten a group that I worked well with. Great group = great class.

Don't take,really bad at explaining concepts, doesn't answer questions in class because he wanted to "challenge" us. Our whole class asked him to post the answer key for the work we did in class so we could study it (ungraded) and he said no. Grade is based on all quizzes and a final. The mean score for the final was 37% if that tells you anything.

The class is marketed as an "intro" and is said to be suitable for those with no coding experience, but his expectations are way too high considering the material & format was new for many of us. The midterm was ridiculously hard (see reddit). HW was impossible to finish, we're talking consecutive all-nighters & still barely getting passing scores.

Zach comes off as an intelligent young man but his expectations for students are way too high. His homework is meant for students who have taken some sort of coding class. His lectures are way too fast given that it is a 50 min class. I recommend not to take him.

This rating is for MAE 101c. No credit for homework assignments, entire grade based on three exams and small portion dedicated to participation. Studying for this class was difficult due to the lack of resources provided by the professor. However, overall the lectures were well done, but not well defined in terms of course content.

It was an amazing course heavily focused on actual learning. Lecture contents are tailored to get you upto speed with all the complex equations/concepts followed by sample numericals on which take-home assignments are based. There are participation points for group presentations, literature reviews and discussions covering various applications!

Blue book exams were rough, but you can have a cheat sheet so it was manageable. Good lecturer, but the book he wrote (the primary material for the class) is not so great as it decides to implement math formulas for some reason (you don't have to remember them tho)
but overall not bad, quite enjoyable. Major downside are the attendance quizzes.

Professor Lake is by far one of my favorite and most notable professors I've had throughout my college career. The class is lecture-heavy and deals with some complex topics, but it isn't for nothing. Definitely, a class that taught me a lot and left a lasting impact on how I think about foreign politics. Very logical!
most interesting class at ucsd. though pretty tough -- just do your reading.

Professor Lake is an amazing professor that is very knowledgeable about his subject. In-class Clicker questions each class (10%) and 3 papers (90%). The lectures are history heavy but very interesting and he is open to questions. The material is presented in a very unbiased way which is hard to do with this subject. Would definitely take again!

David lake is one of the most logical professor I have at UC San Diego, and I really enjoyed the time work with him. It was a shame for me to get an A-,since I mainly lose my points on clicker questions testing on reading materials. Just read the book, and it is the answer to everything!
Really great professor and clear. Excellent materials. Only wish he taught more classes!

Genetics course- FYI - Dr. Wong is cordial but he does not grade assignments in a timely manner. It is Finals week and he hasn't even graded the midterm or any assignments from the past 7 weeks.Too late to know what you need to score on the final or improve,because there is nothing left to work on- no feedback.I have an A based off 3 weeks of work.

The structure of the class is interesting because Dr. Barbaro makes the lectures while Dr. Wong is the one who grades all work and handles all questions regarding the class. Dr. Wong was responsive and offered good feedback. He responded to emails promptly and was a very fair and reasonable grader. He offered good explanations to material questions

Love Professor Martin, great lecturer and incredibly engaging. All readings are posted on Canvas and there's a written midterm and final, but very straightforward and chill if you keep up with lectures, which are uploaded. One of my favorite professors in USP.

If I had just a fraction of this man's excitement and passion for anything in this world I would consider myself lucky. I could listen to him lecture all day. His class is so easy if you read the material. He makes his exams in accordance to the readings and they are impossible to fail.

There's a lot of reading for this course, but he does provide all the PDF's so you don't need to buy any of the books. The reading can be a lot but if you go to lecture he does a good job of breaking it down and explaining it. The only work is to go to mandatory discussion and then you're graded on two midterms and a final. Overall I recommend.
I absolutely loved this professor. Attendance is not mandatory, exams are just essays you are given a week to do, brilliant and caring man. Lectures are fascinating and keep you engaged.

WOW! I'm a stem major so naturally I was hoping this class would be easy (gpa boosters). This course was one of my favorite! Reading is required for weekly quizzes but all open note so they were simple! We had two essays assigned, 5 pages each. The content and lectures were both so interesting. Highly recommend, I'll miss this class

He's an excellent professor and I'm surprised by my progress, especially in reading and writing Arabic. the grammar portion is significantly harder, and if you miss one class it makes a difference. He truly cares about teaching Arabic and I can tell he wants all of us to succeed. El Cheddadi goes out of his way to help. Definitely recommend him.
Youniss was such a gem to have as a teacher.

After getting a bachelors degree and an MBA, I have to say, this professor was by far the best. Professor El Cheddadi makes Arabic so easy to learn and truly encourages everyone not to be scared to speak up and try. We all looked forward to each one of his classes and made it fun. I highly recommend Professor El Cheddadi for any class he teaches.
Really nice and patient, grades easy, and great at teaching

Youniss is the Mr. Rogers of the Arabic professors. Super kind and patient. Every class he always ask how's your day like he genuinely cares. He is well organized and does not overwhelm you with material. He shows interest in your own life and also facilitates an environment that encourages making friends with your classmates.

Great professor with humor! Quizzez but no set due date with unlimited takes. Final and midterm online. In person lectures but provides videos for those who don't go. Passionate about their subject and is nice.

I took am talking her classes for my major requirements, and she is amazing!!! Very engaging and understandable lectures! There are a good amount of cumulative quizzes on the subject matter, so make sure to come prepared for those, and I would recommend keeping up attendance because she explains the subject very well.
Such a wonderful instructor. Always available to help you and is very understanding. She is extremely clear about what is expected of you and outlines everything.

Had to take her cuz of stupid GE but wow she is so amazing. She made Latin enjoyable and just made my day every time I saw her. She's the most caring, kindest professor who just wants her students to find a love and appreciation for Latin like she does. No need to be worried about her bringing your GPA down either. Such a wonderful person.

Dr. Murray is a phenomenal teacher. She is funny and cares so much about the students in her class - that they actually learn things rather than just memorize and pass. She is super welcoming and helpful and treats every question asked the same - no one has to worry if their question is dumb or not which is really nice.
labs were a little confusing, but he is accessible outside of class and TAs always have office hours to help out with any questions.

He's a really nice professor! He cares a lot about his students and visits labs often to check on how students are doing. Lectures are straight-forward and labs can be challenging, but his TAs are always willing to help.
He tends to reiterate things in lecture, but otherwise he's a pretty good professor. He's always wanting people to come to office hours though.
Awesome course.
Good guy

Recommend taking this class 10/10. She makes an effort to get to know you as a person and a human being within the first two weeks of class. Also, she doesn't make you feel bad for not knowing the language as well compared to your peers. Furthermore, partner/group work makes you feel like you belong in the class and makes it super interactive.

LIHL 112 one of my fav classes I've taken at UCSD, had Tita Letty the first quarter she transferred from UH to UCSD! I already knew filipino before going to this class but some of my friends in the class barely understood the langauge and got a higher grade than me in the class. Placement test is easy dont be scared, just a convo with the prof.

Absolutely horrible professor. Has no idea what she's doing with teaching and with using canvas. Many students were very confused when things were due and what the requirements were. Didn't post a single rubric the entire year. Didn't have any clue what our grades in the class were until week 7 or 8. Lots of class time wasted waiting around for her

Overall: Tedious and information-packed. He's kind and knowledgable, but his lectures are very dense and he doesn't spend more than a few minutes topics we could probably spend an entire lecture on. I have a scientific background but even I couldn't keep up. Homework is mostly just data analysis. He never assigned us anything from the textbook.

I was a part of his FA23 class. I personally enjoyed his lectures and teaching style, as the professor for the first in the 41 series, he does a fairly decent job at preparing the class for beyond. He was very open to helping students during office hours / help sessions, and his exams were fair.

I personally hated his teaching style. He fits into this very specific genre of professor that creates lecture slides in comic sans. It's hard to follow what he says because he just reads off the slides in a monotone voice. The lectures were not helpful. Just skip lecture and do the practice problems.

took him for summer session 2. The slides he provided were not useful. 400pts total, 200pts for midterm & 200pts for final. no crib sheet. test were very hard average of the class in the low 70 points (out of 200pts). class recordings picked up some rude comments he said after class. would not take again.
Intentionally made first test too hard to make students fail after telling us the test would be easy. laughed when we all failed

I really liked his slides/lectures, if you pay attention to all of them, and do all the recommended practice problems, the class is about 3-4 or less hours outside of class a week for an A. The grade is heavily curved. I would not give him a five, because he does not feel very kind, but he is certainly not mean, he just does his job satisfactorily.

He was overall an alright professor. Taught what was required, sometimes is confusing in his explanations. Often need to self-study through homework and textbook. Homework often was very difficult. Mandatory discussions. His tests were fair (and much easier) and were based on lecture content.

Many advanced terms beyond knowledge. No podcast, so I learn mostly from other professors(podcasts) Lots of self-study. Bad thing: you gets nothing from lectures Good thing: If you watch podcast and others don't, you are ahead of the game. However, I won't consider it "good" because I am still confused about many concepts, be aware if you take him.

Teaches straight out of the textbook but doesn't go further in depth about it. This class is only bearable because of the other prof co-teaching with him, so the tests aren't as hard and he originally was not going to allow a cheat sheet. No podcasts/online notes too. Despite attending lect, I learned everything from the previous quarter's podcast.

Lecture attendance was not mandatory but discussion was. Did not learn anything from lectures. To properly understand the material I resorted to watching Prof Quarfoort's podcasts (which are awesome btw, great professor). Mackall moved very quickly, not taking the time to explain. Grades are only based on 2 midterms, final, and weekly homework.

Don't waste your time...take this class if your willing to show up for the sake of attendance the leave and go figure out all the concepts from other resources. Horrible at explaining concepts and refused to explain difficult example problems during lecture multiple times; has superiority complex and doesn't care to actually teach anyone anything.

Dr. Branka was absolutely amazing. This was the toughest class I took and the only way I even passed with an A - she made very lecture so interesting and inviting. This is designed for students who are genuinely interested in the subject, not just interested in passing. She was kind enough to let me into the lab after hours to see special specimens

Branka is a good teacher, but grades a bit harshly. There is A LOT of reading and writing, so I would not take this as an upper division GE requirement. As a bio anthro major I really enjoyed the material of the class. She really cares about her students, so go to office hours and she will help. I wish I did it more.

DO NOT TAKE FOR GE/UD SIGWRITING

Her lectures are really fast, but also really diagram heavy, so you miss a lot of info. She tends to ramble on things that aren't on the slides. Class is basically the exams and the paper, and the exams are so ambig. in content. Is it on the slides? During her ramble? Reading? Had to read 40 pages first day.

I've had this professor for 5 classes. She is outstanding. Her upper division Biological Anthropological classes can be a little dense for non-Life Sciences majors so it might not be a good pick for a GE requirement.
I found her unapproachable. She answered emails quickly if I had a question but they were condescending and very unhelpful. Not a nice class or professor.

Can't find a better professor for this course/topic. He is very passionate about research, teaching and understands the core contents. Material was useful, and final presentations were focused on newest methods/tech. Discussion with professors after lectures were also inspiring. 100% recommend taking.

This class was pretty easy, there was just a lot of lecture material. There is no final but instead there is a final project that you have to do in groups of 3. Everyone in the class did get As. This professor just delegate things to his TAs whom are not that responsive. He's not too bad though, very sweet.
Didnt learn anything. worst clas ever taken

Terrible professor. Lectures were verbatim by the book, slow, and often more confusing than just actually reading the book. He was not clear on his grades, with grading for problems varying between students. He put all his recorded lectures online at the beginning of the quarter and just had his IA do all the other work and she was even worse.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCES. His work might be incredibly easy, copied out of the book, but he is by far the worst professor I have ever taken in my now 4 years of college. He didn't have any contact with students, was incredibly hard to understand, did not explain anything, and worst of all his IA was clueless.

Her lectures and readings were relevant and engaging. If you attend half the lectures and do the readings, you'll be fine. The epic comparative analysis was a big task for an introductory class though. She is passionate, open and caring so take her if you want to learn a lot as she teaches at an advanced level.

Pretty enjoyable course overall. It can get out of hand if lecture aren't done. So your grade is really dependent on if you do the readings before class, which can be heavy at times. Lecture are cool if you read what you needed to read.

Her lectures are super interesting and she is pretty understanding. However, her instructions for assignments lack explanation. She expects a lot more than she lets on and is a strict grader. Ask her a LOT of questions about exactly what she wants because she has specific demands but unclear and vague explanations. Wouldnt take this class again.

GREAT professor, and an easy A as long as you attend lecture, do the readings, and put in a decent amount of effort. Final was a video group project. Lecture is super interesting, keeps the class engaged by asking questions. Grade just depends on your TA.

Extremely interesting course that is unlike any others at UCSD. Lectures are done in the lab room before lab in a discussion style. Procedures are explained before each lab with no required pre-lab making labs very manageable. Reports do not require that you were perfect with the experiments, rather that you understand what you are doing.

Honestly this is by far the best lab that i have taken at UCSD, professor Murre is extremely nice. The lab reports r graded extremely fairly and the final is SO manageable. We work with mice for 5 weeks and by the time you are done you will be an expert in taking out mice thymuses. The experiments we do are literally what Murre himself published.

Murre himself is a pleasant man, and I enjoyed his pre-lab explanations of the immune system. However, I cannot recommend the lab itself. The lab manual is lacking, there are no guidelines for lab reports and half of each lab period is devoted to counting cells. Take a lab that actually helps foster your growth as a student.

I just saw my grade and is flip out.  I seriously do not recommend this class at all.  I worked my butt off and ended up with a B. Lab reports due after every lab with no guidelines so the TA gets to grade whatever and however they want.  The professor doesn't care, he just leaves after 15 minutes lectures. Finals were ridiculously hard!

Okay so this lab sucks, final was terribly hard, he does not do regrades even for calculation errors.  He can't speak proper english, and He only gave two A's out of the 24 studednts total in lab.  Just avoid at all cost, save yourself from the pain of having to deal with him.  Even if you know what's going on in lab his class is still impossible!

The professor himself is a nice person but the work is overly complicated. The TAs aren't helpful during studio time at all either. I would think twice before taking this class. also if you don't work well in groups I would suggest you not take this class either. There's 4 group projects over the course of the quarter.
Easy chill 2 unit class, Bussell is really sweet and cares about her students

USP 142a is my favorite class that I've taken at UCSD! Professor Bussell is incredible and makes the daunting topic of homelessness seem more approachable and really changed my outlook on it. Highly recommend everyone to take this class, Professor Bussell is the best!

Very caring, knowledgeable, and overall great person and professor. She is really kind and cares about students. Class material is a bit dense, so you will need to study for exams. There is quite a bit of homework especially in the second half of the quarter, but is manageable if you stay on top of the class. Attend lectures and you will be fine.
Super nice professor. Had nice lectures and the assignments were pretty easy. Just keep up with the work and reading and you will do well.

She gave two huge assignments with about two weeks to prepare them and one of them required you to read more than 100-page documents so not a very pleasant experience. Apart from that, I actually really enjoyed the class and the material in it. She was nice and really good at teaching the content and adding current events to the course.

I really don't know where to begin. She is very caring, understanding & helpful. Responds promptly to emails. She will make time to meet if struggling or have questions. A fair grader & cares about her students succeeding in this course. Make sure to pace yourself & try not to fall behind. Overall an amazing course with an amazing Professor.

Professor Nocera is a very great and kind teacher. I needed an extension and she gave me one even at a late notice. She is very easy to reach out to and get in contact with. The class overall was semi-difficult since it is a lot of content but if you can reach out for help. Overall would take again with Professor Nocera.

Very thorough explanations and lots of great pictures for clarification. There is a lot of information covered in this course, but I got 100% on all the HW's and EC since grading on these is based on completion (the HW also helps prepare for the tests). There are textbooks you could choose from, but I only used mine a couple times for homework.

Professor Judith is my favorite Hematology professor. She responds to messages promptly and is always accessible outside of class. Her clear grading criteria make it easy to understand expectations. The exams are challenging but fair, and I retain what I learn thanks to her ability to break down complex material into digestible parts.

Amazing class structure and lectures provided were helpful for the exams. Be sure to take advantage of the additional resources that are posted on Canvas to help prepare for the exams and assignments. Do not wait til the last minute to take the exams and assignments and pace yourself accordingly.
i did not enjoy
not good!

Very inexperienced professor who is trying his best in the first couple of terms teaching. Pays very close attention to research and advice from other professors to become better which is very encouraging. Sets very ambiguous questions on exams, and in class he can't really gauge what the class doesn't understand and how to explain. Fairly nervous.

He lets you bring cribb sheets to exams, which is super helpful and honestly was the only thing that gave me an A on the midterms. His final was pretty challenging, though I think that may have only been during the quarter I took him because other students said he got easier. The ONLY professor I recommend for such a hard class as 20E.
He is a new professor, but he is great for 20A and is accessible outside class.
Lectures were boring. Tests were easy

Super nice guy I went to his office hours just to talk to him about future planning and college. iClicker lectures and mandatory discussions but the content is very straightforward. He explains his slides well and has example problems for each section that he works through in class. His quizzes are very similar to the homework and practice quizzes.

Fun demos during lectures that were relevant to class topics. Not the most coherent lectures with few examples that were often worked very quickly. Podcasts were posted, so it was easy enough to go back and understand content. Written HW graded on effort. Quizzes and Final were extremely reflective of HW and Lecture slides so they were not too hard
Didn't lean much, but the tests were easy

Great professor overall! Curves the class so you only need a 60% to get a C. Great professor explains the materials well but assumes that you know a little. Grade consist of clicker participation, homework and 3 test, where he drops the lowest. Lecture can be a bit vague, so read the textbook. Homework is graded on completion rather than accuracy.
We didn't receive grades until week 6/7. We didn't know how we were doing in the class and no one responded to any of our emails.

She led part of the class like 3 times so this class is VERY TA dependent but I got a really good one so it was okay. She seems really nice, just some of the activities she would lead felt kind of useless (ex. counting to 20 where each student can only say a number once and if two students speak at the same time you have to restart)
She is very sweet and encouraging. She helped me through my first quarter when I was really struggling. She's a little all over the place, but also gives you room to be not always be on your A game.

You'll never meet Kim, it's completely taught by the TA. My TA was amazing, you can tell they're inspired to teach. It's all acting scenes, not much else is graded. If acting in front of everyone isn't your thing, then don't take, but open to everyone else.

Maybe saw the professor once, TA does everything. My TA was accommodating when a personal matter arose. Class is fine if your group members participate. The midterm was free response and could be graded however the TA wanted. Will have to watch plays outside of class and practice your scenes. Written midterm and a scene for your final.

I don't know what to write, as I have never once met Professor Walsh but she runs this class? No, the TAs run this class and it is all over if you have a not-so-great TA. The TA grades everything from exams, participation, and everything else in this course. It might have been easy over zoom, but this class is my least favorite.
Uncomfortable to be around and snobby. Didn't really like his attitude.
Do not take this professor! Bias and will ruin your gpa!

I actually took Math 103A and Math 103B under Prof. Chung.  He's an exceptionally caring Professor that UCSD ended up losing their hands on, which is super unfortunate; he's tough as hell and his exams are literal hell on Earth, but he will sit with you for hours and help you understand until you get it.  Love this prof!

For some reason I cannot select Math 103 as the classes, but trust me, he is a wonderful professor and I loved his Math 103 series so much! He has such an enthusiasm in teaching and most of the students love him so much. In my class, there are many student choose him as professor for consecutive three quarters. his class content is hard though

Be ready to read a lot of textbook materials, and prepare for the presentations. The in-class presentations will be counted as attendance. Homework and exams are easy compared with other Math 109 classes. There are weekly 5-minute progress checks that weigh heavily(4% each). Really responsible professor and always responsive by email or piazza.

The two midterms and final exam only make up 45% of the grade and there are many easy assignments throughout the quarter that are basically free points. Our classroom didn't have podcast capabilities but many of the lectures you have to attend in-person anyway to take weekly quizzes or give a presentation about the textbook.

Prof Jordan's Esperanto seminar was a breeze - just show up and do the readings. With the free textbook and helpful resources like unstuck ai, acing this class was a piece of cake. Highly recommend for an easy credit!

I took the Esperanto seminar - absolutely loved it! Prof Jordan is super passionate and literally the only thing you have to do for this class is show up and do the readings. 10/10 would recommend him for any seminar.

I took this class Fall 2023 out of interest (the theme was Esperanto & The Anthropology of Language). Really chill class you only have to read one or two articles per week (the rest are optional) and write one paragraph about what you learned/what interested you. Prof Jordan teaches just for fun and is literally a foundation of knowledge.
Jordan is one of the smartest professors on the UCSD campus. You want to show up to the lectures, they're fascinating. MMW gets a bad rap, but Prof. Jordan makes it really cool. 11/10

Jordan is clearly very passionate about history, but his tests, which is the majority of your grade, are ridiculously difficult & about very specific facts he says in passing during lectures. On the bright side, his clicker questions come straight from online quizzes, he developed his own shorter textbook readings and he does offer extra credit.

She is very passionate about her work! She provides all of the readings for free! The exam has an extra credit opportunity, which is 30% of ur grade. I never read all the readings but her study guide for the class helped me get over 100% She is so knowledgeable about it all, if u don't do the readings go to class she answers everything!!!

Professor Rhoades is wonderful at teaching, and is one of the main reasons linear algebra captured my interest so much. The class was really interesting and it was easy to follow his lectures. If you missed class, podcasts and posted notes were always there. The HW wasn't too much and the exams were fair.

Receiving student's response that second midterm were hard, he lowered # of problems and level of difficulty on final. Very caring, always willing to explain things in OH. Though, MATH 18 is a class with a lot of abstract concepts so textbook is still necessary. Testing yourself about concepts/sorting concepts through is helpful for T/F questions.

Professor Rhoades is a wonderful teacher whose lectures are clear and engaging. He's very funny and posted his lecture notes to follow along. Podcasts were also uploaded. He repeated questions in class and frequently checked on the class for questions. HW was very easy with infinite attempts. Tests were very difficult with a lot of T/F sections.

A good professor and lectures are basic. I would say test heavy but you have the option to drop your lowest midterm for a higher weight on your final. Lectures don't cover the entire scope of some concepts and are confusing at times, so discussions/OH are a must if you don't clearly understand something as the basics.

Rhoades is a great professor, and his lectures are both helpful and entertaining; that said, I can't justify giving him a 5 because his tests are unreasonably difficult. All other aspects of the course were great: helpful homeworks and discussions, and an easy matlab component, but the tests were full of curveballs and tough conceptual questions.

He uses chalk to teach so the pace is not fast. The practice question during class and homework were quite similar to the midterms. He gave three midterms and no final exam. The midterms were not easy but manageable. I will suggest go to lectures/watch recording to understand the in-class practice, and go through hw before exams.

Took his class in spring, would not recommend at all. Around half the students in the class failed, completing all the homework didn't even affect your grade, didn't even give a curve because one person got 100%. He is nice but not good at teaching the concepts so you'll have to learn almost everything on your own. Very stressful class to take.

He's good at teaching things given how hard the class is, you're gonna need to do practice problems but he's always willing to help and answer any questions. Really cool, down to earth guy. Sometimes he pronounces things weirdly due to his Spanish nativeness. I recommend if you want to learn good, not easy A.
Hard grader and doesn't like to curve. Cares for the students and tries his best at teaching but the class will be mainly self taught.

To put it bluntly, he cannot teach. Any content covered in class is a recitation from the textbook. There's 3 midterms which are 75% of your grade, the rest is HW. His curve at the end was barely anything which was a huge injustice to his classes where the average score wasn't even a passing grade. He's a kind enough person but a bad professor.
Wonderful professor, never regret taking his class

His lectures were pretty clear and the class overall was not hard. Like other comments said, his homework can be confusing sometimes, but if you go to his office hours, they should not be too challenging. No cheatsheet for the two midterms, but no final exam, which is a plus.

He is such a clear professor and one of the best that I have had at UCSD. He is very accessible outside of the classroom and very thoughtful in his responses. His grading is very fair and his exams are not curveballs as he makes sure you are prepared to take midterm and final. Workload might be a little heavy but the staff will help greatly!

A great person, but a horrible lecturer. There are often times where he will go off on rants somewhat related to the material, but ultimately just uses about 40 minutes of the 110 minute lecture as filler for time. His requirements and grading criterion are somewhat vague so it often leads to you getting docked points for arbitraty things.
amazing professor! He is smart, patient and takes time to explain things to you. Best professor ever!

Don't take this professor. He doesn't grade anything, posts assignments late without notice or extension, and is a boring lecturer. The projects are incredibly time-consuming and even if 25% are interesting, it doesn't justify the amount of BS work you need to do. I beg you to not take this class.

He is the best lecturer I have ever had.  Even if you don't want to take the class for credit I recommend just sitting in on his lectures (they are that good).  The first project is the hardest one, so try to tough it out until you get to the next few.  Can't really prepare too much for the exams.  TA wasn't so great.

He is a terrible teacher. Just look at the capes, more F's then A's. I understand that maybe a few students might slip through the cracks in a tough course but when many students constantly get failing grades then some of the blame has to be placed on the teaching staff. I retook this class with a different professor and actually learned a lot more
Top 3 classes I've taken at UCSD, but easily the hardest and most time-consuming.  The projects are amazing and the material is superb, but man is it difficult.

I hated this class, probably more than any other I have taken at UCSD. It was not because the course was time consuming, because it really was not. It was because the material was awful. I really did not feel like I got anything valuable form this class or the prof.  We had to use Haskell for the homework, which was a horrible decision.

do not take her class. her lectures remain unclear. she only wants specific answers and if you dont provide her with those answers, she shuts down any ideas or thought you have. she also have favorites in class and will treat you differently if she doesn't choose you as her favorite. one of the most impartial and rude professors.

To be graded well, you basically have to agree with what she says. She refuses to listen to other ideas or anything that is different than her opinion. She is very stubborn. She is a very my way or the high way type of professor and won't take any criticism. She also hates on china and india in her class too much. giving lowkey racism.

Honestly one of the best profs I've had here. She is funny and kind and her lectures are engaging. The midterm was challenging, but if you take notes and ask questions you should be okay. She gives good feedback on the work we do and really wants students to do well. The final project was rather large so make some time for it. Would def take again.

Textbook is technically mandatory but you can easily get by without reading. Midterm was the only challenging part of the quarter so make sure you take good notes. She is a good lecturer and a really fun person. Attendance is very important.
Really kind and wanted everyone to succeed

Very nice and understanding teacher, also doesn't care if you turn in things a bit after the midnight due dates. Gives good and positive feedback on assignments. Some of the course guidelines or assignments aren't the best but not her fault as she doesn't set the curriculum, and sometimes she makes alternate assignments you can do instead.

Syn 1 is sevenths writing course so attendance being mandatory isn't her fault. She is very understanding, doesn't care if you turn things late as long as it's not too crazy, within the next 24hrs just let her know. She is a great professor and cares about her students and tries to make them comfortable. All of my classmates want her again for syn2

wouldn't recommend this prof at all. exams do not match what is really taught. she tries to trick you with the exams. imo theya re written unfairly... even the ta is like this question is tricky no cap. she doesnt know how to teach or write a fair exam. stay to experiments.

The professor assigns an unreasonable amount of weekly assignments:
- asynchronous readings (100 pages + sometimes)
- pre-recorded lecture videos (1-2.5 hrs which you MUST watch in order to complete a weekly assignment based on the lecture recordings)
- Group assignments with weekly deliverables

Class is extremely disorganized. I would AVOID.

Professor Yang was the best. He has quite of a thick accent but he teaches really well. He gives quizzes during the "lab" session(not mandatory) which are collaborative. He gave us two midterms and it was open notes and was really similar to all the quizzes and HW. The final's a MATLAB group project of your choice. Overall I would HIGHLY recommend.
looks like he didn't spend time preparing for the class. It just waste of everyone's time.
You won't learn a lot from this class. Basically read PPT or worst. Poor quality

Prof. Yang is a very nice person and he is always willing to help. His tests were just collections of the problems that we did in class or homework and they were not hard. He is also very approachable after class and talk to him would make learning very easy.

He's nice but not too great of a professor. At the end of every lecture he does quizzes that are open note and open book, and that's how both midterms are like as well. The way he explains things can be further confusing. The final is cumulative and is all completely on paper, you are not allowed to use MATLAB at all.

Not required: Team Project, Rady Lab, and asking questions in class for participation points like other MGT classes. His class is a straightforward class where you study and get grades based on exams. Your grades will reflect the effort you put into studying. Make sure to attend lectures because he doesn't use textbooks for the exam.

HW gives you extra points but is just busy work. Focus on the spreadsheets he provides you in each module, they reflect the MT and finals. He is a kind person but could work on teaching. He speaks very fast and cuts students off when asking questions. Talk to the TA, they will help explain material. Would take him again, content is straightforward

Very nice as a person but a very difficult professor. For a lower division class it was exceeding difficult. The midterm had a failing average and a third of the class got a 0% on it. Hard subject but would recommend taking it with another professor.
it's the horrible course I've ever taken.
Very nice professor, but not the best at teaching. He talks very fast and expects you to know the material after one example.

Dr. Reyes loves it when you come prepared with insightful questions, she really cares about her students well being. She can come off a little strong sometimes but she is very understanding if you talk to her.

I honestly think that the tests are not too bad, and he gives out study guides. Just study those, and you'll be fine. Yes, he skips over some stuff in slides (but never tested us on those skipped materials) and sounds extremely monotoned, but the things he talked about in class is very useful for starting a business and in the long run.

Worthless, useless, and extremely agonizing to listen to. Bland, boring, and a dinosaur. I think he should be fired. If you want excellence from your students you should be a model. Overall, a big disappointment and lazy professor.

He is sweet, but not a good professor. His lectures are short and he skips through so much of the material because it seems easy, but then he makes the tests extremely hard and complicated. The questions are tricky and he didn't teach more than half of the things on the tests. The homework is also irrelevant. I didn't learn anything in this class.
His tests are really hard. I don't know why he puts problems that were not even mentioned in lecture. He expects us to know well above and beyond of what he has taught us.
Terrible lecturer, talks super slow. Tests are needlessly hard for the course given and does not really represent the material either way.

I don't think she's a "bad" professor, but she definitely did not explain the material in a way that was easy to understand. She was also very cutthroat with exams and had a very bad curve (if at all because she just straight up decided not to curve the second midterm even though she promised to).

average for exams was always low but never wanted to curve, writes on chalkboard and never uploads any notes online, has a thick accent and writes to quickly, overall, just be ready to learn most of the material outside of class. final avg was 60% but she hardly curved, would avoid this prof and take calc 2 with anyone else lol.

Really tough class. Not entirely her fault, 20B is just a tough class in general but she didn't make it any easier. Our first midterm average was 16/40.She talks really fast in lecture and doesn't explain things very in-depth. If you can grasp concepts by doing a few practice problems once you'll do fine, but good luck if that's not you.
Good professor, tests may be harder than the lecture itself, be prepared to study on your own

Only tests on polar coordinates and neglects all other topics of Calc 2, so you'll be screwed in all other classes you take. Doesn't record lectures, so if you miss class you are screwed. Midterms are only 4 questions, so if you miss 1 question, you're already at a C for the exam. I wouldnt recommend taking her, she won't prepare you for Math 20C.

Generally expects students to focus all their effort on only his class. Does not provide clear grading criteria. Extremely poor communication and lacks tact with students. In the two classes I took with him there was little to no consistency between what the professor said versus what the TAs and tutors said. Prepare to be confused.

Dr. Al Ajrawi teaching at SDSU and I'm her student.
I asked her about this class and she wasn't the professor for this class, she was facilitating the class for once in 2021.
The last feedback is fake and a big lie.

All the 5/5 ratings below are fake reviews, IGNORE them. I actually took the class and this prof completely slacked off the whole summer session. Reused the same syllabus and lecture slides from other ece 15 profs, and lecture recordings were posted weeks later than they should have been posted.
Dr. Al Ajrawi has been a great teacher, lecturer, and a Professor to me, and I fully enjoyed her lectures, she explained everything in detail and it made it easier for me to understand
I wish all the Professors are as articulated, intelligent and resourceful as Dr. Al Ajrawi. Her lectures are precise, concise and detailed.

Being an international student and also being one who left the school system many years after my first degree, I was too scared on how I was going to cope with the BS at UCSD, but your lecturing strategies and encouraging words to students have built that confidence in me. You are a source of inspiration to many.

Professor Nguyen is an outstanding teacher who explains complex concepts clearly and makes learning engaging. His lessons are well-structured, and he is always available to answer questions. He provides helpful feedback and genuinely cares about his students' success. Highly recommend taking his class!
He is really respected and always willing to help students outside class.

I've learned a lot in this class. Although the workload was a bit heavy, the textbook practices, biweekly projects and final group project were beneficial to my learning! It definitely deserved the time and I assume that's how programming learning should be. Professor Nguyen is funny and caring, while being very knowledgable about the subject.
One of the best professors at UCSD clearly taught us concepts, recruited the right tutors, and tested the right concepts. Professors like these who maintain the reputation of the CSE department.
interesting class, beside lecture, it's more like a discussion.
All she seemed to care about was getting her “job” done - not really about the students. Better TA's out there
Fun teacher, I usually don't enjoy writing, but Darlene made it a little less daunting. Grading was made clear and was fair.
The class is easy, very straightforward and easy to write essays. Just never reach out to this professor for any kind of help, such as being an advisor. He will be rude and try to screw you over.

This class is super easy if you understand the basic concepts. It is 20% discussion section, 20% quizzes you do in lecture, 20% online quizzes based on the textbook, 10% for each midterm(2), and 20% for a no-fault final. You do have to buy the textbook but it is worth it to not sit through Roeder's boring lectures.
He can ramble a lot during lectures but as long as you are doing the readings, it should be fine.

Grading criteria is extremely unclear, and professor refuses to directly answer students' questions, instead just responding with more questions. Class is easy enough but exams are pretty unfair: you're expected to write down EVERYTHING even remotely related to the prompt, and just answering it isn't really enough. TAs weren't helpful either.

I thought Professor Gartzke was overall pretty nice. However, he was very vague about midterm and final grading and your grades depend on your TAs as there isn't a rubric for anything. He also doesn't record lectures but does post his slides which are basically just repeating what the book says. Easy class but stressful professor.

She was one of the best teachers I have ever had and I hope other people can have the same class experience  I did. Mrs. Herndon also helped me if I needed help and was very caring and understanding to anyone I had ever seen her interact with. She deserves a raise!
She was a great teacher and I would love to have her again!

Professor Herndon really made this class straight forward with her lectures. She explains the material very clearly. Easy discussion activities and extra credit CQ that really helped my grade! She truly wants students to succeed in class. Very approachable during office hours for any questions about the lecture or homework questions.

Hands down one of the best professors I had at UCSD. She is an amazing lecturer. Her method of teaching was very helpful. She uses document camera to write her notes very neatly instead of chalk board, which was very helpful. The exams were very representative of the lectures. Do the study questions if you want to succeed in the class!!

BIBC102 by no means is an easy class, but Professor Herndon offered a lot of extra credit and her exams were really straight forward. However, she doesn't seem to care a lot and ignored questions in class frequently. She tends to read off from the lecture slides a lot too. Clickers for both participation and extra credit.
Super sweet prof. Class is easy..

Professor Nicolazzo is always very enthusiastic during lecture and seems to truly care about what the students share. The class itself isn't too stressful as long as you keep up with readings and assignments.

English is not even my native language but this has been my favorite class so far. Very lenient with grading (maybe cuz it's online) and the prof went over and beyond to accommodate the students. VERY caring and VERY sweet. The prof is obviously very passionate about the subject which makes the class really enjoyable.

I don't like lectures, but prof. nicolazzo made me want to show up for class! she's an awesome person and lecturer, she tries to get the class to participate and makes people want to chime in. There is no midterm and two take home essays which are difficult but if you do the reading (it is a lit class after all) you'll be fine.

Shes alright. She loves participation and is very passionate. A couple essays and final is take home which is cool. I guess I didnt really like her since everyones input made it to where I wasnt learning much. But other that it was easy and cool.
Wentao is really caring and inspirational. He encouraged us to write for ourselves, rather than follow a formula. You do need to work hard and participate in class, as you should in any other course.
Tough grader, not recommended at all

Wentao is a very patient, caring but somewhat tough grader. CAT3 challenged us a lot in how we can work not just on ourselves but also as a group. He definitely had a high expectation for you. So be prepared.

Wentao is charismatic and joyful in section. He encourages students to participate in
discussion. Very helpful in Office Hours and does not hesitate to help students
with questions, even ones that are sometimes rhetorical or obvious.
Wentao is very considerate and caring. Attend the office hours and he will help your writing. Attendance is mandatory and participation matters. He will give extra credits for evaluation.

THIS PROFESSOR IS AWESOME!!!
Probably the best class I've ever taken. The topic was on psychology and video gaming. Fun Lectures and I had a lot of fun in discussion sessions. 
We also had some professionals from the gaming industry to give talks. Fun!
The assignments were easy. You do need to attend lectures though. Everyone loved this class!

Professor Shen is new, but knowledgeable and genuinely passionate about memory. He is also quite approachable. 
Attendance was not mandatory. His exams can be challenging but if you study and pay attention to what he marks as important in lecture you should be fine. You also get full credit on discussion posts, which are easy to do.
Do not recommend
Easy A if you can afford Professor Izzo lack of teaching skills, poor material and questionable manners.

She overcomplicate basic game theory (probably due to his evident lack of knowledge in mathematics). Professor Izzo gets frustrated easily and is very unprofessional when replying questions and emails.

Do not recommend.
Classes are boring: a mix of lack of knowledge and not particularly good teaching skills.
Some guidelines were not clear for the exams, very test heavy with 90% of the final grade grade being the final/midterm, and unprofessional when replying to emails. Wasn't a great time overall.

Professor Ord has a unique teaching style, but it's effective if you engage with it. The workload is challenging, but the lectures and resources like the free textbook are worth attending. I found Unstuck study and other study tools really helpful for staying on top of the material.
He is not a good professor. He touched me
Lays out the entire class for you at the start of the year and changes almost nothing. All the points and extra credit opportunities are clear and specific. Very clear and specific teaching style.
Best CSE Professor ever!

Sad thing he's retiring, but glad I got to take 30 with him. His lectures are very fast-paced, but they actually make sense, and you will HAVE to know most of these concepts for your quizzes and exams. I learned a lot in his class. He is also patient and hilarious and stays after class for questions. 20+ hours of work per week but worth it.
Class was interesting m, but ideas were a little out there for me… not a lot of connections to things I know about music.

I would lay down my life for Willy and I mean that. He cares so deeply about his students and is very down-to-Earth and understanding and clearly very passionate and knowledgable about the subject matter. He is so easy to talk to and his lectures are engaging. It is impossible to do poorly in this class as long as you actually do the work.

His class is very easy and chill, he records lectures and zooms lectures for those who can't make it in person. He has once-a-week listening assignments which are easy and fun. His midterm and final are papers which are easy to write since you get to make your own prompt.
His class is very chill, the homework was easy just a listening assignment once a week, and the midterm and final papers were 5 pages double spaced.

An amazing professor! Super friendly and nice and truly cares about his students. Only gives two papers for the whole year; a 5 page midterm paper and 5 page final paper. Attendance is mandatory though because he gives clicker-sort quizzes. Overall, definitely reccommend!
VERY VERY BAD! HATE HIM! HE IS NOT CONSIDERABLE OF YOUR BACKGROUND AT ALL!
Professor Swanson is good at teaching, but the exams are very difficult. The curve is very generous afterwards, but because the exams are so insanely hard, it is not helpful for learning.

Math 11 is hard in general, but Professor Swanson made it especially terrible. His tests are extremely hard and his grading style is questionable. He lacks empathy for his students, even saying it isn't his job to "coddle" them in defense of his grading techniques. I don't see how someone without prior stats knowledge would be able to do well.

As a student who has no prior experience with statistics, this class was difficult. However, the course itself is manageable, and you will do well if you put in the effort. In regards to Professor Swanson, he lacks empathy and is the one professor who has made me question my competency as a student. Just attend lecture regularly and you'll be fine.
Good professor however the midterms and finals were overly challenging. To do well, make sure you understand the concepts.

Need to feel comfortable speaking in public, but he's a chill, respectful type of energy. The coursework isn't heavy, more about being honest/open to social science discussions. Not a passive-aggressive type, more smooth energy like we have to talk, keep it flowing. Attendance was mandatory for the most part, but that is the only thing. Good class!
Messy class management. Content itself isn't hard, though.
Horrible and unreasonable
Poor class administration. It's crazy
Took the Human Computing for health course. You might learn a few things but that's not required to pass the class.

The course title has "software engineering" in it but he basically teaches nothing about design patterns and how to write clean code. The course consists of a group project on WebXR and WebRTC. However, you need to google everything yourself cuz he and other staff know nothing about them. After 10 weeks I feel like I learned nothing.
Course is tough, and lectures feel a bit looser and less clear than CSE167. You will want to use external resources to clarify knowledge, including research papers (or the PBR book).

Youtube videos are way better. Things taught are too general but PAs require specific implementations.Time consuming hws and TAs are not helpful. Questions on piazza get one line answers. Plus a hard midterm and a final writing assignment which asks you lots of concepts not taught in class, and a final project due on final week with no skeleton.
Good lecturer. Homework takes effort, especially at the end.

Really hard class, but its doable and you will learn. 

Ravi sets it up in an accessible way- his class used to be taught on EdX. 

The midterm is hellish, assignments are tricky, you will learn though.

The worst professor I've ever met at UCSD. He doesn't know how to teach. Believe it or not, he teaches a Computer Graphics course with neither definition of terms nor image examples, at all! He just assumed we had prior knowledge of everything he talked about and it was so hard to follow what he said in class. Avoid him for CSE167.
Responsive professor with straightforward syllabus and a willingness to accomodate personal situations that impact coursework.

Prof. Uranga was very helpful and was accessible during the day for office hours. Her feedback is very straightforward and she is very passionate about biochem. I do want to say, you have to put in the work for an A as exams are not just content based. The lectures are pre-recorded by someone else and the practice problems are nothing like the hw.

The one thing I really did not like were the discussions + 2 responses to your peers (14 pts), as she had a specific way to do them. You had to cite EVERYTHING, even the stuff you knew from before because the info had to come from somewhere. Homework is timed (8 q's, 25 mins) but is helpful for exams (35 q's, 90 mins). APPLICATION Q's NOT CONTENT.

I took biochemistry with Prof Uranga via UCSD Extended Studies. I loved how she was so enthusiastic about what she was teaching and related it to real life examples as to why it was important. Her expectations are clear, she gives extra credit. Would recommend!

She was one of the greatest professors I have had. I reached out to her regularly on things I struggled with and she was always very responsive and understanding. She helps you understand the content through connecting it to real life. Plus she has a great voice so you'll like listening to her. If you want another chance with Biochem, take her.

Dr. Hannah was an amazing lecturer and mentor throughout my time at UCSD. I took my first class with him during COVID and ended up adding Global Health as a major because of him. He was looked up to by the entire Global Health department, and inspired me to pursue my MPH. He was loved and is missed dearly.

Rest in peace Dr. Hannah!

He's so sweet and mostly easy. There's a lot of readings but you don't really have to do them. The class is only graded by discussion board posts, a midterm, and a final. Everything is generally not too bad because the midterm and final essays were online/at-home.

ASYNC SUMMER COURSE. Class is fascinating: topics include refugee crises, social inequities, decolonizing medicine. Too much reading to realistically accomplish but very enriching. 4 quizzes (you won't get all answers from slides), 4 discussion posts (cite sources for full credit). Prof is knowledgeable (Harvard PhD), personable, passionate!
best professor ever!!

I love Professor Hannah, his lectures are actually interesting, he encourages participation and all opinions in his classes, the class is graded mostly on discussions rather than tests, which keeps the focus on the content and away from memorization. I wish I could take him for every Global Health class. Thank you so much, Professor Hannah!!
Incredibly unfair grading.

I took Dr. Licht for winter 2021 and he exceeded my expectations. While his accent is a bit difficult to understand at first, with time it's easy to get used to. His prerecorded lectures are are short and to the point just like the HW. Very easy midterms and final exams that are based exactly on the study guides he posts a week prior. I recommend!

I did not see this man's face once and I went to every single one of his office hrs. Course was v disorganized and tests were 2 midterms and a final. The midterms were 6 q's and the final was 12, 6 points per q. His lectures don't go over very useful examples and the only reason I did well was bc of the SI sessions. Take another prof if u can

Appreciate how he is accessible for office hours, along with the TA's. I appreciate that I can come anytime to ask questions. Exams are representative of homework, review, and lectures, so you know what to expect.

Licht actually cares. I imagine he dedicated a lot of time & effort to the class. He edits together his notes w/ recorded voice over so his lectures are clear and very precise. Additionally, he held OH 3x/week for Q&A ab lec/hw. Canvas was well-organized. 10-15 HW Q's/week. Exams were straightforward. I really appreciated his teaching style.

Her class wasn't hard, but I had around a 92% and she gave me a B? I emailed her wondering about it and explaining I did extra credit she did not account for. She responded angrily saying she was sick of lazy students sending her these emails? AND even after all that she didn't input my grade right so now it appears with no grade on my transcript

Even though there were no lectures, you can tell she actually cares and wants everyone to get an A. Discussions were mandatory but got cancelled because of the protests. She gave us a lot of extra credit opportunities. Even cancelled 2/3 papers because of protests. Weekly discussion posts were important.

2 discussion posts a week, 3 blog posts (1200+ word essays), TONS of reading (multiple books required but can be found at library), creative freedom with the final (5-7 research paper, art piece, etc.) but you also have to do a 3 page process statement and a 1 page reflection. Learned a lot but heavy workload. Attendance isn't mandatory though.

I took professor Streeby for Ethnic Studies 189, she required us to read two novels a week. Some of the novels are online pdfs. There is additional books you have to buy along the course. Get ready to read because the essays and blog posts you do will be on the books you are required to read. Every class is about the readings.

She is awesome! she gives great feedback on your blog post 5 spread out over the quarter and 1 final creative assignment. She feedback is so detailed, she actually cares. She articulates herself so well and she knows whats up. Opened my eyes to scific and how dope it is for poc. I'm a soci major and it totally related. I love her!

Best professor at ucsd. I learned a lot, felt motivated to go to class, and the professor was very encouraging. quizzes were difficult but fair and if you do the work you'd be fine. He was very understanding and took feedback into consideration. loved the way he taught and organized the class. One of the best professors i've had so far!

Overall, she is a great professor who truly cares about her students and genuinely wants them to succeed. She is very accessible outside of class and is willing to go over a topic multiple times and in different ways until you understand it. Just know that if she detects any B.S., she won't hesitate to call you out on it.

While the textbook is required mainly for homework, she genuinely cares about her students' success. She is accessible both in person and online, responds quickly to emails, and provides additional practice questions upon request, which are helpful for test day. Attending class, though not mandatory, is very beneficial given the course content.
She is an amazing professor. Take her if you can!

Professor Rizk is amazing! She's kind and sweet. She provides study guides and outline notes. Her exams and quizzes are extremely fair and reflective as long as you do the homework and work on the study guide. Easy A.

Superficially nice. Comes off as a very sweet person if you don't interact with her much but a slight conflict reveals her passive aggressiveness. She was very rude, got frustrated easily, and was extremely difficult to deal with. Half of her lectures are recorded but she is more judgmental, strict, and demanding than long-time professors.

Poli 140A. Grade is based off one midterm exam and one final exam, all in short answer format with one long answer. Tests are graded pretty harsh, no curve.
