Was told it was easy but took about the whole three hours to take. Not as easy as Professor stated, even though I studied hard. Disappointed in the outcome of the class.

Worst teacher I've ever had. Uses another Prof's slides and I swear she reads them for the first time when she reads them out loud in her first lecture. Literally knows nothing about the material. Students ask basic questions during lectures that she can't answer. She does not know the material. Not enough space to rant abt more

Very fast when lecturing. The pace and questions she lectured assumed the topics were immediately understood after being taught. Knowledge checks asked questions not always covered in lecture and were worth a lot grading wise. 

There was no curve on the final or final grading scale. 
2.37 class GPA for my section

Schimpf is a really nice professor; her lectures are generally really clear and direct. Textbook not really necessary unless she fumbles a concept around for a bit. Tests were fairly long, but primarily multiple choice and easy. Discussions weren't too necessary, but it is kinda graded. Honestly easy class.

By taking her class, you can tell she truly cares about her students and their understanding of the material. Her lectures are clear and easy to understand and she gives examples to help students learn. Of all chem professors, I honestly think her exams are the easiest: Multiple Choice w/ one page short answer. Loved her!

Definitely take professor Schimpf! Lectures are clear, reasonable amount of hw, gives extra credit and tests are extremely fair (just like studyguide and clicker questions, have a small amount of extra credit, getting a 100% is definitely doable). I just showed up and paid attention in class, studied a bit before exams and got an A very easily.
very condescending
Dr. Al-Delaimy was awesome!He's more than willing to work with you if you don't understand a concept. The class was not that hard if you show up to lectures and study hard for the exams. Good luck

Our TA's walked us through the past lectures & how to do the labs, bless them. Aside from his condescending tone, Prof really really really does know the material, but just not the best lecturer. In office hours, explained things thoroughly and enthusiastically, so take advantage. Lecture had quizzes done on iClickers and homework was done in pairs

Professor Al-Delaimy teaches as though you are a graduate student.  He is condescending when you ask for clarification, and doesn't give clear feedback. The homework was not graded fairly and lab can be a grade-killer (even though it's supposed to help). I would choose to take the class with one of the other professors.
He takes his courses very seriously but he is fair. Those who just wanna wing his courses will suffer. I actually find him a very nice person!

Professor Ramirez's class was the first I took at UCSD, and I am so glad I did! This class was fast-paced, but easy enough to keep up with, as deadlines were clear and consistent. Professor Ramirez is very respectful, supportive, and provides many additional resources to enhance your learning. Take her Summer Bridge course, if you can!

Professor Ramirez is very kind and inclusive to her students, with the class itself being very easy and straight forward. Her lectures can often drag on and make you fall asleep however. Course consists of multiple readings and movies + 2 essays and weekly 250 word write ups about films/articles. Final is an essay.

Taken during SS1. Professor explains things okay, but it depends on understanding of the material from the free textbook she provides. Class is mostly dependent on R Studio, so communication with the TA who deals with that is important. Graded on problem set code and writeup as well as a final project. Read textbook & talk with TA, you'll be fine.

While lectures were a bit out of sync because of the SS schedule the content was pretty straightforward. I will say despite the exams being open note they are extremely difficult and take a lot of time to complete, mostly free response. The research assignments weren't always clear. She is a nice and caring professor tho and wants you to learn!

I took this class during ss1 24. Class was fully remote. Grading was based off of 1 intro discussion  assignment, 5 research assignments, 2 worksheets, 1 midterm, and 1 final. If you do poorly on the midterm, the final can replace your grade. Discussion and lectures were not mandatory.

don't think I'd recommend this class if you didn't have a good science teacher in highschool or learn these topics beforehand. She gives extra credit and allows notes on exams but the questions are hard and her grading is harder. lectures were a bit confusing and don't expect any email responses

The exams are HARD, especially the final. In summer session those exams are open-note open-everything, but still very hard problems. The other assignments and extra credit are basically giveaways so dont miss those points. Lectures are long(3hrs), just endure. She listens to students' opinions and is very nice.

Shes very sweet and valid students' voices,her midterm was very harsh 14 questions with Mutiple questions! keeping in mind this is SS1. So much to learn in a month and you are expected to do HW. The best part of her is she replaces the final if you so poorly in the midterm. HW are also important for your grade! don't procrastinate if you take her.

Very boring lecturer. I can't recall a single lecture I attended that I could focus for more than a grand total of 10 minutes out of 80 minutes. A waste of time to go. At least she structured the course and the exams such that going to lecture isn't necessary to do well in the class.
This is one of my favorite professors at UCSD.

I asked for help because I was dropped from her class on day 1 and she did not respond to my questions in the email and simply informed me that she can't help me. I asked her to refer me to someone who could and she didn't. She doesn't take the time of day to actually help students in bad situations and did not care that she was screwing me over.

Lectures are normal length, and can speed up to get the point. CA questions were different from usual but easy. She talks about the main idea in each of the readings in the lectures which helps. Readings are free and pretty short, overall pretty easy to read. Grade is fully dependent on your TA. Make sure to spend time on your research paper!
Zhiri is the best MMW professor. The readings are shorter but are concise and are to the point. Her lectures can be difficult sometimes but luckily she speaks directly and to the point.

This may have been the easiest class I've taken at UCSD. This is partially because I took AP CSA, and this class is basically the same thing plus a few extra concepts. The final exam is curved like hell; my 87/100 became 87/75 and therefore 116%. It was a decently enjoyable class, with fair PAs and easy midterm, and he instructed it decently well.

Makes his own homework that is super difficult to understand, and lectures are reverse. Meaning you watch lectures at home and come into class for practice problems. He just makes this course very difficult in general and would definitely recommend a different professor.

The lectures were not very helpful, he basically just does the handout in class and that's about it. Midterms and finals were most of the grade, but he did curve the class up by a lot, ended up with more than 100% in the class somehow. Also a bit too generous with due dates, there is no late penalty so you can just submit everything a week late.

Wasn't good at lecturing. The actual lecture time was more of a discussion as we just filled out a worksheet. I had to do a lot of self study. Generous with deadlines on PAs however the PAs were pretty difficult. 60% of your grade is from the midterms and can be replaced with the final. In the end, he curved the class a lot.

profs lectures wasn't very good at lecturing and actual lecture time was more like a discussion and filling in a worksheet. 60% of your grade is from the midterms and can be replaced with the final which can be great if you are good at taking tests. Generous with deadlines on the PAs (gives almost 3 weeks). He curved the class a lot in the end.

Dr. Lipomi has a contagious passion for nanoengineering and chemistry. He consistently makes efforts to engage his students with entertaining lectures and demonstrations that draw course content back to real-world implications. A year into college, he is by far my favorite professor.

Dr. Lipomi is an amazing lecturer and cares deeply about his students' success.

His lectures are eye-opening, and he explains concepts incredibly well in such a short time.

His quizzes are intuitive and easy to understand as long as you read the textbook provided.

His final was a nice surprise and checked for understanding in a calming manner.
Make sure you do well on the quizzes and written assignments. All of his lectures are on YouTube if you want to get ahead.

I believe Prof. Lipomi is one of the best lecturers at UCSD, he handles classes very good. He cracks a joke now and then, has his lectures on Youtube and is very active on Spotify as well. His course content may seem tough, but with his experience in teaching the course, he does a very good job. Would definitely take him again.

Lipomi is clearly very interested in the topic so he tends to draw students in to his interest. He makes a lot of puns and jokes which often are followed by silence but it's the effort that counts, it really adds some fun to the class. I talked to him at his office hours once, he is a great young guy and will help you if you need it.

I disagreed with the professor's no-tech policy as well, I feel like it took away from a lot of attendance and made it difficult for me to take notes. Additionally, hours of films were assigned each week (with some readings that I found unnecessary) which was time consuming. The grade was based on papers, which were graded by TAs.

Really interesting class, only graded on papers. Lectures were honestly boring, but if you're interested in film history you'll love this class, prof is very passionate and elaborative. You're expected to engage a lot with the material, but you can do all of the papers and the final paper without lectures and by only skimming assigned material.

loved this class so much! you're graded on 7 short papers weekly (1-2 pages) which are graded very fairly and you get 9 opportunities so you can skip two. the final is another paper but longer (like 4 pages). i found the lectures to be very interesting, but it can be hard for some to pay attention because it was a three hour lecture once a week.

Professor Tufenkian is an amazing professor and had me looking forward to each lecture! His weekly papers (1-2 pgs) are very doable as long as you attend lecture and do the readings/viewings. Readings and viewings could be long at times, but were always relevant to the class. The class is graded on papers and no exams. Highly recommend this prof!!

Professor Tufenkian was wonderful and showed that he genuinely cared about his students and would even remember your name if you answered a question! The films were enjoyable and classical, so it felt like each class was an immersion into an old theatre. The weekly papers were short and fairly graded, too. Take him if you have the chance!!!

Best professor to introduce you to data science. He was clear about what will be important to know for exams. Gives partial credit on everything. They give so much resources and help outside of the classroom. He's very kind and respectful as well. Midterm and Final Projects can also be done with a partner.

I'm trying to recall exactly why I went to college. Oh. Right. To be EDUCATED.

Been a long time (15 years) since Ms. Dapper's class. REAL DEAL.  Brilliant TEACHER...not social-promoter. 

Was at 634  characters when noticed max was 350. I was "just getting started."

Improving  your ability to write clearly and correctly are  important to Ms. D.

Ms Dapper taught English 205 at SD Mesa College years ago. I LOVED it. If her class were a military boot camp, she'd be the Marine Corps; it's HARD. She sets her expectations HIGH. If you want easy, move on. If you want to develop excellent writing skills, look no further than Ms. Dapper. Her class prepares you for all your subsequent classes.

I took her Eng. 205 at Mesa 21 yrs ago and she still haunts me. Her lectures were like a one woman show. All her. Her papers were the most difficult I have ever written! EVER!! Class started full, but by the end of the semester, there were 9 of us left. She is a tough grader. So many papers, revisions, rewrites! Never good enough. Good Luck!

Ridiculously hard, expects perfection.  Learned in 9 weeks more then what I learned in 9 years in Pennsylvania middle and high schools.   Forget what our high school debate coaches told you, writing is not speaking.  Even writing clearly is hard.  I barely passed. wish the class was not graded.

Ms. Dapper is the most dramatic person i've ever met. She is enthusiastic about teaching this course, but she grades ridiculously harsh. I'm not a bad writer but i still didn't pass the class. She repeated certain stuff over and over again and there's no in-class participation AT ALL.

The Homework assignments were short but very insightful, with optional extra problems. The exams reflected the Homework, Discussions, and Practice Exams very well. The optional Homework problems did not appear on the exams which was nice. Overall Professor Pollack was the best math professor I had at UCSD. Only needed around 85% for an A.

Smart guy but does not listen to the students. Get ready to spend 5 hrs+ per week on his weekly hw and one drop. 2 midterms and does not allow dropping. If you are sick and did poorly in one, you are done. He was teaching new material at the last lecture and expect us to prepare it on the final.
Does not explain anything during the lecture, he just writes stuff down and repeats it and expects you to understand.
Aaron is a solid professor
Overall, a great lecturer. Super nice and willing to help. Homeworks were super manageable, and he gives plenty of hints for tougher problems.

As an exchange student I had the worst experience in his class. Nothing useful is included in the lecture, just talking about how good he was and what happened in the past. But the assignments and tests are always hardcore skills asks you to answer. Another thing is that he sometimes includes controversial political views.
Only teaches superficial concepts and quizzes you on things he will teach a week later. Awful
Just don't don't don't take his courses!!!!!

He is a very passionate lecturer, cares about students, and his lectures are typically very superficial and focus on general applications and the history of intelligent systems. Unfortunately, the grading was heavily weighted on tests that required you to just memorize random facts from his lecture slides. Also, he never responds to Piazza posts.

One of my favourite professors ever (including undergrad and grad school). teaches class as if its a conversation about image processing and one of the most enjoyable experiences at ucsd. Take him if u can, at least to get to know an academic who cares equally about his students as he does about his research!

A really personalised and well curated course on radiative applications especially relevant to industry! Lectures go hand-in-hand with the book's content and assignment covered form a really good base for further evaluations! Personally would recommend attending the lectures, making notes, staying on top of assignments to make the best out of it!

Course is really focused on building concepts in mass transfer while getting comfortable will all the new notations, formulas being introduced. Tests are not a concern as they are inspired from HW questions/Text Book questions! Grading is pretty chill as they were heavily curved (to the best of my knowledge!).

Knowledgeable professor but a bad teacher. Most lectures are just him copying things down from his notes onto the board. He also goes over topics extremely quickly without much explanation, making students often confused. The course itself revolves heavily around the textbook he wrote, making the textbook mandatory. This class is not recommended.
not difficult class

Pretty solid lecture contents with focus on understanding fundamentals of combustion! Really a good course for getting you up to speed with all the key concepts and numerical aspects! PS: Course is test heavy.
Good professor

Pretty well curated lectures and contents to get you up to speed with battery tech! Definitely recommend attending all the lectures, staying on top of assignments and going through the book in detail!

Professor Willoughby is SO knowledgeable, and brings in LOTS of guest lecturers that have a plethora of experience all around the field of political science. His online lectures were a lot, and there is a quiz after every single lecture, with two one-page papers due per week. He also assigns readings, but you'll succeed if you pay attention.

The man is an actual genius, doesn't have prepared notes, he just knows literally everything from the whole course from memory. He brings in very interesting guest lecturers. He assigns a fair bit of work but none of it is difficult, and he also gives out a RIDICULOUS amount of extra credit, and curves tests quite a lot. OH's are at the bar, legend

Thought he was gonna be tough but honestly was one of the best classes. His lectures are fun and he wants you to actually learn more about the world. Offers plenty of extra credit. A lot of reading but go to lecture, read the articles, you will get an A. I'm a student-athlete and this class was manageable. He's a professor I would brag about taking

Dr. Willoughby is one of the best professors at USD. I would have taken more classes offered by him if they fit with my schedule! You work for your grade but have flexibility. Once you understand his style of teaching and formatting then the classes become easier!

Willoughby is a super cool professor and the class is great. If you're not willing to read 100+ pages a week and write a paper/quiz don't take it. It is a lot of work but the material is interesting and it all connects to the course and lecture. The exams are stressful but the weekly quizzes help you stay on top of the readings so it's manageable.

First, I don't think this is the correct grade for me, I had two midterms graded wrong already (seriously?) 
Second, my canvas showed I got an A but she gave me a B+ which means she probably down curved it which I don't think it's right and it's no where mentioned in the syllabus.
Third, she increased the final by 2% after final grades are out.
so confusing. she has so much side talks that is not revelent to the course and that the test are really hard. so confusing .

Just to get it out of the way, she's pretty hot. Had her for 101A; in comparison to that class, 101C is less about memorizing and more about applying the knowledge. With that said, it is still memorization heavy. Tests weren't too bad, just go over slides and know them well. Good lecturer; material boring af, but she makes it bearable.

This class has a lot of helplines that can get you that A. Lecture was kind of dry sometimes, but the tests reflected the slides verbatim. This class is more of a memory tanking class, yet you learn some interesting things about language on the way. Clickers for class and mandatory discussions were annoying, but fair considering the class.
Sorry but she is just too beautiful for me to concentrate.

She was helpful and the material was taught very clearly. It was easy to follow along with lectures. HW is on Kudu and written hw, that is basically just completion based and you grade your work. Cheat sheet allowed on exams. Summer session had 3 quizzes, lowest dropped. Final cumulative, but nothing new. Do the hw and you're golden! Would rec

She made HITO100 interesting, a class that could've been very boring otherwise. She is so good at leading class discussions and really cares about her students. I loved going to her office hours and talking with her because she's so nice and personable, one of my fav profs I've ever had at UCSD

best prof at ucsd i'm so serious. I actually took HITO 100 with her but it would give me that option lol. everything is completion grading which makes everything way less stressful because I was focused on enjoying the class and learning something instead of my grade. she's also so nice and understanding, truly wants everyone to succeed. 10/10
Amazing professor with engaging lectures. Awesome grading policy that focuses on the learning aspect so very stress-free. Would 100% take again!!

Professor Klann is amazing! She puts a lot of effort into her course and lectures, keeping you engaged! She also really cares about your learning more than exam stress, so there is more emphasis on the two course papers which you get to pick a topic within the scope of the class to write. I really enjoyed the class and highly recommend her!

She was a great teacher. She emphasized learning because you want to rather than learning to achieve a certain grade. She trusts that you will do your work as it will benefit you. There were no quizzes or midterms or final just two papers you had to write that were both up to you about topic. Honestly 10/10

Stefanie is a great professor, entertaining, funny, with easy and assignments and quizzes. If you're looking for a GPA boost, this is an easy class to get that while also having a great time learning Psychology. The only downside of her class is that attendance is required, if you're a serial class skipper like me, you'll still have a good time.

Shes a nice lady but the class and assignments is a bit disorganized and confusing. Theres weekly discussion questions and assignments which are done in groups. She likes to push social interaction through zoom but I think this is really hard to do in an online setting compared to in person making the class very awkward at times. Easy class tho.

Prof. Amaro was very nice when teaching this class. Lecture was accessible, with the choice of watching it in person/ zoom or podcasts. The class was structured with 2 midterms + final, allowing you to drop the lowest (including the final). Only gripe is that she would go over the lecture end time by 2-5 min to finish explaining a concept.

Professor Amaro can seem a bit disorganized at time, but she always lectures on interesting topics. There are 5 exams, non cumulative, followed by 5 "team exams" which is repeating the test you just took with classmates. Lowest exam is dropped, including final, so you can stop going to class week 8 if you've done well on the tests. Not too hard.

Professor Amaro is a very caring person, and always willing to stop the lecture to answers questions about the material. Tests are fair, there are 5 tests, one is dropped so you have a chance to skip the final, tests are all Multiple choice.. listen to her podcast and know everything on the lecture slides. you will not ever use the book save your $

She is a very good professor, answers all the questions that are being asked in class. Do not skip lectures because Listening to the podcast more than once and attending lecture would be really helpful in terms of learning the material and understanding the concepts, and know everything that is on her lecture slides. The book is not needed

Clear lecture, 4 exams and 1 final all MC. Nothing gets dropped. Be ready for exam ever other week. The exams are not cumulative, so you only have to study 3 lectures every time. After the exam, there will be a mandatory section to talk about the exam. You will take group exam after every exam as well, it counts to your grade.
He wants you to succeed.

Do you enjoy getting questions worth 10% of your exam getting covered only once in a single slide briefly (what is not a wave)? Do you like relying on DI and SI for exam questions not covered once in the lecture (adiabatic processes)? Do you enjoy self-studying, group-studying, and crying before an exam? Then take PHYS2C with Michelsen! I recommend

if you understand concepts, then i think the quizzes are pretty easy. he also says he "can't teach anything" and hes probably right. he def cant spoonfeed everything and i think he wanted his students to explore physics themselves with him giving the necessary concepts in his lectures.

He makes sense in his lectures. I think the way this class works is you go to lectures to learn concepts and then you read the textbook to supplement your learning to do well on homework and quizzes. Final was free because it was the same as the 5 quizzes. He also gives up to 5% extra credit by attending the lectures, so it was a very fair class.

Michelsen doesn't teach. He reads off his slides and I got nothing from his lectures despite them being mandatory and part of the grade. Quizzes are worth 50% of your grade and the average score for each one was always close to 65%.

Flipped lecture format was a bit annoying, because you basically had to learn everything before class yourself, but his explanations were clear and grading was very fair. You could get up to 10% extra credit just for attendance, which was great as well.

Attendance wasn't mandatory but if you attended at least 25 lectures/discussions you could get a 10% grade boost. PA's are difficult but he give you a lot of time to do them, and you can resubmit within 3 weeks with no penalty. IMO discussions were more useful than lectures but they were ok-- he's just a nice guy

These other reviews are definitely written by the professor. The class does give 10% extra credit but that's for attending lecture. Each lecture attended only gives 0.4% so you have to attend 25/25 lectures to get this 10%. PAs are doable but some can take a very long amount of time, and Exams are very difficult without prior coding experience.
10% Extra credit for participation YAY. Lecture was okay and lots of details not for exam but still helpful. PAs are super doable, a little repetitive in terms of methods used.

gave very good lectures, and lots of contextual info that was interesting in relation to programming history
also he gave 10 percent extra credit for participation, which really helped

Super interesting class, and had a practical component which was nice. Lots of reading, but that is to be expected for a theatre history class, and exams were fair and not too difficult. Very participation based class, and had a large group project component.

What was meant to be a VERY easy class was made extremely tough because of her teaching. The class average was 60% on the first midterm, and she wasn't surprised at all. The curve is basically nonexistent. She will test you on the most irrelevant things, expect to memorize the most insignificant details!! 
Literally made my life hell.

She is a good lecturer but her tests were hard and specific (average was 70%). The lowest test is replaced with the average test score, and she has mandatory discussion and lectures (iclickers). She is nice and always willing to talk and provides extra credit. There are weekly quizzes and no cheat sheets. The final is noncumulative.

she's super nice I love her, and she seems very passionate about her field. but I will have to say this class is quite difficult if you're not a bio major. she expects you to really understand the concepts but doesn't really get deep into the concepts enough for you to get an A on the exams. I studied a good amount for exams but still got a C.

Lecture and section mandatory (clickers needed). Drops the lowest quiz (quiz every week on Monday). Recorded lectures can miss a certain amount (3ish?). Great at explaining the topic and can ask questions. Is very friendly and is always willing to talk. Grading is simple but doesn't give out extra credit.

She talks insanely slow and her lectures are a little disorganized. She talks about a bunch of things in her lectures but the actual content of the class that will be on the exam is only a couple of slides. She doesn't offer a cheat sheet so you actually have to know the material really well. But, she cares for her students and class isn't hard.

Marco is, by far, my favorite professor at UCSD. I took them for MATH 180A-C and although 180B felt like a roller coaster, I had an amazing experience in 180C. They were always caring and kind to students. There were 4 grading schemes, so you can skip an exam if you have to. I could not have asked for a better probability professor. Love you Marco!
He teaches really bad. He just read stuffs from the textbook. The grading scale is good.

Great lecturer, clarifies complex concepts with examples. It's not an easy A course, which requiring a solid grasp of concepts and practice. Highly recommended for a deep, meaningful learning experience.
Take him if you like extremely disorganized lectures and board work, minimal example problems that don't translate to homework and exam questions.
One word: RUN!

I heard that he's leaving, so I wanted to leave a review. Linear algebra is not my strong suit, but I liked this class. His exams are fair (two midterms and a final) and although sometimes he tries to trick you, I really enjoyed having him as a professor. He is very kind during office hours whenever I have questions. We'll miss you Ming!
Clear and fast-paced lecture, he gives examples for every confusing definitions and theorems. The only thing is I cannot stop taking notes if I want to catch his speed.

He was always ready to answer questions, stressed the value of participation for all, regardless of confidence levels, which greatly enriched the learning atmosphere. I especially appreciated his encouragement that there are no dumb questions. His discussions were outstanding, Definitely looking forward to seeing him teach again.

At the start of Phil10, many friends warned me about how challenging and confusing Logic could be. However, with Ayoob's assistance, I've had an exceptional learning experience. He genuinely cares for students and ensures everyone feels comfortable seeking help when needed. Very grateful to have had him and only wish I had taken this class sooner.

Class was pretty easy considering, but the TA was a non-entity, so don't hold your breath for test grades. Reading was interesting but more focused on foundational philosophy of the mind than more advanced things. I really hope you like brains in vats.

Prof Shahmoradi makes complicated stuff sound like a piece of cake. He is the most caring professor I have had at UCSD. Office hours turn into deep discussions about philosophy (and Godel whom he seems to know a lot about), not just homework. His passion for the subject is contagious. Made me decide to major in philosophy. Wish he taught more.

Lectures are boring, quiet talker. The TA's were awful and harsh graders. 4 ethnography writing assignments, a midterm and final. The midterm is a multiple choice test but it was awful and should've been an essay. He gives 20% extra credit, so use it all up. Overall not bad, but not the best.

How come ppl would leave negative comments... Def take him if you need to boost up ur GPA, or just have a space to chill. taking his class during the summer and I love it. He is such a sweet professor and I love his taste of movies. 5 papers and a final paper. Positive feedback. And he really wants to help u improve ur writing through this course.

You go to class, watch some films, and he discusses them. His discussion about the films are pretty much what he wants you to write about on your papers. Responses are based on the films watched in class. Though not mandatory, you need to go to class to find out what films are being watched. No podcast.

His course was fun, interesting and easy. He's very laid-back, chil and gives lots of insightful information on cultural films. You get the option to choose between 2 films each week, and the final is take-home and based on films you have already watched in class. I highly recommend taking him if you want an A and also knowledge about culture/films

The easiest course you can take in UCSD. Although there is a response paper for a film watched in class every week, he simply gives all students A if you complete that. Everyone in our class (like about 100 students) get an A as for the final grade. So he is the best choice to improve your GPA.

TOOK FOR SOCI125M. Had a great experience in this class, took it out of interest and I learned so much. His book is required reading for the class and it was so valuable. He had incredible experiences and insights and brought great guest speakers. Midterm was essay questions on class concepts. Group project is a big research paper and presentation.

I really enjoyed Migration and the Law, prof Fitzgerald is extremely knowledgeable and seems unapproachable at first, but he is very welcoming and does care about your learning and understanding. There are a few in-class short answers, but if you stay on top of the reading and attend regularly, it should be an easy A. I learned a lot in this class!

Amazing professor, he is very knowledgeable about the topics. I took this class as a college requirement and was not interested at all, but it ended up being one of my favorite classes. Midterm was tough but if you study the questions and concepts you will be fine. One 10 page final paper. and DO THE READINGS! there are short essays done in class

Those reading quizzes are real folks! Don't be lured into false complacency because there aren't any at the beginning of the quarter- they come, and they will impact your grade! He's a really cool guy who is an interesting lecturer, and funny too. He makes me feel like I understand the material, and is engaging even though the class is challenging.
Hard class but you learn a lot!

Course was online this quarter, so we didn't work with kids, but still fantastic. Early readings are academic, but after week 3 or 4, all readings are field reports written by former students about working with elementary kids! Short writing responses due MWF: takes discipline to keep up, but easy to do quickly. Take if you plan to work with kids!
Good class, very writing-heavy but still very doable. Dr. Bajic really knows his stuff and if you apply yourself, you'll learn a lot.

class was once a week. short and straightforward writing assignments due MWF, lit review paper due at the end but worked on cumulatively. great instructor who really cared about what he was teaching, non-traditional teaching style but gave really interesting discussions. hes a great prof to learn from if you want to work with kids in the future!

Eh, this teacher wasn't that great.  He's kinda funny, but all he does is read the notes off the slides too fast too take notes.  You definitely have to read the book, but he leaves a lot of copies on reserve.  Take him if you want a class you can learn from your bed.

Dr. C always has the best energy! Assignments were minimal but there was a group paper and project presentation which wasn't too bad if everyone contributed. She brought a lot of guest lecturers and attendance was 2 pts per class. If you ever have questions, she is super kind and responds to her emails pretty fast.

FMPH 130 has been taught by other professors in the past and midterms and the final were online and open notes. Dr. Ciborowski has changed the format to closed notes and in-person, paper style. She expects students to memorize over 600 powerpoint slides meticulously for the cumulative final. It is impossible and sets the student up for failure.

Study guide was literally posted less than 72 hours prior to the midterm. Study guide was extensively long and was basically straight memorization of information. Midterm was in-person, old-school paper style. No notes, based strictly on dead memorization. Would not recommend, in comparison to Professor Long.

Very easy course, great intro to the subject of Public Health. Some lectures were a bit boring, but professor understood that. Really easy to get a good grade, but assignments are a bit mindless. Probably spent 3ish hours outside of class per week, if not less. Exams are open note and fairly easy

Sign in sheet/participation is a big percentage of your grade, if you miss one class your grade is down 2% and she only excuses covid cases. Tests are based off memorization and she wants super specifics when we already have to remember 9 different 50 page slides, TA's were harsh graders with homework assignments, but she is a super sweet prof

Lecture materials are neither easy nor hard for me to understand. However, his exams are difficult and almost everyone got bombed, but he curves heavily. His labs are ok with lenient grading, being comfortable with Solidworks will help. 2 hw every week, 2 lab competitions, 1 midterm & final
The curve saved me. Lectures were boring and slides did not help. Labs were okay. Study practice midterms for the test.

Prof Qiao is very knowledgeable in the subject he teaches. Lots of homework and lectures were always hefty in terms of content. Pro tip: use the practice midterm and final to study for the tests and use that to gauge what topics you need to improve on. Tests reflect well enough what's on the practice tests. Do well on the lab reports and tests.

This class is my worst experience in college. I feel that I want my money back for such a waste of time. Grades wrong, no hw feedbacks, exam made for student get confused even if they know the material.

Homework is extremely confusing, hard to follow w lecture; tests seem almost unconnected to HW; tests contain some super easy questions and a lot of poorly worded ones.  Also sample exams have mistakes. Be careful.

One of the easier ECE classes, but you still need to study hard. The project is a big portion of the course and the initial instruction given wasn't very clear. It is important to attend the office hours if you need help on the project. The final was reasonable and cheatsheets are allowed; no solved problems or equations allowed on the cheatsheet.

The course isn't the most difficult ECE class but I think the lecture notes and explanation were really hard to follow for some reason. I had a hard time understanding the induction machine and synchronous machine. I had to study a lot outside the class, from YouTube and the textbook. Attendance not mandatory, but a bonus is given for attending.

There are a lot of topics in this class that sometimes seem totally unrelated. Cheatsheets are allowed for exams but no solved equations or examples are allowed on the cheatsheet. Some lecture topics are unclear but grading is lenient with partial credit.
Overall the lectures are good, labs and homeworks are doable. Some topics can be unclear and professor does not explain them well. Overall grading is lenient with lots of partial credit.

Professor is inconsistent with labels since he pulls information from multiple textbooks. He assumes you've read the textbook before class and doesn't emphasize small (but important) details. Homeworks take long to complete but are basically all you need to study for exams. He's very passionate about learning and is a great prof overall.

No proadcast for lecture. If you miss something I suggest you to check Rhoades Patrick's lecture on UCSD podcast. He will not curve any exam but if you final grade is above 87, you are in the A range. The exam is hard, don't forget to review the polynomial part (It comes up in midterm 2 and final).

Attending lectures is what will help you succeed. Taught in a slow organized manner which allows you to absorb the info and learn. Would love to take this prof again. Learned alot from their BILD2 course and overall fair grader. Drops lowest scores, easy to suceed/learn in this course because of the professor.
Professor Park is an awesome professor. Her tests are straight forward and very reflective of the content she covers in class. She also offers a lot of extra credit opportunities. Highly recommend!

She is a good professor and cares about her students. No cheat sheet and she has an accent which makes her hard to understand at times. Her exams are all application based so you have to not only know the material but understand it really well. Does offer extra credit but only a little bit. The class isn't hard but exams are. Would recommend.

BILD 2 is the hardest of the series, but Parl made this class so easy and enjoyable! Exams are an exact reflection of what s taught in lecture, and questions are very straightforward. Barely any homework, just expect to spend a lot of time memorizing. Drops the lowest exam (I didn't have to take the final) TAKE BILD 2 W PARK!!!

Everything on her exams will be covered in lectures. Her lectures are easy to understand and decently paced. Super open to any questions along the way too. The final was harder than the midterms, but if you prepare ahead of time and go to review sessions during DI, you're all set.

despite the bad reviews, his class averages are consistently better than the other immunology prof. his exams are open note & MCQ, but like others said he does expect you to be able to connect all the dots so questions can be very difficult. generous ECs (if your submitted questions get picked) + 40% of all the exams are basically free points.

Very nice guy and cares about students, but he teaches content at the surface level and doesn't really help to explain in depth. He expects a lot from you to be able to connect the dots on so much content, but I feel that his teaching makes it seem like you're just memorizing facts, making it hard to fully understand and remember on a deep level

The absolute hardest class ever for no reason. I have heard from other students that the other Immuno professor was a lot better than this guy. If you lose points on assignments, they are deducted from your exam score which makes no sense. Unless this class is a requirement for your major I encourage you to pick a different course you WILL enjoy.

Grade is based on exams & lecture questions only. Exams are open book/note & he includes lecture questions submitted by students in the exams so basically u get free points. He could definitely benefit from more organized slides & he doesn't include everything u need to know on the slides explicitly so pay attention. Overall, I thought he was good.

First of all, the immunology class is extremely difficult. He has many ways to buffer the grading of the exams by including homework and also incorporating a question bank that students made. The exams were difficult and even though open book, it required full understanding, not just control+F. Great professor and I learned a lot!

He assigns a lot of homework despite not being great at actually teaching the material and making it easy to understand. His class as a whole is very unstructured and unmotivating. He'll do an example or two per lecture that he sometimes creates on the spot and a lot of the times won't even know how to solve them himself. I wouldn't recommend.
Cant teach the material in a good manner, I left lecture not gaining anything and had to teach myself for the whole course

Ethan doesn't understand how to teach material efficiently. He relies on assigning a large amount of homework instead of explaining how to solve problems. He also curves his course significantly from the beginning, 90-100% is an A, 80-89% is a B, and 60-80% is a C. Like why curve only the C grade and make it more difficult to get good grades?

You don't have to show up to lectures as they are podcasted which is nice. But overall, his tests were hard and didn't represent his homework or what he taught (which he wasn't even good at). I found it better to learn by myself by reading the textbook rather than watching his recordings, going to lectures, or discussions.

Ethan is a cool professor and doesn't have any "large" issues, but rather a couple of small, irritating things.
- He's not great with tech, so don't expect answers to Piazza or any solutions/helpful documents to be uploaded to Canvas
- It's tough to know what he'll be testing you on for exams

Amazing lectures; very structured and concise. Material can be dense and memorization heavy, but start studying early and make flashcards. No curve, but tons of extra credit opportunities. Averaged B+s to A-s on quizzes/midterm but received an A+. Cumulative final (250 points) but he generously made it worth 225 points in lieu of extra credit!

Lectures are straightforward and clear. Exams look nothing like the problem sets. No answers were provided for the quizzes/midterm so you don't know what you got wrong. Completely focused on memorization. Cumulative final. Never again.

He has the most organized & interesting slides I have ever seen in a class. The exams are very fair, look exactly like the optional problem sets. He is caring & funny, & you can come to him for help. A lot of studying, but he makes it fun for such a dense, difficult class. He's new, but already beloved among Bio students. One con: cumulative final.

great professor, really straightforward & easy to understand lectures. class is very content heavy but he makes it really easy to take in. 2 grading rubrics to ensure people get the best grade possible plus a lot of extra credit opportunities. only issue was major errors in grading this quarter, but im sure it was a one time issue.

such a kind and caring professor, he truly cares about students and their learning 
you will do well in class if you study all of his lectures 
take advantage of all the extra credit he offers so much and that's one thing i really regret i didn't do because he is legit awesome

She was a fun person and could be entertaining throughout class, but her attitude was majorly discouraging at times. If we collectively as a class didn't meet her expectations, she would spend too much time in the start of class scolding us with emphasis on how it makes her look bad. Absolutely ruined everyones mood every time.

I'm so glad I had Madame Sivine so early on in my French career. She can be strict, however, it's because she cares about her students. She is very kind, hilarious, and she will never give up on her students. Attendance is mandatory (only allowed to miss 2 classes), quizzes can be hard (study!), and lectures can be fun! Merci Madame, on t'aime!

She was rather strict and had high expectations of her students but she was always there to help. She was easy to access and had various solutions if you were struggling. She was funny and was always making us laugh while also serious about our learning. Thoroughly enjoyed the class because of her.

Madame Sivine is the best teacher I've ever had. She is so helpful. On more than one occasion she went out of her way to help me, and during this class my French improved dramatically. She cares so much about each student in her class.I truly cannot say enough positive things about her. I would 100% recommend taking class with Madame Sivine!

Madame Sivine really cares about her students learning and wants them to succeed. She is very patient and encouraging. There are a lot of small quizzes that are easy points if you study the vocabulary and do the reading, but this class weights participation quite heavily. Participation is an easy way to up your grade but it can also tank it.

This class starts off ok but gets too much by the end. There is a lot of material and on top of that the questions on exams are challenging because they are too specific or. They offer extra credit which does help but it is still difficult to get an A. Most questions on the exams are not like quizzes. Avoid if you can.
Professor Golden only reads from her slides and doesn't engage you in the materials. There are a lot of videos/articles to go through for the quizzes each week. I wouldn't recommend you take her.

Class is a lot of work. Midterms are pretty similar to practice exams. Final was harder for some reason. No curve and doesn't round up grades even if its by less than half a percent. Content and very interesting though.
She spends her entire lecture reading her slides word for word. If you read her lecture slides you would get the same information as listening to her lectures

Golden seems nice enough but wasn't my favorite lecturer -- I found it difficult to stay engaged during her lecture videos. This class is super time-consuming with each lecture module having a lecture video, readings and/or several supplemental videos as well as 2 quizzes per week.
midterm and final are doable as long as you study. lots of ec. and enjoyable. The paper is worth 30% of your grade but grading was fair.
Class was okay. Two tests and one paper is doable.
One paper, two exams. Lots of extra credit opportunities. I found her hilarious. Easy class, sometimes it can get a little concept heavy, but I enjoyed it.

grading policy is extremely weird, especially losing 6 percent for forgetting to upload an article alongside a paper that was already cited inside the paper and that was turned in a previous assignment. I had to get a 100 on the final to get an A-, when the reason why my grade dropped had nothing to do with the knowledge from the class. do not take

Class was super easy. 1x midterm, 1x paper, and 1x final. She offers a lot of extra credit. Midterm was super easy, and she gives a cheat sheet. Be sure to follow the guidelines for the paper, and you'll do fine. Final isn't even cumulative, easiest class of the quarter.

Class was unexpectedly difficult for what I thought was going to be free credits. The class is graded on a midterm, final, and weekly assignments; midterm/final use questions from old exams and the study guide questions are useful (allows 1 sheet of notes for the midterm and 2 for final). Would not recommend as a no effort class, but it's fun.
Little to no care about the learning process. Gee just lectures, leaves, and assigns homework that has nothing to do with what's discussed in class.

I took this expecting an easy A. Not an easy A. He was a good professor but things were boring at times. The concepts seemed easy but turned out to be harder than they looked. 1 activity each week that took anywhere from 2-5 hours of time. Time-consuming. Hard class in my opinion. I put a lot of time and effort and only got a B+. maybe take again
Was not helpful outside class. Was very strict regarding certain unstated expectations and was extremely rude when asked for assistance.

Good, interesting gen ed class. It is a fair amount of work- 3 lectures and one assignment that took me ~2 hours every week. Professor Gee is a great lecturer and makes a big effort to be available outside of class for students. Would highly recommend if you are interested in the subject

Was excited to take this class given UCSD has a great treatment center for eating disorders. However, you never once see Dr. Kaye or really hear from him. It is all taught by associate professors and guests which a lot cancelled the day of; it is kind of disorganized. No late work is accepted, even with a death in the family or medical emergency.
Loved the format of the class. Different lecturer each class. As long as you attend class or watch the podcast you will pass.

I was really excited to take this class, but this professor was not present once throughout the quarter, there was only guest speakers and assistant professors. The quizzes were unfair, if you got one question wrong then you got a D on it. I don't recommend this course unless they change their grading scheme. Disappointing.

TA's teach this course. They use pre recorded lectures and only meet with students for 1 hour a week. Quizzes every week worth 6 points, 3 questions, only give you 6 minutes. They don't allow you to see all the questions or go back to change your answer. This is for quizzes, midterms and final. If u want an A you must get 100% on everything.

Each week is a different guest lecturer which I really enjoyed. Only 1-2 lecture videos per week so the class isn't a lot of work. As long as you take basic notes on the lectures and reading you should be fine. Grade consists of quizzes, midterm, and final, all of which are multiple choice.

Professor Hibb's is an amazing professor. Attendance is not mandatory (he podcasts) and typically gives the following week's lecture slides in advance. He does a great job of explaining hard material - discussion sections are also not mandatory but super helpful! Quizzes, 2 exams, and a cumulative final. Would definitely recommend Professor Hibb's!

Loved this professor and this class! I've heard bad things about BIPN140, but it was so enjoyable and this professors teaching style made all the information seem approachable. Attendance is not mandatory and he podcasts, but he takes any questions you have if you go. He truly knows so much about neuroscience and excels at sharing it!
Languages at UCSD aren't the easiest, but Frau Wahl did an excellent job at organizing her lectures and making the class as interesting as possible.

I took LIGM1B and Frau Wahl was the best. She had a great sense of humor, tried to have engaging lectures, and did her best to explain grammar concepts in a language all of us hardly understood. I'd gladly take her again for the next quarter.

She is an amazing teacher, especially in regards to introducing the German language to many who have never even tried their hand at learning it. Every class, even when we were doing back-to-back lessons, was super organized and helpful. Herr Wahl is one of a kind, and it really shows.

such a sweet professor & interesting class. graded by 3 midterms & final project but all are super easy and he's very open to help. pay attention to the readings and the main ideas in lecture and you'll be fine

Helpful and friendly professor if you go talk to him. Midterm and final same format with short essay questions. One longer class paper analyzing news media. Do read his assigned readings for his exams. You will learn how news media operates and how their routines shape the kind of news that gets reported.

Hallins interest in his subject is clearly evident.  lots of reading, but also really good lectures on topic to the readings.  For the comm student required to take the course, he does a superb job in outlining what you can expect in more advanced courses.

She drops lowest homework grade and lowest problem set grade, and grades the tests on a curve. There was no cumulative final or midterm, there were 3 separate quizzes on different content. I LOVED HER

great professor! she wants her students to do well and helps the all achieve their best. Weekly homework assignments and 3 tests and a final, but she drops the lowest test score. Meet with her in office hours and you'll do just fine. Show up to class to take notes. She's really funny and gives good lectures. Honestly, a great professor.

Lectures are interesting and easy to take notes to. 3 midterms w no cumulative final. But BEWARE that her exams are HARD as the questions can be VERY tricky. Reading is not necessary, got a B+ in IO and A in criminology with just reviewing lecture slides & taking good notes. Ask her questions during the exam & she'll basically give you the answer

There are two midterms and a final. Each exam is half in-class multiple choice and half take-home short answer. The class is very interesting and as long as you do the readings it is an easy A. Lectures aren't mandatory and she posts her slides online. I would definitely take another class with her.

She's a fun teacher. She's uses a lot of examples in her lecture to help you understand the material. That being said, she uses a lot of "example questions" like "BLANK so and so, what is this an example of" which can be kind of confusing. Other than that though, if you study you should do well. She's nice too. I recommend.

I really wanted to give Kaiser a 5/5 rating because he is a great guy and passionate about this class. He is friendly and fun. Very good EC!

Unfortunately, this class can be very disorganized. Often, the projects don't match the content enough. The final project this semester was not a good choice, but hopefully he will fix that for next semester.

kaiser gives me faith in humanity 
class wasnt easy by any means but i know for sure if it was a different prof i would not have made it through. take a class from kaiser just bc you love yourself not for any other reason

Dr. P is pretty good. He is constantly asking for feedback which is nice to see. The lectures are pretty boring but very thorough, but lacking in examples sometimes. Not going to lie, the homeworks are pretty tough but the the exams are very simple if you go to the review.

Kaiser did a great job of making this programming languages class useful and engaging. Even though lecture attendance was not required, I always was sure to attend because the lectures were super interesting. Would recommend this course with Kaiser Pister!

Kaiser is a fantastic professor who is both caring for students and displays a fair level of expectation from them. He allows all homework assignments to be completed in groups, models the exams almost exactly off of the homework assignments, and will go out of his way to meet and talk to students to make sure they understand the given material.

I had Ellen at UVM for cultural anthropology. The class was easy, with only 4 assignments, and 3 exams which were online. She doesn't require attendance so I rarely went, but from the few classes I did go to she seemed to be funny and interesting. There's a textbook but you don't need it.

I loved having her as a prof! Before classes even started she sent out a survey to understand how we were all doing. Not only was the material interesting but she also like showed concern for us outside of the classroom. Quizzes aren't hard to pass if you read slides/ go to class and take notes :) Honestly super cool stuff and not hard to get an A!
Professor Kozelka grades on participation and a final paper, and her lectures and the readings she assigns are very interesting. One of the best and easiest classes I've taken

Dr. Goldschmied is very caring and accommodating. He is interested in supporting his students in their career and academic development. His lectures are engaging, and he makes it a point to check in on each of his students.

He talks way too fast. He is not very helpful when asking questions. He pushes your question aside and says to wait until he's done talking. But ultimately never even comes back to answer your question. His slides are NOT helpful at all. I have no idea why he even puts his slides online when his tests are nothing like the material studied in class.
He is an incredible professor. Take him. He is honestly my favorite professor at UCSD. Very helpful, witty, and seriously hilarious. It would be a shame not to take him!

Taking his psyc of law class because I liked him for social psyc so much. Thought I hated social psyc before this quarter. Read the book carefully and cross w/slides to get the main ideas, but more of an easy B, work for an A class. Funny and engaging. He posts study guides, offered fun extra credit. Take Goldschmied.
pretty good professor. Talks pretty fast, so you should read the book beforehand. Good at explaining concepts and keeping you interested

This professor does not really care too much to make connections with students. The whole time I felt like i was upsetting her when i had questions. A lot of the other CHEM150 lab professors were way nicer and helped students

I took this professor for chem 150 and would not recommend. I saw no passion to teach and was a very tough grader. I really recommend taking a different professor that is open to answering your questions in class :)

messed up curriculum such that if there is a grading problem, she would not be involved. the grading standards are unclear because TAs are responsible for the grades and they varied. the pace of the lecture is fast that becomes not useful. exam material is only 50-70% relevant to the lecture and lab, other materials = metabolic / cell biology.

Terrible professor during his time at U of Rochester. Likes to give trick questions in exam that is hard to prepare for. Projects take up a lot of time. 

This is for CSC 210 btw.

I have taken both cogs 121 and cogs 126 with Philip, and I can say with confidence that he is the BEST professor in the cogs department if you want to learn both theory-based knowledge and employable technical skills. He is generous with sharing his knowledge, but also humble to learn from his students. A real gem of a professor at UCSD.

A brand new class that overlaps a lot with COGS120 but without the coding. You go through the design process with a group to redesign an app on Figma. Dependent on TA grades because a lot was subjective. Grade depended on how much work your group put into the redesign. Lectures were meh but attendance counted. Easy to get an A/B and super caring.

Professor Guo is a very passionate professor with a very interesting teaching style. Teaches basics of html and css for the first half of the quarter and then the rest are in-class TA grading sessions. Group dependent. The difficulty depends on your group's skills and familiarity with web design. Expect good grade but TA will have expectations.

Philip really made sure that all of us were well-equipped to tackle the group project, and he and his TAs are all extremely caring and willing to help throughout the whole process. Though the project was kind of stressful, they were all extremely helpful. He also gives good advice for life and careers beyond college.

Leo is a very knowledgeable, friendly and charming professor who obviously cared about his students! The class itself can be a lot of work, but that is because it is setting you up for all the upper division courses. He was always willing to spend time answering questions and helping us with course content. Definitely would take his class again.

Leo, though just a PhD candidate, showed extreme promise as a professor! Lack of homework was a blessing, though I didn't feel underprepared for the exams, which have unlimited page cheat sheets, including the articles from each week that were tested on. Great lecturer, and lovely at explaining concepts with one APA paper due that was quite easy.

Kleiman's class was somewhat engaging. But grades relied heavily on a research paper, midterm, and final. There were quizzes each week but had very little impact on final grade. Research paper was graded incredibly hard. The exams were tough but if you studied enough it's possible to do well. Overall nice guy but not a great professor for your GPA.

Awesome professor if you're looking for one to keep you engaged in class. Lectures aren't mandatory but HIGHLY recommended since exam material is heavily based off material covered in class. Very caring and understanding. Super responsive with emails and overall knows what he's talking about! I think he's new but 10/10 experience, highly recommend!

Prof Feeley may be the best prof I have ever had. All of the large assignments (Policy Paper, Midterm Essay, Final), I did not hate doing and I felt like we had the freedom to really key in on what was interesting to us, learn, and have a good grade be attainable. Learned so much from this class and getting an A was never in doubt. Take her class.

Unless you are incredibly interested in development, I definitely would not recommend this class. Professor Feeley cares for her students, but oftentimes I found this to be a little passive-aggressive. She claims this class is designed for success but assigns loads of work and vague midterm/final. Probably least favorite class I've taken at UCSD.
Bless her heart, shes a sweet professor but her notes/slides are SO unorganized lol.
Lecture attendance is mandatory (iClicker), weekly Perusalls (kind of a lot), take home midterm essay, policy proposal paper (long but lots of support available), in person final exam

Very knowledgeable about development, as well as a sweet and understanding professor. Weekly reading and annotations (perusall), midterm essay, policy paper, final exam is also an essay. Iclickers were required but the grading is lenient. My TA was pretty decent, but I could see getting a bad TA being a serious problem when it comes to grading.
He is so passionate about what he teaches. Super enthusiastic, and excited. not a bad lecturer but many did find it boring just because he explained really well.

he moves really slowly which is good, but people do say it gets boring bc of how in depth/slow he goes. things pick up towards the end of the quarter as long as u do the hw and coding labs exams should be fine. it's a pretty fair class. if you don't know python id recommend

Professor Goldman was a great professor. Although he had no lecture slides he posted outlines on Canvas for each week. This class was a lot of reading but you can get through it fine. Attending the lectures was the most useful tool for the midterm and final because everything he stated in the lectures was helpful for them.

Professors Goldman was a kind professor but the way he structured his class for your final grade was not the best. I had an A+ throughout the whole quarter and  got 100% on the midterm, but I ended up not passing the class because his final was worth 50% of your grade. His TA was a VERY tough grader and not the best when it came to communication.

Professor Goldman the best professor I've ever had! His class is very reading-heavy. The readings are long and complicated, but I absolutely loved them. I think SOCI 100 is a class everybody should take. The books in his syllabus are crucial to understanding the world we live in. He is super accessible outside class - he even gives you his number!

Goldman is one of the worst professors that I've ever taken during my time as a college student. Since the beginning, Goldman has been callus of the situations that student like myself have been going on through since the pandemic. Not recording lecture, heavy readings (4 books), and late grading from his TA's. This is unacceptable.

do NOT take goldman. he says that his lectures aren't mandatory but doesn't record them and then penalizes you for not following instructions he only gives during lecture. was hostile to students and their concerns and bases all the exams off of the reading (he specifically says we "cant use anything from lecture" ). terrible experience w him

I had her in Fall23. Coming from a STEM background, I usually didn't like my English teachers, but she was a notable exception who actually made it kinda fun. There's a general theme in the class that you have to follow in your writing, but she gives you a lot of freedom to write about what you want. Overall an exceptional and amazing professor.

Her class was the only English class that I've taken where I actually put full effort into writing the essays because the topics are actually interesting. She also gives many constructive feedback and creates activities in class that makes them engaging, I actually wanted to go to the classes even though they were at 8am

I had Sarah Savage for WCWP10A and 10B and she was by far one of my favorite professors I had at UCSD. Her lectures were fun and she tried her best to make them entertaining by sometimes adding short games. I forgot to submit my final paper and she completely understood and didn't take any points off when I turned it in the next morning.

Sarah is such an amazing lecturer. Though the Warren Writing series can be a bit boring, Sarah made it really interesting and kind of fun. She gives great feedback for essays and gives lots of mental breaks during lecture heavy days. Such a sweet and kind soul and I highly recommend her if you can get a class with her!

Dr. Copp made the most daunting course to take feel so doable. I avoided biochemistry all of undergrad, but taking his class was the best decision. He takes the time to explain things in as many ways as possible and is very accessible. The course is so well thought out and structured that I was never left confused. Take the class!!

I never thought I could understand biochemistry, until I took Dr Copps course. Hes super kind and explains in a way that is ad clear as water. Homework is optional which is super helpful, you get the grade for the work you put in, but there's no anxiety with this class which is a first. Absolute would take this course :)

Dr. Copp is very passionate and usually has a couple of office hours every weeek where he goes over the material that students have a hard time with. Exams are very hard and be prepared to study, and always make sure to check your grade on Canvas.

Dr. Copp is very passionate about Biochemistry and it shows! He is very personable and approachable. It wasn't an easy class but he gives you every opportunity to do well. I would absolutely take another class with him.

Dr. Copp did a great job on teaching the concepts in biochemistry that are usually hard to understand. As he said, the homeworks were harder than the quizzes, which were harder than the exams. Everything was in line with expectations, and there were no surprises during the course.

Never take this professor unless you want to waste 3 hours of your life a week and be bombarded with multiple quiz questions a week. Even the midterm was so extra of them, making it seem like it was a chemistry test with all the guidelines. Worst class I have taken ever.

loved professor hill! i never read the textbook so don't buy it. perusall is used for discussions so interact with the text a lot through there bc that's what the final was graded off of. very clear on expectations and feedback was helpful. the lectures were fast-paced but interesting.

The textbook is useful for studying for exams when he gives the study guide, but I never read it and I don't think it's necessary. He does a good job at explaining things clearly and concisely, my only thing is that there would be times where I felt like he was talking too fast. Other than that, this class is honestly an easy A.

Professor Hill was great during lectures and clearly knows his stuff. The course is very lecture orientated. As long as you attend lectures, and discussions, and have a good overall understanding of American politics, you will be fine. The textbook is not necessary, but recommended.

Cared about students and understanding. Discussion is mandatory for a grade, as long as you show up you're good. I tended to overthink this class and thought it was harder when it really isn't. Hill makes material clear and posts study guides before exams. As long as you pay attention and take notes, you'll pass.

The lectures are pre-recorded. There are main concepts he covers very well in lecture. The discussion readings were difficult imo (im not a poli sci major) but just annotate it and you get full credit (pretty easy). 1 2-page essay, 1 midterm and final. He posts a study guide. I thought this class was more difficult than it ended up being, good prof
Great guy great teacher

Professor Dang is a great teacher and person. Class graded on quizzes (15%) a data exploration project (35%) and a final 1000 word essay (50%) where the prompt is released at the start of the quarter. Great lecturer and helps relate the content to real issues which is very helpful. Lots of reading but can usually just skim over. Not a harsh grader.

Professor Nhat is incredibly supportive and understanding. I learned a lot about CA Government during 3hour lectures and didn't fall asleep once. Graded by: one 5-page paper 25%, one 2-page paper 12.5%, one 1-page memo 12.5%, one 2-page Policy Proposal Fact Sheet 50%. The Fact sheet is the final and there is no midterm. (Summer Session)

Covered the contents of the textbook really well. Went above and beyond with regards to explaining the material. He was also available outside class. There is weekly/ bi-weekly homework. Also attendance is mandatory. The midterms and finals are open-book/open-note. The exams are just minor variations of what was covered in class.

Attendance is mandatory with a focus on learning over grades! A large chunk of the class got an A. HW and projects are relevant to the coursework and concepts taught in class. Professor is really helpful outside of the class as well and lenient in corrections of HW/tests.

The assignments are similar to the previous years so if you know senior studnets you may look for their helps if you need. This class is easy compared to fluid mechanism. There are around 30 people in the class and no TA, so Dr. Chen needs to grade the assignments by himself. I think that the reason he gave everybody almost full credits.

Took CMC History of English Lang:

Indubitably the greatest prof of the 21st century. Socrates reincarnate. The MJ of literature.

If you get into his class, thank the Lord for your blessings. His lectures are nothing short of pure ecstasy. Many strive for greatness, some even come close. But only one can stand on the pedestal: Seth Lerer.

Professor Lerer is easily one of the best professors at UCSD. He's charismatic, kind, and hilarious! You lose a lot if you miss his lectures, but he always makes them fun and engaging so going to class is never a difficult choice. Can't recommend him enough!

He makes many, many jokes in class, not all of which are entirely appropriate. But literature can be interpreted in many ways, and he has a PhD, as he reminded us many times, which makes him qualified to interpret literature. Really a great professor who is an absolutely amazing lecturer.
Coolest professor I've had thus far. He's crazy, but in a good way. You can tell he loves what he does and it makes him an even better teacher. Totally recommend him!!

10/10 professor. The fire alarm went off so we had to evacuate outside, but he just got up on a bench and continued lecturing. Definitely going to see if I can snag another one of his classes while I'm here at UCSD.

Don't love her teaching style. The topics were interesting and the class discussions were interesting, but she was mean when grading. She's new to the school, so she doesn't understand the culture of the department. Many students complained about her being too harsh when grading papers and I agree. The rubrics were not clear.

Professor Gosin started very promising as a professor, but as the quarter went on, I started to dislike her teaching style. Her pedagogy does not align with the theoretical methods she is teaching (critical humility, rejecting research, etc.) and the pedagogy of the Ethnic Studies department. She is harsh and not understanding. Don't recommend.

Dr. Spencer is great with his lectures, doesn't assign homework but you can learn the material through the reading and lectures easily, the tests are straight forward and he grades the essay portions fairly.

Fairly easy class- little bit heavy on weekly content, can feel redundant. Note vocab the professor repeats in lectures- it'll be in the hw and tests. Communicate if you need extensions and the Prof. will work with you. As long as you make an honest attempt on each assignment you'll get full credit every time. Does check for AI work, do your own!
Doesn't let you have your own opinion unless its the same as his. Very one sided class.
Very knowledgable and passionate about material. Clearly sets guidelines of the class and sticks to them. Lenient in grading and always willing to help.

The class is quite easy if you have basic prior programming experience. Lectures were clear and got to the point with lots of example scripts. Homework and exams accurately represented content in class. The professor/TA responded regularly on Piazza.

Focuses more on problem solving rather then memorization, which can be a bit tricky, but with some practice (or literally any prior experience) is perfectly manageable. Lectures were clear, and I genuinely feel confident using the material outside of class in the future.

Not a big fan of this professor. Lectures are essentially mandatory, assigns homework in the last week of class and doesn't get around to grading them until its too late. I'd steer clear of his classes if at all possible...

Overall, lectures and his teaching is average. The most annoying part of the class is the homework and the exams. The homework is usually not hard, however, he really likes to add problems afterwards to mess up your schedule. The exams are hard compared to the HW. He also give unhelpful answers and does not clarify on the grading scale much. Avoid

Clear expectations/grading and actually wants us to learn MATLAB not just learn a few commands. Homework can be somewhat complicated but not unmanageable if this is your first coding class. Very flexible and open to changing things around based on student's thoughts. Great prof!

Clear lectures with good example problems. Homework was from the textbook and graded fairly, with most of the points based on completion. Exams accurately represented material learned from lectures. Professor Zadeh is also very caring and attentive to students' needs.

I love this Professor so much! His lectures are so so fun and interactive! He cares a lot for his students. He doesn't curve or give extra credit and is very clear of that since the beginning of the course. graded on 2 midterms and a final + weekly quizzes
The final was harder than the midterms for me so prepare well!

Prof. Nieh is fantastic!!! lectures are incredibly enriching with deliberately chosen video clips and readings that perfectly supplement the overall learning. Learned so much in this course and the concepts are so inspiring and intriguing! Really wish he can teach more classes! 
Manageable workload. Take good notes and you'll be fine!

sweetest professor ever. I wish I could take him for every class. Grading criteria is very clear, no curving or extra credit. He made mistakes on the exams but immediately corrected and awarded points back to students. Clear lectures, attendance not mandatory. It's a lot of information and takes some time to digest but I loved this class.

He is AMAZING! lectures are fun and he shows lots of videos. I felt like my last midterm was unfairly graded since some of the multiple choice questions he didn't cover in lecture, and I didnt even ask for a regrade request - but he acknowledged his mistake and gave everyone points back for questions he didn't cover. So sweet! recommend

One of the best professors in the Bio department. Always provides examples to pair with concepts we learn in class and explains them very well. I find that it is not that the material isn't hard, but rather that the content and Professor is so engaging that studying for his class becomes less of a chore.

I had originally written a poor review for this teacher, but after our second midterm and final, I believe he has shown significant improvement and has actually listened to student feedback. Still not the best lecturer (I mostly self-studied the course using the textbook) but his review sheet was pretty good and the exams were very fair.
Started out rough but listened to feedback from students and made huge improvements. 2nd midterm and final were very fair, homework and MATLAB was basically free.

After the first two weeks I stopped attending lectures since the content never made any sense. Spent the entire quarter learning by reading the textbook and was able to do fine in the class.
