Towards the end of the quarter he did listen to feedback and ended up improving on his slideshows a lot which made the content we were learning more clear.

I would highly reccomend AVOIDING this professor. 
His lectures were difficult to follow/ he grazes over stuff. 
It's basically a teach yourself with the textbook/ hopefully understand 10% of what he is saying. 
basically learned by 95% textbook and 5% class
Also the HWs are crazy long, not great feedback
Tests were difficult/ thoery based

The class itself is very information dense, and Dr. Herzik seems to restate whats on his slides instead of expanding on them. That being said, his slides are very informative and attending lecture and discussion is paramount to success. Has some helpful office hours but on a whole the tests are tough and need a lot of preparation.
Long dense lectures, but discussions and office hours are very helpful.

he made tests harder on purpose which doesnt make sense and also kinda means that hes failing us on purpose. very unreasonable on tests. he teaches us soooooooo much info and doesnt make it clear in what we need to learn for the test which makes it hard to study bc we are all over the place. i wouldnt recommend taking this professor at alllll

Herzik's lecture is just mediocre. Maybe it was online, I felt like he was just reading the slides, and the concepts would not stick from just his lectures. I had to actually read the book, and I felt like the book gave better explanations. His exams do make you think and not simple but no complaint in that.

(Took class online) Lectures very detailed and straightforward. Very accessible, class was organized pretty well. Grades included 2 midterms, 1 final, 10 discussions and 10 HW. Exam was relevant to lectures but biochem is just a hard class overall so the tests were tough lol lots of "Select all that apply" questions and free response (key words!!)

I really enjoyed this course! Quizzes every week with unlimited attempts. Exams are open book and a little tough but if you review lectures then you should be good. She also offers a one time extra credit assignment which is nice!

Her lectures are pretty dense w/ info and she talks fast. However, I LOVED that the lectures were short, clear, and precise. You can always slow down the lecture speed if you think it's too fast. Quizzes have unlimited attempts; all quizzes and exams are open note. Textbook not required (Yay!). Very straightforward class, I highly recommend

The class is not too bad. Quizzes are unlimited attempts (40%). Two 30 questions mc exams (60%). No homework and book is not necessary since tests are lectures only. Don't memorize the details just understand the general concepts. I recommend typing your notes to command+find info faster on tests. The only complaint I have is she talks really fast.

It's not a hard class conceptually, you need to understand the bigger idea and not memorize every small detail. I don't know why others are want to complain because you can redo the quizzes as many times as u want for a full grade. Exams are a large chunk but its all open notes so its not as hard.

Although Dr. Snyder is extremely intelligent in immunology, I would NOT recommend anyone to take her. Since this class was asynchronous, it was very dense in lectures as the videos were all pre-recorded. She literally talks at 2x speed as if she is reading off a script and it makes the material very hard to follow along.

Very knowledgeable and kind professor - tests and homeworks feel fair/straightforward. Unfortunately the course content overlaps with a lot of other upper division ECON classes, but it's definitely still interesting when there is new ground to be covered.

Previous reviews are quite accurate. She is really nice person and her lectures are unorganized. I also wished that her exams were somewhat different. But honestly, it wasn't a challenging class and she is really nice and that was enough for me. Stay in class, study everything she covers which is not even that many then you will be totally fine.
Her exam is really hard and complicated. She always adds new questions to the exams. I discourage students to take her class.

Please avoid this new professor. Although she seems like a nice person, she really needs to improve her teaching quality. Her notes are extremely disorganized and hard to read, her graphs looks like kindergarten drawings. Had one question worth 55% of entire midterm that she only briefly mentioned in class. she do not even give examples in lecture

Professor Meckel is a very nice person who cares about her students. She even bought the whole class pizza and drinks after a long midterm. BUT I do think she can benefit from changing up her teaching style such as encourage students involvement and more organized notes and etc. Overall, I recommend attending lecture and office hours .
just do not take

Professor Shafir is very knowledgeable about this subject and I wish I could have interacted with him more, but couldn't bc course was online. This course is pretty laid back and grade mostly depends on midterm (2 essays) and a final project. My advice: Start the final early! It's available many weeks in advance and future you will be grateful.
JUST DONT TAKE HIS CLASSES. HE IS NOT NORMAL PERSON. HE IS RUDE AND HARSH. JUST DONT
NIR is heartless and a mediocre educator.

Class was very interesting! Prof is pretty chill and picks interesting topics of discussion. Most of the grade depends on the midterm and final (2 essays each, all 4-6 pages) which have clear prompts. The TA grades them, so schedule office hrs with them if you want specific writing feedback. Both prof and TA are helpful and don't grade too harshly.

Began assigning pop quizzes during week 7 because she finally realized the weekly 2-3 readings she assigns were not being read. Attendance is mandatory and definitely picks favorites with the students. Runs the lecture like a high school class through asking "who wants to read this section" and "can someone volunteer to read this paragraph". 2/10
Great professor, and a funny guy. The lectures were kinda hard but not too hard to do the hws. There were no exams for this class, so hurray!

Awesome professor! His accent isn't a big deal, his niceness worths more! If you go to class, copy all the examples he did on the board, do the homeworks, and make sure you understand the problems from the given sample tests, then you gonna rock this math class! He solves HW questions and provides several examples in class! Extremely helpful!

Professor explains each concepts way more complicated then it needs to be. Not helpful AT ALL. Doesn't want students to succeed in class. Goes over problems really fast, doesn't really care if the students don't understand. Study the sample midterms, thats basically what he tests you on. A LOT of hw, Had to take this class for my major...
Final is ridiculous. Lectures aren't too helpful (can easily learn from the book). Accent makes it hard to understand sometimes. Cracks a couple of jokes in a while though. Decent professor overall.

I pretty much taught myself using the book and the solutions guide. Lectures aren't that helpful. If you get an A on the final, you get an A in the class. Otherwise, he calculates a cumulative grade. The final was crazy hard, I thought I would be lucky to get a C in the class but I ended up with a B and am satisfied.

If you have the opportunity to take a class with Kisun, do it. Lectures are entertaining and make the material understandable. Exams are very fair and and look just like the practice midterms, if you attend lecture and do the practice midterms you will do just fine. He offers a lot of supplemental material to help students succeed.

Very excellent professor! His exams are not too challenging as he allows students to use a crib sheet for each exam. He also reviews the material before each exam. There are times where he goes fast, but I still think he is one of the best math professors in the department. I also can't believe that he is leaving. He will truly be missed.

His lessons were outlined very clearly and explained well. He goes over lots of examples which are great for math classes: very in-depth. He's a super nice person and very accommodating! Tests are straightforward and basically just the practice problems we do in class. Active on piazza and useful office hours.
Probably the best math professor I've ever had. Sadly he is leaving UCSD. Homework is a big portion of the grade in order to help students who aren't great test takes like me.

Amazing Professor! Definitely, he is the best teacher I've ever met. His lectures are well-organized and everything is clear. You can understand differential equations very very easily by attending his lecture. Homework and exam are 100% representations of the things we covered. Exams are not challenging, too.

The professor was overall a minor part of the course. Lectures were basically just read off the slides that he posted on Canvas but if you go it's extra credit. All of the grading is based on essays and discussion participation
Lectures were great. Not a hard class.
legend
loved the class, especially lectures. theres a lot to read but its fine if you go to lectures and section and he explains everything
tough grader, prefer no taking

Professor Vandevelde is an amazing lecturer--he's funny, but also very articulate and certainly knows his stuff. The course isn't easy per se, so much as it's graded on three multiple choice exams which, if you do the readings and study, you'll do well on. Basically, you get the grade you worked for. He's also very personable!

Funny guy and honestly great professor. I watched his lectures online and was able to follow each one easily. Laughed out loud a lot while watching them too from the stuff he says. Highly recommend him if you're interested in constitutional history.
Love this guy. He is so smart and i love listening to his lectures. He makes class very interesting, simple and straightforward. He also looks like Jack Nicholson. Sweet man.
His knowledge is insane! He is open to guidance, extremely kind, educational and overall an amazing Professor.
GOAT.

Highly recommend!! It is a 6-unit class because of the weekly field visits to a community center where we plan out activities for the kids there. These field visits as well as lectures are mandatory and are honestly pretty fun and engaging. There are also readings due every week that we have to write annotations and reflections on and field notes.

Professor is really kind and understanding. The class is set up with a lot of weekly reading assignments and writing assignments, but they are doable. This was a really fun and interactive class, highly recommend!

It was supposed to be an easy A class but it requires a LOT of work. I mean the work itself is OK but I got an unfair grade. She seems very nice but a VERY HARSH GRADER. I don't think she saw the real work some of us put into, but only saw some people's transparent work. I am hugely disappointed at her.
She's clearly invested in the class. Amazing human being.

Honestly one of the best professors I have ever had. I have taken 4 classes with her already and I would be doing more if I wasn't graduating. It got to the point that when I was picking classes this quarter I just typed her name into the search bar and added them all.  I would totally recommend this course and this proffesor for any class.

He explains the materials very well, but most of the class is focused on the lab (as it's a lab class). There are 4 skill demos that are pretty easy, as long as you are confident with the practice you are basically guranteed an A. The class is a bit disorientating though, you need many links and they are all over the place.

This class is really easy. Just doing the bare minimum is enough to get an A. He explains things really well and he definitely gives you the tools to use the knowledge from this class when approaching other topics from different classes.

He is very passionate about teaching the material. He cares about making class an enjoyable learning experience. He encourages participation. He made it very clear that any questions are welcome and that he put a lot of personal effort into the course material. He often showed examples of coding in real time which was always helpful.

He is very good. The lecture is optional and the lab is mandatory. The grade is decided by skill demo, lab reports, and lab participation. I got 7/8 for the skill demo, all full credits for the lab report, and attended all labs. I also submitted all the handouts and quizzes on time. The skill demo is not hard and similar to practice. I got an A+.

His lectures were well organized and easy to take notes on, although the pace was quite fast. He clearly cared about the students' learning and encouraged everyone to participate in class through Mentimeter polls (which served as a helpful review of the lecture material). Tests were challenging but fair; if you study, you will succeed.

Many pointless assignments in my opinion and very tough grading. Nobody in our class got full-credit on assignments, highest grade I saw was an A- on papers. Professor Wilson is a kind teacher, who is very passionate about the Muir Writing Program. That being said, I think there are easier professors.
Grades extremely unfairly. I would not recommend taking her class.

Marion is the coolest and she's asst director of MCWP so she knows her sh%t. Visit her in OH! Definitely attend all classes. Muir Writing has a really strict attendance policy and you'll fail if you miss more than a couple of classes. MCWP classes suuuck, but Marion is really funny and makes an otherwise difficult class tolerable.

This class demands hours of your attention. It's heavy on the research and often multiple assignments are due within the same week. I do not enjoy writing essays, so this class was difficult for me. Dr. Wilson helped me get through it. She always makes herself available to help you if you are struggling. It's a hard class but the Prof. is amazing.
Unclear about assignments. Says you never have to bring textbooks to class and then asks you to take out your textbook next lecture. A lot of work for a pointless class...

he gave us an excessive amount of work to do. Quizzes are very specific and timed. This year, the class had to attend 3 screenings (which were not on campus), help set up an event, work the event, and complete journal entries along with a 1000 journal reflection and a film review during FINALS WEEK. The lectures were not helpful.

He was overall a good professor. His lectures weren't mandatory, but the discussions were. There was one group project at the end of the quarter, but it was fairly easy. There is a lot of reading and there are reading quizzes every week and film quizzes every other week. Overall, I didn't have to put that many hours a week into homework.

A lot of readings and films. Weekly reading quizzes, biweekly film quizzes, a group project, and final. Attendance is not mandatory for lectures but discussions. He also offers extra credits on quizzes but not too frequently. Take this class if you want an A but be careful because everyone's grade drops to A- or B+ after group project.

Assigns a lot of readings, but discusses them in his lectures. Imo, he is a bit unclear during his lectures. But, his slides cover essentially everything that comes up during the online final exam. His reading choices are stellar, I do like reading most of them (except the Debord reading) and this class provides a new lens to view social problems.

lectures aren't mandatory but are definitely very helpful to understand weekly readings. can be very reading heavy but honestly not bad as long as you keep up with it and pay attention in discussion. no midterm, only a group project which is easy as long as you communicate with your TA.

Class is about "normative framework," meaning stan forces his students to subscribe to his manifesto, and you are wrong if you disagree with him. His opinion precedes factual statements and empirical evidence, which is shown in his grading. He lacks an in-depth knowledge of economics where if you try to go beyond the intro level he will be confused

MID. The material is not terribly difficult, however he kind of rambles off in class a lot and the lectures are very hard to follow. Could not get it together for our midterm and there is a final + final research paper. If you have taken a research class before, it should be fine but otherwise I suggest trying to take a diff professor.
Chill younger professor working on his PhD. 4 problem sets, 1 midterm, 1 final. He's pretty good at explaining during class and if you ask him questions.

Professor Izadi went beyond and taught us more cool math than the course mandates! However, her explanations for complicated concepts like the wedge product or Stokes's theorem were sometimes confusing.
Great professor who explained complex concepts well in office hours.
Great professor. Very patient and caring. Lecture is clear and homework is helpful. Exam is not easy but curve is generous. Strong recommendation.
Fantastic professor, incredibly class, really fun.
Really fun professor! Always enthusiastic in class and seemed to really enjoy teaching. Definitely take this class with her.
Professor Mckinley is passionate and caring. She explains concepts clearly in lecture. Also, her TA Nicholas Sieger is extremely helpful and knowledgeable. Go to their OHs if you can.

Gwen is one of the best professors I met! She is excellent, reliable, willing to help, etc. You will know once you take her class! Also, the class is easy to understand but you have to attend the lecture, and her class is pretty fun! The HW is related to the class and tbh, the exams are more than the class but those are pretty good practices!

Econ 140 was one of the few Econ classes that was genuinely interesting. The tests were graded a little tougher than I would've liked, but overall it wasn't too difficult of a course. Prof. Clemens is a really smart guy and you can tell he really cares about the subject. Not an easy A but an engaging elective.

A lot of content but very interesting material. Grade is 2 midterms+final (90% total) along with 4 writing assignments (10% total). Lecture was sometimes boring but he tried to engage the class and answer questions. Really nice guy and brought donuts for the class one day which was cool. Exams were tricky so attend the TA review sessions to prepare
The material is challenging and the lecture is long. But the time is absolutely worth spending if you are interested in the health econ.
Great professor.

I took his class just becuase I thought he would be easy since he's new to UCSD. However, he's incredible hard!!! The practice problems, practice exams and the PPT didnt relate to our exams.  The concepts are dry but at lease he should teach us how to apply. I feel sick that I have to learn everything by myself but not from him. Sad!!!

This teacher held class no more than 3 times over ten weeks, consecutively canceling classes an hour before by posting on her canvas page, not in an email. She promised asynchronous lectures that were never uploaded, and she was impossible to contact and forced students to essentially take a class by themselves through Quizlet-copied quizzes.
Interesting topics but unorganized

Tends to speak mockingly about different cultural practices. Very disorganized, would cancel lectures with little to no warning, sometimes with as little as one hour of notice before lecture; on days we did have class, she was consistently late, whether it was in-person or on Zoom. Class was easy and readings were good. Soured by her incompetence.

She is a very caring and lenient professor, but her class was a bit disorganized at times. Due dates were changed constantly and lectures were often canceled last minute. This doesn't make her a bad professor though... she is a great lecturer and provides relevant, in-depth feedback on your work. But if you like structure, I wouldn't recommend.

Lectures are clear, with slides; assignments are research or reflection. Reading is not required. Hybrid model. Professor Kalleres is passionate about her field and the class. 
Sadly, she is disorganized. She forgets deadlines, doesn't explain her expectations, etc. Unclear if this is typical of her character, or due to recent personal situations.

This professor has a strong accent (french) and speaks very quietly, making it hard to pay any attention. Beyond that there are half a dozen readings per week (each about 20 pages). The assignments for this class are relatively easy however the final is NOT ( 50% of grade) in-person and consists of multiple essays.

I have never taken a class with him before and i can say that i never will again! The assignment requirements were not clear and very broad. The average for an assignment was below a point and it was worth 10 points... Graded on very few things and the final is worth 50%!! Very material heavy and does not post the slides. I do not recommend him.

Very unprofessional. Grading is based on 3 assignments that makes up 50% and the other 50% is the final. Doesn't care about his students. Made me feel very uncomfortable. So much reading and doesn't post lecture slides. Did use full 3 hours of lecture. Do not recommend worst experience ever. Not understanding.

If you're a good student, take this class. You'll have to put in the effort. You'll be fine if you attend class regularly, do at least part of the readings, and can write fairly well. The grade is based on two short essays to write (midterm and final). The professor is very knowledgeable but not great with technology lol.

Professor Shafir offers an objective view of the Israel-Palestine conflict, dispelling myths and drawing light on a situation greatly in need of viable solutions. His passion for human rights and equality is prevalent and his personal experience adds valuable insight to the course. A must take for anyone interested in Middle East affairs.

Would not recommend this professor and class. The professor is extremely critical and strict, always setting high expectations for the class. He rarely says any words of encouragement and is hard to approach. The lectures in class were boring and not that helpful. This class was just not enjoyable at all and it caused me a lot of stress.

His lectures consist of quickly clicking through slides without in depth explanations of anything. For the first midterm he didn't provide any review material or information and ignored all Piazza questions. He assigns a ridiculous amount of homework but grades a random selection of questions. The homework is not representative of tests.

I took him for math2 and he was clear in the way he taught. He is the best of the math2 professors in my opinion. I went to his office hours a couple times and I always understood the content so fast after he explained it. He is caring and understanding. I would def recommend to take him.
The lecturer is really nice and teaches well. The tests are fair. The course is pretty much plug and chug.
Very kind and always available to ask questions. His lectures can be a bit disorganized but he explains content very well. Highly recommend!

Professor Ramachandran was a good lecturer. He had office hours twice a week in case of questions about the lectures or homework. 

Lecture notes were typed out and clear to understand and were posted promptly after class.

I made a Rate My Professor account for the sole purpose of rating Professor Meyer. This is easily one of the worst experiences I have had at UCSD. She takes Shakespeare considerably too seriously and her TAs graded very unfairly and she "didnt do regrades". I delegated more effort to this class than Neurobio to get an A. Anything else is better.

decent prof. not super amazing. attendance quizzes were easy. and writeups are easy which equals 35%. group project + presentation is 35%. midterm and final 15% each but they are graded very subjectively. not sure how hard the other profs are for 112 but this one doesnt take much time or effort, i just dont know about how good the grade will be.
If you pay extra attention to the hw then the exams should not be too hard. lowest exam was dropped, plus everything on the exams comes from the lecture slides and hw
Truly cares about the students' learning and progress!
She has a very strong accent so its hard to understand her but she is passionate about her area of study. Exams are reasonable.
The homework is so tough and have no idea for the project...

Personal experience:    
Lectures aren't good. 30% of homework questions are tough. 70% of midterm questions are tough.

Advice:    
Take CSE203B only if you love math and have done undergraduate-level probability and vector/matrix calculus. Some of the questions can be really tough. Piazza discussions helped figure them out.
Felt the course was pretty difficult, homeworks and lectures were worlds apart.

I understood half of what he said, but all of what he taught. The recommended book is useful. His practice exams are useful. Most if not all of his examples in lecture will help during exams. I'd be surprised if you can't pass the class with all the resources available. He has an accent but answers all questions well..

Why should he put the midterm on President day? After talking to him, he still schedule it from Saturday - Monday (President day, so it's a holiday). Lots of homework that is clustered at the same time. Terrible accent.
His Lectures are clear and easy to follow. The midterms are fair and come from the textbook HW problems.

Professor Misha is actually nice in person if you visit his office. He's not a good lecturer though. (I really feel sorry for him because you can feel that he really tries to help, but couldn't get why we're not following this material)

Took CHEM127 in Fall2018. He is not a bad person as he personally respects you. But, he curved the class to avg of 2.5/C. Pop quiz are give and have median of 0 for three times. He is basically reciting the textbook. Quiz not allowed cheatscheet but midterm and final does. Avoid his chem127 unless you have evidence that he improves a lot.

Literally the worst professor I have ever encountered in my three years as an undergrad. Lecture materials were straight regurgitations of the textbook. Lecture was "mandatory" due to pop quizzes which were irregularly spaced. One time the median score on one of these quizzes was a 0. (That's >50% of the class getting a 0).

Avoid this professor at all costs. Lectures have nothing to do with the insanely hard homework. Midterm and final are worth 80% of your final grade. Midterm was not at all anything like the homework questions and extremely difficult (class average was a 33%). Look for another professor or be dragged in the wrath of hell with this one.

I took this class my fall quarter as a gpa booster and did not know what to expect, however, this class turned out to be very easy. Midterm and final were based on a short group performance and teacher was very kind and helpful. Just go to class and participate and you should get an A, class was not as bad as some people are making it seem lol

Overall she was a great professor often it was hard because it was an 8 am class but other than that it was a pretty easy A the midterm was a small performance and the final was an outside performance but honestly it was really easy. She shows a lot of passion to ballet and it is seen through the dances. I loved taking her class.

She does not know how to teach dance. The class was not beginner friendly and she graded harshly on midterms/finals. The final was outside of class time and not scheduled on webreg. I recommend taking literally any other professor for dance. Class was quiet and miserable.

He's lecture skill is decent, but sometimes drowsy. His teacher assistants are awful, picky, and cynical. They use their own rubric to judge you and deduct points on things not on the rubric, including some extremely unnecessary part. They don't look at the details and do not look the whole page, and there is no way to argue the grade back.

The professor was pretty poggers. Avoid the class if you hate group projects outside your major like me. I had to take this class to graduate and COGS 10 was not offered at the time. There are 4 group projects. The last one includes a final presentation and a video + 10-page written report. The class is really time-consuming, but the prof is great.

Professor Meyers' lectures are pretty fun and interesting, and he's a really nice and non-intimidating professor. This course is mostly group projects, no big exams, and as long as you follow the rubrics provided, you will receive a good grade. It's not difficult but may sometimes be time-consuming.

Gave great real world examples which made class interesting. He gave out quizzes every week, but they can be done in groups. The class itself isn't hard, but since it's ALL group based, your grades depend on other people.

Professor Peach genuinely cares about you passing the class and wants you to stress the least about the class. All tests are online take home exam and open night! Very easy class with only 3 assignments and one assignment at the end of the quarter that only takes a sentence or two long.

Easiest class ever. The professor literally wants this to be your least worried class. She is basically willing to give you a good grade if you just hit submit! 4 homeworks with the last one being a 1-2 sentece response to a question. 3 exams on canvas non-timed. Easy A! Only con is some questions are very specific and all the answer can be correct

Professor Peach genuinely cares about her students and wishes for them to succeed. There are few hw assignments and the exams are open note and can be taken over the span of a few days. Professor Peach is also passionate about what she does/teaches, so some lectures throughout the quarter were motivational and inspiring.

She is actually a sweetheart! Attendance is not mandatory but in class she covers everything that you will need for your HW and exams. There is 4 HW throughout the 10 week and it is 40%  of your grade. Exam #1 is 20%, Exam #2 is 20% and Final is also 20%. All the exams are open note. You do them at your own time and it is multiple choice.

Graded on homework assignments and three take home untimed open note exams. Her exams do contain unintentional trick questions. Super accommodating and is willing to discuss if certain questions on her tests were fair or not. Overall easy class and an amazing professor. Would take again. Do note that her exams are 60% of your grade though.

Prof. Konopacky really wanted every student to succeed. She gave everyone the tools to do so, though lectures, homework, and office hours. The course material is not hard, as long as you follow the lectures and homework. The topics are super cool and she is SO passionate about what she teaches. It's a super fun and chill class!

I always received quick responses to emails. She answers student questions in class, and specifically sets aside time for them. There isn't much math for a physics class. Discussion section acts as homework help. The class is much more about stars than black holes.

lectures are kinda helpful but she does just read off the slides. homework is all multiple-choice and 1 assignment each week, it's more from the textbook than what was covered in the lecture. also sometimes she'll cover things needed to know for the homework after it was due. midterms and finals are multiple-choice & there's 1 project that's easy.
Caring professor with clear and organized lectures. Not too much homework, tests are multiple choice.

Extremely sweet and caring. Lectures are straightforward. the quizzes and exams are slightly harder than the practices/examples in lecture but not too bad. the homework can take time but the final was only 15% of the class and she drops 2/5 quizzes. an A is pretty easy if you do the hw and try hard for the quizzes. would definitely take her again.

I like Prof. Sirbuly's classes because his exams are very concise and he specifically tells us how exams will be graded. His exams for Nano104 were open book so that was a plus point. He also curves the class so very high chances of a good grade. He always responds to emails and doubts very quickly.

I took prof engelbergs class remote. He and TAs respond quickly to any questions on piazza. The recorded lectures were asynchronous and help a lot with understanding the homework. We just took our midterm (synchronous) and I found it to be much more difficult than the homeworks due to lack of references. If you take this class, be ready to study!

Beginning of Ballet - Amazing professor. She really cares about her students learning and having a good time. Attendance is mandatory and counts towards grade. As long you show up and demonstrate effort you'll get an A. You gotta learn some ballet definitions (super easy). Very fun class if you've never tried ballet before.
Amazing professor, made beginning dance for GE very fun she really really cares about her students

Beginner Ballet class - few readings, mostly videos watched on your own time for additional understanding. "Lectures" are a mix of barre and center; Caligagan takes time to demonstrate the movements if there is still confusion (super helpful). "Easy A" for the grading criteria, but if you do not practice on your own time, you will not improve.

I thought she was super sweet and caring in class. When you participated, she was sweet and it was really great. But when I got my grades for my work back (when it was simple things like drafts and responses), she was really harsh about it, and I didn't like that. The lectures are heavy, and she talks a lot. Great person, too harsh of a grader.

Honestly the best class that I have taken at UCSD. She really cares about the class and tries her best to make sure we pass the class and become better writers. Really knowledgeable and gives honest constructive feedback. Class was something I actually looked forward to as we often had really great discussions.

Lectures drag on and on. Tough grader considering the vagueness of her lectures. Grades rough drafts as if they were polished, finished works. Extremely hard to use her creative writing feedback because her tips are so wordy and generalized. Class discussions are tedious; get ready to have everything you say be rephrased and repeated back to you.

Really great, bright professor. Really fosters an environment of family in the class, and you're never too uncomfortable to speak up. However, you will not know where you stand in the class until you get your final grade, which is so incredibly frustrating. There isn't a clear grading system so you're kind of in the dark.

This class was easy and fun. All texts can be found online, so you don't have to buy anything. There's two assignments, and then the rest is just your final short story (one rough draft, one final draft) that has to be 10-15 pages. Show up daily, participate, and turn your easy work in on time and you'll pass with flying colors. Forbes is fantastic

Professor Wenxin Zhou is an outstanding educator, making complex math concepts accessible and engaging. His passion for teaching and commitment to student success is evident in every lecture. Highly recommend his courses for a rewarding and enlightening experience.

i didn't watch lecture that much but i needed to for the midterm because it didn't involve any coding and was mostly actual conceptual questions - i found it weird and difficult considering the 5 coding assignments and the coding final exam. the class isn't too bad and you learn a good amount in R, so i would recommend it
The person talks too fast as if no one will notice his accent and I can barely understand what he is saying!

It's not a hard class compared to others but I found myself lost a lot of time in his lecture. Also, only 20 students show up for lecture. The midterm (50%) is basically you memorizing the practice midterm. Hopefully, he'll try to shape up for future classes. But imo, you shouldn't take him for now, unless you want easy A & not learning anything.
Rough course

This professor honestly did a good job at her job. She was new here, came in with the mindset that we were going to do more than the average writing class, and utilized various texts that showed multiple perspectives on different writing techniques. Also the Harkness model discussion were not always the most entertaining, she teaches well.

As tough as this course is, professor Rangel does a good job at making the material more complex and intimidating than it should be. Lectures are informational dumps that make it easy to fall behind & hard to focus. She gives options: weekly homework or labs, but its all or nothing. Making mistakes reflects heavily; extra credit isn't much.
Grade is based on participation and 3 exams. Exam questions can be a bit difficult but she does her best to explain the difficult concepts.

Challenging course, but Prof. Rangel did an amazing job. Her lectures are detailed and TAs were helpful. I thought the exams were fair as long as you watched/attended all lectures and made sure you actually understood the material. Hands down, one of the best professors.

The course is incredibly difficult, especially since Prof. Rangel pushes a very nuanced and detailed understanding compared to previous courses. She's an incredible lecturer and engages with students during lectures. Weekly learning checks are tricky (select all that apply) and midterms are tough, but plenty of EC. Would recommend OH and section!

Dr. Rangel does not accurately or fairly test students. Material on exams and weekly quizzes are heavily conceptual and complex while material in lecture is elementary. Rangel does offer extra credit, but it is still not enough for you to pass the class if you are not dedicating your entire life this class. Good luck if ur not a bio major.
the most difficult course I have ever taken, there is no way this course is for undergrad.
not easy, but he's not bad.
Took him for 120C. The class was a mess and the final was extremely tough. Kapar seemed to think we were all PhD students. The slides were definitely not maybe for undergrads.

One of the best professors at UCSD Econ department. Makes everything so clear and is there for so many last minute questions during the midterm and final review. Everything combined really helps for his exams.

Wuthrich is hands down the greatest professor the econ department at ucsd has ever had. He deserves every raise possible. 120C is the hardest of the 120 series and it is surprisingly the one I did the best in and I owe it all to professor Wuthrich. His lectures are very clear and everything you need for the tests will be in the lecture. 10/10 prof!
This is for Calc II at Pomona. Great office hours, 1 homework assignment a week w corrections. Overall an amazing lecturer. Super chill and easy to talk to. Miss her a lot.

Lectures were very thorough and straight to the point. We were allowed cheat sheets on every exam, and she gives lots of partial credit. Office hours and mentor session are necessary but helpful. McAdam is a very kind and caring individual and she does her best to check in with students to make sure they are doing alright in all aspects.

I had her for math 3c and she is a horrible teacher. She does not explain things well and spends a lot of time explaining things that we don't even need to know for the class. She overcomplicates everything and makes it hard to understand, leaving the class confused. There are two midterms and a final, and we are not allowed cheat sheets for them.

I had this professor for Math 3C. She does not explain concepts well, kind of just mimics the textbook. The textbook is pretty hard to understand too because there is not much explanation to the solutions to the problems. She gives homework due weekly and two midterms. On the midterms you are not allowed to use a cheat sheet or calculators.
I wish he could teach all my classes. Amazing lectures. Great professor
Actually teaches the material and homework and tests are extremely relevant to the class material.

Worst professor I've had in MAE and gave a bad impression for what to expect from the department. Homeworks were extremely difficult with really tough math, office hours are treated like an extension of lecture such that if you can't make it to both, you're going to do poorly in the class. Exams unrelated to homework, super hard, worth 50% of grade

Terrific professor, easily the best I had at UCSD. Homeworks are usually quite difficult and don't always mesh perfectly with lecture. That said, Prof. Saintillan was always very accessible and I found going to office hours to be extremely helpful (if not required). His classes won't be a breeze, but they are well worth it in my opinion.
Very hard course, but thanks to his big curve I was able to get a decent grade
just great
awesome

A real homie, quality lecturer, clearly an expert on the subject. If you get the chance, definitely pick his brain about any questions you have career-wise related to data science, he's a great resource and he clearly cares about the success of his students. 10/10 would take again.
Enjoyed his lectures and the assignments reflected what we went over in class. He broke down concepts so they were easy to understand.

He's a very professional lecturer. Contents are very fresh and following the trends. He tries to reply any email which makes him super accessible outside of classroom. I really recommend this professor.

EASY A, could not recommend this class more. 2 extra credit opportunities were easy, and a lot of this class is based on common sense. Professor Cezo had caring and engaging lectures. Spent max 1 hour on HW each week. Such a good lecturer though with guest speakers often. Got over 100% in this class because it's just that easy! DO TAKE HER!

Easy A. Attendance for lecture/discussions is mandatory, you get 1 missed discussion and I believe 4 missed lectures before it affects your grade. There is easy extra credit. I got over 100% in this class and never spent more than 2 hours working on it out of the classroom. Lecture is boring, you have online discussions, NO TESTS, easy GPA boost
Assigned a lot of homework and promoted students to join student orgs that revolve around environmental activism.

Mandatory discussions and lectures that almost put me to sleep. No test or real quizzes with most your grade being participation based. Never put more than 2 hours a week into this class and was still the easiest A I've ever earned. Realistically, you won't learn much but ig a good class if you want a GPA boost. Really nice and caring person though

Her class is insanely easy to the point of being dull. Has meaningless, but time consuming assignments. Lots of group discussion boards. No exam. Definitely do not take if you struggle with organization and multiple assignments. The work is really easy, but you have to be comfortable with multiple deadlines. Easy A if you remember to do the work.

Dr. Smith lacked enthusiasm and failed to inspire. Her teaching was uninspiring, offering minimal guidance. The class felt tedious, hindering creativity instead of fostering it. Disappointing experience overall.

Cauleens teaching approach presents significant challenges. Her style can be perceived as aggressive and highly opinionated. When reviewing student work her interpretations often come across as definitive leaving little room for alternative perspectives.She also sometimes attributes views to students that they may not hold based on her own opinions

Cauleen is very outspoken and opinionated, but she knows what she's talking about. If you take her classes with an open mind and a willingness to learn more than the subject matter, you might pick up on something really great.

She is very opinionated, if you say something in her class than you need to be able to back it up. Can be aggressive at times but means well in the end. Grading is based heavily on attendance, she takes not if you aren't there and on the completion of your projects. If you come to class every day and do the projects you will get an A.
No Comments

I ended up dropping the class, so I cannot attest to grading. Professor was consistently late to class, disorganized, and rude to students. She would go on 20 or 30 minute tangents about unnecessary things-- such as students dropping the class, how she's not responsible for printing your essay, etc.. Just not a good classroom environment.

Professor was a mess, only made it through the quarter because of her TA. Super unprofessional because she would get into arguments with her TA about how to run the course. Would not remember her students names, gave an Asian student a nickname because she didn't want to learn how to say their name.

Professor Benetta is AMAZING! She has so much experience and knowledge to share, her classes don't feel like a class as much as they feel like a place of learning (if that makes sense). She's very helpful if you have questions about assignments and will always give good feedback. Not to mention she's such a joy and hilarious

Professor Bennetta Jules -Rosette is unlike many other professors that I have had while attending UCSD , she cares for her students and sets up her classes so that everyone in them have a fair chance at earning their grade. She is brilliant and her lectures are captivating, she is passionate and that is carried on through her teaching.

I really enjoyed this teacher. Unfortunately I didn't take her until my final quarter at UCSD. I would have taken more of her classes if I had found her earlier. She has a long reading list but not all are mandatory. I learned a lot and got a good grade.

Took Spring 2023, difficulty was reasonable. Lectures do iClicker attendance, readings are tested on in lecture through clicker questions. Readings weren't too bad and only major assignment is research paper MMW15 usually has. Final was really hard that I rather take my CSE30 final again than what I had, but was graded generously. Would recommend.

Radcliff is an awesome lecturer. I had her for HITO 100 and she made really interesting exercises for us to do. There is a lot of reading, but the writing assignments are pretty easy. There's three writing assignments total and the first two are pretty short and the last one you have a lot of time to do. She's very nice and a great teacher.

Extremely passive aggressive and politically correct. Needed to control group conversations in class to her liking. Graded on how good your in class participation answers were. Has rubrics for papers with pg/word limits but docks pts for not explaining further. Parrot talk what SHE would WANT you to say and you'll be fine. Wouldn't recommend her.

Very smart but does not mess around. She will expect a lot from u, and wont tolerate nonsense. Brilliant but a straight shooter. Be very very clear with your thesis from the get go, and make sure it makes sense to her and u can defend it. Not all the reading is rlly necessary, but u most be ready to present a solid defensible argument for essays.

Radcliff did a great job teaching MMW15! She's straight forward, fair, interesting, and better than all of my MMW professors so far. She understands that the paper is tough, so she didn't make us take a midterm. Her clicker questions and readings are easy/fair and she puts all of her lectures online. If you hate MMW, then she is a great option.

Students beware, this professor will not reply to your emails and doesn't care about the students. So your grade depends on whether you had a good TA. It's a simple class with light work but I would go for other classes as GPA boosters.

A solid 1 point for both the professor and TA. Always ignoring emails. Cannot ensure the fairness. When  the TA deliberately trying to make difficulties for students for no reason, he choosed to ignore it and connive the TA.  If you are assigned to a bad TA, you even cannot get attendance points although you attend every class.

Easy A overall, but there are weekly quizzes and a movie you have to watch every week. Also, attendance is mandatory and taken usually at the beginning of every class. Need to post 3 times in 3 different discussions throughout the quarter. There is also no midterm, and there is only a final essay, which is very easy. Also, the films were great.

Professor Liao was caring and attentive throughout the course. There were a lot of readings, but I found that focusing on the ones he mentioned in class were the most helpful for answering the weekly quizzes. I'd definitely recommend him!

Generally a decent professor. Easy A if you are willing to put in some effort, but do not recommend for those who really want to learn a lot about literature. I do enjoy his readings but definitely not his lectures. His online lectures are pretty disorganized and grading criteria is also vague.
She is so nice and I loved going to her office hours

Professor Maggie provides you with incredibly interesting material and encourages you to form and express your own opinions. One of my favorite professors I've had. She sincerely cares about her students.

great prof. super friendly and helpful. there's lots or room for improvement and drafts and she genuinely cares and tries to help you if you ask for it.  very approachable and knows how to teach this class despite the dry material and the fact that its mandatory.  highly recommended
Extremely helpful, one of the best instructors I've ever had

Maggie was an awesome professor for my first quarter at UCSD! Learned a lot about the writing expectations and research writing. Topic was interesting (Memory Spaces) and lots of opportunity for re-writes, feedback, etc.  I took it for requirement but I ended up loving this class!
Great professor! He is one of the best math professors l've ever had. He is very helpful and supportive. He gives you the courage to complete math problems. Just a great professor!!

Dr. Rob is an amazing professor. He teaches math in a way that makes it easier to understand. He also motivates you in believing in yourself and having confidence. Dr. Rob is truly one of those rare professors you meet that are genuinely there for you. He is a great teacher and overall you can learn a lot from him and what he has to offer!

Best Math teacher Ive had so far, He really cares about his students. He stays up late sometimes to help students, he has a lot of office hours, sometimes even on weekends. Doesnt mind to walk to a campus cafe or Library to do some extra work together. Also a very safe space for poc students. He also loves math jokes.

2nd class with Cowan and he is so great! Lectures are mandatory and a part of your grade but he is so funny and knowledgeable so they always fly by. He draws a lot on the readings for class lectures and will call on you to give your opinion. Class grade is based on the midterm and final paper. As long as you start early you'll be good!

History of Brazil was one of my GE requirements, I loved his class, attendance was mandatory but lectures were always interesting and professor cowan was pretty funny. Grades were based off basically the midterm essay and the final essay. You have tons of time to prepare so I wouldn't worry at all. Definitely take this class if it satisfies credits

Cowan is HILARIOUS and an AMAZING lecturer and is super passionate about the subject. Participation is 30% of the grade and is based on the assigned reading, which there is ALOT of. There is a 7-10pg final paper which you have all quarter to work on. Put effort into the reading, talking in class, and research for the paper and you'll pass easily.

I took HILA 114 and professor Cowan is great. He makes already interesting lectures more enjoyable, but participation DOES matter. Both in class and with the short weekly assignment. Definitely take his class when you're not fully crammed already, or it'll be harder. Really cool prof and you learn a lot in his class.

I wasn't that interested in modern Brazilian history, but he made it interesting. 50% of the grade was weekly reading responses, so don't slack on these! The one complaint I had is that the prompt for the final research paper was kind of vague. Super chill prof though, as long as you stay on top of the assignments you'll get an A.

Tends to drone on and repeat things a lot in lectures. She knows her stuff and is published in the subject but just isn't the best at clearly explaining concepts and expectations to students. Graded on reading-heavy (closed note) quizzes and a group project. Not very tech savvy.
6 quizzes overall, 2 were dropped and a lot of readings to do before each lecture. Did not really like her as a professor.

When asked questions about lecture she was not able to provide answers. Rubric on tests in unclear. When asked about test answers and explanations about them she said that its in the reading. Essays were not bad.

Show up to class, pay attention, take notes, and review the readings the day before the quizzes if you want to do well. Professor Blair-Loy is kind and well-respected in her field. She encourages questions and discussion from the class but it seems like my section was a bit on the quiet side. The workload isn't bad and I felt comfortable in class.

Took this class for an easy A. Graded on 2 papers, responses to a group member's paper, 2 discussions in class, 4 weekly quizzes, and a final test. Drop your lowest quiz grade + extra credit. Papers were easy and could be written in 20 minutes, 750 words. Lecture was not important.The quizzes were verbatim of the text book and readings.
Did not seem super helpful or engaging. It was more helpful if you asked him specific questions or to explain outside of the lectures. Not a bad professor, but also not the best.

Best Physics professor ever. Because of him, I actually learned how to apply physics concepts in real life.  Later made my P-Chem course easier and helped me to excel in med school & training. This course develops your problem-solving skills. This bothers many students who just want to memorize. Follow his directions--you will learn and score well.

He is not helpful whatsoever. There was an error in my iClicker points, and when I went to talk to him about it, he told me to email him the problem. I did that, but didn't see an update in my grade. He didn't reply back or change my grade despite the multiple emails that both me AND the TA sent him.

This class would be a breeze if you had prior physics experience in high school.  I never took a class of physics before this class (which I deeply regret), and his style of teaching just wasn't for me. I got the class average for most of the quizzes, but I think I did above average on the final.  GOOD LUCK!

He has 5 quizzes, keeps top 4. They're MC and are trickier versions of the pre-lectures examples. If you, like the others think this class is hard, you must be an idiot. If you understand the concepts, you WILL get an A. He is not out to get you. Did not open the book even once, since everything was from posted pre- lectures. Did take AP Physics B.

He's a very knowledgable professor and is passionate about the subject. His lectures are summaries of readings, so attendance isn't mandatory but he clearly cares so they're worth going to. Only issue is with the structure of the class. Only 2 topic proposals and 2 papers, graded by TA's. I wish there was more hw so the grade is more balanced.
Graded by a few things and the readings were very difficult to get through. Lecture was heavy and he is very monotone. Final paper and midterm were very interesting though.

He is the head of the anthropology/archeology department -- meaning he knows many things -- making it very good for when you have questions, there isn't a book you have to read but articles so depending on the date its either reading heavy. he is nice and well organized as well.

Don't really need to show up to class all he does is read from slides. The slide material is not all relevant, you just need to write two papers for this course. Graded by TA so professor is not as important. The essays can be written without the material he assigns you to read

He is the best professor that I think in UCSD. His power point is useful and the exams are the same as the study guide. The questions in the exams are very very very straightforward!!! If he teaches MMW again next year, you should take his class!!! Though his lectures are a little bit boring.
Took his cognitive psychology class at SWC. It was like watching a squirrel on too much caffeine give a lecture. He's a smart guy but his teaching style is all over the place.

Actually took him at SWC for COGS 17. Lecture heavy, which can be boring but he is able to make the concepts relatable. He is very honest when it comes to answering questions even if he doesn't know the answer. Exams are based on lectures only so take good notes but you have access to a notecard for exams.

COGS13 is heavily reliant on group work, and I only saw Prof Davis on the last week when we had to submit our proposals for research. I wish there was more guidance on how to write a proposal because though our group believed we fulfilled the criteria, we still received lots of negative feedback. The exams are very specific to course material.

Took Dr. Davis for SS1 in 2022 and had an excellent experience. Had passion for what he was teaching and made learning enjoyable with detailed and easy to follow slides. Was graded by 4 weekly tests, discussion posts pertaining to each lecture, and a final exam. All very straightforward and stress free! Felt like I learned a lot for summer course.

Very detailed and helpful lecture slides. Midterms and finals are mostly multiple choice questions, and everything on the tests is thoroughly explained in lectures. Super accessible and accommodating. Honestly one of the best cogs sci prof ive had

TOOK THIS PROF FOR POLI100X (wasn't an option for course code)

Very straightforward, easy lectures on Tues and coding lab on Thurs. Very easy to keep up, no need to read. Midterm is extra credit only and a HUGE grade boost. Lectures easy to podcast, but in person, the TA helps you with code in real time. Final was just like the homework.
Took both of Professor Ban's classes at UCSD. She was one of my favorites. Clear and concise, with assignments that make sense and are set up for you to succeed.

Prof Ban is a great poli sci instructor. She is doing direct research in the field on gender in congress and voting so it helps a lot that she is so knowledgeable. Great class, would take more with her.

I really love Professor Ban. She is super caring and sweet and clearly is passionate about Gender and Politics. The essays have clearly defined requirements so as long as you meet them you get an A+. The course information is super interesting and she presented it in a really easy to understand way. She is one of my favorite poli sci professors.

Pamela Ban is a great educator, she is clearly very intelligent and passionate about her field. Her lectures are fun and interactive and she really does want her students to learn & grasp the material. Overall a solid professor
Extremely passionate lecturer and cares a lot about giving a good intuition for the content. Easy exams and homework.

The professor is alright. His lectures are essentially solving the problems from the main text book so you can just go through the text book and not attend the lectures. He did trip up on questions once in a while, but can usually answer them.

This course is extremely time consuming, but I learned a lot. To do better than I did you should go to Prof. Paturi's office hours from the start of the semester. He is very willing to help there. Lots of material so don't get behind! I hadn't taken an in-depth algorithms course so I struggled a lot. Office hours and exam reviews saved me.

One of the few professors who actually care about the institution, apart from his students. Stay awake - he wont spoonfeed. Don't be shy, ask silly questions. Much of what you'll learn in this course is not useful if your next step is to find a job and are not really into theoretical CS. Do attend his lectures, and use your TAs well.
Can't really explain anything well. Has some weird ideas of attendance in class. Always seems to be a bad mood.

Do not take him for Math 18, and if you can, try to sign up for Leesa Anzaldo. He is not even a lead professor, and his lectures do not help you for the exams at all. I had to attend Anzaldo's lectures instead of his because his was just that bad. He DOES NOT lecture at all, instead goes over "problems" on the board. Students are expected to read.

Prof. Agrawal's teaching style isn't for everyone but I personally liked it. He starts class by going over the reading and you spend the rest doing rapid-fire practice problems. Note that he didn't administer the homework or exams - Anzaldo managed all of that, so you take the same tests as everyone else.
You basically teach yourself the material by reading the textbook and in lecture he goes over problems.

Sunny was a great professor. The class is somewhat difficult bc of the amount of hw and labs, but its doable. The exams were very representative of the materials learned in class. Sunny is very accessible outside of class.

BIMM 194, Grade is only based on one exam. He said that the class would be an easy A and we'd be out in 15 minutes and of course it would be according to him when hes been teaching the topic for who knows however long. Class was interesting though and he knows his stuff. Start studying two weeks before and you should be fine. Best lecturer at UCSD!

Overall a really interesting class and great professor! There's 8 quizzes given in discussion which are based on weekly readings and they weren't that easy. 2 midterms, both were pretty fair/easy. The final was a little harder than the midterm but overall ok. And a Carbon footprint project which was a little time consuming but not hard.

Take what I say with a grain of salt; I have a good memory. Mayfield is a great professor who completely understands his topics. He is entertaining to listen to and very knowledgeable without being arrogant. His tests are tough for some, but they were not on anything we didn't cover (well, maybe a few questions) Wish I could take him again

Very interesting and applicable topics, and Mayfield really knows his stuff. Quizzes in discussion are fairly easy, midterms/final are somewhat difficult-all multiple choice, but some questions are worded tricky or focus on small details. Easy Carbon Footprint project, just follow the guidelines. Very doable if you're interested in renewable energy
All multiple choices. It seems as an easy class, but definitely not! It's really difficult to study for midterm and final because he put many unimportant questions.

She is very nice and caring for her students. It seems like she wants ppl to do well and she makes sure ppl understand her lectures. She teaches difficult concepts in a way that's easy to digest. Though, she goes too slow in some sections and too fast in others, but as she becomes more familiar with certain course I'm sure her pacing will improve.

Bad attitude and very rude when giving feedback on your papers. Lectures are hard to sit through and he is very unorganized on how to do his assignments. He is not understanding or caring when it comes to his students either. Do not take him, wait for another professor so you enjoy the material.

If you can, take him. His lectures are very clear and he explains everything you need to know. His exams are lecture based, he won't test on something he hasn't taught, he even gives a list of fair game topics to study for the exam. He is not very easy to email, but he is open to answering questions after class. Great professor!!

Great OChem professor and fair with grading exams. Sometimes he won't post the answers to practice exams which sucks. Grades based on 3 exams, all free response. He doesn't use powerpoints and lectures are not recorded. He handwrites his notes and uploads pictures of the pages to Canvas later. Before exams he tells you what topics are fair game

From someone that had to take 40A twice and then 40B a second time, Professor Siegel is the best ochem professor out there. Going from a C+ in 40A to getting a 95% on his first miderm, I can say that he made ochem easy to understand and his exams are very fair. Def take him if he is teaching that quarter!!

He is one of the best professors i have had and i would highly recommend that you take him. His lectures always held my attention and he explained things very clearly. The midterms and final were easy and straight forward. My advice is pay attention to the problems he gives in class cause most of the time they usually show up in the tests.

Best Ochem professor! Extremely knowledgeable and very inspirational. Teaches slightly different from the textbook though. Grading for exam is extemely linient, points are given whenever possible. He is also in general very nice person, never make you feel stupid. Teaches once every 3 years, so take him if you can!
His lecture is not engaging at all and his exams are very challenging. Exams are worth 60% of your grade. I don't recommend taking COMM 100A with him.

I'm gonna comment anything.
But here's a snippet from his final exam announcement: 
The exam will consist of three sections short answers, a required essay, and regular essays.
You will also be asked to complete two regular essays. These essays are worth eight points each. We will give you four potential essay questions for this section of the exam

Christo has good breakdowns for the readings because they are so dense. He does so when he lectures and reads off slides but that means that on the midterm/final there isn't any testing on stuff he says in class that isn't already on the slides. Good lecturer and has a compelling way of teaching during lecture!
I ended up dropping this class after the exam. Exams are heavily weighted and no extra credit.
He reads off slides during lecture, and somehow expect his student to answer short answer and essay question on the exams...

Pretty chill and understanding, participate sometimes and talk to him and he will like you. Grade is made up of five argument maps on any of the articles for homework which we are supposed to read every night so lots of time to do them and thats pretty much the only homework other than a one page midterm and 5-6 page final.

This professor destroyed many people's dreams of continuing to graduate school. If you want to go to grad school, avoid him. Many of my classmates have taken his class, and this class has become a nightmare for everyone

The scary thing about this class is that you're not just going to get a low grade in this class; you won't have time for other classes. Indirectly leading to low grades in other courses. Some professors at UCSD are too mean, if you want to keep your gpa don't take his classes

The hardest economics course at UCSD; the professor did not follow the college's required B- average; he often gave it C+. The course itself is difficult, has a lot of content, and takes up a lot of time. You won't have time to study other courses. This is the real killer

I have to say that this class takes 1.5-2 times as long as other economics courses; the professor has set too much content. At the same time, professors are inconsiderate of students. If you focus on GPA, don't take his class.

Professor Shishkin is a good lecturer and has good energy when presenting his lectures, the main problem is just that the course itself is incredibly difficult, and the class structure doesn't help alleviate that. The average grade in the class before any sort of curve was a D+ which speaks to how hard it was.

If you are not a skilled writer you should not take this professor. She does not teach class material more or less you have to figure it out and go with the flow. During 1 on 1 conferences if your writing is not up to her "standards" even if you tried your best to listen to her previous advice she would make you feel like your writing was trash.
Julie Moon is a horrible professor

Class is contract graded, so very reflective of the work you put in. Professor Moon is a great professor and I will take her again for 10B. Class does rely on participation, so expect to be called on or to participate.

Professor Moon is very accommodating and caring. My only complaint is that she didn't explain essay prompts thoroughly enough and only discussed them for 5 minutes at the end of class. There is a grading contract, meaning if you complete everything in its entirety, you will receive an A. This is what saved me for this class.

Professor Moon is such a sweet woman. She cares about her students so much. Her class was a bit boring, but we had a quiet class, so it wasn't her fault for that. We do a grading contract, so you choose your grade. Make sure to adhere to that grade's requirements, or else you will drop a grade. She has great feedback for your writing! Love her!
Very easy lectures but the homework is wayy more difficult. Midterms are pretty well reflected by the homework but the final was brutal.

He some how makes the materials seem easy and you thought you got everything after the lecture, but the homeworks feel challenging. Later the tests are just impossible. No partial credit and you have to choose from 50 answers.
Tests don't represent material at all and lectures are spent discussing proofs rather than helping students understand concepts through examples.

v smart person, not a good teacher. Midterms were challenging bc it was a coordinated course (he was not the one writing them). average was a failing grade on midterm 1. math has always been my fav class, i disliked his class; lots of proofs and not enough examples to help us. not accessible at all. Lecture added 0 value (no joke/exaggeration).

Horrible lecturer. He is obviously passionate about math but needs to focus more on what the students need. I literally took calculus in high school got an A and was learning the same material but the tests were so hard for no reason. The average for our first one was a 4/9. If you can't get a different prof just wait until next quarter.

I loved attending her class. She always tried to do experiments in class related to topics we learning, and in most lectures, we had one. She did many practice problems in class and took criticism seriously to improve her class. Her tests were difficult, but if you understood concepts then you can understand how to do the problems.
I really enjoyed her class, she really makes you feel like she cared about you and your education. I am trying to take her again for 1C next year.

There are 4 quizzes worth 40%, and the final is also worth 40% with homework at 20%. The quizzes were a little tough as well as the final, but still very representative of lecture and homework content. Do the homework, it's super helpful for preparing for the quizzes, and study for the exams well enough beforehand.

Prof. Koslover had high expectations but she really would put in the time to help you understand material if you put in the time too. She answers questions in depth on piazza and office hours. Her practice quizzes and finals were very helpful too

Koslover is extremely kind, and a very good professor IF you have taken a physics course prior to taking a course of hers (in the case of 1A at least). She has plenty of resources and works to make sure you understand the material if you approach her outside of class. However, her teaching style does not mesh well with first time learners.

All of the reviews for him that are low, is just because PHIL170 is a hard subject, not anything the prof did wrong. I think he was a perfectly good prof, he was nice, always answered your questions, and helped you figure out the solution. And he drops quiz and HW grades. So don't choose to not take PHIL170 because of the professor.

Worst professor I have ever had in my life. He cannot teach at all. His lectures were extremely confusing, and he held them all asynchronously, allowing live sessions once every 2 weeks, and even then that did not help much. 3 midterms and a final. Hard material if you are not even close to being mathematically inclined. Avoid absolutely.

His lectures are not the best and he doesn't prepare you well for exams. Unless you are willing to study and go to TA office hours I would not take this class. Logic is not as fun as I imagined either.

I don't like to make negative reviews, but this might help someone. His lectures are very hard to understand, and while the material can be difficult, there are much easier ways to explain the concepts than is provided. You can't really figure out the concepts just by reading, coming to class, and asking questions.

The online textbook is basically your only source of learning the material. The professor has non-mandatory lectures, but its basically 50 minutes of him posting power point slides straight from the book. Your grade truly depends on the 4 "midterms" and the final. If you have a good T.A. the material will be much easier to grasp.

Took Molecular Epidemiology with him, and he made the topic extremely interesting. The lectures are engaging and based on literature readings done as homework. Attendance is mandatory but can be made up with a writing assignment. He is passionate about what he teaches. 25% of the grade is a final 10 minute presentation on a paper of your choice.

The professor mainly teaches by writing on the board, but the board is really unreadable. Another key is that the teacher doesn't really care about the fact that most people can't actually understand his lectures. Always talks by himself while only a few people in the class are paying attention - the professor never interacts with the students.

Lectures were tough to get through as his handwriting is tough to read and its hard to follow along with his monotone voice. I was lucky that I took 10B a year before and it made this class a breeze. Stopped going to lecture about three weeks in and basically got through the class using webassign and practice tests
He is so nice and even give us ec for filling out CAPEs. The tests are reasonable in difficulty and time limit. Once you study, you will get a good grade.
One of the worst lecturers I've ever had. Difficult to understand. Really messy handwriting. Jumbled notes that seemed really out of order. DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH HIM.

He was a terrible professor in the 'rate my professor' before the summer2021. Our class teacher should be Yucheng at the first so we choose this class, but Fulek replaced his place before the one day of the course start. A lot of people dropped this class after they saw Fulek, lol. But it's hard to believe he grades so fair and really thoughtful.
Unable to contact the teacher after class, strange, irresponsible, not rigorous.
Very easygoing and caring guy. Definitely would recommend taking a class with him if you get the chance
I love Prof. Roth, he was super caring and helpful even though I was enrolled in the class late. He does not give much work, lecture is once a week, and he gives simple test and one paper.
Instant favorite, coolest guy out of class too. Assignments were so easy even if you can't stand hip-hop. He makes it more about enjoying the long lectures!
Really engaging lecturer even after 3 hour lectures. Very good communicator and makes it very easy to get a good grade in the class.
Very understanding! You can tell he is very passionate about what he teaches! This class was very enjoyable and my favorite part is the guest lectures and guest he invites which involve live music:)
He is a very organized professor! And he gives so useful suggestions!
Talks too much!!!

You can tell they care about the subject and the students. Very understanding and receptive, wants you to learn. Uses pre-made course slides which they draw on during lecture, 2 midterms and no final exam, final project is writing a paper based on the concepts we learned. Flow of information in lecture is somewhat disorganized
She goes to the classroom to read slides and nothing else. The worst professor I've ever had during my time at UCSD. Avoid her if you can.

Homework was easy and graded lightly but tests were shockingly difficult considering the questions asked on other assignments. Lectures were boring and did not contain any information that was not already on the slides posted on canvas. Tests did not reflect content covered in class and despite being a statistics person, I did not enjoy this class.

This class shouldn't have been as hard as it is; from attending her lectures, she clearly cares more about the stock market than statistics. Her homework questions were easy, but we have to randomly prove complex theorems in the exams. Her lecture notes are actually great, but she skims through every topic without elaborating on why it's important.

Professor Hu is a very sweet person when it comes to questions outside of class, but beware that her office hours was not flexible. Her slides are very great and detailed. In lectures, however, she only reads off the slides. She doesn't help with understanding the concepts so only take her if you have no other choice.
The professor just reads off the screen and expects to understand more than what she teaches. She seems very stingy for grades and do not care about her students! Do not take!

Professor Mishanina is one of those professors who clearly cares about her students. Her class was engaging and she was VERY kind. Class is heavily graded on homework which was due every week. Always answered questions I had.

Professor Mishanina really cares about her students and makes lectures enjoyable to attend. She makes great efforts to make sure all her students have their questions answered during lectures and office hours. If you did your work and studied for exams (which are curved), you will do great in her class!

Mishanina is a wonderful professor that made a difficult class enjoyable for anyone that attended lecture regularly. She is personable, breaks mechanisms down so they're digestible, holds 2 office hours a week, and provides practice exams that mirror her actual exams, which are curved. 

Shame on whoever gave Prof Mishanina a one star review!

Professor Mishanina is a really good professor. She is very caring and very accessible outside of class. She always responded to my emails and was very helpful. The class is a lot of work, but it is 6 units after all. I really recommend Professor Mishanina!

I really enjoyed this class. Her tests were very fair, often derived from practice exams or problems sets. Need to know detailed mechanisms but goes over in lecture. Graded on few things - problem sets and tests. Found lectures very understandable

She makes a seminar class extra hard for no reason. Yes, the class was helpful and was not a total waste of time but she assign busy work and is really stingy when it comes to late work. She could make the class a lot more relaxed and people would enjoy it more but she makes it hard. Not too much work so its okay and gives extra credit
Professor Hoon's teaching style in the BICD 83 class was condescending and unhelpful. Their superior attitude hindered student engagement and learning. Disappointing experience overall.
