Professor Hoon has connections and helped me connect with others through networking events. I thought she was good, but the criticism here is justifiable. I thought she did not give good feedback despite the low number of students. Other than that, she was a good and I enjoyed her class.

I dropped the class because she expected a lot out of her students given the quality of herself and the class. I think she was nice as an instructor and does get back to emails although it does take her a while. The only issue I had with her was she was very condescending. Other than that, she was subpar.

This is a 1 unit class for an elective and the professor expects you to find have interviews with a company and go to random networking events while reading an elevator pitch specifically catered towards her class. Do not take this professor even if it's just an elective course. She is awful.

Savvas did a good job teaching Calc 1. There were some concepts he didn't break down enough but most he did well. Homework was tedious but designed to be harder than the tests. The homeworks make for a great study guide and practice for the midterms and finals.

Professor Savvas started out the semester great. He stated the material would be hard, but that there was no reason to worry about our grade... He was wrong. As the semester went on, the material seemed impossible to grasp, and the test averages plummeted accordingly. For the take-home final exam, it was so difficult (nothing from lecture). Beware!

If you can take this professor, dont pass up. Very organized, funny, and explains things so well. Exams are tough and his grading rubric is strict. Youll learn a lot. PS - Hes also super attractive, which helped me focus more

Dr. Savvas is extremely organized (and takes really great notes). Lectures are easy to follow as he doesn't teach too fast. Homeworks can get long sometimes, but in my opinion they were usually harder than the tests themselves. The tests followed a very specific grading format, so make to follow the methods he teaches in class. I highly recommend!

One of the many noteworthy attributes of Dr. Savvas is his genuine passion for math. He knows so many ins and outs of this subject that he makes learning calculus a breeze. One thing I will say is his tests are graded on a very strict rubric. Be sure and study the exact method to arriving at an answer or you will not receive full credit.
Withdrew because he was unnecessarily unfair.

Attendance not mandatory but pop quizzes will keep you coming to class. Lectures are just slideshow readings and quizzes / tests are designed so it is quite difficult to succeed. Strongly advise against taking this professor because you will likely take a hit to your gpa :l

i recommend against taking this. I've felt that the midterms and quizzes have been such a source of stress that it impedes learning. the tests are designed to constantly trip you up and the lectures simultaneously overexplain and underexplain what he wants from you. He is a cool professor but I just really do not think this class is designed well.

So one thing about him is that his lectures aren't interesting, he really just rambles on and on. I can tell he cares but his tests are just not it. Like they don't really go with the content we go over in class. He does random pop quizzes which are annoying. I really wouldn't recommend this class.
this guy is the absolute worst. unfair and brutal. his class is just so much harder than it needs to be.
Good course, very interesting seminar and he did read all of our discussion questions and well prepared.

Grade is dependent on exams that are designed to trip you up. I felt confident in the midterm only to get several questions wrong because of vague wording. Pop quizzes are easy so long as you're consistently studying. Your grade isn't calculated on canvas, so you won't know what you get till the end. Doesn't post slides until end of the week.
AWFUL AWFUL AWFUL PROFESSOR! NEVER TAKE HIS CLASS. HE IS AN UNREASONABLE GRADER AND A TRASH PROFESSOR.
Do not take this guy. please. He's a respected researcher but is a trash teacher. Research better teaching methods man.

structured a simple, lower div cogs class in the worst way and made it extremely difficult to get a good grade. this class is far more complex than it has to be and your grade is not an accurate measure of your learning.

You get to sign up for your grade in the class, and as long as you meet the requirements, you will get it. His assignments actually have meaning behind them and are intended to help you grow as a writer. Very chill professor and overall an amazing person!

Very respectful and understanding to his students. Contract-based grading makes you not worry about specific marks on papers but makes it difficult to improve in writing. Limited feedback, lots of creative freedom with assignments. Overall very nice and a good teacher.

Professor Lince is one of the most caring professors I have met at this school. He lets you take control over your own grade and you have the power to make or break your grade based off the contract you write for yourself. Definitely recommend taking him if you get the opportunity!

Professor Lince did a great job of making me enjoy writing. This course is very manageable as it follows a labor-based grading system. Class lectures and discussions are very engaging. You get to sign up for the grade you want in the course and can receive that grade by following the requirements in the grading contract. Would recommend!
Professor Lince made everything clear from the start, attempting to keep lectures engaging for an otherwise grueling course material.

Both Jin and Rogalski sucked at teaching 20B this quarter. Average grades were failing for the first midterm, and barely a C for the 2nd one. My final got lost, but was found so I have to wait until week 1 of spring quarter for it to be graded. Examples were ok, but Jin always went over the time limit, which was a bit annoying.
Dr. Jin is a nice prof who cares for his students. MATH 20B is known to be hard but, he taught the material well and his midterms were straightforward. His HW was hard and tedious though.

The material was difficult, and I often left lectures more confused. I suggest attending SI sessions as they were very helpful in reinforcing my understanding. Exams were very straightforward and easy compared to the homework sets, which were sometimes very tedious and challenging.
He is very difficult to understand, there is no consideration for questions. Honestly please take calc with anyone else because I learned nothing despite putting the hours in!

Can be hard to follow during lectures and difficult to understand. Really study for midterm and final as that's the majority of the grade. Take another professor if possible if math is already a struggle for you.
Dr. Greene is a very sweet professor. She is passionate about the subject and cognitive developmental neuroscience is so unique and complex. 10/10

Dr. Greene was so sweet & caring. Very accessible to reach outside of class. Her lectures are optional but you need to attend 4 discussion sections. Graded on weekly quizzes, writing reading questions, discussion attendance, & 3 midterms. She is very straightforward and always asks if we have questions. By far the best Professor at UCSD.

I loved this professor, she is easy to listen to and engage with. Grading is fair and assignments are spread out, easy to ask for help. You can tell she enjoys teaching as much as research and wants us to succeed.

If you are not a Phil major, don't take his PHIL classes. He will make you do 3 reflections every week, make you show up and bug you every time that you didn't. I don't doubt his knowledge but he is annoying, he would message you, to the extent where you would want to drop his class every single day. So please run if you don't like philosophy

Took him after dropping out of J. Carr's terrible 120 (do NOT recc), did SO much better. His lecture is clear and concise. If you don't understand something, he will talk you through it until you do. 1 midterm and 1 final, lots of homework during the week. Go to office hours if you're having trouble. Expected a C- and got an A-!

Professor Rickless clearly is passionate about the subject and covers all relevant materials in lecture. Reading was super important and weekly quizzes could show up any day. Super interesting class but on the more difficult side. Attendance is mandatory, but Professor was understanding. Really interesting class led by a knowledgable guy.

He can come off as rude at times when asking a question, but he is a solid professor that will throw in some dorky jokes that keep you entertained. He is devoted to helping to make his students pass and to do well. He does not curve but he will ensure his students understand the material well.

Professor Rickless is a passionate teacher. He requires you read a lot, but as long as you stay on top of it you'll be prepared for the lectures and assignments. His lectures are some of the best I've had at UC San Diego, heck, he's the first professor I've wanted to review. I'm glad I got to take a class with him, and you should too if you can.

Extremely overwhelming, disorganized course. The amount of content in this class is so huge that the professor tells students to not bother studying the whole course. The professor doesn't really teach any concept, just reads an incredibly big amount of slides. Do not recommend it!
his wording makes very little sense on the slides and also the final is worth 47% of the grade which is the reason i failed

Worst professor I've ever had. Avoid at all costs, even if you have to wait a quarter. He does not care about you! Posts homework late, 50% final, and very hard WEEKLY quizzes on SATURDAY. I am dreading my grade, no curve is worth this absolute torture for a 3 unit class I am being forced to take. Not a word on the final average!!! Terrible!!!

2 homework assignment and 1 quiz weekly, multiple choice are tricky, really hoping he's not doing this for the final. Lecture style is confusing and nothing he said in lecture is on the hw or quiz. If you have no choice to take this class with him I even suggest just sneak in to another prof's section, which I did :)

If I could give a 0 I would. Homework is overly difficult and does not help reinforce or teach anything. Weekly quizzes are near impossible to do well on and to top it off he is a horrible lecturer. His slides are terrible and are just blocks of text made difficult to read. Every week is miserable in his class.
Very funny and very great teacher.  She loves what she's doing and she tries to be helpful in class.
Great prof and very funny in class. Easy grader, but the work load can be overwhelming at times. However, overall definitely recommend her!
Superb teacher. She makes everything easy by giving examples. The end of the quarter project is a pain but she's an easy grader at everything so use this class to boost your GPA!

Fujiwara sensei is a great professor. She's really energetic and has a cute personality. Her class is fun, but I wouldn't say it was the easiest. Japanese in general is alot of work and it's a bit hard, but Fujiwara sensei really tries to make the class material fun for us to learn.

Dr. Shelby is a great person, she is not my favorite professor. I've taken her a few times I really enjoy what she stands for and her inspiring lectures, however, the expectations for her students is unmanageable. She has assigned over 100 pages of reading before with not enough time, class time is always crammed content and is always behind sched.

Live lecture once a week and live discussion. Reading is required, but fascinating and moves quickly. Class is very discussion-driven and Dr. Shelby will discuss with the class what we want to talk about! Highly recommend.

Lecture consist of her telling personal anecdotes that relate to the readings, but never acknowledge her white privilege. Doesn't facilitate the best discussions and often interrupts students. Tries really hard but often perpetuates gender binary (ex. only says women when talking about pregnancy; transmen & nonbinary also give birth). Not critical

Dr. Shelby is incredibly kind and articulate. Visit her in office hours because her one-on-one breakdowns are terrific. There is a lot of reading, and you will fail if you don't read and make a serious effort to comprehend. Lecture is long and dense, come well-rested.
She is passionate about her work and her students, very approachable and excited about learning. Assignments were straight forward. I would sign up for another class with her in a heart beat.

very unorganized. canceled class numerous times. only had 4 quizzes and one paper that determined our grade. One week she just decided that she "didn't want to do the quiz". The amount of content is insane and the quiz questions are very specific. She got angry that students stopped attending but refused to learn to use hotseat, iclickers, etc

Honestly, if you do her study guides and memorize them, you are guaranteed an A in the class. She also has random 'pop quizzes' that are super easy and are free points. I hated section because it was so pointless to me. Though it is lots of info, it's easy if you organize your notes. I studied for her tests the day before and always got high A's.
She's so smart and so excited about Anthropology. She is super accessible and easy going. Super funny.  Do your readings and attend class and you should be fine.
Not ralated to slides. Instruction was unclear. Seldom explain some strange abbreviation. Difficult on Homework.
COMPLETE CHAOS

The whole course is poorly organized. He's trying to cover too many things within two months and end up losing his focus on what are the useful parts. The first half is okay, except for his nothing-got-explained and no-sample-data assignments and exam. But the second half is horrendous, he's assuming students to have experiences for those topics.
he made the midterm and homework very hard and not even give a curve

Professor Gupta is a very good person.He always answer questions: he always takes times after the class for answering question to the student. His grading is really open minded : he is ok to adapt the grade if they were a mistake or a misunderstood. I recommended this teacher.
Great Professor. Really enjoyed her lecture and group project she has you do. It's really fun if you actually get into it.

There is a lot of work in the class but it is all manageable. The final is a paper that you have a month to complete. There is a group project in class but most of those points come from participation. Lectures are engaging and she is very knowledgeable. She gives out up to 9% extra credit! Stay on top of assignments and you will do well
One of the best at UCSD
Prof Schneider is absolutely brilliant, her classes were amazing and I loved going, it wasn't a chore to drag myself there. Don't forget your clicker!!!

Dr. Schneirder was an extraordinary professor. She made me want to go to class. The lectures were relevant and interesting. Midterm and final were easy and straightforward, directly taken from the powerpoint slides and texts. I would highly recommend her. I definitely want to take her again. She's truly inspiring.
Wrong solutions for one of the midterm practices.

The man wastes more time fixing small errors on iPad instead of re-writing. Disorganized, sloppy, and unprepared. He finished grading all HW after final then gives us 2hr window to "request regrade." Never responds to emails - LITERALLY. Lacks communication (gen.) with students. Just read the book and you will learn more. DO NOT TAKE him, please.

His class is the worst experience I have ever had. He has a huge load of homework, each would take more than 10 hours. So, don't take his class!

I think he is awful at teaching. Prof Kitsela is extremely disorganized especially in the remote environment. The man makes a simple task seem complicated. Unresponsive to emails although he says "email me once more" yet he continues to not respond. Lots of homework, heavy test. A rewarding class for sure! All the work throughout 10 weeks builds up and becomes a final paper in the end (you have things that have been written for the entire 10 weeks ready to be used). You will be asked to read papers but all of those are super helpful knowledge and are beneficial to further your understanding of childhood development!

I did not enroll this class for the curriculum but came out of it with a sprinkle of appreciation. Very accommodating and did not seem passive-aggressive to me?
I loved her.

I hate to be mean to her. I do not want to hurt her feelings, but I have to say this. She gives out vague instructions and tons of homework. She gives instructions one day before it is due. Two long papers and a book project due on finals week. The writing is overall heavier than my college writing course. Her lecture is so boring and not helpful.

As I student I've learned that the hallmarks of a terrible professor are: boring, gives too much homework, and is a hard grader. Unfortunately for Wishard Guerra, she's all three in spades. Avoid this drab, unreasonable, and unfair professor.

ECL305
- heavily based on weekly discussion posts-->based on readings and discussion
Come to class and make an effort to participate, Professor Pressman WILL notice, your grades will reflect that. You can miss a few classes/hw
- two two-page short "essays" with feedback and time to revise for better grades
- final essay, no revision

This class was great! She is very knowledgeable. The class isn't like your average English class. It's very interesting and engaging. She allows you to be creative with what you write about and teaches you how to critically think about the World. I would recommend her!

I'll articulate myself with concise words so you may understand. Pressman changed my life. I think differently and observed things differently. I see through unwholesome and erroneous ideas because I wield a special power of analysis and critical thought; wielded in and outside of school. The changed cognition is very helpful with other class too.

Her class was one of the best experiences of my college career. Pressman challenges you to think critically and is 100% invested in your education. Take this class if you want your horizons widened. She's is not interested in "playing school," she's interested in changing the world. And you can be part of that. The question is, will you?
Great professor. Interesting and easy class with interesting essays to write. Enjoyed it. She's from Yale too!

Brian Cross was very insightful and had some really interesting films that I would have otherwise would never watch. He is also very chill and just overall pretty easy to talk to, and is pretty much very understanding if there is any problems with assignments and stuff like that

I've had Brian for two quarters now and I genuinely love his class. He is an inspiring artist and truly cares about what he teaches. He is super laid back and only asks that you try your best and show up. He is understanding and actually cares about his students beyond the classroom.Having him as a professor reminded me why I want to be an artist.

Cares about his students and is really funny. Gives good feedback and conducts crit in a way that leaves none feeling awful about themselves. Classes are 3 hours, but his jokes and humor make time pass fast.

His lecture is inspirational, and he always wants us to think very deeply as a filmmaker by displaying certain documentary during the class. However, in terms of his assignments, I am sick of that. His topic description is usually very unclear, and his critique is very self-centered.

I didn't understand his lectures. The gist was social justice issues. He grades tough yet doesn't even do the grading. The readings are difficult & don't help.

I loved Professor Rifkin's lecture and found myself really fascinated with the subject matter, though admittedly they have very little to do with how you're graded. Took this for a DEI and it was a pretty easy A. No exams, all you're graded on is annotated reading and one final research paper. The readings can get a bit long and boring but they're not hard to keep up with. Assignments are all basically graded by completion. You don't even really have to go to lectures to get an A in this class.

Prof. Rifkin does a good job for this course. I would have preferred not to have to take a DEI course, but, since it's mandated I chose BILD 60. This class has ALOT of reading that you have to do and annotate on perusal. There is also an essay due at the end, but as long as you stay caught up you should be fine. He is also very accomodating.

So many readings that are poorly spaced, redundant, and largely irrelevant to the course. He tries so hard to make a lower division biology class into some pseudointellectual philosophy class. Prof. Rifkin brings me lots of inspiration in coding structure. He has amazingly strong logic and good at solving problems via innovative way. This Professor is super nice and understanding. Her class is interesting and definitely worth taking! I feel that grading is fair and she is flexible about tech issues. One of my favorite classes this quarter!

DO NOT TAKE!  She knows her info but she threatens her students by taking away points if you ask for a regrade or to revise a question you think you got correct.  She should not be anywhere students or the teaching field.  You are teaching the next generation of doctors, researchers, etc!  Professor Su, if you read this, reevaluate your methods

Prof. Su is a great lecturer that's totally capable of delivering the materials in an organized manner. Her exams are super fair and similar to the problem sets. Very passionate about teaching & love to help her students.

Great professor! Her exams are very clear and focus on understanding of the concepts rather than memorization. Lectures are interesting and easy to understand. She's always passionate in lectures and explains the concepts very well with very organized slides. I really enjoyed her class and highly recommend it to anyone interested in neurobiology!
Hard to understand lectures due to recording quality. Tests are very challenging. Study lectures and know specifics. Good teacher. Teaches in detail.

Great class and teacher. Lectures are information heavy and reading the textbook is a must. Exams are hard but offer good feedback and will offer points back if you were moving in the right direction. The class isn't easy but you learn a lot. I recommend it for sure.

I had professor Mai for CSE193 which was a research class for the ERSP research program. I learned so much from her about how to find good research paper resources, how to find papers cited by others to find similar research, and how to write research papers etc. It was so helpful I was able to get my own paper accepted for publication!

Best Professor I have had at UCSD! Her class was a repeat of one I dropped bc of 34% on midterm. When taken with Professor Elsherif, I just missed an A by LESS THAN TWO PERCENTAGE POINTS for my final grade! Especially If you are brand new to computer science, definitely take her! She will certainly help you, she REALLY cares, and she is excellent!!

I really enjoyed this class! The professor did an excellent job at teaching students how to program Python for the first time. This class is not test-heavy, which I like because the professor cares about students practicing their coding skills more than excelling on an exam. She was always very encouraging when exam seasons came. Highly recommend!

She assigns a lot of homework and course load is pretty rigorous. There are 4 assignments each week and lectures were mandatory. The course itself is not that difficult but the some problems in the assignments and tests are much more complex and difficult than the ones she goes over in lectures. Also does not respond to student emails.

Not a terrible professor, just mandates a lot of unnecessary high school rules. TAs are nice.

Avoid if not CSE major. Extremely hard class w/ tons of time commitment for HW.

Textbooks are REQUIRED but a lot of HW topics are still never discussed or shown.

If you want to survive with no previous CSE experience you HAVE TO go to office hours.

I would be nowhere without Ivana! She is the most kind professor you will meet at Mankato State. Some assignments can be lengthy and require deep work but only because she cares about the understanding her students get from her classes. Her classes can push you but I promise you will feel good leaving her class. She is the absolute best!

Professor Guarrasi is so sweet, she listens to students feedback and adjusts the class schedule to fit. She is very knowledgeable and finds really good concepts and examples to work through in lecture

Took her for biographies and life stories. She was a good teacher and always clear. Not entirely sure how she may be in an accelerated summer environment but during the quarter there's not much to stress about. She is very kind and will do her best to make sure everyone is on top of things and interested.

She is the worst professor at UCSD I've had so far, I already told all my friends to avoid taking her classes. She has load of works to do, it's insane!!! All my classmate and I were completely stressed out, but she did not care at all. 2 quiz 1 midterm 3 Assignment 1 final in 4 weeks. side notes: she is a hard grader!
She is magical
From the daily check-ins to working with students tirelessly on their writing to just being fricking hilarious, Suzy is the best professor UCSD has to offer, hands-down.

The best day of my college career was the day I was assigned a class with Professor Woltmann. The worst day of my college career was the day our class ended. Funny, caring, an awesome teacher... it doesn't get much better!

Suzy is an incredible teacher and person. My first year of college was overall rough, but her class and her personality helped me survive. As a teacher she's so knowledgable and helpful, and as a person she's caring, really listens, and even brings in treats and her dog sometimes!
Suzy is hands down the best writing teacher in the world.

Shes very paassionate about her material but is oftentimes rude and patronizing. Its hard to approach her or ask a question in class because she makes you feel dumb. She is also hard to understand and goes through material quickly; shes always in a rush and relies on many readings. Lectures are online but feel so long and are not engaging at all.

From her lectures u could understand that she is passionate about the subject but she is very aggressive towards the questions asked in her class she constantly encourages you to speak in class and literally checks u off but is very disrespectful when a question is asked her assignments are ok TA was a tough grader don't recommend I would avoid her
Very condescending.

Professor Paglayan definitely loves her job, she puts a lot of energy into each lecture. Personally I didnt find the subject interesting in general, I thought it was a lot of going through data and not much analyzing it, the paper was ok. She offers extra credit. she expects a lot of participation and being interactive during the ENTIR course.

PHENOMENAL professor. Her course on educational inequality went beyond your typical lectures. HIGHLY recommend!
Favorite professor and smartest at the department

Amazing professor! This class was really hard for me but Professor Roberts made it exponentially easier with her explanations. One class a week was mandatory. Assignments were easy if you kept up with class.

Professor Roberts was amazing throughout the 2021 Spring Quarter. She was super responsive. She created a discord & interacted with all the students throughout a difficult remote environment. The assignments were tough but solvable, and she is very organized. She is extremely smart and knowledgeable, and she is very accommodating! I recommend 100%
Prof. Li is great!!! I learned a lot and it helped me tremendously in my med school application.

I had the great privilege to have spent three years as an undergraduate researcher in Dr. Willis Li's lab. I believe Dr. Li prepared me very well for medical school, exposing me to a field of biology that is playing a progressively more more important role in medicine. He ran a very well-organized and efficient lab, with helpful postdoc/students.
Great professor

I can deal with all the ins and outs of an extremely unorganized class, but it is difficult to tolerate the mood swings of this prof. With him U never know if U are coming or going. He needs a good counselor.

I strongly recommend you do not take this class! It is based on reading quizzes, Packback discussion posts, and a final essay. The quizzes were based on the readings and the discussion posts had to be extensive and accompanied with two responses every other week. The final essay was had the most confusing prompt I have ever seen! DO NOT DO IT!

There were so many readings and "easy" quizzes every two weeks plus Packback (an AI graded discussion software). The final exam was ridiculous, the prompt was confusing and when you reached out for help his answers were confusing and really unhelpful. I can't say if he is good in person, but avoid if the class is online!

Took this class during fall 2020 and wasn't as bad as these recent ratings make it out. Most of the grade was based on reading quizzes and Perusall both easily doable if you did the readings, I skimmed and got full points. The essay prompt was confusing. Grade scale was in the syllabus and canvas did say current grades weren't weighted correctly.

I would find another professor to take. 60% of your grade is based on discussions and reading quizzes which I both found easy. The final was a take home essay with a very long and confusing prompt. I got a 60/100 on the essay and the mean was a 37/100.

There were mixed feelings about Rusiru's teaching. It was a little tough to understand at times because of his accent, but he definitely cares about the students and would always stop to answer any questions. Also gave a generous curve. I always went to his office hours and he would explain every concept very thoroughly, so be sure to reach out!
I love Rusiru. He is so funny and charismatic. I hated the class, but loved Rusiru.

This professor is very new to teaching but he did a very good job at teaching and supporting his students in precalculus. When covering a topic, he goes through everything in detail just to clarify the topic and possibly fill in any knowledge gaps that you have. He is patient and accessible outside of class -- replies to any emails very promptly.
You will learn Latin as well as how to be a grown up. Wirshbo taught me lessons my father couldn't and it all boils down to accountability and taking responsibility for your own learning. Thank you!

If you don't read the material then you won't pass the random pop quizzes but if you take great notes and study them during lecture you'll do great on the midterm and final. Those two tests were very reliant on what was said during lecture. There are 2 papers that you should start early, he doesn't care for fancy language. Not for someone sensitive

Acerbic and abrasive. In a very 1960s style of teaching, this professor calls on people to translate for the class rather than taking volunteers. Not for faint of heart, difficult and particular, do not slack off, he will know and grade you accordingly, wants you to be the best at Latin you can be, don't be scared, just work hard and don't take his humor to seriously. Marcelo is such a silly and amusing guy! He has a deep-rooted passion for statistics and code, including R. He loves R and he is simply trying to share his passion in earnest.

Highly recommend!!!!!

This class is made more complicated than it needs to be. I have taken two other courses that touch on immunology briefly with better explanations than anything Dr. Lu could ever come up with. The class itself is very difficult, they say one of the hardest in bio. However, Dr Lu makes it very interactive and fun. He's very passionate about the subject. idk why the reviews for him are so terrible, but i think prof Lu is very passionate in what he does and is also very understanding in terms of helping us understand the materials and finding ways for us to get points back. his exams are pretty challenging imo, but 30% of the exam is already free points. u learn a whole lot from this class!

Unfortunately, I took this course before researching the professor. Please do not make the mistake as me. Steer CLEAR of Dr. Lu. Top 2 worst professors I've had @ UCSD. He's not understanding at ALL, esp during this pandemic. Lectures are crazy confusing as he's grammatically incorrect and just says random words.

This class was a mess. Great instructor, simplified an otherwise quite complex field (especially some of the topics covered in 1C). Prof. Schneider works hard to make his lectures engaging. Lectures are also recorded. No need to buy textbook. Prepare to write a few paragraphs each week in discussion posts & write-ups. Berk always found time to take and answer questions during his lectures. He was always looking for student feedback and consulted the class many times throughout the quarter regarding how they felt about the content. He really showed that he cared and wanted everyone to succeed.

Dr. Drakes is an amazing and super caring professor! Taken over SS2, so four reading quizzes followed by four short papers about the lecture material each week. Four assignments that rely more on your creativity and knowledge rather than application based questions. All assignments and exams are open-note and open-textbook. Feedback on all exams!

The most wonderful professor! Even though most students said that he is a little bit rude, I believe that if you have enough patience to talk with him, he will like you so much. pretty easy class if you show up, lectures are boring just because she talks too slow

The professor was super kind and caring! Took her propaganda and persuasion class during summer and she was super kind and caring to all her students! Would 100% take her class again, she is very passionate about what she teaches, and you can learn a lot in her courses.

If you can put off this class a quarter or summer for another professor such as Catalina please do it. Currently, taking her over the summer and her exams have been incredibly nit-picky. She tends to focus on a topic not even on a slide or that she covers in passing.

Such a thorough and caring professor! Very clear w the material, she makes podcasts of lectures and has optional live class attendance. I absolutely loved this professor. I took her for Bild2, Bipn100 and now Bipn102. Best bio teacher I have taken. Highly recommend.
I thought she was awesome! Exams bit difficult but fair. She cared deeply about my situation and helped me do well in this course-so yeah. I will take her again.

If you had the choice to pick a different professor I would. She is incredibly undeserving to be at this institution. She does not care about her students and does not value their learning. Honestly a terrible class. Get ready for 150+ pages of reading a week, lots of papers, and mandatory clicker questions. It is a 3 hour lecture that is incredibly boring, slides each have paragraphs of texts on them, and I had to learn everything myself. Don't make the mistake I made by taking it.

Worst lecturer and class I have ever taken. Horribly boring, every slide is full of text and none of it makes any sense. This class was a 3 hour lecture on a Monday night but professor Bergman made it interesting and fun. He is funny and knowledgeable about everything he teaches. There is a ton of reading to do per week but the readings are helpful and guaranteed A if you do them.

Professor cares about his students and makes sure that we are ready for exams by explaining the concepts. Exams were doable if you did all the homework and understand the main concepts. I really enjoyed this class and this professor. The tests were fair but lecture heavy so if you keep up with lectures you will be fine. His lectures were interesting, and packed with information. He was very lenient with grades and was overall a very friendly and caring professor!

The class itself is not very hard. Quiz and test questions are based on the homework so if you do the homework then you should be fine. Professor is alright. Great professor and person. He made lectures and assignments very interesting. Also was reasonable and listened to feedback from students.

He is the best professor I have ever had. Teaches well, very organized, and extremely reasonable and friendly. Never had any trouble understanding instructions or reaching him. Would take every class w/ him if I could.

Incredible lecturer, conveys complex topics with interactive examples. Class was slightly disorganized, but I think after this quarter it will be much better. He is one of the most caring and down-to-earth professors I've had and his class wasn't difficult. COGS100 is hard to teach because many students don't care about it, but he did a great job.

He is an amazing lecturer, very entertaining and is always engaging with the class. He is open to extending assignment deadlines and answering questions at all times. Disorganized yes, but I think he did a good job of explaining the course material. He was nice and easily approachable outside of class as well. Good, solid professor. He wasn't anything amazing, but did his job well and taught the subject in a clear manner. His HW was helpful and midterms were fair difficulty. If you studied and did the practice midterm, the midterms are a breeze. Final was fair, not super difficult, but just long.

Absolutely wonderful professor. Her lectures were easy to follow and the class was open everything except other people. Lots of easy extra credit opportunities and she does her best to make sure we all understood the material. I definitely recommend her!

Class was mainly participation, involved weekly problems sets that took 30-60 minutes to do each week. Midterm and final were a combination of multiple choice/free response. Reza may be knowledgeable but he doesn't know how to teach. He teaches exclusively using PowerPoints and explains math aurally. That's a poor way to teach math. Dr. Reza is very knowledgeable. He has a lot of industry experience which brings a unique perspective to teaching. I only wish there was more time to learn from him in his course. Second class with Prof. Moazzam. He definitely grew on me. His classes cover complex material so be prepared to study ALOT. However, its worth it. The classes I took with him scored me a job! He is hard to understand, but his knowledge is worth taking the time break down what he is saying. 5/5 His UCSD extension courses are solid!

I'm consistently disappointed in UCSD. The professors teaches RF, and a main point in understanding anything in engineering is through the mathematics. Prof. Xiaolong is an inspirational teacher. He is very knowledgeable in computer vision and robotics. His lecture contains a lot of his own insights in the area, which are very interesting.

MATH20D's workload is crazy, the time I spent on this class is even more than my upper division class. Cool professor. Forgets to take a break for students to digest the material, but extremely open to questions and suggestions on how to improve her own teaching. Four quizzes, one midterm and one final would determine most part of the final grade. Pooja always gave exams that were much more difficult than practice exams, and the grading of exams was very strict. Lots of homework.

This professor's exam is very difficult, it takes three hours of handwriting exam. I will never take his class again.

Lectures are very content-heavy and takes a long time not too terrible imo but you have to commit to it. Final was extremely specific to the lectures, pay close attention to them. He taught long lectures that werent very meaningful and the content that he talked about in class was not that relevant. His final was so bad and the 10 short responses barely made any sense.

Fast response on Campuswire, 8% extra credits available (could be more, but my group only got 8%) and the bar for A+ is only 95%. What can you expect more lol. Attendance are just on the Gradescope quiz, which means you can do them without even showing up if you really want.

Easily one of the best profs in the dsc department. His relevant industry experiences and discussions are invaluable and extremely applicable/up to date, which isn't always the case in other classes. Definitely one of the most important classes for dsc majors and one of my favorite classes
One of the best profs in the DS program, super practical perspective and focuses on learning instead of jumping through hoops.

Dr. Goldrath's BILD 28 class is not your average lower division Biology class -- it was much harder, but also a million times more interesting. Immunology is a very challenging class. And Dr. Goldrath did not make it any easier. She's really nice and very intelligent, but her lectures are way too technical and it's really hard to stay interested. She does offer extra credit, and exams are challenging. Loved the class and the professor. TAKE HER!!!! Did not think it was as hard as everyone said it would be. Her exams are very straight forward, and her assignmentsprojects are actually fun. Definitely one of my favorite UD bio classes here at UCSD.

Immunology's a hard topic in general, but Goldrath is a fantastic lecturer. She podcasts and really highlights the info you need to know. Her tests aren't easy, but they're doable if you keep up with the class.

Immunology is hard Goldrath's really really nice, really cares about your education, and really smart too.  I enjoyed her immunology class, but her exams were kind of difficult, but if you improve throughout the quarter she takes that into consideration.  i dont know why, but her final exam was really easy this quarter(wi'10) -UNDERSTAND FACS PLOTS
Very useful class. Learned a ton. Can't miss a lecture though!

Not often I actually rate professors, but Prof. Rai is incredible. Extremely knowledgable about the topic of negotiations, very engaging lectures, and super funny. Prof. Forbes is super understanding and even though exams are kinda tricky involving lots of memorization, she is very clear what we will be tested on! 
Prob one of the best bio profs at ucsd

Loved taking BICD 110 with Dr. Doublass Forbes! Grade is comprised of a few assignments, one mandatory lecture, and two exams. Content requires lots of memorization, but it's worth it!

Great professor, tough class. Lots of concepts to remember, so make sure your memorization is on point and definitely don't procrastinate when studying for exams. However, she's super clear with what you need to know and definitely cares about students' success. Take good notes and go to the review sessions (s/o to the IAs, y'all were awesome!)

This class isn't an easy class and requires a lot of time/memorization of concepts. Dr. Forbes was very straight forward with what to know and her grading scale was super lenient. Most importantly, she is an amazing and encouraging professor! She is so sweet and wants all her students to succeed not only in her class but their future careers too!

Hundreds of lecture slides ALL of which you MUST understand & MEMORIZE in order to do well on exams. Exams are closed notes & proctored. Good luck.

An easy A class. Professor Orfield is very knowledgeable of the material he's teaching, and gives everyone opportunity to have the best grade possible in the class. Graded by three papers (but if you do well on the first  two papers you don't have to take the final), participation, and extra credit. Take him!!

3 papers, all very easy if you do a moderate amount of work and thought into it. The papers arent synonynous with lectures, but sometimes there are scenarios that helps you. Orfield's lectures are clear, thought provoking and grants insight on many science related topics in law. 100% would take again and easily one of the best professors in PoliSci
Incredibly caring for his students and interested in what he teaches. Nothing is more engaging than a professor who is passionate about their class. He also sounds like Tom Hanks which is a bonus

Orfield is a very sweet man who's very clearly passionate about what he teaches. Grade consists of 3 papers and attendance. Attendance is graded at 15% which is pretty high, but you're allowed to miss 3 classes and still get 100%. Papers are interesting and not too taxing. Easy but interesting class.

I took this class for UD elective credit as a non-poli sci major and I really enjoyed the class. Professor Orfield is super kind and understanding. The class itself was graded on three papers and class attendance. (coming from somebody who's a terrible writer and dreads papers, it wasn't that bad!)

This class is extremely interesting, but the material is extremely difficult. Although he wants you to memorize patterns in the biosynthetic pathways, the only way to guarantee you get the exam questions right is to memorize all 60+ 20+ step mechanisms from the class. He is very generous with grading which makes this class survivable.

He teaches only with chalk. If you aren't that type of person consider another prof. lectures are super fast-paced but I recommend attending lectures and when you study, rewatch them at 2x speed and everything clicks. His examples are clear and repetitive so you get to practice writing the mechanisms. The tests are exactly like the practice tests.

He does have similar tests to the exams. The exams and the class aren't that hard. Just know that if you have a decent grade in the class you won't get a curve, but if your grade is really low you'll get a really big curve. Unfair to people with high Bs.

Prof Burkart was a pretty good prof. He does lecture really fast which can be an issue for some people, but I personally did not have a problem with it. His midterms and final were made very fair as they were represented very well by the practice midterms. He cares a lot and if you take the time to rewacth the lectures the material will make sense.

Beware Prof Burkart lectures only in chalk. Very fast paced lecture you don't get much out of going to lecture. He is very good at explaining concepts just WAY too fast so watch the podcasts and pause/process the material it works out. The tests were IDENTICAL to the practice exams/homework, which was SUPER nice, but grading is a little nit picky.

This course is insanely hard and if you get an A- or above you are a mensa genius. A lot of the material is the same as in Harvards Math 55 which is the worlds hardest college course. The project is very fun and allows you to actually apply some of the scientific knowledge in class rather than just do math.

This is one of the chemistry departments smartest and best professors. He goes above and beyond to try and make concepts make sense for students. The topics for this class are conceptually easier than 130 and 131 but the exam questions are more abstract so its about the same difficulty.

Dr Xiong is very knowledgeable. His lectures are well structured and go into incredible depth and details. Most of the grade is based on homework which can be really challenging. Exams are relatively easy and at the end of the day he gives grades graciously.

The quizzes for this class are kind of traumatizing since there is one a week. They are almost always just a question from the homework, but since everything from this class is experimental observations, each question is unique so there are a lot of very different problems to memorize. Exams have cheat sheet which save the day. Great teacher too.

Took P/NP, barely passed lmao. Spent way too much time on this class compared to the time I spent on my ECE classes.. Honestly look for easier options if you are taking for GE. Professor is really nice, but the quizzes are monstrous.. 4 min for 8 questions. Loads of reading and midterm and finals requires you to read the books too.
Professor Lu is knowledgeable and genuinely is invested in the material she teaches. If you are interested in substantively learning about the material, Lu is the right prof.

She does have a slight accent but it's not super difficult to understand her. Just do the readings/papers and show up to discussions and you'll be fine. Says lectures are mandatory, but she doesn't have any sort of assignment to prove that you were there. Does not record/podcast lectures and is unwilling to.
Super helpful and wants you to succeed.

Professor Lu is one of the more difficult professors of the history department. Quizzes are very specific to the readings. There are many readings to cover, and you must know them really well in order to do well on the quizzes. Personally, I found the course to be difficult. However, if you do all the readings carefully, you should be okay.

Professor Mochel made my UCSD experience. It was my last class at UCSD and getting to have her in my schedule made the class something to look forward to. She was caring and always willing to help. Thank you for the best class ever.

I took Professor Leadbetter's class for TDGE 10: FIlm and the topic was women in film. It was an amazing class! We had 1 lecture every week and she would do the class half lecture & half movie. The movies were fun and entertaining. She's an amazing lecturer and gives readings to go with the movies but they are easy.

Kind professor always willing to speak with students and answer questions. Clear grading criteria and quizzes were super fair. We were allowed to have a cheat sheet which helped too. Clicker questions and group project at end of quarter, but it was not difficult. I would recommend.

Good lecturer about the material that you will be quizzed on. In the actual lab, though, teaching/atmosphere depends on your TA. Clickers for lecture attendance, and 4 total quizzes. Quizzes can be a little tough but going to office hours gives good insight into the questions that she will ask

Lectures weren't related to the labs, but you do a pre-lab to prepare. There are a couple of writing assignments and lab reports to turn in that are graded by the IA (hope you get a good one). The quizzes proved to be harder than anticipated but you were allowed to bring a cheat sheet.

Very passionate and kind prof.  You can tell she loves what she teaches and cares about our understanding.  Also promotes opportunities for students and TAs. This class was huge so she was pretty inaccessible during lab, but her TAs were great so it was ok. The lab was tedious but if you have to take BILD 4, I recommend Mel.

Super sweet professor. You can tell she's passionate about not only the subject but also how the students use the information in their futures. Cares a ton about the TAs too. Uses clickers for attendance and theres one drawing before every lab, and a few quizzes + like 3 papers. Genuinely the sweetest, didn't have a single problem in that class.

Super hard to follow along, we were tested on material that I had never even heard of before, and explanations are not clear. TAs are often patronizing and not willing to explain concepts, and what we learn in class doesn't prepare us for the final. You're expected to self teach yourself a lot of concepts from readings that are often incoherent.

Very solid professor but very quiet. Extremely knowledgeable and writes very reasonable tests. Definintely not a free class, but the tests we took seemed easier than the practice tests from previous professors.
Solid lecturer. Uses a flipped classroom model which works well for the most part. Tests were quite doable as long as you attended lectures regularly and watched the pre-class videos.

Textbook is free. All exams/quizzes are open-book but are applications of knowledge rather than memorization. Main portion of grade is decided by your weekly coding assignments. He has a lot of TA's that can help you throughout the week. For a first coding class, I found it difficult. Nice curve and drops one-two of your worst grades for you.

ECE 15 was my first and last coding class. And Prof Gilja made the experience good! Materials were okay. Definitely prepare to spend DAYS on PAs. He gave lots of extra credits (on PAs, attendance, answer questions on Piazza etc.). TAs were super helpful. Def go to tutor hours to get your PA done!
Extremely hard class but the professor is amazing and put a fat curve for the final exam. Always happy to answer questions and has frequent office hours.
Professor's lectures were terrible. She read straight from the book, you're pretty much listening to an ebook. Not very helpful with giving examples or answering questions. Light homework.
(Had Prof. Bryan for MCWP 50).  Heinous professor that does not give any feedback other than stark criticism that makes you think your entire paper is a garbage pile with no direction or potential.

Took for MCWP 50 after getting 99% in MCWP 40. She is kind of nice but an awful grader who will take off points and provide little reasoning or helpful criticism. In her words, getting an A on a paper is often a matter of luck. Many students I spoke to at the end of the class were 0.1 away from the next letter grade and she did not round.
After her class, I am sure I will never write a paper in my rest of life.

Avoid her. She is definitely the tough grader. I never got any letter grade except some kind of A in ucsd, but her grading way just makes me depressed. I even have to use sleeping pills. Although we haven't finish final paper yet, I am pretty sure she will not give any curve to us. I need warn everybody not to take her class.

J.P. Gorin adores film media and that is contagious.
He is both a maker & a critic so his lectures include first-person experiences and that makes a key difference in bringing the material alive.
Yes, he has strong opinions, but he does not expect students to "parrot" him.
Usually has extraordinary T.A.s

Wow, it's been 11 years since I had the honor of attending his classes (though fortunate enough to catch him at the PFA lecture series on Pasolini... Wow, again. It was hard work, filled with perpetual passion; the defining moment of my college days, the exact, rare niche that I'd always waited, and hoped for. One particular memory: a pigeon flew.
JP Gorin is a seminal thinker in the history of film.  It is a PRIVILEGE to have studied iwith him in the 1970s.  Mind changing.
Simply the best

Extremely boring 3 hour lectures that are filled with mumbling.He never has a point. He shows French or Japanese movies only.All the movies were oppressive towards women.The midterm is a 6pg paper(single spaced) and final(12pgs double spaced). The teacher is unprofessional."Realm of the senses" is something that you can expect to see in this class.
Professor Wang tried but his lectures are not the most engaging. His slides are informative and you can self-study and do decent on tests.

I took his class for a GE and it was really easy. I did take it while we were online, the lectures were all recorded and no attendance was mandatory. Lectures really didn't help and were hard to focus through, but the material was pretty basic and easy as long as you can do high school level chemistry. Easy class for a GE

A solid teacher. very understanding if u ask for extension on assignments (won't even ask why). he gave us extra credit just for presenting a couple slides before class (in groups). there's a good amount of HW due weekly (not bad at all), midterms/final was MCQ and were v straightforward (highly recommend quizlet for them). a real decent teacher!

This professor is truly reasonable and caring. There are two posts saying he's being an extremely tough grader but that's not like 100% true. He is reasonable enough that you can simply tell him not to curve the class down. The man actually asks people whether they want to be curved or not. Email him or talk to him in person if that's your concern.

This class was taken for a GE requirement, and as a non-STEM major, I put my all into this class to do well. Apparently, that was pointless as my 91% turned into a C+ because he felt the need to (negatively) curve since TOO MANY PEOPLE GOT A'S. I refuse to understand why this is acceptable. If this happened to you too, please contact the Chem dept.

Probably one of the few professors that does not want to see you fail. Professor Neal is a fantastic professor and human being that truly cares about her students and their success. If you have the chance to take Biochem with her DO IT! 
We had three exams (not cumulative), 7 problem sets, and 16 mini quizzes (1 question). 10/10 would recommend.

Dr. Neal is an amazing person and is very passionate about teaching, however, I was not really a fan of her lectures. They were very material and text heavy and rushes through so it is hard to keep up. However, her exams were open note and remote to ease stress, so it's easy to get a good grade in this class if you keep on top of lectures.

Dr. Neal was by far my favorite professor so far! She structured her class very well and clearly stated what is expected in her class. You get 3 exams, 6 problem sets, and post-lecture quizzes every day which is easy. I truly loved the passion she showed which motivated me to do well in this class. If she is teaching a class, TAKE IT WITH HER!

Professor Neal is one of those professors that can truly make her students gain passion and enjoyment towards her class despite it being something like biochemistry. She is very caring and thoughtful and overall wants her students to succeed. I would ten out of ten times recommend her.

By far the worst teacher I have ever had at this school. She demonstrates no care for her students, offering very little help outside of class and not responding to emails in a timely manner. Lectures were extremely hard to understand, and having now finished the course I cannot tell you a single thing I actually learned.

No offense, but she is the worst professor I have ever had. Practice final, final, and homework are not related. She had a hard time on speaking English so the explanation of concepts and definition is not clear.

WORST professor I've ever had. Not recommended. Her accent made the lecture hard to understand. The practice final and the formal examination is completely different, both on the test site and difficulty. Her syllabus says no curve so the average might be C+. Would never take again.

She has a very hard time speaking english, even sitting in the front row I had no idea half of the things she was trying to say. That alone made going to class tortuous. She never responds on piazza, is very unorganized in canvas, and often made mistakes uploading homeworks and such. I had to reach out to the other professor to understand anything.

She has never made an appearance on the class's Piazza and the students had to rely on another prof who is teaching the same course. She rarely responds to her emails and her midterm exam was ridiculous because it consisted of everything that was NOT on the practice midterm. Her lecture notes are basically transcripts of the textbook. NOT worth

Prof. Bartlett, although a good researcher & nice person, is not the best teacher. His tests are trivial memorization, resulting in midterm avgs of ~50% and essay scores of 69%. His unclear expectations and focus on trivial things in a microbe memorization class led to ochem level grades - AVG 2.67 @ SP22. Shame b/c it is an interesting topic.

MY FAVORITE PROFESSOR EVER! I'm sad that she is retiring, however, she made me enjoy humanities and I actually loved all of the readings she assigned. The lectures were entertaining, essay grades are based on your TA, and overall a caring professor.

I took Professor Caciola's HIEU107 Pagan Europe and the Christian Aftermath and I will say it was a fun and interesting course. She brings very informed and interesting topics to lectures, but make sure to attend lectures as the slides she shows are only available then. Only downside was the midterm and final papers as it was chose your own topic.

I loved Caciola's Hum 2. She was incredibly engaging, and her lecture style made it really easy to take good notes. I absolutely loved the class because of her, and as long as you studied exactly what she said to study, the final was super easy. She also just seems very respectable and clearly knows the material very well.

Caciola's lectures had slides, and most importantly, vocab words to focus on. I found her lectures pretty interesting, and she throws in a couple jokes now and then. Essay prompts, however, were pretty difficult; she focuses a lot on subtle themes in HUM rather than the history itself. Grades dependent on TAs, but Nancy is a good lecturer.

Wonderful prof! Her lectures are extremely interesting and hold attention the entire time. She is very knowledgeable and also super amusing. The reading was interesting, the essay prompts were relatively straightforward, and the final was quite easy. You have to go to class to get the vocab and notes, but it's entertaining! Definitely recommend!

He is one of my favorite professors at ucsd and he was amazing and really caring. He gave a lot of bonus opportunities. I'm sad he's leaving ucsd, if he had stayed I will definitely take his class again.

Prof Willis is super nice, this is the best class I could imagine having. Super easy to understand, attendance is not mandatory at all, lectures are recorded, all quizzes and exams are online. Tons of extra credit, had 130% at one point. Quizzes and exams are completely reasonable. His lectures are given really well and the content is interesting.

dr. willis was by far the most compassionate and understanding prof i've had so far, he understands that students have bad days and listens to students, he gives extra credit, and his lectures are really engaging. the class itself is super easy, and he podcasts the lectures in case you cant make it. i highly recommend this prof!

I got an A in the class and it was relatively easy the professor and TAs were awful. His grading is all over the place and confusing until the very last minute. His exam questions were confusing and worded poorly. The TAs grading was inconsistent which isn't totally his fault but he didn't do much about it. Would not take again.

Professor is nice, but honestly this course was not what I was expecting at all. He overcomplicated things and his questions are worded weirdly. Honestly, I was hoping this class to be an easy A, but I couldn't deal with the deviation from what I was expecting to learn and I just wasn't interested in what the course ended up being about.
Professor Katz was very knowledgable and caring! I definitely recommend them for anyone wanting to learn about incarceration/gender and anything tbh!

Professor Gere is a delight. She shares the context and implications abt the history topics she teaches. HISC 117 requires a solid amount of in class discussion (~50%), so careful if you don't like speaking. Overall, her approach is tactful, lectures engaging, and assignments pretty fun. There are ~1k word papers due every week.

Lectures were podcasted and thus attendance was not mandatory. The class content was very interesting, and professor Gere was understanding and very knowledgeable. A very enjoyable class, although one's grade is heavily dependent upon the TA they are assigned to.

Entertaining lectures and energetic professor, but was graded harshly on papers, got marked off for questionable things, final paper dropped my grade a whole letter and final grading schema was weird. (she said I got an A-, but gave me a 30/40 (75%) and tanked my grade), recc taking p/np if possible but if you're a good writer, you should be okay?

Prof. Gere is a super enthusiastic lecturer, and you can tell she loves the material. Her lectures can be a bit long, but she really is great at presenting the material. There were three writing assignments and they were all graded pretty leniently. She was also really accommodating when I had to submit the final online instead of in class.

Prof. Gere's grading method sucks. I received A's on both midterm papers but then she gave me a C+ for the final which then dropped my over all grade to a B. Her expectations for the final paper were not clear and it is very frustrating to have one paper worth more than two.

The class is pretty laidback. There's not a lot of homework rather a big group project assigned at the beginning of the quarter. The project was a bit disorganized. Some of the ideas taught in class are structured to change your mind. If you are neutral of class material there shouldnt be a problem. The final exam is also another project.

There is a lot of reading for this class but I guarantee you will learn something new that will genuinely change or reform your opinions. The class is incredibly interesting and it is pretty easy to get an A as out of the three assignments, two are fun projects and only one is a short written piece.

Sections are required. There's only 3 assignments, along with section attendance on the grade. I went to 0 lectures, and read nothing and got 100%. But the professor is really passionate and knowledgeable about the topic.

By far best professor that I've taken at UCSD, she is so passionate about what she teaches about. Lecture consisted of teaching + class discussion, and participation does matter. I had a lot going on and communicated that w/ her & she was so nice and understanding about assignments. She also creates a welcoming space for POC & low income students.

The topic is pretty interesting, even for someone outside of the major. The readings are the strength of the class- they're insightful. The lectures are dry and hard to focus on. She's very kind and knows her stuff well, but terminology often gets you lost. Some terms are broad but have specific uses that feel difficult to memorize. Read and pass.

Very good teaching, but just stop teaching in the future. He gets more papers published, and we get better experience, which is better for everyone. But this is just for 120B. For other classes, maybe it's not this case.

Great class and professor! The professor really broke down the material and made it really intuitive to understand. He provides diagrams and drawings during the lecture to help visualize symmetry. He had module knowledge checks after each chapter that amounted to 70% of your grade so staying caught up with the material was critical to your grade.

As the class was asynchronous, Rinhart provided lectures really late, so I felt like I was unintentionally procrastinating. He provided graded hw problems, but the difficulty was not in match with the quizzes. His lectures were good and has a quirky sense of humor. I feel like it would have been a great class in person.

Prof. Rinehart is one of the best professors I had!! He is super fun and makes the lectures very clear and easy to understand. The homeworks were only graded by completeness but they are helpful for preparing the exams so you should do them. Exams aren't too hard if you pay attention in class. HW were 20%, two midterms 20% each & 35% final.

I think the problem sets were harder than the actual exams themselves. Pay attention to the examples done in class, too. This was the first time he podcasted lecture, but you still need to pay attention. Class average is a B- with other grades set accordingly.

I like Kongsgaard. His grading policy was extremely generous and he is a kind man. His style of lecturing makes it difficult to note take, but the course is podcasted. Don't take this course if you don't have previous knowledge about calculus. The exams reflect the practice exam questions very well, but the homework is a little difficult.

Kongsgaard is one of the better math professors at UCSD. He's very friendly and makes tough concepts seem relatively straight forward. However, he does go through a lot of content in his lectures that don't really pertain to problems that you will see on a test. But if you take the practice problems he posts before the exams you should be prepared.
Great professor. Had relatively straightforward midterms, but the final was a bad curveball for me and a lot of people I talked to afterwards

The professor does absolutely nothing to help the students. He simply reads off the slides, which are poorly edited. The lectures are not recorded. Good thing the classwork is light, and the professor doesn't play too big of a role.

Don't need to bother going to lectures, they are pretty useless. Just read everything on what he posts or look at old lab presentations from ucsd. Homework is 1-2 questions per week. Lab reports can be confusing but just go to the extra lab sections and ask a lot of questions, then you'll be fine. Make sure to read old homework/labs for final;
The class is a huge time-sink but the content itself is pretty easy. You can probably get by with not going to lecture as long as you do the hw problems and the labs. Final exam was also super easy.
TA plays a more important role to me. Final is easy as long as you go over the problems done in classes.

Not really sure what we learned in this class but you don't really need to and you'll still be fine. HW is just like 1-2 textbook questions every 2 weeks and theres only 4 lab reports. His lectures weren't really helpful it was just going over 2 math problems and the experiments but that was about it, nothing new learned in this course.

Prof Lovett-Baron is a nice guy but his tests are challenging. I found the course material very interesting but a piece of advice I can give is that TAKE PHYSIOLOGY before taking BIPN 140. It will help you understand the concept better. Overall, he doesn't curve and your grade is only dependent on exams and quizzes. No HW or extra credit given.

Prof. Lovett seems nice, but his class is only based on exams and quizzes. He doesn't curve and there's no additional assignments (for extra points). Definitely a waste of an elective and a GPA ruiner. He may be super intelligent and featured on Forbes 30 under 30, but he can't teach.

Great professor, really passionate and interested with his class. Sometimes went off on tangents playing around with the synthesizer program, but just showed his true passion for music. Clear, very reasonable grading criteria and very interesting and inspiring class. Would definitely take him again.

(took this class for BILD 20) Great professor, you can tell she really cares about students and values feedback. Only thing is that her quizzes and exams were a little difficult, but if you study and go to discussion sessions it's not bad!! There's no homework and only 5 quizzes, midterm, and a final project (+ some surveys to get credit).

Dr.Pillus is a one of a kind professor that is truly there to teach. She takes the time to learn her student's names. She is extremely helpful and welcomes questions. You will learn a lot with her. BUT...she is hard. Her tests will require intelligence. She has a generous curve (The MT average was 60/120 after removing outliers from geniuses).

Fantastic professor! Very help in office hours and is extremely approachable. She definitely has the students' best interests in mind. The tests and material are difficult but the sections are a good supplement for knowledge gaps. She does speak rather quietly and rapidly so sitting at the front is not a bad idea.

Good prof. Nice, SUPER HELPFUL in OH and in the help rooms. She really cares. Lectures are kinda boring but tests are fair/doable if you study & do the problem sets. Attend section too, some TAs are also helpful. She speaks kind of quietly so sit in the front. Overall, decent prof, I'd definitely take her again.

Prof Pillus is GREAT. she loves teaching and it shows. she really wants you to know your stuff, so the tests are killers! you gotta go to lecture, read the book, and do the problem sets. MUST do the practice exams. expect to fail, if you don't. go to section or OH because it helps a ton. be an active student if you want your A
He tries to accommodate the class as much as he can (which is great) but he goes over the lecture way too fast. However, if you go to the SI sessions and complete the homework you'll be fine.

RUN! Do not take him. He is a very boring lecturer and on top of that, was not very accommodating during the TA strike, which fine is not expected, but when the students are without the discussion sections for a whole month, and he still doesn't give extra help for the midterms, which he makes a HUGE portion of the grade, about 80%. Dont take him.
Professor Kim added an extra grading scale to accommodate for student hardships related to the TA strikes. He definitely cares about students succeeding

10c with prof. Kim was definitely tough but we're talking about advanced calculus for people mostly going into fields where comprehension matters. He is kind, answers questions, and meets us in the middle on grading (more than fairly). You will definitely need to study, attend class, and be prepared for homework but I would easily recommend him

lectures move quickly but was a 10 wk course. homework heavy but reasonably graded. He always asked if people had questions before moving forward, although he maybe didn't always understand student questions, this isnt that uncommon amongst advanced math people. Easily accessible by email or canvas/piazza. Overall would take again/recommend.

Really nice professor, no homework assignments but quiz and midterm heavy, final is worth about 50% of the grade. Gives extra credit opportunities, all you really need is to go to the lectures and you'll pass. Easy class for credit

Took during Winter 2023. Great class overall. Professor is an entertaining lecturer. The quizzes are a bit tough, and the class is only exam based, so be aware of that. However, everything is take home. Material is interesting, and I wouldn't say anything in the class is unfair. There are a few extra credit opportunities that are doable and easy.

Lectures were very engaging with tons of guest speakers. Grade consists of 2 quizzes, midterm, final, & 1 extra credit assignment. You get 2 attempts for the quizzes & 1 for midterm/final. Lots of reading imo & its definitely needed for the exams. Study guides have been VERY helpful with discussion sessions before every quiz/exam. Loved her class!

Genuinely such a sweet professor and knows her stuff. She really cares about her students and their mental health. Her midterms weren't hard at all, such easy As as long as you listen during lecture. The final was pretty difficult compared to her midterms and i got a significantly lower grade on that. In general, great professor.

One of the worst professors I've had. Boring and dense lectures, hard to comprehend, quizzes/exams with unclear questions and specific answers. Mandatory lecture/discussion. I was excited for this class, but the professor killed that excitement within the first couple of lectures. Avoid this professor if you value your sanity and grade!

Stay away from this professor. Nice person to talk with, but doesn't care for her students. Her lectures are unorganized and don't grab one's attention. Not enough time for exams. Discussion is what saved me. Was very excited going into this class, but the professor changed that real quick. Take any other bio elective, not worth the stress.

Dr. Niwa's class was quite challenging Discussion sections were helpful. She provides practice midterms and practice final as study tools. However, she did incorporate multiple guest speakers with very dense lectures which were quite difficult to study for. Overall, she's very kind and really wants students to understand the material, not memorize.

The worst professor I've ever had. Lectures make no sense, explanations are useless, and organization is nonexistent. Class midterm average was 67% and she refuses to curve. Doesn't give dates for when her quizzes are due, so you have to check canvas every day. No matter how interested you are in this class, it isn't worth having her as a professor

Absolutely terrible. Lectures make no sense, slides are useless, and explanations are convoluted. She goes over time every class. The midterm was unfair and not reflective of the content. I could not even tell what she was asking for in the questions. I expect the final will go similarly. This is the worst professor I've had at UCSD. Run.

John Lincoln is a brilliant online marketing expert and students are lucky to be able to take a class with him as the teacher. His class is what helped start my online marketing career, leading to a very successful business.

I took this class during trip to San Diego for holiday. John had many guest speakers, was perfect to learn many different types or analytics. John was good teacher and made me excited about topic. Good class for me to learn for my job.
Took course for marketing certification but made me learn a lot about analytics and conversion rate optimization. Also, Mr lincoln is SEO expert,,, very cool!!
Way better class than I thought it would be. Uses interesting real world examples, excited about topic

This teacher was very excited about the topic. He made me excited about Internet marketing. I had no idea how much things there were to do. I especially liked his information on how SEO is changing and social media viral campaigns.

Prof Moumen is nice but French is difficult. for a 2.5-unit class, they make you do a lot of work. Participation really matters and you have to speak a lot. The book is really expensive n she teaches a lot of things not even mentioned in the book. Don't take this class if you don't wanna put in too much effort.

Madame Hana is amazing. She is so nice and she's young, so she relates to her students a lot. Attendance is mandatory (allowed to miss 3 classes) and biweekly quizzes (study vocab and you will be fine). She will build your vocabulary and is not afraid to correct your pronunciation and will help you learn how to spell/pronounce words. Love her!

While Sworder can be a nice, insightful guy, his style of teaching is outright not productive for most students. He provides high-level examples to explain the concepts, but rarely goes throughs actual sample questions at the level we are expected to; leaving you feeling like you barely got enough practice to understand the concepts.

I'm normally an A or B+ student and I'll probably fail. I have been put off of the subject because of his class. He's nice but not a good lecturer. You are teaching yourself or otherwise watching lectures with no structure. He fails to answer student questions 50% of the time and the book is very technical and does zero hand holding (all examples)

I would love to say something nice about this professor because he seems like a nice person, but man does he suck at teaching. I can't even find one positive aspect of his class, like, his class material is super disorganized, he does not answer emails, does not teach properly, super vague about logistics, and oops word limits. Just don't take him

Run. The other 45 posts are not exaggerating, quite possibly the worst class I have ever taken in my life. As someone who prefers the easiest option, taking this with a professor regarded as "hard" would have been 100x easier than taking it with Sworder.
