Lectures are worthless, grade is based off 4 things, and he belongs in a nursing home.

barely any applicable HW probs. has written the same image on the chalk board for the past 8 weeks. Zero instruction. talks about random aspects about being an engineer in class. class is not informative at all. the only way you pass is through 100% self instruction. avoid at all costs. pick a different prof. for a different quarter.

Clarifying my grade, it's not about the professor more like a personal issue. Prof Defrance is a good professor, he likes controversy so he might get a little off topic but it keeps the material interesting and might end up giving you ideas for your papers. He can be confusing but cares about his students learning and will be happy to help you.
Would never do this again. Least caring professor.

This was not a fun class. My mental health state definately deteriorated by the end of the semester. She does not give direction at all, so half the time you spend in class is just trying to figure out what to do, and that's why people get behind on work so easily. She's very abrasive so don't take this class if you struggle with anxiety. rip.
Just took her class in Spring tough teacher but patient and down to earth. You show up to class on time ready to do the work and put in the effort, your good.
I suffer in her class. She is not accessible at all because she is either condescending students or focuses on things unrelated to school. Dont take her class is you dont want to be berated.

This professor is strict. She also lets her emotions get to her. While shes busy with other things for the theater, maybe there should be another teacher that doesnt let their emotions get to them. A professor shouldnt have students fearing or hating them, and shes got both.

I love Samantha. She is very funny and smart. The lectures (from the Prof) were challenging but Sam always made everything so much more clear during section. I learned so much in section. She was always happy and excited to teach and made MMW bearable. I would 100% recommend. She is inclusive to all of her students validated their participation.

Prof is a good guy. But in terms of the class, the lectures he gives are good, he just isn't the best aside from that. The material gone over in the lecture does not really correlate to homework it is all textbook-assigned problems where he assigns too much ?'s per week which are all too time-consuming. hw is also accuracy graded. curves at end

I don't like math, nor am I good at it but Professor Ganzberger made the concepts easy to understand and would do plenty of practice problems in class. His tests are fair and are allowed a crib sheet. As long as you do the homework and review problems he provides, you will do just fine in the class. He also lowered the grade scale at the end.

His lectures facilitate note-taking well and he seems very accessible in-class. Before the midterms and the final, he hosted review sessions and posted problems that would help us on the exam; simply doing all the review problems ensured my getting an A+ in the class.

Ganzberger is a nice dude that really wants you to pass his class. His lectures are pretty good, and there's only one assignment per week. His midterms are pretty rough tho. The homework does not do a good job of prepping you for the questions on the tests, so go to the review sessions and office hours!

I previously failed out of Math 10C and wow Ganzberger was the best. He cares about your success and wants you to do well in class. He is very receptive to questions and accessible outside of class. He rewards hard work.

This rating is for her Russian 1 class at SMC. She is genuinely the best professor I've ever had. Cares so much about her students, she genuinely wants everyone to succeed and will do her best to make it happen. Russian is an extremely challenging language, but she does well to make it interesting and fun with many cultural and political examples.

I took her for Russian 1 in SMC. She's extremely humble(even though she doesn't need to be because she plays a huge role in Slavic Politics on a global scale) and tries her best to be accommodating as possible. Class is really TOUGH, if you're not a Slavic language speaker. But she'll do her best to drill it in you and help you along the way.

I got this Professor for Russian 1. She's great, and an extremely fair grader. But she's uh.. learning Canvas, so get use to that. Homework isn't bad, you'll smash it out in 1 hour AT THE MOST.
I recommend you write her power points AHEAD OF CLASS from Canvas online, so that way you can write what she lectures rather then end up with a mess.

Clearly a genius in her field. The class was composed of students of different backgrounds - native Ru speakers, film buffs, people taking the class as an elective - and she handled the variety well. When I fell behind in the class, she kept the focus on my learning and recovery rather than being punitive. I wish she stayed at UCSD instead of UCLA!

the TA's graded everything in this class so ignore her being a hard grader. her class was really easy and  she is very accommodating if any emergency or mental health issues arise. i've taken her 2 times and its been an easy A, she designs the classes to make sure everyone passes

Take her ! Attendance is not mandatory for lectures although if you go she tries her best to hear students comments and be interactive. The work isnt that hard if you put in at least some effort. The sections are always interesting and the TA's are good.

Professor Irani is pretty harsh grader on the assignments, the lectures are causing more confusion on the subject. She teaches a lot of classes in Communications department. I'd avoid her as any way possible.

Took professor Irani's class in the fall online. It was pretty easy. Just show up to the lectures and read the articles assigned on modules, kinda lengthy. Weekly quizzes after every reading. Participation counts, but you can easily do it on canvas. 3 main papers are pretty simple and straightforward.

I loved Professor Irani's course. She is very flexible and if the class raises a concern to a due date, she is willing to compromise and change it. She cares about her students very much and her lectures are very interesting. There are a few readings each week followed up with a short reading quiz but they are not difficult if you did the reading.

1 OF THE BEST PROFS@SDSU.SUPER devoted as an educator. hella SMART. wise.tenured prof...his office is like a artistic library.he literally is a mad genius.took him multiple times&learned more in my life abt the subject and life in general lol in those 2 classes put together than much of my schooling combined. go to office hours,he wants u 2 succeed

Nericcio is new to UCSD and the CAT program because he usually teaches over at SDSU. He had never taught CAT 125 before and it showed as he met unusual resistance from the students. But it was a great class. a good university experience that was focused on discovering who you are by telling stories about yourself. The videos and books were good.

Challenging class, but professor was great and easily accessible outside of class. Lectures were detailed. Exams were in-person and difficult, but not impossible as long as you made sure to remember all of the details from the lectures. TAs were very helpful and had a great grasp on the material.

Interesting and engaging lectures (as long as language is interesting for you!). Prof always made an effort to answer any and all student questions kindly. No textbook or required readings, just show up to lecture and pay attention and you'll do well. Exams were very fair and the short weekly quizzes were quick and easy.

Pretty average class. I found it very boring so I didn't attend lectures as much as I wanted to. If you want an easy A, this isnt the class but it is possible if you study! The way the exams are wasn't it for me. About 120 questions mixed of true or false and some short answer ones :b. 2 midterms, 1 final, 6 quizzes (one dropped) and sona.

Cooperrider is very clear and engaging in lectures. Material is interesting and he takes time to help students, even holds extra OH before exams. Weekly 4 question quizzes and longer closed-note midterms, but if you understand material & memorize you'll be fine. He also has a cool podcast! Would recommend, and I'd take him again for other courses.

Cooperrider is a solid professor, I would take another course by him if the opportunity arises again. For his 101c class it consists of lecture/notes, class quiz towards the end of every week, and 2 midterms + final. His test are very fair and consists of lecture material, no tricks or gimmicks.
Best prof in UCSD CSE. Super nice! Will take a personal interest in helping you.

The most interesting, enjoyable course I've taken throughout my four years college life, his teaching is very clear and interesting, the interaction with students is also amazing. A meme contest was held, in class and after class he would also share the industry's latest news and his own views.
Professor Kumar is wonderful. He cares a ton, is super knowledgeable, and you will learn a ton from him. Great guy
One of the best professors I've ever had!

Professor Romero uses lecture time to help students understand concepts. His style of teaching is more of active learning, he will frequently put aside lecturing days to go over problem sets. While this is not effective for everyone, it sure as heck was for me. He has a pretty good sense of humor too, which makes the lectures interesting.

Professor Romero's class is difficult, with the grades only based on three exams, each with an average of about 65%. He gives practice tests representative of the exams, and lots of extra credit, on top of a curve to help out his students. He is super accessible outside of the class, has a good sense of humor, and seems to care for his students.
very challenging course

Someone needs to give this woman an award for being the most normal, capable, and organized chemistry professor in Arizona....maybe the world. Don't read another word just go sign up and take her for both CHM 151/152. You will not regret it.

Casual, young, realistic teacher who is knowledgable about chemistry. Easy class if you show up (graded attendance) and do online material (recorded lecture videos so take notes & weekly online homework). Basically, show you put in effort and you'll do good. I genuinely enjoyed her lecture and lab classes! Will take again for CHM152! Solid 10/10

Professor Schnoebelen is an excellent Chemistry professor who cares that her students understand the material in depth. Her exams are challenging, but most of the questions mirror the topics on the homework. Reading the textbook (as needed) and doing the homework are essential to doing well in her class.

Genuinely great. Her lectures are amazingly easy to understand and she was caring and available out of class. But with no curve, you'll have to earn your grades. However, the generous homework, the participation points, and the test grading promote genuine attempts toward improvement. I had never taken Chem before but this was easy to approach!

She podcasts, but I attended most lectures. I thought she was amazing and I really enjoyed her lectures. Her teaching style perfectly matched my learning one, as she talked really slowly, included lots of visuals to help you understand, and really stressed class participation including questions. The hw wasn't too bad and definitely helped for

He wasn't bad, but his teaching style was not great for me. He explained concepts with paragraphs instead of examples which doesn't work for me. Super sweet guy though and the class was curved. Got Cs on one midterm and the final and an A on the other midterm and ended up with an A in the class. You can miss a couple discussions.

Professor Rogalski explains the methods of solving integrals and series well. He cares for students having struggle with what method to use and how to use it for the math problems. It is very difficult to apply the various tests mentioned in lectures, so more practice is required to succeed in the class.

He never finishes his lectures and always makes mistakes on example problems he does during class. There is really no point in going to his lectures as you will get an incomplete confusing explanation for an otherwise straight forward concept. He tests fair though. Homework is hard up to impossible. Expect to learn through YouTube and TAs

Personally, the way he taught did not help me understand the topics - I was only able to get a decent grade because I had taken AP Calc BC before. The homework can be extremely hard sometimes and I spend around 4-5 hours on them if I'm actually trying to do them. The midterms this past quarter were hard but not impossible.

Slides consist of giant paragraphs of text he reads directly to us.He rarely does practice problems in class and the ones he does do always have typos leading to confusion.He doesn't get through lectures,usually only covering half the content.Lectures on new stuff Friday homework due Monday with few ways to get help.Tests are very fair however.

This class was not taught by Prof. Gladstein but by a TA. At first I did not vibe with my TA but she definitely grew on me. At times the assignments felt annoying since they due the next day but nothing was hard by any means. Basically a seminar class, so you have to attend. No final and a couple essays.

Professor Gladstein is very caring and gives good feedback, you just need to make sure that you ask questions when you need help. Since the class is still just starting, they are trying new things that can be kind of messy, but Professor Gladstein is understanding and helpful throughout the class.

No idea what the hell happened, but SYN 2 was all over the place this quarter (FA '22). The schedule was changed probably 10 times, the final was made online at the last minute, forcing everyone to scramble to turn their presentation into a video version, and class continuously got cancelled. That said, the actual TAs were doing their best!

The professor does not teach the class, the TA handles the whole thing. Can't say much about the professor, as I never met her, but the TAs are amazing! There is a lot of reading, and you have to attend section and participate, but it's not hard by any means. Put effort into your final project as well, don't phone it in, and you will be fine.

Least accommodating Professor I've met. Doesn't care about his students at all. Lectures were confusing because they included a lot of coding necessary for the homework but the homework had absolutely nothing to do with the material or the tests. It was on the student to filter out the actually important material that would show up on tests.

Run! Long lectures without clear interpretation. No practice questions during the lecture, making things hard to understand. Simply read the slides. He does not respond after every Thursday night. Use coding assignments that cannot help to understand the materials tested for exams. Extreme hard exams without enough time. Cumulative final.

Attendance is recorded by doing Canvas surveys. I didn't watch a single lecture and was able to do relatively well. Do all the practice exams repeatedly before the midterms and final and you should be able to score above the median grade. He curves like a madman so you only need a pulse to pass. Midterms had a 50% avg. Final had a 36% avg HAHAHA.

Class is what you make of it based on your level of hard work and curiosity. Marc gave us an option to have our own inputs on how to make the class better, took our advice, and added some stuff like extra examples/clearer grading criteria to make learning more engaging. I'd say he really wants us to learn and the material itself is pretty amazing
Favorite econ professor. Learned so much in his class.

Fantastic professor. The class was scheduled to be an hour 20 minutes each session and it was cut short 20 minutes each time which was great. He doesn't allow note taking on laptops so if that is a big issue for you I would maybe stay away. His lectures are so interesting though that I found myself not needing notes. Quizzes/essays are easy and fun

Do not take any class with Silva. He does not teach. All he does is come 45 minutes or so late to the lectures with his cup of coffee. He does not answer questions and kind of arrogant. He says he will curve the class and does not curve the way he promises. He is worthless and shall bot be allowed to teach.

Grading curve was not as promised. Lectures were not even by Silva, but prerecorded ones by Shankar. He said tests are not going to be with memorized equations and everything will be supplied. The tests were almost entirely based on memorized equations. Overall an awful professor and I hope by the time I retake the class, the professor has changed.

Silva was never prepared for lectures, and always late. When we asked any questions in class, he would become visibly frustrated and often refused to answer questions clearly. The entire class was graded on a midterm, final, and final paper that were not representative of the textbook material.
Do not recommend. If you can take anyone else, do so.

Told us to watch the recorded lectures of professor who taught the class last year instead of lecturing. Often showed up late to class (30-40 minutes late), the TAs would improvise and do textbook problems. No equation sheet on midterm and minimal equation sheet on final. Vague prompt for final paper, didn't give further advice on picking a topic.

Would not recommend this professor. Did not care about teaching the class, showed up late to lectures, and used a past professor's lecture to teach the class. The TA's taught the majority of the content. Included a report assignment with very little instruction on how to write the report.

The lectures were alright, the projects were fun. I learned a lot in this class. I enjoyed making a lot of videos and working with people in my section to film. I learned how to use video editing tools. The process of editing videos requires a lot of time, especially because I'm a perfectionist, but I enjoyed the process.

The TA was nice but absolutely terrible, was not ready for each class and never knows the answers to our questions. The professor could definitely be better but the projects were fun and I did learn somethings from this class.

This class is extremely unorganized and poorly instructed. Professor Cho has very minimal interaction with the class. My TA consistently misses or comes late to section which negatively impacts success in this class greatly. Lack of communication between professor and TA's. Extremely confusing and frustrating class.

Ignore the freshmen that got slapped into the lecture hall of 200. Cho excels in the personable small class sizes of advanced senior level courses. Narrative design and screenplay adaptability sits at the forefront of this course. Borrowing from other advanced and graduate courses Cho teaches, youll learn how to perfect your screenplay here.

The only time you interact with Professor Cho is during lectures. Most of the grading and the work is done in discussion or lab which are led by a TA. Cho's assignments don't allow much creative liberty. There are many restrictions on assignments. Lectures are unnecessarily long and tedious. There isn't anything she says that the book doesn't say.
Cool teacher! His homework and tests were fair, and his lecturers were enjoyable.

Took him for Management 45 and he was great. The homeworks are fine, same being said for midterm and final. He was accessible outside of class, and overall a very cool guy. Make sure to do extra exercices

I love Mr.Gallant, he is such a sweet man and is so passionate about the subject he teaches. Not afraid to crack jokes or tell personal stories relating to the history he's teaching. Open book tests, midterm and final. Cares for all of his students and their wellbeing in school. 10/10 recommend.

Loved professor Gallant, his lectures are easy to understand and really funny! The workload for this course is pretty light, and you'll get an A as long as you pay attention in class. Assignments are on completion and tests are very straightforward. Go to lecture, you won't regret it!

He was extremely caring and you could really tell how passionate he is about the subject. He gives 3 pop quizzes at the beginning of lecture (don't be late or he'll lock you out until it's over) and drops your lowest score. He's also pretty funny. Definitely attend lecture and study your notes for the midterm/final and you'll do well.

Professor Gallant is hands down one of the best lecturers I have been taught by. His lectures are frankly enthralling and if I could, I'd take his class every quarter! Take notes and you'll ace the class. Although there is quite a bit of reading, it really isn't necessary to do well. One word of advice though, beware of the unannounced quizzes!

Professor Gallant is one of the best professors at UCSD.  He's easy to understand and makes the course material very interesting to learn.  He has assigned reading for each topic but if you attend lecture and take detailed notes you don't need to read the textbook.  His exams  include a MC section, IDs, and short essay that are fairly easy.
Late, unprepared, and unreasonable

Best class so far. Difficult material but office hours extremely useful. Blatant cheating in Matlab & assignments by some. Real worry these guys will become 'engineers' in a couple of years, and tarnish rest of us. Major ethics violations. Employers & internships: avoid B or lower at all costs. Previous reviewer claims A, seriously doubt it.
Avoid at all costs.

Excellent class sabotaged by a few bad students. Prof  taught really well.  UCSD should not admit students who cannot understand elementary math and english. Employers beware of students that failed/barely passed MAE 143A this quarter. My classmates know  several cheated - including the guy who wrote the previous 5 reviews.
He wrote on the blackboard in illegible handwriting. He seemed to be completely unaware that his students were dozing off, doodling in their notebooks, or staring blankly into space.

As the semester wore on, the students became increasingly desperate. They formed study groups, consulted textbooks, and even hired tutors, but nothing could prepare them for the professor's final exam. It was a mishmash of random questions, typos, and grammatical errors. Some of the questions were so unclear that no one knew what they were asking.
Went to his OHs and they were super helpful. Just watch the podcasts / go to lectures and do HWs in time and you'll be fine.

171A is based off of math 18 for the most part. Prof Gill assigns two hw per week: one written, one programming. They take a bit of time but not too strenuous and mainly review of lectures-which are alot of slides if you handwrite but break down proofs and examples well. Lecture examples are usually seen in different forms for exams and homework.

gives a HW with a separate MATLAB assignment every week including on test weeks. Does give a practice midterm that is close to what you find on the actual midterm. You will need help on the HW and MATLAB. Does give extensions on HWs when asked. Overall not a bad professor, but just get ready to work for the grade. Also he does curve the class.

Professor Gill is knowledgeable, but doesn't seem to care much about the students. His lectures are informative, but boring and slow. He gives two homework assignments every week, regular HW and Matlab HW (they are time-consuming and not easy). He gives two midterms and a final. NO CHEAT SHEETS. He gives practice midterms, but NOT a practice final.

He taught a math class without picking up a chalk or marker all quarter. Inaccessible outside of class so don't bother emailing him, 2 HW assignments every week (Written and Matlab) which will take about 10 hours to complete. 2 Midterms, 1 final no practice final and no cheat sheets. Focused WAY TOO much on theory and not how to solve LP problems.

I've read other ratings and from my experience she was just unwilling to kindly answer questions like curves, cumulative final, etc. I feel like that's pretty reasonable though, and her responses just ask students to know the lectures. In the end, it's a great learning experience and it's really not that hard. (And I think I got curved to an A)

The professor is clearly knowledgeable and it is easy to tell, but she is by far one of the most passive-aggressive professors I've ever had, it is hard to tell the nature of why this is the case given that for the most part she answers lecture questions fairly well,  but her answers to any other questions will make you regret asking.

She is the first prof that seems to have hostility attitude to students, especially when students ask questions that seem "stupid" to her. A student on piazza asked "Will final be cumulative?" Her answer was "Yes. I don't entirely understand why you're asking, though.  Why wouldn't you expect it to be?  And why ask now?"

Super organized class structure. Readings, lecture, weekly homework on readings -> repeat. He's a tough grader, but if you read before AND after class+pay attention to lecture (take good notes!), you will be prepared to get a good grade. You can't skirt by this class without doing anything tho, as he's looking for specific answers to the homework.

His class is fun, and his explanation is clear though readings are hard. He sometimes throws out way too many jargons but he is willing to clarify. Not an intimidating class as long as you do the reading in a timely manner and go to the lectures.

He's an amazing lecturer. He holds your attention well and is pretty funny. Makes dense course readings palatable and easy to parse - he has outlines for each reading posted on Canvas which create a great compass to guide you through each one. He doesn't grade easily, but if you do the reading and pay attention in class, you'll be fine.

He's legit my favorite prof ever. Super caring, funny, and teaches really well. His exams are straightforward, and he doesn't try to make it difficult. Literally would take all my classes with him if i could.

I made an account just to Rate this Prof. Best lecturer I had at UCSD. Makes everything so nice and easy to understand and actually interesting. I looked forward to every lecture this class, it was a nice break from all my STEM classes. Love him please take this class!

Professor Daugherty tries to answer questions to the best of his abilities. But his exams are very difficult, especially the finals. He gets so intricate with the concepts that your memory fails you in the exams. 3 quizzes, 3 exams including finals worth 90% of your grade. He does not curve or round up, even when it's 0.05 pts to the next grade.
Very nice guy and very knowledgeable professor. Textbook readings are assigned but are repetitive of lectures. The class itself is extremely rad, would highly recommend.

Solid professor for microbio. Not the most exciting that I've ever had, but was very nice and straightforward in presenting the material in a way that everyone understood (which is what matters). Exams are based on the lecture slides, quizzes are based on the textbook. Overall not too hard to get an A in if you put in effort memorizing his content.

Terrible professor. Super boring and monotone. Fails to capture any key points because he goes off tangent way too much. You're better off watching the podcast at home because you can skip through the 30 minutes/lecture where he goes off tangent. Exams are super vague. Guidelines are super vague. Assignments are super vague. Terrible, just terrible

Class isn't hard but it's not easy to get an A.  He makes it so that only 20% of the class gets an A but Allen gives way more "A" grades.  If the midterm average is too high, then the final will be hard.  The questions are really specific and you can't miss many if you want a solid A.  I got an A- and there was no curve at all for the "A" cutoff.

Professor Golden is one of the best professor's I've had at UCSD; he is passionate, funny, thorough and fair. The textbook isn't as necessary as he says but absolutely watch (and enjoy) his lectures and that right there is exactly whats on the exams. There's a little homework but its super easy. Highly recommend!!

Dr Golden is awesome! He goes over lectures slowly and clearly so even if you doze off you won't miss much, tests are based on lecture slides so memorize everything and you have an A, 2 simple hw assignments- go to section if you want the answers. No curve for A/B cutoffs but this class is simple enough that you don't need a curve to do well.

He hid assignment grades until after the grade was due so students could not correct mistakes so he would have less work to do. He almost never showed up to class but required you to be there, provided 0 information about what the final would be like (our only exam) and then curved only above 90%, to improve class GPA and hurt most students.
Curve needed for the test. By doing her ps and practice exams will be helpful for the test.

I had her last quarter for 120a and for 100b this quarter. This material is a lot harder for me and I did poorly on both midterms. I am hoping to pass her class since its the last econ course I need to take for my business major. She is understanding and her office hours helped. I wish I had asked for help sooner.

I bombed the first midterm (C after curve) and was about to drop the class. Prof. T said to talk to her if we have questions about the exam so I figured why not.
She went over my exam with me and I realized that I had been studying wrong (I had memorized solutions, but she always changes things up). 
Luckily, that exam was dropped so I did well!
The course is extremely hard, but she is a great instructor.

BY THE GRACE OF GODS I PASSED! I attended all lectures, paid attention and the quizzes and midterms were very hard for me. I failed all the test/final, and passed because of her generous curve. Still try to do your best bc it was nerve-racking. Prof even recommend I drop bc I was struggling. She's nice but not the best at explaining concepts.

Winter 2023. Coursework: 9 MCQ Canvas Quiz Homework (5%), Midterm 1 (20%), Midterm 2 (30%), Finals (45%). This class is very light in coursework; spent about 4-5hrs weekly for lectures + study. Exams are relatively easy and are very reflective of the lecture materials. Genuinely one of the most interesting classes.

Class grading was broken down into homework, 2 midterms, and 1 final exam. Homework was worth only 5% and tests were very dense in material. No cheat sheets were allowed for the final and you had to memorize ~10 chapters of content.
Lecture are heavy and long and is hard to maintain concentration, she complicates algebra a lot, but has a good speaker voice. TEST ARE HARD

Professor Ramey is a very well accomplished economist and genuinely cares for her students, but isn't the best teacher. Class isn't that hard, but concepts are explained in unclear ways, requiring studying outside resources. Lots of regrading, "sorry that was worded in a confusing way," re-explaining, clarifying Q's

You need to have an ipad for her lectures or take notes after class because she goes very fast during lectures. She is an accomplished economist but I wouldn't say she is the best teacher. Sometimes lecture gets a bit confusing. You definitely have to read the textbook (besides lectures) do the homework and go to discussion if you want an A.

Compared to the other physics professors I have had from 1A and 1B, he seems to be the most passionate about teaching and explaining the concepts. It honestly disheartens me because he is not really a terrible professor, that was not the issue. The quizzes however were VERY hard and unfair as they were nothing like the hw or practice tests.

By far the WORST professor I have ever had.
 
Terrible teacher. Lectures are very disorganized. Takes lecture material from other professors and reads off their slides. I had to go to other professors' lectures in order to learn anything. His tests are every SATURDAY, 10 questions in TEN MINUTES, he teaches nothing on the tests. The Final is 50%.

He bombards you with assignments - 2 quizzes, 2 tests and 2 homework assignments (which are 4 videos 16-45 min long and questions on it) EVERY WEEK. everything is due back to back so no time to breathe ans the tests are extremely hard and half the time arent even on things we have discussed yet.

I took this class Spr 2020 and I did not enjoy the class at all. His lectures were once a week and extremely long, often going way beyond the time it would take for in person lectures. He would just read off his massive slide deck and not explain what he was saying. Boring and confusing. Heavily curved which was nice because tests where very hard.

If you are a visual learner, do not take his class. If you like taking notes and studying from your notes only, take his class. I would not recommend him if you can't focus in class or intend to miss a class because he is lecture heavy.

Professor Yetwin is a great lecturer. Unfortunately, his class is lecture heavy and he does not provide any exams, quizzes, or papers for his class except for one Final Exam. So, his grading criteria is based on Attendance (~10% of your grade), Participation (~10-20% of your grade), and a Final Exam (~above 70% of your total grade).

Professor Yetwin is great, he's super passionate and has a lot of experience in real estate. He makes his own textbook with materials he's used in the business throughout the years and gives it to students for free! His lecture style is very good for note taking, and as long as you pay attention and take good notes you'll do great in the class
A lot of the time, he doesn't explain ideas very effectively. He covers a lot of material in every lecture , so it's simple to get lost.

He's a nice guy but really doesn't explain concepts very well a lot of the time. There are a TON of lectures and he covers a LOT of material, so it is easy to become overwhelmed. His quizzes and exams consist of a few easy questions and very very specific questions that ask things he barely touched on. At least his quizzes and exams are open note.

In the beginning of the class it was alright, but them lectures hit hard a s f. Tough grader, 2 midterms, final, 2 (25pt) assignments and quiz every week. The amount of lecture is crazy. It is all over the place. If this class is not required for your major, don't take it. He needs to re organize and condense the lectures bc u will get lost.

Don't take this class with him. Content is not difficult to learn but his lectures are full of experimental results that he fails to explain fully. So it's very difficult to study for his quizzes because his questions are more in depth than what he teaches during lecture. If taking it for elective, don't because it's not worth it.

Dr. Kohn is a clear and knowledgeable speaker. Very informative lectures but he organizes them pretty well. It takes a lot of work to be successful in this class but fortunately he has all slides and simplified notes on Tritoned. He does have podcasts for home learners but he forgot to put on his microphone a couple of times lol.
Even if you have a pretty good functional understanding of the concepts, his quizzes are worded in such a way that you get little to no credit if not worded precisely

Surprised at the previous rating. Paleniks teaching style is great so far (not finished yet) and pretty comprehensive. In depth study guides available for quizzes along with notice ahead of time. The content of the class tends to require that you actually study it to grasp it but that should be expected with micro. A few big writing assignments.

Hated this professor. SO boring. If you skip the lectures, you will not pass. No final, but there are four quizzes and three essays. Even though I was only taking this class as an elective for my major, I only just passed. I hated watching the lectures as they were extremely boring for me.

Professor claimed that you did not need prior knowledge of music to do well in the class, but many terms used for assignments are very technical and 100% require previous knowledge of the subject area. Good thing my TA did not grade harshly, which made the class better for me.
I love him

Professor Kern is a nice instructor in general. He clearly explains everything and is well known as being fair when it comes to grading and evaluations. His lectures are very detailed and often heavy but very engaging. I loved his class but if you skip class, you will not pass. Overall, very inspirational and cool guy.

Professor Kern is great. When I say that it is a level 5.0 difficulty, I do not mean professor Kern is difficult. I simply mean the class is very challenging and is a very high level class. Need to have a high level understanding of POLS and IR to be successful honestly. You should be a junior or senior to take this class. Great professor!

Dr. Kern is an excellent professor. He is clear and direct which is helpful. However, if you skip class you will not pass. Expects quality work but understands if students are struggling and will help them!

Professor Kern is truly amazing! He really does care about how you do in the class and if you are fully understanding the material. The class is sometimes difficult however, professor Kern makes it up with his cringey political science jokes. Best prof I've ever had! Take him if you have the chance!

Prof Macagno really cares about the subjects discussed in class. He truly wants his students to do well. Assignments are easy and are given weekly. If you study for the quizzes, it should not be too hard of a class. There is a group project at the end, make sure you get a good group for this one.

You can tell he really cares about the subjects discussed in class. He doesn't come off as approachable, but he very much is and has a great sense of humor. He truly wants his students to think critically and do well in the class. Assignments are weekly and are easy enough. Group project is interesting, but choose a good group.

Professor Macagno is a very knowledgeable professor and he works very hard to keep the course interesting and relevant to his students. He expects a lot of active participation, but his lectures are very interesting! Studying for tests is a must, but other than that the class is very relaxed.

A really wonderful teacher, clearly loves what he does. Don't be a slacker or a dumbass and this class is easy enough to pass. I loved all the guest lecturers and the way he lectures -- he is great if you talk to him outside of class! He really wants you to succeed if you want to, and people complaining about reading - its a college class, grow up.

Lots of guest lectures in this class, which makes this course unorganized and tough. Besides, he gives trick questions in the quizzes, which means you have to remember lots of details and trivial statistics. Take this class only if you are truly interested in the topic of dementia.
She either missed or cancelled too many classes. Had a quiz every week but no solutions were released so it didn't help me.

Professor Belmont missed 5+ lectures this quarter, either having a substitute teacher or lecture videos. She taught one day completely without a voice too. There is a quiz every Friday, and she does not give clear explanations as to why the answers are right. No final review, We lectured on the last day instead of reviewing material.

She is super nice, young, and understanding. Goes over the concepts very thoroughly, and writes neat lecture notes. I will say many of the homework problems were more difficult or far reaching than things we did in class, but she give good help. Definitely the best math professor I have had thus far.
prof belmont's lectures were super useful when doing the HW and studying for the exams. she was very clear about how she wanted us to write our proofs, and i learned a lot from this class!!
teaching is clear, every week have a quiz which is meaningful, but the hw is kinda hard but you can learn things.

Lecture is usually about 50-60 slides and is not recorded (but lecture slides are posted a few hours before class), but if you keep up with the material and take good notes the course is very manageable. As a non-bio major, I very much enjoyed Professor Komiyama and this course.

The lectures were twice a week and each was 50+ slides. The organization was difficult to follow and very disorganized would not recommend as a GE course. For being a non major class this class was very stressful and not very difficult.
Class is not easy even though its a non-major class. However, just go to lectures and study his lecture notes and you'll be fine. Professor is nice and his lectures are really clear.

The materials are not that difficult to understand but his exams have a lot of short answers and fill in the blank. Going to lectures are important because basically you get one point of your overall grade if you go to one lecture. So 15 lectures15 points. His teaching style is a little bit boring and you have to study for midterms and finals.

This is the most intriguing class I have taken so far at UCSD. Professor is incredibly intelligent, kind and explains information very clearly. It is a lot to memorize, but if you enjoy the lectures, studying isn't and issue. Highly recommend this class, with this professor if you have the time to study for it.
poor lecturer, cannot explain simple concepts well. Not recommend

Lectures were prerecorded and he mostly read off his slides. It was hard to follow, and when I went to office hours to ask for other examples he just read from his lecture slides again. Homework was due weekly, even if there were exams coming up. He knows what he's talking about, but it's a difficult class.

The professor merely repeats other professors' ideas and lecture materials during normal instructions, which provided inefficient online learning access to most of the students I believe. And the quizzes were hard to understand in context sometimes. It was just torturing to take his class.

This guy might be the worst professor I've ever had. Him and the two other teachers for this class for Winter Quarter 2021 put minimal effort into teaching the class. They copied other people's lectures, only to chime in every 20 minutes and say something pointless. This also meant no in-person lectures to ask questions. Don't enroll in his class.

his lectures and slides are confusing, textbook is a lot more helpful for to exams so just read that. there's weekly homework and quizzes and it really ramps up after like week 3; midterm 1 and the final were pretty hard and so are the quizzes - they're worth a suprising amount of your grade and a 0/3 is not an uncommon grade on most of them

Sarah is awesome and MUS151 is a great course. She's passionate and realistic with grading. Extensions are easy to get, and lectures are stimulating and facilitate discussions. She offers lots of extra credit and there was one weekly assignment, one essay midterm, and one free-choice final. The course is super easy and low-stress with Sarah.

She was a great. Posted all her slides online. Gave random quizzes during lecture for participation points but were pretty basic if you followed along. Normally wouldn't go the full 3 hours time. Easy A but does require some effort and time. Discussion sections were mandatory and had short weekly assignments.

Has a hard-to-understand accent but is very caring. Are graded on a few things which means you need to know the material. If you have no clue what's going on, you're doomed. Have to be present in class bc she doesn't post any announcements or reminders.

Professor Shi is very friendly and approcheable, sometimes it can be hard to understand during lectures. Final exam is worth a big chunk of your grade. You are graded by 3 problem sets, 1 midterm, 1 final, and 1 policy analysis. Be ready to read and go over the problem sets to do well during exams.

Interesting class. Professor may be hard to understand at times but an overall approachable and intelligent teacher. She is also very kind and takes into consideration what students suggest can make the class better.  It helps a lot if you take FPMU 101 before this class because some of the material overlap.
There is no textbook or readings, just her lectures. Her accent can be hard to understand and she is not fair with regrades. No midterm, just a final and a few assignments here and there.

This is the hardest class for no reason. She states all concepts are easy and "straightforward" but does not consider that it might not be for some. Doesn't specify what quizzes and tests are on. Just says to study everything which lead many of us to rely on asking the TA's what we should study. You have to teach yourself in order to understand.

Professor Seifert is a knowledgeable and understanding professor, however her courses were made needlessly difficult due to a multitude of logistical difficulties. Though the concepts themselves are relatively simple to understand, she often misses them and her test/homework questions are confusing and unclear. She also doesn't record lecture.
Rude and unhelpful

He comes in truth & grace. Professor Gregoire is a thoughtful, caring & passionate artist. He is experienced within his field and has a wealth of knowledge. I had taken, perhaps 2 years ago, and he was one of my favorite instructors at UCSD.
Not the most interesting class but isn't very hard either.

His lectures can be boring due to the fact that they are two hours long but he is very helpful. He shows you a wide variety of work that really helps with projects. He doesn't have a negative attitude at all. He comes to studios sometimes and if very nice and helpful.

Mathieu is a pretty good teacher. The lectures can get boring since they last for two hours but he has a lot to say and it does help with projects. Your grade comes down to the TA. Be prepared to spend money and a lot of time on projects.
Difficulty. Very difficult. Homework took a really long time, some problems felt borderline impossible, but he taught clearly and was a good lecturer.

Horrible professor. I put in 35+ studying for this class weekly - still struggled (got an A in cse21) No practice problems (says do textbook problems day before, which are NOTHING like the actual problems). Lectures are hard to follow. Homework is challenging and TAs have no clue what is going on. NO CURVE - he gets a kick out of failing students.

Don't get me wrong. His homework and tests are difficult. But he is among the most caring professor in UCSD. When he sees a hand raised in lecture, he would run up to the student in order to listen closely. This really shows how passionate he is about teaching.

This professor is the worst one I have ever taken. You'd better read books than taking his lectures because they are basically the same. The exams are so hard and outdated that I wonder the professor has ever updated the exams or not. His homework are unreasonably hard that most of the students on this class have complained about it. Avoid him !!!

The difficulty of his class will surely impact the amount of time you will be able to spend on your other classes, and Life. Do yourself a favor and take it with someone else, like I did. There's difficult, and there's excessive. Guess which category this class falls into?
Alex Norr is easily one of the best professors in the real estate program. Very knowledgable and generally cares about his students.

Professor Norr is young and understanding. He doesn't live in SD, so he's not too accessible the rest of the week, but he's very helpful during class. He really wants us all to succeed, & gives a lot of tools to do so. His assignments and projects take a long time just because of the nature of the course, so plan for that. Important & useful class
Professor Frank cares about his students and wants them to do their best in his class. Keep up with the readings and go to class.

Frank assigns ALOT of reading, expect to be doing about 60-150 pages a week with mandatory discussions-- however, they are very rewarding and necessary readings for the purpose of the course. good class if you're interested in politics or campaigns (rather easy too, if you keep up with the work), but not a good prof if you're looking to build a professional or deeper relationship as he's very hard to reach outside of class and offered no support to students during the strike, other than the occasional cryptic or condescending message.

The class is 4 assignments, and 3 of them are due in the last 3 weeks of the quarter so it just isn't structured very well. Took this during summer, the work load is kind of heavy but understandable. Grading scale is very reasonable. Nice guy in general.

Very approachable and communicates well with students, asks for feedback. Readings were relevant, not too long, and explained well in lecture. Encourages discussions and questions. Very knowledgeable. Class is reasonably easy as long as you do the readings. Great professor.

I've had this professor for 5 classes. She is outstanding. Her upper division Biological Anthropological classes can be a little dense for non-Life Sciences majors so it might not be a good pick for a GE requirement.

I found her to be quite unapproachable. She answered emails quickly but they were condescending and very unhelpful. All the other ANTH profs have been amazing so I was quite surprised by my bad experience with this professor.

I find it weird she has bad reviews because I loved Professor Mihic. I only took her ANTH2 class which is a beginner class and it was just my GE.. but I loved it and found it interesting. The professor seems to assume that the students have 30+ hours for this course every week. He teaches as if everyone has taken the course before, leaving many things unexplained. Professor Rao is very knowledgeable. The problem with that is he overlooks that sometimes students dont understand what hes saying because its trivial to him. Professor Rao is an amazing lecturer who is very interested in student success! He does a great job giving feedback and really likes to answer questions. The worst ever!
Poor lecturer and exams aren't reflective of what he teaches.

He is the best math professor I have ever had so far. When I was in high school I did not really have a great math teacher so that made me feel a little scared when I enrolled at UCSD. Amazing professor, really makes calculus easy to understand, he does a lot of drawing to help explain a concept, there is not much hw, do the practice exam and you're good to go :)

He was pretty cool, he cared about lot about the individual's learning. He lost me on some of the concepts and made a few mistakes in class but he always tried to catch them. He gave great resources for those that were still confused with an easy to access textbook and other things.

There are not enough ratings on this website to accurately represent the environment of this class conducted by this professor. The professor is not helpful. This professor seems ok at first but is terrible. His average for the final exam this year was 56% which means the average student in his class pretty much failed the exam. Professor Cain was a really good math teacher. His lectures are taught very well, and he is always open for questions. As someone who has always been awful at math, I can say Professor Cain is one of the best math teachers I've had since high school. She was really nice and cared a lot for our individual learning. I will say she used lectures more as workshops for the most part to go through the labs and I don't feel as if I learned very much about statistics but rather learned a lot regarding coding instead.

Dr. Fan's class uses CourseKata to teach R. It makes learning the language much easier. Class time is devoted to labs and you're given plenty of time and leniency to complete them. I really enjoyed this class.

THIS CLASS IS HEAVILY CODING BASED (in R). Very easy if you have prior coding experience, but pretty difficult if you do not, especially if you aren't prepared for it. Professor Fan is very knowledgeable in stats practices of psychology. Statistics is hard as it is, so the overall class is difficult as well. The quizzes are hard even though they're based on the lecture material. The coding worksheets are hard too, especially for beginners in programming. A few grading adjustments were made so that helped a lot.
I've been in Mus95L for a few quarters now and honestly it's the highlight of my week because of him. He makes it fun and enjoyable, while also creating rather great concerts.

I was in MUS 95L for just a few quarters, but every quarter has been a blast with Mike. He's very kind, has a great sense of humor, and is excellent at what he does. He's a phenomenal conductor, and is actually one of the very best I've ever had in an ensemble. His feedback is great, and this ensemble is a joy to be apart of, thanks to him.

Class started good, everything was great and then a week before the midterm she pulled the rug from under our feet. The midterm had too many things for the amount of time given. For the rest of the quarter, things did not get any better. She taught us one way of doing things to later change them.

Professor Katie was the nicest professor I've ever had! She really made sure to create a comfortable space for everyone to learn and the lectures were interesting and engaging. Horrible professor but amazing TA. Every TA  office hour and discussion session has been packed and the burden to teach has been unfairly placed on them. Clearly passionate about the subject, but the class is strongly based on the textbook which is not the clearest. HW and quiz questions all come from the book, so reading is pretty mandatory. Test questions come directly from lecture and quizzes. Hard for an intro to physics

Straight forward grading, clearly spoken, interesting lectures, expected material on the exams, take notes on textbook and you are good. I really enjoy her class. Easy for a first year, I would know lol!

Prof. Lugannani is by far my favorite professor! He is a great lecturer, funny, truly cares about his students. Maybe 3 or 4 homework assignments throughout the quarter. Exam are extremely fair! Fair and hilarious. Teaches by using examples. If you study and practice the old exams enough, you should get at least a B. classes are not mandatory, but extra credit was granted for attending all discussion sections. worst test grade is weighed the least :)
