I struggle a lot with class before but she made it a lot easier to understand the material.

She is a great professor! She is very passionate about teaching, and very friendly. Her lecture is very clear, and the tests are exactly what she taught in class. I just wish the notes are more organized though.

Lisa Ho is kind, and she knows a lot about the classes. I like her as a person. I would never take another class with her. The requirements for the midterm were not made clear or put in writing anywhere. I was docked 10% of my midterm grade over something that was mentioned once in class. A normal week of homework is 2, 46 page academic readings.

I had to take Lisa for 3 classes so I'm pretty familiar with her. She is new but it absolutely does not show. Lisa is an incredible speaker/lecturer and knows the topics very well. If you engage, you will absolutely learn a lot from her. She is not perfect though as she can often dominate discussions and can't seem to relate subjects to students.
She's a good professor. But she gave a lot of pop quizzes. If you don't read everything before the lecture then your lose your participation.
Lisa provides a clear and inderstandable lecture. Makes material easier to process.

Shes new, but it doesnt show. Shes very informed, must do meticulous preparation for class because shes awesome at teaching. She has a no tech policy thats honestly very annoying but otherwise pretty decent.
Mean human being
Not professional at all

She does not prepare for her class and asks a lot of questions to students. Her way of teaching is to use the Harvard business cases. I feel like I learned nothing new from her and anyone can teach this kind of class without a PhD degree. Even though she does not prepare class herself, she has double standards for students. Worst professor ever.
She does not prepare for her class at all, and require the student to teach and her personality is really bad.

Was very flexible with homework. Homework was due every Sunday and no more assignments would be assigned other than that. Sometimes the math was hard but eventually it made sense especially when you visit during his office hours.
A great professor!

If you have previous Japanese learning experience this class is easy for you. But if you like me who never study Japanese before then this class will be a little challenging. Even though I get a B, I felt like a could be done better if the prof did elaborate more during classes. It's better for you to do the reviewing every day.

First time taking an in-person JAPN class and Prof Maruyama made it a very memorable experience. She's very professional and clear when explaining concepts. Very detailed when grading homework. Sometimes threw jokes here and there which lightened up the mood of the class a bit.
She is nice and tried to make the lectures not entirely boring. Part of me wishes she would do more to make her lectures more unique but it is what it is.
She's cool, very nice, and as flexible as she is allowed to be.

One of the best professors I've ever had! Maruyama Sensee is very kind and very supportive. The course structure and contents are extremely well-organized and easy to follow, so as long as you participate actively in class and do the assigned homework, you will learn a lot and get good grades, as the grading is also nice! HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!!

Karen is amazing! I loved having her for AWP. She gives great feedback on assignments. Both books are mandatory to pass the class. AWP is a lot but she recognizes this and will work with you if life gets rough. She is very caring! I definitely recommend her for AWP or any other course! Do the work and build off her feedback and you will do fine!

Karen is such a kind and understanding professor. She almost never lectures, preferring holding open discusssions and zoom group chats for projects. She give the BEST feedback, and is very helpful with revisions and seeking out advice.

Karen is one of the best writing professors that I have ever studied under. She is extremely knowledgeable and always has inspiring and refreshing ideas to add to our discussion of ideas. Granted, the class involved a lot of reading and a lot of papers to write, but she's helped me develop greatly as a writer and as a thinker. Thanks Karen!
The toughest grade I have ever seen. He does not really grade assignments himself neither TAs do, he uses machines to grade with no room for regrading options, sucks.

Good luck if this is your first coding class. So difficult to understand and keep up when new concepts are completely glazed over. The examples in class are so specific I can't even apply them to the homework assignments.
does not know how to teach other than read codes
Hey just wanna ask what is the point of 1% extra credit when he sets the total marks to 101%? lol

Attendance not mandatory but you kinda have to go because lectures aren't recorded & slides won't help you understand because they're so brief. Completely glazes over lecture slides & jumps right into the journals when most still don't even understand the basic vocab. Homework is impossible for me if I don't go to discussion AND office hours.

Dr. Saborio is a smart professor, but not flexible. He refused to allow a late quiz, even though I told him it was due to a disability and referenced my disability services coordinator until I had an official plan. I also had to argue for extra credit for a physical model I made, even though it wasn't required and the syllabus allows extra credit.
Chiara is an extremely kind, funny and helpful professor! She always made class fun and enjoyable and creates a comfortable environment for students! If you have the chance to take her do it!!

Chiara is a very caring  and wants her students to succeed. The content of the course itself isn't outrageously difficult as long as you pay attention and put work into it.  Participation matters so be sure to do so as that might be the difference between a whole letter grade.

If you're shy and don't want to participate, you won't do as well as you want to in this class. Participation is a huge part of the grade and she typically gives B+'s and A-'s. The whole grade is pretty much participation and the midterms/final, so watch out.

Chiara is clearly passionate about teaching Italian. Even though, initially, full language immersion seems overwhelming, she makes enjoyable and is extremely helpful during office hours. I had fun and learned a lot in this class. Highly recommend Chiara.

Chiara is the best professor you could ever have for Italian. She is understanding, helpful, funny, intelligent... She helped contribute to the text book as well! :) You will fall in love with her the day you meet her. Guaranteed.
All I have to say is if you have to take physics, do NOT take this class.

This has been the worst class I've taken at UCSD. The wording on the ppts, homeworks, and tests are not clear and there are a ton of trick questions. The final is worth 47% of your grade so even if you do all the homework you can still fail the class since his tests are so notoriously hard. Lectures are fast paced and I retained nothing from them.

Must attend lecture for attendance/participation credit. Professor uses iclicker questions, and you get points based on your answer. Lectures are not very interesting, but that may be because I have no interest in physics. 2 midterms are taken with one lowest grade dropped. Final is 50% of your grade, and you have to purchase scantrons yourself

He's a great guy, but not so great professor. It's not a Physics class, more like a Life Trivia class. Lectures are packed and require clickers for participation (graded clicker correctness too). There is lots of reading presentation slides and hardcore memorization of random life facts required for midterms and final. SUBSTANTIAL CURVE.

If Professor Zhong is the only professor that available to register for, take another class a different semester. She goes very fast in her lectures and people do poorly on the exams because of the way she teaches. Her lecture notes and her solutions on practice exams and also on homework's show very little work by skipping a lot of steps.

Very hard to understand accent and handwriting at times. Tests are ridiculously hard, they have 0 connection to lecture or homework. The quiz avg was so bad because nobody even knew what they were asking. She ended up letting us retake all quizzes though which is why I give a 2 star instead of 1.

Dr. Jez has very clear expectations and is likely the most effective professor I've ever had. She is very accessible and you can tell she cares a whole lot. If you do well in her class, you're going to do well in life. Anyone complaining about workload shouldn't have come to grad school.

The worst Professor ever! She has unrealistic expectations and came off very condescending and cold. Shes very rude and unhelpful. All my classmates were struggling with the work load and lack of help. She and another professor uploaded a video of them mocking students. Many students had to switch to another Professor. She should not be a teacher!

DO NOT TAKE ANY CLASS WITH HIM. This guy will bore you to death. All his lectures will put you to sleep. He does not answer emails. Does not make himself available after class. He only speaks in big ambiguous terms. He teaches an undergraduate course like you already have had a Ph.D for 20 years and expects you to know everything. HORRIBLE.

He's a smart guy (he won a field medal). However, his explanations are not clear which made me learn all the class material through YouTube. Tests are easy, Homework is easy, and the class itself is easy, but he wasn't a great teacher.

Professor Zelmanov lectures enthusiastically over Zoom with his characteristic Russian accent by going over his pre-written notes, pausing regularly for questions, which makes his lectures very fun and enjoyable. However, his proof-first approach to concepts are not the easiest to understand and turns students away to other Math 18 lecturers.

Made an account so that I can warm people not to take a class with Zelmanov. Learning linear algebra from Zelmanov is like trying to learn how to ride a bike purely from dictionary entries. He overcomplicates almost everything, and I find that reading the textbook and just teaching myself is a better alternative than trying to understand him.

Professor Zelmanov's lectures are mostly proofs and not actually useful examples. They're more confusing than helpful, and I basically taught myself everything thru YT and the textbook. Very test heavy and lots of homework.

He's clearly a very smart guy based on his credentials, but teaching a first semester undergraduate course is certainly not his strength. Extremely confusing lectures, me and most others in his class just attended another professor's lectures after the first 2 weeks because of how confusing his lessons were.
She gives a lot of homework. She is really cool and all, and her lectures are not challenging at all but the homework is really heavy.

Professor Chung is AMAZING! She is extremely helpful, always gives feedback, and gives many assignments that help raise your grade. Most of your grade for this class will be based on the journals she assigns. Get an A in those journals and you will get an A in the class. They are not hard you just have to be passionate about the course themes.
Professor Chung is one of the best professors at UCSD. Her lecture is very inspirational, the reading is heavy but very interesting. You can easily get a good grade if you put into the work

HANDS DOWN THE MOST DOWN TO EARTH PERSON EVER. she genuinely cares for every student that is in her class. I never felt like I couldnt reach out to her and she was really understanding even though I joined the class late, I was able to make it up. That is a rare case. Heavy writing assignments but very manageable and she outlines everything!

Amazing professor. I never thought I would take an education studies related class, I am glad that I did. Even though the class is online, Professor Chung made the class very entertaining, a lot of discussion during class. However, be ready to read. I spent hours reading and write my weekly reflections. The readings are quite interesting though.

Kedlaya is very lazy. All the other professors grade the exams/ homeworks themself during the strike, except for this guy, who sit there and did nothing. We did 10 homeworks during the quater, and only 4 of them were graded.
Never grade the homeworks, never give solution to practice exams. Learned out of null space. Nothing.

He clearly cares about students and is a great mathematician, but it always felt as if class was a second priority to something else in his life. Lectures were hard to follow due to poor handwriting and a general feeling as if he didn't plan what he was doing. Might've partly been because the textbook also sucked but that's not an excuse

I took Professor Kiran Kedlaya's course in Winter 2020. Do ask for help in this class because there is a lot of programming assignments that will be done in this course and it is best you pay attention to lectures and do research on your own. One short midterm and a final project on a topic of choice. Start the project early and not last minute!
His compassion towards his students shows, but he's no way a good lecturer. Hard to understand because of thick accent.

In what world is it remotely sane to charge exorbitant tuition for a course that doesn't teach you anything? I'll tell you: in the capitol of wokeness called California. The purpose of pedagogy is to edify; NOT INDOCTRINATE

This was the easiest class I have ever taken. Dr. Purritty gave us lots of days off, no discussions, hw took about 5 minutes a week. Attendance was never recorded but people consistently showed up throughout the year because they wanted to. She's really funny, smart, and caring. I never got bored in class throughout the whole quarter.
easiest class in my life.

ANTH 21 with Kang is a ridiculously easy A. As long as you put at least a little effort into the few writing assignments that you get, you are basically guaranteed an A. The midterm is an oral exam, curved so that the median score is a 90 and the final is a group project. Kang will frequently adjust the schedule/deadlines to accommodate life events
Professor Kang was a great person, his class was easy. Although there are a lot of long readings, they didn't technically need to be read to do the assignments. The final was oral and very fast.

Prof. Kang had a lot of trouble w/technology & zoom, but the class was very easy. The material is very interesting and relevant. The readings are interesting too but you can get by w/o them. Midterm and final were oral exams. He asked for students opinions on the format of the exams. Other assignments were easy. There were a few EC opportunities.

ANTH 21 is a great class on its own- the material is stimulating and very worth talking about. Prof. Kang specifically is a very nice professor, easygoing, and his grading criteria is well distributed, does not solely depend on midterm or final, lots of opportunities to up one's grade.

I love Amy! She is so smart and quirky and inspiring as a teacher. She makes you want to participate with the types of lectures she has. She really is a free form type of teacher and allows a lot of freedom for you to be creative.
It was a very stimulating class. But get ready to work a lot!
to avoid

His lectures and the provided readings aren't very helpful for the climate change groups projects we work on throughout the quarter as we need to research our own peer-reviewed primary sources. His lectures are interesting, he's chill, and he was easily available at Copa Vida for office hours after class.

Burgasser goes above and beyond to ensure that his students learn. He's passionate about teaching and physics. His style is best suited for physics majors, so non-STEM/physics-opposed students struggle in his course. I've worked in his lab for 1.5 years, and he ensures students feel supported and understand scientific concepts behind research

There were midterms disguised as “quizzes” every 2 weeks. Those “quizzes” were extremely confusing and a good chunk of your grade. He expect everyone to already understand the material he’s supposed to be teaching. Definitely thinks he’s your only class. Very needy. Please stay away from this man. I am beyond traumatized.

Cool guy, rough quarter. Difficult online exams (D-F average, no curve). Upset everyone with the in-person final, but ended up making it a grade-booster after loads of complaints. Final was much easier, all MC, had bonus questions, could raise exam scores and be replaced by original exam grade. 5% extra credit and median grade ended up being an 86.
Avoid him! He doesn't care about students. Passive agressive personality. The worst university teacher I ever met.
The class is boring but if you go to every class and read the assigned chapter, getting an A is doable. I think he had a massive curve at the end of the quarter. Take him!

I honestly never went to class and only went for quizzes, midterms and of course the final. To do well in this class, you must read the book because that's all I did and got an A. He also provided extra credit worth 15 points so that helped a lot. Check TED, read the book, attend class to take notes and you'll get an A.

I was hesitant about this class because of the negative reviews but the professor actually does well teaching. His notes are organized and usually follows along with the book, which is important when studying. I initially intended to take this P/NP but missed the deadline. I studied as best as I could and got an A. In the end, it's up to you!

He literally does repeat the book and the book does not have all of the information required to do well on the quizzes or tests. I will say that he does provide useful study guides on TED but overall he is not a good professor.

He's a nice guy with good intentions, but his class difficulty is weird. Lecture examples are simple to understand. Exams are a bit trickier but still manageable. However, homework is impossibly difficult so be warned. He's not bad but requires a lot of effort.

Gives WAY TOO MANY HOMEWORK that does not match the exam. Homeworks are graded harshly. Gives study guide for exams that do not match the exam too. The course is designed for people who were already good with Calc, take him if you wanna fail.

Ciotti is many things but he is not a good professor. He assigns about 60 problems for hw each week - 20 question hw's for each lecture, 3x a week, plus an additional harder written hw. Does not care about his students learning OR passing, first midterm: 54%. This is 10C, not rocket science. Wouldn't recommend, 0/10.

Professor Ciotti is a very nice guy and I feel like his lectures helped me learn and understand the material a lot. However, this is the hardest class I have ever taken. There were about 3 homework assignments a week, and the midterms were only three questions. Textbook is free, and the curve is very lenient, but overall a very difficult class.

Never struggled so much in a math class I was drowning in homework. 2 or 3 online hw's a week as well as strenuous written hw once a week, which would take forever. None applied. That exams had difficult problems that were nothing like hw. Lectures covered easy ex's and didn't explain well. The median score never was over 55% but bless the curve.

Dr. Servin really cares for her students and always responds to emails. She invited a couple of guest speakers from diverse backgrounds to share their professional journey. I really appreciated when she invited a nurse, given I was applying for nursing school after graduation and it helped me.

Professor Servin is disorganized and fails to provide clear assignment instructions, which results in low grades or criticism for a lack of effort. She does not always respond to messages which is inconvenient given that we only meet once a week for class. Lots of group work, so be with people who you trust and are good communicators.
Yucheng is definitely one of my favorite professors at UCSD. His lectures are amazing and there is not much homework. Exams are graded heavily. Unfortunately he's not teaching at UCSD anymore :(
One of the easiest professors at UCSD.

Repetitive and boring lectures that didn't explain many of the insanely difficult homework problems assigned which were graded for accuracy. Midterm 1 was easy, but midterm 2 and the final were quite difficult. However, there was a generous curve at the end. I recommend Prof. Leonard on Youtube & Paul's Online Notes to supplement understanding.
His lectures are overall easy to follow, but not clearly explained sometimes. In order to do well on the exams, prepare to spend extra time understanding course materials REALLY WELL.

Lectures were repetitive and didn't teach much, but he makes his exams easy/curves to make up for it. Homework was extremely difficult to do without reading the textbook/asking for help in OH or checking answers with friends because it is graded on accuracy. Final exam was difficult but there was a bonus question that was EC. Overall easy A.
Good at explaining difficult topics.

Absolutely amazing class. Hwang is very thorough during lectures and fun projects for people who are interested in aerospace fields. Homework is definitely a challenge sometimes but he provides all the necessary equations needed to complete everything. Very enjoyable and hope to have him in more upper-division courses.

I loved this class, the only thing I was looking forward to every Tuesday and Thursday. For an "intro class", the concepts are very difficult, one of the TAs mentioning a concept we were learning was usually introduced on your 4th year. Despite this, he is very effective in explaining and clarifying everything. Super chill class, would take again.

The content for this class was quite difficult especially for it being a "Intro" course but it was still very interesting but exams were hard. The projects for this class were fun but one is a group project with randomly assigned group members so its something to be aware of. Overall this class was very difficult but I really enjoyed it.

PSY 569 Professor Sereno is a really sweet guy but not very good at explaining the material. If you are a psy major and don't have a math background... do not take this class. The prerequisites should be set way higher and it's impossible to learn the material if you haven't had exposure to coding or higher level math.
I find Sereno inspirational, and I love his eccentricity! He is teaching me in London now, and is still writing on his chalkboard so binoculars are recommended.

Smart guy, bad at teaching.  Random concepts here and there- not really learn anything.  Insists on only writing on the chalkboard.  No powerpoint.  Result: no permanent record of anything.  TA Flavia is awesome.  Get her for section.  Honestly, I think she should teach the class.  Test: always a 53% but curved.  GO TO LECTURE.
No Comments

I thought Dr. Sereno presented the material in a very clear manner. He would always bring up random tidbits that made the class more interesting. The exams were representative of the material he presented. This was my favorite neuroscience class.

Megan is wickedly intelligent and I felt lucky that she was my instructor. She made sure to meet individually with students because she really cared how everyone was doing. I hope that in the future Megan will be teaching other courses, leading seminars, and having workshops - specifically I would like to learn more about her background in poetry!

Megan is awesome, she has the most welcoming energy and cares for you individually. The work was manageable, no tests or quizzes mainly writing a paragraph or two. She made the content interesting and encouraged lots of insightful conversations. The class size is small so be ready to participate. If Megan taught other classes I would take them too!

It's important to know that whichever prof. you get for this class, they don't decide the workload, so don't blame all the assignments on them. Megan understood that at some points it was a lot of work and tried to help us destress. She gives great feedback on your work and tries to make class fun & helpful. I recommend taking her class for sure.

AWP 1, is not a class anyone wants to take lets be real. But she's the nicest person ever. She makes class a little more interesting and explains the readings thoroughly. Has tons of office hours and is soo much help! Take her class!

AWP1 is a really interesting class, but Ms. Haugh makes it even more interesting with amazing discussions and questions that makes everyone want to participate in the discussion. She gives really good feedback on your essays and is helful with your writing. 100% take her class.

Took Prof. Talley for a seminar course and while she tried to make the class inspirational, it could be dry at times as well. Prof. Talley brought guest speakers in weekly and we went on field trips as well. Overall, nice lady and not much work.

Lectures were very difficult to understand and there were very little practice problems that had similar wording to the homework, midterm, and final. Overall, just choose another professor or else you will be teaching yourself a lot of the material.
If there are other teachers please take them instead. I had a hard time learning from her.

I don't even know what happened this quarter. Please take a different professor, she didn't give us anything to practice with, besides a two page practice sheet. Unorganized lectures that are vague and confusing.

Tests were apparently significantly harder than other professors after asking friends taking the exact same class, and others that took this professor as well. Mean and median for midterm 1 was 16/30 (55%) without a curve. For a lower div class this is terrible. Lectures swap between in-person and online, and overall pacing for the class is weird.

This is for MUSC-132. Professor Nestor is not only the best COD play at the university but he is also the nicest and most caring professor I have had all semester. I would totally take another one of his classes if I had to. Course material is super interesting and engaging. Come to class with questions or topics to talk about.
He gives very little homework, is really funny and down to earth, and overall a great professor! Would definitely take him again!
He is a good professor. To get an A in class, just memorize the PPTs! It is worth to go to his lectures: he is humorous.

Very easy and straightforward class. Lecture isn't mandatory but recommended if you want a better grasp on the material. Tests were simple multiple choice and true/false questions on the lectures and the listening material. Personally, the material wasn't my cup of tea but his lectures made it engaging.

An absolute sweetheart; probably the nicest person at UCSD and the easiest class in your life. He gives extra credit opportunities (attending concerts!) final is NOT cumulative, very few assignments, and if you go to office hours he offers to buy you coffee/snacks! very approachable and funny. Also very attractive in a scholarly way.

He gave NO homework at all, which means your grade is calculated based on 2 midterms and 1 final only. The average score of the class is below 50. However he is very accessible cuz he holds multiple help sessions online where you could work through whatever you want. Read the textbook and do the practice problems and put in the effort!
great!

this guy sucks. doesn't know how to teach. I learned better teaching my self. talks for the whole class. example after example. do not take him. Everyone in my class talks about how confusing and awful of a teacher he is. people only get good grades in this class because they study on their own. Peter smith is terrible and he should honestly quit.

peter super knowledgeable and passionate about latin america. reading heavy class. no other work required ideally, dont need to read book. but recommend really reading book because the lecture slides are very brief. gives study guides for tests. one midterm and one final. provides a paper option to boost grade grading of test based on TA.

Lecture, no podcast, grade based on 1 paper and 1 final.  His love for the subject is admirable. I honestly thoroughly enjoyed his self written textbook.  Attendance is not hugely important as long as you read everything.  I would take one of his classes again.

one midterm with short essay format. final includes short essays and long essays. do the optional paper, helps your grade. the study guides basically outline what are on the tests. dont need to memorize so much, class is more about synthesizing. interesting class, even though he can be boring at times.

lectures are kind of boring but he definitely knows his stuff. you really need to pay attention because most of the info on his slides is vague. gives study guides for final and midterm that are VERY helpful. i didn't read much of the book and got an A- because his tests are not based on knowing all the history, just being able to make connections.
his lecture notes were" of a quality ummacthed by any textbooks". Turned a complex analysis course to an algebra course :)

Came here to give a chili pepper but ultimately Prof Novak is an amazing teacher that anyone interested in math should have a chance to learn from. He's inspired by math and treats it like a philosophic discipline which I really appreciated it. He expects his students to take the subject seriously but is very reasonable and very helpful. Recommend.

Curriculum taught very slow; many crucial topics omitted.
"Lectures" were glorified blog posts that imparted very little, insulting towards tuition-paying tritons.
Homework, tests were routine; results were immediate from lectures; learnt nothing.
Worst of all, the cutoff for an A was made 95%, after he realized he made the class too easy.

Professor Novak is a great lecturer. He taught every concept in a clear way with lots of examples. However, his lecture posts contain lots of mistakes. He discusses solution to homework prior to the due (Homework is worth 50% of the grade). Using latex get 5% bonus on test and HW. The class is much easier compare to MATH 31 AH.
an absolute legend. made one of the hardest classes i've ever taken into a fun experience.

Take him if you ever get the chance. He is very passionate about what he teaches and tries to tie in his teachings to what's happening in the world right now. There is a bit of reading but it's all interesting. So far he had one big essay for the midterm but he isnt super super hard. He's one of those professors you'll want to put the work in for.

She was great. The workbooks are meh and she can go fast sometimes but she really cares about the material. She doesnt curve the class but she gives very straightforward quizzes so its not that hard to get a good grade in the class. Overall, lectures were great and the class was by no means difficult idk why people didnt like the class.

Not the best professor I've had. Teaching style is not beneficial unless you have extra time to get help. She makes us use a workbook but does not provide answers unless you go to her office hours. Lectures are fairly difficult to follow, especially when she confuses herself while teaching. Tests are workbook heavy.

The reviews on RMP as well as on CAPEs got me worried for her class, but honestly this was one of my easiest classes this quarter because prof Coil broke things down extremely well during the lectures. Her quizzes and exam were definitely reflective of her lecture, hw, and workbook question. TA Marco was amazing! Prof and Marco were a great team!

Took this class with no Physics background and limited math skills (I hate math!). I passed the class. It was time consuming and the book is dense. Must go to class to really make sense of things. Dr. Coil is always willing to help. Just ask for help. Many concepts and things you must know not memorize, but really know. If I can pass, so can you.

I was anxious about taking Coil based on earlier reviews, but she was really great after all. This quarter she synced her class with Tsai and Paddock so they were all essentially the same. In my opinion, having taken all three of them, she's the best lecturer. She also does not have mandatory lectures and helps students with problems during class.
pretty fun and enjoyable

Anyone who tells you that 105A is a fun class is lying, it is extremely difficult and probably the hardest class I ever took in my life. He lectures with the assumption that you already know all the math which sucks because most students don't. Homework is insanely hard, don't think you can finish without TA help. Easily spend 10+ hours/week on HW.
Great teacher! Fun class!
He is a very good professor. His homeworks were very difficult and time consuming (7-10 hours a week). If you go to his OH, he will explain things further.
Freshman seminar about movie physics is awesome. Very laid back and entertaining.

The course is very informative. Helps with understanding planning and designing an embedded system. 
I liked how we covered a broad range of topics involving hardware design and got to use several EDA tools. 
Really liked how the instructor did the feed back for all the assignments and quizzez.
I enjoyed the mix of circuit analysis and learning Kicad. This course provided high relation between course content and the skills i was searching to acquire.

Very knowledgeable professor in embedded systems. Explained everything clearly and thoroughly and with great detail. Very responsive to emails and questions. Helps greatly to understand the design of an embedded system. I really enjoyed having Kolesnichenko as my professor.

This instructor is teaching one of required courses for us to get a certificate. But his class is not so valuable to pay that much money frankly. and he does not check email regularly so sometimes reponds after assignment due day passes or ignore it. Avoid his class. Moreover, school doesn't care about any student's feedback about courses.

Don't waste your time to take his class. He is not helping any students. even posting questions on discussion board, not checking regularly or no feedback. he has office hours (once a week) although asking on email at that days, not respond later. every homework he has his own same feedback without pointing it out how to correct exactly.

Prof was a good teacher, the classes were just VERY long and VERY boring... the readings were okay, but the discussions and critiques in class were very very long and awkward and boring. Get ready to feel like UCSD is wasting your money and time in her classes.
Professor Nakayama is really good at critique and always listen to student's ideas

Lecture was boring and homework were not talked about during lectures. He was co-teaching with Keith Muller, another one-of-the-worst CS Professor, and the class was just a disaster. It was a low-division course so it was supposed to be fun and entertaining and inspiring --- and they failed to do make us feel that way.

Never take Chin. Avoid him at all costs. He changes grading rubric weeks after. He has incorrect quiz answers and PENALIZES students even when they've been pointed out. Lectures are a waste of time unless you want to lose brain cells. It feels like he doesn't even know the material himself.

Dr. Bristol does a really great job in her lectures. She provides notes and materials for you to study that actually make sense. Very HARD professor with LOTS of homework, TOUGH grading, and BORING class. The kind of professor that will make you hate chemistry. Don't take him.

she definitely does not care about students, she can cause you of anything if she wants to, very bad communication, she needs work on her attitude and the level of offensiveness she puts out, overall, very unfair and rude.

Legendary. Absolutely recommended to every student.

Ivano is a great professor, though he doesn't usually teach syntax.  I also took semantics with him last year.  He's a good lecturer and he mixes humor in when appropriate. Took Santamaria for Econ 103 and enjoyed it. He was very nice and pretty funny.

Took Santamaria in Econ 103 this sem and will have him Econ 105 next sem with him. He was awesome, his lecture were good but you could also just read the notes and you would be ready for midterm and final. He is very funny and very nice!

Just finished writing the final exam. Martin is overall a good person. He cares, he's humble for a person of his position, and he can teach very well. We miss you Mr. Swift

Test are extremely fair, but definitely require good understanding of the material. Interested and genuinely cares about students' learning. Professor Swift is an awesome professor. His lectures are very clear and structured. He makes skeletons of the PowerPoints so you can take notes and also does podcasts. There is weekly homework via Sapling but nothing major.
Very passionate professor. There are weekly discussion posts and a decent amount of reading, but overall the material is interesting enough to be okay wIth readings.

Professor Jones is a wonderful man and likes what he teaches. He does tend to use heavy vocab so I ended up not understanding what he says but he is very helpful if you have questions. Really great professor. Lectures are short but informative. Took several Magagna classes and learnt a lot! RIP

Rest in peace, Professor Magagna! He undoubtedly made my undergraduate experience during the COVID-19 memorable with his softly-graded papers and charm during his lectures. The Political Science Department at UC San Diego and its respective alumni will miss you dearly.
He is really intelligent and he knows a lot about the subject matter--I found the information I was learning to be incredibly fascinating, and I wish I could take more of his classes.

So easy. I went to 0 lectures. Just two papers, and prompts are provided at the start of the quarter. Just ctrl+F the textbooks and skim lecture notes and the papers will take you an hour MAX to write.
Fantastic professor, really enjoyable lectures. Look forward to taking him again.

Professor Zheng is really passionate about the material he's teaching. He is flexible about exams and homework, and are graded fairly. He made the concepts clear and consist to understand.

This class was almost appallingly easy. Professor Zheng has a very thick accent, but his lecture notes are always posted and simple to understand. Start on the homework early. The tests were really easy and exactly like the practice tests. Only like 4 questions on each midterm! Hw was easy too.

TAKE Professor Zheng 's class! He is really passionate about teaching and tries his best to answer all the questions. Ok SO he was not the clearest lecturer and the lack of solution keys was really annoying, but if you put in the time to self-study it pays off. Professor Shields is very understanding with her students. Grades are based on weekly quizzes and assignments. Assignments are short and based on effort rather than correctness. Quizzes were straightforward and based on lectures. Super interesting and enjoyable class!
He was solid, needs to improve outline of class and lab. but he is very understanding and nice. lots of group projects and lab class was very fun

One of the best professors i have had for a class. He is very passionate about his teaching and the class was very interesting. if you paid attention in the lectures you would have no problem passing the class. I would definitely love to be taught by him again.

Course material is the foundation you will need for many other courses later on, so he goes above and beyond to ensure that you fully understand the concepts. so the pr may be nice but everything entirely depends on your TA, the homework are really heavy and require a great amount of time spent on them. i would hear my peer talk about them getting 97 on a homework while highest in my class would be an 84 for the same amount of work done, so just pray that you get a good and easy grader TA.

Dr. G is super cool and clearly knowledgable on the material. Overall this was an easy class. It seems like he has the same few TA's every quarter, and they are amazing. Professor Galderisi clearly knows his material and is a competent lecturer. Great Professor. Explains concepts clearly and comes to class well-prepared. Exams are fair as long as you do the homework problems and practice exams. Responds to Piazza questions promptly. I LOVE THIS PROFESSOR, continue taking his 102 this quater

Professor Hodges is caring. His lectures are overall clear with lots of concept examples. Homeworks are questions in textbook, and difficulty is acceptable. Not a math major but I was way more confident moving forward after 20A with him. I did super well in 20B and C after taking his course. It was really hard but I think it's a mistake to avoid him if you want a solid foundation. He has review sessions and doesn't throw curveballs on his exams.

He does NOT care about his students, takes his lecture material straight from a textbook, doesn't explain notation/concepts in depth, absolutely refused to provide ANY practice material, told us that we wouldn't understand anything at first, but always insists that the material is "trivial" and "simple".

THIS GUY DOES NOT CARE ABOUT STUDENTS!!! Spends all his time trying to teach his class math. Go to another class so you can get an easy A and spend less time on it. And what is the point of numerical linear algebra anyway!?! Is not like it ever gets used in the real world!
Great teacher and goes the extra mile to help you out

I took his class through Ashford U, online, and so far, he has been the best. Responded to every student's discussion posts, gave excellent critical feedback and showed a sincere desire to help his students not only become good writers but to enjoy it and fall in love with it as much as he is.
Amazingly friendly and wants to talk to you. Really hot in that rock star/ slightly nerdy way- pretty freaking adorable. He is really enthusiastic when he reads poetry, too. = )
Amazing prof, he's a real person and not aloof.  I could never get into poetry before his class, now I love it.  Show up, be enthusiastic about the work, get an A.
Prof. Meetze has made me a lifetime lover of poetry and all things poetic. I thought I hated poetry before taking his class and now I can't stop writing.

Her lectures are really good and straightforward. She promotes a lot of discussion in her class since it involves climate change. Her homework and tests were pretty easy. Overall, the class itself is pretty easy.
Really nice professor and makes lecture very entertaining! Explains topics very well and has a good grasp of the  material.

She's a very caring professor who's passionate about her field! Workload is very light: read an article and write your thoughts on it. Prof. Teranes makes lectures engaging by connecting the articles to ESYS ideas and real world issues. Discussion sections help with meeting new people and further understanding those issues. Def take her if you can.

Easy class, just show up and you'll be good. She is super caring and explains topics really well and will not make it boring. The class is mostly based on group work and outside readings. Homework is just a few questions about the lecture and you have a week to do it. It's a breeze and she is such a great professor!
She's very straight forward and kind! It's such an eye-opening class and she makes the topics very interesting. Just do the work and you will do well!

I find Prof Higgins a very nice professor. He is super helpful. Usually someone ask a difficult question in the homework, he will talk about it in the next lecture. Have a couple of chats with him after the lecture and he answered a lot of my questions.
HARD HW HARD EXAM. Final curve is not bad though.
Professor Higgins is generous in giving a good grade. I don't think my effort on this quarter is worth an A but he gives a nice curved.

The curve at the end does not make up for the shoddy teaching job (I was at 68% before the curve to a B-). All of the 1 star reviews are correct. It's hard to find outside resources to study this material, and this is such an important class... I don't feel confident going into 140A, and I wish I could go back in time and pick a different prof.

Pros: nice to talk to, accessible outside class, does hw problems during OH, knowledgeable, answers questions well, curved class at the end, gave practice questions where a few were in exam. Cons: very difficult hw, difficult midterms, difficult final, refused to let the class know if he was going to curve - average was 55% for both midterms.

If you want an extremely easy class that's engaging, take it with Dr. Purrity! She is super chill yet is full of so much knowledge and keeps her class engaged. Truly a professor that everyone admires.
Very funny and educated professor. I would highly recommend Professor Puritty! She is one of the most knowledgable professors I've met and kept the class highly engaged.

As any CAT class, grading depends on the TA. Most assignments were P/NP so were easy. She never taught CAT before so was pretty unprepared for this class but nonetheless did fine imo. Final is a presentation which was online for my class but would have been memorized and in front of section if we were in person.

Her class was very fun and engaging. She really cares about her students mental health and has a obvious passion for environmental science. It was a really easy class and very enjoyable. I really recommend her as a professor.

Dr. Puritty is awesome. Super easy to do well in the class, but also really learned a lot. Class is what you make of it. Lectures are optional, but even at the end of the quarter a lot of people still showed up. She really is that interesting and engaging of a person. Also, discussion sections don't meet at all which is nice. Awesome class, TAKE IT
Professor Ackerman is great! I sincerely enjoyed his lectures and he's also truly passionate about the course content. All the readings in this class are worth a read.
Great prof, but a lot of reading that overlaps with other classes (like MMW, Philosophy, and the sort).

Ackerman is a very intelligent man. The topics he touches on are intriguing and always leave me wanting to know more. The grading criteria is straightforward; if you do the readings, complete the weekly homework assignments and attend class then you will pass. However, the hw does require a lot of careful contemplation. You will learn a LOT.

Ackerman barely lectured during this class (maybe 3 times the whole quarter), but when he did it was very heavy material. The class itself is pretty easy. Readings are optional and the homeworks (due once a week) are pretty straight forward. The content of HDS 1 is also very interesting, so guest lectures are engaging.

Professor Ackerman is at times funny and has a sense of humor. The class is mainly comprised of guests' lectures. He lectures, but it is rare. There are 7 homework assignments consist of questions mainly from the lectures. One midterm and an accumulative final. Go to the TAs' office hours  because they are mostly the ones that make the exam.

The course was overall very interesting. Dr. Gambel was caring and also very good at explaining concepts. I took this course online and all the lectures are recorded, discussion was not required. I was residing in a different time zone so she did allow me to take the live quizzes she had at an alternative time.

Dr. G made BILD3 super easy. She used lectures from a previous quarter (the sound quality is bad but not as bad as people say). Every week she posted lecture videos, two MC questions for each (unlimited attempts), and learning objectives (answer one for credit). There were 4 quizzes, all MC, lowest score dropped. Final was a short quiz. Lots of EC.

Professor Gambel is a really caring professor and her class was very organized. we had lots of easy points from lecture quizzes, weekly learning objectives, and she had a lot of opportunities for extra credit! if you pay attention to her lectures and take detailed notes, then you're good to go for the biweekly quizzes. i definitely recommend her!
Professor Gambel is amazing. She makes the class very interesting and engaging. Lectures are clear and easy to understand. Professor is clearly passionate and knowledgable about the material!

Dr. Gambel is a very caring and chill professor. Her class is structured so well that made this class my least stressful. Material isnt hard and biweekly quizzes are basically on the lecture. Gives lots of extra credit and overall would 100% recommend to anyone. One minor thing is that her lectures are a bit long/boring and some noise, but its ok.

Interesting lecture style, pretty chill class. 3 essays total, 4 pages each. Grade depends on TA so go to them for specific writing feedback. Lots of reading but I did it last minute and did fine. Overall liked the course, material was interesting and her storytelling-esque lecture style was refreshing!

(+): Engaging storytelling lectures, kind, respectful, primary sources that she chose. 
(-): Essay turnaround times are a bit tough but manageable. 

Tip: Midterm is based on lectures. Papers and Final were based on the readings. If you familiarize yourself with the readings from a big picture POV, then you are good. Go to TA OH if you are stuck.
take this class for p/np since I am not good at humanities. Lots of reading and there are 4 papers. Good professor and engaging lectures.
Professor Klein was a very reasonable professor. She doesn't even require all of the stupid discussion stuff. She's really reasonable and kind and 10/10 recommend.

Readings were mandatory, since we had essays on the books we read and midterms were based on textbook readings/lecture notes so lots of reading and writing. we had weekly quizzes about the books we were reading. if you took at least 8 quizzes and averaged 80%, she gave 2% extra credit to your overall grade. very kind and caring professor :)

Lectures are ok, not not great. Lots of HW but he lets you resubmit for 80% max credit. Class is graded by Units ie Ch12-13 would be Unit 1,There are 6 units he lets you redue units during the 2nd midterm and final for higher grades. Just make sure to go to office hours for help and take advantage of the redue and you should pass.

He makes me wonder if this class's prereq is only Math 10A. The material amount is insane and the practice quizzes and HW doesn't prepare you to get over 90 in the real quiz. Need to spend hours to understand what he wrote on the slides because it's all symbols without a whole bunch of examples. Really bad experience in general.
Prior to him, this class is an easy A now he made it 10 times more difficult just please avoid him if you are looking for access to anywhere other than being a Ph.D. cuz he will funk your GPA up

Taking him for 103b currently. I got A+ in 103A, but still find his lectures hard and too fast. He ended up covering all mt material 1 week ahead. Hws are somewhat hard. His grading systems were ... unique. He has no practice mt, and his mt does not allow cheatsheet. His style was not standard and don't take him if you do not like stress.
Best Math Prof at UCSD. Exceptionally clear, helpful, homework is fun and exams are tough but fair. Charming guy, and very clever. Please tenure him, Academia gods.

The problem with this class is that there is no structure, and she is very disorganized. Also, this class is SO BORING, and makes you feel like you are in a grade school class. The worst class of my UCSD career. Overall, not that difficult . But she has a 10 page (2500 word) due during finals. Only take if it is your only option for a requirement.

She is the worst professor I ever have, she is professional in her field but she dont know how to teach. 2 long papers will make up 75% of course grade. She and her TA's are the toughest grader I ever seen, with a average C on 1st paper. Her lectures are usless due to 50% of them are guest lectures. Do yourself a favor and AVOID this terrible prof!

Dr. FM is a lovely person! Her class is truly impossible.Grade is based on two 12 page papers and the TAs and professor grade incredibly hard. Feedback is given late, which makes it hard to improve final papers. Rubric is given, but it is vague. Lectures didn’t mention how to complete papers correctly even though that’s all we are graded on.

VERY work intensive and time consuming class but doable. Most of your grade is based on 2 12 page papers but she gives you rubrics ahead of time and 25% of the total class grade is based on revising and resubmitting your 1st paper. She gives a no questions asked 3 day extension and another 3 day extension for going to the writing hub.

2 full 12-page engagement papers that will make up 70% of the whole course grade. She is an extremely tough grader with an average of 78% of the first paper, with even poor and late feedback or comments. Her lectures are awful and she hardly ever mentioned the assignments or papers, 50% of her lectures are guest lectures. AVOID this professor!!NMSL

This class wasn't hard but it was unnecessarily time-consuming when it came to the final project which is developing a website. Lectures are prerecorded and I didn't watch a single one. This class is the definition of yet another bogus required GE that students have to waste their time taking. Thanks, UCSD!

I get the impression that he really cares about his students. Lots of lectures but at least they were fun. Assignments were fun, actually useful, and had clear grading criteria. Required reading wasn't that useful, but at least it's free. Overall, I highly recommend him he's the best CAT professor I've had at UCSD!

Professor Sinitsyn may be a great professor IN-PERSON. However, online he is the devil incarnate or at least his exams are it seems. Trying to take an ECON test through Canvas while showing your work online is terrible. Not to mention he isn't clear about the curve at all. Take him IN-PERSON or don't take him at all.

Professor Sinitsyn is the best econ professor I met at UCSD. He clearly explains everything in class! The only thing you need to do is just follow him and do the problem set. The exam is not hard, trust me! There are plenty of econ major students who are poor at math, that's why they can't do well in exams.

Professor Sinitsyn does a great job, in my opinion, with teaching Econ 100A. If you work through all of the practice problems he gives out and understand how to solve each one (he always posts the answers before the exam), the tests are more than fair. There's a pretty consistent curve on each exam so don't fret about not getting 100%.

I don't know how he has such a high rating. He teaches his lectures as if you are already an expert on the topic. When doing examples, he goes straight into the hardest example possible and skips massive steps to get to the answer quickly. Extremely hard to follow along with. You better have time to study outside of class to teach yourself.

Sinitsyn is a hard professor, but if you take the time to practice the concepts in lectures and go to discussions, you can do well in his class. Although attendance isn't mandatory, I highly recommend going. His curves for the tests are super nice, as long as you pass them. This class is a lot of work.

Professor Rosas is a great Spanish teacher and exactly who you'd want for a small class size like LISP1D. He encourages participation and helps you if you aren't too good, and grades fairly easily on the exams and conversations. There is a lot of homework, about 3 assignments every week, but they aren't particularly difficult.
He is my favorite Spanish teacher at UCSD! He is funny and nice, and makes learning a new language less intimidating.

Pretty normal professor, attendance is mandatory and most of class is spent reading the textbook and doing activities in break out rooms. Easy class to pass, if you put in some work an A is achievable

Fun and unique class, students give lectures to the class, with input/corrections from professor Yu. If you read thoroughly and participate in class, you will learn a lot. The only downside is that the class is very general and does not go into much depth.

Taught the first 2 weeks, then has students volunteer to make slides and teach the class weeks 3-10. Doesn't even try to help w that process either, and makes the TAs coach the students and review their slides beforehand. We read a chapter of the textbook each week and do literally nothing else. Overall awful course experience.

In week 1, the prof asked for volunteers to teach the lectures for extra credits . She let those students chose which topics they wanted to cover right away, which means most of them didn't even know the materials when choosing the topics. In general, the quality of lectures depends on how well the volunteers understand the material, not the prof.

This class was basically students teaching themselves. The professor did not give any lecture, made the students give presentations instead. This type of class structure is not really helpful for topics taught in this class as most of it is pretty new to everyone (decision making in the brain) and includes a bunch of economics that needs a Prof.
Guest lectures with quizzes each section and 3 midterms. No finals! Just study the lecture content, you will ace it!

He waited until the final week to tell us that he uses a "standard scheme" with a 95 or above for A. His lecture slides are ok but as a young professor, he still needs more teaching experience. The TA's for this quarter are pretty mean, especially after we fill out capes!
He curves his grading scale UP, are you kidding me man!!!???
Great guy. HW not bad as long as you review lecture.
Blazes through lectures and very hard to understand. Be prepared to spend tuition on YouTube university.
Very hard to understand

Professor Elgin is very knowledgeable about his course material. His lectures can get kind of boring at times, but his slides are easy to follow. He releases the lecture slides ahead of time too, so I suggest taking notes before going to lecture. The hardest part of this class is keeping up with the readings, but other than that it's pretty chill.

Theres no hate for prof elgin, he was cool and interactive but he cant help how freaking boring this class is. Its only based on two essays, final exam and discussion participation. I havent done any of the readings or really gone to class and i did good on the essays still. better than some warren profs ive had

The basic professor. Super vanilla. His teaching is okay, tests are okay but a bit long, tries to stay positive even when things are pretty gloomy. Definitely knowledgeable about his subject matter. I feel like if I did not already take an ethics class before this, I would have not understood everything. But for the most part he is just fine.

Essays are about 6-8 pages long, the TA's grade very fairly, averages are pretty high (90%). Very effective at explaining things, you can probably get away with not going to lecture and just doing your papers on the readings. But Discussions are required.

If you have her as your professor, ensure you keep up with the work b/c if you procrastinate, you will fall behind and FAST. She is very uninvolved. She only does examples of problems in lectures and doesn't explain them very well. She requires us to read the math textbook, which is ridiculous b/c she should be teaching us not us teaching ourselves

Hands down one of the best professors. She is very understandable though there is a tedious amount of homework (readings, worksheets, hw problems). These assignments tend to be very easy and balance out the exams which look identical to her study guides. Overall, would highly recommend

Annie Carter is a really good professor, the way she explains things is really clear and good. I had her last quarter and her TA Thomas Valles was really good too. I liked her class a lot. You have to put in work and study in order to do well but it's feasible especially if you utilize the TA discussions.

Prof Carter really teaches at her students' pace. During lectures she answers pretty much every single question, posts her notes online, etc. Discussion worksheets are difficult but graded by completion; homework can be long at times. Actual exams are pretty much the exact same as her practice exams. I've heard she's really helpful during OH too!

Professor Carter is very good lecturer. She breaks everything down and proves every concept. There is weekly homework and multiple reading/annotation assignments, but these are both easy points. This quarter specifically, the study exams were very similar to the real exams so learn how to do these problems correctly. This may change for in person.

She doesn't know how to teach beginners, yells very easily, has made some questionable comments to international kids about how she's speaking English, and the class is structured poorly. She shows up 30 mins late and doesn't have a plan half the time. I didn't I learned any actual dance moves either, just one choreo. I'd take another class tbh.

Honestly I was scared of taking a dance class because I cant dance to save my life! Also, Professer Foster-King took out a lot of time to make sure I didnt fall behind. She is the funniest teacher I have ever had especially when she starts telling her stories��!

West African Dance was arguably one of the best classes Ive ever taken at UCSD, and Dr. Foster-King is one of the best instructors one could hope for. Her expectations are reasonable, her class is fun, and the drummers are some of the nicest people on earth as well, and Id give them great reviews too if it were possible!

This class was way too much work and way too little dancing for what should have been an easy-A dance class. Grade was based on attendance, group projects, self-choreographed final, and scrapbook/notebook. I was placed with a very unmotivated group so I definitely had to work for my grade. More of an African culture class than a dance class.

Sandra is amazing! Love West African Dance now. The class is an absolute blast. You will laugh alot in this class (at yourself and others). Only one midterm routine and short presentation on WA country, create final routine choreography and turn in a collage. Easy A, just stay on the beat and smile, create a decent final and turn in your reports.

This was my first course with Professor Scott and he has exceeded my expectations for a what I would consider a great professor. He is very caring, supportive, and understanding and is truly passionate about what he teaches. He answered every question with ease while also expanding on the subject to further our learning. I would 100% recommend him!

TAKE THIS PROF! YOU WONT REGRET IT. He is hilarious and his lectures are super entertaining- it feels like watching a cool youtube video about robots. He obviously cares so much about his students, and does everything he can so that we get the best grade possible and learn a lot. He also gave over 4% extra credit, which is insanely nice of him.

Easily one of my favorite professors and classes I've taken! Super engaging content, assignments and coursework are very reasonable and manageable, and pretty fair grading all around. Professor Scott makes the lectures very entertaining and interesting - just a genuinely kind and funny guy. Would highly recommend!

Best professor at UCSD. An icon. easy class with straightforward quizzes, interesting and relevant topics. He lets you vote for what topics you want to talk about. very very understanding and easy to access outside of class. i love this man.

I haven't yet finished this course, but I can definitely say that this professor has been one of my favorites at UCSD. Not only is Professor Scott very personable and funny, but he also gives amazing and easy to follow lectures. I am not one to really ever attend lectures, but even though it isn't mandatory in this class I still look forward to it.

He is awesome. The kindest, most passionate professor I have ever had. He's clearly invested in anthropology in all aspects and really makes you appreciate it more. Honestly, he's the model professor. Anything less than a 5/5 stars is criminal for him.
Incredible professor, very interesting class. 10/10.

I took this class during the spring semester online, it was the best class I took. He has great discussions during class, readings. Its NOT like these boring classes that you stared to the computer, and learned nothing. I would definitely take this class again.

Wow. Never let an opportunity like this pass. You will surely regret not taking Professor Berman. He connects with the students in a way that impassions people to identify with the material. In his class, you leave your identity as a student and are fully respected as a multidimensional human being. He has the biggest heart and breadth of knowledge

A really cool professor. The class is can be discussion orientated, but you don't have to participate. You should attend lectures, it's good for your grade and is pretty fun. He'll go on about his ventures during his research or some cool video relating to Anth and those are the highlights of the class. You could probably pass without reading too.

This class was literally so hard & time consuming. There were so many assignments,  it took me at least 10 hours every single week. Instructions were never ever clear, we always had to ask so many clarification questions. If you don't need this class for your major, take another lab. This was my bio lab elective and I regret it so much.

Cons: her instructions on assignments are always vague and hard to follow and she sort of expects you to already know a lot of material that you just have no way of already knowing PLUS there's SO. MUCH. HW. in this class. SO SO MUCH!!!!! pros: she is very sweet and caring, always available to help, unbelievably intelligent, flexible with deadlines

I admit she gives a ton of busy work that takes up a lot of your time every week. This class probably requires more time than anything else youve taken before. But she is more than generous with grades and is always available to help you succeed. I was very overwhelmed at first, but just go to office hours and do your best youll be fine. No exams!

Shes such a nice person but she expects so much work from you its insane this class by itself should be enough for an entire quarter dont count on working or taking any other classes with this class you will regret it if you do cause you have to work on its material all day everyday. But she is sweet, accessible, and generous. Just expects a lot
Very nice and caring. I took this class as a GE and it was a breeze. She made the topics interesting but even then, the coursework and the quizzes were really easy. Loved it.

Shes really kind & passionate with clear pronunciation! Its very enjoyable to listen to her lectures. Materials and notes are well organized. Hw are less, tests are open notes. Youll learn a lot about classical music with a decent grade using bare effort and time! Prior music knowledge is definitely helpful but not necessary.

Lydia is the BEST!! This was my favorite course in the 33 series because of her. She's engaging, kind, and picks out very interesting material and homework ideas for the course. Plus, when our final concert had to be postponed, she fought really hard for it to be rescheduled! I greatly enjoyed working with her and would take anything she taught.

Took this class during COVID. Biweekly reflections that take an hour or so. A midterm that is going to take you a couple of hours to do, and a super time-consuming final that honestly got in the way of my other finals. Easy A but be prepared to actually do work for the midterm and final.

Easy A, but definitely a lot more work than I would've liked given that it was just a GE for me. Weekly writing assignments, gotta keep up with lectures, and a super-grind of a midterm and final. Although you have a week or so total to write and submit your mid and final, they are actual grinds. Writing, writing, writing. She's nice though. Yeah.

The professor himself is a good person, but his quizzes and hw are hard which you would put a significant amount on hw every week. The quiz only contains one proof question, so either you get full credit or a really bad grade. He curves all grades after finals.

Professor Zucker is a gem. He is one of the better professors and he teaches + lectures clearly. Always available during office hours, he explains things well and if you work hard, the curve falls in your favor. ;)

This course is the 1st that he taught in person at UCSD, and I can positively say that his lecturing style is superb in person, but would suck through Zoom, which explains a lot of the bad ratings. Spend some time going over the lecture notes yourself, since the course material can be abstract and can't be absorbed right away during lecture.
He's basically a human textbook. Grading is rough. The quiz average was like a D or so without the curve.
Lectures felt like he was just reading the textbook. Homework and examples did not match the degree of difficulty of the quizzes.

No regard for the students whatsoever. Makes lecture attendance mandatory through clicker credit with at least 70% participation, but 1/4 of his lectures have no clicker question, and 1/2 have one or two clicker questions with about a 5-10 sec gap to answer. So if you happen to miss it, no credit that day. Also had a quiz on the last day of week 10

I was scared of physics because i had bad teachers before. He is very good and funny. He gives some trick question but its the nature of physics. Not very hard quizzes. no exam. final 30 questions some from old quizzes. He explained things very simple to understand. I learned and remember things he taught still. Take him.

This professor often exaggerates everything to sound smart and cool. Exams were PTW: buy the hardback textbook his buddy wrote or fail the exams.

This is a professor that claims to know things and loves the subject, but in reality just wants to sound smart and sell his books and youtube channel.

Would not recommend this prof if you want to learn.

guess Keating really wanna be a youtuber but anyway the course may be a little difficult but the exams are not. simply do all the weekly homework and you'll be good at exams for that they are really really ez. idk if it's the professor or the course but anyway is an ez A upper level course.
you have to go to lectures or you'll fall behind!

He's a funny guy and lectures are interesting. Lots of clickers so make sure to go. Tests are very fair and as long as you pay attention during his lectures and do the homework, you'll do well in the class since he covers the material very well. Definitely cares about his students and gives them many opportunities for help and with test drop.
moves very fast but fair if you stay on top of it
Great lecturer. Clear well prepared and interesting presentation. Friendly professional and intelligent lecturer that encourages discussion.

Very helpful and accommodating professor. Majority of the grade came from either 3 exam grades or the optional final grade. Some of the test questions had bad wording or incorrect answers because she takes student submissions, but they were also open note. There was a LOT of extra credit, like more than enough to boost your grade by over 10%.

I really enjoyed Professor Van Alstyne! I actually enjoyed PSYC2 so much I'm taking PSYC181 with her in the spring. Her lectures are really interesting and she emphasizes what's important on each slide so you have a good idea of what you'll be tested on. Study and you'll do fine!

Professor Van Alstyne is very nice and gives good, interesting lectures. She lectures a bit quickly, but her slides are all available on Canvas. Three open note test for the year, one open note final, and no homework besides SONA participation. The class was very easy and I recommend it to all of my friends.

Tests are open notes with plenty of time. Her lectures are very dense and she goes quite fast, so annotating slides or taking notes prior makes it easier to listen and retain material. Shes very approachable after/outside of class and no formal homework.

I had her for Math 3C and was shocked the course was not only online but prof was overseas. Between my terrible math skills, her distracting background noise (baby crying) and terrible connection the class was a headache. She gives too much work and offered us "flexible" coursework which was not helpful for me at all, I don't recommend her

I took Professor Carter for Math 10B and C. She is extremely knowledgeable and kind. Her lectures are recorded but I recommend attending live. Go to her office hours for extra help! Has readings 3x a week, homework weekly, two midterms, and a final. Highly recommend her but you have to put the work in. She offers practice exams prior to exams!

Professor Carter was the greatest math professor I have had. She is extremely knowledgeable and kind. Her lectures are recorded but I recommend attending live. Go to her office hours for extra help! Has readings 3x a week, homework weekly, two midterms, and a final. Highly recommend her but you have to put the work in.

She is a very kind and understanding professor, however her class requires so much work on weekly basis! 24 hours before every lecture you have to do stupid reading assignments which are 15% of your grade and are graded on the most vague criteria. There is a weekly worksheet which require at least 2 hours of work and same goes with the online h/w.

One of the nicer teachers, very understanding and answers every question asked in class. She does have annoying reading textbook assignments every 3 days along with two weekly homework assignments that are easily accomplishable if you put in the time on them consistently. Very, very good teacher, her study guides saved me for her tests!

Professor Copeland is an alright professor. His teaching style is okay too, you just need to have a grasp of the content the way he teaches. Since it is a 5 unit class, there is a lot, like a lot, of homework due each week (labs, textbook hw, and multiple choice hw). Overall, not too bad of a course and professor but I wouldn't be ecstatic about it

I liked his teaching style. His exams were on the tougher and longer side but if you have a firm grasp of the concepts attained through regular practice then you can achieve an A in his class. Decent amount of extra credit provided with almost 2.5% for an extra practice homework. Exams need grit as they are long and make you think.

His tests are very confusing and the wording is hard to understand. It is hard to know what he is asking for. He is a good guy, but I think that his tests are unrepresentative of the class and the homework. I did well in MathA/B but am not doing well in his class. He gives good lectures but the tests are a killer.
Amazing
It is interesting subject. Class is easy. Open book and laptop. And, no final.
it is interesting subject. Class is easy, no final exam. and we can use note and laptop for each quiz. Easy A

he's a really nice man. The class was challenging, but he knows his stuff and is definitely willing to help you understand. You can tell he loves his work and loves teaching. he does have an accent but i didn't find it that hard to understand.

If you are smart, you will love him. If you are not, then you will hate him. He teaches at a fairly high level. He tends to digress and to not be very interested in the standard fair. Mathematically he is witty, I suppose. His exams are open notes and open book because you either understand the concepts or you don't.

Dr. Falk is a very interesting professor who is passionate about the subject he teaches. The class lecture heavy but discussion regarding contemporary issues are encouraged and really livens the class. The essay exams are intimidating, but I found that he is understanding with pushing back due dates and is a forgiving grader. He brings his dog too!

All the class is is 2 Midterms and and a Final worth 40% of your grade. The class is insanely hard for a core because the tests are all essays and short answers in a blue book. Class is all notes and he goes so fast and won't post them online. Avoid at all costs had to work so hard for just a B+
He was helpful in office hours. he lets you choose to write a paper instead of taking the final if you do well on the midterm. HE was interested in the topic he taught.

Attendance is mandatory and you never want to be late. Overall I'd say he was a good and knowledgeable teacher, but he grades extremely hard! He's definitely not one of the easy going TA's who hands out good grades, you actually have to work for them. Luckily, office hours help, and for the most part he is clear in describing what he wants.

Interesting class and he is very funny and personable. However, he is a very hard grader and puts extra emphasis on participation and attendance. Also when visiting him in office hours he tries to help but is actually very not helpful and repeats himself. He tends to makes things more complicated for a simple question. VERY HARD GRADER!!

Hal wasted a good opportunity to teach us about a very meaningful and relevant topic by being disorganized and neglectful. He doesn't teach at all. All of the students were left to fend for themselves. Despite his terrible teaching style, he is a very nice and encouraging person with a lot of experience.

He is horribly unorganized and his rubrics and assignment instructions are incoherrent and impossible to use, making it incredible difficult and frustrating. I really disliked this class, and I'm changing my major because of it...
Cool, helpful

I did not enjoy this class, despite the syllabus implying potential. I learned very little that can be applied, and DO NOT recommend the course. 3 midterms (short answer), one project/presentation (open-ended, but it was a pain), and a final. The good stuff (stress, user-interface, error) was only discussed for two lectures.

dont take this class for one of you're ge's. the tests arent multiple choice, but instead are short answer. 3 "quizzes", basically like midterms, a final group project and a final group paper. way more work than i wanted to do to knock out my last psych ge. teacher is pretty nice and knowledgeable, but class isnt as interesting as you think.

Professor Shpyrko is one of the best professors at UCSD. He tries very hard to make his lectures engaging, but sometimes they can be confusing as they often skip steps. He is very smart, so often can skip steps and it can be difficult to follow, but he is also very good at answering questions afterwards.

Nice guy, really cares students. However his lectures made me sleep:(. Get ready to read by yourself. Four fair tests were given, which is standard PHYS 2 series convention. Anyway this course is not hard but just too many concepts.
Prof. Shpyrko's 2C is not as good as 2B, so when you are taking 2C, maybe there's better choice. The lectures are less organized than 2B so they are more confusing. Overall, still a good choice.
