His lectures honestly put me to sleep but he tries. He makes jokes to lighten the mood and knows his stuff well. He really does care about the success of his students and will frequently make changes to grading to help out. Really nice guy, simple class, but not the most engaging lectures.
I really liked him as a professor, but, be warned, you do have to do a lot of studying outside of class. E&M needs it
very nice professor, 10/10
He is a great professor.  Truely care about how students are leanring.  Lectures are interesting and much easier to understand than the book.

I agree with the last comment. The Physics Department @ UCSD needs work. But out of all the professors in the 2 series, HWA was by far the best. Despite the tougher subject, he tried to make sure that every student understood the main ideas. Quizzes are most of you grade and aren't that bad if you reivew NOTES! Textbook is pretty much useless.
Good professor. 70% of the grade comes from qeekly quizzes which are not that hard. Out of other physics prof. I found him to be the best.

Just derives stuff on the board and severely overestimates his students. Enthusiastic and cares for his students' learning, but paradoxically refuses to help during OH. If you're from BENG:Bioinformatics prepare to get owned because half the final relied on quantum from PHYS130 or 2D, which everyone else took but you!

I had Dr. Serences for PSYC 102 during Fall 2021, when most people were just returning to in person classes. His class was great and not too hard; grades based on weekly quizzes + a cumulative final + extra credit. He was great at explaining difficult neuroscience topics in an easy way and readily answered questions during and after class! 10/10

Really excellent professor. Makes the challenging material very accessible and dedicates part of class to just taking questions from students. Grades are based on quizzes and one final, and offers extra credit.

Professor Serences is really awesome! The class is only graded on 9 quizzes (two get dropped) and a final. He just lectures/slides but the material isn't too bad. At first, he had pretty ambiguous quiz questions with a short time limit but raised it to 25 minutes and phrased questions easier when students struggled. Wants to see us all succeed!

The course goes through the equivalent of 3 CSE courses (8A, 8B, 12) so it may be a little rough without any coding experience. With that much content, Prof goes through those concepts fast, but does always ask if anyone needs clarification in lecture, and course staff consistently responds on Piazza. If you have coding experience, class is easy A

Prof Serences was very chill and accommodating in terms of remote learning. 100% optional attendance, all prerecorded tutorials. About halfway through the quarter everyone was struggling very hard, and with the final project, but he listened to complaints and changed the grade weighting. Accessible via Piazza too, which helped for the HW.

This guy thinks he's the gatekeeper of law school. Very harsh grader, takes pleasure in announcing his drop/withdrawal rate in the start of the semester, and treats an undergrad course with no prereqs as though everyone should be putting in 50 hours a week. Absolutely insane expectations. Don't take if you want a decent grade w/o a panic attack.
Yes, it was a difficult class, but it was worth it.  The professor was really easy talk with and very helpful in office hours.
You have to work hard to do well, but you will learn a lot.

He is a really nice guy and very passionate and funny. However, he is an extremely hard grader even with a curve. Take home midterm and open book final. He doesn't put his slide online after lecture therefore have to pay attention. REALLY hard grader!! Class is not worth taking on how hard he grades.
Extremeley intelligent, passionate, caring professor. If you struggle, he will help you as much as possible. He loves his students and he loves teaching!
perharps more suitable with undegraduates but totally unfit for teaching graduate course.
Too hard and too demanded for a typical conduct class, which should be more relaxed and instructed.
In overall, a bad professor.

Ridicously and needlessly tough for grading. Obsessed by very small detail and very mean. No one really knows what he expects. That is a pity because Conduct is a required class, and no one wants to take him.

I took him at UF for INR4244 as a new professor. It's obvious he really cares about the material he's teaching. You have to do the readings and he gives pop quizzes to count attendance and class activities to get the participation score. But he's charismatic and makes the class fun because of his personality. I would take him again if I could.
overall mess. Hated every second of the class

If you only take one class for one quarter, she could be an option, or her class would be extremely time consuming and useless. I really do not know why she still persists the stupid and meaningless game that would waste us two weeks to work on it and this game would happen during the week five and six, the period struggling for midterms.

She's a nice person, and she's really excited. But the way the class itself is run is stupid - you end up buying all sorts of stuff you don't need. Only showed up for Clicker points (but she drops the lowest few at the end of the quarter). Super boring. Would recommend for P/NP if possible.

Seriously DO NOT TAKE HER! She is the worst professor ever. Really unorganized! You need to memorized and read a lot of stuff and let you play very stupid game. She teaches nothing, her class is like discussion but you still need to know a lot of stuff to pass this class. Do not recommend this class or this professor.
She is so talented!

If you are anxious about math, this is the teacher for you. He truly cares about student success, and if you show you are willing to do the work, he will do everything to make sure you pass. I hadn't taken a math class in a long time, and not once did he get annoyed or make me feel shame. We need more teachers like this.

Kenny genuinely cares about his students and about their well being (he brought in a counselor around exam time to talk about stress management). He has a deep ability to discuss math and works very hard to educate his students. However he didnt allow calculators on tests and wants you to show ALL work (basically wants you to learn). Good dude.

I took Stats with him at Bucknell, and he is a very caring guy but his lectures are somewhat hard to follow. The class was mainly reliant on self-teaching and his grading (especially by graders) was harsh. Would not recommend if you're new to the subject or not math-oriented but really helpful during office hours and will answer questions.

He has a so many "dad jokes" but he really cares about his students. If you don't understand a concept just ask him during office hours or after class and he'll go over the problem step by step until you understand. He has an infinite amount of patience and is a really cool guy.

I was so uncomfortable during his lecture because the lecture was very very very tedious and all jokes were lame as hell. Everything he covered during the lecture was inconsistent. The content could change dramatically in every 10 mins. The test questions were vague and unclear. Besides, the test sometimes contains unrelated or uncovered materials.
Tough grader but inspiration and good lecturer.

Prof Spitzer is a great scientist and a sweet person but not such a great lecturer. That said, he does curves the grades and I did end up getting an A+ but I did significantly better on the second midterm (lectures were delivered by Prof Su, not Prof Spitzer).

If this class is not apart of your major, do not take it. It is no easy A. The class is compromised of 2 midterms (40% of your grade), final (50%) & section (10%). Go to lecture, don't miss easy points from participation, and study the research articles presented (easy points). This class is hefty with material, podcasts are key.

Dr. Spitzer, more like Dr. steal yo gurl. One look at this old silver fox will make women swoo. The way he talking about excitation coupling will steal the hearts of women faster than the propagation of an action potential, which is in roughly 1-2 millisecond. But seriously hes cool and can teach, if you study hard you can ace it.

Professor Spitzer is really passionate about what he teaches. He goes a little bit too fast when he gets excited. But he's super smart and I have learned a lot more than I expected. Amazing lectures. He podcasts his lectures so you can rewind.

Dutton is great! She cares about her students and what she is teaching. The lectures were easy to follow and the homework was easy. The only thing to keep in mind was that the exams were open-note and pretty difficult. Make sure to pay attention in lecture and organize your notes!

She was the absolute sweetest and genuinely wanted students to succeed. Her background is so inspiring and she cares so much about the field. She was always encouraging students to do their best and how to find opportunities. Best professor I’ve had at UCSD so far. Take her!!

She gives a lot of extra credit opportunities and the midterms and final follow the class material very closely. She even made it so that the final wouldn't be able to hurt our grades because of the COVID-19 pandemic. She is very passionate and made me want to learn more about the subject. Favorite professor at UCSD so far - Highly recommend!

Dr. Dutton is great! Her tests are more than fair (averages on midterms were a B), and she's always willing to help and rly wants you to do well. Gives lots of EC. Grade is based on clicker, section, midterms/final, HW, and muddiest points for credit only. Study, go to review sessions & lectures, do the HW, and you should get an A!

Great professor, and highly recommend. As long as you try to actually understand some of the pathways instead of purely memorizing them, you will do great in the class! Also excellent personality as a professor as she always wants to help you learn the material and will go out of her way to do so.

Professor Moosmueller is one of the nicest professors I know at UCSD. Math 170A's content itself is quite difficult but she genuinely really wants the students to succeed and getting a good grade in her class in not hard if you put in the required effort. Her lectures are also quite clear. Highly recommended, one of the best.

Prof Moosmueller seems to be caring and always creates a good atmosphere in lectures. Lectures are easy to follow with her detailed note-taking and she breaks down concepts pretty well imo. I haven't finished the course but so far exams and HW have not been hard.
Lectures are incomprehensible: learned nothing from her for an entire quarter

One of the best professors in the UCSD math department I have ever met! She is really nice and knows the course content really well. Always there to help and if I got a chance I am gonna definitely take a class with her again!
Don't take her class. You will be constantly stressing. Whenever you think you know what she is talking about, you realize you don't at all. I really struggle understanding her.

Professor taught in a reverse classroom style. Recorded lectures with content, and live lectures for practice questions. Homework was tough at time, but overall doable. Professor pushed for collaboration, and the quizzes were often near replicas of the practice problem done in class.

Made CSE 141 straightforward and does not try to trick you. Graded on HW, Quizzes, and two Exams. HW is the hardest out of the three and she has pretty relaxed deadlines. Cannot go wrong with Professor Zhao for CSE 141.
She is not caring about student at all.

Don't know what she's talking about every class. Make different rules each time for pipelining and never made it clear. TA and she respond slowly and inpatient on Piazza. Many grading mistakes for midterm. Class is short and have 10 min of in class break, really don't know what that's for.

The best professor I've had so far. Dr. Komor is the sweetest person and has such a lenient grading policy. The online tests were harder than the in-person ones for sure! She offers extra credit near the end of the year and I was able to skip the final. She is really easy to talk to and she has a lab, so internship opportunities!

Difficult class (as expected) but REALLY STRONG + COOL prof!! Her tests were difficult but she provided ample material for you to be prepared (for the most part). Also liked her flipped classroom so we could actually practice what we needed. Also had cool guests come in to talk to us about science careers.

She's amazing! Grading is pretty lenient, lectures are asynch and class time is used for practice problems. She clearly knows what she's talking about and has a good command on what she's teaching. She honestly made this class redeem chemistry for me. Only one HW assignment a week and little practice problems after each lecture vid.

Komor is an amazing teacher! She helped me get a lab position this quarter and is just an overall amazing person. You do not have to attend class because each class is prepped for in advance through lecture videos and assignments. There are three midterms, drop one, and you can average your two midterms as your final score. LOVE HER!

I simply cannot believe that she only allowed one fortune cookie sized not card for the midterm. Im perplexed! Anyways, as a smart cookie myself I managed to overcome this diabolical testing standard. Workload is manageable but her lectures dont help. Only take if needed.

Professor Hasan is extremely knowledgeable and caring. The class itself was extremely hard. It is fully based on lectures. I thought I did well on the two exams but I got B's, even though I studied and attended class. Recommend the professor, but the class is heavy in info! Graded based off a midterm and final.

This professor is confused and he also confuses his students by the way he delivers his lectures. He keeps talking for an hour and a half and stops at the last five minutes for questions. The entire course is based on a midterm and a final exam that was based on a 2500 essay and the topics were extremely unclear.

Only 1 midterm and final paper, no other assignments to help fluff your grade. Midterm is closed book so be sure to study, study, study and pay attention in lectures. He doesn't do powerpoint outside of photos and maps, so pay attention when he speaks. If you are a visual learner, this class probably isn't for you.

I really don't know how the reviews credit as as easy . This class is very hard and the midterm and final based on the lectures which he talk a lot in confusing way. I like History but stay away from this class because you will get you confused with his style. BTW he is not clear on what he is looking for in Mid term and the final.

The lectures are amazing, covering interesting history events related to contemporary issues. The class has no papers, just exams. If you pay attention to his lectures and write everything he talked about, then you'll get a good grade.
I heard the Prof Hanes left UCSD and academia. She legit played Eminem - Lose Yourself before every in-person class. It was awesome. They didn't deserve you, P. Thanks for being so real.

She's great at remote courses, so I've taken 3 with her. Don't be fooled by the length of the lectures it's the same if you had a professor who takes class time to write on the board. Exams were hard, but she was fair.
The material was difficult, but Dr. Hanes explained it in a way that made sense. The tests were tricky, though. She was really kind in office hours and the tests came out of nowhere.
Dr. Hanes was always available and really helpful with assignments. This was my 2nd course with her and she wrote me a letter of recommendation.

The lectures were condensed so you don't have the usual time and length of an in-person lecture. This was a good and bad thing. I had to pause a lot to get all the information down. I liked the critical thinking discussions and the final paper was awesome. Dr. Hanes is kind and answers emails right away.

In my opinion, Professor Gui is average at best. You can tell that to a certain extent, she knows her stuff but she is sometimes hard to understand and the lectures are in my opinion, very monotonous. However, all of this aside, the class is easy to get an A. If you listen to the lectures and do the homework, the quizzes are very straightforward.

I used the textbook and found that she was doing the examples straight from there. I would watch the recorded videos at 2x speed and then just read the textbook and got an A! Webassign hw, weekly quizzes, and the hardest part in my opinion was the handwritten hw which was often way more complicated than the lectures or quizzes. Optional final.

Professor Gui is not that great of an explainer. She oftentimes leaves a lot of students confused because she skips over key steps as if it wasnt the first time we encountered the material. The class itself is not hard, but it's challenging to grasp even basic concepts. Her easy grading criteria makes up for her lack of good lecturing.

I couldn't really follow her lectures well and she goes really fast but the way she makes her tests makes it easier to get a higher grade. She posts her notes and lecture videos so going over those after lectures really helped me out.

Professor Gui is super fast paced and gives weekly quizzes. I dont think she really likes answering questions and she is honestly a super tough professor and expects you to keep up with things youve learned from years ago. Definitely have to study for this class.

Great professor and VERY accessible. He truly wants to help you succeed and aids you by providing a ton of extra credit opportunities. His class is honestly quite easy and it promotes a lot of learning.

This class is extremely hard, but he really cares that you understand the material. He listens to feedback, and tries to make sure the class is understanding the material. He stays back after class if anyone has any questions just to make sure people do good. As long as you complete all the work he assigns, you will be able to do well in his class.

Professor Narla really cares about his students, and he's very flexible. If you express your concerns he will listen to you and make changes about the course. He always makes time for questions and really wants the best for you! Doing all of the homework and extra credit may be time consuming but it works out!

Ok, so I wont lie this class is difficult. I came in with no previous physics knowledge and this class was hard. BUT, for all of you out there that have to take this class take Professor Narla! This guy really cares about you, which is hard to find in a prof at UCSD. And he makes it easier to get a good grade in a difficult class (extra credit)!

She tries her best to explain concepts. I agree that she’s new teaching cell bio but at the same time her quizzes and exams are straight forward from her lectures and the extra credit project really helped
The lectures are extremely thick and she kind of just reads off slides, but overall a cool professor. She’s not great, but not terrible either. The tests are also pretty complex and long.
She's still new at teaching cell bio. She tried her best to explain concepts but got stuck on some aspects. With time, she'll be awesome. But her grading is fantabulous!

I have to say this is the nic(est)^{\infinity} professor ever in UCSD. He is simply genius and he is a distinguished professor. He cares a lot a lot about his students and he is always willing to listen to students' concerns. His homework is very fair. His exams are straightforward and only based on the homework assignments.(MATH 170AB)

The nicest professor I ever had.   His main goal is to get students interested in the material, so that they spend time reading about it on their free time.  You will get to learn how you can apply extremely abstract concepts to the real world.  He wants to give everyone a good grade.

Very easy going and clear method of teaching.  He does cover a lot of material and goes fast in class. He is very understanding and is available for help.  Grading method is clear and fair. A couple times throughout the course he gave words of inspiration that built up my confidence.  His notes are thorough, but still recommend the book.
Professor Holst is the nicest man ever!!! I am totally going to miss this class and this professor. He is a little tough to catch in office hours, but he is always willing to help.

Tests are representative of hw/prac tests (flat out tells you what's on the exams). Has days where he explains the material really well; others where he doesn't. Book was****, go to lecture instead. TA's inconsistent in grading hw/labs, HARSH on midterms/final. Very Fair. Definately recommend him.

This was their first time teaching and they are a Ph.D. student and you can tell. They are nice but they move too fast without explaining things thoroughly. The quizzes were somewhat challenging but manageable. If you really want to do well, do the homework with people.

I’ve always enjoyed music theory until the 101 sequence with Karis. He’s an older and well established professor, however he is very difficult and hard to learn from. Be prepared to ask a ton of questions and complete all assignments. He’s very hard to approach and like the other comment, he can be intimidating.

Took this professor for Mus101A. Depending on if you like music theory or not, it might be easier or harder depending on your interest. Be prepared to use your textbook at lot and attend lectures. You miss one lecture and you miss everything. I found him to not be very helpful with explaining things when I was struggling. He was a bit condescending

Alright. The material was interesting, the course load was a bit much but nothing too crazy. Assignments reflected the course well. Sometimes not as engaging. I'd take him again, he was nice, just nothing really stellar either way. He was very pushy about camera use, though, which made me uncomfortable at times.

Most of UCSD faculty is like this, but Karis is the worst in that he could care less about UG students because he's too busy focusing on his career. Great pianist but his lessons are a waste of time. You're better doubling up and paying someone else for private lessons on top of this if you're interested in getting into good grad school programs.
One of the best professors in the music department

Absolutely need to take Nicholas!! Course is based on his lectures, which are straight forward, so no textbooks. Exams are all based on his lectures so you will be ready! Participation matters, so just show up. He cares. Allows partners for exams sometimes. Very flexible! Take him, best class and professor! Accessible outside of class.

Hands down the best professor I have had the pleasure of taking at UCSD. He makes all of his lectures and uses information from his experience in the field so you do not need a text book. His quizzes are based on his lectures and lecture slides, offers enough time to do your quizzes and they are straight forward. Take him and you wont regret it.

Professor Abi-Samra is one of the best engineering professors in the university. His courses are like a breath of fresh air compared to the other engineering courses, as he has simple yet interesting things to teach that aren't difficult to understand. Very caring professor. Homeworks are just weekly take home quizzes and tests are straightforward.

One of the best professors I've met. Really knowledgeable and really responsible. Professor Nicholas always responded my email in time and answered my questions thoroughly. He tried to give us many opportunities for bonus points and made sure that each one of us keep up with the course during lectures. Truly a respected professor.

This class was an absolute breeze. Partly because the material is relatively easy, and partly because this professor has great experience in the field and explains things very well. This professor really cares about his students and is extremely nice.

Amina is a nice person, but very new to teaching. She does not make it a priority to be there for her students. Be aware, there are only 4 assignments a midterm and a final that will make up your grade. If you can avoid her, please do so. None of her students liked her as a teacher. Amina does not know how to run a course.

She is so bad. Please avoid her at all costs. If you don't need this class, don't take it. She is very new to teaching and does not know how to teach without boring her kids to sleep. Very rude and demanding. She is not from the US and has a bad accent as well.

also 174, easiest classes I've taken. not sure if its because of the pandemic but she really lightened the load for us. each class was basically graded on two tests and they were both really easy. basically an essay and Nash equilibrium question, her resources online were also super easy to follow and she's one of the easiest teachers to ask help

I’m taking this for significant writing or disciplinary writing. It’s easy. 3 quizzes+1 final research paper. Quizzes: based on the lecture (all answers Professor will go through during class and do need to use your own word describe anything u feel/listens in order to get full credit)
Research: no clear rubric but TAs are helpful.

EASY!
Well, I should have dropped this course. 10 page essay on a single topic will make you suffer. Gives unclear instructions.

I can tell she is really smart, but obviously I am not smart enough to take her class. A 200-word short essay every week is not that bad. A 10 page paper in Chicago style for the final??? This is a music class, not an English writing class...this is probably the reason why most people dropped it at the beginning of this quarter.

She is the BEST professor I have ever had!! She cares about you and your learning. You can learn from her class rather than complete a course. She is one of the very few people I have met who will care about you as a person and your life outside the classroom, and even your future plans, in addition to teaching in the classroom.
Does not answer questions.
Really nice, genuinely concerned about the student.  Her lectures are very free form and she doesn't always make complete sense, but she is good at holding discussions.

Very young, new professor. Lectures were fairly unstructured, but she explained concepts well, would sometimes ramble but eventually got to the point. Definitely references the textbook a lot. Fairly accommodating and understanding to student needs (like extensions)

If you're not a poli sci major, this class can be a drag. Exams were fairly difficult and you really have to know the concepts well. The term paper was a lot of work. Overall, a brutal class but an A is definitely achievable.

She is a very nice professor, but her lectures are pretty much pointless. She essentially speed reads her slides word for word and does not give any time for questions. Exams were more focused on memorizing random facts over actual concepts.

A really kind professor who is accommodating towards students! Some questions on his exams are difficult but as long as you pay attention and study, its doable. He also provided us with multiple extra credit opportunities throughout the course in the form of quizzes, which helped out a lot with grades.

He is a sweat heart! he is compassionate for his students to become successful but not to be rude or all but he has a strong chinese accent which makes it hard to understand him! you will have to depend on your own to study! some questions from the Exams aren't related or just hard overall. STUDY! and you'll pass his class. 75-B 60-c and 50-F

His tests are always tricky. A good amount of questions he never even talks about. His lectures are super hard to understand. I genuinely didn't learn anything from his class, not one thing. Just hope that you are lucky and get a good TA if you have him. There are better professors to take honestly. Def avoid if you can. His class online is easier.

You can get an A as long as you turn everything in & try because the course is not structured to hurt your grade/GPA. But he speaks very fast and since he has a really thick accent it's almost impossible to understand him like 99% of the time. You have to go to discussions and get lucky with a good TA that teaches you all the material. Not the best

Professor Zhao is a wonderful professor, he gives out a lot of opportunities to earn points. I felt his class was on the easy side, please know I was taking this course during the summer and working full-time while taking another course. I recommend future students to print out his lecture notes and just add notes. Best way to pass his course.

Professor Rosen is kind and understanding and seems to really care about her students' learning. This class was only graded based on the midterm (worth 50%) and the final (worth 50%), both of them being essays regarding the required readings. Overall, the material was very interesting.

the majority of the class is graded on your ability to do well at the homework, which there is quite a bit of. I feel that I know the information quite well but struggle due to the wording of the homework. Rosen herself teaches really well and I enjoy every lecture, however the homework is too confusing for me to consider taking her class again.
super cool professor! You might want the textbook but I did fine with the 9th edition and didn't find tests and quizzes very reading heavy most of it was from the lecture slides/

Ginoo Alicio is one of the best and most caring teachers I have had at UCSD. Though I must admit this class was a bit more challenging than your average high school Filipino course. It is very specific on grammar and tenses. It is important to go over vocab/pages before class so that you are able to ask questions and answer when called on.

Professor/Ginoo Alicio is the BEST teacher I have ever had in my life. I took LIHL132 a long time ago where I met Ginoo Alicio and I'm so glad I did. He is a very intellectual and intelligent man. He cares so much about his students and it shows. Literally the #1 teacher in the world! You will learn so much!

Taken as a remote learning class, both the professor and class went smooth. Class time is mainly made up of going over the previously assigned hw pages in the mandatory textbook. He popcorns people so make SURE you do the homework. One con is since he has some trouble navigating canvas, you won't know your grade until the end of the quarter really.

I did not know how to read or speak in Filipino so I was surprised I passed the placement exam. You do have to buy the textbook ($20) and if you are completely new the fact that it is completely in Tagalog can be scary (just use translators or ask the professor). He's super sweet and cares about his students. Great intro class!

Professor Alicio is such an adorable little Lolo. He is a good lecturer and makes a lot of typical funny filipino dad jokes, which made it enjoyable to be in class. The grades when I took it were dependent on 3 quizzes, 4 homeworks, 1 oral/1 written final exam. Also class is mandatory but its only twice a week no discussion.

This professor is alright, the major downside of this class is the crazy amount of info that is needed to know/remember (im talking a 130 page google doc used to study for the final). There is tons of info. Watch the lectures when they are uploaded, she talks fast and goes through slides fast. Use your TA! They are your biggest ally.

Information overload and I found it very hard to see what she wanted to test us on. She has a difficult accent but her podcasts make it easier to go back and learn certain concepts. A really kind teacher but I found the final exam to be very difficult and not representative of the entire course, which wasted a lot of time. Wouldn't take again.

Seems nice but barely teaches. Lectures are sporadic and not well organized. Some slides had no text; material was confusing enough and her accent & grammar just made it harder. Exams weren't very representative, esp final: she ignores some big concepts to pick on certain minute details. Some questions were vague and point breakdown wasn't clear.

She seemed helpful throughout the quarter, but my final exam had the points added wrong so my grade got bumped down a whole letter! Went back talk to her to fix this but she didn't want to do anything about it bc the quarter was over.. This is the only time this has happened to me and I hope I'm an exception bc now my GPA suffered for no reason

Best Prof by far! She actually does indeed care about how well her class does! She is very clear on what she will test you on. One midterm (40%) and one final (60%). Both the exams were very fair. She still holds her own review sessions and is very helpful in office hours. RECOMMEND!  oh btw, 3% extra credit on final exam from clickers! HUGE!

Racist and rude. Always has something bad AND uncomfortable things to say to students, especially POC and LGBTQA+. Very impatient, stubborn, and refuses to listen to students. Lectures go on tangent.

Please don't take this class, and if you need it, just do what she wants, regardless if it's good or not.

I saw the reviews on this site and was like 'maybe I can survive' but NO. JUST DONT TAKE HER CLASS. Close minded, rude, disrespectful to students and does not appreciate ANYTHING in anyones work. Video projects due every week, then she just talks bad about them in lecture. You dont learn ANYTHING. Also get ready for a GPA drop. GGs

DO NOT TAKE ANY CLASS OFFERED BY HER. Goes off tangent on lectures, takes 5 minutes to answer a simple question, but doesn't even answer it directly. She speaks in algorithms with a heavy accent and just completely destroy's students self esteem. Criteria on student films in her class are just her saying everything you did wrong, in her opinion.

Lots of content. Norm is two films and 20 pgs per week. Lectures were lengthy and accented, but useful in predicting quiz questions. Lecture notes existed, not useful overall. Need to be adept in movie analysis (recommend VIS 84) cause quizzes will hit you hard. I made it bc of extra effort on my own. Harder than HUM series, easier than O Chem.

When I chose Hard Look at Movies, I didnt realize that Hard would be a double entendre. The quizzes and exams within were by far some of the most difficult challenges I have encountered in writing papers at UCSD or UCLA. If you intend to take a Babette class, be prepared to take lengthy notes in order to survive.
Dr Perry is outstanding in his field.  Definitely one of the best; highly recommend

Professor Reese is a very caring professor, and genuinely wants to see the class succeed. Unfortunately the content isn't very attention grabbing, and because of that it's very easy to simply get lost in the class. Loved her as a professor, but I didn't find the class interesting nor very useful.

norman is the best!! lectures are super easy to understand + very interesting. hw is all online and very very easy. midterms and test were also online (bc of covid), and also very easy. norman is seriously the nicest professor and so sweet, and does not give a lot of work. the class is very manageable and easy.

Homework is due weekly. Midterms are homework based (DO THE HOMEOWRK). Lectures are recorded. He's a caring and funny guy. He gave me Doc Ock vibes. Go to lecture and try not to fall behind because everything overlaps. Research paper towards the end gives you about 2ish months to work on it.
terrible teacher but he is very easy. most students get A's. mumbles a lot. just make sure you do your homework.

Lectures are not required. Just make sure you go to at least the last 5 minutes to turn in your homework. But most of the homework is online. Midterm was very long and difficult. Professor is very nice and friendly when you approach him. If you are not good at science, i suggest you take it P/NP.
lectures not necessary.  all the materials are online.  make sure to take all the online quizzes.
she does not care about studetn at all! You can never reach her outside of classs. Alwasy absense in OH and even lecture. Never respond email

If youre looking for easy grades, this class isnt it. On top of the projects which take multiple days to complete, the quizzes are rather difficult. Thankfully, projects account for most of your grade. However, if you wanna actually learn data science, youll love the class. Shes knowledgeable, responsive, and genuinely cares about her students.
The lectures are not very clear sometimes and you don't know what she is expecting for the projects most of the time.

This grading constitutes of four mini-projects and a final project. The professor didn't seem to have a plan as she kept pushing the deadline once students asked, giving only one week for the last. The grades are very subject, and there's very little advice on how to improve. Recommend 185 instead if you want to know more about languages like R.

Homework is very subjective and no constructive feedback provided. Lab is poorly designed as TAs run through R codes without teaching. She tries to make class undergrad friendly by leaving out theory but backfires, as no one can understand why methods achieve the purpose. And when she explains theory, even math/stat/eng grad students can understand

Lectures and assignments are not difficult to follow if your math and coding are not too bad. However, if this is your first machine learning class, this class is a torture. He expects a lot of self study even if you really have no idea of where to start.

Professor Bergon always shows concern for students learning. LIGN165 could be very hard for students without any coding backgrounds. It should have a coding class as a prereq, but this is not the prof's fault. He did a really good job explaining the probabilities while the coding part could be a little hard to scary at the beginning.

AWESOME person, but not a strong lecturer. LIGN 165 goes through a lot of CS concepts very fast (CSE 101, 105, 130), which is great but a little intense, even for a CS student. His lectures are tough to follow and the class is pretty disorganized, but his office hours are gold. Assignments aren't bad though and there are no exams. Great CS elective

Requires programming exp to do well on problem sets. Propose your own final project. Final Grade  70% (5 PS) + 30% (final project). Lectures help build mathematical intuition for deep learning. You need to figure out on your own how to implement what you learn. Highly recommend to those who want to understand ML rather than learn frameworks.

It is nice to have a class at UCSD that gives us exposure to deep learning techniques actually being used in the field. I brought up my final class project in a few of my interviews and I think it made a big difference in getting the summer internship I was hoping for.

I took him Fall 20 and it was horrible. No finals or midterms just weekly quizzes every Friday but they were extremely difficult. The content/problems were WAY more challenging than the practice problems in the textbook, hw, and lecture. We were allowed to use our notes, hw and the internet during the quizzes but tbh that didnt even help.

For your own good, please avoid him. Entering the semester, I saw all the bad reviews he had but thought How bad could it be? Well, it is terrible. He is an arrogant, unhelpful, stubborn man and he is by far the worst teacher I have ever had in all my life.

Prof Green taught the concepts by giving simple explanations then backs them up with examples. The lectures were pretty chill and he'd always pause after a tough topic to ask if there were questions. The quizzes are more difficult than the HW though so be prepared. Some of the types of questions on the quiz weren't in any problems from book or HW
The teacher is a jerk. He makes it hard for students to ask questions in class. Aweful at explaining concepts. His test are extremely hard, the class average was a 55% on the first two tests.
Professor Green is fine at teaching. But his tests are harder than the lecture given. In the lecture he went through simpler examples and the test questions are harder than homework and examples.

Prof Hannah is a nice and approachable professor but he spends too much time over explaining everything which can actually make the concept more confusing. There are tons of readings each week and they're all interesting but too long. Discussion posts every week with a midterm and final. Read and do the discussions and you will get a good grade.

Be all means, avoid this guy. He has a terrible accent, he can't teach. He is extremely rudimentary and can not even operate an online class effectively. It blows my mind this school hires very intelligent people on paper, but they have absolutely no brain power to effectively communicate to their students on the concepts that need to be taught.

This class is a real hidden gem at UCSD. The structure of the class is intuitive and places all the lecture material within the contexts of various marine animals and the various challenges they face. It is a difficult class that covers fairly dense topics but the prof has structured the class in such a way that the material becomes fun to learn.

Hes really patient and really accessible out of class. His lectures are super clear with step-by-step details. He asked for peoples feedback and answers them thoroughly in a PDF format and sent to everyone, then he made adjustments based on our recommendations. Im really bad at math and I certainly cant get an A if I werent in his class.

Best prof ever! Lectures: clear teaching & neat handwriting & many ex, numerous students with other prof sneaked in to listen. He is really kind & ask for our feedback to make adjustments. Hw are easy with unlimited attempts, tests are reasonable. He made videos to teach hard hw problems and even extended his office hours to answer my questions.

He is a caring. The critical issue is that you have to learn Matlab mainly by yourself that isn't "math18" but scores are math18 grade. Even some students post questions about Matlab on piazza, they don't teach you how to solve. How can students know if not lecture provided? Worst thing is that they only grade assignments at very end of the quarte.

Overall this is the best class I've taken this quarter. The subject is easily digestible and fun to learn. I only attended his lecture once because I realized that his notes are so perfect, that I can simply learn out from his notes without going to his lectures. His notes alone has helped me passed this class and that says something.

Professor Xu is the best professor I have ever had. He explains the contents well and he'd stayed up after class to answer student's questions. The quizzes and midterm are not that hard if you do the practice exam. He is an excellent teacher overall and I would take his course again if I had the chance.

She is very nice! And she does care you as long as you care. :3 She is very accessible outside of the class! She will reply your email within a few hours. And she is willing to help as the best she can. :D

Though she is a nice teacher with patience and smiling, she gives me a horrible grade! Before this grade comes out, I worked really hard and revised my essay numerous times, which I thought could be at least a grade starting with B!!!!! Her course crushed my GPA this term...

Her rules were a little weird. She made us use name tags, and wouldn't let us pull out our phones for any reason. Electronics were not allowed, only paper and pencil. She said none of us were close to writing at a college level and the feedback she would give back was a bit bipolar. One day she'd say it was fine, and the next say you misunderstood.

This is one of the worst classes I've ever taken. There are so many papers and so much reading. If you have no music background you won't stand a chance. This class bored me out of my mind, I learned nothing, and I don't even like jazz anymore. Also, there are kind of a lot of papers, so if you don't like to write, pick an easier UD writing class.

Professor Dresser is an expert in music and makes learning about music interesting. I agree with other reviews that without prior experience in music, this class is difficult. However, he does a good job at explaining certain terminologies that are necessary for the class and I really appreciate the work he put into this class during these times.

Both the course description and prof. Dresser stated that this class is for non-music majors and no prior musical experience is required. However, none of the assignments seem like appropriate workload or requirement for non-music majors, and the live lectures are just bunch of students that know Jazz spitting terminologies we don't understand.

Cool prof, nonexistent TAs, unaware of the overwhelming load. I felt like I was taking three 4 unit courses in one. 2 papers, 3+ concert reports, weekly quizzes, 40+ pages of weekly reading and hours of listening, two 90 minute lectures a week. Overall I did enjoy the guest speakers and the material, but the assignments were way too overwhelming.

This man has no concept of what an appropriate workload for already overwhelmed students is. This was a class for non-music majors and he indunated everyone with complex music theory and 20+ pages worth of papers (EXCLUDING MIDTERM AND FINAL). He's kind and passionate but this class was genuinely the worst class I have taken at UCSD.

Has zero control of his TAs, who are usually power tripping and get upset if you question their authority. Also inaccessible. Is extremely knowledgeable in the subject, however, and you can learn a lot if you pay attention. You just won't always get a grade that reflects that.

I LOVE Prof William, He was super nice his first quarter teaching at UCSD and even threw us a pizza party at the end of the quarter! He's very knowledgeable about photo and cared a lot for his students.

I really enjoyed learning from Prof. Shi. The lectures are a great balance between teaching theoretical concepts of control and applications. She works through examples in class which is extremely helpful in understanding the key concepts and solving the homework assignments. Very accessible!

Shes an absolute Angel. Not only shes incredibly knowledgeable and passionate about science and biology, but shes also a very kind person. Biochemistry is the most difficult class there is, but she will make it straightforward and is there to help you. Study her lectures and go to office hours and youll do well. No surprises on exams either.

Great professor, extremely clear lectures, long but super organized slides, fair exams. Problem sets are long but can help you to consolidate the material. Overall, AMAZING professor! Would definitely take Prof Huffaker's class again

Huffaker made this class as straightforward as can be, which is a tough thing to do for something like structural biochemistry. Lectures were very clear and the problem sets, though long, were a good study tool to know what to expect for exams. As long as you watch all the lectures and study the material well, you should definitely get an A.

Dr. Huffaker is a great professor. She is extremely knowledgeable in her field and is able to explain and offer answers to questions very thoroughly. Her lecture slides are basically her textbook, so you should really understand those well. She also is super approachable and opens herself up to students. Overall, amazing experience!

She's a great professor and really works hard to make things concise and slides clear. Never felt like she wasted time or presented any surprising material on the exams. She went over what she wanted to cover within the scope of the class and the exams were easier online in general since the class is really memory and content-heavy.

Professor Nathan did what I had not thought possible: wanted me to switch majors to history. His lectures were clear and entertaining. Yeah, there is a lot of reading in his class and he can be a pretty tough grader. But he was also very helpful outside of class and always responded quickly to email. He def understood the assignment.

Professor Nathan is a great lecturer and his class is clear and easy to understand, but he is a tough grader, even for stuff like discussion boards and participation. He is very quick to answer emails though, and is helpful through both email and office hour. The workload is not too bad, you just can't phone in any assignments.

Didn't address the fact that a guest lecturer never showed up, and missed one of his own lectures due to a "scheduling conflict". Doesn't seem to respond to emails and he didn't address either issue until two weeks after the first missed lecture. Joint course website makes no sense. Get ready to figure out the course structure yourself.

often late to lecture, literally just reads from lecture slides that have mistakes (then he says he'll update the slides but never does), does not hold office hours and inaccessible outside of class, barely answers student questions and answers are not helpful, 75% of your grade comes from midterm and final and they are incredibly difficult, avoid

I took grad classes with Prof. de Callafon TA'd for and worked with him.  He is a good person and does care about student learning.  He expects you to work very hard, but he definitely had times where he gave me the benefit of the doubt and he did not have to.  I continue to learn from his insights.  Busy guy- ask at class. Be respectful, don't BS.

MAE 143B is a difficult course, but Raymond teaches it very smoothly. The first time that I took this course, I didn't understand "anything", but with Raymond it's impossible not to grasp it. The course requires regular studying. The final exam was similar to previous years' finals and fairly easy. A piece of advice; Take Vibrations first.
The tests were on material mostly from the lecture notes. Print the notes, study the notes and use them on the exams or else you will struggle (at least I did).

Nice lady and cares about you as a person. Not the best professor. Very scatter brained and constantly was changing due dates so it was a bit difficult to plan ahead. Reading is dense and boring. Tests are open note/book so if you work in the book throughout the semester you'll be fine. Takes forever to grade.

So you only have to go on certain days. I didnt like her much because she pushes one viewpoint only, but the class was EASY AF! Literally got an A+ with minimal effort. Just do the assignments and tell her what she wants to hear. Dont expect to learn too much.

Marni is amazing. Her midterm is very straightforward, the writing assignments are easy and the group project isn't bad. She really cares for the class and her students, and she makes sure that her class is enjoyable over anything. She maintains a happy environment and often includes jokes and funny videos to lighten up the mood. Overall enjoyable.

Marni is awesome. She really enjoys teaching about primates and hearing about her research is really cool too. Her class is not an easy A but if you do the work and study really well for her exams you should do well. She gives extra credit on her exams so pay attention to the little things in class. Wish she was a full time professor at UCSD!

Such an awesome teacher. I appreciate how she tried to be PC about everything. Honestly awesome class too. Like it was the only class I did well in last quarter. It was a pleasure to go to class every morning. Good GE class. Didn't have the textbook and didn't need it, but you need the workbook.  No work either, just two tests and a final. MEMORIZE
She is super sweet and her office hours were super fun. I'd reccomend taking her. Her class was super informative and I learned a lot.

Dr. Belding is such an amazing Professor. I just transferred to UCSD as a junior and knew I wanted a PhD but was not sure who to turn to or where to start. Luckily, Dr. Belding's office hours prioritize course material questions, but if there aren't any, she takes time help you career plan. She taught me so much and there are many ways to get As.

She was very caring and understanding. I liked that she made all of the lectures and quizzes available earlier in the quarter so you could get a head start if you wanted. Was also super accommodating about late work and extensions due to personal circumstances, would absolutely recommend her!!

I took her class online and all her lectures are pre-corded and uploaded onto youtube. She has around 6-7 videos on youtube for every week but since it's on youtube, you have to watch annoying ads every couple minutes. Quizzes/exams are also difficult. There's minimal student and professor interactions unless you go to office hours.

Took PSYC104 with Belding - absolutely loved her class! She has a way of making a 3-hour block of class not feel exhausting. She was more than happy to go over and clarify any topics students were having trouble understanding. Always showed us examples of how topics we were learning were applicable IRL. Her tests are hard, but going to class helps!

You can learn a lot from Prof. Smarr's course, but did not grade based on the syllabus is noisome. He did not grade several assignments that are included as graded assignments in syllabus. He offered curve to students, but reject to disclose how the curve is added to students' grade, leaving some students confusions regarding their grades.

So sweet and I really enjoyed her lectures. You can tell she cares about how youre doing and the input that you give in class. I really recommend going to lectures in person (if possible) because it goes by quick and I felt really connected to the content that way. All the assignments were interconnected and easy to build off.
Dr. Johnston seems like a nice person who cares for her students, but just like any other DOC class, it is a lot of writing. Luckily, I got a good TA who supported her students.

Dr. Emily is an amazing professor. She clearly outlines what is expected on each assignment, and is very accommodating. Lectures are interesting and relevant to the class material. She provides many resources for extra help, and overall makes her classes a breeze.

Dr. Emily is a great professor. I had her for DOC 2 and loved her passion, so I took her for DOC 3. You can clearly tell that she cares for her students and enjoys teaching the material we go over. From my experience in online learning, grading is based on completion except for a few important assignments, so complete them and you should be fine.

She is very understanding and definitely cares about her students and what she's teaching. All the DOC classes use the same material, so it doesn't matter too much who you take, but I prefer her over Strom. How you'll do in the class is dependent of your TA though, they do the grading.

His lectures have nothing to do with the courses you choose. Every time he evaluates his homework, he says that he is different. He always beats others, gives very low scores and is very stubborn, but the content of the lectures is very boring, and he is mostly busy with his own work. Company affairs, not a professor who teaches

In class explanations are insightful, and the lecture notes are very thorough. Notation can be confusing, but it's manageable. I would recommend this class. My major gripe with this class is the grading, the grading on reports is based more on writing style than code quality, which personally I didn't appreciate.

Data mining: Advertised as OK for anyone, but most quickly dropped. Need strong math/stats and programming to do projects, which are poorly written, confusing. R language is only taught in TA ofc hrs. Interesting lectures, useful in real world, but repetition of data in projects gets boring. Quiz 1st thing every day. He cares a lot about students.
This class is utterly tedious, boring, difficult, and the exam is very difficult and poorly representative of the material learned. Very vague instructions and a waste of Wednesday afternoons.

This must be one of the sharpest professor at CSE dept. The assignments are hard, as are the topics, and exams, but useful. I actually felt that I've learned something, not just absorbed required material. Exams are open book to help in case student forgets syntax or definition, which relieves from stress and often avoids "test anxiety". This helps

This class had a LOT of required readings, with specific, lengthy weekly discussion posts. The readings are also very complex, so they take quite a bit of time to fully comprehend. Prof. Shragge is passionate about his teaching and is a somewhat tough, but fair, grader who gave great feedback. I learned much from this class but it was difficult.

I took two of Professor Shragge's history classes: History of the American Suburb and War and American Society. He is one of the BEST professors I've ever had. His enthusiasm for the subject is contagious and every lecture was interesting. His classes made me wish I had majored in history.

Took Shragge for winter culture of war class, very interesting lectures, he was clearly interested in the material he was teaching which is always appreciated.  Happy to help students outside of class, approachable, grades a little too easily  but excellent teacher nonetheless. Knew people who easily got B's without trying, I got an A but tried.

An amazing professor!!! Intelligent,helpful,polite,and overall just a very nice and approachable person. Interested in striking a conversation,and values your opinions about the world.Prof.Shragge sees a potential in each and every one of his students. Also,he is always involved in his community.
Very good professor. He is very helpful, lets you know what will be on the tests. He also doesn't just lecture, he engages with students and cares what you think. Highly recommended

Professor Gumm is a passionate lecturer and understanding individual. Course structure/material is quite 'loose' and readings are pretty short. Papers are graded fairly. Interesting topics about mythical creatures!
Hard class. But good professor. Reading and writing intensive.

Fantastic professor, especially for online class! Lectures were super engaging, she promoted discussion but also acknowledged and encouraged thought out responses in chat. You need to attend lectures and speak or send chat response to get participation credit. Gothic literature stories were super interesting and I had lots of fun! Best CAT2 class!!

I have taken three courses with her and I must say that she is perhaps the best professor I have had at UCSD. Her courses are really fascinating (I mean cmon now, I have learned about gothic literature, the apocalypse, and mindfulness all within three quarters). If you want to be challenged as a writer and surrounded by good vibes, she is for you !

Prof. Gumm is a passionate and friendly teacher, which is very necessary when teaching a GE writing class. However, grading can be a little bit stingy, hence putting in effort is required to get an A in this class. Grading significantly depends on the TA, so be sure to engage with them and go to office hours.

Extremely clear in lecture, although you should sit near the front because he talks soft sometimes. Always writes out his entire thought process on the board so it's very easy to follow what's going on. DO NOT TAKE IF you are slow, his lectures move quick and if you're gonna complain about him going too fast you are not suitable.

Tolerable at best. Lectures usually only 30 mins long, but he glosses by how he gets solutions so be ready to teach yourself. HW preps you well for exams 1 and 2 but the final was absurd (avg was an F). Drops a quiz, a homework, and can drop an exam but then the final is worth more. My advice: ace the first two exams b/c the final was horrible.

Had an A the entire quarter for Math10A. Just general calc right, do the work and participate and youll do fine. Professor Benson throws a curve ball of a final and puts material that was not even in lecture. If you take him and there are As in the class BEWARE!!!!!! HE WILL THROW A CURVE BALL AND RUIN YOUR GPA!!! STRAY AWAY!!!

Coming from a student who isn't too good at math, this class was easy to follow. hw, quizzes, and midterms were do-able and I averaged a A/B the entire quarter, until the final, which was unreasonably hard and not given enough time. We did not know our grades the ENTIRE quarter. Piazza and emails were left unanswered days before finals.

Lectures were quick and straightforward - it left me with extra time to study with the textbook and actually understand the material (there is something to be said about the fact that I learned more from the textbook than from him). But the final was ridiculous. The mean for the class was an F. I felt he never really cared about my learning.

1) Handwriting on black board was barely legible. Couldn't read or hear anything over Zoom 2) Curved everyone down at the end of semester 3) Only shows up for 10 minutes each class 4) Exams, TA sessions, and lectures are all very different. Impossible to get help. He's at JHU now. FA21 Lin Alg was the worst math class ever.

He is a nice guy and he tries hard to teach, but his writing is incomprehensible, his exams are insanely hard. His final was open book, but I think the whole class completely failed it (12 HARD PDE problems in 3 hrs is just not possible). At least his grading is generous. Overall expect a hard quarter if you decide to take a class with him.

this is the worst math teacher i've ever had... even if you can understand what he's saying here and there it won't help, because tests and homework are lightyears ahead of what he covers in class... its like he teaches you 2 plus 2 and then tests you on a continuous  sumation of an integral by parts devided by an undefined limit

I had him for math20e and it was absolutely the most difficult math course I've ever taken. His tests were super hard and his final was beyond do-able (WTF is a "cupsoid"?). This class is hard and he makes things harder. I only scored around 50% in the class overall and got a B. That's how hard it is. Don't listen to those other students-it's HARD!

It is best that you ACTUALLY read the (very well prepared) lecture notes he has posted online, before class. Also, you should do some "outside reading" because fairly often he will be referencing particular theorems, etc that are NOT included in the book and whose name will not even mentioned. He curves like crazy. Study hard!! Many conceptual prob
She is super passionate about theatre and will give you extra credit if you participate in class. The class consists of watching movies and taking a short quiz or writing a small 1-2 page paper. Easy
The only professor that I had ever seen that criticized students who stayed about leaving class early.

Kim is great. She is a huge resource. I was a playwriting student, and I got more help from her than any playwriting teacher, and that is not her subject. She is flexible and really wants to take advantage of students special skills. I recommend taking her and Jim C. at the same time as their very different styles are good compliments.
Kim Rubinstein is a very nice professor and clearly knows a lot about Theatre. Her lecturing skills, however, leave much to be desired. Seems like she's making it up as she goes.
Life changing!
Professor Andrews is very helpful and understanding. She gives extra credit and is passionate about what she teaches. Her grading is a bit tough ... but the work is possible.

Her class was very organized and routine. She also provided extra credit opportunities that you should definitely take advantage of even if you dont think youll need it. Shes clear on what she wants for the midterm/final podcasts and your grade will reflect if you followed her guidelines. I didnt watch any of the lectures and still got an A

This is a research class so its definitely more time-consuming but if you stick to following the syllabus deadlines, youll do fine. There are weekly discussion boards and five assignments that help you towards completing your final paper. Professor Arciniega is very flexible and open to help students complete their assignments on time. Good prof.

Professor Sheng is honestly the best professor you could take for any math course. He's super kind, caring, and understanding. He gives you practice tests to study with and they're basically the same thing as the exams. Once I did poorly on a quiz because I forgot about it and he let me retake it. Dropped lowest quiz score upon class request.
Really nice professor with fun lectures and fair tests. Recommend.
Fun, relatable, and most importantly, direct. I love this man.

Tests you on very specific details (e.g. numbers he's said in class or are on the slides). His lecture slides consist of figures from scientific papers, which means you better be paying attention to what he says. Watch out for vague wording in exam questions. Not accessible in person, but responds to emails promptly. Cares about students' learning.
Solid and funny professor. Tests are fair and he is very nice with explaining and gives real world knowledge and fun trivia in his lectures for this class. I would happily take him again.

I completely agree with the comment below. I got extra credit points just by doing yoga. It is ridiculous. The class was super disorganized. She does not reply to emails and posts passive-aggressive announcements all the time. Even the TA was confused. The class was just super disappointing overall. Avoid at all costs.

You can literally get extra credit for playing among us with other classmates and its an UD class. For starters, she didnt post an exact syllabus until week 3 into the quarter. Shes always off topic, posts lectures late online late, dont expect to learn much, changes assignments, exams, and the grading constantly. Worst professor Ive ever had.
she likes to ignore students when they ask her for help and clarification. She is very not organized in everything. worst prof at UCSD

Most disorganized professor I have EVER had. Does not hold regular office hours, and forces the students to check the calendar constantly to see when they are. Her exams and assignments are poorly worded. Gets very defensive when feedback is given (or even questions about the course itself). Don't take if you want to stay sane (:

Never have I had a professor so unwilling to listen to their students' feedback. When I asked her a question about an assignment (that was graded on points, but was not provided with any description of what these points are for), her response was defensive and honestly very rude.

First off, this man is a TA, not a professor yet. Some readings were fun to read others were boring as hell. It is really easy to mess up your quizzes. The way he worded his questions and answers was kinda weird. I don't know how I ended up with an A. It was a miracle that I did not mess up my GPA. I almost cried when I opened the final :(

I feel like he wants us to fail the course with the quizzes, the options are so vague and most of the time I am not even sure about the answer after reading the paper thoroughly, what's even worse is that the quizzes take up a huge amount of grade so if you don't do well you won't get a decent grade. The work you put in won't reflect in your grade.

I love Alicia. She's a great dance instructor and really cares about her students. Intermediate Jazz with her was really fun and if you apply yourself and go to class you will get an A. My only critique is that she sometimes changes counts without telling you but if you talk to her about it the problem resolves.

Class was fun because I got to take my mind off studying for a bit. She's enthusiastic and cheerful, which can bring your mood up. Midterm was vocabulary test which was really easy. Final is to perform a dance she made up. Didn't like how she required us to spend $15  and drive to downtown sd to watch a dance performance though.

Alicia is definitely a great teacher to have. Her lessons are clear and fun! There's only one vocabulary test and one essay on a live jazz performance. The only way you'd fail is if you skip too many classes but I don't see why you wouldn't want to go to her class. I'm definitely going to take this class again (you can take 3 times for credit).
Nice lady, I learned a lot from this class. Not too demanding... just take the class.

This was my first time taking a dance class since I was 5, but Rincon made it really fun and I learned a ton.  She's super nice & helpful, DEFINITELY ask her for help if you need it!  Pretty easy to get an A as long as you actually try.

Professor Card was super cool. His class was online and fully based off of readings, discussion posts, and 3 quizzes. Interesting course and easy A which I really appreciated this quarter. Would definitely recommend Prof Card.
Very nice professor :)

Dr. Linke is such a kind and caring prof. She truly cares for the success of her students and was always very open to recommendations from students on how to improve her style of teaching. Her lectures were interesting and you have a clicker question for every lecture so attendance is mandatory. Her class wasnt hard which I really appreciated.
Class was graded on homework, quizzes, and two assignments. Everything was do-able and the class is interesting.
He was a very caring and considerate prof, the class was hard but he made it manageable. His slides were organized and made note-taking easy, I only had to use slides and lectures to study

I think professor Schmelz is really a good professor. He is clear in what he wants you to know for the exam. He replaces lowest exam score with a higher one and he rewards diligence. Biochemistry is intensive so no matter the professor, you have to be ready to grind. Good luck
He is so funny!!! He is such a fair professor, throws out unfair questions, and offers extra credit at the end. I would for sure recommend him!!!

Great biochem prof! very accomodating to covid crisis, made class as fair and doable as could given the circumstances. Lectures are very heavy due to nature of subject but he makes it very digestible. Tests were not open note so really have to know the material, but he offered problem sets as part of grade too. recommend!
I love professor Schmelz! His lectures can get a little boring but if you really enjoy the material and find it interesting then you will really enjoy this class :)
Prof Wallen is absolutely the most amazing teacher. She is so passionate and understanding, I had her multiple times and enjoyed every class I took.

Wallen does not facilitate a good atmosphere for critique. She allows students in the class to tear each other's work apart needlessly. There was little room in the course for creative work and much of her feedback was harsh and unproductive.

Ruth is probably the nicest and most understanding professor I've ever had in my college career. Even if you forget to complete an assignment, she will often times give you a good grade given you do a decent job on the project. Gives really good feedback as well and offers new perspectives on modern photography.

She lectures are extremely boring. I spent the entire time on my computer. I never got any useful answers out of her, though she is nice. She exercises no control out of her TA's, and the grading and ease between TAs was horrendus. The class is extemely expensive, and stupidly time consuming. Don't take ifyou are a science major.

She wasn't a very good lecturer; I spent lecture time chatting on AIM. You learn more from your TA and from doing the assignments. This class is not that easy. It's horribly time consuming; we practically had slumber parties at the photo lab. And it's really expensive; almost everyone I knew paid over $200, and that's not including the camera.
Very knowledgeable and interesting. Pretty harsh grader

I expected to take communication studies, not African American studies. Grading is based on TA. She occasionally has attendance checks based on pen and paper, but rare. Lots of reading (that CAN be optional if you pay attention in lecture)

Boateng was my favorite professor!! She's super cool and I loved her lectures. They're so detailed which make them perfect study guides. We barley had any assignments, and there were only two exams. I would take her for all my COMM classes if I could. Show up to lecture and apply yourself (actually try), you WILL do good.

Do not, in any way shape or form enroll for comm 10 with this professor. Wait until winter, you will be thankful. unhelpful, rude, unorganized, blames students for her lack of teaching skills. i could go on and on, please dont take, you will regret.

Boateng's lectures are extremely helpful. She is clear and concise when explaining class concepts, and conveys information in ways that are well understood. Lots of people in class unnecessarily complained about simple issues and she handled them very well. I also think she's quite funny.

Dr. Zimmerman-Liu is a great professor. She gives thorough and easy-to-understand advise to your essays. The topics are relevant and personally helped open my third eye about society and its issues throughout history. 3 essays, prompts aren't hard. You have to do annotations in Perusall but they're very simple and quick to do. Take her if you can!

I was so surprised to get such great feedback on my paper for once from a Professor. She's really fair with her grading and as long as you follow the directions and rubric on any paper or assignment, you will get a high B or A. She's super caring and encourages students to participate in a healthy way.

Dr. Zimmerman is a really great lecturer. She is super prepared, extremely knowledgable, and really helpful. The class is graded on 4 short essays that help you collect research for your capstone paper, the capstone paper itself, and attendance. She is an easy grader, readings and films displayed help a lot, and just follow her prompts to get an A.
very easy class. grading is done by ta's so honestly didn't really have much interaction with her. but overall, her class was clear and simple
While DOC is DOC, Professor Emily is great. Better than Dr. Strom in my opinion. She gives students the chance to talk, and doesn't tell students with apposing viewpoints that they are wrong.

Great professor if you wanted to learn some mathematical software. The class was interesting as we dive deep into common python frameworks and libraries that focus on solving math problems. His lectures are interesting and I love how interactive his lectures are. Homework may be a mouthful so prepare to put in more hours for homework.

Lectures are discussion based and professor cold calls - and the way she does this is very intimidating. If you are not sure about the answer to her question, she makes you feel embarrassed in front of the class. Readings are interesting and we have only 3 papers with 4 pages each. Overall, I like the class but not her teaching style at all.

Lectures are tough to sit through as they are not engaging whatsoever. She cold calls for attendance- the only reason people show up- lecture attendance was usually at 20% of total class by week 4. Work Load is pretty light besides reading(can be dense) and a few papers. Worst part is showing up to her lectures in fear of her cold calls.

One is able to see that Professor Walter is very passionate about this course. The lectures are discussion based, and I was not a huge fan of it. We had 3 three-page essays and a final 1-page essay/reflection. Participation is highly important.

Unorganized and it took her so long to grade papers. When the class is done for the quarter, one of my paper which was submitted a month ago was not even graded. The university announced that all grades will be released on the 24th, but now she hasnt graded the last paper and its been more than a week since the class finished.

I have to say that this is the worst professor I have taken. Her lectures are not bad, but she is very inaccessible and the requirements for the essays are unclear. The main issue is that she is 100% incapable of seeing past her political ideology to the point of construing opinion as strong facts. She also knows nothing outside of her research
Best teacher ever love him!

The professor abandoned the syllabus around Week 5 and didn't have any rubrics available for the final assignments, noting that this would help us acclimate to "the real world". If you're to looking to learn something, then there is no point in being enrolled in this course. Take a Magagna class while interning for a legal office instead.

Yes, she isn't a very structured professor; but most of her grades are on effort and understanding. You will be pushing yourself in this class, getting uncomphy and stretching yourself, but with flexibility and adaptability you will push through. Manamnus is reachable, understanding, and intelligent

She is incredibly intelligent and nice; however, a majority of your grade is based upon a group project in which you do not get much direction (and she is picky about what goes in it). She piles on extra work not listed in the syllabus. Overall, the course structure (or lack thereof) is confusing AND she has never replied to any of my emails.

Really an amazing professor; even online, there is a lot of reading and a lot of interaction. She makes group projects so you can talk to each other about the difficult material, and gives plenty of opportunity for review, reflection, and growth. Answers all questions clearly, and willing to take the extra step to help you understand whenever asked

Luo's teaching style is something that I would like to see more teachers emulate. She has pre-filled notes with certain blank spaces, so that you can spend time writing down the important stuff in the lectures instead of just everything. Her lectures are simple and easy to understand. It would be a blessing to take another class with her.

Well-organized lectures. She explained materials clearly, and the quizzes represent the materials. Homework is relatively difficult, but half of the questions will be graded on comletion. She does not drop hw, nor curve a lot, but you can still do well if you follow the lec.

From my experience, Dr. Luo is a really nice person and does a good job teaching the material. The homework was similar to the examples she did in class, although my TA was on the stricter side. Dr. Luo is also very approachable via office hours and emails. Overall, I would highly recommend her classes!

Asynchronous with live discussions. Class is very fast-paced and you need to study to make sure you get it all. I recommend going to the live review sessions. Quizzes are every other week in section and straightforward if you know it well. Homework due once a week, and you can redo questions until you get it right, but don't wait until last minute!

Doesn't care about students, terrible 'lectures', pointless assignments, basically wants you to fail. Skip this joke of an instructor unless you enjoy learning everything on your own from the textbook or if you're deliberately trying to fail.

Dr. Pogliano is the best professor I've ever had. He genuinely cares about his students and goes out of his way to create a positive, supportive environment.
