You can tell he is very passionate about his work and his passion rubs off on his students. He is an outstanding man and an inspirational professor.

I'm part of the Phage Genomics Research Initiative and it's my favorite class so far! Supportive lab environment is amazing, and a small class size is a breath of fresh air from large lecture halls. Lectures are interesting, and it's fun to learn by taking part in experiments. It's amazing we have the chance to make scientific discoveries so early.

The phage genomics program is wonderful and Prof. Pogliano is very helpful and understanding while you get used to using lab equipment. The homework and exams in the class are extremely limited and simple, and the lectures, while interesting, are not required to get work done in lab (but they are tested on the final exam).

If you are lucky enough to be accepted into the Phage Genomics Program do it. Beyond the general benefits it is an amazing class and an amazing environment. Dr. Pogliano is absolutely terrific and truly cares about students. It is a unique and beneficial environment. Definitely take this class and professor.

The quizzes are extremely easy as long as you go over recent lectures and know what you have been doing in the lab. You pretty much just get a task and are left on your own to do it but help is available. The class is interesting and the time flies by. The final was not very difficult either and the breaks during it were unexpected but nice.

It's cool that Kevin is a professor because he's so down to earth and seems to get along well with all the students. I loved his teaching style and learning about hip hop culture and music with him. We had great office hours talks and he is incredibly helpful and inspiring. Personally, I love music, so I might be biased but he's as good as it gets.

He's so kind and has superb explanations and examples. Probably, one of the nicest professor I have met too. Honestly, if I didn't mess around this quarter, I would be able to get an easy A. The lectures are rlly interesting too, and I usually hate watching lectures as I am more of hands-on learning guy. Exams are quite easy without trick questions

She's very kind and straightforward. But I thought her quizzes and tests were rather hard. BUt if you're willing to spend time asking her questions and going to lab, she makes it very clear what she tests on. Material can be quite boring but she does her best to make it interesting even at 8am. She's a very understanding person and quite lenient.

She's a very nice person. Very helpful as well. Always made sure that students were understanding the material. There was no curve to the class, but her exams were very straightforward and tested on things she clearly focused on. Very nice personality indeed!!
Very nice prof; always poised and well-prepared for class. Her exams were straight-forward with no curve balls. Too bad next quarter will be her last quarter teaching at UCSD.

Her lectures are straightforward. Tests are long for 50 minutes, but you'll have enough time if you study well. Lab reports are easy if you just follow the guideline. Be sure to follow it. Ask your TA if what you are doing is correct because the TA grades your report. Quiz questions come from the lab manual that you need to read before the lab.

I am never going to take this professor again. He does not explain python concepts well. He is really horrible at giving feedback and explanations on homework and also expects students to participate in discussion boards for 3+ times a week- even if you do not have a question/problem to post. His class is a waste of time and money.

His lectures are useless and do not explain how to complete the homework that he gives. Horrible professor in terms of teaching and explaining concepts in python. Better to spend time on a free python youtube video to learn how to code than spend time and money in his class.

This is more of a essay and writing class with papers and paragraphs rather than learning how to code. Avoid this professor if you want to learn python. Take him if you want easy A without learning anything and spending $700+ on a course for nothing.

Would not recommend this professor if you actually WANT to learn how to code and program. He gives TONS of essays, reading and written assignments. I joined the class hoping to learn how to use python and complete exercises and practice. Instead, he simply redirected students in week 2 to PAID websites where you can buy books to learn python.
If you get him for the online Intro to Programming course make sure you participate in the forums. I didn't have much time so my grade was lowered, but he is a good teacher and person.  Helpful.

Prof Middleton is an amazing lecturer. She is accessible outside of class and cares about everyones input on the structure and topics discussed in class. Participation is important to her, but she allows students to participate in a variety of way to earn those points. You are only graded on participation, a midterm essay, and final project.
Professor Herrera is the best, period, bar none.

Wouldn't recommend him.  His quizzes are extremely difficult with the average around 40% for each but he still doesn't curve much. The questions on his test use the basic concepts but make them so difficult that it's hard to ace it even if you studied many hours for it. If you want a good grade, take another professor because the curve won't save u

BAD! explaining the important concepts badly. homework has ridiculous restriction and is hard to understand. no response from homework until the finalized score comes out(no resubmit chance). could lose more than half of the points even the the code works perfectly in your own tests. did not post any notes for you except for an mostly empty sheet

He's a great person, but the class itself is just the most unclear and difficult class I have ever taken. Literally everything in this class is confusing and insanely difficult, unless you go through a lottery system and get a good TA that will spend 2 hours just for you to complete your homework. It's so unnecessary to make a basic class like this

Gary is the best professor in the CS department, he cares about his students and helps them as much as he can, very nice person, his lectures are very clear and they are very helpful, the quiz questions come directly from the practice quiz, the class is time-consuming, but you learn a lot. consider starting PAs early and going to the tutor's hours.

Hard to discuss him, you love him or hate him. Lectures were pretty boring but discussion sections are absolutely necessary for PAs. PAs themselves are intensely paced and teach you to start early and often, otherwise itll be a pain. Biweekly quizzes are really easy. Overall, Garys nice but you really need to step up your work ethic to keep up.

One of the toughest cs courses I have ever taken. Say bye bye to all 10 of your weekends because you will be spending it on the programming assignments. Half the time you will spend trying to understand the writeup. You must attend the lecture and discussion sessions to even have a chance at completing the assignments in time for extra credit.

Required class by Summer Bridge to fulfill the DEI requirement. I genuinely enjoyed this class because it helped me understand my identities better and how they intersect. First intro to CRT was very eye-opening, especially to injustices that occurred at UCSD. Everyone should take this class before they leave UCSD. Prof. Dean is a very wise peson

This was a Summer Bridge class taken in 6 weeks instead of 10. I understand my identities better and how they intersect, so I'm minoring in AAPI Studies because of it. Contribute to discussions to better understand topics. There's some readings, a few essays, and short writing assignments, but it's all very manageable. TAs are very caring people.

I took this course during Summer Bridge for 6 weeks instead of 10. Dr. Dean was very nice and cared about his student's opinions. Attendance to lecture doesn't matter. TAs handle all of the gradings and answer your questions. Online lectures were always at least two hours. Readings due every week, but fairly easy class. Only 2 essays and a project.

Fun seminar to accompany the 2Excel program. I loved the weekly writing, it was easy and a great opportunity to reflect on myself and my journey through college. This was a mostly self-directed seminar, without much appearance from the prof (or anyone really), but when he did have a video he seemed cool.

Amazing professor. The class has weekly readings, a few essays, and a group project. However, they are all straight forward, and easily digestible. Dr. Deam cares about his students and makes the class to where everyone can succeed. However, attendance is mandatory as he assigns a reflection question at the end of class to turn in before you leave.

I feel she should not be teaching, especially not this class. She has a very orientalist approach to eastern cultures and it is very discomforting to be in class. In general, I feel she doesn't have a clear grasp on the subject she's teaching. She seems like a nice person, but her class is one of the worst experiences I've had at UCSD.

The difficulty of this class is largely based on the TA's, however, Lapp makes the rubrics accessible early on and you will know what you're getting into early on. The format is clear cut and builds off the reading material very fluidly and naturally. Did not go to office hours, but still had the ability to work for a solid A. Exams can be rough
Great professor. Good about of reading overall, but loved her teaching style and was very caring. Would recommend!

She worked together with another prof for a freshman seminar, which was essentially MUN for the French Revolution. Great class, she only intervened when she really had to. Gave good short lectures in between, to give us more concrete info on France at specific moments. Very friendly lady.

She's pedantic in her delivery and the lectures mostly consist of her creating spurious connections between various religious and cultural texts. She does not value any secular/rationalistic insight when she calls on students. Numerous claims made by her in class also show a fundamental misunderstanding of cultural/social phenomena.

Hes honestly a decent person and is nice, but he doesnt teach what hes preaching. The tests and what we retain in his lectures are always completing different, if youre going to take him get ready to learn chemistry basically on your own. And he grades so religious on the exams to the dot.

Professor Czworkowski is one of the best professors I've ever taken for chemistry. I did only take one class this semester, but he gives thorough lectures. He is very open to asking questions and even calling out the right answer. 88% is an A! Tests go by homework, review problems, and what he emphasizes in class. Would take again for Chem 142 :)

People are making a big fuss over nothing. He's a really good guy and the material is so easy that theres no need for him to really teach. Midterms multiple choice, quizzes, and no clicker. Honestly, his lecture slides were all i ever really used to study. I messed up on one midterm which is the only reason i didn't get an A. Would recommend.

Came to lecture everyday, when it got tough (ch 4, ch 9) I fell behind in the lectures, but if you stick to the book, do all the homework and make sure you understand each one (sapling gives you explanations - use em!) the midterms and the final are pieces of cake. Exactly what I wanted out of a class - I learned the material and gained an interest

Czworkowski had a great attitude and seemed glad to teach, however, the way he taught was not very useful for the way we were graded (i.e. quizzes developed by TA's). There was plenty of opportunity for help with office hours, discussion, and the chem lab. Final and midterms were fair game.

Dr Joel is a great lecturer and very knowledgeable in his field. He uploads his slides but they're not as comprehensive as the lecture, so attending lecture is important. This class has A LOT of readings, and you have to refer to them in the assignments. There's not that many assignments and he values quality over quantity.

Great professor, lectures were interesting and engaging. If you answer a tough question in class or ask an interesting question hell give you extra credit on your next test, so he really encourages class participation. Always was very personable and funny too. Tests are straightforward as long as you go over the practice exams and problem sets.

Frank is an excellent professor who can answer any question you might have, he is very accessible as well. This combination makes him the perfect professor. He is also very fair with his expectations of his students. Would recommend anyone interested in HVAC take his class, 10/10.
Best Class I've ever taken
Amazing class, even better teacher!

She is a good professor and is very knowledgeable in Women's history. She is a great choice. She posts lectures to YouTube each week, there is a discussion and a lecture response due each week. There are 5 papers due throughout the semester so prepare for that. She gives clear expectations for assignments and also gives helpful feedback.

Great professor, funny, witty and knowledgeable of material. Definitely made me laugh with "straddling liberalism." I think she's gone now but if she were to come back definitely take her. Material is very useful, she assigns a lot of readings but we go over them in class. Midterm, papers, and final are straight forward.

Professor Riggs is great, very understanding, very knowledgeable. A lot of assignments and tests but they really help you write your final paper. Great class, awesome professor. If she comes back in fall take her course whatever it is!

She is wonderful. For HILA 121 she required a lot of small work and one large pape. There are 3 midterms but the paper was the final. First gradings are hard but then once she gets a feel for the class, and the students understand exactly how to get full credit, its much easier. Very formulaic grading. She is entertaining and very helpful.TAKE HER!
Dr. Riggs is awesome. She is so helpful during conferences. She never talks down to students. Take her! This quarter she taught food psychology. Interesting stuff!

Atypical class format - mostly guest lecturers & spontaneous discussion. Terminology & quiz materials are best discussed during office hours, or you're on your own. The assigned workbook is not difficult but time-consuming - start early! The final essay is flexible. Overall, the course material & discussions were super interesting & inspiring!

One of the most incredible teachers I've had in my college career. Not only was Professor Placek extremely well educated on the topics, she was also kind and genuine when it came to helping students. I've been having a hard time in my personal life and the professor did everything they can to help me succeed in class and I'm forever grateful

You're basically teaching yourself. She has weekly hours for questions, but other than that you're on your own. So disorganized, we only have 3 assignments to determine our grade and she gives no extra credit. She doesn't respond to emails quickly either. Don't get me wrong, she's nice and everything but I would NEVER take again. NEVER.

confusing recorded lectures and one discussion a week. she is supposed to have the lectures uploaded by discussion time, but they are uploaded basically the day of. each week we have new writing assignment prompts that are unreasonably long. one week had a requirement of total 12 paragraphs, way too much work on top of other classes

Professor Placek is caring and obviously cares A LOT about the material that she's teaching. If you've never learned about anything she talked about, a lot of it will be super educational and novel! However, lectures and slides were unorganized, no communication & difficult/wordy quizzes. Whole class was afraid of failing lol.

I took this class over a year ago and thought to leave a positive review. The material is what it is but prof makes it as digestible as possible, and makes things as intuitive and applicable as possible. All of the test material was similar or had appeared in lecture verbatim. This class was a vibe.
The quizes are fair but homework and tests are heavily based on computation than the actual comcept. Many problems could be modified to set up instead of set up and solve.

Even tho the stupidity and uncreativity shown in the design of 20D and hw is revolting, Prof J has a very deep understanding of pedagogy: not only he answers all types of questions on Piazza with great details, he also tried to relate ode to daily physics problems with the just right amount of proof and explanation. Good luck w/ the future, Prof!

Upsetting to read some of the bad reviews because he was a great prof in my experience. Hes a cool guy, his lectures are easy to follow and he encourages questions from students. and he honestly made his exams easier than he probably should. My favorite math professor so far :')

A real gem in the math department. His lectures are clear and keep you engaged until the very end. He is very funny and provides context on difficult problems. His exams reflect his lectures and the practice exams. Overall he cares about his students and will go out of his way to answer any question either after class or in office hours. Underrated

This guy was AWFUL. He gave us 65 minutes to write 12 PARAGRAPHS of mid terms. Like dude. This is literally a 101 class. Relax. So much pointless work. In the beginning he stated that the point of the class is to advance our reading writing. No. It made me never want to take another humanities based class.

Took this class 100% remotely/ asynchronously. Class was set up in weekly lectures/ assignments due that forced students to not fall behind which was a huge help to procrastinators that push things off until right before the midterm or final. Being an upper division history class, there was a solid amount of reading, but overall a solid professor.

I liked Professor Henderson's class and his teaching style. He is obviously very passionate on the subject, and his lectures are informative and helpful for the assignments and tests. Lots of reading, but its very interesting and not difficult. Some assignments were pointless but overall he is a great prof. Def take him asynchronously if you can.

Nice professor! I think I learned why philosophy and humanities are so important in terms of college education. You should definitely do the readings though. Self-study on philosophy will help as well. 2 papers, 1 final exam, pop quizzes from TAs. (Make a good decision on choosing TA!) Overall, it was pretty hard but worth taking his class!

This class was definitely tough, and taking it over the summer made everything go so much faster. Professor Armour is great though, and his lectures cover everything that will be on the exam. He also provides problem sets and practice exams which are super helpful in preparing you for the exams.

I took this class fall 2019. It was not that difficult but I do not like him as a person. He is arrogant and disrespectful. He shames students that ask questions that he thinks are "dumb" and did not explain the concepts very well. I would not recommend taking him. He gave us a small notecard to use notes on the final which was nice.

The class content itself was easy, but the class was difficult to get through since he talks about himself (and not in a fun way) so much. I took this class 2019 fall, and I remember part of our graders were clicker questions, so you had to be there in person at 8am. Also, for some reason, he chose to do his Q&A session from 7am, before class.

I took 6B with Dr. Hoeger during the winter. The pre-recorded lectures were long and this class required a lot of my time. The exams were HARD but he is generous with his curve. He provided a lot of practice materials (DO THEM!). I was pushed to do well in this class and I do not regret taking his class. Not an easy A, but def worth the effort.

He doesnt seem like he cared about students at all. No matter what circumstances we have due to COVID, the syllabus says no exceptions, so unless you're dying, don't bother email 'cause he'll just ignore you. Hw and Quizzes are still due during the day before final, so you know, focus on those instead of your other finals instead.
Not prepared for online teaching at all. He was all over the place schedule wise and unnecessarily rude when asking questions. Would NOT recommend.

I had her for HUM3, HUM4, and HUM5, all online. Her explanations are good but not engaging. The classes are pretty boring and her rant about her credentials to a student that had a question was awkward and unnecessary. Finals are difficult and long but graded very leniently. She is a little intimidating to approach but overall a good prof.

Professor is incredibly rude and insensitive to language and cultural buriers of foreign students. Went on several rants about student interrupting her and questioning her authority, by citing all her credentials and experience, when student was genuinely confused and agreeing with her response. Takes every question as questioning her authority.

Really disappointed with her lecture. I looked forward to taking HUM5 but she just doesn't match my expectation. The texts were great reads but her interpretations are awful. Either too shallow or a sudden far-fetched "deep" interpretation. Dedicated teacher but her ability to interpret texts is just sub-par.
She is a good professor. You can definitely tell she has certain opinions but so does everyone in the department so it is fine.

Prof. Giordano is very much a professional, but still finds ways to make HUM fun. Her lectures are informative, and she encourages attendance to the reading hour. It's a HUM class after all, but she makes it feel less daunting. Book list is pretty affordable, and interesting too. We read Cavendish which no other prof did. Definitely recommend

Unhelpful feedback on assignments - RUDE FOR NO REASON. Forget about asking for help, he'll make u feel dumb if u have questions. He teaches ALL courses for UX/UI so ur stuck w/ him for 7 courses, which isnt worth it - he's so condescending. Get ur cert elsewhere.

She's very kind and understanding. For her online class, you will have to do a personal growth journal every week for homework and attend Zoom lectures on Tuesday & Thursday. As long as you study the lectures and study guides, you will do good on your exams. Her lectures are interesting and she really works hard to ensure her students aren't lost!

This was my first coding class and the prof made the material easy to understand. We're graded mostly based on problem sets and labs. He has a really useful class website that has all the notes from the lectures to help with them. The problem sets weren't extremely challenging but some problems required a bit of googling.
Dr. Vul is a totally amazing teacher. His enthusiasm, material, and energy keep me interested and I learned a lot. Best class of college so far. I recommend him!!!
I wish I didn't have to keep the comments clean in this section.  Just awful.

The homework sets were pretty hard, but great tools to prepare for midterms and the final. If you work hard in this class, you will get an A. It was a bit hard at times to understand concepts during lecture, but going to his office hours helped A LOT! He is a really nice professor. After taking this class, I understand statistics inside and out.

not a great professor. he was confusing at times. Not so helpful either. The TAs were much more helpful then he was. if it wasn't for section i don't think i would have understood the information as much. I do not recommend him.

She only reads through slides and some slides have low resolution and you can barely recognize them. Gives EC on participation, which students in other timezones cannot earn. Reached out to her multiple times to ask about a wrongly graded thing and never heard back. Overall awful experience. You pay a lot tuition and you only get ignored, how sad

I really enjoyed professor Teodorof. She always made sure to answer student's questions in lecture and it was evident that she wanted us to learn the material. The pace of the lectures was a little quick, but I took this online, so I understand it is hard to gauge a proper speed. Overall a fair and great professor.
Shes the seeetest professor Ive ever had a class with at UCSD. Im currently taking it over the summer and I am enjoying it so far. She offers about 5% extra credit to your grade which is amazing.

Tests are easy and straightforward from PPT and problem set and she emphasises the parts that are going to be on exams during lecture. She gives 5% extra credit by simply attending the discussions and she provides the 100% final option.(at least in summer session) Professor is very nice and cares a lot about students' understanding and performance.

Material can be difficult, but her exams are as fair as they can get. There's a lot of details and pathways to memorize for this class, but she'll test you based on understanding rather than how many tiny details you can cram and memorize. Do ALL the problem sets!! Very useful and questions will show up again on exams. Helpful during office hours.
Has a very thick accent and is hard to understand. The class itself is a lot of vocabulary, so the accent made it a bit tough. Watch videos outside of class and you should be fine.

Probably the greatest professor to grace this campus. He was hilarious with his explanations and analogy but they made sense. Too bad he was only here for a quarter. Would take any math class with him again.

Took a chance for summer session and I'm glad I did! One free response problem set per week (collaboration encouraged), midterm, and final. Her lectures and powerpoints are enthusiastic and well-explained. She seems very friendly, and she is responsive on the discussion boards. The only prof at UCSD I can't complain about! Take her class!!
The best professor ever! The lectures are informative and interesting. Highly recommend!
Professor is really nice and patientShe always gives useful tips for your portfolio which decides you will pass or not. Take her

I like a lot of things about Dr. Vienna. I learned many valuable writing skills. She taught me the importance of critical thinking.  Her assignments were challenging, bit they helped  improve my writing. That what matters!

Great teacher! I like her teaching style and her helpfulness. Her lectures are well organized and she does not mind to clarify if you do not understand. Her assignments are useful and help achieve better results in writing and critical thinking. She is always available for the discussion after the class meetings. I respect this professor a lot!
She does not care about students at all and she is always late for 15 minutes. I do not think this guy counts as a college professor.

Had no issues with this professor. Explained concepts clearly, and I learned a lot. If you have any prior experience with coding, this class is very easy. If you are confused, reach out to instructor or TAs early, as class moves very fast.
Terrible communication, never replies to any emails, not even to the TAs. Failed an entire final because of a technical error and does nothing to fix it. Don't recommend

Megan is a decent professor. Ive also taken Professor Ellis for the same class and everything is very similar. She's kind and offers a good amount of EC. Grading structure and material is 100% the same as Professor Ellis

Dr. Bardolph is such a sweetheart! she really cares about her students and does a decent job of explaining concepts in lecture. The assignments are fairly lengthy but fairly easy. The last few questions tend to be more challenging, but since Google is allowed, it's manageable. Would recommend!

I wouldnt have minded the amount of weekly work assigned if the professor was able to give feedback to us or grade it in a timely manner. I still have ungraded assignments from week 3 and it is finals week. Prof. seemed to be a little preoccupied which is understandable in these times but it made class difficult for the students.

Fascinating class: digs into social issues, great for humanities majors, but lectures are dry and long. LOTS of writing--smaller assignments and a big final paper. Group project was annoying and felt kind of useless. However, bt is a VERY caring professor, offering frequent deadline extensions and no-fault individual extensions, they were great!

Bt (the name the professor goes by) is caring and kind. There are fewer writing assignments than I expected. Don't let that fool you though, because one must make sure to do well on the assignments. Most of the time, the TAs and professor grade everything reasonably. Take advantage of the generous extra credit opportunities.

i could tell bt cared about our overall wellbeing and learning. the group project is kind of annoying if you're stuck with flaky people but bt graded pretty leniently; otherwise, there's some short writing assignments that are graded by the ta. lectures were boring but also covered important issues

B.T. cares about us so much! I absolutely love their lecture and will definitely take B.T.'s class again if I have the chance. Four response papers for about 300 words, one major assignment (1000 words), and a final group project. The first two's grade depends on your TA and the final project is graded by B.T. Overall, an easy A.

Seems like a cool enough person but lecturing is definitely not his thing. Course could have been much more interesting if lectures were on topic. He's great at responding to emails but the 10+ person group projects are ridiculous and made the class not worthwhile.

He is a great professor. He's pretty funny and helpful. He tells you exactly what he wants and how he wants it. Meeting those standards is super hard but at least there's a clear goal to work towards. I learned a lot about writing and the topic of the course. Would recommend.
Prof is a cool and respectable guy. He moves through material fast with very minimal instruction. Must pay hyper attention during class and be ready to get called on.

He is super funny, genuinely cares about his students, and gives fantastic and informative lectures. Discussions were fun and high energy as well. There is a fair amount of reading but I never read any and did well. There are relatively simple weekly discussion prompts and other than that there are only 2 papers. 10/10 would recommend.

Mareike is an awesome prof. Her lectures are clear, she puts a lot of effort in additional resources, and she really cares for us students. Most outstanding are her office hours and general attitude. She always seeks to help you, not only for matters in this class but way beyond. She is a brilliant mentor and taught me a lot for my future. Thanks!!

I can confirm the good ratings. Prof. Dressler is a real gem. She makes clear pre-recorded lectures. Grades on hws, quizzes, midterms, and final. You are allowed to drop the lowest hw and quiz - she even offers an extra credit assignment at the end, which bumps up your grade. Always helpful and super nice in Office Hours. Can recommend her 100%

Dressler is an awesome prof. She makes prerecorded videos & posts them early on to Canvas. So you can watch the lectures at your own pace. Her hw teaches you to prove and reflects nicely what you do in class. We had 2 midterms & weekly quizzes. That was a lot but reflecting on it really helps to spread the weight for your grade. Final was fair. TOP

I was frightened to take this class, because it is known to be very hard. Indeed, the material was not easy, but with Dressler's phenomenal lecture I survived and even learned a lot. Videos and slides were bomb. Quizzes were hard. I went to her Office Hours once in a while, and she was more than happy explaining everything in detail to me.

Funny and really nice Professor. She does lecture videos and even uses Discord for class discussion. That's so cool. She helped me understand some concepts during office hours. I appreciated the different grading options she offered. She used quizzes, 2 midterms, and a final. Everything was masterable if one understands the material.
Great professor, just takes his course!!

Professor Duarte was very accessible outside of class and focused a lot on learning rather than tests and quizzes. The lectures mainly covered example problems and the homework was pretty similar as well. The reading quizzes were directly based off the reading and everything in the class was structured well. Overall I recommend this class very much

Took online Grades consisted of reading quizzes (unlimited attempts), HW and a 10% final, no midterms. Cares more about you actually learning instead of only focusing on grades. Lectures were of practice problems. Easily accessible if you needed help.

Great lecturer overall. Truly cares about his students and goes way out of his way to listen to our opinions and concerns. Tries to do what is best for the students. Test in the beginning were very easy and fair. Later tests were more difficult but still fair.
Gives good feedback on HW and lets you keep submitting it until it's correct. Homework and final project involves coding in Python. Learned a lot about Finite Elements.

One of the absolute worst professors I've had, his lecture are very uninteresting with no real examples, only focusing on mathematical concepts. The HW is mostly just mathematical proofs rather than actual solid mechanics problems. If you actually want to learn the concept and how to apply it avoid professor.

Personally I don't feel the professor is prepared for his lectures. He would write his notes down with really bad handwriting. Most tutors were tough graders and deduced lots of points in some unnecessary parts. Tests are relatively doable and easy. Overall, I would recommend you to avoid this professor if you have a better choice.

I have enjoyed every CSE course until CSE 105 when I have Kyle Meyer for my instructor. His lectures are awful! Always jumping around lecture slides to correct himself minutes ago. It is such a frequent thing because he is never prepared for his lectures. I'm a senior and I've taken a lot of professors with bad handwriting and this one is the WORST

I personally felt like he explained the material pretty clearly, though it seems like most people disagree. The homework was pretty similar to lectures, and group work was allowed, which made it not too bad. My #1 complaint is that the professor is very unresponsive on Piazza and through email, which is frustrating when the whole class is remote.

I agree that he's not good on his lecture skills, but it would be a bit over to say he's the worst. Assignments are hard, but some of the questions are pretty insightful and don't seem to be copied from the Internet. Only watching lecture won't help you do the hw, you will need to read a lot from textbook, but finishing hw does help learning.

He's not a good teacher. I also only learned anything from this course because of the textbook. His lectures are impossible to follow, he just rambles on and on writing what he's saying. Super hard to understand. The homework is also really hard and they are largely hard to complete from watching lectures. Please change your course if you read this
HUM IS HARD :'(( But Prof Cox is a good choice; makes the quarter interesting and worthwhile.

It was Dr Cox's first time teaching HUM2 this quarter, but I really think he did a great job. His lectures got long a lot of times, but I really appreciated all the insight he gave me. His final exam is based off of his lecture. The TAs grade everything so your grade is up to them. I took HUM1+2 w/him and I can definitely say he's a solid choice.

Dr. Cox does a really good job in explaining concepts and themes during his lectures and those really help on the final exam. Some of his pre-recorded lectures were really long and it can get boring, but you get a lot out from his lectures. I gave a 4 in difficulty only because hum in general is difficult. Overall, he is a solid choice for hum 1!
Hum needs a lot of work, by Prof. Cox made it enjoyable and easy. He helped me when I needed, go to office hours and talk to him about anything.

I found Professor Cox's lectures to be very intriguing and had no problem staying focused even though he doesn't use slides. Attendance isn't mandatory for lectures, but everything he writes on the board (usually a few key concepts per class) you will need to know for the final. Overall I loved his class and absolutely would take his classes again!

He seems nice and accessible. But not really. When you attend the office hours online he gives ambiguous answers and so called "hints" and a lot of the help is given by IAs. He is trying but not really that good. I mean probably because this class is not that easy after all.

Professor Miller really isn't terrible! A lot of people here are complaining about how unstructured the class was but this is an upper division course you have to be accountable for yourself! Sure he wasn't the most accessible but he was very helpful at his office hours. Take notes on the lectures, do the learning objectives, and do his poll q's!

Let me just say: theres a reason everyone in BICD Fall 2020 gave this Professor a 1/5. Professor Miller models the qualities a professor shouldnt have in a time like this due to covid. Mainly, hes difficult to get ahold of and the exams are not representative of whats being taught (there are no curves either). Good luck to those taking him.

Although I did well in miller's class, I would not recommend him to anyone. He is completely inaccessible outside of class since he never responds to emails, his exams are unnecessarily tricky, and his lectures are long and messy. He never provides a straight forward answer to questions. Overall, I only succeed due to the help of my TA.

Told us I might make it a no-fault final if you scored lower on it than the midterm, never did. Doesn't curve and since some people excelled in the final than the midterm, I among others got full letter grade to half a letter grade down. Very few A's. Don't take him.

As long as you complete the HW and understand the notes you should be fine. The HW is usually way harder than the exams and material covered. However, the HW is based off textbook problems so if you have a solutions guide to the textbook you will do well. Attendance is also not mandatory nor needed as long as you read the notes before you start HW.

Lectures are a little fast but not too bad, he posts his notes after. Quizzes are just like lecture examples so pretty easy. Super lenient bc covid, hw was 50% and quizzes and final the other 50% no fault final too

I have mixed feelings about Professor Stapleton. He is a super nice guy and clearly cares about his students, but he makes the class too easy. I had to basically relearn all of this course's content for 20E, because he really only covered the most basic forms of this content. I definitely didn't learn as much as I should from his course.

It had been a long time since I did any calculus, so I was worried I wouldn't understand the material. This professor made lectures clear and his quizzes followed the examples from the lecture, most of the time. I do not regret choosing his course.
Very easy A, and his lectures were extremely helpful and basically allowed ez 100s on quizzes.

This is my second class with Dave. This man has changed my lifefor the better! He is a tough grader, but I cannot imagine my time at UCSD without having taken him. His lectures are captivating, he listens to his students, and he really wants you to succeed. His material(s) are accessible and relevant. Please take any class you can with him!

This is my second class with Dr. Frederick and it was my favorite of the quarter once again. He gave us the option of not having to attend any lectures and submit an individual project or mandatory attendance for lecture and a group project. Very interactive with great guest speakers. Homework takes longer than you'd think but very fair.

Professor Dave is one of the most engaging professors at UCSD. This is not an easy class, you need to put in the work, but a good grade is achievable if you try. Professor Dave is passionate and makes the class fun. Youll gain valuable skills from this course, and also hear some great jokes.

I was really dreading having to take a lab course because it seems scary, but the way he broke down the components in research really helped me understand how a lab is really supposed to be run. Engaging research topics, and the interactive parts were actually helpful.

Professor Frederick is funny and makes class engaging. He truly cares for his students. I also love the way he structured the research paper. We were able to work on the paper throughout the whole quarter rather than working on the entire paper in a short period of time. Study guides were also so much better than exams. I hope I can take him again!

This prof still doesnt know how to teach, write homeworks, or write tests. She manages to not explain anything well and then make the tests and homework extra confusing, both gramatically and mathematically. Avoid this prof if you can.

I love this class and Prof Puha. The material makes sense if you think about it in a logical financial way. Puha writes the important stuff from the previous lecture on the board in the beginning which helps get you started for the day. One HW problem on each hw comes directly from the notes so you have examples of what she is asking for.
Overall, she is nice and responsible. She did talk a little fast while answering questions, but you can learn a great deal from her if you work hard.

The worst professor I have ever had. She does not know how to teach, and her homework and exam questions really confused me (I do not know what she means at all). You need to spend a quite long time on her class. Aviod her!

She does not know how to teach. She CAN NOT write HOMEWORK and EXAMS. The questions are always confusing and most don't make sense grammatically nor mathematically. She posts remainder homework questions TWO days before the homework is due. Her office hours don't help either. I have a great love for maths and I think she made me doubt my passion.

He is the worst professor I had at UCSD. He even failed to give one of the students their OSD accommodations. He barely teaches, never responds, and has exams that are unnecessarily difficult. UCSD would be better off without this professor.

This class was TERRIBLE! The professor doesn't lecture well, you basically have to rely on the readings to understand anything he's talking about. He didn't seem to care much about students, and constantly posted multi-part lecture videos late in succession to each other which gave a lot of us anxiety about learning material in time for tests.
Doesnt teach anything. Must do all the reading to pass. Tests are so detailed you cant skip over anything in lecture or in the readings. Not an easy elective. Waste of a class
Professor definitely knows his material. Makes the class very easy. Quizzes in class but aren't to kill you just to know you read. Show up and you'll be fine!

Professor is willing to yell at you in the middle of class for not doing well without consideration of the student's circumstances, responses through emails are disrespectful and low effort, will also change class environment to just look good in front of the department,, and establishes a guideline that no student can earn more than 95 on hw.

Many times she just talked about how good is she , how good is her son which does not relate to the class at all . It was a big mistake I took her class .just a waste of time . She is not an organize person , boring class and stressful classes . Please go to find a nice professor to take. avoid this professor.
she likes to talk about herself the whole time

Intermediate class. Requires so many presentations. It's better if u speak and read fluently. Learning about Vietnamese is fun though. Co KimLoan is very passionate about her teachings. She really talks to us like a family member or like a mom. She lectures us about life and about knowing ur roots. If you're viet, definitely take it to learn more!
Nice and fun class, not so bad, but it's nice to know some vietnamese before going in

Takes 2 weeks to grade a simple homework assignment, 3 for tests. Poli 30 is a class of semantics, and professor Butler is an apathetic man who has no time to explain all of the nuances. TA's carried the course. He has like 8 or 9 TA's split up doing so much. I think he's condescending too. His lectures are like 7 minutes though?

the only thing hilarious about this professor is their grading system and how they word questions. unnecessarily hard class simply because the questions on all of their homework and quizzes are worded in the most confusing structure. the content isn't difficult to understand the real struggle is to understand what the prof is asking for

Maybe the professors/TA's for my classes this semester are having a rough quarter because honestly, the class is unorganized on canvas, grading is slow, and overall just an OK class. My biggest complaint is that I didn't receive a grade for any homework assignment before the midterm so it was a struggle to see what I needed to work on.

super funny, uses jokes and personality to make lectures more engaging. gives out prizes for answering questions. no pressure to get stuff right, if you don't know it's no big deal. material is pretty easy as long as you know what the scientific method is and how to do simple math

I've never taken a stats class before this course and I found it to be pretty simple. He grades by 4 homework assignments, a midterm, the final exam, and attendance to sections. The HW doesn't take much time and is relatively simple. The hardest part about this course is definitely the tests, you must do the readings and practice problems for them.

He's the best TA the Chem Dept has ever had. He was so clear with every concept that he taught in class, and created such genuine interest in the course. I am now motivated to make pursue Chemistry and pursue my career in science. And I owe it all to him. He also took notes and paid attention to every single student in theclass. Strongly recommend!

Professor Gilson's Molecular Simulations Lab is one of the best STEM classes I've ever taken in 6 years as an engineering student. From course policies to lecture quality to Professor Gilson's kind and inclusive manner, it's clear that the goal of this class is to enable as wide a range of students to learn and succeed as possible.

Zirui is a super diligent TA, and he is very hard-working. I can still remember the first time when I saw him in his office hour, he helped me a lot by offering decisive ideas about how to study better. His kindness and zealous in studying affect me a lot. Of course, he literally is a top student at UCSD. I really appreciate his effort here.
Best tutor for DSC20 & 30; I will receive F without him :) Strongly recommend.

Worst Professor ever. His requirement reading are 4 books and each book around 400 or more pages, and lots of option books. He never give us the clear title of book just simply show the author, everytime when I search the book will spent about 30 minutes not include read. His term paper needs four resources and trust me it will spent you 48 hours.

Horrible Professor! Doesn't care about students at all, his mission is to bullet his lecture and leave HW to students. One thing that needs to mention when he talks you will hear for example: "Hong kong history, eh eh eh eh eh eh enter a new era ".

Prof. Zhang is very keen on his research interest on World Literature. As a pinoeer scholar of Chinese literature and cinema, he is extremely knowledgeable and good at answering questions with no mincing words. I highly recommend him to all students who share the same interests.

Your grade depends on your TA, and if you're not lucky, you're TA will be nit-picky on every mistake you make. Don't bother talking to the professor, unless you've talked to the TA first. The TA will do everything in their power to not give you the perfect score. Although the professor's nice, the TAs try to make this class harder than needed.
Grades depend on TA. Not much work to do.

I really dont know what the other ratings are talking about. She was very rude, and inaccessible, and played favorites in a way that made me incredibly uncomfortable. Glad she is gone from this school and has left elsewhere.

Eliasson is probably the best professor in the department. She is really passionate about teaching and it really comes through in her lectures. OH are basically mandatory to do well on HW so start early and ask for help. She and her TAs are very approachable, but be prepared to spend lots of time on dynamics. Lots of extra credit opportunities too!

She gives pretty good lectures. The material is hard and there's no assigned book so you need to go to class and pay attention. If you're stuck, her office hours and TAs are pretty good. Overall, definitely recommend. One of the better professors I've had.

Dynamics alone is a VERY difficult class, but Dr. Eliasson explains it in a way that makes it easier to understand. That said, going to office hours is absolutely crucial for this class. It's pretty much the equivalent of two classes in terms of workload and the tests were extremely difficult (but there is a generous curve at the end)

Veronica is so far the best professor I encountered for my MAE classes. She has very clear and helpful lecture note which is rare to find in this school. Have to admit that her materials and tests are very tough, so dont get too frustrated if you dont do well. Just go to her office hours and she will help you a lot.

Professor Roy is a great lecturer and seems to care about his students. Grades are based on five multiple choice quizzes and biweekly assignments. The quizzes are very straightforward and graded fairly. Overall, the class is not too difficult and the material is super interesting!

He's such a sweet guy and very clear in his teaching style. It's not an easy A, but if you're interested in ecology it's a fantastic class, one of my favorites at UCSD. I recommend going to class because it makes it more enjoyable, but it's not necessary. Lots of memorization, but I learned a ton! Highly recommend!

Great prof! Only two exams and they were representative of the lecture material. As long as you read over the slides a couple of times, you should be ok. The articles for discussion are interesting if you are into ecology, but they aren't necessary in order to get a good grade. I would definitely take him again!

Really enjoyed Dr Roy and the class (EBE major bias!). His lectures are interesting, sometimes I got a little sleepy but overall he is a good lecturer and funny. Test questions come from slideslectures and are tough but not impossible and he curves at the end. A lot of reading but most of it was supplemental (ie not required!). I'd take him again

Still have yet to receive my final grade for this class, but this was probably one of the more tedious classes I've taken here at UCSD. ALOT of memorizing, have to reread the lectures many times. Would recommend going to class since he didn't podcast. Personally, I would say to avoid taking this classavoid this professor.

This guy's class is a total bummer. GPU programming is a complex and interesting topic, and this guy's class just dances around the concepts. Grading also makes no sense at all. Do not take. (Easy to get a good grade, though)

There is no way to gauge what your grade will be in this class. Quizzes are stacked on top of homeworks and no feedback is given for any of the assignments. Even for the midterm project, no rubric is given, so you think you are meeting all of the requirements, but will most likely get below a B on it. Youtube will teach you better. Not a GPA boost

The material is not hard, but you probably won't get an A either. The quizzes involve debugging code and drawing diagrams using PowerPoint... Grading guidelines are left vague. He curves, so even with your 93% you might still get a B. He's been teaching for several years, but handles the class like it's his first quarter here. Would avoid.

The whole class is designed to set you for failure and give you lower scores. Contradicts his own instructions. Be prepared for bad essay scores, because this is how class is designed. You can't get a good score, because next weeks assignments are based on correcting the mistakes.
He may be tough teacher and a tough grader, but if you want to pass once and for all take him. i took SDCC1 my second time with him and passed. HIGHLY RECOMMEND him.

Follow his instruction and you will pass, that's for sure! You have to understand all his concepts, and by doing so, you will improve drastically through the quarter. He is extremely strict, though. However, he concerns your grade much more than the other teachers do. Take his class, and do your work, you will pass this class.
He does have a high passing rate, but that can't be an excuse of his unpleasant or even insulting way of talking.

This class is a lot of work and you will likely get some bad essay scores, but don't let that be discouraging. Prof. Smith genuinely cares about his students and wants everyone to pass on the first try. I wouldn't have passed without taking his class. Best professor.

Always goes over her lecture time. She'll state "Opps I went 10 minutes this lecture, sorry," yet she does nothing to fix it. I understand it's recorded but each of those 10 minutes add up. If it were in person she wouldn't ask us to stay an extra 10 minutes. Condense your videos if necessary before posting. Also doesn't post lectures on exact day.

Teaches wrong ideologies to students. Promotes female students while shames males. The class was a contradiction with reality of life. Women prefer their male romantic partners to be taller than them, make more money than them, be physically and emotionally stronger than them, but yet they want equality at the same time, yeah makes perfect sense!

Professor Dauber-Griffin is seldom prepared to teach. Her lectures are often not about the material. She often goes on talking about irrelevant topics and personal problems. Her delivery of class material is often driven by emotions rather than logic.

I don't agree with my classmate. I can just imagine how difficult it is to teach this class. She did a very good job using her personal experience on occasion to illustrate the theoretical concepts. She did not go "on and on and on". She explains theory and concepts very well. I would always take her again.

Awesome concept for a class. However, Andrea didn't really teach. She went on and on about her personal problems every lecture. She also wasn't clear on what we had to study for the final. Her answer was that we had to study "everything". Thus, with her lack of explaining things, I'm just hoping to pass. Take any other Professor but this one!!!

She was the best professor I have ever had at usd. She is so educated and attending her classes via zoom genuinely felt like I was watching a movie. That's how good of a story teller she is! She made the concept very simple. Tests and quizzes were so straight forward. Her class did not cause stress, as you learn vital life lessons from from her.

Worst machine learning class in UCSD. He barely taught anything in the class with helpless lectures. Don't expect to learn anything from his class because he did not even have a good understanding of what he taught.

Professor Milstein is an amazing lecturer. He is very clear and pauses often to make sure everyone understands. His tests are tough, but he is very interested in student success and is an incredibly fair grader, and he is more than happy to help with understanding after exams. Definitely take advantage of office hours and ask questions often.
Milstien is one of the toughest professors in UCSD. His exams are demoralizing. However, he s an awsome teacher and is very helpful to students.

This is,without a doubt, one of UCSD's best professors. Explains the material clearly and is really invested in student learning. If you have questions he is very helpful and strongly encourages questioning. Step by step instructions. An overall treasure to UCSD!

Amazing professor because he is able to bridge is intelligence and experience to students unlike many research oriented professors. If you're confused at all, just ask him a question. His tests are not confidence boosters, but the grading is fair.

one of the best professors in UCSD, no wonder why COMM is the best program in ECE dept. Although exams are difficult, you definitey learn a lot. He is very willing to help students out too, He tries to answer all the questions students ask and give the best explaination.

Not the best lecturer in my opinion. The lecture dose not prepare you for homework and exams. Had to reread the textbook after each lecture to finish the homework. There are quizzes every week. Trick questions, but not too difficult. Make sure to double check. Finals are not easy.
Professor Arovas is an amazing lecturer. The exams are fair, and the lecture notes are great.

Bad lectures, but fantastic lecture notes. Lecture is really fast and he glosses over the difficulty, so it's hard to know what should be obvious and what's subtle. For me the clarity in the notes more than made up for the lack of it in the lecture, and 110B was one of my favorite classes.
Was very rude in office hours whenever I talked to him 1 on 1. Also the whole class grade was based on one final exam

If you are taking ECE 103 with him, you can study from the required text since that text is a gold for qualitative aspect on semiconductor. If you are taking ECE 135A with him, good luck with readings (different notation from 7-8 references). Professor Tu is a very nice researcher that lacks the ability to explain introductory level knowledge.

Very nice professor, but you're going to need the book because lectures are horrible. Different notations all over the place from different books, and very mono-tone and difficult to keep attention. Exams are not too bad: Although average is low, curve is lenient. Go to discussion because TA practically gives answers to HW and insight on exams.

Worst professor/teacher I've had in my life. Can not explain a single thing without confusing you even more. His PP notation is 100% different from the course textbook which makes it impossible to do well on the exams even when you teach yourself from the textbook. He doesn't do one thing right as a professor and yet is super tough on grading.

Awful lecturer. Unclear explanations, and frequently teaches concepts incorrectly and then backpedals to clarify, causing lots of confusion. Homework has little to do with what was taught in class. He's not malicious and is totally willing to help students, but is unfortunately unable to.

The labs are really long and annoying, but that isn't the professor's fault. The lectures were okay, and the final exam was graded a bit harshly. Overall not a bad professor, I'm just glad I'm done with this class.

she was empathetic to students during covid, making the final optional and ensuring she and the TAs were accessible. my TA was fair and helpful, and from what i heard most of the TAs were the same; i def recommend clearing up any doubts at office hours. she curved the class fairly and the labs had clear grading criteria.

Heard many rough things about PHYS2CL but this professor is great. She's relatively new but her lectures are great refreshers of PHYS2B and definitely prepares me to do the labs. The grades depend on your TA but she curves the lab sections so everyone is on an equal playing field even if you have a harder TA (just try to be above average)

This was the most interesting class I've taken at UCSD. This class highlights social justice in the world. It was intellectually stimulating and allowed for a lot of discussion between students. Professor Blaise was a great listener and was genuinely interested in what students had to say. He created a safe space for students to openly talk.

Professor Blaise was one of the nicest professors I have ever had. The class consisted of 4-5 mandatory zoom lectures, weekly discussions, and a 5-6 page essay for the midterm and the final. He is always accessible to answer questions and he gives you his number if you want to contact him and receive a quick response. Loved his class a lot!

Dr. Blaise is one of the most respectable professors I've ever come across at UCSD. He truly cares about his students, and verbalizes it frequently. Class consists of doing readings, submitting weekly discussion posts graded by completion, two papers, and showing up to lecture. Easy A if you try, and you learn a lot about social justice and equity

Both classes were very eye opening and important. I definitely agree with Prof Blaise that participating in discussions helps us remember these topics for a lifetime. Since then, I was also able to serve as a TA for Professor Blaise and he has been a great mentor ever since. I definitely rec this class!

Boring lecturer. Political agenda demonstrated within every assignment. Class was not interesting nor intellectually stimulating. Grading was all over the place (TA didn't know what she was doing). May problems with his computer(viruses would turn off laptop lol). Just appeal to his ideals and you'll get an A. Attendance is unfortunately mandatory

Professor Babin is a great professor. His module system was amazing and he was super passionate and knowledgable about the subject. A lot of your grade does depend on 2 papers though, but if you're lucky with your TA it should be fine. Quizzes and tests are super easy as long as you do the modules! Overall, I would highly recommend his class!

Class is pretty easy. I didnt take any notes and barely listened to lecture videos. This class is organized very well for an online format because of his module system. Midterm and Final were easy. The 2 papers required some effort but was very doable. Overall easy A. Teacher is clearly passionate about this topic so thats great.
Just a fun guy and is really enthusiastic about music. Took a course on Bowie by him and loved it!
Professor Babin was a great professor and his class was very enjoyable!

Professor Babin adapted to the online format the best out of any professor I've taken at UCSD so far. The module system is awesome, and all of the content is super interesting. Essays are easy so long as you've been enjoying the music, and it's great music, so that isn't difficult at all. Great choice for a DEI.

This has been the most inefficient lectures I've seen at UCSD. The professor wrote everything from scratch in plain math during the live lecture which was very time-consuming. I'd rather prefer slides that have math derivations pre-written on them.

I think Professor Chaudhuri is a great lecturer. Her handwritten notes in particular are FANTASTIC - they are detailed, well organized and easy to read. I wasn't a fan of the class structure - 7 exams worth 70% of your grade was very stressful. The exams were challenging but doable in my opinion - plus the class is graded on a generous curve.

She is overall a nice person but her class needs a major re-structure. Her lectures are vague and have no relations to her homework. The quizzes and exams test knowledge nowhere to be found in lecture or the homework, that means if you miss a tiny detail in lecture or you did not dig in by yourself, you will likely to fail her quizzes.
Mediocre teaching. Many quizzes have no relation to the topics taken in class.

7 quizzes, 5 hws, and a final. Exams are fair and straightforward. Hws are easy if you start them early. Drop one quiz and hw. Lectures go into mechanics of supervised learning algorithms. She also covers related linear algebra and statistical concepts of the algorithms but doesnt go super deep. Very friendly to students questions.

Homework is difficult and time consuming. Most of the examples solved in the slides have mistakes which she mentions in class but are not corrected when posted on canvas. Two full chapters from the book were skipped assuming that we all took Math 18 which is not a prerequisite for this class. Self studying is required for this class.

She uses a lot of "ummm" during the lecture and can't explain everything correctly. Her quiz are very tricky and it is really hard to do not lose point. Some of them even didn't mentioned in the classes. And she made lots of mistakes on PPT every lecture, even for important procedure. She is not a good teacher.
3 question quizzes that are worth 20% of the grade and a 40% final. Doesn't teach half the stuff on the quizzes and doesn't offer much help on homework either.

Professor Tamam is so great and she is super patient at any time. Besides, you can learn a lot in her office hours. You can easily get A if you keep following the class and do the hws. Midterms are also important for the final grade. Anyway, highly recommend her!
Self studying is what you will have to do for this class because you wont learn from the lectures.

Super boring lectures. Graded on only a midterm and final paper. Crazy long, boring readings but i didnt do any of em and still managed to get an A. Boring class overall but if you do well on the tests you should be fine. Attendance not mandatory.

Stay away from this class if your TA is Mike because he is a horrible TA and horrible grader. Unclear grading criteria. Professor said one thing and TA did another. Although the professor knows the material well, the way things are graded will throw you off. Many students questioned the grading. I would not recommend this class to anyone.

Prof. Chandler is a somewhat boring lecturer who paces his lectures very slowly. The class was very easy. One in class midterm that everyone did well on and a take home paper final (two 3 page essays). Interesting material that should be an easy A but also a rather boring teacher.

His lectures are extremely boring, especially if you're unfamiliar with foreign affairs and politics. Professor Chandler knows the material well, and kept us informed with current events. I stopped going to class toward the end of the quarter and I kept up with the readings, power points, and current events and I was fine. Take home final a plus

Really knows the material, but for some he could be very boring. His slides are slightly disorganized; he likes to jump between different powerpoints, but I do like that he draws from current events. In class mid-term and take home finals were graded very generously for me, but you def. have to study for them.

Very clear, considerate and nice prof. Dr. Wang has truly inspired me in this course, and goes over many fascinating current research topics pertaining to sensory systems. Offered extra credit, had clear test questions, and very clear lectures. Was always ready to help students with their questions and make the class better overall. Def recommend!

Great professor and I cool guy. He's really nice and approachable, but does have an accent. Speaks slowly and repeats himself so that you can understand the hard concepts or catch words you don't understand. Is concerned about the student learning and tests are lecture based and pretty straight forward. Good class.

Beware - He does have a Chinese accent. He also wants you to read all chapters, but he tells us to do so so that no one will complain about anything s/he did not understand because of his accent. Exams are short and completely lecture based, and he sets curve to B/B+, not B-. Some of this neuro stuff are so complicated that even he doesn't know all

This prof is one of the only profs Ive had during Covid that genuinely sought to make the class as doable as possible. The quiz questions really prepare you for the midterms and finals. The TA review sessions were great. The lectures are very straightforward and informative. Would highly recommend this prof!

Took her in spring 19, during the pandemic. Class structure was very clear, 90% of the total grade is made up of exams and the rest with quizzes. She explains the material well and always answers questions. Slides have all the information you need for the open book/note exams.

Do not take this professor. Her lectures are unhelpful and reading off the slides is better than trying to listen to her. She is clearly knowledgeable about her field but she is not a good teacher. Expect independent study. You could know all the content and still get B on the exam because the confusing wording. There are better professors at UCSD.

Professor Gershon is a great professor. She's very accommodating with the current COVID/online situation with the class format: pre-recorded lecture broken up into 20-30 mins, weekly interesting readings, weekly surveys (ungraded quizzes), weekly online participation, a group project, and a final exam. Her lectures are always engaging and concise.

Relatively new but one of the best professors I've had. Books are fairly priced and actually enjoyable to read. Entertaining and informative lectures, fair papers and exams, fun and interesting group projects, and she really cares about her students. As long as you put in the work, you should be able to get a good grade in her class!

I really enjoyed this class with Sofia. She's very kind and caring about her students' wellbeing, learning, and was very accommodating with the COVID/online situation. She has a variety of exercise activities in class outside of just textbook activities and speaks Spanish very clearly and at the right pace for a beginner student.

Loved taking Spanish with Profesora Lana! She's very kind and I loved that she was always willing to stay behind class to answer any lingering questions. Be aware that when taking LISP 1AX, from day 1, everything is in Spanish. All instructions are in Spanish and you even have to use Spanish when asking questions. Great immersion!
Prof Edelman gives excellent guidance and makes it easy for you to structure your papers. He asks the right questions and sets you up to succeed.
One of the kindest, most caring professors. So approachable and wants to see his students do well.

I love it when professors want to see you succeed and do well. Prof Edelman presents his work very thoughtfully and seems to care about his students. He is very efficient and gives good guidance. He's an older teacher and doesn't like technology so don't expect PowerPoints, etc. I'm taking another class he is teaching.

Professor Edelman wants you to succeed. His lectures are a bit old school, but it is not mandatory to attend. His essay questions guide you to be successful and he gives you many prompts to choose from. He grades quickly and is very efficient. Highly recommend this class.

Not the class I expected it to be unfortunately. Lectures are purely verbal from the professor with no material to go back on and review, as there are no slides, class page or podcast. Many books are required and most have no more than 2-3 chapters of reading in them. Just not really worth the time, effort or money for a disorganized class.

As people mentioned, his lectures are disorganized and really hard to follow. The slides only provide little information and have little connection with what he's talking about, making his lectures a hearing test. Exams test heavily on details, specific sentences. Though the topic of this class is interesting, taking the class is suffering.

DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE ONLINE... as someone else mentioned, he talks very fast and mumbles making it very hard to understand him. Out of all my professors he was the only one that couldn't figure out closed captions on zoom which was unfortunate. You're only graded on exams where you have to remember a specific line he said, which was incoherent.

He has an accent, which isn't his fault, but he speaks very fast and mumbles as well. He often rambles and goes on tangents. Takes him 2.5 hours to get through 17 slides (most of which have no words on them). Tests ask very specific questions that require you to remember a specific sentence he said in class. Very difficult to follow. Can get boring

If the class is listed at 5pm, plan to see him at 6pm. I took 169 and then 129 -- absolutely the same course, likely teaches two out of obligation, I had to listened to the same jokes from the 90s for two quarters in a row. What did I learn? Get a PhD and coast on that while disregarding students' time and no one will bat an eye.

This class was very challenging (and unorganized), however it was the most interesting class I've taken at UCSD. Dr. Rama is definitely knowledgeable and likes probing the minds of his students. 1 MT, 1 Final, some extra credit SONA. You have to go to lecture to pass. Reading the book(s) will help boost your grade. Hard exams, curved well.

Paul is the homie. Pretty straightforward class. Show up, skim the readings and you'll be fine. Paul genuinely cares about his students too, so it's pretty easy to talk to him. The weekly quizzes suck but are manageable.
quizzes out of two points suck.

Paul is such a gem. He is extremely knowledgable about all aspects of urban studies and planning and has connections in the industry like no one else. Expect guest speakers and group assignments. His teaching style is dependent on you caring about the material. If you aren't passionate about USP don't take the course, but if you are, he's the best!

I absolutely LOVED this class! I was a bio major (now a cog sci/psych major) and I found the public transportation class to be my favorite class I've taken. The small class size gives you lots of opportunity to interact with Paul directly. He's just the sweetest guy and you'll learn *so* much you never even considered about transportation. 10/10

Lectures are pretty structured and you can expect what to come. Learned a lot about public transportation which I would never have known if I didn't take the class. He is approachable and makes lectures casual, like a conversation. He has a lot of practical knowledge many academics don't. Would definitely take another class from him.

Lectures generally unrelated to the assignments, midterm, & final and are pretty boring. But, assignments themselves are easy and I barely watched lectures. Grading depends on the TA and section is required. She knows a lot about the topic but this class could be boring for someone not interested in experimental music.
A really nice professor who explains the course material clearly. Lectures can be a little fast paced but she uploads the ppt slides ahead of time for everyone.

Professor Swan taught the best class I've taken online. He makes going to zoom fun since the material is very interact. Class consisted of weekly quizzes, a final, and making a video presenting your favorite illusion! All the exams/quizzes are open book with no time limit! Take him, he's the best.

Jonathan is an amazing singing instructor. I've only taken his class once, but I already know I'm going to try to take it as many times as I can. I had never sung before, but in the span of 10 weeks, he took me from being a complete novice to being able perform in front of my friends. Highly recommended!

I took Jonathan a while back for MUS 4 and just had to come and write how amazing it was. Classical music was not something I expected to be my favorite music class but Jonathan did a great job at being entertaining. I truly recommend him as a professor.
A nice and caring person; my favorite music course so far

Professor Jonathan is passionate about what he is teaching and I truly enjoyed his lectures. For online courses, there are a few essays required. The assignments did take some time, but if you follow with his lectures and listen to all the materials, it's not hard and even inspiring.

Jonathan is a great professor! His lectures were super interesting, easy to follow, and thought-provoking. He always explained musical terminology that would be new to many students. There were 4 writing assignments that were pretty straightforward. He always provided feedback and was accessible to students. Overall, he is a fantastic instructor.

so he is a really nice and empathetic professor, but his lectures never really helped me understand the topics. it always felt that he would expand on topics before even explaining them. perhaps this is just what does not work for me, but still a genuinely good professor!
Awesome professor, super knowledgeable of what he is teaching and very kind guy. Midterms are pretty difficult imo so be sure do keep up with the readings.

The prof. knows what he's talking about and is passionate. Lectures aren't mandatory but very helpful. Get ready to read a LOT. The midterms are take-home essays. Overall, the class really makes you think. There're only 20-30 students so it's a more intimate setting. I'd say this class is difficult but doable.
Professor Rutherford is super clear and helpful, best I ve ever had so far. I got a nice TA so the grading was generous... ;)

Excellent professor! Slides are extremely helpful for taking notes and studying for finals... Of course a lot of grade is based on essays so stay close to your TA's... class is not too hard though and as long as you read the books and keep up with lectures you are bound to do all right.

Kamioka sensei is really nice and this is a typical but sorta fun japanese class to take. Felt comfortable in her class and she showed some interesting japanese culture content too which I really appreciated.

She really cares about her students and the subject she teaches. During this difficult time, she does everything she can to improve our learning experience. When I took 10A with her, I filled out a reflection saying more pop culture references would make the class more fun, and in 10B this is immediately implanted. Tests are easy,a lot of homework
Wonderful professor! I love Kamioka-sensei and I took her for Japanese 10A and 10C. She is very nice and caring and doesn't mind joking around sometimes. Highly recommend!

Kamioka-sensei is really kind, she tries to not only teach you the language but to teach you about Japanese culture. This course depends a lot on what TA you get for tutorials, but having Kamioka-sensei as your lecturer will help you learn the basis to be succesful on your quizzes and tests.

GREAT sensei! She wants you to get good grade and gives out extra credit generously at the end of the quarter if you are willing to make efforts. She is really kind and cares about her students. The class was fun and I learned a lot. I got nearly full marks. HIGHLY recommended.

Marta is an amazing lecturer and her passion for the material really comes through. I highly recommend taking a class with her if you have the chance. She gives great feedback and replies to emails very quickly. I took her class online and she did extra things to make us feel more connected which was really nice.

I love Marta! She explains things so clearly and is always available if you have questions. Shes so nice and always tries to make jokes and connect with her students. I really loved her class! The material we covered was also very interesting.
