I have taken a lot of courses in different fields and in comparison to many others, one thing is clear: Dr. Collett really cares about her class and students. She was always helpful and welcoming and even went beyond regular office hours to help students in need. Very approachable and seems to put a lot of effort into her classes. Challenge but fun
Great teacher. Highly recommend

Material seemed hard at first but she gave us a lot of opportunities to do well and exams were fair. She would also take time out of her day just to have additional office hours, which were very helpful. Told the class what to study for on the final, which definitely made it much easier. A super caring professor, definitely one of my favorites!

Best prof I've had at UCSD to date. Material was clearly & effectively taught, online tools were used as advantageously as possible, and assignments were helpful & fun! Prof is super caring and attentive to students' learning, actively implemented our feedback, and thoughtfully dealt with any student's personal concerns. Take anything he teaches!!!

As a professor he's ight, however he is obnoxious and overdramatic when it comes to students who try to speak their mind in regards to the course content I tried meeting him outside of the classroom, but he didn't seem to care. I have nothing to bad to say about Comm professors at UCSD, but this guy is clearly privilege and not what everyone thinks

My favorite professor at UCSD so far. Great professor, even better person. I didn't read the textbooks and still did well, but I also attended every lecture, so you definitely need to do one or the other at the very least.
Interesting and inspirational, get ready to work with others a Lot.

No midterms or final, but many pop quizzes and an oral exam is what your grade consists of. Quizzes are composed of BORING and LONG readings. They're like literature. Participation matters in DI so try to speak. The professor himself is chill, but not knowing my grade was scary and annoying. Group projects were interesting, but choose chill people.

Plenty of time-consuming group projects given. Pop quizzes weren't hard, but were based on long readings. Did not enjoy oral exams at all. Lectures were actually interesting and fun listen to. But, I felt like I was going through his class blindfolded. There was no clear grading criteria and I barely got any of my grades back during the course.

Some small assignments that were pretty fun, but the midterm and final make up a bulk of the work and the midterm at least was graded by the TAs really harshly. But work pays off, and he's a great prof.

One of my favorite professors. Very funny and has a dry sense of humor. He's also super approachable and helpful. Midterm was easy if you study off of his study guide and just pay a decent amount of attention in class. Readings are long but not completely necessary to do well in class
i luv u prof hajnal

Such a bad professor. He lectures too fast, doesn't explain enough and the midterm was much harder than he let on that it would be. The average grade was a 74 but he didn't curve it at all. He does not help students much and does not teach at all. The TAs are non-existent. Change your concentration if this is your professor for this class.

A White academic who behaves with little regard for the lives and experiences of actual people of color. Painfully out of touch. Questions asked in class frequently erased the humanity of marginalized people, for example posting images of random people of color and asking "what's their race?" as a class discussion question

Jim short is a great and funny teacher. His grading on papers can sometimes seem arbitrary but never super hard. The class was super interesting and you definitely left it actually learning something new

I had him for for TDGE 10 over the summer and I overall really enjoyed the class. His lectures were really engaging and he sets up his online classes in a very organized way that made it easy to stay on top of things. He had weekly quizzes but as long as you focused in class, read the plays and watched the movies attentively you'll do well.

Jims abilities fall short, in all different ways. He is at teaching and doesnt care about his students. He also gives out grades arbitrarily, entirely based on his mood. Since he is short with everyone constantly, he doesnt give out good grades. AVOID Mr. Shorts class, choose somebody else. UCSD is not short of professors.

It is very ridiculous that Jim always smiled and said nice fake comments on your paper but in the end there is only a B for everyone. and C+. This is just unhelpful for students to understand the problems they have and improve, instead it seems like a tacit revenge for the teacher on his students because the class is so boring. No one enjoyed it.

I had him for fall 2020. Really caring professor who broke down concepts to make sure students truly understood the material. Aside from kudu hw, there is a workbook with problems that you can work on (optional) but I think it can really help ease you into the hw which can be difficult. Quizzes are like the hw. Overall, a great prof.
Too much busywork that's not applicable to exams, doesn't grade partial credit on exams. Whatever you do, even if it's following all the right steps, it will be wrong on some technicality. Avoid.

Amazing and caring prof. A true, true gem. Had him in the spring and he was just awesome. He honestly made me enjoy physics! I would truly recommend him. He clearly wants to see his students succeed and will always take the time to explain something to you

The professor himself seems nice and wants to help students, but his lectures are slow and boring. The class is difficult, especially if you fall behind. I would recommend a different professor if you want more energy in the lectures. However, I took this online so it may be different in-person.

Absolutely useless. Only goes over (if you are lucky) 1 example that is super easy but then hits you with some very hard problems for the HW and quizzes. You could replace this guy with a gust of wind and get an equal learning experience

Quizzes were fair and sometimes easy. Homeworks were easy. The final was more challenging but still doable. Lectures were great, sometimes too fast, but I just reviewed my notes after and was fine. She doesn't post her completed slides so definitely watch lecture recordings. Maybe I just get Econ easier than some but her class was enjoyable to me.

Unclear grading system. Doesnt do much for students even though its a pandemic. Only focuses on students who got good grades and bases her grading system off them. She goes too fast and her exams are too long. She did listen to feedback but it wasnt enough. I wouldnt have taken her if I knew how she was. Beware thats all ill say -cal student
queen. love her. made me like econ fr

She sped through lectures, made it extremely difficult to learn Econ for the first time, didnt upload completed notes, quizzes were impossible + the pace of lectures and difficulty getting help during COVID was extremely stressful. Youd probably be okay if youre good at Econ but if you have no prior knowledge at all, she is not the one for you.

I took her for Econ 1's summer session at UC Berkeley. Amazing prof and the class was so much easier than I thought it would be! Really good at explaining things, and the makeup of the grade was REALLY fair
SPEECHLESS! Comments down below are objective.

WARNING DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS 1. NO syllabus until week 5, the class reminded him like three or four times 2. Will NOT respond to your emails 3. NO office hour in the first three weeks 4. Change his assignment deadlines frequently/ add assignments all he wants 5. NO rubrics 6. Only grade 1 assignment till the end of the quarter

In my 4 years, the worst class I've ever taken at UCSD. To be fair, it's his first time teaching an undergrad course, but as of right now I would highly suggest you stay away until he finds his footing. I'm ripping my hair out trying to figure out what to do as lectures are pretty useless, and there is little feedback in terms of graded work.

One of the worst professors I've ever had. His lectures fall into 3 categories 1) Ramble on during the whole class about nothing relevant to the coursework 2) Show the class some graphs and wait for us to make our own conclusions instead of teaching us 3) Get bombarded with questions about his awfully written and ambiguous homework.

Professor Arreola is a great teacher and her classes are really fun and you learn a lot. I felt 10 times better at speaking, writing, and reading in Spanish by the end of the semester. Definitely recommend her and this class.

I did 100% online and there was a lot of reading and work on launchpad every week. You have to pay for a launchpad subscription!The exams were only one hour and the questions were made up to trick you and they were hard. It was interesting and I liked the book, but its a lot of work & reading so If You have little time etc go for another teacher!
She makes the material interesting. Attend lectures and read the articles which are pretty short and you can get an A. 2 midterms and a final. she is really nice and understanding

Professor Spilkin is amazing!!! She is one of the few teachers at UCSD who is down to earth and extremely easy to talk to!!! I have taken a few of her classes, and am glad I got to meet her and be in her classes. Love her!!!

Dr. Spiklin is the epitome of a bad professor.Her test questions are vague, unclear, and so specific to the point where she is no longer testing on your understanding of the material, but rather on the footnotes of an unimportant detail in the textbook. DONT TAKE HER! This class/ Dr. Spiklin is a waste of your time, effort and tuition.

Although the material seems pretty easy, her test questions are vague, tricky, and she asks overly specific questions that are pretty ridiculous. However, the material is interesting and easy to read so if you attend class and do the readings you'll get a good grade.

Professor Hartblay is honestly super understanding and does not make life extra difficult for her students. The content of her course is interesting and she encourages creativity with her assignment design. You should usually ignore reviews from lower year classes since many students from introductory courses whine after being caught for plagiarism

very interesting course and lots of readings but thats any course. Loved the content but the assignment was very complicated but she gives tons of feedback and provides help! she also makes the class atmosphere comfortable and fun. it is a discussion based course so be ready to participate a lot.

She is really slow with getting back to emails and returning marked assignments on time. Her lectures were interesting but she really needs to stop procrastinating and give marks back on time. It's easy to do well in her class if you like and good at creative writing.
unwilling to help, not understanding, just don't take her if you have better options...
Such a disaster Dont take him

This was one of my favorite classes ever taken. You must be ready to have a good understanding of inorganic chemistry to feel comfortable in the concepts, but the professor takes care to explain everything very thoroughly and answers all questions with clarity. Plus he is one of the top scientists studying the carbon dioxide system in seawater.

Take home midterm (33% of grade), open notes final (66% of grade). However, both of them were graded pretty hard. He speaks very fast during the lecture. Do the homework, even though not graded, one of them will appear on the exam. He has a British accent.

I never hated a professor like Curry Sean so much. I took his Math142B on Spring 2018. The course material was so difficult, and his explanation was so bad. I had to read the textbook by myself. Because of him, I did not graduate successfully, and I lost my summer holiday. Never ever took his class again.
He cares his students and wants everyone to succeed.
Super nice professor. Clear notes, decent homeworks, fair exams.

Good lecturer, but ran out of time going too in-depth into examples or answering questions. Math 20B is a HARD CLASS, and requires LOTS of work. It matters the work you put in more than who you have. The practice exams really helped with the midterms and final, and SI helped with understanding the homework and lecture examples.
The final exam is super hard. And the professor combined his office hours for two classes which makes it hard to ask questions for final exam

Seems like a nice guy but recorded lectures were extremely confusing. I had to basically teach myself. Thankfully there were a lot of extra credit points available or I would have completely failed. Homework took a very long time to complete.

Seems like a very nice, knowledgeable guy, but just wasn't prepared for online instruction. He occasionally posted slides and recordings but they weren't much help (just read them verbatim, overcomplicated). Read the textbook, do the Sapling HW, and refer to his notes if you need more help. LOTS of self-teaching is needed. HW load is manageable.

Professor Crowell just isn't prepared for online class at all. He didn't start posting lectures until Week 2, and never posted any lectures on time. By finals week, we still hadn't learned 3 of the chapters that were on the final. I'm literally studying chemistry during winter break because I'm so unprepared for my next chem class now.
literally had to teach myself the class from the textbook, i feel thoroughly unprepared for my next chem class

He is a talented researcher, but he has not prepared for online teaching. We had 3 chapters to go in the final week. If you have learned at least something about General Chemistry, then it's okay to take him. Otherwise you gotta avoid him.

Prof. Ostertag's lectures were really great! He explained the material very thoroughly and the homework wasn't that bad. The 3 scripting projects were quite challenging but starting early always helped. Overall, highly recommend!!
Highly Recommend!

Great professor who is eloquent with the subject at hand. Homework is not tough at all until you get to the 3 scripting projects, which should be treated like mini-PAs. His lectures are engaging and it's not so bad to sit through all 50 mins of it.
I highly recommend this professor if you are going to take CSE15L. Lectures are fun and interesting. Highly recommend this professor.

she is an amazing professor, you can tell she is really passionate about what she teaches and very knowledgeable as well. i had a lot of fun in her class because it was my only in-person one this quarter, the only thing is that we only had three assignments that our entire grade was based on, but as long as you pay attention in class you'll be fine
Great Professor! I also had him for Philosophy 101 and both classes were very engaging and enjoyable.

Nice guy. I like him a lot. Hes young and chill and makes jokes. His class is not the most interesting class out there but it is epistemology... His paper prompts are not so easy and the papers are ridiculously long.
Knows what he is talking about. Exams are fair. Would take again.

Great lecturer. He is very good at simplifying challenging course material. His expectations are tough but fair. He is approachable and friendly - always willing to meet outside of class and office hours. I highly recommend him.
No Comments

For online Fall 2020, this course was a breeze and required almost no studying with the open note quizzes/tests. However, he and his TA were super bad at responding to emails, which was frustrating. Grades were based on weekly quizzes, a midterm, and final, with SONA/cape/participation EC. I probably would've enjoyed this class more in person

He's a great lecturer but.... He's unorganized and unreachable. He didn't respond to questions on the discussion board. We believe he messed up our grades this quarter and he isn't getting back to us rn. He never responded to mine or my classmates emails throughout the quarter. It was impossible communicate with him (or his TA for that matter)

I loved Professor George. Hes hilarious and has the best stories. He makes class so enjoyable. I took his class during undergrad and HIGHLY recommend. He offered me a position in his research lab off campus at Scripps that I had to turn down (sadly) due to my student athlete commitments. He is a wonderful person and helped me believe in myself.

Pretty straightforward class. All the lectures are from previous class recordings that you can watch whenever. He hosts discussion Q&A's if you need help or have any questions. Its a lot of information but the material is interesting and the exams are open note.

Super cool prof, very important to attend lectures via podcast, if not in person. Slides super helpful. Class topics never boring, I think about the things I learned in this class every day, and I'm not even a psych major. 40% midterm, 60% final. Great lecturer.

lectures focus on a few key biomechanics concepts (ie stress, traction, strain). the 7 hws (50% of grade) consist of a physics & design problem. the physics problem can be hard since he doesn't go over how to solve problems in class. there are 2 timed, proctored quizzes (15% each) and final exam (20%). discussion is tedious, occasionally helpful.

He is a very knowledgeable professor and often talks about history of science, however, I didn't find his lectures useful for exams and homework problems(format very unique to the class). we didn't have any slides and the course overall was very disorganized. There wasn't any course schedule to study from the text.

The scope of this class was difficult to understand in one sitting, but his lectures and insight made it a little more convenient for us. Make sure not to fall behind, and you should find this class very practical. Attend OH, go to section - The TA we had (Aaron) did an unbelievable job! Recommended.
Great prof. knows his stuff well. very nice. very hard class thou. You have to got to every lecture and section to fully understand everything

Professor is an audible version of the textbook.  The ENTIRE quarter was spent doing nothing but deriving equations.  Exams cover material not covered in class...get ready to teach yourself a lot of rather difficult material.

Lawrence Saul knows his material - he focuses on making his class lecture heavy, so you should always watch them when you get the chance. Lots of homework, but it helps drill the material into your head.

I have been taken classes at UCSD for about 4 years, and Professor Saul along with this class is one of the best I have had. He explained concepts very well, and I learned a whole lot, even though I had some math background. Just be aware the weekly assignment takes time, and the final exam could take up to 12 hours to complete.

One of the best profs at UCSD. The amount of effort he puts into teaching is unmatched. He is super intelligent, humble and genuinely cares about students. He is really an inspiration. The Homeworks will take up a lot of time so be prepared to put in a lot of effort into this class. The grading curve is generous especially at lower grades.

A man has talent for research and wisdom of life. A sentence I just came up with. Have to comment somewhere haha. Even though it is torture for me to finish the looooong homework and take the loooong exam, I don't regret.

Great lecturer, but the homework is absurdly difficult and often has nothing to do with the lecture. The tests are so long that you'll be speed-writing through all of them and still not finish, which I found utterly ridiculous.
This professor was very kind and accommodating during these trying times. Im really happy I ended up taking her for MGT 166. I learned a lot from her.
Easiest class taken during online courses. She gave almost everyone an A. Dropped the other profs class for Lisa and it was a smooth ride. She is especially lenient because of the pandemic!

She's not a bad teacher, and is really interesting in the topic she teaches; she spent her life working in business ethics and retired to now teach about it. I do have a serious issue with how unfair of a grader she is. She added in random grading criteria halfway through the quarter, and even though I got 100% on all papers/exams, she gave me a B.

She thinks to be more ethic we should be vegetarian; pay more money to airline is greener. She says something like I don't know what you are talking about when students are presenting the team project. Grade hard for exams. Got full points on home assignment but still got bad grade. Our team is at the middle-upper level in the class but got C-.

Shaffer is knowledgeable of content and explains well. Really shows well-rounded analysis of ethics situations. Ethics isn't the most interesting but learned a few things. Clickers make you go to lecture for Partptn pts. Assignments and final are simple. TED is best friend in this class, all there. Easy class and good prof,  Take for Sixth GE.

As long as you do well on the homework, it is quite difficult to fail in this course. However, professor Deian Stefan has a tendency to either rush through lectures or to take too much time on certain material - nevertheless, he definitely knows what he is talking about and answers many questions in class. His CSE127 course is overall pretty easy.

The lectures were not podcasted and a bit hard to follow, but the final was pretty easy, tons of extea credit and can replace the midterm. Pa's can be challenging but dont take too much time. Deian is a caring and funny professor, but you cannot rely on the lecture slides solely and have to teach yourself using materials elsewhere.

Main problem is his weird philosophy about teaching. He gives no guideline and no practice for final exam, while his lecture is not organized and a lot of times unclear. He podcast without recording his voice... (What's the point?) All he does in review sessions is to answer question with another question like "yeah, but why, and how" like Socrates
Tough but super caring professor. Learned a lot; didn't appreciate it then but kind of do now.

This professor is very responsible, and he tries his best to teach. This is my 2nd most miserable at UCSD, behind Shacham. I have spent at least 15hrs+ on each PA and HW and got an average of 80% in total. However, I barely passed my midterm, and I have not gotten anything from this class. Be prepared to do tons of self-studying if you take him.

Took Prof Kousser during SS1 as my third time trying to pass Poli 30. THIRD time. The course, in general, is hard. Why lie? I wish I would have taken it with Kousser the first time. He is the best Poli 30 professor to take it with. Do the 4 homework projects (each worth 15%) and you'll forsure ace the midterm 20% and final 20%

Thad is such an amazing professor. Honestly do not take POLI 30 unless Thad is teaching it. He is so great and he is willing to help you with homework if you go to office hours. Also gives extra credit. He kind of talks up the homework assignments to seem hard but they really are not that hard at all.

Best professor ever. No, but really -- Prof. Kousser is super nice, approachable, and tries to keep things interesting and fresh. One midterm (easy, he gives a study guide with exactly what you need to know). One final (also with study guide). No quizzes, no clicker, section mandatory and helpful. Super easy, even the math parts. Take this class!!

Prof Kousser is a clear, personable lecturer who knows what he's talking about. I've heard from other students that past Poli 30 profs weren't good, so definitely take Kousser if you have the chance. Attending lecture and paying attention in section are enough to do well

I TA'd for this class.  Thad is the best lecturer you're going to get for Poli 30.  If he happens to be assigned to teach it, and it's a requirement for you, take it!  don't wait.  Explanations are clear and entertaining.  He works closely with TAs to ensure grading is fair and consistent.

The MATERIAL isn't uninteresting but the COURSE is very dry. 90+% of every class is looking at data tables with little focus on theory. Don't worry about the research paper. Follow the directions and you'll do fine, but give yourself ample time to complete it. Final puts too much emphasis on applying theory when the rest of class is data-driven.

James Rauch is without doubt the best professor I have ever had. He is so full of knowledge, I wish he was the president. This guys knows his stuff, and manage to explain it in an understanding way. Just follow the lectures, do the optional homeworks and practice midterms and you'll do great and actually have learned A LOT.

He allows to brings notes to the exams, however, his TAs grading criteria is very rigid. If you do not answer the exact same way they wanted, you dont get the whole points. The professor doesnt help at all in grading, so even if you use the exact same information he said, it doesnt matter because the TA will be the one who decides.

James is the most knowledgable professor I have ever met. He is able to answer any questions students ask as he teaches us on stuff he actually did research on. As long as you go to class and take good notes, it is an easy A.

His lectures are very dry. But he really knows what he is talking about and is quite knowledgeable. His tests are very hard but he has a very fair curve and allows you to print as many notes as you want. Going to class really helps and saves you from a buttload of reading.

I was dreading this class going in but Prof Rosenfeld made it very engaging, more so than most of the classes that I was looking forward to. Grades are based all on participation and papers, but she's a very easy grader. Seems to just want you to show that you're engaging with the material and doing the readings. A lot of reading the first 4 weeks

She provides thorough feedback on all assignments in a prompt manner; her feedback is very constructive, which allows me to make effective revisions. The class is heavy on reading and writing essays, but the assignments are manageable. Read the articles assigned, as it will help you with your essays.

Be prepared for a heavy lecture class. Although not graded by much (2 essays, midterm, and final) you will have to pay attention in order to receive a good grade. He is very tough on grading essays and often doesnt explain what you specifically did wrong throughout the essays. If you are a good writer and enjoy history this is a great class for you

Get ready for a very lecture heavy class! Only a few tests and essays, but because of that, they cover a huge span of information from units, so they are difficult. His tests were super long and consisted of multiple essays and short questions. No homework, just make sure to keep up with reading outside of class! Overall a super nice guy!!

HIST class at USD, it has been my worst prof so far. He is extremely boring, reads from the slides with no explanation, and makes large assumptions about the knowledge of the class for an intro history course. He was clearly inexperienced, I learned nothing, and there were a ton of pointless quizzes. He spent too much time on the economic aspects.

The worst professor I have ever had. Seems extremely inexperienced when lecturing (reads directly from the slides without any outside input) and SO boring. His final study guide is every term on the powerpoint of which he hasn't ever explained. Readings are never actually discussed only quizzed on making them pointless for future use.
Hes a nice guy, a little bit boring but I like him overall
Very sweet but teaches a VERY hard class. Available to assist but you need to put in a lot of work. Would recommend over others

one of the realest profs i've ever met. this class had a few quizzes and weekly assignments, but the workload was very manageable. prof haines is super understanding, funny, and very down to earth. he genuinely isn't trying to trick anyone and wants his students to succeed. i really appreciated this class during covid too. 10/10, absolutely stan.
didn't accommodate for students during a pandemic
Knows more about this subject then most. Good lectures and lots of hands on experience. Take as many classes with him as possible.
Tom is an expert in anything on the tech side of music, also has a great ear for the recording studio. go to his office hours
Tom is great. If you get a chance to take classes with him, jump on it!

Professor Booker was a very kind professor, however, I had difficulty understanding her content and often had to rely on my TA to "re-explain" concepts with examples. Though I acknowledge that the class is meant to be theoretical, she provides little to no examples. She also doesn't stick to her syllabus as she goes over time often.

Prof. Booker's a good lecturer, but her lectures tend to be dense. She tends to fill slides with a few pictures or quotes before dissecting them verbally, which can be hard for note-taking. She was also occasionally hard to reach by email. Prof. Booker clearly knows about what she's teaching, but her lecture style may not be well suited to Zoom.

Best professor ever honestly, she is the most I see standing professor you will come across. I took her for 3 courses comm 100A, comm 114D, and comm 146 so I can tell you for sure that you wont regret having her as a professor. I would definitely take more classes with her as a professor :)

This is my second time taking a class with professor Huezo. His teaching style is very straightforward, yet helps you think beyond the surface of the ideas. He is focused on making the class comfortable for the students. Structure wise, it is the same assignment every week, but the readings are amazing and relevant with the course and real life.

Alex is the most caring professor I have taken at UCSD. I took this class as an UD elective & learned so much this quarter. Hes always extremely clear about whats expected on midterms & projects. Weekly readings are pretty heavy in the middle of the quarter but slow down, nonetheless they are extremely interesting! He truly helps students succeed

PHIL12 is pretty interesting and the professor did a good job at explaining the material. Your grade is made up of 3 problems sets, weekly quizzes, and a final 1000 word paper. Its pretty difficult to get an A in this class but easy to achieve a B. Attendance isn't mandatory and Tracz always uploaded lecture videos the same day.
cool dude. his lectures are very informative and concise. he cares about his students. simply the best prof in this department.

To a student who has never taken calculus before, Professor Driver not for you. His lectures can get pretty confusing/hard to follow at times. I knew all of the material previously due to AP Calc, which is the only reason I passed. Despite that, he does care about his students. Not the best nor the worst. Try for a better professor if you can!

Professor Driver is a good instructor. His proof in class is clear. Attendance is not taken, but missing the class definitely makes you hard to catch up. Exams are easier than what is taught in class, so understanding the class notes is essential. He is accessible outside class, and he is also very helpful in clarifying any question one may have.

Good instructor, helped navigate through the initially uncertain world of complex analysis. Explanations were good, although his proofs were a little wonky, I'd never seen anything like them before; probably just because of the type of class. Would recommend.

Lectures weren't clear nor helpful. But the midterms and finals were fairly easy because they were very similar to his practice exams. Study the homework questions and practice exams, and you'll be fine!

I agree with the first comment, He is hilarious, but unintentionally. He can be somewhat confusing in lecture, but his exams were almost identical to the practice exams; explains why the avg on MT2 was 91!, very enthusiastic about linear algebra, very nice guy; master the concepts because the T/F questions are tricky, the rest is pretty mechanical

Favorite class and favorite prof at UCSD! You can tell Professor Kaiser is very passionate and knowledgable about what she's teaching, and has also done some really interesting field work in Haiti which she integrated into the class. When I walked up to turn in the final, I wanted to tell her how much I enjoyed the class but was too shy haha
Lecture not mandatory, except on 3 or 4 group meeting days where it is mandatory. Class is podcasted. Pretty easy class imo, would definitely recommend if you are not looking to struggle too much.

Professor explains concepts pretty well and in a way that's easy to understand, yet does jump from one concept to the next without full flow of the material. There are case studies, one midterm and a group project final. When the group meets for the group project, class is mandatory, and class is podcasted. Material was really interesting!
the worse professor I had ever had. Just trust me. With everything online specifically, it's just the worse thing you can do to yourself by taking his class.

Professor Cha cares very much about his class and expects people to participate. When it comes to quizzes, I think that they definitely get more difficult as the classes progress. You have to be ready to learn many characters per week. The class itself, grammar, hw, isn't too bad and mostly well paced. Great professor, would recommend!

I love this professor. He makes learning Chinese fun and exciting, and I can tell he truly cares about the student's learning. It can be intimidating speaking Chinese in front of people, but Professor Cha made me feel comfortable and not judged. It's fun talking to him about anything--doesn't need to be Chinese specifically. 100% recommend.
What if I don't want to take it

This man is hilarious.  I could not contain myself in his class sometimes.  He makes the 10 lines of dialogue per lesson seem like a full-on soap opera.   Pretty much everyday he'd randomly stop class to talk about his disgust for the election and even postponed a quiz when Trump won.  Workload is overwhelming at times but I learned a ton.

If you ever take Prashant Mali's BENG162 class in the future, then you're in for a real treat. Not only will he not answer your emails, but he will give u quizzes/lab reports unrelated to his lectures, just so he can enjoy watching you struggle while he sits back and collects his funding from the University. Got a question to ask the TA? good luck.

Mali's lectures made it relatively easy to understand the material. He seems to genuinely care about students. Quizzes and HW were reasonable, sometimes included extra credit. However, final projects were incredibly difficult and unrelated to class content. The class also claims to accommodate both python and MATLAB users but heavily favors MATLAB.

overall, the prof seemed invested in student learning. this course was linear algebra + calc + matlab. there were 3 hw assignments, 2 quizzes and no final exam. the written hw was doable, but the matlab problems were hard at times. the final project was the hardest part; it was time-consuming and not related to the concepts we learned in class.

Professor August is the best! He is so patient and respect all his students. He gives a lot of help on labs and his labs and exams are truly fair. The course itself contains a lot of hw though and in a fast pace, but he is definitely a great prof. You can learn a lot in his class. Wanna take him again.

I love Spanish 1A with Profesora Villavicencio! She's very sweet and makes Spanish fun! For anyone taking LISP 1A, be aware that from day 1, everything is in Spanish. All instructions are given in Spanish and you're supposed to speak only Spanish (even when asking questions). Great immersion but it was a little jarring in the beginning.

I feel bad for writing a less than desirable review because Professor Geiss is a very kind person, but the amnt of work and the level of grading is absurd. Each wk you have a disc. post (requires outside research, reading, writing), reading on perusall (with comments), 1 quiz, & in-class assign (groups). Quiz ?'s are not from lecture or material

Geiss was extremely caring and considerate during the class being online for spring. The topic is pretty interesting, however there is a lot of busy work in my opinion. It does cushion your grade from exams, but there is a lot of assignments and readings to do on launchpad. If you can dedicate some time, you'll be good.

I literally never rate prof but Im making an exception. She is not a bad prof but she gives way too much work for a class. Its like her class is the only class the students are taking. Her tests are very hard and long. The average for midterm 1 was C+. I spent more time studying and doing work for this class than in my molecular bio. AWFUL PROF!!!!

Class was pretty easy. We had three midterms, which is unusually many, but the upside was that if you did extremely well on them, you didn't even have to show up on the final. Overall, she was a great professor, and there's nothing to fear from the class. Very little homework, just some notes we wrote once a week.

Jenna is not a professor, she's a PhD candidate and this was one of her first times taking the class, but it was really easy. Her tests were open internet, book, note, everything. The class was really straightforward and excellent for people, like me, with no coding experience. Final grades are on a curve, and her quizzes are fair

Professor Xin Tu is the most caring professor I have ever had. He cares a lot about his students and their success. Although he is sometimes hard to understand, if you ask go to his office hours, he is always more than willing to help and extremely clear and detailed when explaining. He is a very understanding professor and I loved his course.

Professor Tu is a very caring professor, however, sometimes it is hard to understand him in lectures. However, when you meet with him during office hours, he is very clear. He is a very helpful professor. He does give quizzes almost every lecture and lets you drop 5 of your lowest scores. Furthermore, exams are similar to practice exams.

Professor Xin is a very nice man but extremely difficult to understand. His lectures are all over the place and no one ever really seems to know what is going on. He gives quizzes most classes but lets you drop FIVE of your lowest scores.

He is an amazing professor who genuinely cares about students. You can tell by the many random posts he makes on Canvas that he is really passionate about what he teaches. While I hate biology, his class was not that bad. Would definitely take him again!

Gives me grandpa vibes, he's so nice & passionate! Can write an essay to replace the lowest exam. Easy class if you put in effort. He explains stuff in lecture thats not on the slides. Curves 86% to an A, extra credit related to class + CAPES eval. Answers everyones questions very clearly. MC, short answer tests. Has dry humor but i like that LOL.

Dr. Hedrick is one of the sweetest professors I've had at UCSD! He is very understanding with the grading scale and he is curving the class, providing an extra credit assignment and some for CAPES. He also reviews quizzes/concepts covered during office hours and really focuses on student's learning. I would totally recommend this prof!

I took BILD 30 to fulfill my science requirement so I didn't put much effort into the course. Prof Hedrick is a solid instructor and knows his material well, but his lectures were very extensive and attendance was not enforced, so I didn't show up. No textbook for the course, but you did have to make a book report from a list he selects for you.

Very interesting topic, Hedrick is a great lecturer and you can tell that he really enjoys the material. Basically only graded on the midterm and final, with an optional book review for extra points. Lecture isn't mandatory but some details on the slides he goes over more in depth during class, and appear on the midterm/final.

Perhaps one of the worst profs I've had. Definitely an intelligent person, however, this professor's ability to teach high-level nanoeng topics is shameful. Undoubtedly, Prof. Chen understands the subject he is teaching nonetheless, I believe his lessons are unclear, convoluted, and unintuitive.

Okay professor who teaches biochemistry for nanoengineers, nowhere near as bad as the biology major version of the course.  Proteins were the worst topic but if you paid attention in freshman biology you'll do fine otherwise.

Whatever you do, don't take this professor. I don't know if she's new at teaching or something, but she has the most demanding courseload- for a basic spanish class. Easily 3-4 assignments, each sometimes worth more than 20 points, EVERY NIGHT. She'll get on your back for not speaking in breakout rooms, call you out, and make this class hell.

There are always great discussions in this class. Professor is very up to date and cares about what his students have to say. 100% recommend! I honestly didn't want to take this class but I'm so glad I did, it turned out to be one of my favorite classes because he was such a good and caring professor!!
very easy to pass class. participate and he will love you. stay quiet and he will grade you harder. tonsss of reading. very open minded and such a nice guy. loves his students. highly recommend

Joe was awesome! So chill and genuinely cares about his students. Loved his assignments because he left room for students to use their own creativity and really challenge themselves! Keep up with the work and you'll be just fine. Total grade came down to a portfolio, listen to his advice for that! Overall, pretty chill class and a great professor.

Professor Babcock is one of the best and most caring professors I've ever had. He really wants his students to succeed and tries very hard to engage with us. He encourages students to be creative and think critically when writing. He's also very encouraging and accommodating. Definitely recommend taking his class, he's the best!

Professor Babcock is by far the most caring writing professor I had. He is so friendly and patient that you would want to work with him to improve your writings. He gives out so many helpful comments and techniques that help strengthen your writing skills. I would totally recommend him to any student.

Prof Bain is a great teacher. The class is about prog rock and metal. It's a lot of work, but if you like the genre then you will love the class. The lectures are podcasts, there are required listenings and readings, and for participation there are discussion posts. A lot more work than my major related classes (chem, bio lab, and math).

I loved MUS15 with this prof! He comes off as a bit shy, but he's very knowledgable and passionate about music. Lectures consisted of PowerPoint slides and in-class listening. All in all, this class was awesome and I would love to take another one of his classes someday!

Professor Loose is so insightful about the Victorian Era. Her lectures are very reliant on you having read the texts, so come to class prepared and ready to participate. She's very laid back and her lectures are longer but not boring. Her door is always open if you need extra help!

I love this woman! She's one of my favorite professors at UCSD. She's always super understanding of students' mental health problems, she's very aware of social issues (though totally unaware of pop culture), and she's very friendly. Her lectures are usually discussion based, and it's always a great conversation between everyone in the class.
She is a really funny character. She made the lectures so engaging and very interesting. She is definitely a great professor.

For the shy people, she made it possible for them to get participation points by simply making eye contact with her. It was great! And the class, which was 80 minutes, was just the class talking about our interpretations of the readings. I now want to double major with Literature because I loved the the learning style of this class and the topics.

Great Professor, great power points. easy essay topic. willing to help. good reads and overall I would definitely recommend this class. p.s. gives quizes, cancels class once in a while, can be late, class is a big discussion between students and proff, shows films,  and very funny.

Professor Brodard is a great professor. She's very understanding and you learn a lot in her class without it being difficult. It's an enjoyable class to go to, just make sure you try to participate often.

My favorite French instructor from the 1 series! Such a sweet lady that really cares about her students learning French. She is really understanding and teaches a lot about the culture as well, which made the class more interesting. I loved learning from her. The class isn't easy, but do the work, pay attention, and participate!
Emmanuelle is a gem! Really enjoyed having her as my conversation teacher.
J'aime Emmanuelle!  She' really caring and puts a lot of effort into ensuring all her students understand the material.
Fun, but you need to be consistent.

Professor Lerer is an amazing teacher. He is one of my favorites in the UCSD English department and he is always open to talking with you outside of class if you have and questions or concerns. He's engaging and hilarious and lectures are always enjoyable.

Awesome lecturer! Best humanities professor you could have gotten. Relates the Bible to Harry Potter, even curses and stuff without losing legitimacy -- he knows his stuff and any conversation you have with him will be interesting and he's respectful of students too. Loved coming to class.
Wow, BEST PROFFESOR, she is extremely helpful, she loves the class and it really shows, she encurages you to do better all the time. BEST PROFFESOR. TAKE HER CLASS!!!

Professor Eckles is super funny and believes in her students (sorta like a momma bear and her cub). If only I had time, I definitely could've gotten a B. Nonetheless , she made a UC level class seem fairly easy and straight forward.  Take time to study and you're golden.

This was the first time Dr. Eckles taught this course, and it sucks that she's leaving to teach elsewhere. She was an amazing lecturer, chose really good readings (there were a lot, but it's basically a philosophy class, so of course), and really cared that we were learning. Exams weren't easy but were very fair. No homework, just reading.

Dr. Eckles is one of the best biology professors that I have ever had in my life. She makes learning fun and interesting. Her lectures are very animated and captivating. Be prepared to study her lecture notes though because the exams can be difficult. I wish I could take another class with her. She is really good at explaining difficult concepts.

Dr. Eckles was an AMAZING instructor made bio Lab super fun & interesting. She explains what we are going to do for lab that day and we worked in groups. We have a quiz every time we had lab (super easy 5 questions)you need your notebook for every lecture don't forget it!!! She signs it off easy points. Easy A!!You will love her!(I took her at swc)

Monteon is such a terrible professor, when I found out he was Harvard educated I couldn't believe it. So boring, monotone, and confusing! I tried giving him the benefit of the doubt since we transitioned to online learning but man, he needs to retire. In my 4 years of education this is the one professor I truly regret ever taking.

Monteon couldn't figure out how to use Zoom making classes extremely frustrating. He'd record lectures but never post them because he couldn't figure out how. We had to remind him the quarter was almost over for him to give the first assignment. NO JOKE! Harsh grader, terrible communicator and technologically challenged. DO NOT TAKE!

Lectures are long & I wouldn't recommend this class for people who aren't history major/minors, but I really liked Monteon as a professor in general. He's very easy to talk to during office hours and encourages you to ask questions. He does tend to jump from here to there so I recommend using office hours to clarify the subject matter.

HE IS SO MONOTONED! I could not sit through a 1.5 hour class and hear him speak. He is very nice, though. Take this class ONLY if you are interested in Argentinian History...otherwise, you're wasting your time
Professor Monteon is an excellent lecturer. Although the material can be dry at times, he knows how make students laugh.

100% would take this professor again. His classes were extremely straight-forward and his explanations of new concepts was very well done. Lecture structure consists of learning new concepts then practicing them for the rest of the period. Register with him if you have the chance!

Dr. Perkins is a really nice guy, but there are some problems about his grading scale and lecture. All his tests are cumulative, tests are taking very few points that a little error can be big grade drop. As well, he is a tough grader, he picks on every little single error. Both of them combined, it is very hard to get a good grade.

His lecture only talks about simple concepts but his final is extremely hard I go over every lecture and hw multiple times before test but still struggle so hard his final was nothing like the homework the difficulty level skyrocket suddenly. will definitely avoid his class in the future

I think Professor Perkins is caring and truly wants his students to do well in his class. I feel like under the circumstances of spring quarter, he tried his best to accommodate students and help us out. He can seem intimidating, but I think it is majorly that he wants students to learn to adapt and be independent well rounded thinkers.

He was honestly the worst professor ever. I had to try and learn on my own which was really hard and honestly I didn't learn anything. I would recommend literally any other professor besides him because he is not much help and just caused me a lot of stress during the pandemic. If I could I would give zero stars.

Horrible lectures, very confusing. Class was seemingly organized at first but when it came to planning exams, he did not plan for overlap with other classes and could give us little information as to what would actually be on the exam. Most stressful class I have taken so far, and that is saying something at UCSD.

He seems to be organized. He has his own book, his own website Notations are confusing, the book just refers you back here back there. Some concepts can be expained using simple words but he chose not to. The whole class is about a few examples. If get stuck in anyone of them, you are getting confused for the rest of the class

Great Professor

It seemed like he didn't have much of a lesson plan and just went through the book showing us things. He mentions through out the course that he is not a fan of Matlab which kind of takes the motivation away from students. Clicker midterm and final. Fun and challenging final project.

The midterm was so easy, and the final was so much harder, don't know what he was thinking. spent lots of time lecturing things that he didn't even ask on the exam. not respecting students by ignoring emails

Professor Noel is an awesome professor who explains the material very clearly and his lecture is very interesting so you will never distract. If you have any questions, just go ahead and ask, he will respect you and try his best to answer your question by applying lots of examples.

This guy is a champ. Had him over the summer, he actually made ECON 100B enjoyable, even though the class was 3 hours long. I wouldn't have wanted any prof for that long, but Noel is entertaining and laid back enough to make it a good 3 hours in class.

Professor Noel is a cool guy and very intelligent. He has a Phd from MIT so that can initially be intimidating. Gonzales is the best professor ever. I took the class at LaGuardia CC and I wish I can take classes with him again.
He is the best teacher throughout my college. He explains very well and detailed. I wish I could have him for another semester.

I came into the class with no interest, and I was sad when it was over! He really goes out of his way to make sure you understand everything, and gave better instructions on how to write a paper than I ever received in my writing classes. Highly recommended.
Very good professor. Knows what he's talking about. Highly recommended. Students know what is expected of them. Keep up with the class & you'll do well. Very fair grading.

Mookherjea is hands down the best lecturer I had the pleasure of studying under. It's clear he is incredibly passionate about the subject matter of his courses, and I know his classes have influenced many student's choice of specialization.

professor is clear, interesting if you are into the subject. I was just in it for the last ECE class. He was also surprisingly easy since prior I heard rumors of ECE 108 being one of the hardest ECE classes.

Mookherjea is really funny in a condescending but sarcastic way, and teaches excellently. Neat handwriting, writes big, speaks at a good pace, what more could you ask for?

He realizes that the majority of students in ece 53a are not ece majors and cuts out a lot of the crap only needed for the ece major.  He is funny and very enjoyable.  Classs is very fair.  HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!

Great teacher compared to most CSE professors.  Just be sure to not fall behind and read the textbook at the same pace as lectures are going (practice the problems too).  The average for the first midterm was 30%, so you know it's going to be tough.  Very clear and understandable.
He was busy with earning money from his administration position. He didn't care about the quality of the lecture at all.

Lectures are not organized. He made the midterm very hard, and so many students failed it, so he had to give us a make-up midterm. He cares about teaching, but his unorganized notes and hard homework made it difficult for students to follow.  Fair grading in the end.

Sorn is one of the best professors I've had at UCSD. He explains concepts super well, has very detailed slides, and gives us a lot of opportunities to earn our grade. Sorn is v knowledgeable about the material. We had synchronous &(optional but necessary) asynchronous lectures & daily &weekly quizzes. I honestly had a hard time learning. Sorn is a very caring, knowledgable prof. He has a knack for explaining concepts. Questions on tests and quizzes were just like in the homework and he gave a boatload of extra credit.

The test format is half FRQ and half MC. I felt like lectures brushed over concepts so quickly, but the exams were difficult. He gives problem sets which are challenging, but answer keys are very vague. I wish I read the book because the lecture style wasn't for me and was quite confusing..

I adore Sorn as a professor and this was by far the most rewarding class at UCSD. I learned a lot which helped me understand material better for the MCAT as well. He wants you to succeed - go to office hours, do the problem sets, etc. Tons of extra credit. He is a genuine professor who made one of the hardest classes at UCSD fun and easy!

First, he just reads his slides. He never adds detail to his slides and wants student to understand it. During this COVID situation, he does not give us clear announcements on exams. Your grade is decided by midterm and final. Although Mackie's lectures aren't the most engaging, I was able to not listen and briefly read them later and scan the readings. Mackie is very mediocre. He mumbles a lot during lecture and mostly reads off the slides, but at least he podcasts everything. Clicker questions make lecture mandatory. I ended up learning the most from my TA (shoutout Leo!)

Honestly one of the worst professors and classes I've ever taken. He just reads off the slides during class, and treats the lecture hall like a group of high school students. AMAZING PROFESSOR!!! She's so kind, understandable, and overall very caring. She cares so much for her students and gives everyone the opportunity to speak and provides awesome feedback. Easily one of the nicest professors I've had so far. She deserves the best

Professor Dorr is very kind and compassionate towards students, she strives to make a connection and she loves hearing our discussions in the class. Amazing professor who really cares about her students. Easy work load with only two short papers that you get to choose your prompt from, and one group presentation on a reading. Lecture is interesting because of the material and she is great at delivering it. 2 short papers and a group assignment that is not too demanding. You do need to show up to class, though. I really enjoyed this class. Work load was mild enough that I could spend time engaging with the material given. I would absolutely take a class with her again!

Worst "professor" ever. Power-point slides entirely copied & pasted from the textbook, the audio is him just reading the same exact notes on the slide. terrible professor does not respond to emails doesnt help makes things more confusing than they are avoid taking this professor at all costs

Lectures were TED talks with no relevance to the lab.  He taught us for an hour, total, throughout the whole semester and whenever you asked a question he would give long stories not answering. terrible prof i didn't understand anything in lay man term and i fail uwu
The best professor I have ever met in UCSD, even throughout my life!!!!!!
This man is a living gem, a true saint, and a master class professor. He cares about his students and dedicates so much time to them that it's crazy. The best instructor I've ever had hands down.

Pros: most enthusiastic lecturer I've ever seen, delightful to help out students, goes over material well paced and make sure everyone can understand, super clear hand writing and posts detailed notes available online, take home midterm and a portion of take home final Cons: no cheat sheet which takes 50%, extra lecture & crazy grading scale

You can hear the excitement in his voice when he lectures. He keeps you engaged in the material every step of the way. He literally teaches the material so all you have to do is be engaged. Excellence.

Incredibly caring professor. I felt like her quizzes were a little too easy at times lol but hey, I'm not complaining! Accessible outside of class and responds to questions really quickly. She's an amazing teacher and also takes notes during the lecture while explaining the concepts. Final was no penalty and it could only improve your grade.
TAKE HER CLASS

Abby is the best professor Ive had during COVID-19. She adapted the class amazingly well to online format. Tests are very fair and homework has unlimited tries. She genuinely cares about students mental health and is very lenient on deadlines. Fun extra credit parts. Replies to questions real quick. Love her cats. A very sweet person in general.

Professor O'Rourke did a great job adapting to the online format of the lab! I was nervous for group projects, but I ended up being very thankful to have people to work through the course with. (Took BIMM 121 in person). Her lectures and slides were made in such a way that material was easy to understand. Concepts and lab calculations explained in an easy to follow way. Lectures were interesting and she made it very clear what would be on the tests.

This lab class was moved online abruptly because of COVID-19 but Prof. O'Rourke helped ease that transition for the students regarding deadlines and workload. Part of the material she incorporated was a lab simulation for different experiments which I really enjoyed because it gave me the semblance of an actual lab class which I really appreciated!
Very unorganized. Don't take her class. She doesn't care about students and her grading uses unclear criteria. DON'T TAKE HER CLASS. Worst class experience I've ever had at UCSD.

This is a case where the material was abstract and challenging (game theory), and he tended to go too fast through explanations, leaving students confused after lectures. Strange grading standard You will never know why you lose point

Homework is encouraged to be done in groups. Not the best at explaining complex concepts or answering questions.

She didnt even curve the class. lectures are confusing. exams are not like homework.

She's a nice lady and is patient with her students. Offers a lot of help. Just do the optional homework and you'll be golden.

Prof Jed is amazing! I am so glad I got to take one of her classes. She made literary theory a lot of fun and actually entertaining. She communicates abstract theories for the class in a very comprehensive way and I feel I learned different things that I will remember and will keep with me.

She's a very sharp professor who is interested in connecting literature to all areas in of the academia. The readings are sophisticated and intriguing. Definitely recommend her.
EASIEST A EVER EVEN FOR  CLASSES I TOOK IN COMMUNITY CLASS.

Stephanie has many interesting ideas about literature that she is more than happy to discuss outside of lecture as well. She is overall a very approachable, friendly person, and if your have her as a prof, you are in for a treat.

I took MUS 80 last summer. It's a summer-only class and has small class numbers, which was great for her teaching style. I had one of her classes before, but this one was a lot better. HUGE workload for a GE class!!!! Never enjoy the music in the class!!! I am worried about getting a NP right now!!!

One of the WORST professors I've had, hands down. Lectures were dry and boring. Dr. Sousa is a great professor, you definitely have to work for your grade but that is what makes a great teacher. Her exams are very straight forward, as long as you do the readings and go to lectures you will be good.

Easy, A, not conventional, but does change your perspective on many matter involving music. Lectures are great, and include everyone!

fun class and easy A

Amazing, amazing class !! Not your conventional course but showed a wide perspective - everyone will learn something new for sure regardless of your background. Interesting listening, easy assignments and the final was super fun! Well structured, executed by the prof.
This class was honestly amazing, I learned so much!

Masha is an excellent lecturer. Her explanations are thorough, straight to the point, and easy to comprehend. She is a great professor. Some people might say, "oh, she is easy". But I think she just don't want anyone to fail her class. BEST MATH TEACHER. Amazing and clear lecture. Tells you exactly what are on tests and no surprise questions on tests.  No Matlab quiz (well it is not really a quiz anyways) Midterms and Finals are easy af with cheat sheets (1 per midterm, 2 for final) Honestly, she is the best.
Best math professor at ucsd. Highly recommend

She's a phenomenal professor. Every exam was straightforward with no tricks or curveballs. She's helpful, kind, and a brilliant professor. I wish she taught 20E so I could take her again. Two cheat sheets allowed for the final, and one for each midterm. All the tests were based on material covered in class and in the practice tests she posts.

She is a horrible professor. Very weak in her mathematical knowledge. She is lazy, and does not prepare for her lectures. I don't know how she got a PhD from Princeton, a school that I would like to try applying for my graduate studies. Stay away from her.

Pretty good professor, he made pretty easy midterms, and the TA was really good! Honestly, it was just a fun class that all you had to do is pay attention and you will pass. Such a boring lecturer, such a boring class. The saving grace was that the TA was great. Two exams, two papers, clicker questions at lecture, homework reading due online before the next lecture.

His lectures are boring but he tries to be entertaining. The online homework is tedious and definitely useless, tests are reasonable, and the short essays are not bad. The grading is very clear and it honestly depends on the TA too.
Decent Professor, Lectures can get boring at times. Grading is very fair. Overall, he's decent. Attendance is required because he uses iclicker
This dude it straight boring. His class is tough and honestly you have to put in a lot of personal effort to do well in the class.

Great lecturer with a good grasp on online teaching methods. Quizzes are very fair, with good practice quizzes and HW problems. He is an angel of a man.

prof engler is extremely caring & knowledgeable. there were four 10-question noncumulative quizzes that were worth 25% each. he was accommodating to student challenges due to covid; recordings of live lectures were uploaded, he gave us 24 hrs to work on the quizzes, and the last quiz was made optional. the textbook readings supplements lecture.

Dr. Burg was an amazing professor and extremely knowledgeable about the subject. Dr. Burton is so incredibly nice and will take the time to explain if you don't understand. He is a little boring to listen to in lecture, but defiantly go to lecture because of clickers. Also he doesn't podcast so I suggest you audio record the lectures yourself. Overall a really good courses, but the tests are all free response and long. Know the little details for tests.

Exams focus on so many trivial details and there're so many researches mentioned in class, you can never tell which ones are important. Avoid list checked.

Burton was the more interesting lecturer out of the 2 for this class, although his lecture notes aren't as clear and organized as Hastings. Midterms are pretty much all multiple choice/fill in the blank/true false type questions, so they weren't too hard. Good class overall.

He posts lecture notes every week but you still need to watch his lecture video because the pdf doesn't contain the solution to his examples. Helpful lecture and caring. Do HWs on Webassign. Exams are fair. He gave students 4 hours instead of 3 hours to complete the final to make us feel less pressure (Final is not hard at all!).

This quarter was remote so he gave lectures asynchronously. I honestly tried to follow them but I just gave up and took notes from the book and did the HW problems. His class was really clear and doable. I respect him how he handled this remote quarter. He is really helpful and caring too.
Extremely fair midterm/finals. Anything you saw in HW was in the exams. Decent lecture's that help a lot with concepts along with good examples of problems.

He is the best professor I have had at ucsd. He really dives deep into concepts and answers questions very well in lectures. He offers extra credit from doing all the online hw. Matlab is straightforward like in Math18. Exams are extremely fair if you know how to do the online hw since most exam problems are based off of this.
Take his class. you won't regret it!

Mike is an interesting character. His comments on American art, postmodernist theory, and current events are striking and poignant. His voice tends to be lost on most college freshmen, but he'll preach for anyone, and if you're in his company just sit down and listen. You'll be rewarded.

Course begins with intense readings/lectures. Cools off when you begin your research project. He lets you choose whatever topic you want for the research paper. Books on geisel reserve will help. IMO the camnitzer on conceptual art is the one you should pick your topic from. Definite bias for theory. You will be rewarded for challenging yourself
Intimidating at first. Be sure to ask follow up questions if you dont get something. Good feedback on essays.
Tough grader, but sets clear expectations.

He made too many mistakes in his lecture notes, problem sets, and even exams, which causes confusion for many students. Also, you need to teach yourself because he is not "teaching" - he just reads his lecture notes line by line. Avoid him!

GIbson is a new professor, so I was apprehensive going into his class after seeing the negative reviews on this page. Would recommend!

some of the early ratings are brutal. lectures are written out and theory based graphics are incorporated here and there-- definitely a decently engaging course. in addition to recorded lectures, notes are even typed out and posted at the end of the chapter. nothing unexpected on the midterms. more math than theory based, definitely recommend
Prof Gibson was good enough in comparison to Prof Ramey(Who teaches 173B). Enjoy your time with him before Ramey ruins your life.

I took his class before and he is a nice guy. He is available for students outside the class and wants to help his students to learn Econ. He does a pretty good job in caring for his students and helping them to get a good grade!

Professor Diels is a very carrying professor. Her lectures are very interesting and easy. Her exams are not super difficult, but I recommend studying on time. Also, she assigns three papers and they aren't difficult.

I took professor Diels in Fall 2018 quarter. She is not a bad professor and I am glad I took this class with such an easy and great professor. Diels missed quite a few days of lecture and either cancelled class or had a guest speaker. Lectures were alright, sometimes boring and other times entertaining. Overall, I recommend her.

Natacha is great!!! I loved this class. Attendance is not mandatory, but you should go because she goes over all audio clips and such that will be on the tests. This class inspired me to take another music class afterwards, but this one is still so much better.
Easy A. There were 3 papers and 2 test

Readings are tested, 1 mid, 1 group project, hw literally does not help your grade, inflexible. His exams are already tricky but couldn't go back once you submitted an answer. Not very engaged during lecture. Maybe it's just bc classes are online but I've had more understanding profs
Great professor who presents the material in an easy to follow manner.

I recommend this professor. I went into his OH for reviewing the exams and he was very nice and helpful. The class itself wasn't too easy, I studied hard from the notes and the book and I still got B+ without the extra credits (which bumps your grade by 1/3).
good professor, but you have to pay attention to details in the text because the exams can be a bit tricky
Test very hard..They tricked you on almost every question. His lectures were interesting though and he cares about the students. The test is what makes me give him a bad grade

Jay really cares for the students. He wants you to take away more than random facts from this class, but real life application. Very annoying professor. He focuses nearly entirely on subjective aspects such as 'what is your opinion and why do you feel that way'. Lots of 'reflexive thinking/writing'. Any learning to be had in this class you can just get from reading. Disrespectful of opinions different from him. Easy A.
The professor is very kind, and makes lectures very interesting for students.

Goes by Jim. He's an amazing and enthusiastic professor. Makes the material interesting. He does give a decent amount of work tho. Not hard but tedious. Just keep up with the readings and watch the assigned movies. Short 10 question weekly quizzes. Assigned 3 essays, midterm and a final. If you get a little behind, he offers extra credit!
His lectures are a little bit confusing but if you review your notes you should be fine. His tests are based on the examples he does in class.

This was during COVID19 at end of spring quarter, some lectures were confusing and some example were more overly complicated than they shouldve been. Tests were fairly simple as well. But ferrara made the right choice by making the final optional and only being able to boost our grade. It helped so much with stress

Great professor. Graded on weekly homework, midterm, quizzes (2 out of 6 were dropped), and a preliminary assignment. Lectures were content heavy but examples were clear and easy to understand. His homework was a good amount also gave extra credit on the homework. His lectures are sometimes a little confusing as they are pretty theory-based but then he does multiple helpful examples. His tests are rather easy and based on examples he does in lectures. Also, he podcasts! He curved our last midterm a good amount, very good prof take him!!
Best math teacher ever in UCSD. His notes are clear and understandable. Exams are reasonable. Took his math 20C and got an A- even though I did horrible for the final. Just take his class if you can.
She's an ok professor and sometimes unclear with what she wants.

Tiange is a nice professor. Easy A if paying attention in her lectures and doing practices on time. She gives extra credit to raise our grade as well. If she can be more prepared on homework prompts and the syllabus, it maybe easier for us to organize the work. Overall, I would take her again

Since I am not a music major, it was not easy for me to follow Mus 2b in the first place. But Prof. Zhou had spent a lot of extra time to help me to catch up. She shares a lot of funny stories of her own learning experience in the past.

She is definitely the professor to turn to if you want to learn some true stuff. She really cares about students and grades by effort. Easy A class if you're seriously learning.

The material itself isn't that challenging, but she isn't great at explaining things sometimes. She goes at a faster pace and assigns things out of our capabilities sometimes to push us. Prof. Binder is a very understanding, sweet man. He gives you everything you need in order do very well. Dr. Johnson is an AMAZING CHEM 150 professor. You will have to do a lot of homework, quizzes, lecture-review, and vocab. Don't forget your SIG FIGS!

Dr. Johnson is the best science teacher I have ever had. She provides PowerPoints and worksheets to help students understand the material along with giving lectures and practice problems that help you understand the material. If students arent understanding the material shell always take more time to teach us. She truly cares about her students.
I like professor Christina. She is very friendly and kind.
Amazing professor!! do the homework, show up to class, study for exams and quizzes and you'll do great!!
Difficult series of classes, but Johnson makes the class enjoyable and you will learn a whole lot. I do not usually give out reviews, but she is the best prof I have had at UCSD

Marc is an amazing choice if you are looking for a good conversation instructor. He makes class extremely fun and sociable, and class is actually something to relatively look forward to. He is easygoing and makes you feel comfortable to make mistakes, which is definitely important in language courses.

Yang is clearly very knowledgable and qualified, but is extremely hard to follow and does not have a teaching style that resonates with students who dont love math, or naturally understand it seamlessly. 10C, thankfully, is a relatively easy course compared to the rest of the sequence, however, i've definitely had better math lecturers.

Smarr's lectures were boring but the class isn't too hard. She does a few clicker questions each lecture but they aren't that bad because you can talk to the people around you. Midterm and final were straightforward- you need to study for them, but it's not crazy difficult.

Prof. Smarr is an experienced lecturer and as a result her lectures are very well structured and convey lots of interesting and useful(for the papers) information. She quotes the text a lot and gives page numbers, and the essays reflect the topics discussed on those page numbers. Take her class if you are interested in the material, she's great!

I did well in this class but thats not to say Smarr is that great. Her lectures are pretty dull and changes slides RAPIDLY which is pretty frustrating. Class is graded by your TA. So if you do take Smarr, make sure you understand what your TA expects of you. Overall, midterm and final are relatively easy. just read up and look over lecture slides!

Her lectures weren't very informative and all you really need is her slides, which she posts after class. Clicker questions every lecture. 3 papers, and a midterm and a final. You really need to read the primary sources from the class, as it shows up in your essays and tests. This class is very dependent on your TA and how hard they grade.

I am not sure if Smarr really knows how to teaching materials. Lectures are super un-organized and you learn nothing from her lecture. mandatory attendance is annoying. No study guide which makes her even harder. DONT TAKE HER

Prof. Chavez is an industry leader, and brings a lot of valuable work experience into his teaching style. If you actually pay attention and care in the class, it is easy to earn a good grade. This class teaches you more practical skills about Transportation Planning than any other

Over the entire quarter I don't think Professor Chavez had taught once. He runs the class in a weird format, 1 hour groupwork, 1 hour guest speaker, and then 1 hour discussion. Our weekly readings consisted of 3-4 articles found on the internet. What do we even discuss? Where does the learning come from? Why is discussion worth 45% of your grade??
There is no test or anything, if he likes you, you will Ace it. I got a C and I dont know why. Zero Communication!
He is terrible.  Does not respect student time and effort.

ProfessorVilla is amazing, and incredibly accommodating during the COVID-19 transition. Generous with extra credit! Her exams are very similar to the practice ones!! There are quizzes in discussion, but they are always announced ahead of time, and basically just supplement your participation grade. Overall awesome prof, you'll learn a lot from her!

Regarding the prof, she has good intentions and does care about students. Regarding the course, the lectures were way too dense and she often jumped around with no logical flow of content. I often left class quite confused and had to watch the podcasts many times to get an understanding of the concepts.

Prof. Villa was a great lecturer that really cares about her students. During the online finals caused by coronavirus concerns she was ultimately the most considerate professor I had. She let us drop one midterm or the final and gave us 3% extra credit for doing capes. She also doesn't give minus grades and an 88 is an A. Would recommend!

The course itself has a ton of info to cover, and Prof Villa does a good job getting to it all. Sure there are quizzes in discussion sections. . . that are only worth participation points and have advance notice. You have to understand material for exams, not just memorize it. Of course they're hard, this is an upper div UCSD course

Everyone's talked about the awful lectures already so I'll review the other stuff. Midterm 1 average was 75%. Discussion have quizzes. She has an obsession with microscopy and spent the first week studying it in detail. Not sure if that is standard in Cell Bio but if not, it explains why the course is very rushed. Take another professor if you can

This professor is hands down the single worst professor I've had at UCSD. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the professors should be more considerate of the situation their students are in. This professor does not care. He still continues his boring and useless lectures and the Markstrat is simply a joke. I wish we had other options for MGT 112.
