This professor is terrible. Lectures are pointless. He makes you pay for a simulation that goes on throughout the quarter. Quizzes are easy but not that big of a chunk of your grade. Pointless homework and pointless presentations, also makes you pay for a question service. Would never take him again probably the worst lecturer ive had at Rad

This class is heavily centered around an online simulation, but laptops aren't allowed in class. Lectures are boring and pointless because when he isn't talking about the online simulation we can't even refer to on a laptop, he's just lecturing about the textbook we can read for ourselves. Waste of time and a shame to be learning nothing useful

I think he hates his students. During the final presentations, he was ripping us a new one like Simon Cowell on American Idol, Season 1. Well he's not that bad, he is a very good lecturer but most the class/lectures revolved around an online simulation; I feel like I didn't learn very much. The quizzes were easy but the simulation was a lot of work

He's a very stereotypical old white professor who thinks his work is amazing and talks about it all day when in reality he just managers a yogurt store and worked in the South for some mental health government program. He hates electronics in class, wines about our generation often, and doesn't ever acknowledge people have it harder than him.
Kwan is a very responsible professor and he is very knowledgable. He always walks extra mile to help students

Kwan is a good professor. His ratings are low because he has a heavy Cantonese accent and a soft voice so he's difficult to understand sometimes. He's also very nerdy and makes weird jokes. His exams are very easy and straightforward. Grades are fair. He's not at all intimidating so ask him if you need help. And besides, it's just basic calc 3.

You don't need to attend lectures in order to do well, but he really simplifies concept and stresses what you need to know so go. The final was challenging, but the mid-terms and quizzes were not. He curved the class even more than the intended so he does acknowledge the student's overall grades. He's quite funny too.

This professor is terrible. I could not understand anything he said and he was rarely able to answer questions. Definitely a language barrier. The exams are also unrelated to the homework. Pray you get a good TA.

I LOVE THIS PROFESSOR! Lectures are very confusing because it's quite difficult to understand him. but if you took AP Calc and has a good understanding of the subject the class wouldn't be difficult. He is super generous on his grading. Quizzes, midterm and his final are pretty easy. he is super cute too! i love this guy.

This is the worst professor that I've ever had the displeasure of meeting. Most of the students in her class are repeats, and more must completely change their career goals due to her. It is beyond me that she is continuously able to teach.

It seems like a lot of work because you have to read 20-40 pages every class and write a 5-10 sentence summary and come up with a quiz question and explanation, but you get used to it. Best part is the quiz questions you make are the Q's on the tests and you get them all before the tests as well as the answers, so like you should get 100% on them
WORST CLASS IN MY ENTIRE LIFE. The curriculum for this course needs to be changed.

Probably the worst class I have taken at UCSD. She is not clear with what she wants in her papers. When you ask her for help she looks at you dumbfounded and tells you either you should have known/look it up. Class is a joke that did not prepare HDS majors, people have failed this class 2,3 times, something needs to be done to change the curriculum

This class was the hardest class I've ever taken in my entire. The amount of stress I had for the class was very hard for me to take in. You will struggle, but you will definitely learn a lot. Refresh your excel skills. Get ready to write a bunch of papers. Always go to office hours. If you are lost, don't be scared to ask your TAs.

Really hated that class. The material wasn't interesting in my opinion and just having a midterm+final exam without any extra credit possible (I asked) isn't the best. Worked hard on my exam paper to get a 69%. I would recommend taking this class only if you are really interested in it and ready to read a lot, with a background in humanities.

Professor Roudakova was interesting and very clearly passionate about what she was teaching. Like most social science classes, the TA is in charge of grading, but as long as you pay attention to instructions you should be fine. There are 2 papers (which are easy- you get to choose the subject), 1 midterm and a final. Overall it was a good class!

Prof. is a good lecturer, she is very knowledgeable and really cares about the content of the class. There two essays, plus a midterm and a final. Essays are not super difficult because she gives you a lot of freedom in what you want to write about. Exams are a fair representative of course material. Definitely a good choice for the 100 series.

Professor Roudakova has been one of my favorites yet @ UCSD. She is a real inspiration and cares for each of her students. Her lecturing skills are on point and she can keep you engaged throughout a long class.
A wonderful, brilliant woman who really helped me to think critically and address issues I'd never considered. I loved this seminar.

His lectures were well-explained and the homework had strong connection to his lecture. 173A is the first offering and it might be a bit disorganized. I wish the course can move at a faster pace with less time spending on proving convergence rate and more time on application. His exam requires time on calculation, but overall the exam is fair.

Extremely disorganized class, no textbook, no references for all the abstract concepts, lectures notes were barely understandable, there were no reviews for the exams, and professor Rayan was totally inaccessible. He has a good hold of his knowledge but is very poor at conducting a course. Would not take again.
Do not take this prof.
Good lecturer.

Professor Saab has very clear lectures and always makes following his class easy. His class flow is very clear and its always clear where he is going and what he is doing. I have to say homework for the class is a lot but understandable. The class in general is very calculation heavy.

When I had Professor Charlesworth, he was an average professor, but he cares a lot about his students understanding his lectures and will go out of his way to help. Though, I think he is one of those professor's that is too smart for his own good, I think he will better understand his student's prior knowledge with more experience under his belt

This is probably the hardest class I have ever taken but at least he is a good enterainer. If you are not in a love relationship with mathematics you better stay away but it has totally helped me to prepare for harder classes. If you are only so so in math you should reconsider. What's more, I recommend you go to his office hours!

Although his homework was very hard if you started early and got help from the UCSD tutors you could finish it early anyways. Comparatively not a lot of work, just takes the effort. I learned the most from his class. Not strict or quirky, just go up and ask him how to do a problem and he'll teach you.
You can receive good grades as long as you work hard enough.

Charlesworth's class starts like any other professors, but the homework is seriously on another level. It was so hard and personally made so that there is no help for it online, and they count for a fairly large amount of your grade. The MTs and final are about average in difficulty
Great!

She's in the bio department but teaches physics so that tells you something right there. Her explanations are convoluted and half the time she just expects you to know everything. If you try to ask a question during lecture she gets irritated and brushes you off without answering it. Would not recommend if you haven't taken any physics before

Hard professor and confusing lectures. In lecture, she does not go over the basics and goes straight to hard problems that she expects you to know right away. Also, she uses powerpoints and goes through them really fast in lecture. Her tests are extremely hard and not similar to homework problems.

Expects you to know things when she doesn't teach it.  Harsh grades with certain things and makes you figure things out for yourself (not necessarily bad but provides little help). Do not recommend taking her.
Dr. Schoetz was very enthusiastic about teaching and making sure we understood the material. Well structured lectures. Wish she would talk a little slower though.
very harsh grader and she often tells students that their arguments and beliefs are straight up wrong.
She's a great teacher if you're on her good side.
She is hard to understand and whenever she asks for someones opinions, she will tell them that their opinion is wrong. No matter what you answer.....
I had her for Spanish. She is a really tough grader, no lee-way on homework, tough to understand

I feel like some reviewers are being to harsh on Prof Shurin. The material is very stimulating and he consistently paused during lectures to answer questions that people had. He has clickers that are relevant to the material. The main downfall was that there was no clear grading criteria for quizzes/exams. Would take again though.

The class and the material itself are fairly easy to understand and grasp. The issue is that the quizzes and exams are very specific. Understanding notes from the slides is not enough you must write down pretty much everything he says. Attendance is mandatory. He doesn't really consider the student and their needs. Take anyone else.

I have never felt like doing a review before until I took this professor. The quizzes are on information you just learned and are so easy to lose points because some questions are free response and others are MC so you will lose all the points. The midterms are a mix of free response and MC and fill in the blank with some questions worded terribly

It's obvious he doesn't care about his students. He refuses to allow us to view the answer key for the midterm. He requires section attendance when the entire school has been told to not make attendance mandatory for the safety of the student body.
He genuinely cares and tries to make the material engaging, he just has a lot to teach as he is trying to set students up for success in future ecology classes.

Although the professor is accessible and literally gives away lab answers in discussion/OH, the class was incredibly disorganized with unclear grading criteria on the labs. Debugging was a pain and the teaching staff was unresponsive on piazza. He left us to fend for ourselves on the final project, which proved to be a disaster. We weren't ready...

Makes the labs a lot easier than they need to be. It is kinda hard to follow what he says in lecture but he does care about student feedback and tells you exactly how to approach the labs (except for the 4th lab). At that point it's your responsibility to understand enough digital design to implement the lab after being babied in the other labs.

Incredibly poorly organized class. Lectures are super hard to follow, and assignments that are easy once you understand what you're doing are hard to get started. For many assignments I had to watch lectures from other section as they had info my section didn't. Didn't give rubric for final project worth 45% until two days before it was due.

Classes are all lecture based.. She gives 2 unannounced in-class assignment, each 10% of your grade, and if you miss it, there's no make-ups. Lecture slides are unclear and sparse if you're counting on them. Exams are long essays + she gives study guides based on lecture material. She's monotonous and serious throughout so not a fun lecture either.

Honestly this class wasn't hard but what screwed me and a lot of people was missing one of the days where she gave an unannounced participation assignment which was worth 10%. Also, if you don't include some specific words and definitions from her book will deduct A LOT of points. Both midterm and final are in class long essays.

The class was a pretty straightforward, exciting, and accessible course. Professor Abrajano does give you a midterm and final study guide before class but, remember to fill out the study guide so she can look over it and provide you with feedback. If you do this, you will do well on the exams, but if you don't, then it is hard to do well on exams

Grading for attendance/participation is a joke, but definitely not a very funny one if you're an unlucky student. Had 2 in-class assignments, each worth 10% of your overall grade, given on random unannounced days. What if you missed a day? Screwed. Lectures off of undetailed powerpoints, so hard to know what you missed if you missed lecture.

She was Awesome!! She really knows what she is talking about and really wants you to do well. She wants to educate you into action and to know that you can make a change. Class is very easy, just make sure you participate so she knows you and that you show up to class because she has a sign in sheet. 2essays and no final:) shes sweet

He's a passionate professor but talks so fast. I skipped all his lectures starting week 2; highly advise against doing this. He talks so fast that it's hard to get down a lot of the info he says. It takes me 3+ hours to go through each podcast. Super heavy reading :( Rec. to make a midterm study guide and work with ppl, final is ok

You could tell he is passionate. His lectures are interesting but gets unorganized at times bc he'll explain 1 painting for 30 min then spends 30 seconds on the next? Also fast talker. Kinda didnt understand the point of reading such long articles if it is exactly what he says in class. 60% of grade is the final, so you kinda HAVE to do well.

His accent helps retain my attention despite my disinterest in the content, but lectures aren't mandatory. He's kinda funny but assigns a TON of reading. I didn't read a single one and still think I did okay. He podcasts, discussions are required.

Norman Bryson is a giant in the field of art history. You wouldn't know it considering how approachable/available he is to students. Seriously, read his book _Looking at the Overlooked_. It's amazing. If you have interest in visual art at all, you should take one of his classes.

He is passionate and cares for the students, and he posts his lectures online, no attendance. 55% final 10pg essay, 15% question memorization final exam, and 30% in-class essay. I really don't see the point of the final exam. Why do we need to remember the names of paintings, authors, and dates? We will literally never use that in the future.

I had him as a professor, not a TA, so my grades dont really reflect his influence. His lectures are nothing special. I would just sit down and zone out because I knew I didnt have to pay attention since I do all the readings anyway. Nothing special. People didnt like his lecturing but I didnt care cuz I was able to zone our in peace.

Deavenport's a chill guy who only gets irrational over phones during lectures tbh. Aside from that he has a very real personality and really makes you feel like he's listening when you participate. DOC 1 honestly depends on the TA for your grade tho, and since mine was pretty chill I got lucky with the A.

Deavenport is a really boring lecturer and he doesnt allow cell phone use during lecture. And your grade really just depends on your TA. Some TAs will really go in depth when talking about the required readings while others barely talk about them. So honestly, if you get a good TA then you could get away with only reading some of whats required.

Juan was a great professor and made his class very enjoyable. While going to lecture isn't mandatory you should go if you didn't read. We had listening and pop quizzes, both of which are easy as long as you listened to the music. One paper, but lots of time to it. Concert assignment, but it was good time! A great class and professor overall

He's a great professor who is really passionate about what he teaches! Made it fun to learn about the topics and provided lots of different material to understand the topics. Assignments aren't too hard and overall was a good class

Professor Juan is very knowledgeable and passionate about his work. His class was like having another history class but with music. His quizzes and tests were very manageable and to study for them all you have to do is listen to music. There is one very short paper but he gives you over a month to do it and writing it was simple.

Juan Rubio is a very funny professor. He is very knowledgeable about the subject he teaches and has a quirky personality. His class has pop quizzes as well as listening quizzes but he tells you beforehand and gives you some time to prepare. Overall, the course entails a considerate amount of reading and you should keep up with the song listenings.

Professor Rubio is a funny guy. His accent is slightly strong, but really passionate about what he's teaching. Listening quizzes are slightly difficult, and pop quizzes are a little more difficult. You really need to put in effort into listening the songs, as well as knowing significance and background of songs and artists.

His homework and quizzes are not that hard, its definitely challenging, but whats the point of easy problems anyways? Midterm is hard because of the limit of time, the question themselves are so interesting and stimulating. If you want some challenges and get some really useful stuff on algorithm, please take him because he is a good lecturer too

Gives unreasonably difficult quizzes and exams. I don't understand why we have a quiz and an exam on the same day with homework due the night before. Poor choice of professor for an undergraduate course. Do NOT take Ragesh. Skip him, even if it means taking 101 a different quarter.

He is horrible, does not use piazza so students cannot reach him. Quiz are so hard. Once he said he would give us an easy quiz but turned out to be the hardest quiz ever. Midterms and quiz on the same day, and homework the night before.

Quiz on the same day as midterms and makes the quizzes unreasonably difficult. Just did a quiz right before writing this out and it was a Leetcode red level difficulty problem which we were expected to write an algorithm for, show runtime, and run on examples all within 15 minutes. during lecture he said our quiz would be "simple".. .unbelieveable

Quizzes every friday with material on the homework due the night before. Homework takes a long time and has lots of proofs. You definitely do not get enough time for the quizzes (you get like 15 minutes and a lot of it is spent reading and understanding the questions). He also gives quizzes and midterms on the same day.

You can tell Professor Zamosc really enjoys what he teaches. Every class consists of him lecturing the whole time and he only grades midterm and final. As long as you go to lectures and read the slides it should be an easy A. The book is required and he does use some material on the tests. Overall great professor and class!

Just attend lecture and make sure to get a general idea of topics. Review slides. You're only graded on midterm and final. Makes pressure to pass higher however they're not too difficult. He curves exams. Readings will be on exams but I did none of the readings & still pulled a 90 on midterm since I attended lecture. Readings weren't too heavy.

Readings are very long but not relevant to daily classes. As long as you get a general idea and attend lectures you will do fine on the midterm/final. Both exams are multiple choice and there are 2 essay assignments

grades were 50% from midterm and 50% from the final, so theres a lot of pressure to do well on tests, there are no other opportunities to get grades up. I would recommend taking this class P/NP if you dont want to stress about tests. Lectures were super boring but you can study for tests fine if you do half the readings and review lecture slides.
He was pretty easy going, and easy to follow. Tests are multiple choice and essays are easy as well.

Second quarter with Prof. Lin. He writes on the blackboard instead of on iPad this quarter, which makes things so much clearer. He tries to make every proof clear (even tho some are still too hard to understand). He is super excited when he talks about manifold and topology, ik it's his research interest haha. Great class overall! Great prof!

Such a great professor. His class may not be jokes-based, but everytime the professor is always well-prepared. His class really helps me develop my proof ability and reasoning. Office hour is extremely helpful for both understanding the materials and the homework. Professor Lin is also super approachable and always willing to consider feedbacks.
My favorite professor in UCSD! He's always so kind and patient, you can solve every problem during his office hour :))
Lectures are heavily proof-based. Confusing sometimes, but the discussion section is extremely helpful.

Nice proachable but no flexibility with rules. Not really good at explaining concepts. What he did is bringing up new concepts, then do proofs without familiaring the entire class with it or gives some INTUITION. Proofs get too abstract sometimes and seem to jump out of nowhere. Need to improve his lecture style as well.
The exams are really tough, but the professor is really good and prepares you well for them. There is a very generous curve, where 85+ is an A, 70+ is a B.
She is smart, too smart. The class is challenging and the homeworks are difficult. Professor Lin's lectures are very inspiring. You will learn a lot from the class and, yet, still fail the exams.
She's a genius.

Really good professor. She really cares about students. The lectures are sometimes a bit to fast to follow but she posts lecture notes online which are really helpful. She is also very accessible outside class. Quizzes are hard but if you spend time studying you can pass. (Also she brings chocolates every time before quizzes).

The homework and quizzes are really hard; the average scores for quizzes were always failing. The content of the course is very difficult, and t doesnt help that the quarter system packs everything so densely, so you really need to go the extra mile to really grasp the material. I highly recommend going to discussion and her office hours.

I can tell that he really cares and is a good person, but his lectures too long, pedantic, and overly intellectual to the point of being unintelligible and almost pointless. For most of his lectures, I don't really know what I'm supposed to pick out from them. Other than that it was a typical MMW class, with a midterm, final, and research paper.

I enjoy Professor Blanco's class. He is extremely passionate about his work and overall the most wholesome professor I have ever had. He is an extremely nice person and he just exudes a kind energy. Only 1 midterm and a final plus iClicker questions that are super easy. His tests are very writing based so you must know your stuff!

Clearly MMW is not his subject of specialty but many of his lectures although founded in some sort of historical roots end up going down problematic paths. He ends up coming off as though he is appropriating culture at least once a lecture and misrepresents historical figures by giving examples of their actions w/o providing context. Easy class tho

Professor Blanco demonstrates a great passion for the class and the material. However, his lecture style is awful. Most of the time he either spends time talking about a topic way too long or saying more than what is needed. There was no midterm, only one clicker quiz question each lecture and final. Ridiculous grading scale. Would not recommend.

The class was very easy it consisted of two papers, a midterm, and a final. There were no homework assignments besides the papers and study. The professor made the class very interesting and really drew in the attention of the class.

a lovely professor. Lectures are clear and easy to follow, includes just enough math to explain the basics but tests very little math. 3 written reports. people struggled grade wise but this class was easy. tests test facts from the slides so know all of the slide info really well. tests a mix of concepts but know all of the details on slides .

Probably the most disorganized class I'll ever take at UCSD. She had no structure for what we needed to do and didn't really teach. One of the guest speakers we had probably taught us more in a day than what we learned in a quarter. Too bad the TAs were actually cool. I heard the last professor for this actually had a structure so idk what happened

Highly do not recommend taking her. She has no structure and assigns homework that can take you upwards of 3 hours to do. It felt like the class was a complete waste of time and was filled with busy work, including the midterm. I feel like i learned absolutely nothing from this course. I am not paying tuition at UCSD to not learn.

This is the worst professor I have ever taken at UCSD. The class is VERY pointless with busy work that can take you upwards of 3 hours to do. It is an absolute waste of time. For the Final, she wants us to write about all "musical parameters" learned in class for 32 group's video performances and their made up scores. DONT take her for MUS 5.

One of the hardest computer science topics combined with some of the vaguest, least helpful and most confusing lectures and slides I have ever seen. Heavily homework based with each assignment taking 30+ hours to complete. Assignment writeups are not clear leaving students to put in mountains of extra time trying to put pieces together. Stay away.

Very unorganized. Passion isn't the only ingredient for teaching. He is unable to give clear explanation for any of the materials. Students are constantly confused and had to do extra work outside of the class to understand.
Great lectures, fair exams, nice curve at the end. I recommend.
I have to say, this is the worst class I've ever take. I'm afraid to fail the final exam. Waste time. Never gonna to take this again!

I will NEVER EVER take his class anymore. His slides are the most terrible ones I have ever seen. When you are doing his HW, you will always find something that you don't understand because he didn't write them down on his slides. The most annoying thing is, his HW is not hard, but you always spent huge amount of time doing it cuz nothing is clear.

Shares wisdom resources, applications. Helps with strengths, critical skills. Covers technical, process, career. People, places, things to further individual interests. Come away with portfolio pieces, good understanding of quality of work expected for professional portfolio; and how to improve and develop additional works. Thanks!

Professor Arneson clearly knows what he is talking about in lectures. However, lectures are bland and include Iclicker quiz questions. He gave a generous curve on the clicker questions. Essays aren't too bad. The final is easy if you prepare the free response in advance and understand the main ideas.
Arneson is a passionate 73 year old professor. Never before have I seen someone with so much energy at such an old age. Hats off to him, and may UCSD experience many more years of his good work!

Powerpoints and assigned readings just consist of heavy blocks of texts and endless rambling. Clear grading criteria isn't provided, so your grade really depends on your TA. Clicker questions are used to test reading comprehension and are graded on accuracy, though Arneson has admitted his Clicker Q's don't always make the most sense.

I love his blunt honesty on every topic we talked about. The only critique I have for him is that his notes are not very simple to understand and he comes to class late and disorganized. But overall - he's a great philosopher and teacher!

He provides EXCELLENT notes on the course topics, reading is mandatory but he explains it if it is unclear or difficult. He was also very helpful and wiling to answer questions in office hours. He also provided a great environment for class discussions. He has a somewhat dry sense of humor but it was always entertaining and endearing.

Honestly I loved having Aaron for Phil 27. He was so caring and open to what people had to say. He seems like he genuinely cares about what people have to argue and why they came to that conclusion. Overall, his lectures were interesting and he was an overall cool person.
Avoid this man for Math 9. I truly dont think he realizes we have other classes too judging by the absurd amount of homework he gives. Class is mostly based on midterms and final.

This man ruined my life. He assigns an absurd amount of homework every week and truly believes that everyone should dedicate every amount of time they have to his class. He's condescending during office hours and his tests are extremely long and difficult. Avoid this man at all costs.

His Math 9 class at SCU was a debacle. Luvreet had absolutely no idea that he was teaching the lowest level math class at the school. Guy thought he was teaching a bunch of math majors. I honestly don't think Luvreet realized that his students had other classes and other commitments. He gave "parallel problems" which he claimed would take 20 hours.

Luvreet is the hardest teacher I have ever had. He makes his class ridiculously hard to get a good grade, even when he gives points back for doing corrections. If your work and answer isnt exactly as he wants it, he will take away as many points as he can. His homework and exams are also way harder than the problems he does in class. Avoid him.
This is the worst class I have ever taken in my life. That says it all. GOODBYE GPA

Professor did not explain the material very well and was just generally not a great lecturer. Homework was extremely minimal and easy and lectures are straight out of the textbook, so not necessary to read. He wanted problems solved in a very specific manner and the class did not understand what he wanted. Very weird and confusing class in general
Simply put: amazing in every way you can imagine! She is an exemplary professor for all Sociology professors on UCSD campus! 100%!
The best professor ever! I looked forward to going to class every time. She is super cool and cares to hear about her students' opinions. Take her if you can, no regrets!

I just wish all the professors at UCSD were like her. She is a very nice and caring individual who truly cares about her students, this can be seen in her conduct. The topics covered in class were very interesting and her explanations were clear. The grade was broken down to (5) 20% criteria which made things more pleasant and less stressful.

Professor Lawston is an amazing person all in all. Her lectures are super straightforward and you know what she expects out of you. She's personable, relatable, and intelligent. Would take her again for sure.
One of the best professors in the Political Science Department.

The grade is one big research project paper and a few oral presentations; prof spends a lot of time lecturing and discussing expectations but provides plenty of opportunities to workshop your project and paper. The unique topic addressed with lecture heavy classes, though very approachable for first-time students

Avoid this professor! The class is VERY lecture heavy, and he just spills out material without any engagement/connection to real examples. The class is based off of 2 oral presentations and 1 final research paper. There was very little guidelines given, which was difficult since you don't know what he's looking for. Focuses more on language than SJ

Dr. Haviland is highly respected in the field and you get a real opportunity to soak in some excellent lectures- those complaining about "clear grading criteria" are obviously not as invested in learning as they are about their GPA. He is very busy but still makes time for his students. Take any class he teaches! He's great

OK Haviland is good at what he does, but this course is by NO MEANS STRUCTURED! You're entire grade is based off a project paper with no cear prompt or grading criteria - even when asked he was vague with answers. That being said he is willing to help. The paper isn't easy, but does prepare you for work as an anthropologist. He is a great guy ovral

I am a better writer and think about words and language differently because of this class. I enjoyed Prof. Haviland's lecture style and they way he relates concepts through his research, which puts it into a context that makes sense. Useful feedback on papers and gives you a chance to rewrite them. Independent students will do well. Def. take him!

I took her for101. The lectures were sometimes pretty fun. However, the only study guide for midterm was about drawing trees(syntax). So you don't know what to study before exam. if you take her, go to the lectures or you won't understand the content by merely looking at the slides that dont help. The average for our class was C. Not recommended

Dr. Wittenberg is an excellent professor! She is very knowledgeable and passionate about linguistics, and makes it so fun to learn. Little HW, exams representative of course material as presented in lecture and the book, and fair grading overall. I really enjoyed this class and learned a lot. Wonderful prof!

She is THE COOLEST professor I have ever met. Her lectures are interesting and provide all the informations for student need to know for a straight A. If you do all the work she asks you to do, read all the readings, you will find that the course is not that hard at all!

What an amazing woman. Professor Kaplan is by far the best lecturer I've ever had the privilege of listening to. The material in the course is difficult, so it requires an EXTREMELY open mind. Students who complain that she "rambles" just aren't paying attention. Tough, tough grader, but her lectures are worth it. And, she's funny! Take her. Do it.

Amazing lecturer. She gives a lot of readings but if you do at least 80% of them it should be an easy A. People will say she comes off condescending and stuff but honestly if you just ask questions with an open mind then you'll learn a lot. She did undergrad at Yale and grad at Berkeley, and she's also an activist so she knows her stuff.

She is very passionate about what she teaches, but she doesn't take criticism well and often rambles for the entire lecture. I found that it was difficult to keep track of what she was really trying to say through all her rambling. She also posts things late all the time even though she expects students to get everything done on time.

She is such an amazing person and the lectures that she gives are inspiring and I am happy about the readings list that she chose for the quarter.  I think she has a room for development for time management and making times for office hours for students, but other than that, she is a great professor.

Professor Rodriguez is very sweet but she's all over the place as a lecturer. There's so much information packed into her lecture slides yet so goes through them super fast making it difficult to keep up during lecture. Midterm had some really specific questions that were barely covered during lecture but just buried somewhere in a lecture slide.

Professor Rodriguez seems very nice but you can tell she's very new to teaching. Lectures are so dense and all over the place. She goes through all the slides so quickly without expanding on the topic or attempting to break it down. Homework is really tedious and overwhelming.

Probably one of the best math professors Ive ever had. He really cares about his students and will always want to help if you are confused or have any questions. Midterms were pretty fair and reflected his practice exams. Final was cumulative but doable. Take his class if you can!
Amazing professor. First midterm very fair, second midterm was more difficult and the final was cumulative but easy if you did all the homework and studied the quizzes.
Grad student teacher a pre-cal class. Very boring lectures. Quizzes every Thursday night lecture with little to no time to complete them. Lots of homework every week and harsh grading.

Professor Cao is easily the best professor Ive ever had in my 3 years at UCSD. Ive never heard anyone explain such difficult concepts with such clarity and articulation. He is truly a master of teaching. He schedules office hours to fit your schedule, its amazing! I cant recommend him enough.

Professor Cao is my favorite professor over the two years I've been at UCSD. The best way to describe his class is a Rubix cube, difficult but enjoyable. Despite it being difficult at times, Professor Cao is always available to help and will schedule numerous office hours just to help you! Wow he's such a good teacher.

I cannot praise Professor Cao enough. He was always very understanding and helpful. Professor Cao single-handedly made me want to switch from Electrical Engineering to Computer Engineering. In lab, he is very articulate and well prepared. His best trait is that he is a Well Educated (and) Extremely Brilliant professor.
Infantilizing pedagogical approach (i.e. approaches teaching as if she was teaching at high school level or lower). AVOID if possible.
Imada was totally inaccessible. She asked us to email her TA before emailing her and even had a FAQ to prevent us from asking her questions. Would never take her class again. Awful.

She is an amazing professor! She guides you through difficult text and helps you on your research topics. She is very dedicated to teaching students and would gladly work with your schedule to meet with you. She is an awesome professor! Take her and you will not regret it! But you have to be willing to work and earn your grade.

Prof. Imada is brilliant, compassionate, and attentive. She really cares about her students to the point that she brought food almost everytime for everyone in the class. I learned so much from her. I recommend her to everyone. She seems intimidating but I mean for her appearance, I feel like you have to be intimidating to be taken seriously.

I agree that the class acted like high school students. She was rude to the class. There was a heavy reading load but it was repetitive so you can skim. I learned a lot from the class. Her lectures were mandatory but she is a good lecturer. Very good slides. She gives extra credit assignments
This guy loves boba as much as he loves cs. I heard he once did a miniso challenge driving down from norcal to socal.

Professor Chen is an amazing lecturer and very knowledgeable about many fields in Computer Science. However, what I found most compelling about my experience with him was his desire to promote excellence in all of his students. He has inspired not only me, but my peers to achieve great things. I would take him again. Light it up!

Professor Victor Chen, aka the CS god of UCSD, is unequivocally the best CS professor in California. His perception and understanding of computer science is other-worldly; he can see into the matrix. I have learned more about computer science from him in one quarter than my entire computer science career. His tutelage is worth its weight in code.

Professor Chen is the most well rounded professor Ive ever had. His wealth of knowledge in how to masterfully tackle the vast realm of CS interviews is bar none. He inspired me to shoot for what I always thought was impossible - a job. Before taking this class, I never thought I would amount to anything, but he helped me realize my true potential.

Professor Chen is the epitome of well-roundedness. I've ever had! He was very successful in dispensing his wealth of knowledge on the subject of achieving excellence in job interviews. His invaluable lessons have been invaluable in my professional development. His courtesy and generosity make me question the common saying: "chavalry is dead."
The study guide is really helpful! Just make sure you memorize the key points and match the music pieces, you will ace it!

Professor Allen taught Music 4 well. Although it was her first time teaching the class, I could barely tell. She always showed up prepared and happy to teach us. Although most people (including myself) take this class as a GE, it's rather interesting. Professor Allen and my TA gave me a fresh perspective on music.

This class was fine! She keeps the lectures interesting, I just find it kinda extra that we have to write two essays on the midterm and final. Also it's annoying that the two essay assignments are graded from 1-10, kinda drags the grade down if it's not perfect. Anyway, I'd recommend for a solid GE.

Although her teaching style was a bit confusing, she was a caring teacher none the less. She has a bit to improve on with her teaching style, but the students gave her a harder time than needed. Students were rude to her instead of giving her helpful feedback. She just needed more experience. The class is very test heavy. 95% depend on the tests.

I got an A in AP Physics A in high school and a 5 on the AP test. However, I was still confused after her lectures. Her teaching method was extremely confusing, and whenever I asked questions, she did not really answer them, leaving me more frustrated. It was easier to skip lectures and learn on my own in half the time.

Out of all teachers in JCC. If you truly want to learn something useful, I highly recommend taking any class from David Kadanoff. Well spoken, open minded, inspiring, fair, doesnt discourage anyone. The only downfall would be if you dont like reading, youre unlikely to get a good grade. Still, a remarkable teacher.

One of the greatest professors I've ever had, both in and out of the soci department. He is clear and organized, lectures are interesting, provokes intellectual thought and discussion, expectations are reasonable,reading is do-able, interacts with his students, genuinely cares and is funny. Overall, phenomenal human being.
He's a very fair grader. He cares about his students and makes class interesting and funny. He uses personal anecdotes that are actually funny. Lectures are fun and fly by.

Class seems easy, midterm isn't too bad if you study. The final paper is worth 30 percent and he will grade it ridiculously hard and it will destroy your grade. Even if you participate every day, he still won't give you full points. Went in thinking I was definitely getting an A ended up with a B+.
Great professor! Super interesting lectures. Grade based off one midterm, final and paper.

Professor Beauton conducts MUS 95L, the Wind Ensemble, and he is amazing! He picked fun, challenging pieces to learn, and the audition was very relaxed and comfortable. In rehearsal, he knows how to get good work done but still knows when a joke is appropriate. Class is long but only once a week. Very funny, great conductor, 10/10 would take again!

She's a very straight forward lecturer that explains concepts very clear. Maybe it was so clear to me because I've learned most of the concepts in high school before, but her lectures were very educational for me and really helped me do well on my midterms and exams. The midterm levels didn't compare to the finals tho, the finals was challenging.

Took her for MATH 10A. A little hard to understand and goes over course material very fast. Doesn't explain complex concepts very well and doesn't thoroughly explain her thinking process either (when solving problems). However, if you have any questions, she will try to help.

She's really good at explaining fundamental concepts and the first two midterms were easy but the final destroyed all of us, though I think that is more of a department problem rather than her. You can tell she's just there to teach but she's really good at explaining and making things clear.

Does a lot of proofs but clearly states at the end what you need to know from it. Homework sometimes is really hard but it's good for over preparing you for the tests. The tests were pretty easy in comparison.

Her lectures are proof-based and are great for trying to get a more fundamental understanding of the material. I personally did not enjoy this lecture style but I greatly appreciated her kindness in matters regarding late or absent work as she was considerate in granting extensions for homework. Tests were relatively easy.

A very fun, loving professor, but the lectures are not helpful nor mandatory. The midterms and finals are graded based on the problem sets, so KNOW THOSE BY HEART. Section is optional, but gets you extra points and the TAs can help you on the problem sets. Class was difficult because it's based on exams, but know the sets and you'll ace it!

Doctor Wilhelm is able to treat his students like adults by letting them decide on their own attendance (ec discussion included) because he is an endlessly fascinating character with robust knowledge of his subject. By far my best prof of the quarter. I learned in every class but did not feel my test performance reflected that. Happy with my grade

I have never had a professor like him before. He is super entertaining, and I have never went to a class where I have been able to feel focused during the entire lecture. He was really clear on what was important, so getting an A in the class was not hard. I read three days for the midterm and three for the exam. I usually get C's and D's back home

His tests are only vaguely similar to the problem sets and are different from a lot of the stuff he teaches. The grading on the midterm was also pretty bad, as the graders were clearly looking for key words to give you points so that even if you answered the question, you wouldn't receive full points.

Prof. Wilhelm is a good teacher, but his tests are really difficult. He claims that they follow along with the problem sets, but they differ heavy, as the test is far more conceptual while the problem sets emphasize understanding experiments relating to the concepts. The difference is significant enough to confuse you.

Loved this class! Very straightforward, grades were solely based off the quizzes and final. She provides so many resources, practice, office hours, and you can go to any section with any of the three TA's (which is nice if your scheduled discussion is early in the morning). Attendance for both lecture and section are not required.

Attending the lectures and discussions are not required. It is very important to read the one required textbook for the class. She is very engaging and makes a lot of good references . However, there is a lot to go over so you have to practice on your own or you won't pass. There are only 6 quizzes and 1 final for the class.

Online HW and weekly quizzes are based on the HW. You don't need to go to lecture if you are able to teach yourself the material based on the HW. He can get boring sometimes but he seems like a cool guy. Gives a practice midterm and final which are totally fair game if you understood everything and lets you use a page of notes.

Tucker is an absolutely terrible professor, who seems to be very careless about his job and students. His lectures are very unprepared, as he constantly makes mistakes, and he skips around material; forgetting to cover some stuff and then coming back to it. There's also an insane amount of HW, double or triple what is usually in other 20B classes.

His class has more homework versus other professors of 20B. Near double the amount. His practice exams are easier versions of the exam, where as other professors make the practice exam harder but the exam easier. Unless you have the time to invest into his course or are confident in your mathematical skills, skip him. No Ds, no pass means an F.
I'm Jedy and he's such a bad professor: disorganized, tends to make mistakes, and lectures are completely useless
The practice midterms and practice final are basically the real thing. His lectures are useless but easy A if you do the homework and can copy down the practice midterm on your cheat sheet.
His exam is based on homework.

Professor Das is a new prof, so he's still learning what works for his teaching and what doesn't. He cares a lot about his students and is always willing to help outside of scheduled office hours. Test questions are fair, but time can be an issue. Tests based on homework, cheat sheet allowed. Has an accent, but is understandable

Super nice and passionate about what he does. I took him for TDGE 10, and the class is mainly based on watching movies during lecture and taking quizzes. Extremely understanding of students and makes all exams (quizzes/midterm) very manageable.

I absolutely love professor Tregar. The topic she chose for this course was serial killer films so her lectures were very interesting. There were 10 question quizzes after every lecture, a film pitch, midterm, and a final, which were all pretty easy so this class is an excellent choice to cover a fine arts GE.

Dr. Breit is great! There's weekly reflections to help boost your grade, 4 quizzes and a cumulative final, and she gives study guides for all of them. Really lecture heavy, but she makes the material interesting to keep you engaged! Definitely recommend!!

Weekly reflections are easy and help you stay on track. She genuinely cares about the students (even offering partial credit if you forgot to do it one week). Attendance is not mandatory but she doesn't podcast, so go! The notes are clear and easy to understand. Two non-cumulative exams, great review guide. TAKE HER! She's awesome. Best professor.

She is such a cool professor! She is really funny and passionate about the topic she teaches. She podcasts and offers extra credit. Grade determined by 2 non-cumulative tests and weekly reflections. She offers a mini-study guide that is helpful and her tests are very reflective of it. She does include a lot of neuro-bio so beware of it!

She made my first quarter here much easier! She knows who you are, what you should work on, and how you can address the issues. Approachable and caring! Muir writing is hard (like really hard, harder than hard). But she makes you understand the circumstances and helps you navigate yourself. I hope I can take MCWP50 with her!
the TAs grade however they desire. poor communication, absolutely no feedback on your paper. don't take this class

Super easy A, but for a DEI, this class was actually a lot of work. The first weeks were easy, but then you had 3 research essays. Grading was easy, but writing a 6 or 8 page research essay isn't a light task. No midterm, no final, and no quizzes though. If you're better with papers than you are with tests, then this is the class for you!

Professor wasn't that bad but kinda incompetent. Most of the syllabus didn't make sense, especially dates and stuff. Readers were not on the same page with the Professor as far as what to expect on assignments. Prof wasnt balanced when it came to the material, clearly had her own agenda.

One of those classes you'll never forgot. The class was about 80 people and 90% girls. I'm a guy so it was pretty awesome. VERY VERY EASY A. The professor gives EVERYONE pretty much AT LEAST an A-. TAKE HER! EASY A + GPA BOOST!

Easy A as long as you keep up with all the busy work. Don't stress too much over the work-- just get it done and the grading's pretty generous. Be careful though: if you write things contrary to P.Allen's opinions, you will be graded down. Attendance is required. You'll need the reader to complete the weekly assignments, but you can skim.
Great Teacher. He is always willing to help and genuinely believes that the students are able to succeed as long as they put in the work.

Professor Ben is really approachable out side of class. Whenever I have questions on my writings, he replied my email really fast. He give good and important feedbacks that allow me to revise it properly.

Professor Sheredos gives specific tips on how to revise your essay. He also makes the sessions less boring by discussing the articles we are reading and gives us better concepts on what are the things he would expect to see we write.
He cares a lot about his students and gives great feedback.
He has been a very caring person outside of being a great lecturer. He does a great job at make the readings more understandable. Would gladly take him as a prof. again if given the chance to.

Prof Biernacki is the best! Although the class is graded on few things (a midterm essay and final) he's super helpful. As long as you attend lecture, the essay is easy to write and he provides SUPER helpful review sheets that come in handy for the final. 10/10 would recommend
Lot's and lot's of reading. Also the professor is very liberal and although he says he will not go into political issue in the beginning of the class, he went political at least once every week.
Sweet, approachable man. Very passionate about understanding the Holocaust. My regret is that I didn't take more courses with him while I was at UC,San Diego.

This guy is the best professor I have ever had, I just want to hug him. He is such a gentle soul- so genuine, so lovable... kindness just radiates from him. He is a brilliant man as well, and you will leave conversations having one of those "hallelujah" brain-blast moments. Honestly, take any of his classes if it's the last thing you do. PLEASE!
He's kind of all over the place but its an interesting/easy class. reading the books is the most helpful for the final, his study guide was specific

He is my TA this quarter but he did not know how to be patient to his students. And when I asked him questions after DI class, he always seemed not patient to me as well. His grading was really really tough! I got 10/20 for my first essay, 32/40 for my second paper. He did not mention how to write it or showed sample essay to us before submission.

One of my favorite instructors. He encourages engagement and creativity very well and is an all around great person. I feel I have learned a lot and was not too overwhelmed, he also gives great feedback.

Michael Ano was probably the worst teacher I had at UCSD. I never understood what the class even was supposed to teach us, he would just show us clips from random things like "Comedians in Cars Getting Coffee" and then ask us to talk about it. None of what he assigned or showed us had to do with the subject. I would not recommend this professor.

This class made me feel like I was back in high school with literally all the busy work in the world. I honestly didn't learn anything except that he feels as if all the students in his class are liberal arts or non-stem majors because he assigns so much pointless work. Would NOT recommend taking him if you're a stem major.

The class was about art, and he made it fun, but the lectures were a lot of the same thing. I would say you don't need to go, but he occasionally takes attendance. All the work is on the TAs, so I never went to his office hours. He's a fun guy, and pretty easy to pass.

Professor Ano genuinely cares about his students and encourages participation and critical thinking. He is very energetic and still has that eager attitude towards teaching that many professors lose or do not have. Overall, he is a super cool dude, the workload is very easy, but the lectures feel little pointless sometimes.

Super thick accent, very difficult to understand. Only take Math 11 with her if you have a background in statistics (basic high school or AP) otherwise you will be very lost. She doesn't have the best command of the material, but her grading rubric is easily accessible and very lenient as well. Exams are not that difficult. Does not podcast.

Her "class website" was vague and not useful. The syllabus didn't even list the percentage distribution (%HW, %FINAL etc)for the class. Huang is very last minute, and let us know the night before the due date that we had to use a different portal to submit homework. Lectures not useful. Would rather her speak in simply than sigmas n calculus..

Professor Blomstedt just started WCWP 160 and it needs more recognition!! The class is not very difficult, you have a lot of freedom in terms of what you write about. If you put effort and actually do the work you'll get a good grade. Participation, homework, and attendance account for 1/3 of your grade (easy points!!). There is 1 major paper only.

Liz is a very solid instructor; knowledgeable, insightful, and cares about her students. WCWP 100 is required for all Warren Transfers, but she really made the curriculum interesting and useful. I definitely left the class feeling more comfortable with writing. Also, shes very clear on her grading and expectations. Highly recommend.

One of the most chill professors at UCSD and definitely out of the Warren Writing profs (I know because I've been waitlisted many times and finally got into her class). The bulk of homework is taking notes on assigned readings and she gives good feedback on mandatory drafts which is really nice/helpful. Lectures are interesting, would def re-take
Very repetitive but that makes the course real easy. He's a really nice person and teaches in a fun way. Doesn't take grading too seriously, seems to give marks away without a care in the world.

A cool  professor. lectures are repetitive but repetition means less stuff for u to remember =]. Class is straight forwardjust read over the pdf files  and u'll do fine. 4 quizzes (last one is the final exam), each is 25% of the class and yup, final is NOT cumulative. Easy A imo, average was higher than 80% i think. IMPOSSIBLE TO FAIL
Easy class, cool material but the lectures are repetitive

Gives a lot of unnecessary homework due whenever you have class (basically every other day). Tougher grader is not even the right word, she will literally critic every assignment you do even if it's good. She makes it MANDATORY for you meet up with your group a couple times. Class time is almost pointless but it IS mandatory. Be ready to read!

Krizovensky does not make anything clear. She does not giver clear instructions for homework or essays and then expects well written papers. One of the most picky professors I've ever had. Even when you follow the rubric she will find ways to lower your grade. Avoid this class and professor at all costs.

You never know what Jaclyn wants. There's always random homework assignments with bad directions. She will call you out in front of the class and is not afraid to tell you how awful your writing is. She wrote me feedback on a rough draft and I used it to rewrite. She then told me my new draft was awful. Don't take this class, didn't help me at all.

Jaclyn is an amazing instructor. I resisted to devote to the class at first, but after couple assignment I realized my shortcomings in eng writing as intl student. If you read the book and discuss with Jaclyn, she will give precious response that lets you score really high for assignment. ELWR well prepared me for college writing. I am not an ad.

It's sort of sad to have an analytical writing professor to have so many grammar/ subject-verb agreement mistakes. Homework assignments are due at such random times you have to check online constantly in order to stay on track. She does not clarify her online instructions more specifically, and after you turn in a would say it's done incorrectly.

This man is super unorganized and can not lecture for his life. I can confirm, the ratings do not lie. His lectures are hard to follow and he does not take the feedback of his students. He removed the practice questions from web-assign and made the class more difficult because he was already poor at lecturing. I was left without a fighting chance.

midterms were obscure and much harder than problems in the textbook. Too many problems in 50 min. Lectures are unclear, hard to follow, unorganized. He did answer many questions online which was helpful. If you want to do well it's better to read the textbook and have a comprehensive understanding of the material, then pray for partial credit.

His first two midterms were too long (7 ques) while previous midterms given at the school were 4 problems. Luckily TAs were QUITE lenient. He talks too slowly; lectures were a mess. Bad at teaching material. Went a few times then decided reading txtbook was more efficient. final was manageable. Only reason I did well  thoroughly studied txtbook

This was his first year teaching as a professor, so the course wasn't perfect. However, he did help a lot and answer a lot of questions online and during office hours. The tests were not graded too harshly, where lots of partial credit would be given. He is a nice guy and is willing to help you, and will probably improve as a professor next year.

Honestly, I don't think this professor is qualified to teach at UCSD. His handwriting is terrible. Although I took Ap Calculus AB in high school and got a 5, I can barely understand his teaching materials. His midterm was harder than the assignments and his lecture materials. I had an extremely hard time for the first four weeks, so I dropped it.

This artist/professor is highly recognized in the art world. Unfortunately many students didn't appreciate him and think he "sucks" because he does not teach technique. He tries to engage your higher thinking and conceptualism. He appreciates those who truly want to learn and push intellectual boundaries; not those focused on technical skills.

Very nice professor but terrible lecturer. Mostly focused on Molecular Biology rather than biochemistry. However he teaches molecular biology terribly! Thankfully i took molecular bio before this class. I didn't show up to lecture because i had already learned his material. Super easy class but it wont prepare you for the next course. He podcast.

Professor Opella is very good at what he does. His slides are well made and reflect the most important parts of ochem. I lose attention because he has a voice that is easily tuned out. However, he recaptures my attentions with his jokes. Unfortunately, because it's too early in the morning, the jokes are often lost on the class. He's very helpful

Professor Opella is straightforward when it comes to exams. He goes over only the most important concepts and right before the exams, tells us what questions to expect. Unfortunately we get pretty behind compared to other classes. It is quite possible to get an A in the class; but we warned: you won't be as adequately prepared for 140B.
Great Professor, great guy. He's the reason I pursued biochem as a major. Textbook heavy, but then again, most bio classes are.
Great professor! Lectures are interesting. He is very approachable and very helpful. He has a great sense of humor and is very approachable. LOVE THIS PROFESSOR! He is my favorite prof. at UCSD.

Hardly ever taught it was mostly her TA doing the lectures, only saw Prather 4x. Material can be interesting but mostly dry. TON of memorization, she gives you a pretty good idea of what to study but at the end of the day you need to memorize a LOT of boring stuff. Guest lectures are boring. I wouldn't recommend.
Great personality and was a lot of help outside of class. She is a great teacher! Be prepared to take notes and email if your have any questions! She was always willing to help!!

Avoid at all cost. This class is a joke. It is 10th week teacher hasnt been to class since 5th week just to distribute the unfair midterm. Also, midterms were never handed back. Nobody has any idea how they are doing in this class. Pathetic.  once again AVOID

Prather is the worst professor I've had at UCSD: she not only didn't teach well but barely even attended lectures for an entire quarter! She has no shame in asking other teachers to substitute while never showing up. She never even handed back the midterm and it's already 9th week. She is the perfect example of why our education system is failing.
Bets teacher ever nothing else just is so nice and cool
Do it. Enroll. Just do it.
There was a lot of changes in the class since he had never taught Ethn2. But overall his lectures are really interesting and he really cares about his students. The class is not too difficult either.
The structure of his class was very confusing. There is a lot of work involved, but he cares deeply about his students and gives great lectures. Attendance is required.

Prof. Yang is very caring about his students and he is very creative about his lecture. To let us understand some abstract theories, he lets us to involve and act in the shoes of narrators. He always gives one project for students to do each quarter, which allows students to express their own voices in their own artsy way.

funny and humorous prof. definitely go to lecture or else you will fail the midterm and final. lots of extra credit offered and the lecture is interesting so you wont be bored. midterm is open novel and there is a big project due at the end and builds up by writing notebook entries with different prompts every week. also depends on TA you get.

must do the readings because of midterm and pop quiz. There is one big paper due at the end of the quarter. Lectures are ranting and story telling. Beisdes that I love his class, it's really opened my eyes.

Rona-Tas is well experienced in his field but the class is pretty confusing. 9 HW assignments worth 63% of your grade, final assignment 20%, 5% participation and midterm 12%. Had to buy expensive software programs (SPSS & NVIVO) and the work was hard, but if you go to his office hours he is really helpful and the one on one is worth it.

Grade based on weekly/biweekly assignments (10 total), 1 midterm, 1 final. Very caring, allowed us the chance to try again for a couple assignments that a lot of the class was confused about. Lectures somewhat all over the place. Responds to emails very fast but short responses.

2 in class midterms and one final. There are three short writing assignments. Test material all relates to lectures and readings. I did not do all the readings but attended almost every lecture and got an A. Course offers a good selection of sociology related movies. Interesting lectures. I would take again.

Akos is passionate about the films and our ideas - but ultimately he has joined the dots with the sociology and the films we are watching, and classes could get boring when not talking about the films. I thought he was kind, approachable and a generous marker. A good easy(ish) and enjoyable sociology option. I'll remember him more than the course.

Worst professors I have experienced at UCSD. He claims himself as a historian, which made him the most harsh paper grader I have ever seen. Most Ironically, though he enjoys critiquing the traditional powerpoint lecture style among other professors, he does the same thing and it seems no better than any others. For God Sake Don't choose him.

Interesting guy, but hard to please. He comes across as quite harsh in his tone and language. He is clearly extremely knowledgeable/ smart, but seems to struggle to teach without making students feel they are dumb. He is not impressed with slackers, but also not impressed by people who try hard, raise their hands in class, and participate often.

I had Professor Tanaka 25+ years ago for two classes and he was fantastic. I doubt he's changed that much. He pushes hard but if you do your work and push back, you'll do well. I am a fairly right-wing fellow, he's pretty liberal. Got on great in classes about the atomic bomb and other stuff. Maybe he's changed, but I liked and still admire him
He is not clear about any of his teachings and confuses students. He does not take feedback well .

DON'T TAKE HIM. His standards are too high /he is too arrogant for how unintelligent he is. His harsh grading does nothing for his students' actual learning. I heard he brags to other professors in the dept about how many low grades he passes out. Who does that? Clearly, he's doing something wrong. He is a terrible professor and person.

Every lecture is very content heavy and Professor Vaida makes it a bit more difficult to understand the concepts than it already is. I feel like he could explain the materials better but the class in general is not too difficult if you just practice the previous exams he gives you. There are weekly homework assignments that you work with a partner.

Professor Vaida is an extremely nice and caring instructor. Although his lecture slides are content-heavy, he makes it clear what he wants you to focus on for the exams. He's also super helpful so ask questions during class. There are weekly homework assignments. To understand the material and pass the class, go to the weekly problem sessions.

She only gives us one C PA through the entire quarter at the end, which leaves us unprepared for CSE30 when we're assumed familiar with C and given lots of hard PAs in C. Her lectures are also short and useless, like she doesn't have anything to say so decides not to say anything. Having left her class, I feel like I now know no more than before

Her lectures are very oriented around real-world connections. She spends a lot of her lecture going over a topic and how we see it in our lives, but she also makes sure to get into the nitty-gritty as well. She doesn't like prolonging her lectures longer than necessary, which is nice.

CSE 12 was significantly easier at least for me, not really sure why, and Professor Zaitsev did a great job explaining many of the difficult concepts in my opinion. I have managed to get 90+ on every single PA so far and ace the midterm without really needing extra help or anything, though the 8 A.M. class time is not ideal. Overall recommend.

Great professor, horrible class. Professor and TA's kinda just throw you into assignments and expect you to know how. In order to do most of the assignments I had to go out of my way to ask a million questions (i'm not one for questions, which is why in most of my classes I can get away with just paying attention). Work was annoying and tedious.

She is a really caring, patient, inspiring and positive professor to work with. She would spend half an hour during office hour helping you with installation of text editor while some other professors just simply assuming you have already known everything.

Genuinely feels like a powertripping dictator in a class of totally indifferent students. Not only outright changes the contents of the official course, but provides vague assignments that don't teach anything about artistic technique. Only take if you need it for a ge or major requirement. Aliases as "Kiki" or "Staff" to deter negative perception
She was a good TA. The only thing is that you gotta make the essays count

The professor was not helpful at all and I had to teach myself the whole course because his lectures were useless. He has a thick accent which makes it more difficult to understand what he's explaining. The only useful thing was the homework, but I mostly relied on youtube lessons to finish them. You're better off with khanacademy and a laptop

Wang is a great guy but a pretty bad professor. Stopped going to lecture after week 3 and did well above average on the midterms but the final was TOUGH. Do the Hw (its mandatory anyway) ,read because he will test on theorem definitions, and make sure you understand the past/sample exams and you will do fine.
Although his lecture is heavy and homework is hard, his questions are motivated and useful to prepare for exam, espcially you are math major

Terrible professor. Accent is not understandable and lecture makes no sense. Jumps around topics in lecture. I studied hard and passed only with the curve. Is disorganized and I learned more from the textbook than him. Textbook itself is bad so I didn't learn much. Doesn't post lectures online, because they are handwritten on chalkboard.

Lectures are interesting but can reason through problem solving too quickly. Would be nice if lectures were podcasted to revisit her problem solving techniques. Exams were fair and didn't have surprises, just do the homework and review lecture material carefully. Overall a caring, smart professor who wants to help you succeed.

Although his lectures are a little boring because he just reads off of the slides, he is an overall really nice guy that cares about his students. He has a very generous curve and wants his students to do well.

Horrible lecturer, you can get past the accent, but he just reads off the lecture slides, and as a student with no physics background whatsoever, this intro class was really difficult. Don't take this guy.
The quiz questions are straightforward. Posts solutions to optional homework. Do all the homework and you will do fine.

Lectures are essentially useless for the quizzes. The homework (straight out of the book) can sometimes be helpful, but he does not help at all with it through lecture. This class was essentially a guessing game.  The clicker questions (which are extra credit) seem to all be trick questions. This class was frustrating and I would not recommend it.

I wouldn't recommend that you take him if you can avoid it. He has a monotone voice and very little interest in being a teacher. This disinterest in teaching is apparent in his lectures.  Doesn't help prepare you for the quizzes. Get your nose in that textbook right away.
Most of the class is showing up for labs, but the other portion is wicked hard tests that you must study for.

15L is just basic stuff about Unix commands, vim, git, Makefiles, and other stuff that you can easily look up online in 5 seconds. Instead, they make you memorize things. Altintas is fine, but can get a little bit difficult to understand at times.

Going to class isn't required, but you have to understand the lecture slides to do well. Go to labs, do the homework, and memorize commands! Course material is boring except for shell scripting. Not a bad lecturer, but I hated the class and the content; total waste of time when we can look up vim and Unix commands in < 1 second.
Going to class isn't at all required to do well. MEMORIZE the lecture slides, go to labs, and do the hw -> ezy A

Teaches with good intentions to cover a lot of topics and debuggers. A lot of content that can easily fly over your heads. The lectures aren't mandatory, but understand the slides for the labs (which are mandatory). Be prepared for the scripting project - hardest part of the course. Get decent on the midterm/final and you'll be fine.

Professor "M" for magnificent :o, is the best Math professor ever! He is caring, professional and very dedicated to the success of his students. His exams are fair and his lectures are well structured and easy to follow. I would take his class again if I could! Do not choose easy, choose GOOD! Fall in love with Math!Take him! You will learn!:)

Archie is an incredible teacher. If you work hard and show up to class he will find ways for you to succeed. That being said he wants you to get to a certain level of understanding but he will help you along the way and develop your mathematical skills significantly. Archie was my inspiration to become a math minor. Take his Class!!

Midterms are doable/ easy. Final is a lot harder compared to midterms. Amount of homework assigned isn't too bad . Love his hats and how consistent his outfits are. Does plenty of examples in lecture.

He's a good professor but he lets students talk over him during lecture which is distracting. His lectures aren't the clearest so make sure you do the homework and study for tests. Ask for clarification if you don't understand something, he is really helpful, but will assume you know what he's talking about if you don't speak up!
The Final was challenging but nothing impossible. Great professor to talk to outside of class. Make sure you do homework and really learn the material.

I would take this professor again if I ever get the chance. Class was incredibly interesting especially considering its a movie genre (cyberpunk) I never thought I would discover or enjoy on my own. The attendance was mandatory but I wanted to go to class anyways is was that good.

Very passionate about the subject matter. Go to class to understand the art because you will be writing about it in your assignments. Trigilio takes attendance and sometimes has pop quizzes, so be careful about that. In the discussions, you learn writing principles. Textbook is not used, and other reading is online.

He is very passionate about the lecture, and not a lot reading required for his class. However, his essay topics were kinda absurd and hard to write about. I liked his creativity, but I just don't think these topics would help me in writing, as well as getting a good grade. The class has podcast, but we got easy pop quiz sometimes during lecture.

Class material was interesting, more focused on art. Interesting lectures, but I mostly skipped, careful though he does random lecture participation quizzes. He can be a bit pretentious, but a plus is you don't have to buy books for this class, all online! Overall glad I took him over other Cat 2 classes and I liked my TA a lot so it was fine!

Very funny and cool professor! This class is much more rigorous than I expected - it involves understanding both the technical aspects of and the concepts behind filmmaking. The midterm and final consist of a take-home essay and a video. His lectures are very helpful for the essays so take lots of notes. Put in the work and you'll do fine.

I was in her group discussion course rgding baboon social, hierarchy, dominance, etc. One rqmt was a 24 hr total, not consecutive, viewing of an animal of your choice at SD zoo. Class discussions very interesting and active. The zoo rqmt was worth every min. BTW, this was in 1976 or 77. She made Anthro memorable & real, even years later. Thank U.

Awful. She is super unorganized. Rambles about pointless things that aren't on the test or on the slides she's presenting. Wastes teaching time and says PRIMACK (the book) explains it better and in detail. So read the book in detail if you want to pass the tests. Research paper big portion of grade. This professor is pretentious, NOT recommended.

Really loved the class but the grades just killed my feelings towards it. Interesting lectures but terribly made exams. The exams are so specific about the answers. It's like asking you to describe an elephant but giving you 1/4 points just because you didn't mention what the tusks are made out of. Exaggerated but similar idea. D class average.

Honestly, one of the worst professors that I have ever had. She is incredibly unclear, her slides are pointless and the tests go in more depth than was ever addressed. I would suggest never ever taking this course and professor if at all possible.

Seems like a nice lady, but not a good lecturer. Came off as very pretentious. Lecture slides were not great--have to go to class to get details, and lectures are not podcasted. Exams were more difficult than expected.

she is a great professor; very kind, offers extra help when needed, tries her best to make sure the students understand everything, and takes us on field trips. She is not the best lecturer and it is easy to lose focus since she just kind of reads the powerpoint. The class is very doable as long as you make an effort to understand the information.
