Prof. Streeby is super nice and her class was very easy. I hardly read any of the required texts and still got an A. As long as you show up to lectures and show involvement with your TA you'll do fine.

gives very tedious work. Paper every week. Although Friday's lecture is not required, a movie and a response is required. Lecture is boring and everyone is on their phone. Attendance taken every lecture. The prompts she gives are very complicated that requires a lot of reading
There's one midterm essay, a group final project, an individual final project, and a final essay so it's a lot of work. Not super hard though and she offers 4% of extra credit

Streeby is a very sweet person, and she was extremely passionate about the topics of her lectures (superheros, AIs, and more!). She strongly encouraged lecture participation, although it was not required. She occasionally gave out prizes, like comic books, as incentives. There were, however, lectures that were boring.

She gives lots of speculations, plus a midterm and a final paper, which are really time consuming and boring. Lectures are far too boring and long to listen, but you have to attend for the in class writing assignments. She sure is a good person but not a good professor. Try to avoid her.

Carly is a young professor and so she may not have much experience but her exams are extremely fair as they are basically her powerpoint slides. Discussions are mandatory and more difficult than exams. Also she doesn't utilize any Sapling in her teachings so homework may be difficult. Show up to the lecture so she doesn't get lonely!

Chem 7L lab is dependent on your TA for they grade your lab reports. Lab reports are already formatted and just need to be filled in. Material for the lab report and experiments are all covered in the lectures. Carly is extremely thorough in her lectures and practice problems are just like the final. TA's will determine your grade though.

Carly is a fairly recent professor here at UCSD but she's an awesome professor! Her lectures are 100% like the material on the exam and she gives zero curve balls. Her lecture slides are well thought out, concise, and clear! Her exams are similar to the practice/learning objectives/lecture slides. Take her! And show up to lecture :)

I never went to lecture and just watched her podcasts, but she does explain a lot of the material you need to know. I mostly relied on my TA to help me with extra questions I had. The grading for the lab reports are straightforward and easy to follow.
Very straightforward in her expectations for the course and always explained the lab manuals/calculations for lab reports well. Her final was very straightforward and her grading system is very fair.

Dr. Fletcher was an amazing professor, she explains topics in lots of detail and is open to help everyone. There is reading circle group work and some independent work but the class overall wasn't too difficult and was really interactive. I learned a lot of interesting material & didn't think I would enjoy learning about illusions as much as I did!
Class is understanding & work based, no trick questions, if you know ur stuff & just put in effort into research or study, you'll get an A

Not a too difficult, but way too much work for only 4 units. There are group projects analyzing psychology illusion papers, mandatory in-class assignments, a "final" free response exam, and a poster that had to be made making up our own experiment with an illusion. Material is pretty light and interesting, but I wish to have known more.
You're only required to do your assignments to pass! No midterm or final exams. Easy A, definitely recommend!

the worst professor i have ever taken. I am normally a decent student,but this professor was extremely horrible and I nearly failed this class. no notes online, and notes in class don't make any sense. professor has thick accent, and TAs do too. he wasn't bad for lack of trying, just completely incompetent- ie he forgot his notes one lecture.

Professor Wang's lectures focus on logic behind theorems rather than examples, which help me understand how they work. However, his accent makes the lecture a bit hard to understand. Also the homework can be hard sometimes(but useful). The difficulty of tests depend on individual If you are able to do all the homework on your own, you will be fine.

Lectures are terrible and flies through the material. Exams are not representative of the practice exams or the homework and are nearly impossible. Only good thing is that he will give a generous grade curve depending on the class.

Professor Wang is actually very nice and accommodating to his students. His test can be hard but theres generous grading with lots of partial points. You will have to go back and read some parts of the textbook after lectures since the material gets difficult quickly. Puts out old midterms w/ answers for practice & new practice midterm to help.

By far the worst professor I've had for any class. He intentionally made the tests impossible. He gave you the previous quarter's tests to practice but then made your test a hundred times harder for that reason. He is delusional, and thinks his tests are easy, as if everyone in the class has a degree in mathematics.

Definitely comes off as someone who cares about his students but when you approach him, it's obvious that he really could care less. I emailed him many times and never once did not answer to my emails especially towards the end of the summer session. His quizzes are easy, and readings are fun but midterm and final are totally different from quizzes

Honestly, a swell orator, who makes psychology more interesting & interactive. His midterm was intense, & the final will probably be more difficult. Then again its summer, so personally, Id avoid him for a 5-week session. Readings are simple, and homework/quizzes are straightforward and short. Nice, considerate and outgoing guy for a PhD student.

This professor gives you everything you need to get an A in this class. His lectures are really thorough. He also posts detailed lecture notes right after class. The lecture notes and the problem sets were especially helpful when studying for both the midterm and the final. All in all I would recommend this professor to anyone taking an Econ class
read everything and you will get a good grade
Great teacher and his class is really easy. His tests are very straightforward and the study guide is helpful. His lectures are interesting but clicker attendance is required.

Best prof ever had at UCSD. Really care about students and he is not a tough grader at all. Actually he encourages students to ask for more points in hw and exams and would usually give you more if you ask him to.

He may not be a good lecturer, but he really cares about his students. For instance, he would require those who didn't do well in the quiz to attend his office hours and made sure if they understood the concepts.
Nice guy, but not a good lecturer.

Although he has a really bad ascent, he is a great professor. He'll ask the class if they understood the topic, and if no one answers, he'll go over it again! The material is pretty tough, so just go to his office hours. Exams are average and he wants you to fight for your points. I would recommend him.
Very intimidating professor.. he likes to yell at his students. Once you get past the accent and his unrealistically high expectations, he really is a genuinely nice guy. The class is ALOT of work.
Just terrible. The more I go to class, the more frustrated I get.

All over the place, comes late to class and then asks students to stay late. Assigns huge amount of graded homework. Not a clear lexturer. Spent the class teaching myself, as it was hard to grasp anything from lecture.

I used his clicker questions and assigned Canvas problems to study which helped me do well on the weekly quizzes. It's clear to see that he wants every student to perform well and his office hours are always helpful. He curves nicely (63% as a B-) and his lectures are always to the point. The final is similar to quizzes. I hope he teaches 6C!
This class is full of memorization so if you love to memorize, you'll do great. If memorization isn't your thing, you will not like this class.

This class is difficult and Dr. Bennett definitely talks very fast. There are easier professors to take this class with but if you want to learn the material take this class with Dr. Bennett. I can't recommend his lectures enough. He offers a modest amount of extra credit, which helps since his exams are difficult. TAKE THIS CLASS!

I recommend going over the slides before each lecture because there is A LOT of material and Dr. Bennett talks fast. He is super helpful both in class and office hours. What worked for me was engaging with the material (questions and mind maps) before exams. You'll have to put all the pieces together at the end. Very rewarding learning experience!

This is one of the most interesting classes I've taken at UCSD but if you don't like memorizing cellular pathways, I would not recommend this class. While sometimes his sensitivity about the topic is well that of a researcher not a clinician, he provides clear explanation for a mind glowingly complex topic.

I enjoyed the class but be warned BIMM 134 is a GPA killer. Unfortunately the previous CAPE distributions weren't released when I took his course bc I would've only taken it PNP. He's a good lecturer but speaks really quickly which can make it hard to follow the dense material. Otherwise, he's generally friendly and very knowledgable. Good luck!

I went about 1/2 the time and got pics of notes for the times I missed from others in my section. She doesn't like phones/laptops. She didn't post lecture slides until the last few lectures after I asked her. The DI section is mandatory. The final was easy b/c she was clear on what to expect and quizzes were online. Overall, the easiest GE.
Quizzes are doable if you attend the class, and final exam is not easy. Overall, this class is ok for GE.
Terrible

strict no electronics policy; doesn't post lecture slides (likely because she doesn't want people to not attend her 3 hour lectures). I enrolled after the first lecture and when I asked what my options were to obtain the material I missed her attitude was "too bad." Poor lecturer; rattles off lots of information without much purpose
never take this prof's class. never

The way he speaks is way too slow. Hard to catch up on him because he just talk too slow in lectures. The readings are not very relevant to his lecture, but you need to read. He gives you the exact test question a week before, so you can prepare for it.
Amazing professor. Best professor I have had for math at UCSD. You do not need the textbook. Just study his lecture notes and you'll easily be fine for math 109.

Good professor that tries to help his students, but tests were hard. I also think it depends on who your TA is since they're the ones who do the grading and some grade harsher than others. It would help if Pelayo were to provide a study guide for his exams.

Professor Pelayo is amazing :) ! He explains everything clearly and he really cares about the students' learning, he always stops and asks whether we understood everything he just talks about. He expects us to understand the concepts thoroughly, which means the tests can be a little bit hard. So just go to the lectures and review the notes!
tests have almost nothing to do with the homework, take another professor

Very detailed and clear in explaining concepts. Very patient. Exams are not too hard. Some questions come from examples he taught in the class. Going to class is necessary because he is an excellent professor.

Dr. Winward is always prepared for class and really enthusiastic about lecture. She gives us all the tools we need to succeed and learn behavioral psychology concepts. She gives plenty of examples for each term/concept and that is very helpful when studying.
Very knowledgeable about the material. She has a very clear voice.

She is such an amazing mentor and instructor. She is so easily approachable and she has so many useful tips for students who are planning to continue to graduate school. I felt that I was actually being prepared for the real world instead of learning things that I will never use later.

Dr. Winward is probably one of the best professor there is at explaining the material. She goes out of her way to have office hours right outside the lecture hall so we don't have to go far to ask her questions. She does a phenomenal job in explaining all the topics and key terms.

One of the best lecturers I have had at UCSD. Her greatest strength is coming up with examples on concepts that most can identify with. She uses real and common scenarios to help explain difficult concepts. She's also funny and eager to address student's concerns and or questions.

Cohen was awesome. He and DuBois are the chillest MMW profs there are. I didn't do the readings, but went to lecture and took detailed notes - he mentions and covers the readings in lecture. He gives study guides to his exams which, if you do, you'll get an A. As for the essay part of the class, honestly depends on your TA.
Cohen is a cool and fun guy but I found his lecture kinda boring and monotone. He wasn't an amazing lecturer but his tests were straightforward and easy.
I heard that he is leaving UCSD, don't know why. Took his MMW 12, now that I'm taking MMW13, through comparison I feel like he is sooo good.... SAD

Cohen's a really great dude. His lectures were much more interesting than the ones I encountered in MMW 11, and his midterm was incredibly easy. You have to attend lecture to understand the concepts and there's a lot of reading, but in lecture he goes over the most important aspects of the reading, so you really don't have to do it.
His tests are super easy and his TA's are easy essay graders. He brought a puppet to lecture; he's great. Definitely take this man

Tom is an amazing lecturer who really cares about his students. I'd never taken a coding class before, but was able to earn an A+. The PAs are still challenging and require that you put in the work, but he and the TAs are eager to help via OH, coding labs, & email. Class is podcasted, but you have to attend enough to click in for 10% participation.

Amazing professor. He's a PhD student and made the whole Introduction to Python course. Class consisted of Coding labs (did not need to finish them, just show up and work on them), Coding Assignments (got lots of help at Office Hours), Clickers (had the option to opt out), A midterm (just like the study guide), and a final project. great class! 5/5

For my first quarter at UCSD, she made it far less scary. She posts a notes outline for you to follow along with during lecture, so I highly recommend printing the notes or bringing an iPad/touchscreen laptop to class with stylus. Her class is easy as long as you do the homewok (Sapling). Her class is the reason I decided to major in chemistry!

Take this professor if you want to understand ochem AND get a decent grade. Her lectures are entertaining and very organized, and on top of that she provides fill in the blank notes that are a life saver. Her practice problems are very reminiscent to the exams, although the actual tests may have some short answer problems. Cannot recommend enough!

She was extremely helpful, organize, and clear with everything she did. Lectures are amazing and not boring at all. You learn new things every day with many practice problems during lectures. Homework is extremely clear and straightforward. Lectures and homework correlate with each other. She is super caring and understanding

Sonia works hard in order for her students to succeed and it shows in the assignments/practice problems she puts out for us. Although she is a fast lecturer, she provided us with outlines that we could print/fill out while she lectures, which are organized and very helpful when studying for exams. Practice problems are reflective of exam material.

Sonia is one of the best professors Ive ever had especially in a stem class. She is super nice and approachable and willing to help. Unlike most ochem profs she makes the challenge seem less frightening. Her notes are insanely helpful and organized. Her lectures are so easy to follow and she does so many practice problems in class its so helpful.

Her class is interesting. I certainly learned about punk culture. Her final is based on memorizing what each song sounds like (100+ songs), and I am not musically gifted. I still did well in this class because I put a lot of effort into the 6-page music essay at the end of the quarter. She gives us breaks during (3-hr) lectures and finishes early.

So I took Professor Hochman thinking this class was going to be my fun class which I could actually enjoy a topic (since I am taking all science courses). I WAS DEFINITELY WRONG. While this class is fun if you are just doing pass no pass DO NOT TAKE PROF HOCHMAN FOR A GRADE!!! I just took her final and it was so much harder than expected!!!!!

The class is super lecture heavy, and they're a bit boring. The reading is extensive, but you can honestly get by with just skimming it. Keep up with the weekly listenings, and you will be fine - make an updated excel sheet with the artist, title, genre, etc and you will be ready for midterm. Take advantage of the extra credit.

This class was originally thought to be a GE grade booster, but I had so many tasks to the point that I had to push back a lot of my major course assignments. Though the professor wanted to make an informal class, it becomes alittle excessive when the final expects you to know over 100+ songs, alongside the background behind each song

I am computer science major and I am taking this class as GE requirement. Thanks to this class' crazy essay assignments, I am having hard time working on my major class study. Be ready to write bunch of essay. Currently I am writing 6 page Music essay. It could be much better if it was 3 page essay. And be ready to read and listen. They are crazy.

It takes you about a week to get used to his accent (don't panic!) In his first lecture he will try to intimidate you into dropping the class but after that the lectures are easy (but he is not good at teaching). Just do all the homework and teach yourself using the textbook you have to buy and you'll be fine.
The course itself wasn't too difficult, but his writing and accent makes it harder to understand the material. Homework graded on correctness and the exam questions were worth a LOT.
clear lectures, prof methods are easier to understand than the book, however there is no podcast or lecture notes, its only blackboard. midterm and final straightforward

Honestly the course material isnt that difficult, but he grades homework on correctness and is a tough exam grader. Missing any part of a question leads to a 25 percent point deduction for the problem, meaning it is almost impossible to get by on partial credit.

O'Brien is a really cool prof. He is obviously very knowledgable about the texts and is passionate in his lectures. He certainly does not hold back either, which can be rather amusing. But he does not use slides or anything, so you have to take good notes during lecture. Overall interesting and not difficult in terms of essays and final.

He's quite the character. Always somehow makes dry texts interesting with funny commentaries. The prompts are straightforward but the final was a little tricky. Again, like with other HUM classes your TA determines your grade so go to their OH if you can, but don't be afraid to contact him as well!

He's hilarious and his lectures are really interesting. His essay prompts were very straightforward and easy to interpret, but the ones on the final exam were a bit confusing. If you pay attention in lectures and discussion, you should be good. He's really sweet and one of the best professors I've had at UCSD! Take him!

O'Brien is able to come across as a pretentious germanophile and a rebellious, anti-hierarchical-academic outsider at the same time. At first this is amusing: his lectures are closer to rants about a world external to the classroom that he no longer understands, and are filled with admonitions about pursuing a career in academia. You don't need to show up to lectures, but they are entertaining nonetheless. But then, you quickly learn how stringent he is on papers. His blanket assumptions about what good writing is (Try telling David Foster Wallace a paragraph can't be a page long). And should he disagree with your argument, expect a C. My best advice if you're already enrolled in this is class is to visit him during office hours to get a gauge on what he wants, because the criteria is often arbitrary.

Prof. O'Brien is hilarious as a professor, but he isn't as good as Lyon or Lee. Using our Humanities "Compare and Contrast", I would say that O'Brien's class pacing accounts for this quality difference. Whereas Lee finishes texts, O'Brien tends to only cover 20-35 pages of a text each week and then moves on. So, most of the reading is for you only.
Easy class. Make a game, play other people's games, have fun, say nonsense with strong feelings, write one paper.
Pros: extra credits, interesting topic, enthusiastic, one paper only Cons: pop attendance

She is horrible and treats the students like little kids by the way she talks and gets their attention. Unreasonable as you are not allowed to use electronics or it will count as an absence and 3 absences equal an automatic fail in the class. She even tells people who missed missed 3+ classes to drop the class. Assignments are fine, depends on ta.

BEST. CAT CLASS. EVER. Hands down. No essays in the traditional sense. Class is based on videos; main project is to make a short film (3-7 mins, though my group went over to 9min) with group which was very fun. Topic of vid was about design fiction of world 100yrs from now. Only essays are just reflection paper on the video. Highly recommend!
Really did not like her class. It was a lot of work for a writing class and made no sense to me. Her lectures were not engaging and were all over the place. Really glad to finally be done with her

The lectures are literally a quiz and then you leave. There are 12 quizzes so you can stop coming after that. You read the book for the quizzes, but if you ask, Gibson will just give u answers. You do need the book for the homework and lab quizzes (which were so annoying) but Gibson was very kind and I enjoyed his class.

MAE5 by Professor Gibson is one of the easiest classes I've ever taken. As long as you go to every lecture and lab and do the work, you'll get an A. He gives a quiz every lecture but the previous versions of similar quizzes are all given online.
Turbulence

Honestly, this class is easy but the biggest pain!! He never once lectured, you have quizzes that you take every day. You can either do the readings and be prepared for the quizzes or you can just ask him to show you an example during the quiz and he will basically give you the answers. The projects are definitely doable but all on your own!

If you read the syllabus you can stop attending class by like week 7 and still get an A.  He gives you the answers to in class quizzes as long as you ask (he'll encourage you to), and the top 2 (out of 4) lab quizzes are taken (meaning you can stop going to lab since the first 2 quizzes are pretty easy). Homework gets tough though.

Many readings and some long with difficult content. She does an amazing job explaining, historicizing, and contextualizing the readings. Most lectures include some helpful and relevant videos or films. Manageable class, but she does expect you to have a really good understanding of the material and deeply analyze the texts for the mid + final paper
She's a great professor. She was very good at dissecting and explaining difficult texts in the class and answered questions in a helpful way.
Very easy. No tests. Section is mandatory. So stuck-up though.

Amazing professor! She makes class interesting and has so much knowledge on the subject. Class was very fair, and reading was manageable. Consists of a reflection paper due each week (1 page double spaced -7 total), a midterm paper (5 pages) and final paper (6 pages). Great class and the TA Sal made it even better!  Definitely recommend it!

She is amazing! She doesn't need to look at her notes even though she packs so much information in her lectures and encourages students give their opinions. She is extremely knowledgeable and has a sense of humor, and made me want to take more of her ETHN classes! Also, she invited many relevant guest speakers that really opened my eyes.

Super tough class; its basically an entire quarter of memorization; except the exams are memorization and application so much of the learning occurs beyond the classroom. There are assigned readings that aren't graded but you should do if you want to pass the class. Alot of difficult content he expects you to know, but good lecturer; chill dude.
He is such an amazing professor and he is very good at teaching in a way that you enjoy learning in his class.

Great prof, really knows how to teach at a begginers level and in an interesting way. Tests are sometimes kinda weird but not too bad. I personally struggled at remembering to do the online hw and quizes but they're easy otherwise.

There are clickers and online homework/quizzes. Lectures are long + detailed. Bring a laptop bc you won't be able to keep up by writing. Reading is a must. Exams are MC and FR, are based on ability to regurgitate information and also understanding the material conceptually. He curves based on avg of  top 10 students  100%. Hard class bc detailed Q

I find him just ok. He wrote our textbook, but the lectures weren't that great. He teaches and holds office hours, but he tends to talk a lot about irrelevant stuff probably because he has gone over his own book too many times. Tests consist of MC and free response. He likes to make you think, so don't expect memorizing would work.

Good professor. Tons of reading, but what he assigns is actually interesting. Attendance is mandatory, but classes are mostly spent discussing the readings, so make sure you get them done. Grade is based only on 2 tests, but he also gave 1 extra-credit assignment and curved a LOT. His TA Ben Merrill is really sweet and understand, loved him!

Professor Csordas is one of the most unique professors, I've been fortunate enough to meet. I was impressed by his research and past educational career. During class, I was frequently engaged and the readings were super interesting. You won't find another class like this at UCSD. Make sure to show up even if you don't finish the reading.

He is a facilitator for the small seminar-style capstone for Global Health. He's kind of quirky and follows the mold of an absent-minded professor sometimes (b/c he's so busy!) He's still very knowledgeable but is not super approachable.

Professor Csordas is one of the brightest anthropologists out there today and this class is one of the most interesting you will ever find. It's not for everyone, and you must read the material, but if you do, the payoff is great. We were graded on two take-home essays of 8-10 pages. If you come to class and do the reading, you will do fine.

Good professor. His practice midterm/final really help in studying for his exams. If you study an hour or two every week outside of lecture, you should be set for an A. Readings aren't required but you need the textbook for Connect hw, which is ANNOYING, but it keeps you from falling behind, and it's a nice grade boost worth 20% of your grade.

It's really hard to follow along in lecture in this class and we moved too quickly. We never stopped to make sure everyone actually understood the material, so I feel like I just forgot everything once the course was over because I just learned how to compute things for the sake of problem solving, which isn't the right way to learn accounting.

Felt like a writing class. Power-points were unorganized and hard to take notes on. Asking questions can irritate him and he will respond sarcastically to make you look like a clown. Not a bad guy and he knows what hes teaching.

Really enjoyed the content of this class. Professor Kim was very open to students feedback and asked for some after midterm 1 via google form. Offered extra credit but barely anyone took advantage of it. I didn't have any linguistic background and still got an A in her class. Read the textbook, know what's on her study guide, and you will do great

I found this class and the material really interesting. Dr. Kim has high expectations for her students which I appreciate. Be aware that she has a thick accent and does not podcast. A background in Linguistics (LIGN 101) is definitely recommended. Don't do homework last minute and STUDY a lot for the midterms. Textbook is needed for quizzes.

Grade on attendance, quizzes, midterm, final. Very standard COGS class, the material she covers is 1:1 to the textbook. Midterm was the most difficult, with multiple, fill-in, and paragraph. A lot of vocab. As a lecturer, she's a bit monotone. Class didn't take too much time, great for setting up 14B, but wasn't memorable either.

Really a good guy. Maybe the kindest professor I meet in my life. I am a Chinese student and maybe the course is a little bit easy for me, but the professor provides lots of chances to give us bonus, and grading is really kind. He is humorous, too, every class will start with a cartoon story. He is little bit busy, but always takes classed himself

Friend is a great professor who cares for his students. His lectures are videocasted, which means you have the option not to attend every class. The only thing I dislike about the class is that we have to learn Mathematica for the homeworks. To succeed in dynamics, remember this: find the position vector and you are gold.
A friendly professor who cares about students, teaching important course with unique but effective method.
worst. don't
dont

Just dont. The professor is awful. Uses the classroom as a platform to spew nonsense in an authoritarian manner. She knows her lectures contribute absolutely nothing to the class so she makes you do pointless thumbnail drawings on every slide she puts up. Nothing in this class is clear. Grading makes no sense at all, especially participation.

This professor is incredibly unprofessional, messy, and childish. She gets upset when students leave lecture and changes grading dates to fit her agenda. Her lectures are really long and she chooses to grade in a biased way that favors certain art styles. Not a good representation of what makes an art teacher great. Terrible

Would rate 0 for this professor. Does not deserve to be an art professor: not clear grading rubric; required to draw thumbnail for every page of powerpoint during lecture (more than 100 pgs each week!), and not posting grade util the dropping deadline. It is week 7 and her syllabus was not even filled.

New lecturer, so he's still rough around the corners. His lectures are very theory based, and so are his tests. However, he is good at taking advice and seems to be adapting his teaching style to his students as he teaches more, and he is caring towards his students.

The class itself is hard, but he makes it easier to understand. He does write really fast though, so be ready to write fast! If you talk to him outside of class, you can tell that he really cares about if you understand the material and is willing to explain things thoroughly. It's a shame that this was his last quarter teaching at UCSD :(

Don't be daunted by all the bad ratings, he's a solid choice for MATH 11. He podcasts everything and section is optional. Just make sure you turn in the pen and paper homework and online labs on time. He's reasonable, straightforward, and a great lecturer. He does have a thick accent but that hasn't prevented me from understanding him.

I can list a tons of reasons why he's amazing: podcast available so basically do not need to show up to class, no attendance, cheat sheet, best hand writing eva, explain concepts nice and clearly, post hw/sample exam solutions, <10 hw questions per week, fairly easy exam

Great professor, really fair. The material is somewhat difficult and unintuitive at times but Reza does a great job of teaching it. Pleasant professor explains thoroughly. This class is not a cakewalk but if you are understanding the homework and doing extra problems then it is possible to get a good grade

Skips class more often than I do, has substitute teachers give the lectures. Notifies us of midterms last minute; the only redeeming qualities about this class was that the substitute teachers were often better at explaining than he was

went to every discussion and lecture and still manage not to do well, I have to beg the TA and go nonstop preparing 4 days for the final, this suppose to be just GE for warren college and how is it so difficult to get a decent grade aboVE B- ???? PHIL 27 was so much better with other professor, AVOID AT ALL COST, PITY YURSELF

When the quarter started, I though he has spent too much time yelling why abortion is a basic right. After seeing Alabama's anti-abortion law, I wish everybody can listen to him yelling. Not only because the wrongfulness of the law, but people should see how men are also actively defending the rights.

Professor means well, and "individually", his class is fair and reasonable. In comparison to other professors, this class is unfair: Insane amount of reading compared to other professors, just to get a B (where others are "easy A"). TAs look for specific words and tough graders, and structure is confusing.  No clear regrade policy if you disagree.

I like Doppelt as a person. I really do. But I strongly disagree with his teaching style. Have to buy the $70 reader off campus when other profs would provide pdfs. His midterm and final are very nit-picky, and demand very detailed answers. Takes attendance. Discussions have quizzes. Appealing answers is near impossible. His lectures are okay.

You will have three papers, one due each month. Prompts are clear and "very" specific which is helpful. If you attend class, you can essentially write your entire essay based on your notes. Don't be intimidated, it is a great class with a great professor. Work hard and you will do well.

HORRIBLE. I cannot believe this Professor is allowed to teach at such high ranking school. He is extremely strict with no merit, condescending, and does not treat his students as if they are actual human beings. He will revert your entire course grade to an F even if you have 100% if you fail to complete any assignment no matter how small. AVOID.

Professor Shugart is absolutely amazing. You would be hard pressed to find a better professor in the Poli Sci Department. If you are in class and do most of the reading it would be very hard to do poorly in any of his classes.  He is a MUST take Professor if you even slightly interested in Comparative Politics.
hard to enjoy the class
I like him

Cold-calling is not as bad as the other reviewers have made it out to be. Just do the readings and you'll be fine. If you stumble trying to answer, he usually tries to guide you. Really knows his stuff, very clear in class. However outside of class it's difficult to get help from him and his grading policy is not clear. He's a little awkward.
Highly recommend for first step into machine learning.
I recommend the professor.
Disorganized, with too many channels to publish the same information

We got hands on experience on different Machine Learning and NLP algorithms through assignments and group projects. He encourages the students to try different approaches and provided feedback for the projects.

Dr. Arsanjani covered all machine learning techniques with natural language processing and introduction to deep learning very well. The course content included tackling real life business scenarios. Class lectures were less focused on math disciplines that make up machine learning

All of her slides provide the information that is necessary for understanding what is going on. They are very detailed and accessible on TED. I just wished she taught the whole class for 138 instead of splitting it into 3 professors.

He is 1/3 professors who teach 138. Most of his slides are just pictures which is really hard when you have to look back and review the notes for the midterm. His teaching style just didn't really help, he would only put a few things on the board that did not coincide with the slides.

Professor Litman has a distinguished resume, but does not care for the students. Only an in-class written midterm, in-class written final, and an online case brief. Everyone in our class failed the midterm - failed, with an F.

Makes mistake here and there up to the point that I don't even know what I am learning anymore. Also, the test is more complicated then it needs to be even though the class is already hard itself. Plus, he sometimes curves down the scale which doesn't make sense at all

Honestly an easy class. Calculus is fairly simple enough to begin with already, so I liked how the professor tried to explain the concepts on top of doing examples in class. Solid choice in my opinion. I know a majority of the class would disagree, but if you have a good understanding of maths, you'll develop well in his class.

Ed really tries his best and I appreciated it. I prefer step-by-step lessons instead of a complex explanation of the topic so I struggled a lot in his class. His study guides are pretty similar to his midterms, but I still had to learn from the SI.

Caring and a cool guy, but he doesn't know what he's doing as a prof just yet. Confusing lectures, waaay too much online homework, never told us what would be on exams. Discussion was the only place that helped me. I failed every exam but the fat curve brought me up to an A every time, so I feel like I passed without learning anything. :/

I went to lecture maybe 7 times max? This prof wasnt too bad, he really tries to teach the concepts instead of step by step. A lot of it was self studying the HW, class didnt help much, he explains things a lot more difficult bc he has a lot of math knowledge. Prepping for exams was hard bc no practice exam + barely a guide. Prepare to go to SI

Professor Shaheen is very kind and very passionate about the conservation about the environment but she has a thick Indian accent which made it hard to concentrate in class and grasp all of the content.

The material is easy to understand, but she was a bit unorganized and that threw off everyone during lecture. The homework assignments are group work so that can be annoying. She genuinely cares about her students and wants everyone to pass.

A very nice and caring woman. She is clearly very smart and knows her stuff, however her English skills are lacking. It is often difficult to decipher what she is saying. She has a very thick accent and often her sentences don't make much sense or are hard to follow. Her tests and grading scale are easy, but you'll have to work if you wanna learn.

Dr. Shaheen is the best professor at the UCSD. It was her first time teaching ENVR30 but she is very caring and really accommodates to the students' needs. I would recommend taking her for ENVR30. She really makes the class as easy as possible.

She was literally the worst professor Ive ever had at UCSD. She gave us the rubrics a day before the labs were due. No one had any idea what was going on in lecture. She threatened to give us clicker quizzes. When she did, she gave questions completely unrelated to the lab material. She asked us what angle a sunray hits a raindrop to form a rainbow
extremely disorganized
Great capstone class and awesome interaction with professional engineers who provided us with great mentoring
Although his class is tough you WILL learn about reinforced concrete. All the theory that he taught I was able to apply out in the industry.
The way he teaches is just bad. You will not learn anything about reinforced concrete from him. Worst SE Professor in UCSD.

he has an accent and sometimes cracks jokes and dances. kinda cute and funny~ used text for 2 hw assignments(w/in first 3ish weeks of quarter) and never touched again. interesting class.. but he couldve done a better job of teaching statics and torque better... but the labs for se1 were interesting :)

It's WCWP 10A, so it is already a drag. But if you get her, RIP. She gives probably the worst advice I have ever gotten on essays, so incredibly vague it is worthless. The 15 of us would actually talk bad about her every day before she showed up, and it was all of us. I didn't even know 2 of my classmates spoke English until they chimed in. Ouch.
Take her class as letter grade, fat curve in the beginning, fat curve in the end. More than half the class got A's

Okay, so her lectures are about 100 slides per class and she tends to drone on for the entire duration until there is a confusing clicker question, but I found getting an A pretty attainable. Go to lecture(mandatory), discussion(mandatory), take your online quizzes, and READ THE SLIDES ON YOUR OWN. Byrne is not very reliable, but there is hope.

She is probably the worst professor at UCSD. She is not clear on what will be on tests. Literally reads off her slides does not elaborate. You literally could do the same in your dorm but she makes attendance mandatory by using iclickers. There were multiple times where all answers on questions were right but A was just a little more right to her

If you have taken Biology in highschool, then this class will be a GPA booster. However, I don't recommend this professor since she only reads her powerpoint slides that essentially sums up the textbook. Attending lectures are unnecessary, but she has iclicker. Her exams are mainly factual recall.

Pretty fair when it comes to grading lab reports, however I wish that her quizzes were easier considering the typos and errors in her keys. Thankfully, her slides are well-detailed enough to understand the labs as the lab manual was not edited very well. Final was a bit tricky as she does like to give some trick questions. Not bad, but not good.

Xuidi is overall a very good lecturer and he has a passion for math that is admirable. He makes great use of lecture time and goes over useful examples. He was also very accessible outside of class and I learned a lot from him during his office hours. I wish he was a bit more engaging in class though, other than that, Xuidi is a great prof!

Well-prepared for lecture. Explanations  in-depth > text, helps get the content. Accent isn't too thick. If almost done with lecture but down to the last minute or two, he'll hurry to beat the clock. Open to questions outside OH. As a slower learner, he sometimes doesn't know where my confusion is, but I'm a harder case to deal with too xD.
Well organized, clear lectures. Homework level was manageable. Good prof overall.

Xiudi is a super responsible instructor. He is always well-prepared for discussion and care about students a lot. Also, he is knowledgable and provide effective hints on difficult questions which are helpful to better understand the course material.

Xiudi is a great director, his way of teaching stimulate self-study and encourage group discussion after his class. I went to his office hour several times and each time I got decent suggestions for studying multivariable calculus. WILL DEFINITELY TAKE HIM AGAIN if he still is able to teach. Easy A+

Fantastic professor! Dr. Welji is extremely accessible outside of class and gives great help in office hours and individual conferences. She gives clear feedback on essay drafts and is very committed to helping students improve their writing. Class discussions were always interesting and it is clear she cares about her students and the course.

Really nice professor but her expectations are wayyy to obscure. Really fun discussions but assignments have no rubric. I feel like if she likes you you'll get an A, if not, then tough luck no matter how hard you work.
I loved her i think she really cares about her students

Good teacher but has very unclear expectations. She also has a tendency to net pick things she recommended you to do. Very confusing. She does, however, care for your understanding and holds very interesting discussions. Make sure you visit office hours often.

Awesome lecturer! Haleema really loves teaching and you can see that in the classroom. Her class required online quizzes to make sure you're doing the readings and 3 short essays. Her lectures kept you engaged throughout the class. She seems to really care about her students and was always asking for our responses in class. Very interactive teacher

I loved Chris! His lectures are always intriguing and he makes a large lecture hall feel personal and fun. I am NOT a math person, so there were times when I was stressed out, but like another review said the homework was much harder than the exams so it ended up being fine. Since math is required, I would recommend taking Chris's class.

He goes by Chris which I thought was interesting since most people go by Professors or Dr., but he was really funny! Made lectures really engaging and fun to attend. The homework was pretty hard sometimes, but the problems and examples he did in class were reflective of the midterms

Awesome professor, while the homework is much more difficult than his lectures, the lectures are reflective of the exams. Speaking of lectures, theres never a dull moment! Would take his class again, if you show up and take good notes its easy to get a good grade.

The labs were a pain, and Chris's lectures were a bit on the disorganized side, yeah, but at least he would remember questions he couldn't answer the previous class and explain to us the next. I really appreciate his trying to make class funny. Open office hours even though it got crowded in the tiny office.

He's super unorganized during his lectures and most of his notes don't make sense. He can't explain statistics concepts at all and he gives midterms are totally different from the practice ones. However, his final wasn't too hard and that the only positive I can say about him
She teaches math like it should be taught. Amazing lectures and fantastic teacher!
She helped me understand math in a way I could never understand before. GREAT teacher!

She is the best professor I've ever had. She is brilliant and SUPER NICE. I loved her lectures. She knows how to make math easy. Her grading system is fair, and she is very welcoming during her office hours. She is the only reason that I don't hate math!
Professor Mirzaei is the best! She is brilliant, and makes sure everyone understands the course material well.

Absolutely loved her! Extremely nice and welcoming outside of class. Never makes you feel stupid when you don't understand something. Posts midterm and final practice exams and puts extra credit on the tests. There is weekly homework, but it is straight forward and is exactly what is taught in lectures. I will miss her :,)

I dont know if my comments will be helpful. But as a student, I have to share my experiences. If you want to have a good life and nice future, please skip this horrible guy. What should I say about him? I believe he will have his own payback one day. He doesnt deserve to be a professor. Dont know how to grade a student; dont participate

Grade consists of one take-home midterm and final. He lectures a lot but there is no clear outline and he does not post anything online. He gives extra tips/instructions during class for midterm and final, so try to attend. His lectures are quite interesting. The films were interesting as well, all dealing with the topic of madness/mental health.

This was not an actual teaching. Professor Scull  essentially summarizes the reading, so if you keep up with the terminology in the textbooks, you do not actually have to pay any attention whatsoever during class. No value is added by the professor.  Would have been better served with a decent lecture or discussion group.

Prepare to type your notes or write very fast, because he goes through events and details very quickly unless you ask him to write the names on the board. His lecturing style is like storytelling, so it can be hard to know what's important; they are usually details he repeats more than once. Grading is 50/50 midterm and final but he does 40/60 too.
Does not use TED or any lecture slides... based purely on what he says in class. Hard to understand at times and VERY disorganized.

She's disrespectful with her comments and how she treats people. She goes by books that are subjective that prove no point from her lectures. If you disagree with her, she will put you down in front of the whole class.

Professor Molina is amazing. This class was structures around Los Angeles when I took it but topics change every time she teaches this course. Assigns minimal reading because she actually wants you to finish the reading. 2 papers which are a combination of primary research and reading. If you read and participate you will pass.

She gets caught up in her agenda, which pretty much is evil white people ruin the wonderland known as Boyle Heights. She ignored the Film Industry, the Westside, the Valley an names like Huntington, Sherman, or Mulholland. But we did hear about how awful the East LA interchange and she didn't even mention the traffic. A disappointing class.

Literally the easiest class at UCSD. Lecture won't really help you with the class; all the information that you could need or want is contained in the reading. In addition, her lectures are not nearly as interesting as her book. She grades really easy. I stopped going to class after Wk 2 and wrote all my papers the night before and still got an A+!

I completely agree with the post below. I was really interested in the way that Los Angeles formed and how it grew to become such a large city and the urban planning of LA. We didn't talk about that whatsoever and instead focused on sociocultural issues of LA. Lecture is very boring and doesn't really matter. Required three 5-page papers.

One of my favourite professors. Kimmie loves teaching 331 and shows lots of movie clips to help you remember things. She makes class very enjoyable and is very upbeat and willing to help. Only negative is shes a slow grader. Would 100% take all of her classes if I could though.

This thing I like most about her is her enthusiasm- it's obvious she loves what she does and that energy definitely transfers to her students. Her lectures are super interesting. She's very clear and organized in her lectures, her tests are straightforward and 99.9% of it comes straight from her notes. Definitely definitely take her!

Kimmie is an awesome professor, she is extremely enthusiastic about psychology and it really shows. She is a very personable professor who loves feedback in class. Her lectures are never boring, she adds a lot of videos that are relevant, and her slides are easy to follow. Her tests are very easy, but there is no curve! RECOMMENDED.

While there are a lot of readings, in section each student is assigned a reading that they have to present on. I got most of my knowledge from these presentations, and they helped me understand the concepts much better than if I had just done readings. Lectures are also helpful, and Kozen is a very nice and understanding professor.
ETHN 20 with Kozen requires you to read A LOT, the lectures are pretty boring unfortunately, but this class is a pretty easy A

He was overall okay. He fell behind schedule so that we had MATLAB assignments due without much lecture material to go off of, which sucked. His tests were pretty standard difficulty, (with no proofs!!) but there were some curveball questions . Unlimited attempts on online homework was great. Cheat sheet was allowed for exams.
Lectures were dense and not very well explained. Most of what I learned came from reading the textbook. Homework was exceptionally easy but tests were intense.

Unreasonable matlab homework that has nothing to do with anything learnt in his class. In his matlab homework he gives you a definition and let you solve the questions you have never seen in regular course materials.
Heavy accent, he put his notes online. But his online homework assigned by a awful website that sometimes allow just one attempts. You could have far better choice.

I took both 102 and 152 from him. He actually improves a lot in 152. Tests are not hard as long as you speed up during the test. He gives decent curves also. It would be nice if he posted enough useful homework and study guides for the exams.

Just a joke of a class. Prof seems interested in lecturing, but not in any of the outside-of-lecture or administrative aspects of running a class. Now 3 weeks post-final and course grades have yet to be posted. TAs scramble to cover as much as they can in section. Just study from old exams, very little changes year to year.

I don't know why so many people said he curved very generously, but I checked the past final grades and they're not curved, and most people just got above 90%. But this class definitely not for me, too much memorization. If you're taking many courses, don't take this class, it's too heavy.

I made the mistake of spending too much time memorizing drugs rather than group mechanisms.  Super cool class and a great professor to teach it, really respects his students! This quarter was the first time no one failed the class!

Difficult but great class. There are SO MUCH information to retain that it makes metabolic biochemistry look like child's play. Dr. David is a really nice guy though. He definitely knows what he's talking about, and is always willing to help. However, this class won't be offered next year.

For an 8am class, a final that is worth 100% of your grade and material that is way to detailed this class is incredibly difficult, requires intense studying and memorization of Drug Names/classes. As if that isn't hard enough the few multiple choices given are penalized for wrong answers.
The only thing I learned in this class was how to fall asleep during lecture.

I learned a lot about the basics of linux and visualization. However, I learned essentially no new physics and spent much time simply trying to use computing packages instead of doing practical scientific computing. Kuti himself is of little use, but there is some value to the course.

He pretends like the class is very easy and he wants to give out as many A's as possible. His lectures are very interesting and keeps your attention, but BEWARE the exams are extremely difficult and time crunched that even if you understand the material fully, you will likely still do VERY poorly.
He would like to walk around in the lecture room without a microphone, which makes the lecture soooooooo inaudible!!! Also, please be aware of VERY TOUGH TESTS!!!!
Misunderstood, stories for days, textbook narcissist, extremely intelligent, very supportive and caring if he decides youre worth it.

Lectures seem unorganized but in fact are really well-designed. The best part of the class is the ugly puppy model, which includes all the important principles of accounting. I narrowly missed all three A-insurance quizzes but got the A bonus on final. It gives me a lifelong lesson: one step close to perfect means nothing. Only perfect is perfect.

People thought that he was really hard, but he grows on you! He wants you to succeed and if you put the time and effort in, then you'll do just fine. If you notice an error in his work, tell him. I almost failed the class due to a careless error, but him knowing my face saved me and i ended up with an A
3 hour lectures in summer class - a lot! But participation encouraged

I respect Professor Nasser as an esteemed and experienced professor. At first I was astonished by his age, but as I took his class throughout the quarter I was amazed by his lecture style and notes. The materials taught in this class may look simple but actually not easy, so keep in mind to catch up with the class progress. And there is no curve.

Took him for Statics and Solid Mechanics I. His lecture were very clear and reasonably slow so everyone was able to follow along. He also gives you all the materials you'll need to succeed in his classes (homework solutions, past midterms, problem sessions). Overall, a very straight-forward and friendly professor.

Prof Nemat-Nasser is an amazing professor.  His lectures were clear with neat handwriting and he would take pictures of his notes to post online.  He truly cares about his students and wants them all to do well.  He assigns weekly homeworks to be turned in and he posts practice exams (exams are very fair).  I highly recommend taking his classes.
Interesting lectures, amazing professor! Homework reflects exams. Gives practice exams. What else are you looking for? Take his classes!

The best SE professor that I had so far. He has outstanding notes and tests reflect that of homework problems. His lectures require clicker attendance, which stimulates a learning environment every lecture. He is also available during office hours, even though he may be tired. I would definitely recommend him to everyone.

The first eight weeks of this class may be easy for anyone with basic probability and stats knowledge. However, as the class progressed after week 8, things are getting way harder. Therefore, brace yourself for the final because it could be extremely hard compared to the two midterms. But fortunately everything is based on a curve.

If you fail Ong's class, you have only yourself to blame. He grades based on the curve, and the average is always a B. He also gives you all the past midterms and finals with their solutions so you have plenty of material to practice for tests. Great professor, jsut study hard for the exams and you'll be fine.

Prof Ong really knows his stuff. He listens to the class and tries to adjust accordingly. I took 106 the second time it was taught and comparing the tests from the last time it was taught, it can be seen that he really is trying to improve on the way he tests and presents the material. Prof Ong is great! :) It isnt easy but it also isnt impossible.
He is a responsible professor. Although this course is not easy at all, he made it at least approachable.

He knows his stuff.... but the lectures are way too fast and often assume that student already know a lot...... does not entertainment fundamental questions..... has no tolerance for idiocy so I feel reluctant to ask questions even when I don't know what's going on.

She is passionate about the course; that is unquestionable. Problem is she expects too much from students. Most took this class for P/NP yet she wanted everyone to treat it as if it were our major course. She assigns too many readings and movies. She also wants us to BUY all of the books and bring them to class. Not too strict a grader, though.

Get ready to read! There's so many reading assigned and if you ask her about anything, you will only get more confused. Her instructions for paper are not clear and you have two midterm papers and a final paper, which is kind of heavy.

For the first half of the quarter, I had no idea what was going on because her explanations of definitions and concepts made no sense. Class was solely lectures which failed to make it engaging, and the readings are very long and tended to be dry. However, after the first test, I understood a little more and things became more interesting.

Not an easy A but I learned so much in this class. Lots of reading but you're not expected to memorize anything just to be familiar with main concepts. I skimmed almost every article, showed up to class, payed attention and I got an A.

Other reviews seem like STEM majors trying to get an easy A for their DEI requirement, in which case this is not the class. Dr. I is easily one of the best professors Ive had at UCSD. She cares about her students and wants them to come to class and actually learn. Challenging, thought provoking class, but expectations are made abundantly clear

A very easy class, especially if you have prior knowledge of the anatomy of the brain. There are iClicker questions, so you have to go to lecture. She also allows you to do 2 extra SONA credits than required, which raises your overall grade 2%.
a lot of information but the tests are fully based on the lectures and she podcast so its easy to look back and study... She drops your lowest midterm grade which is also helpful.

She talks VERY fast and can be hard to understand, but going through it on your own is helpful (all lectures are podcasted). There's 3 midterms, but she drops the lowest one (and test questions are straight from lecture, so pay attention!) No homework, and un-graded clicker questions every class for attendance.

This course is memorization heavy- not an easy A if you don't put some time into it, but not a bad course if you like the brain & nervous system. Her lectures can be confusing & fast, but she podcasts. Clicker questions during class so pay attention. 2 midterms & 1 final that have small details from lectures, and she curves them a bit.

Class is based almost entirely on lectures, and definitely not an easy A. She is fair with her tests and curved them a bit. She is very knowledgeable about her subject and explains things well. You will learn a lot in this class if  you apply yourself. Attendance is not mandatory, and all lectures are podcasted with slides.

This class was really interesting. We read a couple of books and had to discuss what we found interesting and share it with the class. We watched movies and quizzes weren't really that bad as long as you read and paid attention. The final was a little different since you had to bring 2 guests for a performance you make. Good regional spec for ERC

She is knowledgeable, cares about her students, and is easy going. She IS NOT clear on what she wants for papers, and was extremely controlling over the projects. She's extremely helpful and super nice. Her grading policy isn't that tough. I thought I was gonna do horrible in that class, but I did pretty good. Take her!!!

Tere is a very nice teacher and really puts an effort into helping her students become better writers.  If you go to her office hours, she is willing to help you with your essays.  If it weren't for the fact that Muir 40 itself is tedious and seemingly pointless, I would recommend any class she teaches.

Same teacher I had for Muir 40. This time she was a little less clear about what she wanted because I tried to apply what I learned in 40 to this class and it didn't work out well. She's still cool though. Recommended.

Graded by midterms, homework, and final, and homework was only 5%. Horrible lecturer. Talks slow. Takes long breaths between words like he didn't plan what he would be talking about in lecture. What he teaches in class hardly relates to what's asked on homework. He posted a practice midterm and final which helped, allows a cheatsheet, and curves.

Garay is pretty unenthusiastic, barely scratching the surface of topics in lecture. Sometimes it seemed like he didn't care at all. The course definitely requires a solid amount of studying if you want to do well on the tests. If he gives practice test the actual test will be somewhat similar. But sometimes he wont. If that's the case, know it all.

Barely teaches during lecture. Assigns homework (10 hws, only worth 5% of grade) that covers some material that isn't even in the book. I asked a TA where a certain homework topic was in the book and he simply told me to "look it up". Even the book chapters to read on the syllabus are wrong. One of the most disorganized classes I've ever taken.

The class was very hard to follow along with just because he spent most of the time working on deriving equations (which you will be required to do for tests without using a cheat sheet). Even though the notes were provided, sometimes it would skip steps. I wished they focused more on practice problems than conceptual derivations.

Worst professor ever met. Told us there was gonna be a final during week 9. Not responsible at all. At the beginning of the quarter he specifically said there was no final for this class. Already reported to biology department. Don't ever take his class because u never know what's coming.
He told us there would be a final 3/4s way through the class, when it was already too late to drop it. Usually for upper division bio seminars, you write a final paper not an actual exam.

Professor Xu is a very smart guy. You can tell he knows exactly what he's talking about. The problem is, the class has absolutely no idea what he's talking about a majority of the time. He has a thick accent, but you get used to it over time. Xu does seem like a good due, but he doesn't seem to really care about teaching the course.

He's not a bad lecturer. He's not riveting, but not the worst. He gets the job done and, as many have said, his slides are well put-together. The key to any physio class is just understanding the body -- do the readings if you can (the book isn't too hard to read). He tests mostly lecture, but there were some answer choices in the MC from book only

Very knowledgable professor who lectures nearly straight from the textbook, which is  good thing because his exams are 100% based off the textbook so there's multiple opportunities for you to review the material. I wish he were more transparent about the grading though. I don't know what I got on the final or how much he curved in the end.

Lectures are only helpful if you do not plan to read the novels/ readings she assigns. However, reading on your own might be slightly more effective than attending her lectures. I learned almost nothing from the lectures, and often found myself frustrated with them. She is often repetitive of old tropes, and she subversively discourages diverse discourse on social issues. Her voice is hard to hear and she often doesn't use her mic. Her lectures are very disorganized and hard to follow and take notes on.

She is a very smart and kind professor. Readings must be done before class because she summarizes the readings but will randomly call on people to fill in the blanks. Her exams are very straight forward, as long as you do the reading you should get a good grade. The essays are also very straight forward. I love her humor and how passionate she is.

Unfortunately Sanchez is probably the worst DOC professor in the program. It's a joke to compare her to the other DOC teachers. If you don't read you will do very poorly since she poorly explains the material and main ideas behind it. Go to her office hours, especially for her essays;she will clarify everything you need and give you feedback on your work. Her tests are very easy--- if you remember characters, locations and themes.
She works with dolphins. She is the most amazing professor I have ever had. Her lecture is heavy but she explains clearly and uploads everything. Study guide is helpful for test.

Almost got A+. Her lecture was really amazing, and it is easy to see her passion in music. There were 3 concerts to go and concert report for each. Two quizzes. 5 reading responses, all the readings are related to contemporary music, boring but easy to respond. Tests were easy as long as going over the lectures and listening examples.
He is a solid professor who is passionate about the subject, and who also cares tremendously for his students. His class is also pretty easy to get an A too.
Professor Xu is quite possibly one of the three best professors I've had at UCSD. His mind is on another level and it is so fun analyzing political data with him at the helm.

The thing about 130B is, its more of a chinese history class than a chinese politics class. I still learned a lot, but I could have learned it from a couple of hours on Wikipedia. Class isn't hard though, and Xu is a nice and funny guy. Maybe worth taking if you are really looking for a less difficult class.
Phenomenal Professor, probably worth it even just to sit in.

Be aware if taking her diffusion class. Worst professor ever, not helpful, never upload notes and slides. She takes note on her laptop which looks messy and passes very fast. I expected worse. Lectures were fine, I didn't have to read textbook much. I don't understand all the concepts but I know enough to do well on HW/exams. However, McKittrick is sometimes disorganized and lowkey clueless. Didn't love her but would take her again .

I strongly suggest do not choose her diffusion class ! She wont share much slides about the class. What is worse, she always make mistakes on her blur handwriting during the class. Be honestly, this class is suitable for student who want to know more about semiconductor, and the content of the class is fine, I have to acknowledge. I love Grace and so does everyone else in my class. She's funny and the class is small so she knows everyone well. This is a great class to take to get foundations and push yourself, and it's fun. Take if you are non-white. Teaching assistant gives and hours long rant about how dangerous white people are. "People ask me what's the most dangerous thing I've seen while living in Chicago. It's white people"- Tezeru Teshome

Weekly quizes that seem to have no specific answer but still are graded HARSHLY. Going to the lecture and taking notes still won't guarantee a good grade. Nice but can't teach. Does not give clear lectures yet expects us to know what she has in her mind to do the multiple choice weekly quizzes.

He does this thing where he gets really excited while he teaches and is super cute and smiles at you and you think you understand it because of how good you feel but then you go to do the hw and get destroyed. Nice man, very helpful.

You have to WORK to get an A with Surko. No two ways around it. Understand his derivations, but study the book for the quizzes. TA discussions are crucial to your success in this class. Go to them. Finally, understand the hw. Do this and you will get an A.

Nice man, knows his stuff but don't rely on his lectures at all, he will absolutely confuse you. I ended up reading the chapter and doing each hw assignment 3 times just to make sure I understood material enough to do okay on weekly quizzes... An extremely poor professor. Spends lectures deriving complicated equations that are close to useless on quizzes. TA and book are the only ways to comprehend the material, and quizzes are still difficult. Clickers/attendance required for a grade. Avoid him!
Who else fooking gives you money in class? Enough said, could not be happier to have a professor who was genuinely invested in my comprehension of the subject.

A very energetic and enthusiastic professor. Uses a lot of contemporary examples, pop-culture references and tries to keep the whole class interested. Extremely enthusiastic about teaching the material. Practically yelled his lectures to the students. Going to his class was very enjoyable and sometimes unpredictable. Bringing balloons and other types of gadgets to lecture. His exams closely resemble the practice ones he posts on TED and what he goes over class. Don't miss lecture!

Professor Mateer was a great teacher! His lectures were engaging, and he has a great way of presenting the material. He's very enthusiastic and passionate about econ. Hands down best lectures ever. Engaging, fun, and exciting. His demonstrations in class combined with his energy and enthusiasm causes everyone to be engaged, and you will not be bored. The worst professor I've ever had the displeasure of encountering, bar none. His slides are messy and confusing. This professor is very unclear, i stopped attending lecture because i never learned anything from lecture. He doesn't really follow the book and is all over the place.
Unique class, unique professor. Although his material is hard to digest, you learn a lot from it. If you survive this class, you can surmount any college course.

This class is so challenging and you will feel more lost every lecture. But if you do the practice midterms and go to office hours you can score average or above which comes to an A-. This class is so challenging and you will feel more lost every lecture. But if you do the practice midterms and go to office hours you can score average or above which comes to an A-. I can list a tons of reasons why he's amazing: podcast available so basically do not need to show up to class, no attendance, cheat sheet, best hand writing eva, explain concepts nice and clearly, post hw/sample exam solutions

Diego is an amazing professor. He always knows how to make class fun. He assigns about as much work as any other professor and while it can be time consuming, it is not difficult at all. Diego is nice and very lenient. He makes things easy to understand and is clear with lectures & assignments. I have taken Diego twice, going to my third time next quarter! He is so passionate no matter what he is teaching, he makes hard readings and difficult concepts way easier to understand. Everything is take home and he gives at least a week for bigger papers to be due. or even longer. Such a refreshment, HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!
Go to office hours.

Took this in 2015. While he didn't cover a lot of breadth in topics, he did cover it in depth. Great class, really drills the 4 fundamental subspaces and least squares into your brain. Midterm was very tough with low averages though I did well; final was relatively easy for everyone.

This course was the hardest course I ever attended, but I knew it so I worked a lot from the start. However it was the most interesting course I also ever had, so it made studying so much easier. In the end, good homework and project grade gave a big advantage on the midterm.

Ken is a nice guy no doubt. He tries to be funny and engaging. Unfortunately, he talks/writes too fast and is bad at explaining material. Nuno, the other ML professor, may not be constantly cracking jokes, but he actually spends the whole hour and a half explaining material simply and clearly (at our level). Ken teaches like we are already experts.

Couldn't agree more, there really are some professors that are so bad you have to rate them. I'm not just writing this review because I'm salty, I've done really well in the class thus far. Absolutely love Professor Jordan! He sometimes drifts off in lecture into personal experiences, but his life is really cool, so it doesn't matter. Lecture goes fast and you need to write it down cause the slides and what he's saying are complementary, but different. His tests are applying information learned, so you have to understand.

mmw sucks, but Jordan is a great professor and makes the class a lot less worse. He is a very entertaining lecturer, who is obviously very fascinated on what he is talking about. Yes, you have to read a TON, but compared to other mmw professors it isn't that bad.

Okay all of you looking for the easiest mmw professor, mmw is a hard class no matter what professor you get. Jordan is a cool professor, but his tests are the hardest things ever. You have to do the reading since there's clicker questions in every lecture, but just read over his session summaries before exams, do the readings, and you'll be fine.
Great lectures, funny, really cares about the material, very knowledgeable.

Ms. Sanders is actually amazing. She knows AWP is intense, mostly because of the workload, but she makes it clear she's here for you and genuinely wants you to succeed. She's super sweet and funny, keeps everyone entertained, and an amazing teacher. If you have to take AWP, take her. Also, go to office hours. They're beyond helpful.
The AWP program was painful, but Ms. Sanders was a great lecturer. She kept everyone focused with her personality, and the feedback outside of class helped me pass this class.

I can't recommend Prof. Sanders enough. She genuinely wants her students to pass and she's super considerate. She works with everyone, heavily encourages people to go to office hours, and is super helpful when giving advice and feedback. She also jokes around with students and creates a comfortable class environment. I was blessed to have her!

Dr. Pantoja is the best professor ever. Her CAT 1 was the first class I took in UCSD, by which time I was panicking. But she was SUPER CARING and had done whatever she could to help students. In my opinion it was the best of all the CAT 1 courses. Great Teacher, Great Subject. If they are offering her class for CAT 1, TAKE IT!!!

Amazing professor. Can't say enough how great of a class it is. I looked forward to going to her class and wasn't stressed one bit the whole quarter for the class. There were two ways to earn extra credit as well that boosted my grade to an A- and they didn't take much time at all. Hope I have the chance to take Dr. Pantoja again.

Pantoja is a sweet professor. She is very helpful, especially when you contact her for Office Hours or just by emailing her. Ask for help  get an A.

Dr. Pantoja is the best professor ever. She is super attachable and is very caring. Lectures definitely give you a clear picture of the readings. I knew nothing about religions and English is my second language, but she helped me survived the class throughout. A life-beneficial class. Go to lectures and student hours! Highly recommend her :)

I took Mariko for TMC 198 my first quarter at UCSD, Im a third year now and she is still my favorite professor I have had. Since the class she has been a recommendation for my last two jobs. Class discussions are super interesting and homework is super minimal.

She told us that this is her first time teaching English, and that should've been a red flag to me that something wasn't going to turn out right.
