EXTREMELY hard to understand. :(

This was her first time teaching in English so I can understand that it was hard for her, but I literally had no clue what she was saying for 95% of lecture. Spent way too long on proofs which are never on tests, and would have a hard time understanding questions that students asked. Textbook was king for this class. Do not recommend her!!!

You would be marked down many points on an exam if you got a correct answer but did not use the exact method he wanted you to use. He would waste lecture time explaining why trig laws became trig laws. He also made all homework written, sometimes taking up as much as 8 pages for one assignment.

Tests are exact same format as practice tests. He is accessible out of class and willing to answer your questions. Lectures are sometimes hard to understand due to his accent, but you get used to it. His curve was amazingly generous being that 40%  C-. He is always on top of updating the class on grade posts and posting alternative help.

prof zhang was listed as staff for math 4c in the fall '18 quarter, so as suffice to say he doesn't have much experience in teaching but he is very forgiving and easy-going! midterms and finals are almost exactly like the study guide and his final grade curves are very generous. 10/10 would take again
Best professor I've ever had. UCSD BRING HIM BACK PAY HIM ALL THE MONEY IN THE WORLD

By far the best professor I've ever had. He talks pretty fast but you get used to it. His tests are very fair and the best way to study to by looking over lecture notes with examples and attend SI tutoring. His grading is very clear and straightforward.

The best math professor I've ever had! He is so nice and really cares about his students. He wants us to learn math and is available to his students outside of class as well. He made me actually enjoy math even though it is not my best subject, and motivated me to work hard in the class. His tests are fair, straightforward and I learned so much!

Snellman is great ! If you ever get lucky enough to take him please do not hesitate he is clear and really energetic about getting students to care about math! Never have I had a Math prof like him. He actually made me enjoy going to class and doing math !
Hes probably the best math professor Ive ever had. Its a shame that theyre letting him go.

He has a very soft voice sit in the front. He doesn't podcast. Lectures arent mandatory but he gives pop quizzes so you can't miss. Quizzes 20%, 1MT 20%, final or paper 60%. Lectures aren't mandatory, but informative.  No textbook needed, and reading is helpful but also not mandatory.  Grading was based on one MT and a final or a final paper 6 pgs (your pick).  Really nice, and he is one of the heads for Kavli institute.  It helps to have some of a genetics or biology background but not needed

I took Dr. Sarshar's Organic Chemistry class in 2003. He is a great lecturer and uses the Socratic approach to help you learn. The first exam I took I got a C. But then I worked harder and pulled an A. I am not always great recognizing things, but he is a great teacher.

Arrogant, rude, god complex. You'd think  someone would get this creep out but it's to the schools adv that you drop this (lose your refund) and have to take it again with a diff teacher. You think the school cares if you a. pass b.learn? Nope. I'd rather get pelvic cancer anyday.

By far the best class I ever took at UCSD!!! Yes, he's exteremely arrogant and demanding, but his lectures are fantastic. He explains things so well and makes you REALLY learn ochem. Class average was a 1 out of 50.  Meaning most got 0 and or even - points. Big woop-di-do you went to Berkeley. Just an all around jack off wanna be prep banana republic wearing greaser, lose the attitude you're nothing special.
Hot prof that wants students to learn.  Study hard for his class and ochem is a breeze.
Bill is an inspiration to us all

hey he's pretty good

a really good lecturer and professor! he is a funny professor that talks jokes during the classes. the midterms are easy but the final will be harder. but if you have a good job on the midterms you will get a good grade finally. there are readings as homework but if you don't read you might still have B or at least past this course.

He works well with the TAs, Jamal and Anna, and the exams are very representative of the material that is discussed in class. I would definitely take this class again if I could, and I hope Professor Schurgin teaches other classes as well.

Chill/interesting class. Prof is passionate about the subject, and he is very interesting and engaging. Tests aren't that hard if you rewatch the podcasts of the lecture and add to the notes you already have a few days before the test.
She doesn't curve. Grade is only based off of a few things. Quizzes, midterm, and final are open note, but it was still really hard and specific.

Her test/quizzes are open notes. She doesnt podcast and doesnt write down every topic she tests on the whiteboard. An A is possible if you listen to every second of the lecture jotting every single thing she says not missing a word. lets be real who in a 80min lecture catches every word. Dont be fooled by open notes exam. Textbook not helpful.

Heather Broccard-Bell is a great professor to take for Bild 3. Do not listen to anyone who says otherwise. If you go to lecture and take notes on the things she writes on the board, you are almost guaranteed an A. The people who say she is bad are the ones that skipped every lecture. The discussions are mandatory with open note/internet quizzes.

I really liked her as a prof, but i can understand the lecturestyle might not be for everyone. More specifically if you go to lectures, its a really easy class to pass. She has a test everyweek, but these and all exams are completly open note. So as long as you go to class or read the corresponding chapters of the book, its a great class!

The professor's hand-writting is quite bad, or even worse when you find that she actually puts every note on the blackboard. If you are not a native speaker, or have no idea about most terms in biology, you'd better select another class or another professor.

I had no previous coding experience and was able to safely pass. Lectures are dull so I skipped a few. No one goes to discussion but it and office hours were my saving grace. Make sure to make friends so you can ask questions about hw! Videos online and the book also help. Final is open note so take notes of everything and go to review sessions!

The material wasnt actually hard, its just that Vardy makes it so needlessly complicated. He goes beyond what other lecturers do in CSE 20 and his explanations are not clear at all. Great example of why you shouldn't take a staff class unless you have to.

Great lecturer, really cares about students. His midterm and assignments are pretty straightforward and the TAs are helpful. However the final exam was horrible, the worst Ive ever had. Still would recommend the lecturer and the class. I still ended up getting an A because I got more than 100% on other parts.

Vardy was a great professor and this is coming from someone who struggled in his class. His lectures were clear and his tests were fair. I think he doesn't have a higher rating on here because the classes he teachers are very difficult for the most part which can cause some students to be upset, but I would recommend him to anyone.

Vardy lectures a bit fast and sometimes it can be difficult to follow if you are writing notes. CSE 20 is more of a math class than a programming class. You must have strong knowledge of math to succeed. Final and midterm are open notes, so take advantage of that. Homework is time consuming, but if you get started early, you should be fine.

Fortunately I had an amazing TA who helped me prepare for the midterm and finals. Other than that, lectures were kind of boring. Guest lecture did appear in some of the classes and I always enjoyed them. We had 4 response papers, 1 midterm, 1 final. Grading for midterm and finals were surprisingly lenient and easy. Ps. She gives pop quizzes

Professor Gore is amazing and really passionate about the topic.  She definitely keeps the class entertained with her humorous examples taken during lecture.  No midterm! She gives you weekly quizzes, which are easy as long as you do the readings.  Readings might be difficult to understand so make sure to go to her lecture! Definitely recommend her

I felt that some class materials were emphasizing "left-hand" side especially in Economics-related parts. So does the grading rubic (this is just how I felt. so it's just an opinion.) Other than that, the professor is overall great in carrying out course materials. Clarity for exam is fair enough. Do the readings and go to class then it's fair game

She keeps classes relatively interesting as there are a few guest speakers and she often incorporates videos into her lecture, but often times, class is boring. She also doesn't seem to be an expert as she made multiple factual errors over the course of the quarter. She gives you study guides and easy pop quizzes so it's not a difficult class.
Really engaging and powerful woman.

He left grading until last minute and i didn't know how i was doing in class until after i took final. Bad "lectures" and they don't even help. Makes a lot of errors when writing test. Previous year tests not good indicator of final/midterm. Not clear. When students tell him that in matlab his code does one thing, he insists it does another.

He gave practice finals from the past three years, but the actual final was nothing like those. Instead of testing our matlab skills, it was more of a reading test. Asking you specific things from past assignments that were not even the main point or even about matlab itself. He MISSED the deadlines for grades too.

Loved her class! We did a lot of work outside and some group projects. The readings were hard but I just started skimming them. The lectures were great but kind of long sometimes. She always answered my emails which a lot of professors at UCSD don't do. Clear directions on HW. She always spent time in class explaining them, so go to class! :)

Professor Bush treated this class like an upper division class. It was her first time teaching at UCSD, but the grading criteria was unorganized and complicated. Her projects were all last minute and very vague, and a lot of work. I took two USP classes before, and this was just unreasonable. Lots of reading too. Would not recommend her.
Fantastic professor. Took him for 103B, and am taking him for 102J. Such a shame he is retiring - easily best lecturer I've had at UCSD.

Cool guy, knows his stuff. More USP than PS so watch out PS majors it gets dry. Must take notes during lectures he doesn't podcast or post notes. Midterm and final both in class with study guides given a week before tho. Your call.

Stevie is awesome, probably the best professor at UCSD. Never seen a prof be so energetic about lecturing. Is is also a genius when it comes to UCLA and his book Beyond Chinatown is praised by other professors all over the country. Basically, he is a stud.
Interesting lectures and pretty funny.  However, he randomly winks at people and it freaked me out when I was the target for no reason that I could guess.

this class requires you to read the book and to go to lecture.  the books are really really boring. he is a really close speaker (literally).  there is like no way to bs any of the short questions or essay without reading.  remember to choose a short answer that people won't choose, because the grade is based on the best answer.  i aced it.

There weren't a lot of homework assignments, which was nice, and she gave extra credit a few times. Takes attendance using pop quizzes on iClickers. Lot of stuff was covered in the class but her final wasn't too hard. The midterm was worse. Homeworks were easy, and she graded nicely on the final project paper. The subject wasn't that interesting.

Prof. Biswas is very knowledgeable about linguistics, but for a lower div class that most people are taking for DEI/GE, it could have been easier. Only 1 midterm and 1 simple term paper, weekly readings are super boring but on the test, weak study guides imo. Really sweet and personable lady, class is just okay. Uses iClickers occasionally.

The information just wasn't interesting to me. You can skip class and get an A because she posts her lectures slides online and doesn't elaborate much on them. She does do occasional pop quizzes but if you look on the lecture slides when they're posted, you can see if clickers are used that day. Easy A but boring class. Great GPA booster.
She's a really good professor who always shows up to class prepared.
The subject matter is interesing. The professor is caring about the subject, and made efforts to clarify the topics. Young professor. Good luck for the future.

Dr. Ryan is hands down the best professor I've had at UCSD. She is extremely caring and is so willing to help her students. Her lectures are pretty content heavy, but the material is very interesting. There are 2 midterms and a cumulative final exam that is only worth 20 points. Her exams are pretty fair and I would highly recommend her.

Absolutely loved this course and Professor. Dr. Ryan is extremely kind, helpful, and knowledgeable. Assignments are relevant and helpful in expanding your knowledge about topics learned in class and grading and exams are fair and representsribe of lecture content. Would def recommend Dr. Ryan and hope I can take her again

The textbook isn't necessary, she even says that all the exam questions are from her powerpoint. Great lecturer, has extra credit opportunities, easy HW, and fair (but still tough) exams. She even has in-class exercises that're actually enjoyable. The only assignments that required some effort are 2 papers, 1 of which is co-authored.

She is super knowledgeable about this topic and is incredibly nice. Takes time to answer all questions and is just a great lecturer. The TAs were also super helpful and the midterms and final were very fair. Definitely recommend.

Dr. Ryan is so nice. She's my favorite prof in the FMPH dept. Her lectures are smooth and the slides have all the info you need so you can just listen and not bother taking notes (she said so herself). There are assignments but they aren't hard bc she doesn't want grades to be a burden. You can tell she has lots of experience, knowledge and wisdom.
one of the best professors, eASY A
Natalie is awesome !!! Her class taught me sooo much!!! Im a way better actor because of her. Today was our last day of class and everyone was so sad.
Her grade was terrible. If you want get an easy A, skip her!!! She did lots of meaningless things in her class and they were so boring.

The subject matter is very intriguing but might be a bore for others. Be wary you are graded on papers. I highly encourage you go to office hours with the TA and the professor. Overall, I really enjoyed the class I just wish there was a clearer rubric for the papers. Also save the handouts they are very very helpful.

He's an angel sent from the heavens. Reminds of a friendly caring grandfather figure who treats his students like his grandchildren. He likes to joke around and is very soft spoken and approachable. He takes the time to answer questions in class and really break things down. He simplifies things so much and makes them so much easier to grasp.
Nice and friendly, the lectures are easy and there are almost no homework except then the readings, but the midterm and final papers  are tough graded. If you ace the paper then you should be fine.

i took prof. anagnostoupolos for history of ancient philosophy. the lectures were lit and well-attended; he's very funny, and also kind if you approach him afterward. i'd advise that you pay attention and/or read the handouts thoroughly because they'll answer the essay prompts. overall: two 5pg essays & one 10pg essay. :)
I took the class to get a basic intro to philosophy as well as complete one of my general education requirements. It was worth the effort and I really like the professor.

The best professor in UCSD. A UCSD career without him is such a pity. His lecture is informative and interesting, even though it's 3 hours long, you will never get bored. His examples are typical and make sense; he's clear in structure. He and Wieland are two Macro Econ professors that you get to take for all costs, A REAL GEM!

Lagakos is an EXCELLENT professor, take him if you can. I had a 3-hour class with him on Monday nights and his lectures were always enjoyable and informative. He's hilarious, freakishly good with names, and very knowledgeable on the topics he teaches.

This guy's awesome. He and Levkoff are the best profs in the department IMO. He is uses very relatable examples, which is tremendously helpful, and takes  the time to make sure his students understand the material before moving on. Unlike Candido and Tang who just try and spew out as much info as possible to stay on "schedule". TAKE HIM if possibl

Honestly, the best econ professor I have ever had here at UCSD. I have never understood materials for an econ class this well. As long as you attend lecture, you're covered. He sincerely cares for his students (the ones that show up to class). Honestly wish he was teaching more classes at UCSD

Agler's lectures are always fast- paced, and mostly repetitive with the textbook, but his explanations are helpful towards understanding the material. He is funny, has patience in explaining stuff, and gives generous curves. Homework based on correctness, hard quizzes; midterm and final are not as hard.
He is pretty laid back, but he is really messy with his use of the board. I liked his attitude but sometimes he seemed too informal.  In overall a good teacher.

I recommend him very much. Provided his own mini-"textbook" for the class which only cost $30 at the student reserves center. So even if you missed a concept in lecture, the textbook is all in his own writing. He's a pretty good lecturer too, and very helpful and approachable in office hours. Exams were very reflective of the material.

I thought his midterms were a bit hard since it was all concept based. Though the curve was crazy which I guessed helped everyone. I never attended his lectures cause as long as you did the hw and understood the material you're fine. Final was very similar to the midterms and practice final so that was an easy A.

His class was super hard and the midterms were hard. The averages were not great but he is not a bad professor. His teaching style is very different and he tries to make examples but ends up failing at it. His class is curved but if I were you, take another prof. Also use the book extensively!

James is a great lecturer, but very very bad at writing tests, but not in the sense that it's material that hasn't been covered, but in the sense that there is no clear answer to every problem, it is never fully known how much 'explanation' he really expects. Also he is the only math professor that makes section mandatory and graded. Avoid him!

I feel like all math classes should be taught like his. He cares more about the intuitive meanings behind integrals than the calculations, which (if you actually pay attention in class), makes more sense than simply plugging numbers into formulas. His way of explaining these concepts is clear and actually makes you interested in math. Great prof!
His lectures are really clear and engaging and he explains concepts incredibly. What more could you want?

He is probably the most unusual professor teaching 170A. He does not focus on intense calculations or proofs but rather the broader picture, namely, the concept and trade-off of every method. Some assignment can be time-consuming but graded leniently. Exams are generally OK if you recognize what he expects you to learn from this class.
Dilts is an alright professor. The class is way too much work and exams were pretty challenging. He will curve the class if people mess up.

Sammartano makes her classes a delight to go to. We are required to go to out-of-class performances, and to research about a dance artist of our choice- but those works are not hard, and pretty much enjoyable. She also gives good feedback on our dancing styles, and inspires her students' passion in dancing. A definite good choice!

I love her so much!! She made ss2 less stressful and more fun! TDMV2 is very easy (1 2 page paper for the midterm and a fun group final project). Her free spirit and kind soul made me look forward to this class every week!
Amazing professor and she is quite attractive. Her dancing is unbelievable, she is super athletic, and flexible! Something about her that left me wanting to dance more - glad I enrolled.

wonderful dancer and teacher! I loved this class! not too much required work outside of class. no tests or quizzes. required: view two dance performances, 2 page response to one performance, 2 page research essay for midterm, choreograph a group piece for final.

Tonnie is a really interesting and fun teacher. Her dancing style is really unique and it's cool to watch her. The final was really simple (part written part actual doing a dance routine). Overall easy class. You have to go to two dance performances outside of class and write up summaries but it's easy. Take it!
A good class but don't take it if you want to have a high GPA (no curve, strict grading).

You can see that he actually cares about his students. When you talk to him he actually understands your concerns and wants to be of help to the students. That's something I hardly found today among most professors. Extraordinary TAs also. Reasonable workload and you can't do badly if you invest time. This class is not meant to make your life hard.

Professor Wishon is the best history professor I have ever met. He is very humorous when explaining concepts and very clear about what he is teaching. You have to attend all lectures because he will not post PPTs online. The exams are all about the key themes and concepts in class. One 1250-1750 word essay. Strongly recommend!

Funny and sarcastic professor but beware his lectures can feel so long. He just puts up a picture of a map or a couple bullet points and talks for such a long time. Every lecture he gives new key terms/themes which end up being the study guide. Test is reflective of the study guide. Not really necessary to read the textbook.

VERY Lecture heavy and you HAVE TO read a lot, since he WILL NOT repeat what you read in class but those are covered in tests. And he WILL NOT podcast. Graded by mid and final, plus one essay. He will give you primary and optional resources for the discussion and essay. Workload 200p per week. Discussion is extremely important. You must take notes.

Great professor. Talks slow so that you can follow along, but it can get boring. She goes over plenty of examples in class and the tests are fair. She responds to emails quickly but comes late to office hours. Hand written weekly homework must be turned in at the beginning of class.
Great professor. Material is clear, and class format is pretty organized. Pay attention and ask questions though, because the material is hard.
Great professor. Clear lectures and notes, gives plenty of examples in class. Exams are definitely fair. Take her
Tests are not hard if you attend most class. She explains the course materials clearly and makes helpful summaries in slides. Definitely a really caring and inspirational instructor!
Mr. Dechner was the best and most real professor I've ever had.

She is a very good professor. Very understanding if something is too difficult. Exams are based on her lectures and very straight forward. She would changed the grading scale after each exam to always have the same average which benefited everyone. She can answer any question very well. Very much enjoyed her as a professor, would recommend

She is an amazing professor that I ever had in my life. She is so caring, kind, and friendly to all her student and try to help the student as much as she can. There is a textbook, but if you listen to her lecture, no book needed. Her lecture is so interesting. There is a research paper as well. I definitely recommend her for sure! She is awesome.
She was an excellent professor. She was very caring and made chemistry more approachable and doable for people who are not naturally good at it.

Dr. Ray was my instructor at Palomar. she did not shy away from giving us higher level material from her UCSD classes. However, she's very lenient with grading and exam corrections and because of this her classroom environment revolves around challenging oneself, working w/others, and truly learning to appreciate chem. Take her, she's brilliant.

Professor Ray is probably one of the nicest professors at UCSD. She could make some mistakes at times during lecture, but she's very good at explaining the concepts and answering any questions. Also funny, which makes the lectures somewhat entertaining. 10/10 would recommend. Considerate, nice, easy to talk to.

I'm not a massive chemistry fan, but I loved Prof Ray. She's clearly very passionate about the subject but very accepting of the fact that students in Chem 6A may not be. You may need to call her out on some in-class errors, but her exams are very manageable, she tries to minimize tedious memorization, and she gives some charming chemistry puns.

Offers a ton of extra credit that more than makes up for the lack of a curve on tests. Quizzes are online and are very similar to the homework, so there isn't much of an excuse to get bad grades on them. The lowest score of the cumulative quizzes, the midterm, or part of the final exam is dropped.

Be ready to learn on your own. He lectures by re-writting the whole text book out. The material on the textbook and his lectures are not representative of the material that you will be tested on. The textbook and the lectures do not help so much to do the homework and the tests so be ready to put in a lot of work to pass this class.

If you're looking to learn math well, do not take this man. He's a nice guy but a terrible teacher. If you are willing and capable of learning the material THOROUGHLY by yourself then feel free to take him. His lectures are confusing and do not help with the homework. Tests come from book and past tests combined. Flip a coin and pray if you'reWeak

Prof. Buskin is not a good professor. Do NOT choose Buskin unless there is no other choice. He gives tons of examples in class and does not explain how to solve questions. Homework problems take a few hours to complete because they were not covered in class. TAs grade harshly, and the midterm comprises of 5-6 questions which are weighted heavily.

Buskin is a nice person, but I don't like him as a professor. He has a thick Russian accent and on top of that is often not the most articulate of people. His accent paired with his stumbling of words makes his lectures VERY hard to understand. He also holds his mic right by his mouth and it's really loud. Just hard to understand and listen to him.

This class is difficult bc who gives a crap about Calculus analysis. Had Sterbenz for Math 109 and will take him for 142B- he is better than buskin at explaining material. If u wanna read a lot and watch youtube and listen to lectures about excessive PROOFS in a heavy russian accent, take Buskin. His tests are okay, lecture material all from txtbk

Crammed too much material into lecture and read off slides - really boring. Study guides were unhelpful and tests were graded harshly - they expected 10 points to be made in a 4 sentence short response. Simulation was weekly work and only worth 15%. Changed the syllabus during the quarter from a 3 page essay to 6 and was only worth 15%. Unfair

Honestly this was the most frustrating course I've taken at UCSD and I'm a 4th year. Lectures were difficult to sit through, felt like I didn't learn anything I couldn't have found on Wikipedia. Material hard to follow, exams difficult to prepare for as study guides were largely unhelpful/irrelevant. pSimulation game was a waste of time.
Lord Vaughn's course was a lot of fun. Most notably, the simulation game was very entertaining and engaging. She tends to be a tough(er) grader but the test material is generally straightforward.

She is an okay lecturer but her lecture-style does not facilitate note-taking. She has way too much stuff covered in a short period of time. However, the real tragedy is her assignments. While there are not tough, there are not explained properly. She always expects something very specific but the explanations are very vague.

Man, this prof will teach you so much about global health and the future of the field. His experience and knowledge in the global health field really adds to the class and makes you think. He really cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Truly wish he taught other global health courses on campus because I would take them. 11/10 class
Amazing professor that taught me a lot about Global Health.

I took Mackey's GLBH 148 Global Health Policy class and it was amazing. He really cares about his students and is accessible outside of his class. He can be sassy and isn't afraid to call students out for ignorant ideas. He is very analytical and the paper at the end of the term counts for a lot of your grade. PAY ATTENTION and you will pass.

I loved this class so much. You get a broad overview of global health and epidemiology! Dr. Pitpitan is really good at explaining and is pretty chill. Didn't think the exams were too difficult, just a lot of memorization from lecture. The response papers were annoying though especially with 0.5 margins instead of 1 inch

She is a solid professor and there are opportunities for extra credit. Her class is fiar but it really depends on the TAs. I recommend coming to class and not just looking at the lecture slides because she will mention things for future exams. She is not very accessible out of class and I wouldn't recommend if you like hands-on professors.
Has terrible testing skills, where he prioritizes memorization over learning of the biggest concepts/
Avoid him. I never have a course with so much homework but curves to B-. Such a mean professor, giving B for all hard working students. Most students drop the course in the middle of the quarter.

Professor Talke does a great job of explaining a difficult yet rewarding subject. 150 is just one of those classes you have to grind through but in the end you will have gained some useful knowledge and skills in the world of CAD. The tests are difficult but very straightforward if you put the time into studying your notes and the reader.

Prof. Talke is an excellent professor. He does not MAKE this class hard; it's just a difficult class. His lectures are engaging if you choose to pay attention. His homeworks are time-consuming but extremely helpful. If you're a serious student you will appreciate his teaching methods, and you will learn A LOT in his class. One of the best at UCSD.

Very thorough class. The topics aren't entirely related, but Prof. Talke does a very nice job presenting the material (his passion for this is QUITE evident, which makes the class enjoyable). His class structure is blackboard lecture, powerpoint summary, and a verbal summary of the material at the beginning of the next class. Study EVERYTHING!
He is definitely a tough grander, a lot of my friends failed in his class. Avoid to take his class!!

I'm sorry to say but his lecture is so boring... He talks in the lowest voice i've ever experienced in UCSD. Everything on the quiz is what he had talked about in class. His quizzes count 30 percent of the total grade which is super important, but forgive me I really can't concentrate. His arguments about movie and film are so flawed to me also.
The worst prof I have ever met. In the final, he told us we have to write 12 pages essay, and he still assigned us 100 images to memorize.

he is the worst professor I have ever met. He gave us 2 essays questions a week before final and expected us to finish those 12-16 pages during the final week and prepare for his own final which includes 100+ image bank. He doesn't care about his students at all

This class was reasonable and interesting until the final they sprung on us a total of 20 pages for a take-home essay given only a week to work on it. Nothing was changed when the class expressed their view that it was unfair. The final was worth 60% of our grade

The midterm is 13 of your grade and the final is 23. I got a 76% on my midterm and studied like crazy for the final but managed to pass the class with a B-. It was super hard to memorize those 400+ slides and dates but tbh I had fun with it. Just communicate with the TA if you're struggling and you'll be fine. And study! The book is a life saver!

Those who bash him are upset because they're use to the traditional rigid lecture format of classes, but he is not that way. He's such a sweet&calming presence. Many teachers can make you feel pressured, but not him. And lectures feel as if it's a conversation where he's just passing on his immense amount of knowledge. It's actually a nice change.

I'm sad I only got to take one class with this professor. She went above and beyond with detailed feedback that actually helped me improve my writing. She was also willing to work with me over email since I couldn't make it to her office hours. Discussions in her class were some of the most interesting I've had and made me want to work with kids.
As a disabled student, this professor was one of the worst I've had so far in terms of accessibility and willingness to accommodate. She's not responsive to emails asking for help.

He is very charismatic and keeps your attention during lectures. He has a very unique style of lecturing. Instead of using power points, he prints out papers with notes and puts them up on the projector. He gives us sheets with notes. Can talk very fast and for this course, he taught us a lot of material, which was hard to be an undergrad course.
His lectures keep your attention because he's quite a funny chap. He also gives out lecture notes, which are quite useful. Probably my fav professor out of the bunch.

Holland is awesome!!  He teaches the bio section of this course and he makes class worth going to.  I skipped out on all the lectureres, but I made sure to make it to all Holland's lectures.  He's funny, interesting to listen to, and actually kept me awake.  The class overall sucks-I took it for a gen.ed and Holland made it worth it.

The only Professor in this class that I was actually able to pay attention to and not fall asleep during his lectures. His section is the biology section which is the most interesting part of the course and he is kinda funny and approachable
he's so funny. he at least kept me awake in there.  he teaches the biology part of the course and gives nice handouts for you to study and to help for the final.  he's coo.

Sanders will tell you what to do, but won't "help" you. She will tell you that you are wrong, tell you why its bad, but when you ask her if somethings better she will ask you if you think it is. She isn't supportive doesn't mind seeing you distressed, I am always so confused with what she wants as a writer.
Class is so hard, the more you study, the less you understand. Boom. Mic drop.
She's a dang icon! Even with a messed up rotator cuff she was KILLIN it!!! I love her and will never forget her
i absolutely love her. she's so great at dancing and has taught me so much.

Took her for fine arts requirements. Pretty easy class. Easy A as long as you go to every class and participate in group projects. Kinda boring for people who don't like dancing, but hey, it's two easy fine art credits.
She is a teacher that you will remember for a long time.  Take a dance class and let it flow and change you
VERY CARING AND CONCERNED TEACHER...VERY PASSIONATE!!!

Awkward and unclear but she cares about you as a person if you ask for help. Don't understand the point of the class and she gets nervous a lot. Says mmmmhmmmmmm A LOT, its distracting. Extremely boring, could be done online, absolutely no engagement or interaction. Try to get it with another professor offered. Just go to keep your scholarship.

I dread coming to this class everyday. Attendance is mandatory but it does not help at all. It's boring and she gives no feedback whatsoever and expects a lot while providing little guidance. In no way did I enjoy this class.

had her last year for muir 50. is quiet and really wants you to participate in discussions. very helpful in giving you feedback on your paper, make sure to take notes when she does. Class is hard work though and time consuming.

Tried very hard in the class, yet I did not pass because my "good ideas" were not being written well. Went into the final essay with a B in the class. She likes anime and lord of the rings, so make sure to pop that into the first day of class to get a head start on brownosing! Other classes were a lot easier for others who worked a lot less.

Recommend her if you have to take M50. Shes very nice, kinda shy but her standards are very high. The course is made to be demanding. Yr life will be consumed by this class so plan yr schedule accordingly. You have to ask her alot of q's to understand what she wants in yr papers. But shes willing to help outside class.

Horrible teacher. held back all of my papers and graded after class ended. failed me out of graduate school. i graduated with honors from berkeley but she single handedly failed me out of graduate school because she did not like my politics, nothing to do with my skill. I was extremely ill that year and ended up having multiple surgeries.

Pretty boring and very liberal class and teacher, but she's nice enough and pretty chill. Her seminar was fair and you basically only have a 1 page summary due each week and then 1 final big paper, but if you split it up well it isn't that bad. I probably wouldn't take her again because of the liberal thing but I wouldn't be upset if I had to.

As an adult, in the history of my life I hold very few grudges. Two, to be exact. Professor Hartouni believes she is above the law, and perhaps she is. She readily will destroy graduate students' lives. I am aware of a few instances, three to be exact. She holds her opinions to be above those of her peers and is not a teacher, she lives to research

She's obviously very knowledgable, and I would certainly not recommend this class to anyone not interested in law, but I really appreciated that she took graded the class according to its "intermediate" elective standing. If you are interested in law, I imagine she would be a very valuable reference.

She's an interesting lecturer, but this particular class was just total unstructured BS. She and the other prof weren't clear about what they wanted on the summaries until about 4 weeks in, and there was no clear rubric on the huge final project, so my group was kinda floundering around hoping we were doing it right. Frustratingly unorganized.
DONT take his class! He just read off the powerpoint and he doesn't if you fail the class... He just try to get out of here asap

His lectures are boring but at least you have all the material posted online. You practically have to get perfect scores on the midterm and final to get an A. The curve is just so unfair. 89% is a C! I got 35/40 on midterm and 77/80 on the final, which is 94% and that was a B+, not A. So you can get screwed with the curve so high

Don't need to buy a textbook. His material is very useful. He usually reads his material. Tests are fairly easy, so everyone can get full credit for the test. if you miss one question, it's hard to get A. Despite your expensive tuition, if your goal is just to pass this course, take him.
Nice guy!!! Best econ prof at UCSD!!! Definitely choose him!!!!
I got almost every question correct on the final exam, but this professor failed me because he didn't think I showed enough work ON A MULTIPLE CHOICE EXAM
I feel cheated out of a chemical engineering education. This woman doesn't know how to teach or manage. I wish I had gone to another university.

Everything she lectures on is out of the textbook, but lectures are clicker-heavy so you cant skip class to study on your own. She doesn't write/read her own tests and during the final had to give out corrections every 10 mins. Do NOT take!!!

The class was easy, but she's a horrible professor and apparently a horrible exam writer. She'd just basically read off of slides and didn't know how to do her own example problems. CENG 100 was an easy course, and for the relatively simple concepts covered in the class Talbot was an OK professor. get a different job

It ended up not being what I expected, and her lectures started getting a little confusing. We had 4 quizzes, 1 Midterm and 1 final. Quiz questions came straight from hw (which wasn't mandatory to do). She's very sweet!!

Full disclosure: I took the class in the summer, and I anticipated it to be relatively more condensed. However, I believe the prof. was unfair in curving down the class because we did better than expected; the passing grade (originally 40%) became 55% only after the final exam. Also, the lectures were useless, as he mumbles and is mostly inaudible.

My worst class experience in UCSD. The whole course organization is a mess. 2 of the 3 midterms are graded with mistakes and the quiz if full of unnecessary details that will not let you learn anything really helpful. Professor can be hardly reached out of class and both the information for EC and the curve are not given clearly.

He made the class way harder than it needed to be. I was lucky to get my grade because I did really well on the first midterm. TAs said he asked them to make quiz/test harder to make a curve. Honestly, there were so many specific details about every part of the brain you either knew it or didn't. Each ppt would have about 60-80 slides a day.

Midterms were focused on details and pretty hard. If you get him and dont need to take the class for a letter grade, Id reccomend taking it pass/no pass. I didnt find the class interesting and definitely wouldnt take it again.

If you study for this class, you'll get a good grade. But you HAVE to study/read. I would recommend making a study guide that combines info from TA slides, kahoots, lecture slides, and Pineda's study guide (only reason i got a decent grade tbh). Don't rely on Pineda's EC or "class curve", he's a strict grader and notorious for screwing up grades.

His lectures aren't the interesting in the least bit. He has two midterms, six quizzes, and then the final. Takes very little time trying to reinforce concepts and is constantly behind schedule and trying to catch up. Would definitely avoid him if he ever comes out of retirement. Take Rangel !
I took his class during summer session. I would say I spent a lot of time per week doing the homework. However, if you finish the homework its pretty easy to get an A. Matlab is just time-consuming.
if you could finish the homework, you definitely could get a A
This course is really easy. If you could understand the homework, you would get "A"

Dr. Herz was fantastic! Such an entertaining and helpful professor.  He really cares about his students and if you take the time to go see him in office hours , you will most definitely do well.  He is very passionate about his work, therefore, it makes the subject matter all the better!  Do your work, go to class, and you will do just fine!
Made MATLAB so easy to understand. I took it over the summer and he helped so much. Professor Herz is really knowledgeable and teaches well. I'd highly recommend.
Best teacher in the entire world. Good soul, kind person.

Good professor. Although it's a bit boring at times because she mainly does historical background, it's really important to understand all the readings. Readings are really interesting and don't take that long to read. Do the readings, go to lecture, put in the effort and its an easy A. Really enjoyed the class, definitely gave me a new perspective

RMG is very honest and humorous.  Even though this was the first time she taught the course, she was well-researched in the subject of feminism in Hindi cinema.  The coursework is straightforward, but you have to be ready to watch an on-average 3 hour film EVERY week if you want to participate in class.  Hindi movies are sooo long!

Do not be fooled - she is a very tough grader. Don't be surprised when what you thought was an A paper comes back covered in red ink. She grades comparatively, so she determines where your paper stands in relation to the rest of the class. Also, she likes to grade indian students especially hard because she thinks they all take her for an easy A.

This was a great professor who really knew her stuff when it came to the topic of the class.  She presented the material in a clear way that made it very easy to understand and follow. Midterm and final were straight forward with no tricks. Highly recommended!

He has an understandable accent and a slow pace for lectures. Grading criteria is 40% Midterm+60% Final and he reads powerpoints (outlines of textbook) ALL the time, so no need to come to class. He posts all powerpoints, homework and solution online. Go over powerpoints (and the textbook if you want) before exams, do homework, earn an easy A.

Worst Professor I have ever had.    -Accent makes him hard to understand -Just  read powerpoints, no one goes to class. 20 ppl show up from a class of 300 to his lectures. -Horrible lecturer, no passion -makes things harder than they are -Designs horrible test, free response has 6-7 parts A,B,C,D,E,F and Last 2 are worth like 10 points each

Great enthusiasm, very knowledgeable. Sticks mainly to Powerpoints, but does a healthy amount of board-work as well. Exams will not surprise you, but know how to do basic college math (geom, algebra, calc)!!
What a great teacher. 10/10 would recommend. Makes great wine. A real G. TAKE HIM IF POSSIBLE!!
Lectures are great, makes occasional jokes. However not the most prepared. Overall okay.

He's not the world's most interesting lecturer as he tends to get caught up in tangential issues. We were also the guinea pigs for a Haskell-based curriculum but everyone hated Haskell so much that it practically disappeared by time the midterm came around. Not the worst, but nowhere near the best professor.

One of my favorite professors. The OS material is rigorous and difficult, but he presented it well, often (successfully) using various interactive techniques to engage the audience. It also stood out to me that he enthusiastically spent time interacting with students, personally providing help and very interesting insights during lab sessions.

Homework is due on one day and there's a quiz on the other. The material is a bit difficult, but his lectures are good and the final grade is curved. I had an 80% but it turned out to be a B+. Spend ample time on the homework and pay attention in lectures.

Rhodes is a good prof his lecture is a clear and he gives good examples. Beyond that this class is awful, I chose CSE as my major not math, doing proofs every weeks sucks, you spend a ton of time doing hard math proofs that 99% of the class will never look at again. Class is a total waste of time.
She's one of my favorite professors so far at UCSD. Very sweet and tells you exactly what you need to know. If you participate and come to class you can easily get a good grade in this course.

This professor is rude, and will criticize you & your work. Professors are to be inspiring instead of trying to put you down. He is by far the worse person to interact with. He will tell u how disappointing your work Is w/o encouraging u, insult u & say ur somewhat intelligent, & expects u to be a super human at his level. He is disappointing.

The class itself was fun, it was 60s music. Got to listen to music everyday and watch films. It was interesting topics. Only issue is he is a tough grader. Would take him for pass/no pass, he ruined my GPA
Great prof. Love his lectures.

TWS was a great class. It's a bit tough to take notes in his class, tbh, because he gives a lot of context and background info about the books. If you are curious about Africa/African lit, I would really recommend hiss class. It's basically a lit class, so of course there's going to be many books to read. But they're all great books.

Probably the most difficult TWS class I've taken. Required to read 7 books. 2 essays, 1 midterm, final. Don't fall behind in reading, otherwise, the midterm is fair. It's actually a class you'd have to put work in, so definitely don't think it's an easy A.

He is a good teacher who tries to dig deep into the material. If you pay attention during the lectures, you barely have to study for this class. The exams are similar to the practice midterms / finals.

He is intelligent. I have to admit that he is not a good teacher because he is too clever to understand what we are thinking about; however, he is such a good person, and his tests are so easy that if you do the practice exam, you'll be able to get a full score. Take him, he is great!
gg ez

To call Professor Petkov awful would be an understatement. Although it's clear that he knows his stuff inside out, he simply isn't very good at teaching. Explains simple concepts in a way that makes you doubt the things that you already are familiar with. Try to avoid him unless you are very well acquainted with the course material.

not the best at explaining 20d topics. could have connected them to math 18 topics for the ppl that had taken it. At first I thought i wasn't going to learn anything from him, however the more I went to lecture, the more I understood his style and the more I learned. Heavy accent. Only cheat sheet on final. used pdf once or twice. very little hw

He's a good lecturer with a unique sense of humor, but he makes quite a few arithmetic mistakes so it's easy to get lost if you zone out. His homework (eHomework instead of webassign) will drive you crazy. His midterms and final take the whole 50 min/3 hours because you really have to figure out what the question is asking, so they're a bit tricky.

My math experience for 20B (with quarfoot) and 20C (with tesler) was pretty subpar, especially for 20c. however, 20d with allen is super great!! he is very explicit about what will be tested on, and as long as you take good notes and do the homework, you'll do well in the class!
Great professor. Explains things well, gives a lot of extra credit, and he's a great guy in general. You'll want to be in lecture.

Grant Allen is super chill and he gives out tons of extra credit. We received 5% on our final grade for attending lecture and we were also able to replace our lowest midterm score with a 100% if we completed 100 problems from the textbook. He gives you lots of opportunities to improve your grade, but his tests can be confusing, but overall fair.

Engaging professor and is funny in an awkward way. Homework is a little misleading so don't be fooled into thinking the midterms will be straighforward. The hardest thing about the midterms/final was figuring out what the question wanted to do, so you really have to understand lecture. Aside from that, he allows extra credit to make up for failure.

She was okay, too intense for an introduction course. What helped me a lot in the course were the tutors, they were really helpful during the labs. I would take her again because she was fair on her quizzes. I just would watch out on getting on her bad side.

extremely condescending and repeatedly ridiculed students in class for asking questions. Labs and homeworks are ridiculously challenging and do not prepare you properly for the midterm and final. However, one positive is she does tell you exactly whats going to be on the quizzes and provides a study guide that prepares you well for exams.

Terrible. How could UCSD hire someone that does not respect every single one of their students? I'm noticing a trend within the CSE professors mindsets; Only help and acknowledge the 'A' students, everyone else is not smart enough to excel in CSE. Her recent scandal describes her personality perfectly. Search her on google to read about the scandal

First, look at the tags of this particular review. Now, think of the opposite of these tags. That is what Professor Marx represents. She is not hilarious, not caring, and does not give good feedback. Try asking a question in class, and you will earn yourself some public humiliation. Also, materials in the lectures do not match up with the labs.

at the beginning of the quarter i didnt think she was too bad. as time passed, the class became harder. i didnt know how to implement the material, and failed the midterm because of a stupid crossword puzzle? she would tell you one thing would be on the test/quizzes, and pull some minute detail from weeks ago that WASN'T on the review guide

Absolutely no skipping class, and If you take good notes you should try this. the prof does have some accent so if you cannot understand her in the first few classes just drop it. But after all she has good exams, if you did all of them prepared you'll be good.

Mediocre lectures. She tends to mumble and has a slight accent but it wasn't too bad. You can tell that she really enjoys what she teaches if that counts for anything. Non-mandatory lectures but you should go bc it makes the midterms easier. Definitely go to discussion. Only 3 midterms, no final. Everything is just memorization.

My TA  saved this class, the prof was horrible, couldn't understand what she was saying. She was irresponsible, not well organized and she often just rambling around unrelated materials. She talked about her political standpoint in class and she was like " yeah, I'm right, that's the only truth" which was super offensive to some of the students.

She goes off an a tangent every lecture. Doesn't post slides or does podcasts, so you either have to go to lecture/section to get the info you need. Luckily my TA gave us what we needed to know for the midterms. Only 3 midterms, attendance is 5% of your grade. I skipped 5 lectures and got 100 on the China midterm. She's hard to understand at times.

Very friendly and approachable guy, is open to different ideas for projects / assignments, but lectures are pretty meh and I don't think half of the class was able to understand him well. (Even given he's the creator of Pd, and the class was essentially all about it.)

You know the professor knows his stuff when he's the one that is the creator of the program that you're learning. Prof. Puckette is really helpful and keeps his lectures informative. Definitely recommend his class for all Music/ICAM majors.
Not a good teacher, but a great guy!

He is not a great lecturer.  He starts explaining one thing and quickly gets distracted by something else and never explains anything wholly.  Also, lecture is pointless because he posts all of the videos of lecture online, alongside all of the PD patches.  The way to survive this class is to scan through the lectures and get help from the TAs.

He is a genius but isn't good at explaining things to students. Hope that you get good TAs to help you w/the homework assignments, book is a must. This class isn't one you want to take for a GE, it's catered towards people  w/a strong interest in the physics behind music and it helps if you're a science major. We had no exams in this class!

Day 1 no self introduction whatsoever and starts class 10 min early. The class was essentially a beginner course to using Adobe CC but her lectures on Mars were completely irrelevant and boring, probably irrelevant for an astronomy class too. She also talks in a heavy accent and don't seem proficient enough in English to be teaching.
Very tough class but makes you think outside of the box about film and art

The class in only difficult as you compress a 10 week course into 5 weeks. Other than that, Alex does an amazing job of explaining physic. This course made me like learning about physics. He takes his time to really teach you all the possibilities of one single term or formula. I am glad UCSD finally got a good professor. 10/10 would recommend.

definitely a cool dude. i always tell people that i came out of the class actually understanding physics which is such an unprecedented thing for me. Just go to office hours, learn from your mistakes, and you'll do well. Take it for the incredibly approachable, passionate professor, stay for the puns and the t-shirt/cargo shorts/flip flops combo.

One of the best professors I have had at UCSD so far. He genuinely cares about every student and makes an effort to learn everyones names. So friendly and encourages everyone to ask their questions. He's INCREDIBLE at explaining difficult concepts. Bonus: lectures are never boring and getting to see him in person is incentive to come to class!

Alex is a true gem at UCSD. He has such a passion for teaching and is the most patient professor ever. He genuinely wants you to speak up if you don't understand and will make sure you 100% get it before moving on. He's way more available for questions than he should be, and is the most friendly guy ever. Also well deserving of the hotness pepper..

I took him for SS1 dreading to having to take physics again after dropping in spring quarter., but it was actually nice. He did his best to make physics painless. His quizzes and tests were fair and he was really helpful outside of lectures. Wish he taught more classes. I thought I would've done terrible, but he's so encouraging! Love this guy!

This was his first time teaching at UCSD and I must say he did a fantastic job. He had a clear grading criteria and he definitely tries his best to help out his students and is extremely approachable. He also wants his students to succeed, so he gives A LOT of opportunities for extra credit. Definitely recommend!
Actually she's amazing.
Omh I love her!! She is so sweet and a great professor! The class is fairly easy, just pay attention in class. Take her class while you can! :D

What are previous posters talking about? She curved SP09 2 pts(88%=90%). Entertaining & easy lectures & you HAVE to go to ALL of them. Posts partial slides w/ no way to guess how to fill in the blanks. Exams harder than they seem; references to jokes in the class I didn't get. EC diagnosing case studies a fun learning tool. Not easy A but not hard.
final exam was hard. a lot of the questions on the exam seemed like it wasn't covered in lecture.
hard class
Best professor I've ever had. He loves his students and will make sure everyone is doing well even emotionally. He has great stories to tell and his lectures are very interesting and dynamic

This class requires a lot of reading as every class consists of in group discussions based off of the assigned reading; however, the discussions are always engaging and so useful. Professor Zarate himself is so caring of his students and his passion and knowledge in his field is transparent. He is genuinely such a great guy. Take him if you can!

Professor Zarate is very passionate about what he teaches. He is a fairly new instructor but does a great job teaching the material. Mostly all the classes consist of little lecture and mainly discussions in groups about the readings. He has such a great personality and I truly enjoy attending his class. I will take him again given the opportunity!

Professor Zarate was one of my absolute favorite professors at UCSD. The class I took with him was required for the CGS major, but I would take a class in the future with him even if it were just a filler. He expects a lot from his students, and the classes are ALL discussion based, so if you don't read and come to class you won't do well.

A caring professor with a new style. His aim was to teach us practical tools for future stats/COGS courses. However there is a lot of (tedious) work, I'd compare it to CSE classes. Quizzes/test every week with a group PA due every two weeks and a lot of google forms every day. He will change the class format, but I learned a lot despite struggling.

From the beginning of the course until end the professor was unorganized. She used Acadly for attendance/assignments/quizzes, & as a way to make announcements. However, she never fully got the hang of it. She posted readings late as well. It is now 1 week after grades are due and shes yet to post them, and fails to respond to emails.

He's an OK guy. However, exams are NO JOKE. The class consists of one midterm, and one final. Nothing else. No extra credit. No lecture slides used. No podcasts. Just go to lecture, do ALL of the readings and you'll do fine. There's a curve at the end.

the FUNNIEST professor I've ever had. Attending lectures is a must, most q's on exams are taken from lecture. He really knows his stuff and is brilliant! His lectures really hold your attention and teach you alot. but his tests were unnecessarily hard. the good news is he curves tremendously, so a C could really be a B. Would 10/10 take him again.

(Review based on SXTH1: First Year Experience) Christenfeld makes this trivial class a true learning experience. He is learned, passionate, engaging, and funny. He promotes students to think deeply about social issues and college life. He cared about what students think and enjoyed discussing with students during and after lectures.

I love this professor! I will take a class with Dr. Christenfeld ANY day! He's hilarious and makes the class more of a discussion than a lecture. I've taken both a lecture and seminar style class from him and they were both classes I looked forward to all quarter. Do not be fooled- his tests are hard and the questions are long!

I took this over summer. A 3-hr class was kind of long but at least he was pretty funny so I didn't fall asleep. It was more like a discussion class and I never took notes because there's no right or wrong. Your grade is based on attendance, discussion, a 3-question final. Questions on final were relevant to discussion and were common sense stuff.

Easy professor to take for an A and very encouraging towards students. Homework every week that includes reading essays, novels, watching movies, and writing a short paragraph on each of them. There is a late-term exam and take-home essay for final.

Professor Heinrich is one of the Easiest professor I had at UC San Diego! He is really generous about extra credit, 10 points for submitting the final paper earlier, and 5points for final exam. The only thing is that we are required to write weekly reports, 400 words each. If you have decent writing skills, you will Ace this class!

Ari (he goes by Ari) is such an amazing professor.  He has amazing insight on the importance of translations, has done translations himself (I think his specialty is in Chinese lit), and his feedback is valuable and thought-provoking. It's very easy to just go up to him and ask "Hey Ari, what do you think about this?"

Professor Heinrich is a very kind professor who explains her material very articulately during her lectures. The readings are sometimes dry but on the plus side, you'd only have to take one exam. For the exam, the Professor provides the class with a very extensive study guide so there is no excuse for failing.

Professor is very nice, knows her stuff. Covers a lot of material, but the material and readings are interesting. assignments every week and one presentation. Thought it was as easy A since I got full points for weekly assignments, but when we got our quarter grades it was a little shocking. Hard grader? Maybe just a little harder than I thought.

She makes class unnecessarily difficult. My advice, take someone else if you cant put a LOT of time into this class. She will purposely try to call people out by using her roster that she has with your picture and name on it. The group project is graded hard and can possibly lower your grade at the end of the quarter, which sucks.

Professor Marquez is a really good lecturer but she grades the final project (group presentation + paper) pretty harshly. The midterm and the final were pretty easy and there are clicker questions every lecture based off of reading and previous lectures. Really enjoyed the material, but wish she graded the project a bit easier.

Professor Marquez gives clear lectures and is willing to explain things further if you ask. Her midterm was pretty easy, but there is a project (presentation + paper) due week 10 AND a final exam. She grades the project very hard but gives extra credit on the exams.

The first year, the avg grade pt she gave was 3.58, which I guess was too high so she followed that up with a 2.52 (see CAPE). She seemed nice in OHs or just talking one-to-one, but she was also pretty anal and snapped at ppl for using phones (did she think we were in high school still?). I think she made the course harder than it needed to be.
Overly strict and inflexible, unapproachable, unkind.

Cool teacher. Soft spoken, really nice guy, and randomly funny at times.  Classes are very interesting, lectures are easy to follow and the readings were informative.  No busy work.  Read the books, don't miss too many lectures and youll be alright.
Showing up is unnecessary. The essay topics are taken completely from the books.

Midterm = 40%, Final = 60% and optional weekly hour discussions = 5% Extra Credit. Easy 5 points if you skim a bit and put in your two cents during the discussions. Tomoyuki the TA is a very caring individual who will help you on the essays. Easy A if you do all the above.

I think Fujitani is an akward lecturer with overwhelming powerpoint slides...but if you actually sit and listen to what he is saying, you'd be blown away.  He feels deeply about his topic matter and it is inspirational.  Plus, he is really nice and funny if you talk to him after class.

Seemed to be disconnect between lecture (which were confusing) and labs (which were easy). Pretty good lecturer overall. Class is 70% lab, 30% final. Final was fairly simple (simple enough that if you get 100% on labs, you only need 67% to get an A-). Class was not podcasted so attendance is recommended (slides are provided nonetheless).

Easy professor, almost 60% students get A in this class. However, you will learn NOTHING if you only take his lectures. If you really want to learn something, you need to learn by yourself. So if you just want to find an easy A class and don't want to learn deep in a topic, this professor is fine, but if you really want to learn, DO NOT take him.

It was his first time teaching this class but I thought he did a good job. The midterm and final exams were pretty straightforwards, but the projects were pretty tough (expected). Having said that, the class suffered for a SERIOUS shortage of help, especially on Piazza. As of writing this, only 31% of questions received instructors' responses. SAD!
I'd like to talk to this guy about money.

Easy class overall, final had a lot of bs questions which were just regurgitating material  without understanding, but still easy if you read over the material. Lectures were very clear and helpful, however he is very inaccessible outside of class and was not very helpful on the discussion forums.  Overall, I'd recommend though

She is a good lecturer, but she makes the exams pretty long. For the midterm, she made 60 Qs for a 50 min class, which was a bit long to complete on time. For the final, she made 100 Qs, which was doable for 3 hrs. The class has 1 midterm and a cumulative final, all of which are multiple choices. She also seems very enthusiastic about teaching.

Her midterm average was in the C range and then she proudly boasted about how that was what she was expecting out of us. Not two seconds passed before she went on to base her lecture around how were where whinny children. Had I known how antagonistic her grading style would have been, I never would have taken her class.

Take her! She is a real knowledgable and very funny person. You can tell she tries to get the class to like her and she succeeds for sure. I enjoyed this summer session with her and I hope I can take her again for another class. The tests are fair and everything is from her lectures so go to class!

This professor came to our school and expected us to learn "everything" about biopsychology in one month.  For a one month class it's very important to grade on the basis concepts and provide clear explanations on what should be studied for the exam.  When we asked her what to study, she said "everything, and everything was on the test.  Worse yet!

She is amazing. Gives great explanations for the material and really knows her stuff. Funny, nice and gives fair tests that don't try and trick u. Only reason I gave her a 3 for difficulty was cause I took it during summer so reading about 12 or so chapters from the text was a lot but simple enough if u didn't wait for the last min. Great prof!

This guy is probably the only man I've ever met that can explain mathematics in a clear and concise manner. His exams were hard, but there was no tricky stuff or curve balls. If he ever taught here again I would take his class again in a heartbeat. I'm terribad at math and I still got a B in the class.

Amazing professor. In fact, the only professor that has impressed me so much that I chose to come here and give a rating. Caring, funny, passionate, and enthusiastic. Both a great lecturer and a wonderful person. It is a pleasure to have been taught by him! I usually despise math yet Szypowski is the one professor that made me enjoy Math 20 series.

The BEST math prof I have taken at UCSD by far. Very clear lecturer and always trying to do his best to make us understand the material. His test are an actual representation of what the homework/practice exams are, not like other profs that throw you something you have never seen before but that uses the concepts you know. Take him if you can!!!!!

CHOOSE HIM IF YOU CAN!!!!!! HE IS AMAZING!!!! He explains everything so well that I dont even need to read the textbook. His HW is short and his tests are very fair. He is funny and he generally cares about students! Choose him and you wont regret!

Likable, makes jokes, explains content clearly . Exams are very fair, based on in-class examples and HW. HW is not overly long (thank you, Szypowski). Lectures are conducive to good note-taking. I wish he were staying at UCSD!

he seemed disorganized and didnt have mastery of the material. low incentives to attend lectures because exams were entirely based on the textbook. It was his first quarter teaching here so Im gonna give him the benefit of the doubt. He does take feed back well and would bring in guest speakers that were informational. Also offered extra credit.

Professor Quest is so far one of my favorite professors in UCSD. He is really respected. His lecture is so interesting and clear. As long as you follow him, its easy to understand, and he knows a lot of fun facts. The mid and final are similar to the old exams. As long as you do all of them, you will get an easy A.
Study the materials before his lecture, you can get an A.

Professor Quest is really respected by students. He's always willing to help you, either in class or during office hours. Also he explain things very clear. One of the best professors in ECE, don't hesitate to take his class.

The professor shows great concern to how students understand his materials. Exams are predictable and are very similar (nearly exactly the same) to the sample exam. 37.5%two midterms, 37.5%final and 25%labs. Labs are hard for this course.

Professor Quest is very well respected; however, his lectures seem redundant.  However, he is clear about what is to be expected on exams.  I basically learned all the material on my own weeks before the final and got an A- in the class.  Do every single practice exam, and you will be fine. Old discussion notes from 2008 are very helpful as well.

Took Anth 3 over Spring quarter and can't recommend Professor Levy enough. The class consists of clicker quizzes each lecture, a midterm and final. Midterm and final consisted entirely from lecture and reading content and you're told exactly what is expected. Overall an enjoyable class with some interesting lecture topics and guest speakers.

I highly suggest taking a class from him. As far as teaching goes he's only ok, but he is pretty well regarded in his field so you will get to hear a lot about the research he is doing! Also pretty easy, I don't think he wants this class to be hard, our midterm was just a completion thing and he give EC
Take only if you are interested in the material. He may seem goofy but he is very experienced.

Extremely knowledgeable about subject and one of the leading archaeologists in this field. The grade is heavily based on the research paper. Fair/easy grader. Tests are straightforward and based on textbook reading. He puts his PowerPoint slides online.

Professor Levy is an extremely fair grader. His expectations are outlined on the course syllabi and he grades based on those requirements. Although the work load may seem overwhelming, it is extremely beneficial for those students pursuing archaeology. He is also more than willing to help those students  applying to graduate programs.

Fake as they come. She is one of those Dr. professors who thinks she's above everyone else, huge superiority complex. She turned a blind eye to her TAs' sloppy grading. For the most part we had guest lecturers so she really does not teach the course. Would not recommend.

She's absolutely wonderful and such a kind person. I enjoyed her class-the time flies. I recommend talking to her before/after lecture or during office hours for some really beneficial advice. I regret not having done that much. Overall, a true gem for the public health department at UCSD!

Dr. Johnson's lectures are organized in a way that reflects on assigned readings. She also has a different guest lecturer every class meeting which makes the course very valuable and interesting. She's approachable and gives great advice for anyone interested in this field of study.

I'm currently enrolled in a MPH program because of her and this class. Dr. Johnson is very inspirational and approachable. Lectures are interesting and different from others in a good way if you're into learning about diseases and that kind of stuff. Try to put the material in your own way of understanding when studying and you'll do fine.

As mentioned from the previous posts, Dr. Johnson is very kind and approachable. Tests are pretty straightforward, just do the assigned reading. She goes over interesting topics during lecture. Would have gone to class more often but the fact that it was at 8am was no bueno.

Pretty passive aggressive and if you don't participate she'll threaten tests and pop quizzes. That said, she gives extra credit opportunities and curves tests. I did not enjoy her class because she tries to be friendly, but then randomly snaps and gets pissy.. She posts her slides, but attendance and participation are non-negotiable. She's OKAY.

Good prof, very friendly, talks a lot. Lectures are pretty heavy but she makes sure participation is a huge part of your class experience so make sure you speak up. Lots of group assignments, which I'm not particularly fond of, but it's a Rady management class so it's to be expected. Pretty good prof and her TA was really clear and nice.

He's average and he's friendly enough. Lots of group projects. Make sure you participate VERY VERY often or you'll lose points. Overall, he's okay and his guest speakers are always cool and work at big corporations or notable companies so you'll get a chance to talk with them.

Makes her class accessible to many learning styles with podcasts, optional clicker grading, open discussion, and short online homeworks that reinforce concepts. It's obvious that she cares & wants students to succeed, and she designs her class around learning. Sit in front and she'll help you with the clicker questions, it's worth it to show up!

Professor Antonovics is amazing. She explains concepts really well, is patient with the students, has podcasts and lecture slides, has alternative grading options(you can skip class and just watch the podcast) and gives loads of practice tests. She's brilliant and you won't regret taking her,
One of the best professors I've ever met at UCSD. Very clear lectures. She makes a lot of effort to make the material easy to understand. You'll never regret taking her Econ 1.

Professor Antonovics is very smart and energetic professor who puts a lot of passion into the work that she does. She's very engaging and although the material itself is hard, she provides the right resources and presentation of content to perform well on her assessments. Her lectures are very concise and provide lots of examples to take good notes

Kate is a very nice and caring professor. She does her best to explain things and are always prepared to answer questions. Her tests are very straightforward and similar to lecture materials. However, if you're careless and unclear with your materials, you'll perform poorly on your exams as they're often small number of questions (each worth a lot)

This is the first and only rate my professor comment that Im giving through out my entire undergrad studies and Im giving it to him because he is AMAZING. He is passionate, very clear. Tests are not hard if you review examples in the notes and hw problems. If I took his class a year before, I might switch to pure math. Take him at all costs!

Greatest prof i have ever taken so far. Explains everything clear with great passion. You could feel his passion of math and that would influence you as well. Math 109 turns out to be the most interesting math course I have ever taken. Exams are not easy, but straightforward if you pay attention during lectures. Office hours are helpful as well.

He is a good professor, but he teaches too fast. His midterms and final are also difficult. Yes,whenever he uses symbols on the exams that were not used in class, he explains what they mean on the exam days. However, it's quite unfair to do that because that could throw the students off. Compared to the homework & midterms, the final was tough.
He is the best professor I took this quarter.  Take him if you could.  Test materials are all on the lecture notes.  Very straight forward.  I like his teaching style a lot.
The concepts are very difficult to grasp. He is very good at explaining the concepts, but the class is still very hard.

He is a respected professor. He cares about students and gives inspirational speeches. He is also super intelligent, which he doesn't need any notes when he is lecturing. However, I found his class hard to follow because he talks pretty fast... it would be better if he explained more of the examples than the concepts
He has my whole heart <3 #keepsnellamninUCSD
Snellman is great at explaining and his tests are very straightforward. I would definitely recommend him especially compared to the other math professors at UCSD. He is great!!

seriously my favorite math teacher/professor. his lectures are coherent and he makes the concepts very simple and easy to understand. this is saying a lot, but I would actually retake the 20 series if it meant learning from him.
