Talks sort of fast in lectures and doesn't use podcasting, but honestly, he's one of the best professors I've ever had in the math department (and at the school as a whole). He does a great job of breaking down concepts to be easier to understand, so if he's teaching any other 20 series course, take his class! You won't regret it.

Westman is an okay professor; he likes to crack some small jokes during the lecture. Work on midterm study guide. Our grade consists of midterm (25%), 6-page paper (25%), and a 12-page final essay (50%). The final was sent out a week before the day of final, and it's take-home final. Difficult unless you're constantly reading material.
He was very helpful and kind.

Westman was not bad compared to all the other profs. You don't really need to take detailed notes, just listen and jot down important things. The final wasn't a take home essay like other CAT profs, you had to go and write an in lecture essay, it wasn't bad if you listened in class. I think there were 2 (3?) essays and a final. Not too bad/ hard.

Professor Westman is a pretty cool teacher. He is very heavy on lectures, and skipping class will make completing papers a bit difficult. Each lecture is long and has a lot of content, and can be quite boring at times. However, getting through the lectures will pay off in the end when you have to write essays for the final.
The workload of his class is way less than other CAT1 professor's. His nice, respected. As a history department professor, he was really present at some historical events!

Professor Steenbergen is seriously one of the kindest professors I have encountered at UCSD. Really cares about the students and the material is interesting. The course is super easy but you learn A LOT! There is no final or midterm, but there are a few write ups you need to complete, very easy. Take this if you want to go into education!

Easy class. 5 points for writing a reflection at the end of every lecture. 25 points for each "Investigative Assignment" (there's 4 total) that are 3-4 pages, but really easy to write. I would often start them 2 hours before the deadline and receive the 25 points. Then there's the final paper, which isn't too bad. Show up and you'll do just fine.

Definitely one of my favorite professors - makes me wish I wasn't graduating so I could take another class with her. Lectures are detailed and clear so you don't need the book. Slides are informative enough to stand on their own, but they can still be supplemented by examples discussed in lecture. I loved this class thanks to Professor Gasperi.
Shes great

Professor Gasperi encouraged me to think. The subject of intelligence is one that everyone thinks they understand. With this class, Professor Gasperi gave us tools to understand the topics in intelligence today and in the future.

Professor Gasperi is by far the best professor I have had at UCSD. Her lectures are easy to follow, her tests are based on lecture, and she is just an overall amazing human being. You can tell she is passionate about what she teaches, and she truly wants every student to succeed. She is an incredible asset to the UCSD psychology department.

Professor Gasperi is a brilliant, entertaining, and inspiring professor.  She was able to teach a complex and highly controversial subject in a way that was easily accessible, intellectually honest, and culturally sensitive.  She's also very easy to talk to outside of class.  I would highly recommend her for this class and any others.
Hes a great professor who explains things really clearly. Coding assignments are about as complicated or slightly less than other cs classes. Midterm was great!

He's okay. I prefer well organized top down approach but his lecture he's really more of talking about stuff with bottoms up approach then deducing it to solution at high level stuff. For beginners, I wouldn't recommend him. I'm frustrated.

He does a really good job explaining, is super helpful if you go to his office hours, and does a good job making the class very informative. His exams are kind of tough though, so go to class if you want to do well.

Fantastic professor!!! Against recommendations, I took this class with no programming experience whatsoever and ended up with a B+. This is easily the hardest class I've ever taken, but I learned so much from it and I would take it again in a heartbeat. If you have the option, take him!!!
Highly helpful. He will answer all questions on piazza. However, be prepared to dedicate a fair amount time on programming and reading if you are a beginner in computer science.

Although the materials Prof. Aamari gave are really hard, his notes are helpful and his practice exams are also indicative. Overall, I like this professor, and I have learned a lot! By the way, the homework are tough.

He's a great professor! I really loved this class. He does give a lot of homework, but I found it manageable. He obviously cares about how his students do in his class. I would definitely take him again.

LECTURES ARE SUPER DENSE. but i really appreciated it being organized and easy to follow on PPT. He was very enjoyable and always had savage jokes and replies on piazza. Class is work intensive with labs and hw due every week but doable and prepares you well for exams. read the book for better explanations when u get confused. that really helped

i've never taken AP Stats, or any stats class at all so this was harder for me to learn. He talks super fast during the slides which makes it kinda hard to take notes in lecture, but he does post every powerpoint beforehand. He's not terrible but I wouldn't say he's 10/10 either.

Oh my goodness, I love this class. I'm not even done yet but I absolutely love him. If he taught all the math classes I'd need for a math minor, I'd do a math minor. He's super nice, I love his lectures, and he's really cute. Plus he has a nice accent. Very easy to pay attention in that class. I honestly wish we had more classes per week!!!

Sinay's center-liberal attitudes give off an arrogant and self-serving vibe. Many of her numerous readings are either twenty page ramblings on an idea you could summarize in a sentence or are some New York Times opinion piece presented as absolute truth. Loved the course and guest lecturers, but she's really holding the course back.

Error- by textbook-barely cracked it open I mean there is no official textbook so I got confused. There are several books you need to read and articles as well. These will be on the midterm. Then there are projects and essays. All are engaging and interesting though. The discussions are the best part though!!! I miss them...

I am so glad I took this class! It is a real treat at UCSD. Signing up for this class was one of the best decisions I ever made. The small class size allows your voice to really be heard and you get to discuss so many amazing topics. I made friends I wouldn't have made otherwise. Everything we did was eye opening and interesting. LOVED THIS CLASS!

TMC15 is one of the best classes that I have taken at UCSD so far. The small class size and regular guest speakers was a huge plus for me. Grades are based off of an in class midterm, final paper, and group project. True, there are a lot of readings, but getting the audiobook versions of the assignments definitely helps save time.

TMC 15 is a great class and one every student should take. Prof. Sinay encourages you to think beyond the classroom and how to apply what you're learning to help others. She was always open to meeting with me and mentoring me on next steps inafter college. She's well connected in SD. Great book list. Do yourself a service and take this class!

He's really tough on proofs and his final is 75% of the grade. But, his office hours are really helpful. Since he knows a lot of many different applications of Numerical PDE, he's also interesting to talk to.
Professor Bank is actually a good lecturer but he is tough on proofs and rigorous treatment of materials. He is far better than rating here, I don't know why his score is so low.
A lifesaver. Best teacher I have ever had.
I had no clue what he was saying from day 1 until the last day, only the TA helped me
He is the worst proffesor I have ever had.  He is in love with proofs, and they make the class very confusing. Avoid this proffesor.

Professor Coulson is pretty boring but I'm pretty sure it had more to do with the course than her. She teaches well though and her grading system is pretty ideal. Midterms that adhere strictly to the subject material and homework that you can work on with TAs (HW is worth like 50% in this class so it's free points)

I don't understand why she insists on teaching us programming and computer science. Cogs 101B was about learning, memory, and attention in the brain. COGS101C is supposed to be the language portion of that same material. She's talking about finite state automata, feedback loops, programming logic, etc. and I wasn't at all prepared for it.

I'd only rate the course to be slightly harder b/c the material is so dry. Yet Coulson is clearly passionate about the subject & tries to make it as interactive as possible, mainly thru HW. While lots of HW might seem bad, it helps a lot to really immerse into the subject & helps loads for the final. She's also incredibly friendly & understanding!

2nd worst class i've ever taken. incredibly dull. she lectures too fast to take notes. no study guide, basically just tells you to study every lecture up to the exam. gives contradictory information as the TA. asks general questions then marks you down for not giving the specific response she wanted. DO NOT TAKE HER UNLESS YOU ABSOLUTELY HAVE TO!!!

Very boring. TA is a harsh grader. No partial credit so if you get one small detail wrong, the whole problem will be wrong. She should give TA a grading guide since what she says is different than what the TA says

Todd is one of the best professors I've had at UCSD. He's super passionate about what he teaches and he's always organized. On top of that, he's just a fun guy to be around because he's constantly happy and joking. I think he mentioned at some point that this was his last quarter at the school though :(

If you ever have the chance to take a class with Todd, don't miss out. He keeps his lectures interesting and easy for beginners to keep up. He knows the material super well and is always willing to help out if you're having trouble.

He is a very enthusiastic character and thoroughly explains the topics, which makes it relatively easy for a beginner. While it is tempting to skip the classes because it's super easy, he does have several pop quizzes.
He's a nice and enthusiastic teacher. Participation takes 20% of total grade. The final project on the last day of lecture was so sweet. Expecting for an A or A-. I'm taking his class next quarter.

He was under the staff category but I am so glad I got him! He has a lot of teaching experience so he's amazing at teaching and his lectures are very helpful, this is coming from a student that hasn't touched an instrument in her life. There isn't a lot of  homework and the midterm was reasonable, plus we got to practice before hand with the hw.

Hes ok. He gives a midterm, final paper and final. Dont expect to get a graded paper back because he never did in our class. His lectures are long. Only gave one break in a 4 hour class. Make sure you participate in class or else it will be boring.

Professor Khalil has been phenomenal all semester! I took his on-line course - It has been great learning about music and cultures from all over the world. His lectures are extremely interesting and truly opened up my mind to music, instruments, and other cultures. Highly recommend this course!
He is simply amazing. His lectures really give you new views on music from different cultures. He is also experienced in almost everything he teaches. He is a fun and interesting Professor.

Dr. Khalil is amazing! I really loved his class; I learnt so much from him! If you enjoy music, then this class is very enjoyable. He focuses more on the different instruments of the diferent regions; he even brings the real instruments and performs. His tests are easy and straightforward. The final paper was also very easy to do. It was truly an e

We didn't use a textbook, but there were assigned readings that I didn't do, but I did perfectly fine in the class. There was one midterm, one final paper and one final. The final's just like the midterm, and its non-comprehensive. If you attend lecture and take good notes, there isn't much you need to study for. Alex is cool and really easy!
Dr. Mebane is a really great lecturer. You can tell she really cares about the material and her students learning it. She is always very prepared.
Dr. Mebane is really wonderful! She is young but very knowledgeable, super chill and fun class. She is very patient and kind. Quizzes and exams are very predictable and she grades fairly leniently

Honestly, she is the best. Gives homework due every lecture, but only checks to see if it's done. It's fun to read with her, she makes the test interesting. She goes over grammar quick and swift. A great teacher that truly cares about her students. 15/10

Dr. Mebane. Julia. My girl. I hope you're reading this, because you deserve to know that I come to your class smiling every day because it's clear that you care about how much your students are learning and that they enjoy the material. Latin is a hard language, but the way you break it down makes it so manageable and enjoyable. TAKE HER CLASS YALL

Mebane is one the rare professors that actually cares about her students. She'll dedicated to her students, but this doesn't mean her class is easy. Don't skip class, participate during lectures and you'll be fine. I definitely recommend her and will be taking more of her classes.

I really enjoyed this class. I hated the material, but prof Steck made it do-able to be able to maintain an A throughout the semester. Although i think its gonna drop after the final. Prof steck is always available to help and offers plenty of lab office hours to ensure students dont fall behind. She always attempts to teach material in an easy way

Professor Morgan is great! He is very funny, kind hearted and knowledgeable. That being said, this was one of the hardest classes I have ever taken in my entire college career! Only take this class if you're ready to read up to 8-10 books for the quarter, take pop quizzes on each, and do a cross comparison between four different books at a time.

He is very straightforward and easy to understand when explaining topics. His quizzes are very doable with a little bit of studying. Unlike other physics professors, you get to make your own cheatsheets and ask TAs for formulas on the quizzes. Also, he is very approachable and willing to clarify points in his lecture if you ask him one on one.

He's such a nice professor. Take any class you can with him.  He's really fair with grading (even bumped up people's grades without asking because averages were a bit lower than expected).  He is a genius and is not arrogant at all!  No question is dumb to him - he will help you out.  I would highly recommend.

4 quizzes (60%) and 1 final (40%). Pros: Clear and informative lecture slides, nice accent, practice exams are SUPER representative of actual exams, don't need to read textbook, and simplifies material well. Cons: Sometimes reads off the slides, a little fast lecturer, and sometimes doesn't answer questions well. Overall, I recommend him.

Concepts in lectures can be confusing sometimes, but he is not going to test you on the hard part. Homework problems are harder than the actual quizzes, but practice quizzes are very representative. Review all the practice quizzes and quizzes before taking the final!!!! He may simply copy and paste the exact same problems on the final.
Lectures are super clear and helpful and makes physics easier to be understood. Tests are extremely fair. His cool accent and punny jokes are a plus

I really like her & what she teaches. Shes just an extremely difficult grader. Ive never received anything below an A since I began writing essays back in 6th grade. Ive taken 2 Ap English in highschool so Im very familiar with what is being taught. She does not hesitate to give you Cs and Ds

Professor Sanchez is a very passionate teacher. Lectures did not really enhance my understanding of the course readings . Lectures were mostly summary of the readings and she asked the class what they thought to discuss analysis. Sometimes seemed like we were told what to think rather than convinced because we only addressed one side of DOC issues.
She's the most inspirations professor I've had. She allows students to be engaged with the material and encourages people to share our stories.

She's a good professor, as long as you do your readings you should be fine. Make use of her office hours though bc her powerpoints go by fast since she tries to cover as much material as possible. She is really passionate and I would definitely take her again.

Honestly I got more out of googling the questions I had about the HW than I did attending lectures. You can see that she's trying, but she skims over stuff and doesnt really go into details when we do iClicker questions and 3/5 of the class gets it wrong.

Prof Asaro is amazing! She goes over everything as many times as you ask in order for the you to understand the material. Her tests and quizzes are very fair and overall was a very fun class that I looked forward to. It is a language class so you will need to memorize vocab and conjugations, but if you keep on top of it you'll be fine!
She really cares about students. You do a lot of reading in this class, but not an insane amount. 2 5pg essays, 2 quizzes, 2 projects and final make up your grade. Would def recommend.
very helpful, wants you to do well. Recommend taking
Appreciate taking her course. She genuinely works to help her students do well in the course. There's a lot of reading and class discussion is mandatory so I suggest reading.

Dr. Asaro is a very intellectual and caring professor. She is available outside of class and wants to help you learn. She has a lot of extra credit opportunities which is really nice! Homework, 2 quizzes, 2 tests, 2 papers and 2 presentations. Pretty clear and solid class. Loved it!

Weekly assignments with partners (never know your grade on it). I was worried I was doing poorly because we never got a grade, but I took the time to write this review so you don't worry. He gives As to everyone who puts the effort in. Don't bs your assignments. Lectures were interesting but he doesn't explain much about terms.

My 5th year in college..the EASIESTTT bio class. EZ 150% A. Just do hw, and attendance. you get A. No mt, no final, no reading, no need to pay attention, no need to study. sorry Newsam, but it's the easiest class of my life. If you want to pay attention, go head and you will get A+. If you want to do something else and not pay attention you get A.
no final, no midterm. Just go to class everyday and do the homework then you get an A. Homework is not even graded so just doing your homework will get you an A
unorganized assignment, project and lecture. You may learn many fancy words in his course but actually he cannot explain any of them clearly. Do not take his course.

Kesden does truely care for his students, but that doesn't make up for the fact that he's horrible at teaching. Lecture is like an open forum, u ask and he goes on a tangent. HW are taken from other universities, so there's not a 1 to 1 correlation between the two. He doesn't talk about nachos. Start early and and pray the TA can help you :)
doesn't seem to care about students who aren't doing well in the class

Grading for exams and the final project was lenient. Your group is solely responsible for learning how to use Android Studio & version control. In lecture, he'll go over concepts then follow up with life examples. At times he could get off topic but usually he's trying to emphasize certain traits & patterns. Start the project early!

Prof Kesden really cares about his students and he is always willing to help. The grading is very lenient and all the exams/quizzes are very fair. However, the instructions could be somewhat ambiguous, and most students do not like his lecture style. In general, he is a good professor for this class, and if you get a good group, you will be fine.

Very kind but assigned more work than all my other classes combined. Unrealistic work load. Hundreds of pages of reading every week, 2 pg paper response every week, 2 presentations (one is discussion lead but really a 2 hour presentation), one 10 pg paper, one 20 page paper. Dominated my quarter and took away from my learning in other courses.

She is a very caring and elegant professor! JAPN 190 is mainly composed of student-lead discussions so I actually do know much about her lecture style. She is really approachable. Read her comments, they are really helpful.

Hands down she is my favorite professor at UCSD. I also had her for honors in the sociology department. If you don't do well in her classes it's all on you because she cares a lot and is willing to give a lot of time and effort to her students. If you ever get the chance take her!

Very helpful professor. She is approachable and kind outside of the classroom, and has a very relaxed and intelligent demeanor while lecturing. Assignments are easy and flexible (you get to choose between options for the midterm and final, and write a research paper on a topic of your choice).

Horrible at getting info out to students. Guidelines for research paper given out three days before paper due. 5 days given for two final papers to be written. webct not updated.  If this professor actually got the prompts out with at least a week to write the papers, I would recommend her. But since she doesnt, I cant. Made my finals week hell.
Never missed a class, studied, and participated, and still struggled. If you do so-so on 1 test forget it. He offers no extra credit and is a very tough grader.

I enjoyed this class. His lectures are a little long but he posts them before class so it is easy to follow. Gives a lot of short clips, most are funny. Grading consisted of 2 short papers and a group presentation. Very nice and engaging professor.
He simply reads his power points. No point going to class since he posts all of his stuff on his website.

course is comparable to intro to poli sci w/ a media emphasis. prof seems very passionate about his research & course content. the dense readings are a must bc youll write 6-pagers on 3 separate topics every 2-3 weeks and an 8pg final on 4 topics

Really sweet guy. Very clear lecturers. Made it so you don't have to read the textbook (except for homework of course). Strikes a nice balance between teaching background intuition and omitting unnecessary stuff. However, would still recommend going to discussions & OASIS in order to emphasize the important formulas and whatnot.

Great teacher. His lecture's are pretty clear and concise and easy to understand. The exams he gives on 20D are less focused on really long problems or the longest problems in 20d, but more on understanding the concepts. His final was a big challenging since it gave a curveball question, but all his questions from the exams are related to homework.

Gawlik is a wonderful professor who really helped me become more confident in my math abilities. His midterms were pretty hard and were tricky at times, but just makes sure you know how to do all the homework questions he assigns and you should be okay. He is very approachable and always willing to help you -- he's a little shy in front of class.

Wonderful professor to have. Lectures are the perfect mix of background intuition and practical examples. If you watch closely, you'll notice he does a great job omitting unnecessary information. Test questions are reasonable and taken from the course content. You are accountable for knowing what's in the textbook, but you won't have to read it.
Awesome professor. Textbook material itself is pretty hard to understand, but he breaks it down well.
The most attentive and helpful professor I have ever had. I wish he still taught classes at the university but it looks like he moved on to another university.
Camac is the best professor I have had. He shares his business' projects with the class to help with the final project
Excellent final class. Kyle is a pleasure to work beside. He is a consummate analytics pro.
The certificate program is legitimate. Professor Camac was great at providing insights into data mining and how companies utilize in his business. I'd recommend taking his classes.

Excellent program. Knowledgeable professors that helped me hone in on my skills in data mining. Professor Camac is a great teacher. I can see why the university hired him for the final capstone style finish.

Lectures can be boring, but they are useful in understanding what will be on the midterm and final. You can tell he cares about students learning which is always good. The material will seem difficult, but really all you need to do is make sure you have all the equations on your cheat sheet and understand what they mean

His class is horrible !!! His lecture is totally useless and boring, the homework was really difficult, and his midterm has nothing to do with the homework. Unless you are really good at self-taught, please don't take this class with this professor.
Fairly difficult material, but even if you bomb your tests and show up to lectures, office hours, youll get an A-/B+. Very helpful in lecture and OH.

Vibrations course, professor is really cool dude. Hard to understand sometimes, so I stopped going after second week. HW was only 5%, so I never did it. Just studied the day before the exams, about 5-6 hours. Practice midterm is helpful, and some problems on exam are taken straight from the book. Easy to pass, harder to ace.
Also took him for 131a. Awesome guy. Think of him as a russian labardia. Always willing to help students in need. Rumor has it he's the ladies man of the MAE department.

Professor Petkas has a captivating enthusiasm for history! He is a very collected individual who uses precision to convey your interest and ingrain the vast pictures of history. His expertise does not overshadow his virtue. He aims to support the hard work of every one of his students. Come seeking to learn and your grade will follow. Great prof.

Professor Petkas is a fantastic professor. He knows the material from a unique perspective. Show up to class, pay attention, skim the readings, and you'll earn an A. Show him that you're interested. Meet with him outside the classroom. He is a unique individual.

I wanted to update my comment given how she has developed as a professor since I had her last: I love how she is so kind and caring with students, has an open question policy where you can always ask questions- even in a huge lecture hall- and gives extremely clear assignment directions. She makes it really easy to focus on the material at hand.

This class is super boring- one of the most boring classes I've taken thus far. The assignments are easy and the exam wasn't terrible. She's fine but talks on and on and will take up every second of class time talking and talking. If you don't mind a boring class with a friendly teacher, you'll do well, but I wouldn't go out of my way to take her.

This class was extremely boring. I actually stopped going to lecture altogether after the 3rd week. Discussions are necessary to pass. There are only 2 essays and one is the final. Each week we have to read usually 3 articles that are fairly long and write a reading response. You can actually just read one and base your response on that.
The topic she chooses is really interesting.

Prof. Gates is a fantastic professor who really puts effort into her lectures and tries to make the course as student friendly as possible. Assignments were easy while still making you think, and the final was split into eight 250 word essays. Lectures were mostly interesting. Would definitely recommend this CAT class to anyone taking it.

I'm really surprised to read the others reviews. Profe Hidalgo s by far the best teacher I had this year at UCSD. She's nice, understanding, funny and her class is amazing. I got an easy A+ with doing what she was expecting, nothing more. I'd recommend her class on the border (or any of her class) 10/10 !

On the day of the final she locked herself out her office. We had to wait an hour and a half until she got them out and only had 45 minutes to do our final. Throughout the entire quarter we didn't know our grades because she didn't return our papers until the day of the final.

Where the hell does ucsd find these people? She left most of us unprepared for muir 50, we didn't learn much of anything about rhetorical analysis, she's almost degrading to a point, she tries to intimidate, if you don't agree with her she throws a fit or gives you a bad grade even if you can back up your opinion. My god, someone fire her already.
Ditto for everything everyone says. Stay away. Not helpful. This has nothing to do with her being a lesbian, this has everything to do with her being a horrible instructor!

Quite possibly the worst "teacher" ever.  I got an A- but only because I signed up for tutor session with other muir 40 teacher/teaching assistants.  She only talks about her views and if your thesis doesn't align with her own premeditate thesis, then she recommends you "re-think" the purpose of taking this class. She oozes with negativity.

Extremely helpful, respectable professor and he really knows a lot about international policy/relations. 1 midterm, 1 paper and 1 final. Quizzes in the discussions but not too difficult. Very straightforward and he is there to help you if you ask him. He is also a great speaker and his lectures are energetic and interesting! Highly recommend him.

Loved every minute of his class. If you're into IR, please take him! He's actually a prof (at our very highly rated grad school), so VERY qualified. Take advantage of that! Readings are dense, and POLI12 (intro to IR) should be a pre-req to his class tbh. He asks questions and relates the content to the real world a lot. Learned so much!

Smart guy and very interesting material. Pleasure to hear him lecture.I finally started learning about methods people are actually using out in the world to measure and combat poverty. Highly recommend! TA does all grading , though. Midterm was take home and final was in class. He also podcasts so attendance is not mandatory but section is.

Simply amazing. I was very lucky to take his course as undergrad. Class average is usually high not because everyone in the class is nerd, but because Haggard is so good. Interesting readings and not hard homeworks and exams.

GREAT professor, very helpful！！Hard to rate the easiness, because it really depends on the TAs. I got 93 for the final grade but it's only A-. Because A is given to a certain percentage of students in each section and my section seems really intelligent.
Fun lecture, interesting, new perspective, with a unique ability to communicate with each student differently.
Wilder is a very interesting person who seems to know everyone who has started or sold a company that is now very large. He is also very knowledgeable when it comes to entrepreneurial topics.

Wilder is a fascinating professor with extensive knowledge and success in the business world. Class is discussion based and he really likes to highlight and have the students argue opposing views on pressing political and international issues.

I think Dr. Wilder's class is really helpful. He is a successful business man and has traveled a lot, so he has a lot of real life experience. If you get involved in class discussion, ask him questions and you can learn a lot from him. His class is very relaxing because he is such a cool guy; tests are not hard especially if you did the reading.

Professor Wilder is captivating and enthusiastic. He relates real world current issues in with the curriculum. All in all, I learned so much more than I thought I would in International Relations in a jet-packed semester.
Great patients! Great experience
Awesome class
Great Class
Enthusiastic
Great!

Prof P is an amazing lecturer that really know the material. The movies were interesting if you take the time to get into the films. The reading is heavy, but you need it to be prepared for the midterm/ quizzes. Overall a really great class

This professor's actually a lot more concerned with your reaction to the readings than the historical, factual details. As long as you can write well and explain your perspective clearly, there's no reason not to ace the class.

Professors are not simply transmitters of objective knowledge, and there is much that is suspect in Pickowicz's own work.  William Hinton, the greatest American voice on modern China, wrote a massive critique of P's scholarship titled "Through a Glass Darkly" which I would highly recommend reading before the course or alongside P's text.

Rewards you for your hard work, but you will be working hard. Reading is immense, but the exams come straight from it, so you can't slack off! Pickowicz was such a charismatic lecturer, and Miriam was the most amazing TA.

He's a great professor in terms of the dedication he has for his research (which you will get a taste of because you will be reading his books and watching his documentary). The reading is a lot, but they are very fascinating. His quizzes and tests are on the readings, but sometimes the questions are too broad so it's hard to nail it on the spot.

She is a very sweet and kind person, not the type of professor you would be scared to approach. Lectures are posted online and she basically discusses the same things that are in the textbook. There are lots of quizzes and tests, but almost all of them are open notes and online. I highly recommend.

The best professor I have ever had. She truly cares for her students and is flexible when it comes to deadlines. She encourages conversation and her lectures are always interesting, with videos and interactive material. Not to mention she is hilarious. Never have I fallen asleep in her class.

Easy class, nice teacher. A little unprofessional with her lectures, but I'd much rather have that than someone who is monotonic and literally reads off the lecture slides. Very good teacher and cares a lot about her students success. If you want an easy GE, i definitely recommend taking her.
He is a good professor and his office hours are useful

So far the best ECE professor I've had at UCSD. Amazing lecture which prepared me well in the following courses. If you want to get a good grade in his class, besides working your ass off, you have to understand the material well. ALL EXAMS ARE TESTING THE TRUE UNDERSTANDING OF COURSE MATERIAL. BE PREPARED.
Hardest class I've ever taken, but great professor who genuinely wants to help you learn the concepts.

Professor Ford emphasized the basics for longer than previously, which made the harder portion of the class much easier. His office hours are awesome and are a very good time to get almost one on one problem solving help. He is there to help you understand if you ask.    He has changed his format of teaching the class since 2010, it is better now

The ECE35 curriculum at UCSD is standardized across all professors, and a lot of how you do is just how much you practice, so I can't really say much about his teaching methods. He's a nice guy though. Kind of a warm grandpa type. Very hard to stay awake in lectures

Professor Sandin is absolutely a funny lecturer, his jokes make the class enjoyable. However, he is not familiar with teaching. His lecture is confusing and not helpful, you need to do readings for homework and exams. Additionally, he does not allow students to use calculators in a STATISTICAL exam, although his exam is easy.

Saritas would use a lot of examples in class which helped a lot when referring to the HW. He explains the concepts well and the exams looked a lot like the HW. He sometimes wrote on the board quickly though, hence why I give him a 4/5. He bases his notes off the textbook, but going to lecture still helped since he's adding some useful side notes.
I really enjoyed her lectures.

Dr. Jennings is a great and kind professor. She wants her students to learn the material and she cares for those that struggle by taking extra time to guide and help these students. Go to lecture. The tests are fair if you study her notes. You don't meet many professors that leave a positive impact on your life, but Dr. Jennings will. Good luck!

Really cares about student. She may appear disorganized at first, but she knows her stuff. Mostly tests on materials covered in class, but reading the book helps a great deal. Discussion is part of the grade. Tests are fair.

Lectures were a waste of time. She just read the power point slides to us. Look at her slides to see where to read in the book or just read the slides (those are just summaries of the book). Her tests were very similar to the practice tests. Overall, not a very good professor, avoid if possible.

This lady shouldd teach geometry with all the tangents she goes on.  Read her slides outside of class,  don't go to class. It's a waste of your oxygen. She's perfectly nice, she just doesn't teach anything in lecture. The book is your savior, as is discussion.

Jeremy was my TA for many math classes throughout the 4 years I was there. He knew linear algebra very well and could change ways to explain something so we could understand. He really cares about the students, and I truly couldn't have survived many classes without his help. He is very approachable, and he inspired me to be a good TA later.

Schmitt was a great professor, everything was clear and concise. Exams were nice because they were only a few problems and questions were pulled from either hw/lecture and reworded. He's generous with notes, and wants to help you pass. Alot of people did well, but if you don't take it serious/miss too many/skiphw lectures its possible to fail.
Professor Schmitt is one of the best math 3c professors you can take at UCSD.

I didnt really find her helpful at all. Whenever I tried to ask her questions via office hours or after class, she wouldnt seem to care if I had trouble understanding a certain concept. My original intention was to pursue a Psych minor, but her class and her personality just flat out lost my interest in psychology.

Prof Dimler's lectures were interesting. She showed lots of funny videos and has a very outgoing personality. You don't really have to do the reading for this class and will miss a few points about the videos if you don't attend. Otherwise it's not very difficult, it was uncurved with a 94% A but had a few points extra credit with easy exams.

Professor Dimler is my favorite professor at UCSD. Her lectures are consistently interesting and engaging and she does a great job explaining content very clearly. She always tries to find videos to work into her lectures and she loves to answer questions during class. Tests are almost all based off lectures and not too hard.

Professor Laura Dimler was great! She tests off what was presented in lecture slides/class. She is a little unforgiving about missed online quizzes (she wont let you take the online quiz if you are sick or just flat out forget to do it, which imo can easily happen throughout the quarter). I got an A by reading the textbook and studying the slides.

Agghh! SHE IS AWESOMEEE!I have never seen a teacher as enthusiastic in her subject as Laura Dimler. She knows what she talks about. She will answer every question, no matter how stupid they sound. If a question is beyond her area of expertise, she will not try to come up with an answer to make herself look better. She WANTS you to learn and succeed.

Shes the best. And muy bonita... so like overall theres no reason to not learn and do well. Shes funny and cool as well. Took the class pass/no pass but I should have taken it for a grade for the GPA boost.

Excellent Professor. Approachable outside the class. Very nice person. He speaks a little bit slow, but if you concentrate, you could really learn a lot in his lecture. He understands the material very well. If you have plenty time, you should definitely take this professor.

Get to know him.  He seems a little unapproachable, but if you take the time to talk to him after class, you'll find his class so much more rewarding.  He is brilliant, and I learned so much once I put in the time.  Grading was a bit stressful early on, but it was very generous at the end.

He is the most caring professor I've ever had. I took both CSE 21 and CSE 101 with this guy. The lecture is long and abstract but if you try to pay attention and go to office hour, he is more than willing to help. Midterm and final were straight forward and you can use cheat sheets. Overall, great professor, even give you advice about grad school.

Pretty average professor, lectures are decent but he goes very slow and goes off on tangents a lot. Assignments are fair other than a very poorly organized implementation project. Midterm was brutal, final was easy. Huge curve. Overall decent

This is a pretty tough class, and there's not really a way around that. Kahng did a good job of providing lots of resources through the Moodle forums, lecture notes, and lots of problem and review sessions. Do the homework (and start early!) and you will come out alright. The curve was pretty generous at the end.

Real nice guy, knowledgeable about the field. Lectures well, talks to the class often and explains the material thoroughly. If his lectures don't make sense you can always read his notes which are very inclusive. Get to bring some notes to the midterm and final which is nice.

He is a great professor because he is caring and tries to make you understand those damn hard principles. Lectures are super clear and logically structured, thus his hilarious style would make you remember forever. However, he could give you everything you've expected for a college professor except an A on your gradebook. Just remember this.

One of the best teachers at UCSD. He is a very fair teacher and warns everyone the class is not a cakewalk so you will have to spend time out of class to understand the material. He always responded to my emails and held office hours which were very helpful. If you put in the time to understand the material, you'll do fine. Very interesting class.

Great teacher, you can tell he is very passionate about the subject. Holds regular office hours and very helpful. Be warned that the class gets extremely difficult at the end, which matters the most. His final is 65% of your overall grade, so you better be ready. Not an easy class by any means, take other electives if you can.

This class is easy as you can practically copy his notes word for word on your cheat sheet for the exams which everyone did. Huge warning: The TA made a simple addition error on my final and the professor changed the scale on my test only so as not to give me the score I earned in the end (grade appeal process was not helpful). Pray the TA can add.

Class wasnt bad, we had 3 quizzes worth 60% of your grade and the final exam 40%. Lowest quiz gets dropped. lectures were Fun, Dr. hunt tries his best to keep class interesting but there just so much the guy could do when the class runed for 3 hours. I highly recommend Dr. H if you really wanna learn about the subject.

Dr. Hunt is a good professor. The guy really cares about student's success so he put us to work! we got exposed to so many research papers and if you're planing to attend graduate school, this is the kind of professor that you wanna take!!! The class wasn't a walk in the park but if you put the time for it you'll be fine.

PSYC 153 was a class I looked forward to. I learned a great deal about this subject and I'm not a psyc major student. Lectures are basically going over the slides which he will post, so I stopped going to lecture after 4 weeks and actually did better. His tests were straight from slides and readings but u need to go over every material to get A.

I do love some of the Psychology professors, but definitely not Dr. Hunt. His questions are hard & tricky. He gives 3 "quizzes" (they're midterms), but he lets you drop the lowest one! Thats the only thing I liked about this class! Psych of emotion should be interesting & emotional, but Dr. Hunt made it dry. The readings are needed & boring.

The professor as a person is kind. However, the workload that she gives is quite insane, and the readings are uselessly long. Despite giving us exam topics beforehand, the questions are vague and the graders just grade it base on intuition rather than rubric. A lot of people in my section got nuclear bombed in a video project thats worth 25%
Would not recommend. I did not learn anything and her readings are too long . Lectures are also very useless.

This class is very interesting and is one of the easier classes. Her lectures are really interesting and gets the students involved. The midterm is based on the readings but further guidance will be given. The final exam is a research paper. Overall, not too bad.

Super caring and woke professor! She's very knowledgable about what she teaches, and she likes to incorporate activities in class sometimes to make the class more engaging. ANTH23 was my favorite class fall quarter, and was a great start to my first year at UCSD.
Lovely professor! Teaching accurately and clearly. I went to his office hour several times for related questions. He may share lots of interesting things with you and discuss with patience.

Professor Kolesnikov is very kind and cares about his students. He is very approachable both in class and during office hours. His accent is very easy to understand and his lectures are easy to follow because he gives a lot of examples relating to the homework. I would definitely choose him over others for future math classes if he was an option.
Great professor. Awesome accent

His lectures can be confusing.Sometimes he will spend all lecture on a proof and not teach you how to do the problems in the homework. Other times he will provide numerous examples.Tests aren't too difficult, he doesn't throw curveballs, and the rubric is super forgiving.Do the HW and make sure you understand concepts.Can be funny, not bad overall.
Very helpful outside of class and very clear in his lectures.

Postero isn't a bad professor herself but her class is a pain. She assigns so much reading it's way too easy to fall behind. Her lectures don't cover what's going to be on the exams it's all in the reading. They're just there to summarize and explain context.I felt like I should have used those times wasted attending lecture on doing the readings.

Very passionate about topics definitely knows her stuff since she's done field work. A LOT of reading. Exams don't reflect lectures just read. She grades on attendance so make sure to show up to class. Extra credit but not enough to make significant difference in grade except if you're borderline. Take home exams. Getting A takes work.

Lectures I felt were pointless to as they didn't reflect what was on the exams at all. I would just go on days where she will show a film as the films may be on the exams. Just do the readings and look at her lecture slides for clarification. There's A LOT of reading - a little too much if you ask me. She gives extra credit & does take home exams.

My favorite professor ever! Her Indigenous Peoples of Latin America and Human Rights class transformed my world view. She helps students learn how to think critically and deeply about every perspective of an issue. She is passionate about everything she teaches, and no one can rock a lecture like Prof. Postero! I looked forward to every class.

Nancy is an angel. Her contagious enthusiasm and youthful energy are inspirational. She really loves what she does and is extremely knowledgeable. Lectures are always interesting and engaging, she likes to have class participation. Workload is not heavy and exams are very reasonable. I highly recommend Nancy and any class she teaches.

He assigns everything the last couple weeks of the quarter and grades based on his opinion of how he thinks you should perform and does not go off a rubric. Very unfair grader. Final was chill bc you can choose your own questions and it was short and there is no midterm. Lots of reading and super boring. Lecture is mandatory and once a week.

Everyone who takes CAT125R has to listen to her read a teleprompter for hours even if she is not the listed professor, so Its important to note her poor performance. These video lectures are absolutely excruciating, what she refers to as rhetoric, is actually a dull, impossible to relate to list of definitions included to add content to to CAT125R
Often pushes politics over facts.  I don't like that in an institution of learning.

This class was insane. A lot of reading required so you have to put a lot of time and effort into this class. 3 assignments + an in class final that consisted of 8 short response and 2 long essays. Her lectures are long and boring.. Wouldn't recommend to anyone

Overall I think the subject that Losh teaches is interesting.  It does get a bit repetitive at times. There are only 3 papers due for her class, which are all pretty easy and not 10+ pagers. Her instructions for assignments are vague and it really depends on your TA. The final has short answers and essay questions. Easy if you attend lectures.

Don't be fooled by the description of the course. It's not as interesting as it seems. Lectures are long and boring. She doesn't allow electronicslaptops unless you sit in the first row so she can see what you're doing. Too much reading required, like a book a week. Grade is dependent on the TA. 3 big papers AND an in class final :( would not rec.

He cares and gives his all. When he has students that need more outside of class help he certainly gives his time to help others. He is enthusiastic when it comes to the basic physics to a experimental physics that is new and adventurous to the whole world of science. I feel that this man is sometimes underestimated.

His lecture slides are way more helpful than the book. He really gets you understanding the material and physics didn't even feel like a hard course anymore. I suggest taking his class and review the lecture slides and do the homework 'cause his quizzes and final are exactly like the book problems, plus they're manageable to do in the time limit.

He is the most amazing professor I have ever had at UCSD. I hated physics and did pretty bad in 1A but he is so clear and helpful that I have been doing great on his quizzes. I definitely recommend you go to his office hours he is sooo helpful and very welcoming. He has made me go from hating physics to loving it.

It's a hard class, but it physics, its not supposed to be a walk in the park. He is really helpful though and encouraging. You really should go to class though because he does proofs and stuff that you may need for tests. Tests are hard though and long.

Dr Maple, like all of the other physics professors is not the best, but he come up with good examples to review in class. His exams are quite possibly the hardest things I have ever concieved, but, hey it's physics. Prof Maple is a brilliant physicst!

Ryans a young dude that just started teahcing and he's a super cool guy I asked him a question walking outside after lecture one day and we literally walked from Marshall to Revelle just talking about his class. Hes a nice dude who cares about his students. Wish I could take him again, his classes and lecture not mandatory and theres xtra credit.

I had him for his first quarter teaching, so he was still trying to figure things out. His tests were super easy, but that's coming from someone who took AP Chem (you'll be fine in the 6 series if you took AP or IB or whatever). Classes were not mandatory, discussions were not mandatory. But he seems like a cool guy. Hopefully he figures it out

Honestly professor Ryan is great professor. And Im glad i had the opportunity to be in his class. Its his first time teaching so there is  room for improvement on his teaching skills but he definitely is there if you reach out to him. Going to his office hours or staying after class, hell be there with you until you understand.
Love this guy, caring, helpful & understanding.

Ryan is literally the best professor I have ever had at UCSD. He is so funny and knowledgeable. He was also nice and friendly. Tests were fair and he made it very clear what to expect during the exams. Highly recommended. He was so nice and he was always willing to help students.

I took his social networks class. There are group presentations every week and everyone is assigned a specific role. The final is a paper. The prof gives good feedback and comments to prepare you for the final paper. He is one of the nicest teachers ever. And he really knows his stuff. He answers your questions and gives many examples to help.

Recently I found out how much this guy makes and I was surprised. Although he makes plenty he still cares a lot about his students. He is extremely excited about teaching. This class itself is super interesting and is the most interesting CAT class so far. Its a project based class with a couple of essays. Overall not too bad.
Professor Fowler is a nice guy and very approachable. The lecture was all from the book. Class was pretty easy, grade is based on the TA. Syllabus was unclear. Overall, it was an enjoyable class.

Super enthusiastic about his research and likes sharing it. Attendance is not mandatory, unless your TA says otherwise. Discussion section is mandatory. 2 essays, 1 group project. Grading is based on TA. I had an awesome one named Ash.

Lectures are extremely detailed, take notes! He knows HIS STUFF. Class is a WHOLE LOT better. Readings are helpful, lectures are very clear, he tends to get excited and talk fast, but he's very approachable. The grading was great, 10% MT, 50% final, 40% reading response (3 sent. summary)... I'd recommend the prof, but NOT the subject.

Skyler was a great professor and his slides were very clear. Studying off of the slides was all you needed to do for the midterm and final regardless of having read the readings. He explains things very well in class and engages in a lot of discussion which is very interesting if you are actually somewhat interested in politics.

I really enjoyed her class! She never fails to make the class happy and laugh. She is very engaging and animated. She make sure everyone understands the vocabulary and grammar. The quizzes are weekly (but are easy), and the midterm and final are an actual replica of the quizzes. She gives you all the tools to succeed. It's harder to fail than pass

Professor Pita is the funniest professor I've had. Unlike the other posts she is teaching and I've had 2 classes with her and currently enrolled for the next one. She makes lecture go by so quick and manages to teach while engaging the students. We have quizzes every Monday but they're a piece of cake. I love her class.

This course is taught by a TA. I got Bernardo. He is the coolest. Easy A. Mon: quizzes about the hw in the workbook & a review on grammar  Wed:  go over grammar & readings  Fri: submit 1/2 short summary on the readings & talk/analyze the readings 1 midterm, 2 take-home papers & 1 final; all were easy.  study weekly quizzes for the midterm.

Heads up: Pita will most likely not be your professor. You will have a TA. I had Susana for my TA and she was great! She was really good at explaining concepts to the class. You will have about 15-20 workbook pages to do each week so stay on top of it! Understanding the HW is essential to passing weekly quizzes. Attendance is taken daily.

I had Ana as a TA and basically a teacher. I never saw the professor or I don't know how she's like at all. Everything depends on your TA: the way things are taught and graded. My TA was pretty good. Quizzes were pretty easy if you study and don't make careless mistakes. A lot of reading but can be found online. HW and quiz every week . Be prepared

This teacher is the only teacher I've ever had who helped prepare me for my life outside of school. I highly recommend anyone take his class to learn about the art of performance art. I learned I could do anything and make anything happen if I just had enough imagination. Thank you, Tony, for helping to shape my life. You're a hero to me!
Great person, and truly inspirational. Cares a lot about his students, and the world in general. yay!

Prof Ochoa is a top notch prof. I learned loads and he genuinely cares about the students. I found reading the cases after the lecture to be more helpful because it's tough reading, but he randomly calls on people to answer questions, so if you don't want to be embarrassed read before class. Overall a fantastic experience, not easy though!
No curves, 70% is the benchmark which I just passed. Only once per year. The reading is so hard!
Worthwhile class, especially  if you have any interest in the environment.

He is really straightforward abt what you need to know. Make sure to attend the review session because he will hint at things he will test on. It was easy for me to get an A but I attended every class (lecture's super impt b/c there is no textbook, you read case law) and kept up with the readings. He also provided snacks like cookies for the final.
Tons of homework. Avoid him.

I am a graduate student and I have taken many ECE courses, to be honest, Professor Young-Han Kim is one of the best. He gave amazing lectures and he can explain complicated knowledge into simple understandable concept for his students.  I rarely give professor this kind of review but he's worth it.

Great Prof. He cares about the students and the TAs are very helpful. They are all avaiable out of class too...The course is hard and his test are pretty challenging. He puts a lot of effort in his teaching and expects students to keep up with his level of teaching...

Class was a easy, teacher is barely comprehendable.  Went to first lecture only, and after that attended every other discussion.  TA is very very good and helpful.  I havent got my grade yet but im assuming it is roughly a B.  Practice exams with solutions on WEBCT are literally identical to tests, just different numbers.  Easy class
Good English but his accent is terrible. Many students went out after 15mins during first day of class.

I don't know what it was with this but I just couldn't tackle this class. I would think I was above and beyond on requirements and would get a below average grade, with feedback that would say I did a great job. Grading rubric is a big thing, and it's really hard to get a response from her. Nice lady but tough.

When talking to other students in my class, most thought the class was boring. However this class changed my life. The insights that she taught were amazing. It was a privilege to take her class and learn from her. She's tough but this is the class I learned the most at UCSD. She exposes conglomerate media very well. Hope to take her again.
Eh? When I took her she seemed to be fairly responsible. She's suspicious of sweet talkers.
I had her as a TA and she was no good.  She didn't clear up our questions and seemed to get us more confused.  Her grading was very harsh as well.
very clear. lectures facilitate note taking. you will use information from this class is upper division communications classes. nice woman. keep on top of the reading.

Funniest guy ever. Not really intentionally funny, but he always cracked me up. Chill guy, he pauses in order to make sure everyone understands the concept. Thick accent, but understandable. Exams are more on the theoretical side, but nothing too difficult. Homework assignments could be lengthy, but there were not that difficult either.

Prof. Brivio tried really hard to teach us the concepts properly and in depth, he did not dumb down the material. The problems from homework and exams pushed us to think instead of mechanically reproduce a solution; this seems to have gone over the head of many students. He prepared us well for the 20 series. He was also available outside class.
favorite phrase, "DEEZ GUYYYY"

He tends not to "dumb things down" and explains mathematical concepts in a way that should feel intuitive using traditional mathematical symbology. He will take time out of his schedule and make sure that the student understands the concept if you approach him. Sometimes it's frustrating because he does tend to lecture past the allotted classtime.

He has a thick Italian accent which is very distracting and very difficult to understand concepts. He also over complicates things. His handwriting could definitely be better. I found that his jokes were, for the most part, confusing and not funny though he tries. He's a chill guy and I would have him again if he taught other classes.
I learned a lot in this class. He's a new professor but I hope he sticks around the neuroscience dept.

He is 100% ok with just watching podcasts (<25% show up). Posts all slides + many resources. Extremely knowledgeable about material. No tests. 6 hws/midterm/endterm (33% each). Explicit about formatting expectations and will mark off. All slides recycled from past years. Very responsive and helpful via email - ask lots of Qs! All HWs are in Matlab.

ECE Grad student here. Classes are optional, everything is video podcast and he encourages you to watch those instead of attend. Very responsive with email about HW. No exams, mid term and end term individual projects. Weekly homework, with TONS of MATLAB. Uses all the proper words so things aren't dumbed down. Had to Google alot. Positive overall.

Terrible!  His lecture notes are terrible and it's hard to recognize his hand writing. He just used plain words to explain the equations in the slides without any derivation. You will definitely screw up unless you have a strong undergraduate signal processing background. Should not let a SIO professor teach at ECE department!

hodgkiss rocks. He gives very detailed and thorough explanations, making things very easy to understand. The class wasn't difficult, but I felt like I learned a lot. He doesn't use piazza, but gives good email responses. Also his podcasting is just damn convenient
Super easy grader. and Super lax on deadlines.I took her once got an A and then decided to take her again. The class structure didn't change
I really liked this class. It was a ton of writing but the material was helpful to write the essays and very interesting.

I really loved this class.  Her lectures and the subjects were interesting.  She would sometimes talk a lot but I really enjoyed it.  I know it's a SOC class but was also relevant to Poli-Sci and Film studies.  Read the material before the midterm and final, pay attention, do the study guide, and you can get an A.  Also, shes very nice.
She blabs a lot. Not that interesting. VERY scattered ex: didn't remember her own instructions for the exam. Not a very hard class but you wont get a lot out of it.

Boring. This was the class supposed to be the most interesting out of all DOC's and i could not help to fall asleep almost everyday. Lecture is horrible just reads off powerpoints which are just quotes and hardly says anything other than that. she is approachable i give her that. however, just find an easy TA as long as you got the A who cares!

I've taken Heidi for soci 2, soci 115,soci 127, soci 142 and plan on taking 2 more of her courses next quarter. I've gotten A's in every one of her classes. I LOVE HER. She's super chill, easy to talk to, and she's actual person who will sit there and tell you her thoughts and feelings on subjects and I LOVE IT.

Straightforward lectures and lots of examples. Exams are not impossible. He gives ample time to solve the couple problems on them. Be prepared to read the textbook and practice a couple hundred practice problems throughout the course if you want a good grade unless you're a genius. I'm still salty I was 0.001 away from an A- but he gave me a B+.

He's not easy. His teaching was fairly straightforward, he gave you everything you needed to know. His tests are really challenging so do all of the homework problems (and all of the problems in the book tbh). The tests are open note and open book but after doing every problem in the book you don't really need it. Passing isn't hard, A's are though
Professor Radic is a great professor. He teaches well has fair (but difficult) tests. Do problems and you will pass. Getting  high grades, however, is extremely hard.

His class is not hard at all if you can understand the concepts by doing practice problems, you should attend OH to clear up any questions or else it will bite you in the ass during the exam. Overall, just practice and you will get a good grade

He failed 55 students in my spring '16 quarter (41 F's, 14 D's). You definitely have to work for your grade. Do literally every single practice problem in the book and then 100 more. His tests are very fair--all open book/notes.  DON'T think this means they're easy just because they're fair tests. You still need to pour in hours of work.
His class is A LOT of work (more than ten hours) and a single grammar/spelling mistake could cost you one point ... despite him being a good professor beware...
Best Professor Ive ever had! He wants you to succeed and teaches almost in the best way possible. Lectures are very engaging and teammates were fun
excellent professor and the more important, he's a great human being. His lecture is interesting and he's open to all opinions.

Take this class as a writing or presentation class. Do not think you could get something on your resume. Most projects are boring and don't have an even difficulty. If you happen to pick a brand-new project, you are doomed. Be serious for your writing. Writing and presentation count as most of the grade. Really time consuming. So not recommend.
He's a great human being. Hands down the best professor I've had so far.

She is the most caring, understanding human being ever. I just want to have coffee with her. Her class is definitely an easy A but you have to pay attention to her lectures. Her tests are 95% based on her lecture rather than the textbook. She is relatable, motherly, and very pretty ( i mistaken her for a student!). Highly recommend.

Really boring professor who doesn't care about concept of theory but also doesn't care about technique. Literally teaches nothing. He acts like he's never taught before. Very specific about project criteria when normally in an art class as long as you vaguely follow the prompt it's ok. 10/10 would not take again.

I got a lot out of this class - context-wise and improving skills elsewhere: deductive reasoning and better writing. However, the exam was ridiculously hard compared to the standard of other uni modules. Doing lectures and readings was not enough. I recognise the concrete skills I gained but worried about a huge stain on my academic CV...

Schreiber is a horrible person. I know he is smart and I received an A- in his class. I went to him for a grad school recommendation. He said he would do it and I gave him 4 weeks to complete it. When I tried to keep contact to get the letter he would not respond. Luckily I had 3 others. He seems to take joy in feeling superior everyone.

The best professor. Genuinely enjoys teaching and he makes the material interesting. The material we learned in his class stuck with me the most even though i thought I wouldn't find it interesting. When the class if over he stays in touch with his students and helps out with any kind of letter of recommendation.

Schreiber is a genius, the best professor I've ever had and an absolute joy to be around. He cares so much about his students, is inspiring and encouraging, and pushes his students to learn at a whole new level. Not to mention he's at the front of the research in his field and not half bad to look at! UCSD needs more professors of this caliber.

Professor Schreiber is truly the greatest professor I have had in my life. He really cares about you LEARNING the material and pushes you to expand your academic capabilities. Unfortunately, this is his last quarter at UCSD, so those who did not have him were really missing out.
Great holocaust teacher you really learn a lot from the class I had the 4-6:40 class the topics were so interesting and she gives you a break the class isnt hard just show up

Professor Hillman is incredibly committed to her students. She is able to facilitate a high-level discussion that explores historical evidence, philosophical background, and real-world applications. Attendance is mandatory- but you won't regret it. I highly recommend.
I only read some of the books. Essay is easy enough. Go to class and take good notes and the exams will be simple. Very straightforward and very interesting class!
She's really smart and she reads a lot of books. She is really passionate about her field. Her classes are always intellectually stimulating.
Hillman really promotes discussion in class; if you do the readings, class can be very interesting. If you don't, it probably won't hurt your grade (She is quite lenient).

Professor Crawford is one of the kindest, most genuine teachers I have ever had. Even better, the lectures in his Integrative Medicine Seminar are extremely interesting. His grading is based on participation and a group presentation; if you put in the work, you will get an A. I would totally recommend his class!

Dr. Crawford is a great guy, he genuinely cares about his students. His lectures are amazing, he is always well prepared and you learn so much interesting information that you can actually apply to your life. His exams are straightforward but require a ton of memorization. Not as easy as I thought a nutrition class would be, but so worth it!

Definitely one of the best classes you can take as a bio major here at UCSD.  There is quite a bit of memorization involved, but the material is so interesting that it makes it easier to learn it.  Dr. Crawford is a very good professor overall and makes it VERY CLEAR what he wants you to know for the midterm and final.  Highly recommended! :)

Probably my favorite professor and class so far at UCSD. There is 1 midterm, an easy project, and then the final. Tests are pretty fair, but you definitely need to study the material in depth. There is a lot of memorization to do, but the information is so interesting and applicable to daily life that it makes it easier to want to learn it.

As far as biology courses go, Crawford's was pretty standard for UCSD. Put in a few hours a week and you'll get an A no problem. The midterm (40%) was short-answer and harder than the final (50%) which is all MC. Diet project is easy, free 10% of final grade. Curve is generous as well. 8281000 was an A. Good lecturer and very nice, approachable.

Doing the readings for this class is your best bet. I would also recommend taking this class only if you have an interest in education (especially higher ed) and/or inequalities among races/socioeconomic classes. I thought this class was extremely interesting and I will take the knowledge with me for awhile!

She was nice and willing to work with you. She is all about interaction. She won't randomly call on you but won't allow same people to answer over and over to encourage you to interact. When a few people did not do great on midterm she offered extra credit in the form of an essay. You will read a lot. Her lectures and notes are very useful.

Her lectures are based off the concepts in the books. You learn a few terms and apply them to exam essay. Pop quizzes are given based off readings. Lots of readings. I got an A on every exam by skimming through readings, and going over important vocab to use on the essay/exam. Be prepared to interact with classmates.

All this professor does is go over the readings and regurgitate the main points of the authors, she does not add anything in lecture. She also gets visibly frustrated if she asks a question and no one participates since she does not plan her lectures according to the length of the class. Grade is based on one midterm and one final.
She made the class really interesting, and she was really helpful when I asked her for help.

You get a lot from her class. PA is challenging at first but once you get used to it, it is not much harder than other CS PAs. The final exam is hard but you do not have a plenty of time to be prepared because the last PA is time-consuming, which makes it much harder.

YY's lectures are pretty clear, and she always asks for students' feedback. Group projects are not too bad, but you need to test them thoroughly. The midterm is fair (easy to get above 85 but a little bit hard to go above 90), but the final is definitely harder.

In all honesty, lots of people I have talked to mentioned how difficult Prof Yuanyuan class is. While the programming assignments are in fact tough, she is an intelligent professor and a great lecturer. Learnt a great deal from this course. If you want to learn a lot about OS, do take this class with her, highly recommend her as a professor.

I sensed that the professor dedicated her teaching. Before midterm exam, she held an extra class on Saturday to help students to prepare  the exam. She also held the extra office hour on Sunday (Yes, on Sunday) to ask students' questions regard to the exam materials.  I cannot find another professor willing to spend this much time to help students.

Lacking in ethics. I found an ambiguous question during an exam and asked the proctor how to answer it. The proctor told me to answer it and write down my assumptions. YY marked the question wrong. When I asked her about it, she said that I was right that the question was ambiguous but my lower grade on the exam "didn't matter to my GPA anyway."

This was Irina's first and last course taught at UC San Diego; she was nervous towards the start, but got much better. Her lecture style can be dry, as she mostly reads off of printed handouts, but she has a solid grasp of the material and can answer all of your questions. Tests and weekly homeworks are fair and similar to the lecture content.

Prof. Elgindi is clear and articulate. He lectures at a reasonable pace. It's easy to follow his proofs, and he really tries to make you understand everything. Elgindi kinda encourages participation by asking you to pitch ideas for a proof. Approachable and will answer questions ASAP. His speech can be dull and monotonous but still will recommend.

I think she's a great professor and genuinely cares for students. She has a bit of an accent but I think overall, she's a good lecturer with a good mix of theory and application. Stats is difficult so you have to work really hard to do well especially in 181A and 181B where the material can get confusing. She give extra credit too!

Relatively she is a good stats prof if you consider other alternatives. She doesn't have accent and her lectures have many examples compared to other "theoretical" classes. There is bonus credit for giving her feedback during the quarter. Her homework is pretty easy and there are some R exercises. Final exam is hard compared to homework and midterm
AWFUL. She does not take questions well and tests are very difficult. Do not take if you have another option.

She's not a bad instructor. Her accent is not too bad either but exams seemed fair and I actually liked the class. It could be because I already knew the material so I could be a biased opinion. Be prepared to use programming and do simulations in R! Sometimes it can be a bit time consuming but the class was not too bad for me at least.
She's helpful in office hours but honestly she is so whatever

Dr. Prosser is amazing! If you're going into the field of marketing then definitely take her class as she gives lots of real life experiences. She wants all her students to succeed so exams are open book. But that doesn't mean you can slack off. One assigned group project which is enjoyable. Just come to class, do the work and you will pass!

I'm very interested in marketing, and Prosser was a great intro to the topic. You get 35% of your grade by participating. If you just show up, a B is guaranteed, and you get an A if you study a little. The group project is fun if you get good partners, but Prosser + TAs help you if you don't. Really great class if you like groups and participation.

Prosser simply reads her slides to you. Class is mandatory. Seating is assigned and for the large project you can't choose your own groups. Tests are open book (If you want to use the E-Book you have to bring a second laptop). If you want to learn something avoid this class it's worthless. If you can put up with showing up everyday it's an easy A.

Professor Prosser is one of the best professors at UCSD. Attendance is required but classes are fun. She gives clear instructions for all of her assignments, project and exams. She's  also very helpful and tries her best to help you succeed. Try your best at the assignments and reach out to her after class and you will learn a lot from the class.

Professor Prosser is one of the most dedicated professors that teach at Rady. Her class was one of the most fun and stimulating classes I have taken at UCSD. Her marketing class is also very fun but has a big group marketing project. She even helped me immensely in applying for graduate school and even wrote my recommendation letter. A+++

Cares for your writing and really wants you to pass. Provides specific feedback which is good for revision but it sometimes made me cry at how much stuff I needed to work on. Ms. McCarthy really helps get you ready for college writing.

If you are a professional Flamenco Dancer from spain you will get around a A- if you are an actual person good luck passing. He expects way too much for a general education class. Wait for the other TDMV 142, Salsa Dancing. He is a terrible teacher. Avoid this guy like the plague.

Homework solutions half-filled, often remarking to "check the lecture slides". Lecture slides don't contain any of his notes. You must attend all lectures and decipher his handwriting/follow his speedily written blackboard notes, because he won't provide other resources for homework/studying. Doesn't give you textbook sections to study. On your own

Extremely unorganized. Tells students to buy one textbook and uses a different one for all lectures in first 8 weeks. Exams have mistakes that throw you off. Nearly no partial credit. His handwriting is awful and he doesn't try to fix it despite several in-class complaints. Have to attend all classes because schedules cites 3 books every lecture.

Hard to understand his accent, and he's not good at explaining physics. HW is not graded, but study them for the quizzes. Quiz every week, one final, all MC. You can drop 2 quizzes. At least 2-3 questions (out of 10) on quizzes are tricky. Go to the TA section to really understand what's going on.

Professor Palacci has a French accent, but I personally had no difficulty understanding him. He has a solid sense of humor and does a lot of demonstrations (e.g. Bernoulli's apparatus), so his lectures will hold your attention. He emphasizes concepts, so you get a break from memorizing formulas :-)
