I didn't like the fact that his quizzes always had at least two  tricky problems that weren't line with the difficulty of the homework.  He uses Piazza so the class can have a forum for discussion.  Clicker questions are worth 5% extra credit, which is nice.  Overall, decent.

Well prepared for lectures that brought out his kind personality. Taught useful math concepts for tackling tricky potentials. The class was collaborative and I learned a lot from working with others and meeting new people, both women and men. Perhaps maybe some people should get to know these so called aloof know it alls? #noqualms #cuin100B

God bless this man and his wonderful accent and jokes. Fogler is the boy, he taught Electricity and Magnetism like no other, is lowkey the only reason I know how to Fourier Transform and is just a real solid dude. He really cares about the students and how much we learn and that really goes a long way in this major that's full of aloof know it alls

Boring lectures, iClicker questions that forces you to go to his lectures, stupidly long online hw, and the quizzes. I felt that the quizzes were somewhat reflective on the hw but the lectures and the textbook barely helped while doing hw so alot of people just bombed the quizzes and final. Take anyone else if possible.

Lectures are boring and unhelpful and clickers count for 10% of grade and correct response matters. Only three attempts on homework and it is very hard. Quizzes are hard (no equation sheet given either) and grading scale for quizzes isn't well-defined (quizzes have different amount of total points) but he drops 3 out of 9. Would not recommend
I've only been to two of his classes. Hi voice puts people to sleep. I don't know enough about him. He smells and his quizzes are hard.

Dr. Kristan 's lecture notes is the treasure! I don't really take the class with him since he's retired now. But his lecture note is perfect for physiology study, and it helped A LOT about my bipn 105 study. The note is super organized!

tough class, lots of info. tests were okay, but its the grading that was harsh. would never know if he wanted a general vs very detailed answers. midterm averages: 60%. 10% of your grade requires you to pick out specific details from the textbook. even though people say he tests concepts, which he does, you still need to memorize everything.

First, this is not an easy class in general. There is a lot of memorizing involved and if thats not your style, avoid Mam Phys. Kristan's class is good though. He gives the material in a strait forward way and has very fair exams. You dont have to read the book, just go to lecture/listen to the podcast and review his outlines and your good to go.

Very knowledgeable and helpful, especially if you go to his office hours. Exams are very fair and require you to use your knowledge of the CONCEPTS, which is what a test should do anyway. He likes to test on physiological mechanisms of being poisoned. Very clear in class but be warned... his voice is very soothing... Great professor, great man.

Great professor. He really has a strong mastery of the subject and teaches it very well. Tests are kind of tough because they require you to really apply your knowledge of the subject, but they are definitely completely fair.
Katrin is a really nice IA and is really approachable outside of the classroom. WCWP 10A is only really hard, because the department is very strict about giving out As on papers

Now she teaches at the University of Houston. She knows a lot about critical theory but never gives a complete class herself. Her approach on pedagogy and respect towards students is questionable: she turns them against each other and exploits her research assistants. She changes the rubric after the work is turned in.

The syllabus was disorganized and inaccurate. She gave weekly quizzes that were supposed to be on the readings alone, but she would include information such as the dates of the author w/o announcing it. I guess to sum it up, on the first day she said "put your heart into this class" but she couldn't be bothered to show the same level of respect.

It's a literature class, so you should be reading and writing; sometimes the assignments have no direction, since the prof. forgets to give instructions. She has no experience or knowledge of the English classics. This is a big minus for those of us who are majors in English.

She's a great professor with a great personality. Just had a very disorganized syllabus that was never updated, which the students had to reap the consequences. A LOT of workshop with A LOT of writing assignments and drafts. It was way more than I expected. Plus it's mandatory to go to 3 readings (useless imo). Midterm was fairly easy, however.

I liked Mrs. Commisso's class. The subject is boring at times. I was astounded how many of my peers don't know about majority vote and process. I will not make the professor and teacher accountable for any of that.

She's not a good lecturer. She says um and repeats herself a lot. She's also unabashedly left-wing.I mostly agree with her politically, but in one lecture I was so annoyed with the left-wing arguments she made without support that I felt she was pushing me to the right.She teaches the course as if it's still 1999. Papers were unrelated to lectures.

She's not a good lecturer. She says um and repeats herself a lot. She also puts her own notes exactly as she is reading them up on the screen, even though they contain abbreviations and acronyms that really should be spelled out to make it easier to understand. She flips around somewhat chaotically through her notes, which are in Word format not Po

she simply is the worst professor I have ever had. She is extremely difficult to work with and has no concept of honoring prior agreements. She is completely over the hill and makes up for it by belittling students.

Professor Commisso is extremely knowledgeable about many aspects of central/eastern european development, and it is nothing short of pure pleasure to take a course with her. She tells funny jokes, is highly charismatic, and offers a variety of prompts for the midterm/final (one 8 and one 10 page paper). TA's were hot so that was a plus.

Awesome, here lectures are easy going but here slides can look empty. Tests are fair and based on lecture. Recommend studying if you want a good grade but class is worth taking. I think it was her first time teaching but she is already the best psychology professor I've had.

She puts up slides but doesn't really go in depth in them and expects you to take notes at home. She speaks directly from the slides but doesn't really engage in the topics and with the students. She does attempt to make the lectures somewhat interesting though. There is a lot of reading!!!!!!!

Professor Yvette Jackson rambles on every lecture and does not engage the class at all. She reads directly off the slides and even then, she is still confused. Also, Professor Jackson does not take time in the lecture. She moves on each slide too quickly for any information to digest. Don't let her ruin your GPA!

Pros: No homework just readings, attendance not mandatory, might add 1-2% to final grade Cons: tough grader, No extra credit, graded on midterm and final with an optional paper if you dont do well. However, he will inform you that he will be be tough with grading it. Exams are short answer/essay.

Worst professor I've ever, hands down. Skipped vital QM concepts. Grades were 100% subjective, lots of evidence showing he didn't use any specific grading scheme. Denied to provide a grading scheme to UCSD physics department. UCSD Physics department is just as guilty as Abarbanel for ruining students grades that quarter. They will not take action

You're in trouble if you take him. Out of 100+ students, he gave 20+ an "I" at the end of the course for lack of turning in the "ungraded" HW. The midterm did not count for credit so 100% of grade was the final. Of the people that got grades, he just picked grades out of a hat it seems because people with same percent got different letter grades.
Does not care about what students learn from his class
good
No Comments
He is the best teacher I ever had.
He's a funny teacher who will make you laugh!
classroom is never dull. always different and interesting. Very knowledgable, super cool and totally approachable.
This is seriously the funniest professor you will ever have. He's also young and hot!

Steinert teaches the core course in UCLA. Just prepare to get a B. I'm not joking. Always mistakes in lecture, the unclear guide on homework, and you basically learn everything by yourself. You will never really understand the course materials from his course, and no one can help you! If you can, try to stay away from his class as much as possible!

Prof. Steinert-Threlkeld (you may know him by his moniker-Zacheycakes) is totally hilarious and breaks down difficult concepts so that they are easy to understand! If you go to his OH, I'd break the ice with a joke (preferably from stand up comedy b/c I hear he loves it). He is helpful when he's not sarcastic, so beware of asking dumb questions.
Pretty great lecturer

Dr. Schoeninger is very knowledgable about her subject, although exams are hard as she does not give much guidance on what to study. Her essay prompts are also very vague. We had a Midterm (all short answer), a 10 page essay (pick a few readings from class) and a Final. No additional assignments, only weekly readings. Lectures are read off of PP.

Well, most of the lectures are pretty good, and interesting too. She genuinely likes her subject and communicates this too. The readings are a bit boring, the exams are bit hard and we  could use more guidance on what to study. So, it was okay if you like the subject.

One of the best professors  at UCSD. Really passionate about the subject, and although she is highly respected in her field, she does not come off that way, she's very down to earth and helpful. Yes, you have to work hard and study in the class, but you come out learning a lot, and it's an upper division anyways. I am not an anthro major & got an A

Seems very knowledgable. In the end it's not her lecture, but rather a content of assignments and quizzes that annoys you. She will either gave a very easy or a very hard quiz. If you do the reading it's fine, I guess, but the reading is long, very boring. Usually. Her midterm paper was a 6-page single spaced essay on a 4 page article. Enough said.

She seems like she knows her field and would be a great adviser for grad students, but she is so unclear and unhelpful that I would suggest avoiding her. She knows exactly what she wants, but makes no offer to inform students what that is so you spend the whole class scrambling to meet her requirements.
Best professor ever at UC san diego. Love him!!!!!

Not very clear at explaining and lectures are difficult to follow. i learned mostly everything from TAs, but he did switch to using mostly powerpoints after our class suggested it to him. His tests are easy as long as you do the homework. Read the book. Test questions are almost exactly the same as questions from book.
He has bad handwriting. He's really unclear when he talks. Basically he can't teach. Good thing our TA told us all the answers/exactly what would appear on the midterms.

Easily one of the worst professors I've taken.  I practically get straight A's and got my worst grade in this guy's  class.  He can't teach, his exams are not representative of the material, his writing is not legible, boring.  You will not learn anything from this class.

Professor Hoffman just goes over the same examples in the textbook during lecture, which is not very helpful. He is not a great lecturer and has horrible handwriting. I ended up learning more from the TA's.

as long as you do the reading and go to class you're fine. A lot of people don't take psychology classes seriously and expect to get an A with minimal effort. Just do the readings and don't be lazy. Aramovich was a pretty nice guy, always willing to answer questions. He was also mindful of 3 hour lectures being hard during the summer so it was ok

The tests were very detailed and it was almost impossible to remember this much information when you're being tested on 6 chapters. If you don't read the textbook you're not passing. 2 tests and 1 paper. Final was noncumulative but it was still terrible. He's nice and makes you think about the material. If you're taking it in summer take it ALONE.
He's awesome but you better be able to explain all the theories or you aren't gonna do too well. Tests are extra long, but the examples you give will stick cause he's effective.

Craig is an awesome teacher. Being a reletively involved student, he loved to laugh with us when we'd joke about course content and loves making funny examples to help us understand logic topics better. While being a serious teacher, Craig is always willing to help and really loves his subject, as well as knowing it like the back of his hand.

The class was difficult, yet entertaining. Since it was a small class he was able to give individual feedback to each student. His comments could have been more constructive, though. He places a great deal of emphasis on originality and being able to present. It is definitely not simple to get an A in his class; he will make you work for it.

First tests are the most difficult but it gets easier from there. READ the chapters before hand that way you have some background but it is not completely necessary. If you have questions he will be there for you and will accommodate. Would definitely take again!
makes class fun and interesting. not too much homework. well prepared for tests

Tanabe is not a good teacher to say the least, grades as if she wants you to fail. Most of the people in her class want out but have no other choice because a four hour lab is so hard to fit into a loaded class schedule. A lab class should be fun and interesting, she makes her lab feel like a sort of war zone where students are fighting to survive

Does not understand how to have a student/teacher relationship, by that I mean extremely hard to talk to and/or reason with. Gives unreasonably hard quizzes and tests in relation to other sections of the same lab course. Provides unclear information regarding what is required and her grading style is ludicrous.
She is so monotone and doesn't answer the question when you ask for help. She's super boring. I would die to get out of her class.

Just added another TA to the list. Always say "you get points off for doing this..that..." just like she has the power to make up her own rules. And the word "fair" doesn't exist in her dictionary. Unfortunately, we can't pick and choose our own TAs for the lab sections so your final 5% evaluation at the end of course will definitely be biased.
Mike Gao is the best professor I ever had. He is the most passionate about music and taught me the most useful things in college. UCSD needs more professors like Mike.

He likes what he does and he's a cool guy but he's pretty disorganized and his assignments and exams are random. Attendance isn't really mandatory but if he sees there's barely anyone in class he'll assign something in class, and he doesn't post up his notes online so if you miss the notes then you miss them completely.
this guy is poor in lecturing skill.. grading is something u cannot understand...
One of the BEST professors so far! Mike is a really cool and relaxed guy who knows his stuff, and he's really smart too! Take notes from his slides and you'll get an easy A!
Awesome class. Professor Gao makes everything clear and super interesting. Go to lecture and section, and you'll do great -ufsi

Dr. Combes is a great professor. He keeps his class interesting by letting it be student-led. Be sure to do all of your papers on time and it should be easy if you enjoy writing research papers. He is not a tough grader. Also, participation is graded. He loves for students to discuss things. By the way, he teaches at Columbus State now, not in Cali
Really enjoyed his class. It's the only one I took that I didn't keep looking at the clock. Makes the classes really interesting and keeps the students engaged.
He is definitely not an easy grader, but he is very knowledgable and fair. You will learn a lot from him, but be prepared to work for an A, or even a B.
He's the TA for poli 11. He is super helpful and approachable if you don't get something. It also doesn't hurt that's he's good looking.

Worst professor I've ever had for a math course. He would start to do problems without explaining what the objective was. His notes were extremely hard to read and did not do a good job of explaining them thoroughly. Please avoid taking him at all costs.

Hes a ridiculous excuse for a "teacher". He assigns massive amounts of homework then tests you on what he did not cover in class or in the homework. I am failing a subject i usually get As or Bs in. My teachers in community college were honestly a godsend compared to this dude. He should be fired and i will forever think less of UCSD for hiring him

is not a good teacher. for example, he will go through a problem before explaining the steps to the problem or giving a clear explanation. the tests do not reflect the homework or lectures. I'm taking his summer math 10c class and he has a failing class average and said he will not be curving. he is ridiculous.

takes problems from the book and makes them way harder for homework, tests are not representative of lecture or homework, does not explain anything well, failing class average, insane work load. Doesn't inspire anyone to learn just relies on repetition and hard work (good to some). Worst class I've taken at UCSD.

He's like the coolest professor I ever took. During the first couple weeks he would often talk about things you never heard of outside the class, include how you would like if CS is good for you and etc. He gives extra credit for you to network with others. He's the guy that inspired me onto the path of Computer Science.

Favorite professor at UCSD! Sad he's leaving after this quarter. If he ever comes back, know that almost all of your grade is homework based, so it's not hard to pass, but the tests trip people up. Projects / homework is time consuming

For me, he is good. His class seems like a supplement to the readings. You learn some basic concepts from reading assignment, then he explains the easy error point in class with a lot of interaction with students. He has unique grading criteria that interacting with your tutor counts. The extra credit is for interviewing alumni or attending iLead.

Not really helpful. His lectures are completely different from the readings which are completely different from the homework. Only good thing about him is easy exams. Wouldn't recommend if you wish to learn.
Prof. Adam is the cooliest. His class will teach you to be practical and give you life advises. His lectures are interactive and very fun.  Would take him for all my CS classes.

For one conversant with Adorno, Durkheim, etc., she seemed surprisingly insular. I guess for some engaging with these works is more about the ego rather than searching for a guiding life philosophy. There are two essay examinations and a 10-page paper, but it is all manageable. Would have been nice if the professor had embodied what she taught.

She's a nice professor and very straightforward. She's also extremely helpful and accessible outside of class. An A is easily doable in this class if you just show up and pay attention in class and do the assignments. Her powerpoint slides are also very thorough and helpful for studying for tests. Remember not to procrastinate on the essay.

She's super nice and super sweet, and she is able to explain difficult concepts well. Overall the class was a little difficult, mainly because the material was complex, but she went over everything in class and explained the main concepts we needed to know.

This prof was super sweet and really knew what she was talking about. Her lectures hold all you need to know. There was only a midterm, final, and one 8-10 page research paper. All of them were straightforward and you knew what she wanted from you. 10% of your grade is also based on participation and we had many discussions in our class.
The class was not easy, but his way of teaching really made me understand it. plus, he answered my questions patiently even if some were dumb.

He goes over the material very fast during lecture so  you must make sure to do spend more time understanding the concepts he covers. Pay specific attention on the practice midterm and final because it will improve your grades drastically.
Took him for summer and really liked his style of focusing on proofs and teaching pure math instead of mindless computations.
Somewhat thick Romanian accent but very understandable. Drimbe is very invested in his students understanding the material but you need to review notes and study outside of lecture to keep up.

I took this class within summer session. The professor himself is a nice person and is accessible in office hours. However, have the book open while listening to lecture it will help a ton! He focuses heavily on proofs which is why the class is so hard, because other professors dont focus on that at all. Overall, it wasn't a good experience
The genius
He is a great Professor.. His book on mathematical methods were useful.

One of the oldest and worse professors at this university.  He grunts all the time and the rest of the lecture is very fuzzy.  And to add more fun into the mix, the textbook is plagued with errors.  Just take someone else! don't risk your GPA, it is not worth it!
I don't know why a 99 year old man is teaching the most important course in 101 series? The lecture is absolutely useless and the only way to learn something is to study yourself.
I don't know why an 99 year old man is teaching the most important course in 101 series? The lecture is absolutely useless and the only way to learn something is to study yourself.
I WISH THERE WERE MORE PROFESSORS TEACHING THIS CLASS.
She is the best! Seriously, take her class.

Amazing professor! She is seriously one of the best professors I've had at UCSD. She is super friendly, funny, and understanding. Her class was an absolute pleasure to be in and I would recommend her to anyone.
Fun teacher!!  I learned so much from her!!  She uses her experience as a teacher to give you advice when you get your own classroom.  Very accommodating and very funny.  Makes class interesting!!!!
Great, funny, really the best teacher I've had at UCSD.

It was her first time teaching (ss2), and she did a wonderful job. We had 4 quizzes, and 1 cumulative final. The quizzes aren't too bad if you study well, but the final was hard. Read the book, talk to her/ask q, and do book problems. Her lectures are all on the board, which is really good since you understand what she is saying. I really like her!
Really easy professor to learn from, and uses a lot of clear examples to explain her concepts.
Best teacher on earth. I am gonna miss him.
AMAZING. if you have the chance take him.

Best math professor I've ever had. Teaches material well and prepares you for the tests. All you have to do is show up, do homework, and review and you will get an A. He is funny and helpful in office hours. Loved him
Professor Longo lectures and notes are super organized. His midterms and final were fair. He explains the concepts very clearly! Homework was similar to the test!

If you aren't good at calculus he makes the class so much easier to understand! He uses most of the class time to do examples so you understand the material and his lectures are really interesting. I had an emergency and couldn't take the final and he was super understanding and made the whole situation easier. He truly cares about his students!

I was interested to study with Yolande Snaith initially because I found out that she choreographed Stanley Kubrick's final film Eyes Wide Shut, which blew me away - I loved that film. I had only done a few dance classes at UCSD and was still unsure about continuing, but Yolande's amazing teaching and choreography has inspired me - I am hooked!

Apart from being a fun and compassionate human being, Prof. Snaith is one of the most inspiring and original dance artists and teachers that I have ever studied with. She really encouraged me to persevere with dance at times when I doubted my ability - she really saw my potential and helped me to grow! And she is an incredible performer - she rocks

Professor Yolande Snaith is an awesome teacher, mentor and choreographer. I have learned so much from Yolande and her creative process is both challenging and inspiring. The choreography we created and performed was so engaging, unique and moving - she really opened my eyes to the possibilities of what dance can be, and expanded my perspectives.

Very easy class. Everyone who comes and dances and turns in the essay will get an A, if not an A+. I love her english accent and she is very fun to work with. She spends the first hour on warm-up and then finishes up with a routine and/or an across the floor. Overall, more relax than exhaust. She e-mails back quickly if you do have a question.

She is AWFUL! If you are have not been dancing since you were 5 then DO NOT expect an A in this class. She just does her own thing and never gives any insight into how you might be doing in her class. Her dancing technique leaves a lot to be desired (how did she become and instructor I'd like to know). DO NOT TAKE HER! YOU WILL BE DISSAPOINTED!!

4 wk, in class course. 2xwk for 4 hrs 40 min, incl a 40 min break. His intro to class of 11, he expected a 60% failure/dropout rate, 4 dropped. Still waiting on grades. Expect 3 of 7 left failed. He was more concerned about getting every slide read than our actual quality of retention/learning. Lectured then gave daily quiz on previous lecture.

Explains way too fast that you won't be able to understand what he is teaching. No homework is given only lab reports and tests. He goes through powerpoints fast without even asking if we understand the material. I do not recommend.
Watch out, no homework in this class. If you find it hard to keep up with course material without assigned material, choose another professor.

I would take this class again, but not again with Professor Dibrov. He seems like a nice and funny guy, but inky opinion he is not a good professor. He teaches course material way to quickly. In lecture all he does is read off of the slides that he posts online. There was no homework, only exams, so if you are a bad test taker, good luck!
Tests are hard he just lectures off a powerpoint no homework

Amazing professor! I took her Deutsch classes almost 20 years ago and I still talk about her class with my own students. I was struggling in my science major when I decided to take her class. She was a caring and enthusiastic teacher. Her classes became my favorite part of college, I looked forward to her classes. I would highly recommend her!

Frau Riebling is an awesome professor. She's so nice and enthusiastic, and she's always willing to help students. I was late for two lectures where there were two quizzes, but she let me make it up for twice. She also gives full credit on homework and quizzes to everyone, as long as you don't make any apparent stupid mistake. I highly recommend her
She's a nice and friendly German professor who is patient with students.  Her class is all in German so that is pretty tough.  If you want to learn German, I would recommend her.

EXCELLENT professor. She's from Germany, so she has a PERFECT accent and is SO helpful. The grammar gets harder in this class, but she's so good at teaching it. Her grade is also more reflective of how well you OVERALL understand the language and grammar than the points you get in the class.  If you screw up on an exam, she lets it go. It's great!

I definitely recommend her. Tests are a little difficult, but she has so much enthusiasm and cares so much about the students. I can't imagine a better instructor for learning German from the ground up.
I loved this class! Professor Romo is super inspirational and cares about the environment and that kinda made him Hot... But overall he's not. He's just a really cool professor.

Professor Romo is amazing! He teaches Sustainable Development from a natural systems design perspective which is what "sustainability" is really all about. No text book. Great lectures. I will use what I learned in this class for the rest of my life! The previous student obviously never showed up for class - and Romo doesn't even teach USP170.
I don't understand what ALL the hype is about... TA is responsible for everything and he is worst TA ever! Grades too low and you really dont know whats the expectation...

Super easy class. I took it over summer and it was an amazing learning experience. This guy is the most knowledgeable in the field of sustainability development. He gives interesting lectures. Always available during office hours and an overall nice and wise man. I totally recommend his class

Class was a breeze. Took it during summer, Romo was super cool. Lots of interesting lectures, and no need to take notes. Everything online. Participate! Engaging in discussion is important to him; he wants to see that you at least try to learn what he is teaching. Take home paper for midterm and presentation for final.
worst ever. Didn't learn anything from her class

She is insanely helpful during office hours and conferences. Take advantage of them! She really cares about her students and will put in extra time to help us. She's a fair grader and her in-class assignments really helped to improve my AB and paper. She made me like MCWP 50 a lot more than I expected.

her tests and lecture material hardly coincide. its already confusing as it is so this makes the class extremely difficult if you dont already have a profound interest in physics. would not recommend this professor for anyone I know

Although she's teaching the 2 series, it feels like it's the 4 series due to the class being extremely math heavy (especially during lectures), which is probably why everyone seems to be getting so worked up over her. If you aren't extremely fluent in Calculus DO NOT TAKE.  I'm a physics major though, so I'm fine with it!

Her lectures and quizzes were truly irrelevant, exactly as what the previous rating says. I compared with other professors' syllabus for the same class and found that her quizzes covered only 60%, 80% and 55% of materials relevant to the class in general. No wonder average grades on her quizzes were constantly near 4, with even nearly one standard away from the average.

One word to describe her lectures and quizzes: irrelevant. She makes every single aspect of the content lose the intrinsic logic. Her quizzes are of little relevance to the pieces of knowledge she demonstrated. If you take her class, which I strongly recommend not to, you may learn much less than what you hope.

Her lecture and lecture slides are just a bunch of jargon. Very confusing lecturer. You pretty much have to learn most of the stuff yourself. You never know what she's going to put on the quiz, so it's crucial you don't study the wrong thing.

Cares a lot about students' opinions. Overall very fair in grading and wants everyone to succeed. Attendance and discussion sections account for a big portion of your grade (40%) so try not to skip any classes.
I really enjoyed her class and the way she set up the exams to only test based on what she taught in lecture. I took it  during summer session 1 but it wasn't too overwhelming. Definitely take her!
Great teacher, would definitely recommend!
Very helpful and lectures are clear. She obviously cares about her students.

It's 2017 now and I took CAT 3 with Professor Knight in 2009. I'm almost positive that if it weren't for this class, I wouldn't have the critical thinking skills I have today. I remember all my peers complaining about her because she was challenging in ways that were beyond just memorizing bio facts. One of the best courses I've taken in my life.

I took CAT 3 with her back in 2009, and the class still resonates with me today. It is the one of, if not the most impactful and important college classes I've ever taken in my 5 years at UCSD. Her teaching style is clear, she is straightforward, and the topics she teaches are thought provoking.  Would most definitely take this class again.

The problem w/this prof is her students. CAT 1-3 is FRESHMAN comp; most of them are very immature & don't get why they have to work hard for good grades. Working hard in Tara's class means very carefully analyzing comics & animation for more than a cheap laugh, & becoming a responsible thinker - growing up a little. Immature types don't like that.

At times, the class was fun (I mean, how often do you get to watch "The Simpsons" during an UCSD lecture?!).  Unfortunately, her lectures' organization, and her clarity, were rather poor for the most part.  Journal entries (6-7 sentences), three essays (3-4 pages, 1 week to write them), and a final essay (8-10 pages, 1 week).

She is very impatient, her lectures are uninteresting and irrelevant.  She has a very low opinion of her students.  The assignments and class structure set you up to fail unless you drop all your other classes and devote all your time to CAT events and movie screenings.  I wish I had checked in here before taking her class.
He uses an extremely difficult and convoluted method for solving simple dynamics problems.  The TAs were very helpful in their office hours and graded very generously.  Overall, avoid if you can.
Makes problems longer to solve with his own methods. Lectures are straight from his textbook. Makes things more complex than they have to be

Has his own books and teaches in his own method which is very complicated to understand. Online, you can find a solution  usually is about 10 lines at most; but his solution takes 2 pages long!?! Honestly, I have got B+ for all my six MAE upper-division classes, but this is the only class makes me suffer and almost fail. Avoid him at all cost!!!
His lectures are just of him working out the examples in the textbook. Has his own methods to dynamics so other professors/chegg/other books don't help. Quiz heavy.

Has his own textbook. Lectures are direct material from his book. Teaches his own methods. Some may find it easier, but I find that methods from other books are easier. No midterms, 4 Quizes (60%), 8 Homeworks (16%), Final (24%). Would avoid whenever possible.

I like his teaching style. He's less structured than some of the other O Chem profs, but the exams are straightforward as long as you pay attention in lecture and do the textbook problems. The textbook problems are more important than the sapling problems, so keep that in mind. Midterms weren't bad, but the final was challenging. Overall, solid.

Lectures are helpful and necessary for learning mechanisms. He doesn't podcast, so what he write on the chalkboard is most important. The exams can be challenging but practicing the previous exams will help A LOT b/c he literally copy and pastes questions. He also requires sapling, but Im not complaining cause that's a 10% grade cushion.

Dr. Hermann is a nice guy. Lectures are helpful because he does the mechanisms that the book doesn't show in detail. The tests are okay. Look at his practice or previous exams!! VERY VERY similar to what he will give you. (emphasis on VERY)

Hermann was the nicest professor I've ever had. He's understanding and really treats students as equals. His tests are also straight from the homework but for some reason, the averages for my class were not very high. Overall, pretty easy and very approachable if you have questions.
The professor is really nice. He likes to take questions from the textbook and put it on the exam, and he only tests on mechanisms. I would definitely recommend taking him for ochem.

He does not grade your essays. Your TAs do. Good luck if you end up with a bad TA. Lee tries to make Hum as bearable as he can. Lectures are entertaining. There's a 10% grade buffer from participation. He even offers extra credit on the final and for CAPE evals. Take him! He really makes sure to teach you how to write in the humanities style.

Professor Lee gives interesting lectures that explain the background and intricacies of the books well. I love his lectures!  I also appreciated that he had three lecturers where we took a break to watch movie renditions of the books. He is a caring professor and I really enjoyed the luncheon he hosted for students (not just because of the free foo

Lee is a solid choice for HUM, but lectures became uninspiring after the first week. By the end it just felt like he talked at you for an hour and a half and you left. TAs play a much larger role in the class that the prof. Papers were graded fairly (by TAs) and the final was decent. The material could have been presented a lot more inspiringly.
Great professor but the final seems to be hard.

If you didn't have to do HUM papers, this would be great. Lee is funny and entertaining, yet practical and informative. He is unbiased in his analysis of the religious and political topics covered, which I respect. I liked that he held luncheons to get to know his students better - who does THAT at UCSD? The papers are hard, but that's HUM for you.

Great Professor who consistently shows the relevance of the course with current events. I always looked forward to going to his classes. Be sure to take notes and attend lecture as all the material needed for the exams are there.  Class is highly recommended for those who are interested in public policy.
Great down to earth Professor. The readings are as cool as him
Awesome professor. Extremely interesting book and lectures.

I recommend Hilmer. Book is really cheap and its useful for tests. Tests are short answer questions that are on topics going on in the news and pertain to the information he teaches in class only. There are homework assignments every session but they literally can be done within 20 minutes.

Easy class as long as you go to class and read. Had to turn in weekly hw which was essential in passing because most of the questions from exams related to them. Exams are like essay questions. Cool guy... knows his stuff.

Professor Verdicchio is a wonderful person and excellent professor. He offers his students abstract/alternative perspectives on topics that expand your worldview. I learned a lot and had fun. Highly recommended.

He is an amazing professor and person. He has a lot of wisdom to offer and very positively impacts his students. He is extremely intelligent and at the same time is very easy going and approachable. He creates in his class an environment  in which everyone's opinions are valued making his class a space where students learn from him and each other.
VERY cool guy. His lectures are a little unorganized because he improvises a bit. But he's very interesting and his grading is very generous.

He didn't even show up the first three weeks of the quarter which was awesome. When he finally started coming, class was kind of a drag while he would talk about opening sequences but watching the movies was really fun and debating about it in class held my interest. Didn't really have time to get bored in just an hour a week.

Great teacher, really knowledgeable, easy class. Grade is based on four easy quizzes, participation, and attendance. Speak up in class, he likes having discussions. Movies are pretty boring but he goes over them scene-by-scene in the next class so that prepares you for the quiz.
Very easy going guy! Makes the class as simple as possible and really explains and helps you with each assignment. I highly recommend him if you want to excel in an English class.

Professor Hornbrook provided me with my first papers that weren't easy A's and I was very thankful for that. I had to work hard for my grade; I improved my grammar, research skills, and persuasion techniques. This class was fun and very interesting. I would definitely take him again!
Amazing lectures. Quite a bit of homework. But really helpful professor. He will even answer questions through text at 2 am if you ask for it. Overall highly recommend.

This was my first English class I have ever gotten a B in.  He is very knowledgeable and expects the most out of his students. Not an easy class, but I enjoyed the challenge.  Failed an essay, and he let me re write it. He often tells stories which makes the class interesting, and makes an 8am class entertaining.
Poor teacher. Method and assignment is useless. But apparently there are worse teachers.

The whole grade was based on two exams. While the exams were difficult, it was a fair coverage of material and were very comprehensive. The lecture slides are posted, but he talks about topics not written on the slides so attending lectures is important. Lots of guest lecturers make the class more interesting.
rambles on and on and loves himself.
No Comments
A usual class. He is a chill prof. Doesnt care much about the deadline. He may assign a hw just few days before its due. Copies exam and hw questions from previous years

My friend is taking ENVR30 next fall, and was nervous after looking at these reviews. Prof. Gowan was fantastic in my opinion. Lectures were fun, and she does a great job of presenting a lot of different viewpoints. I think the first reviewer must not have come to class. She said we needed to attend, and those of us that did did very well.

Midterm grades were posted immediately and curved after she got rid of ?s  that a lot of people got wrong. I liked that she admitted when she wrote a question poorly. Need to come to lecture; going off of the posted slides is not enough. Emailed that grades were going to be delayed due to technical glitch with egrades. Engaging, great assignments.

She is so unbelievably unorganized when it comes to grading. Our midterm was  W5 and we got them back W8. What if people want to drop? She also said that we had to participate in 3 total discussions online, and she posted one on week 4/5 and then never posted again until week 9. Our grades were late 2 dys. Tests are so content heavy and detailed.

Tips for getting  an A for this class. 1. go to every TA OH. TA will show you how to do assignments step by step. 2. attend lectures. He gave 4 pop quizzes w/o drop, but supper easy. 3. record his review lecture for exams. His reivew covers EVERYTHING on the test, and the text book is really helpful for understanding difficult concepts and terms.

A lot of works to be done in this class. Econ tutor did not offer this quarter so all works had to be done by myself. Homeworks, research paper, and quizzes could be done by group. Professor Tayman helps a lot, he cares about his students. He goes over what's going to be on exam before the exam so focus on what he's saying. READ THE BOOK!!
Pretty hard class overall...only 8% received solid A's. You really need to stay on top of things and really know how to do the homework (he doesn't really tell you how to do the work).

Alot of work in this class. Don't be fooled. Econtutor can only help you so much. Tayman hates econtutor and recently started to grade harder and critique homeworks and papers harder. If you go to econtutor you can pass, but if you want to get an A, you have to work.

There's a lot of work to be done (midterm, final, research paper, assignments, pop quizzes) but most of it can be done in groups and the workload should be expected for an advanced statistics class. He gives a pretty generous curve, and all the material is straight out of the book. And like the previous rater said, EconTutor does help a lot.

Very easy class if you do most of the readings/watch the movies. I personally didn't like her lectures, they didn't have much of an impact on me. They were difficult to understand and sometimes, she would ask confusing questions and get mad when nobody could answer them.

Professor Hernandez is awesome! Her lectures are interesting and she really  cares about her students. She is always happy to help. As long as you complete all the work (2 context assignments, project..), attend discussion, and do well on your take home midterm & final then you will get an A in the course!Hope to take another course with this prof.

Jillian Hernandez is one of the best professors I've had at UCSD thus far. Her grading criteria is clear and there are no surprises. No reason anyone should get less than an A. She posts Powerpoints online but you have to go to lecture to get the entire information. If you don't do the reading, go to class. Nice, funny, caring, relatable professor.

Posts her powerpoints online, but not everything is on the powerpoint. 1 Midterm (25%) and Final (25%) , both of which were take-home exams. For the Context Assignments, you have to attend 2 events and write a 2 page essay relating the events to  course themes. 1 Creative project (10%) Section participation (20%) 2 Context Assignment (20%)

(This is for the Michael Jackson class)I loved this class! Lecture slides were posted, so attendance isn't mandatory, but the lectures were so great I went anyways. If you study the slides, the midterm and final are very easy. There are a ton of extra credit opportunities, especially if you attend lectures!

She's so energetic about music, and plays a variety of examples in the beginning of lecture. If you know piano or have prior experience in music, you should get an A. There's one midterm, two evaluations of piano and singing, and then one final exam. There's also a group performance at the end, in which you perform with your section.

Corey Stone was not the best lecturer for Math 10C. Lessons always seemed convoluted and pace was way too fast. Lectures were focused on examples rather than clear concepts. Learning from the book and practice exams is a MUST. Both midterms and the final seemed "fair" even though the class did below average. Wasn't too helpful during office hours.

Professor Stone was well paced in covering the material for the quarter, a little slow for my preference, but not bad. He is very clear when explaining certain concepts especially during office hours. I highly recommend attending SI sessions because the extra practice really helped. Both midterms and final were fair. Overall a great  professor.

HE IS AMAZING. IF HE IS TEACHING TAKE HIM! The lectures were super clear. He really cares about answering people's questions during lecture. I absolutely recommend him. Just make sure to check your homework answers carefully because the grading is kind of strict on the homework.

I had him for differential equations and he's one of the best math lecturers I've had. He is very clear and easy to follow. Midterms are fair and if it's harder than expected he will curve it generously. A really nice and quirky guy.

I was a bit wary of taking Stone's class after seeing some older reviews, but he must have improved a ton from fall to winter quarter! His lectures were clear and he gives an abundance of examples in lecture. It seems like he's still trying to find the right length/difficulty for his exams, but he does curve if he doesn't get it quite right.

Lectures are an open dialogue. Expect to participate. You should want to participate! She is a PH.D so a lot of what she teaches she is able to relate with her own work experience. 2 Homework Assignments, 1 short class presentation, and a final. Lots of reading, but all of it is fascinating.

Pretty boring class, she had a PPT but doesn't just read off of it she really elaborates and gets into detail. She's passionate about the subject. 2 HW assignments 50 points each, 1 midterm, 1 final exam both super easy. Honestly just show up and pass.

No quizzes. One midterm, one final. One short presentation, a few easy write ups, and a couple easy xtra credit opportunities. She is very clear with her expectations. She has long lectures, no break, but always finds a way to relate to some interesting stories/ video clips. Follow along every class, you will easily get an a.

Honestly , I don't understand what are all these good reviews about. LONG lectures, 3 hours in a row- NO BREAK. She spent a lot of time on things that she doesn't even test about. She was always late in times- we had to have lectures even before the midterm and the final! and also we didn't have any test with open notes as mentioned here .....

Great professor. She's the kind of professor that is passionate about their subject and is very thorough. If you study and show effort, then you will pass with flying colors. She's young so most of the kids in my class are sort of disrespectful which is a shame. She's friendly and smart, she's willing to work with you if you talk to her.

I took his classes when I was a 1st year Ph.D student. Over the years, I found his lectures to be extremely useful in designing circuits. I keep coming back to his books (MicroCMOS and system design book). I appreciate how he taught circuit design with more emphasis on intuition and less on numerical simulation.

First day of class he states something along the lines of "everyone thinks I'm a bad teacher, but I'm not. I just have dumb students." Very unhelpful lectures. A lot of the times he doesn't even go over things you should know, he just states you should know it. Only ECE163 professor so you're SOL anyways.

He is the best in analog circuit design and he knows what he teaches very clearly. I like the way he teaches. he tries to make students understand by themselves. overall, if you are interested in studying, not just getting a good credit, you should be in this class.

His lectures are basically him copying his online notes onto an overhead projector with 5% of it being different material. His office hours consist of him telling you that you should already know the the answer to the question you're asking. UCSD could save money by scrapping lecture and having us teach ourselves and still achieve the same effect.
bang sup sux song

He's my type of professor. He lectures basic concepts and the core of the techniques we need for 20D. His lectures were not boring and class was full every lecture. His midterms were straight forward but the final was very DIFFICULT!!! I butchered the final but still got a B+ in the end. Just do the homework and grasp the techniques he teaches.
Lecture is way too easy, barely learns anything. Homework, however, is very hard, expect the same difficulty on mid and final.

Take this class with Prof. Oprea if you can! He is very clear and explained things so well that I did not have to read the lessons in the book. This class requires you to do a lot of problems, but if you keep practicing, you will definitely get an A. The midterms weren't curved because they were so easy but beware the final was very difficult!

Class is very clear, easy to understand. Homework a bit more difficult, but do it because that is all midterms are about. Final, however, was IMPOSSIBLE. Absolutely unrelated to class material, homework, previous midterms, etc. Great professor but be very cautious with final and midterms!
He breaks down the lecture into clear concise concepts. Plus he's so cute and friendly!

She has the everyday life projects where you talk about one topic per week and how it relates to you. The final and midterm aren't too bad just do the readings, even though there are a lot of them. Lectures are basically the readings and she posts the slides online afterwards so you don't need to go to class.

She gives out a lot of reading, but goes over all of them during lecture so it's in your best interest to go to class. We often have interesting, discussions in class and she's a very engaging lecturer imo. The final is take home, but lengthy and completely free response. Quote out of context: "The only place socialism is a swear word is in the US"

She is generally a pretty chill and laid back professors with some jokes here and there. She moves too quickly through her slides though. HER MIDTERM WAS HARD. On top of that my TA grades hard too. Hopefully the long ass final she gave us can save my grade.

Prof Itzhak is a new prof at UCSD, her lectures mainly involve reading long articles posted on TritonEd, but I only read 5 and then relied on the lecture for my notes. She will eventually post all her slides online with most of the analysis. We have to write 3 reflection essays before the midterm and 3 after. The final is very work-intensive.

Prof. Schuller is indeed not a good teacher. He has strong accent and frequently goes off topic and he is a little bit disorganized since the only thing he writes down during lectures is his calculation. No online homework/clicker needed, no attendance. That's a pro. After all get along with your TA might help a lot, the course itself is not hard

Prof. Schuller is a good researcher but not a good teacher. He has strong Romanian accent so sometimes his explanation is hard to get. Basically learn nothing from him so be prepared to go to ta's review session and do practice problems. The great part is the curve is reasonable. Choose another professor if you have better options anyways.

Ivan Schuller does not teach the class material. If a weekly quiz expects you to know 100% of a topic, Schuller teaches you roughly 20%. This is because he goes off on tangents and explains things that you don't need to know at the expense of what you do. Fairly generous curve though helps. I wish Schuller made it worth my time to go to class.
Learn nothing from him

Professor Foit is an amazing lecturer. I found his lectures very interesting. Definitely take this class with Professor Foit you won't regret.
Awesome prof!! Very fun and interactice class, great elective, perfect class to take if you're on the verge of adding one more class to your load.

If you're looking for an easy elective for your business minor this is not the class for you. This is by far the hardest class I took at UCSD but with hard work and participation, it is possible to get that A.
Still bad after looking back

I took this class years ago and I was now googling professor Hernandez to see what she is up to. It was a great class, but it is only now years later that I understand many things and put them together. What I learned about media and capitalism has given me perspective now, in Law School.

I took her class years ago. I have graduated since and came to RMP now because I see my classes and professors differently now. In retrospect, she was an excellent teacher and mentor. She was tough but opened my mind to many new ideas. I am now in graduate school.  She was more of a grad school prof type and was great when you got to talk 1 on1

Prof Hernandez's lectures were very interesting and I learned so much from her! I enjoyed her teaching style but with 300 students packed in that  old room, it was sometimes hard to hear her and to fully follow lectures and discussions.

Terrible experience having this professor.  Did not try to help the students out at all, ridiculous essay assigned, and she gave no information as to what was going to be on the midterm.  Overall her teaching style is extremely unorganized.

I had her for TDGE 11 and she is really laid back and easy to pass. There's weekly quizes on the films we watch in class and she basically wants you to pass. The quizzes are super easy as well as the midterm. Would defintley recommend if you want to get credit for your art GE.

One of the most hardworking professors I've ever had--and it shows on all of his lectures. He makes sure that the students can get something out of the class and goes out of his way to make the class interactive and fun.
Grade break down to many small assignments.

We had two papers, each roughly 5-6 pages. Otherwise, the bulk of our work was on creating podcasts (lots of fun!) and analyzing the rhetorical and transformative power of comedy. Kiik was very quiet and monotonous in lecture (I could see the script he read on his PowerPoint slides). Otherwise, he is a very nice and approachable prof.

I really liked the class dynamic. We had class discussions and went over the readings one by one (with a student leading each reading). We had to do them all (which was a lot at times) but I learned a lot and was overall really happy with the course.

HIUS 136 was a moving and eye-opening class. Professor Gutierrez is a really great professor with really interesting arguments and a great lecturer. On the other hand, as far as courses for the DEI requirement go this is definitely one of the harder ones--lots and lots of reading and your entire grade is based on two 10 page papers.

Every class all he does is stand in front of the room and talk. Incredibly boring and unhelpful so don't bother going to lecture. Readings are long and difficult to get through. Much of your grade will depend on your TA. The one midterm and final were 8-10 page papers.

Professor literally stands in front of the class and reads off a sheet of paper. Worst lecturer I have ever encountered at UCSD! Don't attend lecture, just do the readings. I recommend taking 7C with another professor, like Luis Alvarez.

Good professor, he's available if you need help. Very boring but his comments are very interesting if your listening. three options for grading just did the 20 pages instead of the midterm and final option.

Our group absolutely enjoyed this class. He was very accessible and very supportive. I'm glad the Latin American Studies department got him to teach the intro course here at UCSD; the skills we learned and the research we've already done will help out a lot with the thesis later on.

He is a really good professor, his lectures are very entertaining, and he is very knowledgeable about the subject. It is a hard class that requires a lot of careful reading, but you'll end up learning a lot and completely understanding Mexican politics.

While his lectures were informative, his tests were awkwardly formatted and phrased. The textbooks were excessive, 4 were required, 2 actually read, all containing the same information.

Professor Shirk did a good job with lectures, however he required WAY too many materials for the class. While his book was both interesting and informative, the other books redundantly covered the same material. The combined 4 books cost over $200 and only two were required for regular reading.

I did not like him as a professor. I was very interested in the material but he had boring lectures. He tries hard during his lectures but in the end he isnt interesting. His exams are hard and his study guides are not helpful.

Class took at NYU. "Environmental Art and Activisim". The class is not focused on any topics, it's more a discussion about life class. You basically work for her project and don't have any opportunity to make/speak about your own. But it is an easy A. Show up and discuss in class and you'll have an A

I had Natalie as a prof at NYU, where she teaches now and is tenured. The class, "Environmental art activism", sounded promising, but wound up being  a waste of credits and time. There was no structure to the class and she didn't submit a syllabus until the 3rd week of the semester. I didn't gain anything from her class and barely learned anything.

Natalie is a wonderful person, and I became very close with her over the course. However, I often felt lost with her instructions. It was not unusual for her to assign literally impossible things. She is interesting, but unless you are completely flexible in everything from body(climbing) to mind to time she may not be worth the elective credit.
can't remember my class #.... do remember that she is craaaazy. great artist but WOW. i don't even know what this class was about. given, i was young and dumb, but she was all over the place.

She was directly insulting and did not care for student opinions. She forced students to work on her own projects which had little relevance to the course description. Guest speaker was incredulous as to the lack of material taught in class. She never came to class on time, sometimes an hour late.

Out of many professors I have had, Dr. Steiner was amazing. She engages & challenges you to think about what you are saying. Her course was well planned, she was specific about expectations & sets goals that are achievable. No, she is not an easy A professor but I actually felt like I learned in this course and that's the point of going to school.

Worst online Teacher I have ever had! She offers no help! she is also very rude if you ask her for help. she does not respond to email or gives feedback of any sort.  I along with 43 other students are petitioning our grade. I hope Brandman University will let her go as she give Brandman a bad name!

I personally don't agree with all the negative comments about her. I had her for Hum and she was great. The essay prompts are straightforward, reading is doable, and the final is decent. She helps out a LOT if you go to office hours.
APPALLING.  CLOSEMINDED.  ONLY WANTS YOU TO SAY WHAT SHE THINKS ON YOUR ESSAYS.  MEANSPIRITED.  AVOID.

she's pretty bad, don't be fooled. she's not helpful in office hours, except to inform you that your ideas (as long as they're not hers) are quite wrong. luckily, she tells you exactly what she would prefer you write about, so if you're good at defending an argument you (a) don't understand or (b) don't agree with, she's wonderful.

Diaz is a good teacher and shows her passion for teaching everyday but her personal feelings are too much of a focus for the classroom. Vegan feminism globalist class that was supposed to be English. Professor Diaz is very passionate about what she teaches! She is an amazing professor and would highly recommend her for English 100. ZULEMA DIAZ!  She's an amazing teacher! She genuinely cares for her students. She's the type of teacher that will stay after to help you understand the work better. I was dropped by the professor for missing two consecutive classes. A little ridiculous considering I had all assignments turned in and was always a part of  the class discussions. Attend lectures, study each slide and actively participate- a good grade in this class is achievable. Scheffler is a super good teacher if you stick through the first 4 weeks, which are the most confusing (what to study detail wise).

Hard class, nice guy, POOR teacher. His lectures were worthless; he rambles, goes off on tangents and is always introducing things you 'don't need to know'. Tests are HARD. Yes this course requires a lot of memorizing but GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS. he is extremely helpful during office hours if you show interest that you want to learn. Easy A if you are dedicated.

I loove Dr. Scheffler. He has very generous office hours...12 hours a week!!!! I went to his office hours religiously and am so happy I did. He is so helpful, you just have to ask and show some interest in the material! He explains things well and goes beyond the text book to give even more knowledge for understanding. So inspirational!

She tends to go on tangents during lecture. Really slow. The content itself is quite interesting but I had more fun reading it off the textbook than from the hearing it at lecture. She isn't the normal prof for this course and honestly I hope she isn't again. PSYC 6 is an interesting course, but I did not like Sanders as a professor. Her lectures were boring, slow, and have no lecture slides. The class is straightforward, but the exams are actually pretty hard. I have a solid psychology background, and I struggled with her exams.

Getting at least a B is easy, but her lectures are really boring and slow.  You need to read the book for the tests because she doesn't go over everything in lecture.
She was a little hard to follow at times. She often drifted in lecture to her own stories. She was very nice though. Her notes were not very helpful, discussion saved me and my TA was great.

TERRIBLE PROF!!! Cares a lot about students learning, but besides lecturing, all the other aspects of the class are ran by the head TA. Be sure to go to lecture and go to sections, esp the head TA's sections. Imo interesting class. I definitely learned a lot of biochemistry which was actually useful in other upper div classes such as cell bio. TAs make the exams, so definitely show up to one or more sections. Montal is very passionate about biochemistry and it definitely shows! Would recommend.
lectures a little bit boring. strong eastern european accent. she seems to be a little bit dogmatic in terms of mulitculturalism

Professor Klimova is a very boring professor. She spends at least 20 minutes reviewing what she said two days ago in lecture and spends the last 30 talking monotonously. Not a very great lecturer. Cool guy but a little awkward. Interesting class with good articles chosen though. As long as you show up to class for the quizzes and show that you somewhat do the readings, should get a good grade.
I had Virginia for MMW12 and MMW13 and I absolutely loved her! She cared a lot about her students and was kind and helpful.

His lectures can get a little off topic. This makes it hard to sit through but remember he's a jazz musician, don't expect too much structure! Haha. Recommended for those with insomnia and no concern about their grades.

Very easy course. The lectures are good. Material covered is very elementary. Its an Easy A course.

One of the scariest professors to walk in on late, but was very helpful in understanding the course. Gauges class understanding of material by class participation. Tests are fair. Hilarious teaching style.
Professor Tartakovsky not only teaches well, he is also very interesting to talk to. He made the class fun to attend.

I thought Prof. Eric Lauga was the best professor in the MAE dept but after taking Prof. Daniel Tartakovsky's class I have completely changed my mind! Prof. Tartakovsky should get a professor of the year award!

His style of teaching involves a lot of student participation and active learning. Even if you are wrong (or if the class is collectively wrong, which happens a lot), he teases in a good way and the humiliation is significantly reduced. Great professor! Tests are very fair and representative of the material we go over during lecture.

She is one of the most caring professors I've seen. You don't have to read if you go to lecture. She let the students choose the key terms for the final. For a rather repetitive and boring course, Dr. Nguyen is an excellent professor. Her lectures and slides can be a bit convoluted in class so you should probably pay attention closely. This professor truly cares about her students. The lecture after the election, she teared up telling us to be careful if we choose to protest (as a student was run over the night before during a protest). She explains concepts clearly, and genuinely wants you to learn. Definitely a solid choice.

She's a good teacher for a relatively boring subject. She's passionate about what she teaches, but she does need to work on her lecture skills a little bit, but she is a new professor after all so she'll get better over time. If you have to take DOC and she's teaching it, I recommend her.

She's a new teacher here and you can tell. She does not allow technology (including laptops and phones) in lecture, which is really unrealistic now-a-days. She gets very upset if you talk in class and will call you out. If you go to the lectures, you do not have to read. If you read, you do not have to go to lecture. Great prof. Not great class.

This class was alright, I guess. She isn't too great of a lecturer -- she tends to drone and move quickly past important/crucial information, and doesn't have much information up on the PowerPoint. It's hard to take notes in class because of how fast-paced lectures are. 5 online quizzes, 1 research paper, 3 exams. Study fro them and you'll be fine.

5 online quizzes, 2 midterms, a paper and the final. If you study for the exams and take the quizzes there is no reason you wouldn't pass this class. Some of the test questions are the same as the ones on the quizzes, and she puts the open response questions on the study guide. Class may seem long, but we always watch a movie. Class taken at CSULB.
Professor Wills is a musical genius, and he freely gives his time to his students outside of class to help prepare for exams.  You have to put work in outside of class time to do well.

You can tell that Wills has been teaching this class for a while. The tests are fair, but you will have to take the time to study all the material & there is a slight curve.

He's such a sweet professor but his lectures are very boring and long. He likes to go off tangent and talk about a topic for quite some time. We had bi weekly quizzes in discussion, one midterm and one final, but they were all pretty reasonable although they were in free response format. I would recommend him!
He just reminds me of my grandpa, so sweet and education.

Professor Wills is a very old school type professor. His lectures in person tend to be very dry due to his monotonous voice. However, he is VERY knowledgeable and VERY helpful. Good lectures and combined with homework don't even really need to read the textbook. Difficult tests but is accessible and will help if you work for it.

For 6a, Berniolles basically had the same exams and grading scale as johnson. I think people expected her to be different but she literally had the same exams as Johnson. She is accessible outside of the class in case you have any questions or problems. If you skip class multiple times, you are likely doomed since she does tend to work problems out on paper. I found that her lectures go over basic stuff but the homework and test are way harder than the stuff she lectures on. I find that unfair.

Honestly, Berniolles isn't the worst professor BUT I'd recommend a different one. She goes super fast in her lectures, and you can't keep up with notes at all. Her tests are difficult and her homework is harder than her example problems. I think she is a good teacher to ask questions, but in her lectures she isn't successful. She has clicker Qs :(.

Dr. B has an excellent class! She is very accessible and clarifies any questions you may have. Her lectures provide a great overview of the chapter. Professor Lepic is really knowledgeable about linguistics. Lectures were mandatory for participation grade, and there was a lot of reading for each week. He's a great teacher and gives very good examples to explain what he's teaching.  He is very funny and makes the subject interesting. He is open to hearing different views.
His slides and references are hilarious. Has two multiple choice questions as group work each class. He gets you to engage in lectures.

The lectures are boring, because the materiale she teaches is kind of boring. It is the most theoretical part of the finance theory. Too hard final compared to the problem sets and the midterms, but her curve is so generous.

If your answer does not exactly match the grading rubric, you will lose points. TAs were also not very helpful compared to other classes I have been in, though they were adequate. This class will break your 4 years of 4.0 even if you think you know the material, just because of stupid grading. I would recommend attending class more than I did.

She reads directly off the slides for all of lecture. Course material is fairly straightforward and explained well, but the test grading is utterly confusing. Easy up until the final. Final are all concept questions that we never were exposed to in lecture, problem sets, or online notes. Final is INSANELY hard so go in with a strong A if u want to do well in the class.

since no one has updated recently... she literally reads off of her lecture slides which are posted on TED. her tests so far are exactly off of the Problem Sets and her grading is very generous; either you do well on your midterms+ final or you do well on just your final then she'll take the higher score. Pretty easy, self teaching class.
very knowledgeable BUT stay away if possible hw is too long, too much material is presents

terrible, just horrible

Mackie is a really interesting person but is not the best teacher. His lectures are read straight off a slide show and he is very dry as a lecturer. You don't need to go to lecture often but discussion is mandatory. He has really good TAs though and they help on the midterm and final.
Unnecessarily difficult class. Very hard to follow Prof. Mackie during lecture, and very unclear as to what is expected. Take another intro Polisci class, this one is not worth it.
Very boring. The professor speaks in a single tone.

Highly organized class, great slides in BB, grading is clear. Flexible office hours. Care about students. Would def. take him again!

Lectures are great - interesting, entertaining, but on-topic. Says you have to read, but I never actually cracked the book because his lectures are so complete. He encourages questions, even those not strictly on-topic. Participation for grade, by either answering a few questions or raising a few of your own. Very little homework. 100% lecture.

I learned more about hominin evolution in his human diet class that all my other biological anthropology classes combined. His lectures are funny and engaging yet always focused and on-topic.   Readings are pretty minimal (2 short articles per week on average)and 100% online (yay!) Follow the study guides and you'll ace the exams no problem.

For a beginner, her class material is not that hard but It is really hard to understand at first. After a period of studying, it gradually makes sense but the class already left you far away back... I Know that is kind of academic requirement but I still did not like her teaching style.  Know your material clearly, or it is hard for you to pass.
J'ADORE Madame. She's so dedicated and an amazing professor to have. Funny and really enthusiastic. One of my favorite profs at UCSD!
Not a bad class, but MUST know your french and be really good at it.

Took this class in the special summer session. It's very hard if you haven't taken french in a while or are just learning the 5D material. Most people had taken tons of french. Small tests and quizzes and a oral final. Françoise loves her students and is very nice.
Dedicated, experienced, commited

Miller is an inspirational and respected writing professor. He is devoted to make his students better writers, better thinkers, and better scholars. Very good professor. He gives a lot of good feedback on your paper. If you want to pass SDCC1 and really learn somethings in writing, take his class.
BEST PROFESSOR EVER! Everyone in our class passed SDCC 1 this year. It was possible thanks to the experienced teaching that he showed throughout the class. Definitely recommend him!
so good!
Prof Miller is so experienced with this class that he helps his students to gradually build confidence.

FIRST OF ALL, her lectures are extremely unorganized and unprepared. She claimed in the first lecture that she was rated as the worst professor last year, only to spend a quarter proving it. This is one of the worst classes I've ever taken.  The professor is disorganized and unclear. Just heard that Prof. Varghese will be leaving UCSD to go to Duke.  A big loss for UCSD. I really liked her.  She has a high standard and a good role model for students. Dr. Shyni ma'am is my role model. Thank you Shyni ma'am for being so energetic, enthusiastic, and fresh in teaching methodology. Your research is equally great.
Let's you retake midterms if you don't pass. A little hard to understand because of his accent, but overall great professor.

Jolany is a really good professor and one of the clearest I've ever had. He won't test you on anything he doesn't teach in class. He interacts with the students during his lectures . Very kind professor and polite.  I would take him again if I have the opportunity.
His accent kind of made it hard to understand his lectures. But when he posted videos and offered very long office hours, my frown turned to a smile. Very helpful and sincere.
Nice professor. His video lectures are very helpful for exams. If your grade is not fine , you can retake the mid exams.  I really love Jolany

Jolany understand students very good. He is nice and kind teacher. He explain everything very clearly. His video lectures are helpful for exams . He invite students for challenge to solve questions in black board

GREAT professor if you care about culture and racism. Lots of analyzing. He wants participation, and discussion was mandatory. Good prof.  Nice accent & Funny. Homework and finals are hard. But he gives good grades.

i hate thermo, but this guy wasn't too bad. had pretty understandable lectures, but was kind of mean when you answered something wrong in class. haha - he says aluminum funny.

His exams are irrelevant to the lecture and he does not tell students what would be on the exam.
