I love this guy man. Taught my first class in college ever and the guy truly taught me some very important skills to use in college. He's a dreamer, but best of all, he knows how to relate to his students and make life easier for us. He's way too smart for this job though, taught way beyond what we need in the lectures lol.
Attend lecture, do homework, go to office hours, No reason why you can't pass the class. I got an A+ my first A at UCSD

Tiee's lectures weren't very helpful, but they aren't mandatory. He lets you have one 8x11 sheet of notes on both midterms, and two sheets for the final. The tests are very similar to homework assignments and the practice tests that he posts. He has various grading scales, and will use whichever one maximizes your grade. Overall an easy A.
Tiee was great for math 10C. He posts all his lecture notes online, so attendance is not mandatory, but if you attend lecture he is surprisingly funny
He's a great professor. He's not harsh with his grading and will do his best to explain every single problem to you.  His tests are easier than the homework.

I definitely think he could improve his teaching skills, he taught us conceptual information in lecture but never showed us how to implement it. Expected us to know things we've never learned before, homework assignments are HARD.
Way too hard, and his teaching style is not the best.

The class is more about "which opinions do you agree" more than "what did you learn." The course touches upon regular intro gender study materials more than social movements. It is nice to be exposed to introductive ideas before getting deeper, but sometimes the lecture gets too deep into schools of theory of gender study. Doable for DEI

Great person! Went to office hours a few times, always friendly and open to talk. He does have a slight accent though, but he's definitely a fair grader and will tell you exactly what will be on the test. Great TA's, overall easy class in general.

As a person, prof Lee is really nice and caring about his students, but as a lecturer, he really needs to speak up and not mumble things... I'm seriously having a hard time understanding him. Otherwise he really provides a lot of his materials online and is super clear on grading criteria, just pay attention in class and to the materials!
So the grading criteria for this lab course is confusing, and the lectures are boring. Lots of statistics contents which make you wonder if you're actually taking a physics course.

Sinha really cares for his students but he... doesn't really have a good teaching style. His lectures are usually 100% conceptual, which doesn't really suit electrical/magnetic physics. That being said, your ability to problem solve is based on reading the text book and doing assigned problems. Tests are "eh" fair. *Allows cheat sheet on quizzes.

i recommend taking him. His class is an easy A, if u pay attention.He has 4 quizzes(20% each) and drops one. For this class, he put practice exams before quizzes and final, and the questions in the tests were almost identical. He can trick you so pay attention to the detail. His homework assignments are not graded. iclicker is used as bonus.
Sinha is a great professor. First of all, he is very clear if you are attentive. Second, his quiz is relatively easy. I got A+ and A in 2a and 2b. Last, he is very funny. I really recommend him.

I took him for 2A and 2B. 2B was a lot harder than 2A. I got a A for 2A but a B for 2B. He's a very nice helpful person, but his lectures are boring and not that great of a teacher. I taught myself everything and if it wasn't for clicker, I wouldn't go to class. Google or Meet students from his past classes, he reuses quiz and test questions.

This guy is awesome. His energy in class makes him one of the more engaging lecturers that I've had at UCSD. He also really cares about his students and is interested in what they have to say. Loose class structure, he let's you decide how much you want to enjoy the class. Definitely take this if you want a fun, interesting class!

Okay, I heard good things about this class so I went into it pretty confident, however BEWARE because this class is by no means easy. TAKE IT PASS NO PASS. Very few people actually get good grades and for the work demand that is actually required it is not worth it. Fun flashback to childhood but that is it.

Simply amazing. Quizzes + midterm essay + final quiz & final essay. If you pay attention in class then the quizzes are very easy, & you pretty much get to pick your own essay topic. Everything but the final quiz is take home because he's considerate with those who are still learning English. Very helpful during office hours & overall a great prof.
One of the more enjoyable profs at UCSD. Took him in the late 90's and found him not to follow the mold of some of the other lit profs. He was will to listen and give constructive criticism.

Potts is one of a dying breed- truly excellent professors. Yes, lots of reading, and he grades you harshly, but he loves what he is talking about, he offers you so much in the way of paper ideas- practically decided my thesis for me-  and he has fabulous hair. If you like a broad range of topics you can write on and wonderful books to read take him

He is a great and patient teacher. I have no previous experience whatsoever and I was really anxious at first about taking a COGS class but I learned a lot and actually had fun programming our "robot" to dance. You take 4 online quizzes that you can retake anytime and there are no due dates. The midterm and final are group projects.
Gives great feedback when reviewing papers, very caring, engaging, 3 papers per quarter with plenty of time to write them

He's very funny and knows a lot about the subject that he's teaching.  Typically he lectures for an hour and then shows a film for the next two hours.  All of his lecture ppts are online so if you just read those then you can get an easy A.  Almost every week he has a small online quiz that is super easy since you get an hour to answer 5 questions.
Professor Thayer is the sweetest teacher i've had. She's caring and understanding and lectures are interesting. She is a very good teacher - TAKE HER! no doubts, you won't regret it.
Wonderful theater teacher. Very involved with student's performance and progress

This class left me hungry to learn more about the craft of acting. I was disappointed to learn there wasn't an Acting III class. I know my classmates & I would eagerly enroll for other classes with this incredibly gifted teacher and acting mentor/coach. Everyone in our class grew more confident & effective in communicating purposefully in public.

This was such an amazing class.  I looked forward to it each week and I miss it.  Emmelyn was a terrific instructor.  She gave honest and authentic feedback to each of us. An occasionally she would  share with us hilarious stories of her time working in the theater.  Since she has been in the business she knows what she is talking about!
Emmelyn is a very gifted teacher. I highly recommend her classes, whether you're just starting out as an actor or wanting to brush up your skills and take your acting to the next level.

Very clear and precise, his lectures are very easy to follow and understand. He is good about keeping to his office hours schedule and the exams are pretty much like the homeworks. Also, he has neat handwriting which is a huge plus on the blackboard.
Prof is good. But exams are long
Professor Kaitlin gives awesome lectures along with appropriate homework. Her quizzes are also helpful to understand the contents of lectures.

Great professor. She provides multiple chances to improve your grade. Her curves are always in you favor. From the first class she made it clear that you can't get a grade lower than your raw score  Another note to mention is that she sometimes makes mistakes in class, but when corrected, she would cancel any point deductions made due to her error

Her lectures and exams are very clear. She lets you replace a midterm grade with your quiz grades or just drop your quiz grade (which ever helps most). Her exams are also very fair,  if you listened in lecture and did the homework you'll do well in the class. I would definitely recommend Dr. Fisher.

Probably one of least chill prof's I've ever seen. Tends to explode at students quite a bit. The material is easy, but she will take points off of your tests for the smallest things. It's not hard to get a 95%+, but it will be hard to get 100%. Also she makes A LOT of mistakes during lecture; don't take her if this is your first time w/ chem.

High level of enthusiasm! You can tell she really loves the topic she's talking about. As for the course, as long as you pay attention in lecture and really know the concepts she stresses, you'll do fine. Very lenient on grading (88 is an A- excluding any curve), so she's a great way to start general chem!

Casey is a caring and genuine professor. In lecture, he uses the chalkboard to write down concepts, problems and proofs. For his 2 midterms and final, he includes extra problems that can increase your score (you can use cheat sheet!). Recommend to study homework problems and understand concepts. The tests may be challenging but the class is curved!

This man is the only person that has UCSD's physics department going. He's a real gem. So intelligent, caring, and understanding. He knows what he's teaching and how to teach it. Yes, the class is tough, yes, his tests are hard, but his curve is majestic and he really helps you get it together. Plus, he's super easy on the eyes.

I like this guy. He is pretty good at explaining physics and makes everything easier to see. He has a very quiet voice though so make sure you sit in front. His tests are very fair and straight forward, nothing will surprise you. Just do the homework. Very approachable and answers questions promptly.

I took Conger SS1 of 2016. He's a great lecturer  and explains physics so that we understand the concepts and math behind physics, though he is a bit monotone.  The class was 60% 3/4 Quizzes, 40% Final. He drops questions and class is curved. I had raw score of 82%, 91% after questions dropped and got an A post-curve.  Overall very recommended!

He lectures well, and his explanations and examples are very clear. He will also respond to you (quickly) when you ask him a question.  His quizzes and final are very difficult, however, even with the notes he allows you to bring. There is a (very!) generous curve, but the difficulty of the exams may dishearten you.
He tries his best to give inspirational and helpful lectures but ends up getting most of the students leaving the class or sleeping during the lectures.
The worst professor ever met in UCSD. His lecture materials do not related to his exams.

Egregiously organized class. There was even confusion even over grading a MULTIPLE CHOICE midterm. One of the first professors I've had where I had no proper idea what was coming when I walked into the Final Exam. Discussions are far more helpful than lecture. If possible try to avoid taking this prof.
Literally the worst professor at UCSD. Horribly organized class. Some of the material that was announced on the final was never covered and not even on the book! The exams were really hard.
Is a nice professor and helpful, since his lecture notes are online. . Thank you!
Good lecturer who explains well.
She is a really great lecturer. And if you can understand every example in her lectures, you may get a good grade in exam. It's the summer session, she made 20C be concise and wonderful.

Michelle Bodnar was new to teaching (as far as when this was written), but her absolute passion in teaching made her lecture better than even experienced professors. Office hour is the goto choice if you don't understand something or want to learn more. Textbook is good to read but  not necessary since her lecture is most times better than textbook

Bodnar is truly passionate about math. Her lectures were interesting, and she was able to make the once tedious contents interesting by using fun analogs and hilarious examples. For example, I still remember this question: ''Mary was in mad love with David, and the rate of change of her excitement is blah blah blah..."

Everything in her class goes just well. A great lecturer who can make everything clear and interesting in lectures, having office hours (with TAs) every weekday so easily accessible for questions, grade fairly and always gives a curve if the exam goes hard. Homework loads are a little bit heavy but definitely worth doing it.

Really kind, energetic, and helpful. Perhaps a little too kind to her students, but constantly gives good advice and confidence, which for me is my preferred learning style. She's also a mezzo soprano, and as a fellow mezzo, she gave me better tips than my previous voice teachers (all sopranos) had. A really lovely teacher, thoroughly recommend.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS. This was the WORST professor I ever had. He is an arrogant and pompous lecturer who insists that his students meet standards of what he calls the "real world". However, it is obvious that he has very little "real world" experience.  Got a D from him, re-took with a different professor (a competent one) and got an A.
Expect him to be the president of UTA. PMR consp.

He lectures as if he is reciting what he memorized the night before. He is a pompous egomaniac who has nothing but contempt for his students; he is downright rude. He DOES NOT care about you, he is only there for his research. Avoid at all costs.

Prof. Karbhari was the best prof. I've had in my years here. He was a very difficult grader, but he taught the material well, was clear in class, and was extremely helpful outside of class. I'm happy for him and his new post at U of Alabama, but I know his prestige will be missed.

Not an easy teacher, but what is most annoying about him is the fact that he is ridiculously anal about everything. He took students' SKATEBOARDS AWAY during exams because he thought they might be using it to cheat! Tests and quizzes aren't easy, so DO YOUR HOMEWORK AND LABS WELL!

I had him for CSE 100.  His class wasn't super easy or super hard.  But he was super helpful during office house.  He is approachable, friendly, and willing to help, which isn't true for a lot of other professors in the CS department.  Overall a good teacher, would recommend.

I do not like his lectures because he basically reads off Kube's slides, but he's helpful during his office hours and does care for students. His tests are trickier than other CSE 100 professors. Overall, his grading is fair and the average grade is a B. Also a weeder class for those who do not really understand data structures.
Tests are tricky.

One of the best professors I've had. Crystal clear and interesting lectures. Is easily available outside of class and very helpful. Exams are not easy, but not unreasonable either, all the material is reflected in either lectures or assignments. Would take this professor again without hesitation, I definitely learned and retained a lot.

I think this may be his first time teaching 100, but he is doing an amazing job at it. No other CSE course I have taken has come close to how helpful his lectures are and how well they complement the programming assignments. Admittedly, exams require attention to detail, but if you work for it, you'll do well. Absolutely great professor.

I took Boerneke for SSI 2016, and I believe it was his first time as a professor for this class. He was awesome and provided me a great base for o-chem that allowed me to really grasp the concepts and succeed in 140B. He was also pretty funny and his lectures were very engaging. Definitely would take another course with him if I could.

The questions on the quizzes were representative of the example he gives in class. All quizzes were plug and chug, so just make sure you have the equations written on your cheat sheet and you'll be fine. My lowest quiz score was 8/10. Just show up and pay attention, and write your cheat sheets. He's not the greatest teacher but grades fairly.

He is very clear.  Teaches what is in the book so the material is reinforced.  He doesn't require clickers which is golden.  He listened to students' feedback and changed his course accordingly.  The quizzes are very fair and if yu go to class and do the homework you will be fine.

I gave him high scores for easy as hw is easy (there are platforms that walk you through them) and tests are alright if you understand the material and study the examples he uses in class. Practice problems don't help. He's pretty bad at explaining things and reading the book is much better. He has clickers which suck because it forces you to go.
The only week that I actually learned physics from class is when sub came in for him.

Avoid this professor AT ALL COSTS. This is literally thee worst professor/teacher I have EVER had in my entire academic career. He does not explain concepts well and provides poor examples during lecture. The only period of time where I actually learned in his class was when he had a substitute professor fill for him during the week.

Can I rate her 0? I literally took another class in order to learn what she didn't teach. Doesn't go over any example problems. The first time you actually see how problems are solved is after the homework, after the quizzes, during the reviews. Lectures were useless. The only class I've gone "I'm skipping; I'll be more productive with self-study."
The worst ever professor in the USA I have taken. If you want pass the class with a good grade, better sit in the class and never ask any question!!!
Do not take her class. It's horrible!!! The Professor is useless.

Class material is relatively easy, but she makes it hard.  Very unhelpful and misleading.  Went to all office hours, did all homework, and ended up with a C in the class.  Went to her personal office hours because she said she would offer help for upcoming tests, did not happen.  Avoid her if you can.

take the time to rework your 4-year plan to not have her for this class. I ended up with an A (which she muct have pulled out of a hat) but pray that I will never need this information again...oh wait, i'm an engineer

Emison is a visionary in Paralegal Studies. He facilitates an environment of extreme learning. I have never learned so much in such a short amount of time. Also, he is probably the best resource in the UCSD program for obtaining an internship. The only complaint I had was that he only taught one class,  I wish he taught more. He is that good.

Mr. Emison is very hard working. His enthusiasm towards his research and goals are what make him a focused and dedicated professor. He is well qualified, dynamic and enthusiastic. He ensures that his students get the quality education they deserve. He also has very good communication skills to explain the subject in a simple and systematic way.
He is well-prepared for his lectures. And he has really clear hand-writings. The exams are fair and well-related with his lectures.
He is a friendly professor. He is patient when students are asking questions. If you go to his lecture, you will excel the test.

1. His MATH 20D includes 60% or less of the textbooks. Comparing to MIT OpenCourseWare's 18.03, his classes contains more power series solutions and less Laplace/Fourier/Convolution, which prevents many's deaths. 2. He can answers 85% percent of all questions popped up during/after lectures. 3. His test is at about 40% of his lecture difficulty.

Decent lecturer.  Write all his notes on the board. Homework and in-class examples are important since questions from his quizzes and tests are similar to the homework questions. And pretty patient during his office hour.

I could not understand him because of his heavy accent. However, he wrote down everything he said onto his tablet, and emailed all the notes to us. For the most part, his notes were helpful. His examples from lecture were not really helpful for homework problems. But he is willing to help students.
Prof. Paar is a great lecturer. Please don't be afraid of the bi-weekly quiz. As long as you make some notes during the class especially the derivation, you will be just fine.

It's easy to overlook how good of a professor Paar is if you don't pay really good attention in lecture. If you put in effort to listen and understand during lecture though, he becomes a great professor. My suggestion is to right down any questions you have about the lecture and come to him after class. He was willing to stay as long as you want.

Great professor to have if you are a physics major or are really enthusiastic about physics. Has high expectations, but he always presents the material very thoroughly and cares about students learning. Quizzes are very concept/intuition based and involve mostl derivations and explanations rather than computations, which may be tough to get used to
Prof. Paar is a really caring professor. Also, if you truly likes physics, you won't be afraid of his quizzes like some may do.

Very fair class. Even when the material gets more difficult in the latter half, it is still manageable because all 8 quizzes (which are weekly--sometimes a pain) are multiple choice. Just don't slack off in the class, as it's fast-paced due to weekly hw/quizzes. Teacher himself is very old but he's nice and cares about us. Read your book :)
Her teaching is OK. Tests are not easy(but on the fair side). The grade cut-offs make it difficult to get an A and curve does not help a lot. Aim for 91% for a solid A.

I really liked Chilukuri's nutrition class, but here are pros and cons. Pros: Cares about students, ties material to real world diseases, and engages students with questions during lecture. Con: Some details gone over in lecture aren't in the book, so if you didn't understand her explanation in lecture, you might need to ask her after class.

The course itself is very time consuming. Weekly quizzes, 2 or 3 lab reports, a midterm, and a final. She doesn't podcast, so good luck if you miss the 8am class. Final research paper is an independent 10+ page project; don't expect much help. Competency tests are complete bs, TA's will grade you on how "proficient" you are at lab techniques.

I liked her a lot, she made lectures clear and interesting, and tests were SO doable, but she did say her tests aren't as hard as they were once before, planning on TAing for and the information is fun, its based a lot on diseases from deficiencies. Def a doable class!
Easy-going and funny. Brought us snacks more than once. East to talk to.

Do not take her for nutrition. She wrote her slides right before class and then was frequently having to change them because they were filled with errors-same goes for her quizzes. It made the material extremely confusing for a relatively easy class. The exams had questions on things she only mentioned once and weren't even in her slides.

Took this class during summer-- professor really cares about the students and their grades. As long as you pay attention/study the lectures, the midterm is fine (short answer/long answer). The final was a 7pg policy proposal (you get to pick the topic yourself), but he let us rewrite our finals after turning them in and getting feedback :D

I suppose I have a very different experience than most with Mr. Ward. I did not find him amusing. I found him to be a Poli Sci snob and a stickler for the rules of academia. The "cool-guy" persona seems like a front to me. I really had to push myself to attend his lectures since my eyes hurt from rolling them so much.
Great guy. Takes his time out of class to clearly explain what needs to be done. Good humor too. Essays are explained clearly and thoroughly.
He''s sooooo good looking.  Also he''s smart and was always there to help me.  Just remember to staple your work before you turn it in because he doesn''t have a stapler to offer you.

Very well-versed in Political Theory and explains all of the readings explicitly in lecture. Expects precise writing and general understanding in the course, but will help with anything if asked. Attendance not mandatory, but if you do not go, do the reading, and vice-versa. Genuinely funny, introspective, and intelligent young professor.

He was a funny and entertaining professor; knows what he's talking about. This class is mainly about drugs and how they function within the brain, so it's a lot of information, but as long as you pay attention and memorize the information, the class should be fairly easy :D

Datko is really funny and a great teacher, I highly recommend taking him for any class that you get. I had him and he was really clear and concise but certainly does make you study a lot of material as everything is "fair game." Overall, I would take again. He is definitely a professor I will remember in my later years.

This isn't an easy and fun blowoff class. You need to spend hours memorizing terms in other languages. It is poorly structured with long, pointless lectures. The only redeeming qualities of the class is that the professor is really nice and honestly sweet. Also, the final (performance with your group) was really fun. Good memories. Will be missed.

Avoid. Class is half lecture, half dance. Lecture is on a country's history and you are quizzed on the respective country's handout. Her lecture is totally unrelated to the quiz (quizzes are terribly formatted and arbitrary--memorize termsdefinition in the country's language). Not responsive with email and sometimes provides confusing comments.

8 quizzes, 2 papers and a final group performance. The quizzes are on dance terms which are in the native language so it's very hard to memorize. Plus, her lectures are not related tohelpful for the quizzes. Final performance is fun but you need to spend time outside of class (3 hrweek). Not recommend this class if you want an easy A.
Confusing lectures! The worst Professor at UCSD! Just don't take this class.

I was counting the days/minutes/seconds/milliseconds for this class to be over. She's an impudent being. Her comment were off-base most of the time. If you want to be verbally admonished, take her class otherwise stay far away. She may be a nice person outside of class, but if you're her student, forget about it. RUN!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
Albright is so clearly into the subjects he's teaching about it makes the lectures so much more interesting. Loved this class.

He is awesome! He gives interesting lectures, and everything that appears on the tests are almost all from the lecture. It is a little bit tough, but he taught me a lot. There were no homework, and the grade comes from three parts: 100 for final, 50 for midterm and 9 for sona-credit. there is also 9 for extra credit, and can  improve your grade.

Albright was a great professor. Lectures were very interesting and held my attention. He grades on a normal curve centered on a C+ but with extra credit, you can increase your grade by as much as a full letter. As long as you go to class, pay attention, take notes, and review them, you'll do well. Book is probably helpful but not necessary.

I loved his class! You can also tell that he genuinely enjoys teaching the material. He's also very well knowledgeable about neuroscience and the man is highly intelligent! Also, attendance is important since he tests mostly on his lectures, not so much on the book and he uploads lecture slides. Overall, he is a great prof and is great at teaching.
Good Job!
If you can learn through an accent this professor is fine. She goes through many examples, is well prepared, and understands the material very well.

Took this class for Summer Session 1 2016 and I felt the class was so difficult :^( She is very UNFAIR during testings because she let the people who got their exams starts first. She should let us take it on the same time. Also, FINALS was way more than practice exam and TOO DIFFICULT. AVOID HER AT ALL COST!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Hopefully SHE'LL CURVE!

Had her for 20B which I found to be more difficult than later math courses. Lectures were essentially examples from the text written on the board. Master the homework and you will be fine in this course. Make sure to take advantage of section, too. Exams were challenging but doable. Moderate accent sometimes interfered during lectures.

Personally, she has a slight accent but she's very fair and kind. Gives examples relevant to the homework and her final, and tells you roughly what should be on it. She was also fairly forgiving in partial credit, and hardly, if any, trick questions.

Her lectures do not help much.  You will learn more studying the textbook yourself. However, her tests are easy and she picks questions straight out of HW and practice midterm so that's a plus. She is an easy grader. In all, it's not that hard if you actually pay attention and go to her (or her TAs) office hours and review sessions.

His teaching is alright. Sometimes he does not teach some topics but expects you to know the material through the assigned reading. There are mistakes in his book one in a while. Lecture is pretty chill as he gives you time to play games. He assigns a lot of problems for homework. Tests are easy and straightforward but there is no curve.
His lecture and homework is much easier than the final, few people get an A in the final.

Professor Haff was a pretty good teacher. If you did well in Math 180A this class is no biggie. Tests were hard. Although Professor Haff probably won't be teaching this class again as he is a bit older..
Awesome Professor!!

One of the best math professors at UCSD, in fact, UCSD's math department never ceases to impress me with the professors (the ones that teach upper division at least).  He was super friendly and really friendly too. He also kind of talks like Sean Connery minus the Scottish accent.  His TA Will, was also amazing. I think he TAs for him all the time.

Would NOT take again. For a GE course, the materials are extremely heavy and demanding. Lecture is long and without powerpoint, making it very difficult to keep up. Overall I felt I learned nothing but was constantly stressed from the workload.
Horrible professor.

She didn't teach or use material very relevant to what the course was supposed to be about. Avoid this professor if you're looking for GE's. Her lectures are just her talking so I would avoid if you're visual learner. Readings are up on TritonED and reserves but VERY unorganized. Avoid for GE, I feel she's perfect for like grad classes for ETHN.

Unncessary amount of work for just a ge class. She has a strict no phone policy but you can use it as long as she doesnt see it. Dont let her hear your phone though. Assigns a lot of reading that are super dense. Class is boring and hard to keep track of what she is teaching. Would not recommend.

She said, she hopes this is the most challenging course you take here even though it is an introductory course to ethnic studies. She gives out a lot of readings per week but they are all up on TED. Your grade mostly depends on your TA since they are grading your assignments. This class is a lot of work if you are taking it for a GE.
He is an  amazing professor for my Econ 2 class. Clear ppt lectures and use daily life examples. I recommend for all of yours. You can really learn and understand it. Study hard!

He's a graduate student, and was allowed to teach for the summer; it showed. The class was 24% midterm, 54 % or so final. Basically the grade was determined on the tests. He started out slow, and then was rushing through the power point by the end of class.

Took his class a while ago, but just reviewing now. As you can see, you'll either love him or hate him. He's brutally honest, but spot-on accurate with his notes. It may not have been the best experience getting notes from him, but he's the professor who helped my writing more than anyone. If you're not sensitive about your work, don't hesitate.

Knows what he is talking about but definitely had a list of favorite students -- and of not favorite students. If you're on the latter list, it has most likely very little to do with your work ethic and more to do with the fact that he just doesn't like you. If you're on the good list, this course should be an easy A!

Really sarcastic and funny. He'll try to convince you to change your major from writing to something more practical, but he'll help you out if you stick around. He can be harsh sometimes, so if you're sensitive stay away. I learned a ton from this guy though, so I suggest giving him a shot despite his classes being difficult.

This is a professor that will challenge you to push yourself.  He is blunt and does not sugar coat the truth, but if you are serious about being a better writer you need to be prepared for critique that is brutally honest. There is no "fan club."  If you work for him, he will work for you.

his office hours I walk away with my next idea for my paper, if you don't get n e thing out if office hours its cause you went in there expecting him to tell you what You wanted to talk about aka you didn't Think before walking in there.

His lectures are very condensed, so be ready to type/write really fast! He doesn't have any clicker questions or quizzes, so most of your grade relies on your final draft of your essay instead. I've taken him for SSI in 2 3-hr lectures per week , and he makes sure we're let out at least 30-40 minutes earlier. Read the course reader and you're fine.

Class was great the few times I went.  He's very passionate about what he was teaching (Edgar Allan Poe).  Two midterm papers (5 pages long each) and a final research paper (8-10 pages long).  Good thing about this was class was that one of the midterm papers you could switch out for a dramatic reading, which was super fun. Great prof and class.

Dr. Cassedy presents material in a more conceptualphilosophical way, therefore it was easy for me to get lost in his train of thoughts because he elaborates so much. I did very well on the midterms without attending class all the time, big concepts important, his test will ask you to talk about things in the readings.

His way of explaining things is extremely difficult to understand and follow. I showed up to every lecture and went to his office hours regularly and yet still got C's and B's on his midterms. Extremely hard grader. Wouldn't recommend him for religion.
Really good teacher.

Had her for 20D and E. Only went to lecture once between the two courses, so I have no idea about her teaching style. The homework could be tedious but was manageable. The exams were fair for the most part if you studied the textbook and hw (she borrows problems from the book and her own practice exams). Generous curve. Take her if you self-study.

Professor Shin is one the sweetest professors I have met so far at UCSD. Her class demanded a lot of reading since we discussed it at the next class lecture and participation counts. At times it was difficult to understand her as English is her second language but she clarified whenever someone was confused. Take her if you have the chance!

Fina is awesome. Her Venezuelan accent combined with her effort to understand modern student behavior and perspective makes her a joy to have as a professor. Though she can be very blunt (probably because of her cultural social boundaries), she is an incredibly useful resource if you ask her the right questions, participate, and earn her respect.

Not as bad as many make him out to be. Very willing to help if asked. Lectures were useful as supplements to the text--be prepared to lean on the text later on in the course. Points were given via i-Clicker for attendance and participation, so be ready to go to lecture. Exams were not horrible, but don't expect an A if all you do is go to lecture.
So his accent makes this class super hard the only way my friends and i have survived is off of us holding study groups on our own time.

Professor Zimmerman's lectures are really long and boring. The lecture slides are kinda impossible to take notes on because they're mostly pictures. Choose a different professor for Chemistry if you can.

He is very passionate about what he is talking about and is willing to help any time somebody asks. Again, it is an 8 am class so it's at times hard to stay awake. He has a slight accent but is still relatively easy to understand. The work load for the class is fair, and the quizzes/ midterms are pretty easy granted you do the homework.
Doesn't explain anything, just reads off a powerpoint slide. You'll be consistently 1 to 2 chapters behind every other class, so you'll be screwed for 6B.

Unfocused lectures and ultimately unnecessary readings made this course worse than it could have been. "Land and Labor" seemed to fall to the wayside as the plight of Native Americans/immigrants/slaves was hammered on again and again. Grade is highly dependent on TA, so go to section. Overall would not recommend this course.

Although attendance is not mandatory, lectures can provide a lot of study material. However her lectures are disorganized and unclear to the point where one could miss a lot of main points because there was no exact focus in comparison to  guest lecturers'. TAs are also dependent on your grade based on effort and participation and can be helpful.

The class I had her for, Land and Labor, was a steaming pile of communist/socialist propaganda and race-baiting garbage. She was a pretty alright professor herself, and attending lectures are pretty important, but the reading wasn't very important. Discussion section is mandatory and suuuper helpful.
She never posts lecture slides and its unclear what she wants us to take away from the course. She is also very unhelpful and is really rude to students.

The course itself had potential and I enjoyed my discussion sections with my TA, but Professor Harper mainly read from her notes and her slides didn't have that much information. She tried a little harder with her lecturing style after a few guest lecturers from the presented. She could have focused on the more broader topic of Land and Labor.
a real easy A, as long as you're willing to sing you're good. don't even have to go to every single class. (in fact, I skipped half of it last quarter and still got an A)
Love Phil!
He needs to help his students more!!
Love this class :)I've taken it three quarters now. Fun grade-boosting course. Professor is great
Class is a lot of fun. Phil is very entertaining and has a lot of stories about the old days. The music is always challenging. Make sure you take this class the quarter they have a concert scheduled.

I was taught by Dr Ghiara last year. He was an incredibly passionate lecturer, committed to helping his students succeed! Definitely take his class as you can as he is very straightforward as to what he expects in exams. Great class and professor!!!

Excellent professor! very passionate and made the class very enjoyable. You couldn't fall asleep in his classes if you wanted to. It was a bit dumbed down, and the tests were very very easy. He really cares about inspiring the next generation of scientists.

Incredibly easy A makes the fact that Ghiara is a "meeeeeh" teacher somewhat more palatable. The lectures aren't confusing simply because the material itself is very straight forward. He didn't seem to care much about his students, but he demonstrates a lot of passion for his subject and teaching itself if that makes any sense.

Dr. G is an amazing lecturer and truly cares about his students. If you are a bio major, definitely try to take his human reproduction class before you graduate. He is very clear about what he expects on exams, and if you pay attention to lecture, text book reading is minimal.
Ghiara is the best lower div bio prof at UCSD. He is a genius in the field, and is also blessed with humor and incredible teaching ability. Take as many classes with him as possible!!

Lecture's were really boring, class was Super easy. He flipped out one time when I raised my hand and said: "key change." He also sang us Taylor Swift and dressed like a Cowboy. Experimental mucisian, hilarious. His website Clintophonics gave use hours of entertainment, I advise you look that up. I got an A though so I didnt care how boring it was.

His class is honestly what you make of it. If you choose to not do the readings, then lectures will have no meaning to you and will feel like a very long 50 minutes. However, if you're actively engaging in the readings, his lectures provide very good insight that you might not have picked up on. Also, going to TA office hours is amazing.

If you're not a math major then I would definitely not recommend taking him. His tests aren't anything like the homework or what he went over in class, they're totally out of the blue. If you can avoid him then definitely do.

Go to class, he explains everything you need to know very well! Fair tests and final. Homework can be tricky, but treat it independently from what you learn it class, homework is harder and will not be tested on the exams.

I am not sure if it is the first time he teaches math 109. Overall his is good. MATH 109 is a hard class that requires a lot of proof. If you do not attend the class, you will be easily lost in tons of rigorous proofs. He writes the proof clearly and his method is easy to understand. His exam is pretty easy.

I had Oliver for 20D and 20E. He's a really good professor and one of the clearest I've ever had. He answers questions on piazza and in email very quickly. You can tell he actually cares about his students. He won't test you on anything he doesn't teach in class. His tests are really fair. Good guy good teacher.

Amazing Professor. Heknows how to teach. The tests cover exactly what is in homework and lectures. He isn't trying to trick you. Go to his office hours. He's a great person and professor. Hoping he's stay at UCSD.
He literally just reads from the slides, if you miss class its definitely not the end on the world

Good class.  Prof. Beardsley is a great guy to see during OH and very adept at teaching.  Class consists of midterm, final, 2 short papers.  Participation counts in section, too.  Don't have to do 100% of reading to do well.

Very simple, straightforward powerpoint presentations that make note-taking easier.  Explains the material very well and uses relevant, easy to follow examples for key concepts.  He definitely cares about teaching us poli sci.  Tests and papers are fair; difficulty of the course depends on ur TA and how interested in the topic u r.  Intelligent guy
I learned more then i thought i would. you don't have to do the readings to do well, but a lot of it depends on how much you go to class and section. highly recommended.

Her lecture notes are clear and straightforward. As long as you understand the material from the lecture, you're ready for the exams. Her exams are based on the material she covered in class. Everyone is welcomed to go to her office hour and chill. She is there for you. If you think her class is hard, wait till you take Chem 6B.
She makes you work for it, but she's very accessible and patient. Overall, good professor.

Gets annoyed by little things. Very confusing lecturer. Does not curve, which doesn't make sense considering the rigor of her tests. Says she wants her students to succeed but is very rude to people who do not understand the concepts. I got an A but no thanks to her.
I don't know if the same German TA is teaching this quarter but I was in his section last quarter and he was beautiful.
She does not curve.

Decent/Easy Advanced Elective Class and generous curves! However, the TA I had was the worst TA ever.  Zachary B. (TA)  makes the material more harder than it is,  bad at optimization problem, never reply back to emails from students, and grades harshly on midterms/finals.

Really generous curve on each test and a little at the class at the very end. You really have to not try to fail. Lecture was different from the homework which was different from the tests. He likes to throw in trick questions as well even if you study all of it. Lectures were very dry, but its 100A. Econtutor!

Difficult class. The practice tests do not fairly represent the actual tests. There tends to be exam questions that are not in the book nor in the lecture notes. Professor Andreoni is a very approachable and nice person but does not present the material very well. The lecture notes can be unclear and terminology is different than the book.

He is literally the worst professor ever. Practice midterms have NOTHING to do with what he will actually give you in class. Messes up lecture notes all the time and it gets very frustrating. I'm sure he is a smart man but he is an AWFUL professor and should be kicked out of the econ department. AVOID AT ALL COSTS

Excellent professor and made this class very enjoyable. I was not looking forward to this class but he definitely made me want to come to every class. He was pretty cute and a lot hipper than he looks too.

Textbook was hard to understand, and the entire subject was irrelevant, but the teacher made up for it. She wasn't phenomenal, but she was better than most. Good lectures, only homework was reading. Be careful about the tests though: 50 minutes to do 17 MC and 3 essay questions. Essay questions asked a lot. Make sure to read for the class!

Three hour lectures or the prof reading from the slides. As long as you studied the slides and skimmed the textbook, you can easily ace the multiple choicetrue-false midterms and final. I only went to lectures the week before an exam. Easy A and no discussions. SONAs can be mostly done online. She's a new teacher so I suppose it can't be helped.

Took a 6-9pm class from her. Lectures are boring, reads directly from slides. I would never stay the entire time. Tests are fair. Guest lectures from her assistants suck. Definitely went to the book for clarity on topics. Typical intro class. Every topic is briefly covered. Filled with eager freshman. All about memorization.

At the first half of the quarter I doesn't like her lecture. Her handwriting confused me, and i just can't understand the lecture(maybe I need more time). So later I move to the front seat and I study before the lecture. Well, I feel good, but the grade is actually not. The final is not that hard, also the midterms. There's no quizzes.

For a first time professor, she is not bad. Hopefully she'll improve as the years go by. The first midterm was easy; the second not so much. The final was in between. She'll help you if you ask for it, but nothing is spoon fed. Put in the work yourself and you'll reap the rewards.

Okay, so the people here are being far too harsh. I had Xu Wang the quarter before, and she is miles better than him. For a first time professor, she is honestly pretty good, but yes she could use some improving. Try going to her office hours, as she does try and help.

In the beginning, the lectures were not clear enough. But after the second midterm, she changed and improved a lot. The exams are indeed tough, but if you go to review session, you can learn a lot. The reasons why I give her a relative high point are 1. she showed improvement, although the final exam even more difficult   2. she is cute

I am not sure what to think of this professor. She is a really nice person, but her lectures are not that helpful. I had to rely on the book a lot. Her midterms, and especially the final, relied heavily on concepts. I do not know how this class has been my most difficult class out of the math series. Choose your professors wisely...

She is very passionate about biology and the course is very interesting. The course tasks get a bit repetitive and the quizzes are not too difficult if you review the lectures. The snack break during the final was unexpected and interesting.  You are basically given a task or tasks and expected to do them by the end of each day of lab.

She is very kind and and loves to support the students. She and Dr. Joe make an adorable team and really care about getting their students excited about biology. Lectures are clear and she is very helpful in lab. Glad to be taking another class with them next quarter.
Awesome professor. I found no other words to say.

I thought that the class was fun. It was co-taught with Prof. Larsen when I took the class, and Prof. Pogliano helped me out even when it wasn't her turn to teach yet during OH. Test questions are all straight off lecture slides, no tricks to them, you just have to read everything clearly so you don't mis-read the choices.

Good class.  Lectures were good and all on powerpoint.  She puts up all her slides before class, so you don't have to copy anything.  Very knowledgeable.  Co-taught w/ Rachel Larsen - 2 midterms w/ lowest grade dropped (first one is easier than the second), microbewiki project (which is pretty time consuming), and a final- all multiple choice tests

Open Source Hardware Movement was extremely interesting.  There wasn't really a lecture portion to it, but he gave a lot of insight and feedback on projects.  He's very diverse, and has a lot of ideas.  I think this course closely resembles an internship, and you'll learn a lot if you want to. Grade depends on effort; so: Work hard, and get an A.
He is really good prof. His 141 and 141L is not easy , but his class is easier than other 141 and 141L classes

Really really great prof. He wont let you down like other prof but he will bring you up. Encourage you and let you do well not only in his class but in real life. You wont regret if you take him. You will learn alot from him. Other good points are mentioned by other people. He is the best prof that i've ever taken.you can reach him anytime in gchat

Not as organized as his 141 lectures. The exams included true/false questions on random facts in the lecture slides, but most of the material is reinforced in the homework assignments. Overall, a good prof to take. The class included a project to improve a cache prefetcher, which was very difficult but very leniently graded.

Very good lecturer, really knows his stuff. Down-to-earth and lenient on deadlines, as mentioned before. If you take 141L, make sure your assembler is very good, it'll make your life easier. Both the class and the lab take lots of time.

Very friendly professor, tries to get the class involved and tried to learn their names. 1 Midterm, 1 final, 4 assignments and 4 quizzes. All based off of readings and lectures. Make sure to do all of the readings. They will be important for assignments and tests

She basically copied her slides from the book so showing up is essentially useless. When she cottoned on to the fact that people didn't want to come, she started passing out sign in sheets. Not showing up will knock your participation grade a bit. If you do show up, bring a book or some other work you need to get done.

Her class isn't  bad if you read the lab manual and attend lectures (there's iclicker). 6 weekly quizzes (1 make-up quiz) 3 midterms, no final. If you want a good grade, make sure to do the ASSIGNED READING.  Readings are roughly 40 pages a week depending on what experiment you are about to do.
It was her second time teaching this class and I thought she did a pretty good job. Although I would probably get a crappy grade, I did enjoy her class and did learn a good amount.
If you want to take note during class, don't take his. His writing is terrible because of his artistic french symbols.

Amazing professor! His lectures are really inspiring. He has a French accent which may be hard to understand at first but gradually you'll get used to it. Very clear hand-writing, get ready to take notes. Very little homework compared to other math  professors. HIGHLY RECOMMEND
Amazing professor. Saved me from academic disqualification. I love this man.

He's  a good lecturer, but I highly recommend you to review the chapters afterwards to understand the material better. His exams are fair and there is no curve. The HW is really easy so no worries there. Attending class and section helped me a lot so if you can go, go. Overall, prof is a really nice guy who wants his students to do well.

Professor Pelletier is an amazing guy if you know him. Go to his office hours and let him know who you are and he will help you lots. He does have a semi-thick French accent which confuses a lot of people in lecture. But the concepts are not hard to understand if you do the homework he assigns. Will need the textbook to do the homework.

Expected a tough course; however, this was ridiculous.  Lectures were more confusing than helpful and he goes on long tangents which do nothing to further the course material.  Death by powerpoint with no helpful information.  Reading wasn't helpful as it's impossible to predict what will be on the exam (which was poorly written and confusing).

Absolutely loved this class!!! Professor Sammartino is a super super interesting guy and this class does not disappoint. Yes, the lectures are 3 hours long but much of it is spent watching demonstrations not taking notes. Exams are on the hard side but this class is totally worth it and the grading options make it reasonable. Hoping he comes back!

BEST PROFESSOR HANDS DOWN. got me into psychology. cares a lot. knows his material and i know people say his material is difficult, but if you're interested and go talk to him in office hours, he is more than fair
One of the prof you can't miss at UCSD
I LOVE Dr Sammartino The best teacher I have ever had in my life THE END

Prof. Sammartino is passionate about his the subject matter and teaching it to students. He is one of the most articulate and smart professors I have taken at UCSD and I have learned an incredible amount from the two classes I have taken with him. He does a 5 quiz model dropping the lowest scored quiz plus allows extra credit. Awesome instructor!!

Honestly the best math professor I've had this year. He holds review sessions before the midterms and finals. He is a really good lecturer and explains the content extremely well along with examples. Plus he has a good sense of humor

Professor Buss is great because he is the antithesis to the stereotypical college professor. He is funny, knows his stuff, and will always be there if you are willing to be there for him. I am not very good at math but people like him are the reason I keep trying. If Professor Buss ever reads this, thank you very much.

Professor Buss makes a lot of errors when he's doing his calculations on the board, but he's still good at teaching concepts. Most of the time he managed to fit in anywhere from 1-3 examples per topic, usually with increasing difficulty. His office hours are extremely helpful. If you have questions then definitely go cause it'll be worth it.

Seems like a nice enough guy. However, his lectures are very theoretical and does have many examples in them. It could be tough to do the homework without a few examples to show you how to do it. Study groups are very useful for this class. I personally did not learn much from the lectures, so be prepared to read the textbook and use other sources.

Samuel Buss was the best teacher I had at UCSD. Someone please buy him new chalk though, poor guy struggled with his $60 Japanese chalk from Amazon the entire quarter but ended up having to use old chalk from the math department. Expect subtle humor and overall adorableness. He does great lectures, even if its not prepared on a powerpoint.

He's one of the best professors I've ever had at UCSD. The CSE department is filled with great lecturers, but Graham is definitely in my top 5. Even if you know the material, go to class anyway or at least listen to his podcasts. He will enlighten you.

Extremely nice, caring, and a genuine genius (google him). Probably the fairest tests I have ever taken, which means if you study with a real intention to get an A you will get an A. Slipped up on first midterm (literally failed) but aced the second and final and got an A in the class. Course is interesting and useful.

Take this teacher! He has a very nice grandpa-like disposition; I really liked this prof. He cared about his students and he's very intelligent. And, tests were extremely fairrelatively easy (cheat sheets). Go to lecture because there is (kind of) no book, and no slides. Plus, he's got his own Wiki page :-)
Probably the nicest professor ever.

Great professor. Very clear and tests were extremely fair (including the final). As long as you study the example problems from class and example tests, you'll be fine. Seems like a genuinely nice guy too. He's the one responsible for Graham's number!

Jim was one of the most influential prof's ever. He changed that way that I think, and he really pushed me to challenge myself. He encouraged me through all 4 years of college. He is not easy, and he can smell bs miles away, but he really encourages inter-disciplinary thinking and integration.  He does cut slack when you need it.

Took him for summer session and he himself said that his class was an easy a and it was. all that was required was to read plays and watch the movie before coming to discuss in class. He asks for small analysis of scenes and the final and midterm were replicas of classwork. Lectures are pretty boring tho.

Not mandatory to attend lecture since all you do is watch plays but I found it interesting because he would leave 10 minutes at the end to discuss these intricate details about the film. He opened my eyes to the way movies are filmed and taught me to pay attention to details. Easy A. You only write 3-4 essays. 1000 word essay is your final.

Barely any students show up for his class because there are no real incentives to come. You can watch the movies at home and submit the essays online. Essays are based off a lot of fluff--a bunch of opinions of why everything ties together. Unfortunately, I feel I wasted time with this class (I attended every lecture).

This class was fun, easy, & interesting. Professor Carmody focused on several films wherein a few minutes where watched in class & the rest on your own time. After each film is discussed you are to write a short paper on the given prompt. Attend class for specific lecture tips that help with the paper & participate in discussions for extra credit.

The only thing that really bothers me is that Professor Kastner does not put up enough information online. There's no syllabus, grading scale, lecture notes, grades or rubric for assignments online. So although the attendance is not mandatory, it is nearly impossible to do well without showing up in lectures. It's too inflexible for a college class
Granger is AMAZING!!! He helped my writing so much! Go to office hours, toughen your skin and get ready to improve. He's honest and brilliant, if you can handle honest you can learn a lot.

Granger is to be taken with a grain of salt. His approach to literature is what I look for in a professor: pure passion. His theory class might be the hardest class I've taken at UCSD but it's extremely interesting. He's one of those unfound geniuses that you encounter very few times in your career. Highly enjoyable discussions in class.

I HIGHLY recommend to avoid Granger as a professor. He may appear laid back and say that any style of writing goes, but it's definitely a lie! Unless you cater to his weird tastes in your writing you can be sure that you won't get an A. Absolutely terrible professor, worst I've had at UCSD

Granger is a genius. He may seem a little out there but the way he thinks is pure brilliance. I have taken many of his classes and he is by far one of the smartest professors at UCSD. You just have to attend class and bounce ideas off him. Awesome guy.

Wonderful professor. Granger is incredibly helpful during office hours, and if you listen, he will improve your writing. Those who are complaining probably couldn't take the criticism. Like any other class at UCSD, if you don't have some talent for it, you won't do well. It's not his fault if you can't write and won't listen to his advice.

Professor demands way too much for a 4 unit class. Her lecture slides were very long & dense. Defeats the purpose of a PowerPoint. Needs to be more short & precise when explaining. She seemed unable to explain topics in simple terms, which says a lot about her lack of teaching experience. She is a very tough grader on assignments.
I personally enjoy this course.

I loved Prof Hughes' class. Does she expect you to work hard? Yes. But honestly, if you're not prepared to put in the work why are you at college? There is tons of reading (literally 7 books) but keep to a tight reading schedule you'll be fine.

Very intelligent, passionate and really knows her stuff.  Does she talk a lot? Yes. Are there lots of readings? Yes.  She will not hold your hand but the lecture outlines and the simplicity of the midterm and final questions put you in control of your own fate.  Honestly, maybe not the most charismatic teacher but you'd have to be a moron to fail.

Professor Hughes is beyond intelligent. Don't enroll in her classes if you are truly interested in history. Her lectures are extremely interesting. I learned the most from her class than any I've ever taken. Only a midterm and final but you MUST do the readings and incorporate them.
Don't take this class!!!! The professor makes you read 7 books in the quarter, and you can barely survive if history is not your major. If it's for a GE, don't take it!!! It's a big time waster.

I took the Revelle Honors Seminar. Nothing too special. Just show up and listen to various other representatives from various departments in UCSD. Have fun in this class! A lot of people in this class look very uninterested in what is going on, which I find quite rude because the Provost pushed for a seminar like this.  Don't let his efforts drown!
Very experienced lighting designer, I enjoyed taking his class and it's given me more direction as to what I want to do later in life.
Very knowledgeable about lighting design. Super nice. Not always the clearest when giving project instructions, but the class is so laid back, it doesn't really matter.

Luis is the BEST writing teacher I've ever had.  Yes, he made me work for that A, but that's only because I started the quarter with horrible writing skills, hence the 2 on easiness.  Like all Muir Writing teachers, to really take advantage of him, you have to go to office hours, Hence the 3 on helpfulness and 4 on clarity.  TLDR; take him.

I've been taking classes with Mr. Cratty on and off for years, and I don't know another instructor who has such a comprehensive understanding of theory, along with a passion to convey its importance to his students. He's a relaxed guy, who works with his students and really loves classical music and the Beatles. He's inspired me to major in music.

This class was fun, relaxing and low pressure. I improved my baseline skills and developed new proficiencies and knowledge. Dr. Cratty  is a gifted and accomplished musician and instructor.  He is very patient, incorporates music theory and history, and has a knack for giving individual attention to students at their various skill levels.

I am so lucky to learn piano with Dr Cratty. I was in his class in the past 5 quarters. He is super nice and patient. I could' t image a professor in UCSD music school could teach a beginner like me so patiently. He didn't only teach us piano skills , but also the theory and history of music! You could learn the different countries' music in class

This extension course is a stress reliever! Basically just practice at home, come, learn, and you will get an A. The professor is friendly, good humored, sometimes gets sidetracked with his interesting stories. Learned a lot from him!

Dr. Carver is awesome. She is extremely engaging, and you can tell she is knowledgeable and passionate about what she teacher. She's more than  happy to answer any questions thoroughly, and is a professor who is approachable. This class is really hands on, and it feels more like a discussion than a lecture. For sure one of my favorite profs!

Chill and humorous teacher. Lecture slides can be all over the place at times but she explains the concepts pretty well with hands-on activities. both books are not required since her exams are mainly based on lecture. but itll come in handy for the essay portion of the exams. 8 pg  research paper due at the end of the quarter.

Dr. Carver is awesome. Her lectures are engaging and interesting. She really knows her field and it definitely shows through the material. There's always room for questions and she always answers them thoroughly. It feels more like a discussion than a lecture which makes the class a lot more enjoyable. Hands down my favorite teacher so far!

She is so nice and helpful. you will learn a lot in her class. BUT if you want work in her lab, think again; her LAB COORDINATOR SUCKS.  she is so RUDE and SELFISH. I don't know why Dr. Carver lets this girl to coordinate her lab. DO NOT take 199 with dr. Carver because you have to deal with her lab coordinator.

She may seem hard to approach, but once you show your interest in the subject she really helpful in explaining the material. She helped me a lot to prepare my debate part and spent time in out of office hours. Great teacher and has a lot of experience to count on from her own lab.
Dr. Kokotovic is a real babe, but you should have seen him when he was younger!  Smokin'!
The best LTSP professor EVER.
My favorite professor in the Literature department. He is very organized, dedicated, accessible and a great instructor overall!
Best teacher I've ever had, he's so organized and clear in the discussions. LOVE HIM.
good
Favorite professor at UCSD

I've taken three of Professor Goldwasser's classes. She is one of the sweetest professors you will meet and her courses are interesting. Make sure to show up to class EVERY TIME bc her iClickers are crucial to your final grade. Lectures can feel a bit long.
Attend office hours! She is extremely helpful and nice! Must do readings in order to do well. Tourism class was extremely interesting. One of my favorite Comm professors :)

Her multiple choice are regarded as hard only because she tests beyond memorization, and wants  students to apply the concepts learned related to understanding the construction of meaning in film. She's really nice and encourages going to office hours (she requires a participation grade), and the papers required are focused but easy to do well on.

Let me start off with the positives: Prof. Goldwasser is incredibly nice and she is there if you need help. Negatives: Her multiple choice and matching are insanely tough even if you know the definitions to the key terms. She tricks you! Her lectures are boring and difficult to follow which makes it hard to want to go to class.

Really enjoyed this class. Prof Weinstein is a great lecturer and keeps things interesting. Tests aren't hard, just listen and know the music and its context well. He gives you points as well. Lectures are still important as most material you need is verbal. He is also very clear on what he wants from you and very passionate about what he teaches.
The content of the class is interesting to begin with but Prof W. is a music grad and is very much into removing the layers as he calls it of the socio economic narrative of the blues.
Great professor! His lectures (powerpoints especially) really help you to understand the course material. Lots of reading and hw for each week, but it greatly helps for the midterms.

Very passionate about the subject (The Beatles) and makes every lecture interesting. Though this is a music GE, keep an eye out on your grade. It is fairly simple to get an A, but keep in mind 1 point on anything, be it a test or TED quiz is 1% of your grade. That said, do one 1 or 2 extra credit assignments and you're more than fine.
An amazing class, one of the best lecturers you will encounter. Josh has an extensive knowledge of his subject and truly involves his students in the class, even in the enormous warren lecture hall

He is definitely knowledgeable on the subject, but his lectures are pretty dry. The daily readings are long and he requires weekly journals, a midterm essay, and final. Your grade depends entire on your TA, so hope for a good one.

He is boring, but his presentation helps you stay focused because he puts everything on the powerpoint. So, taking notes for his lecture was easy. Just read the assigned materials, and go to every lectures for iclicker questions. Iclicker is worth 20 percent of your grade, so it can help or not help depending on how you use it.

Professor Propp is extremely knowledgeable, but his lectures were not that clear and interesting, for the points he made somewhat lost connections and were hard to follow. Though he's not the best lecturer, he's definitely a great scholar from whom I learned a lot! Clicker Qs/tests are ok for me. Readings are long and time-consuming yet helpful.

Although his lectures are a little boring at times due to the subject, he is fun to listen to sometimes since he'll include small jokes in his lectures. The midterm paper is fair and he gives more than enough time to work on it and the final exam is extremely easy as long as you do the course readings and pay attention in lectures.

Unlike most people, I actually really enjoyed this class. Propp was very into his material, and he made the classes much more interesting than the actual material. He had a decent sense of humor, too. The TA, on the other hand, was awful. She would tell me to do something for a paper, and then when I did it, she marked it down. So beware the TA.

I had to retake this course and so glad I did with this professor. His accent is not a big issue, can overlook it easily.
